fakten.text_en: Chapter 2 contains the EICAS messages (message as title), chapter 3 the non-annunciated issues, chapter 4 the known misbehaviours of EPIC Load 9.0. Each chapter first gives a mitigation procedure, then additional information.

fakten.text: Jede Reset-Prozedur muss im ATLS festgehalten werden, ausser die FOL-Prozedur bestimmt etwas anderes.
fakten.text_en: Any reset procedure must be recorded in the ATLS unless the specific FOL procedure stipulates otherwise.

fakten.text: Muss eine Prozedur täglich angewendet werden, wird für jedes betroffene Flugzeug ein Eintrag im Aircraft Status (Briefing Card Items) gemacht.
fakten.text_en: If a procedure has to be followed every day, an entry is made in the Aircraft Status (briefing card items) for each concerned aircraft.

fakten.text: Die CDL aus dem DDPM ist als Appendix publiziert, weil sie eine Simplified Method für Mehrverbrauch und Performance Penalties bietet. Die Drag-Index-Methode der AFM-CDL ist mit dem Flight Planning System nicht kompatibel.
fakten.text_en: The CDL from the DDPM is published as an appendix because it provides a simplified method for additional fuel burn and performance penalties. The drag index method of the AFM CDL is not compatible with the flight planning system.

fakten.text: Revision 05 vom 23.09.2026. Neu: Cabin Pressurization Oscillation During Cruise (3.8) und Appendix 1 (CDL).
fakten.text_en: Revision 05 of 23.09.2026. New: Cabin Pressurization Oscillation During Cruise (3.8) and appendix 1 (CDL).

themen.name: EICAS Messages
themen.beschreibung: Bekannte EICAS Messages mit SAMBA-Prozedur: HSTAB LO RATE, FD VERT MODE OFF, FLT CTRL NO DISPATCH, STEEP APPR NOT AVAIL, AT FAIL und BRK OVERHEAT.
themen.beschreibung_en: Known EICAS messages with a SAMBA procedure: HSTAB LO RATE, FD VERT MODE OFF, FLT CTRL NO DISPATCH, STEEP APPR NOT AVAIL, AT FAIL and BRK OVERHEAT.

bibliothek.einleitung: Bekannte EICAS Messages mit SAMBA-Prozedur: HSTAB LO RATE, FD VERT MODE OFF, FLT CTRL NO DISPATCH, STEEP APPR NOT AVAIL, AT FAIL und BRK OVERHEAT.
bibliothek.einleitung_en: Known EICAS messages with a SAMBA procedure: HSTAB LO RATE, FD VERT MODE OFF, FLT CTRL NO DISPATCH, STEEP APPR NOT AVAIL, AT FAIL and BRK OVERHEAT.

fakten.text: Reset nur ohne korrelierte CMC Message (MCC prüft), am Boden mit Parking Brake, einmal pro Leg: PITCH TRIM SYS 1 AND SYS 2 CUTOUT Buttons PUSH IN, THEN OUT. Danach Pitch Trim NOSE UP, FULL NOSE DOWN, AS REQUIRED.
fakten.text_en: Reset only without a correlated CMC message (MCC verifies), on ground with parking brake set, once per leg: PITCH TRIM SYS 1 AND SYS 2 CUTOUT buttons PUSH IN, THEN OUT. Then pitch trim NOSE UP, FULL NOSE DOWN, AS REQUIRED.

fakten.text: Im Flare oder nach dem Touchdown bei Autoland mit weiterhin engaged AUTOLAND 1: keine Crew Action. Ursache ist ein Glideslope-Miscompare nahe der Piste. Ohne Autoland disengagen APPR1/APPR2 und die FD-Modes.
fakten.text_en: In the flare or after touchdown during autoland with AUTOLAND 1 still engaged: no crew action. The cause is a glideslope miscompare close to the runway. Without autoland, APPR1/APPR2 and the FD modes disengage.

fakten.text: Probe Covers entfernen, ADS PROBES HEATER PRESS IN, 5 bis 10 Minuten warten, PRESS OUT. Verschwindet die Message, war es Eis auf den ADS Probes und der Flug kann stattfinden.
fakten.text_en: Remove probe covers, ADS PROBES HEATER PRESS IN, wait 5 to 10 minutes, PRESS OUT. If the message fades away it was ice on the ADS probes and the flight can be continued.

fakten.text: Erscheint in der Pre-Flight, solange die FADEC stromlos ist, und erlischt, sobald sie Strom hat.
fakten.text_en: Appears during pre-flight while the FADEC is powered off and extinguishes once it is powered.

fakten.text: Vorübergehender Zustand der AFCS-Logik. Keine Maintenance Action, wenn die Message nach wenigen Sekunden verschwindet.
fakten.text_en: Transitory condition of the AFCS logics. No maintenance action if the message disappears after a few seconds.

fakten.text: Ab 520 °C Bremstemperatur am Boden. Parking Brake setzen, Ground Crew warnen, warten bis die Message weg ist, Chocks nur von vorne oder hinten setzen, bei GREEN Reifen prüfen, MCC melden. Dispatch für bis zu 10 Flight Cycles.
fakten.text_en: From 520 °C brake temperature on ground. Set parking brake, warn ground crew, wait until the message disappears, position chocks only from front or back, check tires once GREEN, report to MCC. Dispatch for up to 10 flight cycles.

themen.name: Non-Annunciated Issues
themen.beschreibung: Probleme ohne EICAS Message: Fuel Leak RH Wing, RA am Boden, FMS-Reset im Anflug, VAP, TO ENTRY INHIBITED, CPDLC Route Clearance, Escape Slide und Kabinendruck.
themen.beschreibung_en: Issues without an EICAS message: RH wing fuel leak, RA on ground, FMS reset on approach, VAP, TO ENTRY INHIBITED, CPDLC route clearance, escape slide and cabin pressure.

bibliothek.einleitung: Probleme ohne EICAS Message: Fuel Leak RH Wing, RA am Boden, FMS-Reset im Anflug, VAP, TO ENTRY INHIBITED, CPDLC Route Clearance, Escape Slide und Kabinendruck.
bibliothek.einleitung_en: Issues without an EICAS message: RH wing fuel leak, RA on ground, FMS reset on approach, VAP, TO ENTRY INHIBITED, CPDLC route clearance, escape slide and cabin pressure.

fakten.text: Im Descent: PACK 1 OFF, Altitude max. 31000 ft. Das schaltet das OBIGGS ab und senkt den Tankdruck. Ursache: OBIGGS High Flow Mode im Descent plus Turbulenz, die das Wing Float Vent Valve schliesst. Stoppt bei etwa 1100 bis 1350 kg pro Wing Tank und unter 4000 ft AGL.
fakten.text_en: In descent: PACK 1 OFF, altitude max 31000 ft. This disengages the OBIGGS and lowers the tank pressure. Cause: OBIGGS high flow mode in descent plus turbulence closing the wing float vent valve. Stops at around 1100 to 1350 kg per wing tank and below 4000 ft AGL.

fakten.text: Multipath durch Gebäude, Fahrzeuge und Gegenstände. Unter den Antennen braucht es 5,0 m freien Radius. Nach dem Power-Up mindestens 5 Minuten Warmup. Besteht die Flag vor dem Takeoff, Standard Abnormal Procedures.
fakten.text_en: Multipath from buildings, vehicles and objects. A clean radius of 5.0 m below the antennas is needed. After power-up at least 5 minutes warmup. If the flag persists before takeoff, standard abnormal procedures.

fakten.text: Im Secondary Flight Plan ZFM und TO C.G. (Perf Init 2/3) löschen. Reset im Final: Manual Speed, AT, grüne FGCS-Modes. Go-Around: TO/GA, Flaps 4, Gear UP, 150 kt, FLCH, HDG (bei Flaps 5: Flaps 2 und 160 kt). ATL Entry.
fakten.titel_en: Secondary flight plan and FMS reset
fakten.text_en: On the secondary flight plan delete ZFM and TO C.G. (Perf Init 2/3). Reset on final: manual speed, AT, green FGCS modes. Go-around: TO/GA, flaps 4, gear UP, 150 kt, FLCH, HDG (with flaps 5: flaps 2 and 160 kt). ATL entry.

fakten.text: VAP um 1 oder 2 kt erhöhen, oder im Anflug Speed auf MAN und ursprüngliche VAP manuell wählen. Abhängig von VAP, ISA-Abweichung und Missed Approach Altitude.
fakten.text_en: Increase the VAP by 1 or 2 kt, or set speed to MAN during the approach and select the original VAP manually. Depends on VAP, ISA deviation and missed approach altitude.

fakten.text: Reset von MAU 2 und MAU 3 löscht die Message und erlaubt die Eingabe der Takeoff-Daten.
fakten.text_en: A reset of MAU 2 and MAU 3 clears the message and allows entry of the takeoff data.

fakten.text: Alle Seiten lesen (--CONTINUED--), mit APPLY (LSK 2R) laden, Modified Flight Plan prüfen und aktivieren, dann ACCEPT (LSK 1R) für WILCO. Nicht einfach DIRECT TO zum Clearance Limit.
fakten.text_en: Read all pages (--CONTINUED--), load with APPLY (LSK 2R), review and activate the modified flight plan, then ACCEPT (LSK 1R) for WILCO. Do not simply fly DIRECT TO the clearance limit.

fakten.text: Tür ohne Jetway oder Treppe öffnen: Bereich unter der Tür frei von Personal und Equipment. Fällt das Package ohne Jetway, bläst es sich auf.
fakten.text_en: Opening a door without jetway or stairs: area below the door clear of personnel and equipment. If the package drops without a jetway, it inflates.

fakten.text: Bei geänderter Cruise Level 50 ft darüber eingeben, z. B. 25050 für FL250. Sonst wechselt das AMSC das Cabin Target bei jedem Überschreiten.
fakten.text_en: With a changed cruise level enter 50 ft above it, e.g. 25050 for FL250. Otherwise the AMSC changes the cabin target each time the level is exceeded.

themen.name: FMS Known Misbehaviours
themen.beschreibung: Bekannte FMS-Fehlverhalten mit EPIC Load 9.0: Engine Out, Speed Constraints, Ceiling, Flight Plan, RNP und Speed Targets.
themen.beschreibung_en: Known FMS misbehaviours with EPIC Load 9.0: engine out, speed constraints, ceiling, flight plan, RNP and speed targets.

bibliothek.einleitung: Bekannte FMS-Fehlverhalten mit EPIC Load 9.0: Engine Out, Speed Constraints, Ceiling, Flight Plan, RNP und Speed Targets.
bibliothek.einleitung_en: Known FMS misbehaviours with EPIC Load 9.0: engine out, speed constraints, ceiling, flight plan, RNP and speed targets.

fakten.text: Wird nach einem Engine Failure der START/STOP Selector auf STOP gestellt, setzt sich der FADEC-Prozessor zurück und das FMS nimmt wieder All Engines Operating an (EO RANGE springt auf ALL).
fakten.text_en: If the START/STOP selector is set to STOP after an engine failure, the FADEC processor resets and the FMS assumes all engines operating again (EO RANGE reverts to ALL).

fakten.text: Mehr als 20: Descent Constraints können schon im Climb kommandiert werden. Mehr als 47: FMS-Reset möglich, bei beiden FMS gehen alle Daten verloren.
fakten.text_en: More than 20: descent constraints may be commanded during the climb. More than 47: FMS reset possible, with both FMS all data are lost.

fakten.text: Mögliche Ursachen: Anti-Ice-ON-Tabellen über 31000 ft, zu tief vorhergesagter Climb-Verbrauch, oder MAX END als Cruise Speed Mode.
fakten.text_en: Possible causes: anti-ice ON tables above 31000 ft, too low predicted climb fuel burn, or MAX END as cruise speed mode.

fakten.text: Das FMS fügt nach dem aktiven Leg eine Discontinuity ein und baut die ganze Arrival neu auf. Modified Flight Plan anpassen.
fakten.text_en: The FMS inserts a discontinuity after the active leg and restrings the entire arrival. Adjust the modified flight plan.

fakten.text: Fehlt im Secondary z. B. die ZFW, wird die Alternate Performance nicht berechnet. ZFW im Active Flight Plan löschen und neu eingeben.
fakten.text_en: If e.g. the ZFW is missing on the secondary, the alternate performance is not computed. Delete and re-enter the ZFW on the active flight plan.

fakten.text: Fuel-Wert auf PERF INIT 2/3 als Pilot-Eingabe setzen.
fakten.text_en: Initialize the fuel value on PERF INIT 2/3 with a pilot entry.

fakten.text: Mit ECON und STEP INC: Optimum Step deaktivieren oder CAS/Mach manuell eingeben. Mit ECON Cruise kann die Mach Target auch zwischen zwei Werten wechseln.
fakten.text_en: With ECON and STEP INC: disable optimum step or enter CAS/Mach manually. With ECON cruise the Mach target may also toggle between two values.

fakten.text: Nach Go-Around und Alternate-Aktivierung kann der Approach-RNP-Wert (z. B. 0.3) en route stehen bleiben.
fakten.text_en: After a go-around and alternate activation the approach RNP value (e.g. 0.3) may remain en route.

themen.name: Display & Datalink Misbehaviours
themen.beschreibung: Bekannte Anzeige- und Datalink-Fehlverhalten mit EPIC Load 9.0: FMA, CPDLC Uplinks, MFD, Radar, SVS und Synoptics.
themen.beschreibung_en: Known display and datalink misbehaviours with EPIC Load 9.0: FMA, CPDLC uplinks, MFD, radar, SVS and synoptics.

bibliothek.einleitung: Bekannte Anzeige- und Datalink-Fehlverhalten mit EPIC Load 9.0: FMA, CPDLC Uplinks, MFD, Radar, SVS und Synoptics.
bibliothek.einleitung_en: Known display and datalink misbehaviours with EPIC Load 9.0: FMA, CPDLC uplinks, MFD, radar, SVS and synoptics.

fakten.text: Go-Around ohne TO/GA Button: Bei Windshear ersetzt WSHEAR die angezeigten NO APPR, NO LPV, NO G-APPR, NO RNP, NO L/VNAV Annunciations nicht.
fakten.text_en: Go-around without the TO/GA button: in windshear WSHEAR does not replace the displayed NO APPR, NO LPV, NO G-APPR, NO RNP, NO L/VNAV annunciations.

fakten.text: Mehrere grosse Uplinks: FMS 1(2) TIMEOUT und SYNC IN PROGRESS, erholt sich selbst. Doppelte Waypoints: Route im Modified Flight Plan vor dem Aktivieren prüfen.
fakten.text_en: Several large uplinks: FMS 1(2) TIMEOUT and SYNC IN PROGRESS, recovers by itself. Duplicated waypoints: review the route on the modified flight plan before activating.

fakten.text: Den Uplink auf der MSG RCVD Seite oder im ATS Log bearbeiten.
fakten.text_en: Handle the uplink from the MSG RCVD page or the ATS log.

fakten.text: Die falsche Piste ist nicht auf den aktiven Flight Plan ausgerichtet. Sie verschwindet über 25 NM Map Range oder durch System und zurück auf Map/Plan.
fakten.text_en: The wrong runway is not aligned with the active flight plan. It disappears above 25 NM map range or via System and back to Map/Plan.

fakten.text: Bearing wird als TRUE (Suffix „T“) statt MAGNETIC angezeigt.
fakten.text_en: The bearing is displayed as TRUE (suffix "T") instead of MAGNETIC.

fakten.text: Hazard Icons bewegen sich in Kurven leicht. Bei IRS 1 und 2 FAIL zeigt ein Self-Test TEST und das Bild nur auf dem PFD.
fakten.text_en: Hazard icons move slightly in turns. With IRS 1 and 2 failed, a self-test shows TEST and the pattern only on the PFD.

fakten.text: CARGO/RECIRC FAN Undetermined: RECIRC Button OUT/IN. Engine Anti-Ice amber gestrichelt vor dem Start: FADECs noch stromlos.
fakten.text_en: CARGO/RECIRC FAN undetermined: RECIRC button OUT/IN. Engine anti-ice amber dashed before start: FADECs still de-powered.

fragen.frage: Wie berechnet sich die Contingency Fuel beim Basic Procedure gemäss OFP-Definition?
antworten: 3 % des Trip Fuel, aber nicht weniger als für 5 Minuten Holding auf 1500 ft über der Destination (ISA)
5 % des Trip Fuel, aber nicht weniger als für 10 Minuten Holding auf 1500 ft über der Destination (ISA)
5 % des Trip Fuel, aber nicht weniger als für 5 Minuten Holding auf 1500 ft über der Destination (ISA)
10 % des Trip Fuel, aber nicht weniger als für 15 Minuten Holding auf 1500 ft über der Destination (ISA)
fragen.erklaerung: Beim Basic Procedure gilt der höhere Wert aus 5 % Trip Fuel und 5 Minuten Holding auf 1500 ft über der Destination in ISA.
fragen.zitat: 5% of trip fuel but not less than for 5 minutes holding at 1500 ft above destination airport in ISA conditions
kontext:

OM-A 8 Operating Procedures

FUEL Policy: General:
Tankering is a practice whereby an airplane carries more fuel than required for a flight in order to reduce or avoid refueling at the destination airport.
Tankering is categorized as either operational (e.g. fuel supply shortage) or economic (due to significant fuel price difference).

The following fuel policies exist:
Policy: Description:
ADDNAR possible ADDNAR may be planned if operational limitations are met

MINIMUM FUEL minimum fuel for safe operation (discretionary fuel on flight crew's decision)

OPERATIONAL (e.g. due to fuel supply shortage at TANKERAGE destination) operational tankerage shall be included in the ADD component in coordination with OCC and will be part of the minimum block fuel.
This policy shall only be used if explicitly stated on the OFP

ECONOMICAL

(e.g. due to significant fuel price difference) TANKERAGE economic tankerage shall be included in

the discretionary fuel component.

This policy shall only be used if explicitly

stated on the OFP

Note: Any fuel policy presented in a special charter briefing will supersede the policy on the OFP.

To ALTN2: Calculated routing from Destination to Alternate 2 (if applicable)

fragen.frage_en: How is Contingency Fuel calculated under the Basic Procedure per the OFP definition?
antworten_en: 3 % of Trip Fuel, but not less than 5 minutes holding at 1500 ft above destination (ISA)
5 % of Trip Fuel, but not less than 10 minutes holding at 1500 ft above destination (ISA)
5 % of Trip Fuel, but not less than 5 minutes holding at 1500 ft above destination (ISA)
10 % of Trip Fuel, but not less than 15 minutes holding at 1500 ft above destination (ISA)
fragen.erklaerung_en: Under the Basic Procedure, the higher of 5 % Trip Fuel and 5 minutes holding at 1500 ft above destination in ISA applies.

fragen.frage: Auf welchen Wert darf die Contingency Fuel reduziert werden, wenn ein Fuel En-route Alternate (Fuel-ERA) gewählt wurde?
antworten: 2 % (mindestens 5 Minuten Holding)
3 % (mindestens 5 Minuten Holding)
4 % (mindestens 10 Minuten Holding)
0 %, da der Fuel-ERA die Contingency ersetzt
fragen.erklaerung: Mit einem nominierten Fuel-ERA kann mit 3 % Contingency Fuel geplant werden.
fragen.zitat: A flight may be planned with a contingency fuel of 3%, provided that a Fuel En- route Alternate (Fuel-ERA) has been selected.
kontext: 8.1.5.5.4 Planning based on Fuel En-route Alternate (Fuel-ERA)
A flight may be planned with a contingency fuel of 3%, provided that a Fuel En- route Alternate (Fuel-ERA) has been selected.

For the Fuel-ERA the following applies: the Fuel-ERA shall be located within a circle with a radius equal to 20% of the total flight plan distance

the centre of this circle lies on the planned route at a distance from the destination aerodrome, whichever is greater: equal to 25% of the total flight plan distance or at least 20% of the total flight plan distance plus 50 NM

all distances shall be calculated in still-air conditions

the Fuel-ERA shall be nominated in the operational flight plan
fragen.frage_en: To what value may Contingency Fuel be reduced if a Fuel En-route Alternate (Fuel-ERA) has been selected?
antworten_en: 2 % (minimum 5 minutes holding)
3 % (minimum 5 minutes holding)
4 % (minimum 10 minutes holding)
0 %, because the Fuel-ERA replaces Contingency
fragen.erklaerung_en: With a nominated Fuel-ERA, planning may be done with 3 % Contingency Fuel.

fragen.frage: Wofür muss die Final Reserve Fuel ausreichen?
antworten: 45 Minuten Holding auf 1500 ft über Flugplatzhöhe in ISA, mit dem erwarteten Landing Weight an der Destination
30 Minuten Holding auf 3000 ft über Flugplatzhöhe in ISA, mit dem maximalen Landing Weight
15 Minuten Holding auf 1500 ft über Flugplatzhöhe in ISA, mit dem erwarteten Landing Weight am Destination Alternate
30 Minuten Holding auf 1500 ft über Flugplatzhöhe in ISA, mit dem erwarteten Landing Weight am Destination Alternate
fragen.erklaerung: Final Reserve Fuel entspricht 30 Minuten Holding auf 1500 ft über Flugplatzhöhe in ISA, berechnet mit dem Landing Weight am Destination Alternate (oder an der Destination, wenn kein Alternate nötig ist).
fragen.zitat: fuel to hold for 30 minutes at 1500 ft above airport elevation in ISA conditions, calculated with the estimated landing mass on arrival at the destination alternate aerodrome
kontext:
8.1.7.3.5 Final Reserve Fuel

Final reserve fuel must contain:

fuel to hold for 30 minutes at 1500 ft above airport elevation in ISA conditions, calculated with the estimated landing mass on arrival at the

destination alternate aerodrome,

or the destination aerodrome if no alternate

is required

8.3.7.2 Fuel Monitoring and Fuel Checks

The flight crew must continuously monitor the fuel situation and distribution to identify any trend in comparison with time elapsed.
Fuel checks must be performed: before leaving the parking position

before take-off (the crew must verify that not more than the planned taxi fuel was used otherwise a re-assessment of the fuel situation shall be done)

after reaching initial cruising altitude overhead or abeam a waypoint listed on the OFP
in cruise at hourly intervals, overhead or abeam a waypoint listed on the OFP until leaving cruising altitude

Airborne, each fuel check must be recorded on the Operational Flight Plan (OFP) including the: actual fuel on board

actual fuel used

compare the actual fuel used with the planned fuel used compare the actual fuel on board with fuel required for the remainder of the flight

determine the usable fuel that is expected to remain upon landing at the

destination aerodrome

When having committed to land at a specific airport, the flight crew shall declare “MINIMUM FUEL” if any change to the existing flight plan (e.g. holding, rerouting) may result in a landing with less than planned final reserve.
This is not an emergency call, but Air Traffic Control (ATC) is informed about a possible emergency situation.
fragen.frage_en: When must the crew declare "MINIMUM FUEL"?

As soon as the calculated fuel at landing falls below Final Reserve plus Alternate Fuel
When the calculated usable fuel on arrival is expected to be below Final Reserve
As soon as Contingency Fuel is completely used up
fragen.erklaerung_en: MINIMUM FUEL is declared after commitment to a landing aerodrome when any change (e.g. holding, rerouting) could jeopardise the Final Reserve; it is not an emergency.

kontext:
8.1.5.5.2 Planning without Destination Alternate

A flight may be planned without destination alternate, provided: the duration of the planned flight from take-off to landing does not exceed 6 hours, or in the event of in-flight re-planning, the remaining flight time to destination does not exceed 4 hours

two separate runways are usable at the destination

the appropriate meteorological reports and/or forecasts indicate that for the period from 1 hour before to 1 hour after the expected time of arrival,
the ceiling is at least 2 000 ft (600 m) or the circling height plus 500 ft (150 m), whichever is greater, and ground visibility is at least 5 km

no adverse weather forecast (e.g. thunderstorm, sandstorm, fog-patches irrespective of PROB or TEMPO in the forecast)

the wind is within AFM/OM-B limits for the planned approach, no gusts, no wind shears expected or forecast braking action at least medium

Refer to 8.1.7.3.6 - Additional Fuel for ADDNAR fuel considerations.

Note: Runways on the same airport are considered to be separate runways when they are separate landing surfaces, each having an approach

procedure based upon a separate navigation aid, which may overlay or cross such that, if one of the runways is blocked, it will not prevent the

planned operation on the other runway.

8.1.5.5.4 Planning based on Fuel En-route Alternate (Fuel-ERA)

A flight may be planned with a contingency fuel of 3%, provided that a Fuel En- route Alternate (Fuel-ERA) has been selected.

the centre of this circle lies on the planned route at a distance from the destination aerodrome, whichever is greater: equal to 25% of the total flight plan distance or at least 20% of the total flight plan distance plus 50 NM

all distances shall be calculated in still-air conditions

the Fuel-ERA shall be nominated in the operational flight plan

The minimum VIS for circling shall be the higher of: the circling visibility for the airplane category, if published or the minimum visibility derived from table above

or the VIS of the preceding instrument approach procedure (IAP)
fragen.frage_en: What are the lowest circling minima for Helvetic (Category C)?

fragen.frage: Die gemeldete Controlling RVR liegt unter dem anwendbaren Minimum. Bis zu welchem Punkt darf ein Instrument Approach (DH unter 1000 ft) fortgesetzt werden?
antworten: Bis zum FAF, unabhängig von der Höhe
Bis 500 ft über Flugplatzhöhe
Bis zur DA/H
Bis 1000 ft über Flugplatzhöhe
fragen.erklaerung: Gemäss Approach Ban darf der Approach nicht über den Punkt 1000 ft über Flugplatzhöhe hinaus fortgesetzt werden (bzw. nicht ins FAS, wenn DH/MDH über 1000 ft liegt).
fragen.zitat: past a point at which the airplane is 1 000 ft above the aerodrome elevation
kontext:
8.0.2.2 Approach Ban

VIS RVR and Landing Performance Assessment If the reported visibility (VIS) or controlling RVR for the runway to be used for landing is less than the applicable minimum, or the landing performance assessment according to 8.3.2.25 - Runway Condition Assessment indicates that a safe landing cannot be assured, then an instrument approach operation shall not be continued:
past a point at which the airplane is 1 000 ft above the aerodrome elevation

or into the final approach segment (FAS) if the DH or MDH is higher than 1 000 ft

If the required visual reference is not established, then a missed approach shall be executed at or before the DA/H or the MDA/H.
If the required visual reference is not maintained after DA/H or MDA/H, then a balked landing shall be executed promptly.
In the case where no RVR is reported, and the reported VIS is less than the applicable minimum, but the converted meteorological visibility (CMV) is equal or greater than the applicable minimum, then the instrument approach can be continued to the DA/H or MDA/H. Refer to 8.1.5.4 - Conversion of Visibility to CMV.
fragen.frage_en: The reported controlling RVR is below the applicable minimum. Up to which point may an instrument approach (DH below 1000 ft) be continued?
antworten_en: To the FAF, regardless of altitude
To 500 ft above aerodrome elevation
To the DA/H
To 1000 ft above aerodrome elevation
fragen.erklaerung_en: Under the Approach Ban, the approach must not be continued beyond the point 1000 ft above aerodrome elevation (or into the FAS if DH/MDH is above 1000 ft).

DA MDA increment

Type of Aircraft Value to be added to Minimum Descent Altitude (MDA)

The take-off minima shall be selected to ensure sufficient guidance to control the aircraft in the event of both a rejected take-off in adverse circumstances and a continued take-off after failure of the critical engine.
Where there is a specific need to see and avoid obstacles on departure and/or for a forced landing, additional conditions (e.g. ceiling), shall be specified in the OM-C.
The minima of the required meteorological RVRor VIS for take-off are listed in the following table:

Minimum RVR or VIS (1) Facilities
500 m (day) Nil (2)

Centre line markings or 400 m (day) Runway edge lights or Runway centre line lights

Runway end lights (3) 400 m (night) and Runway edge lights or runway centreline lights

Note 1: The required RVR VIS must be available for a take-off runway part of

at least the length of the Accelerate Stop Distance (ASD).
The reported RVR or VIS value representative of the initial part of the take-off run can be replaced by pilot assessment.
Note 2: The pilot is able to continuously identify the take-off surface and

maintain directional control.

Note 3: Runway end lights may be substituted by colour-coded runway edge

lights or colour-coded runway centre line lights.

When the reported visibility is below that required for take-off and RVR is not

reported

or when neither reported visibility, nor RVR is available

a take-off may only be commenced if the flight crew can determine that the

visibility along the take-off runway is equal to, or better than the required minimum. This may require a runway visit to assess the actual visibility.

For Take-offs under VFR operations refer to 8.3.1.1 - Flights Taking-off from

VFR Airports expecting an IFR Clearance for the En-route Portion of the Flight.
For Take-offs with less than 400m RVR refer to 8.4.4.1 - Low Visibility Take-off with RVR of less than 400 m.
fragen.frage_en: What is the minimum RVR/VIS by day for takeoff when no runway facilities (Nil) are available?

fragen.frage: Auf welcher Höhe liegt das Stabilisation Gate für Circling und Visual Approaches?
antworten: 1000 ft AAE
300 ft AAE

fragen.zitat: Gate 500ft/AAE for: circling approaches visual approaches
kontext:
8.3.2.39.2 Stabilisation Gate

As a general policy the flight crew should aim to be stabilised as early as feasible.
The stabilisation gate is based on barometric altitude, therefore RA shall not be used as reference.

Gate 1000ft/AAE for: straight in instrument approaches (IMC or VMC)

If operationally required (e.g. ATC request) the gate for the approach target speed and engine thrust setting may be lowered to 500ft observing the following restrictions: all other parameters are fulfilled at 1000ft

speed bug set to VAP at 1000ft

speed trend towards VAP

maximum actual speed VAP 20

Gate 500ft/AAE for:

circling approaches

visual approaches

Crew Coordination The flight crew should mentally be minded to execute a missed approach and only land if all parameters allow doing so.
This “inverse mental setting” contributes to safe landings.
The PM who does not actively fly the airplane decides whether stabilization criteria are fulfilled. Therefore, both flight crew members are intentionally involved at this stage of the final approach.
A go around shall be initiated if the stabilization criteria are NOT fulfilled at the stabilization gate.
Should stabilization criteria have been fulfilled at the stabilization gate but defined criteria indicate unstable conditions beyond the stabilization gate till the end of the final approach phase (50 ft/AAE), a go around shall be initiated.
For detailed approach procedures and callouts refer to type specific OM-B.

antworten_en: 1000 ft AAE
300 ft AAE
50 ft AAE
500 ft AAE
fragen.erklaerung_en: For straight-in instrument approaches the gate is at 1000 ft AAE; for circling and visual approaches it is at 500 ft AAE.

fragen.frage: Wie ist ein CAT I-Approach (Type B) in OM-A definiert?
antworten: DH nicht unter 250 ft und VIS mindestens 800 m oder RVR mindestens 550 m
DH nicht unter 200 ft und RVR mindestens 300 m
DH nicht unter 200 ft und VIS mindestens 800 m oder RVR mindestens 550 m
DH nicht unter 100 ft und VIS mindestens 1500 m
fragen.erklaerung: CAT I: DH nicht tiefer als 200 ft und entweder VIS mindestens 800 m oder RVR mindestens 550 m.
fragen.zitat: Category I (CAT I): a DH not lower than 200 ft and with either a visibility not less than 800 m or an RVR not less than 550 m
kontext:
8.0.2.23 Type B Instrument Approach Operation

An operation with a DH below 250 ft. Type B instrument approach operations are categorised as:
Category I (CAT I): a DH not lower than 200 ft and with either a visibility not less than 800 m or an RVR not less than 550 m

Category II (CAT II): a DH lower than 200 ft but not lower than 100 ft, and an RVR not less than 300 m

Category III (CAT III): a DH lower than 100 ft or no DH, and an RVR less than 300 m or no RVR limitation

DH not below 200 ft and VIS at least 800 m or RVR at least 550 m

fragen.frage: Um wie viel kann der Auftrieb gemäss OM-A schon durch geringste Ablagerungen von Eis, Frost oder Schnee reduziert werden?
antworten: Bis zu 10 % (bei bis zu 20 % mehr Widerstand)
Bis zu 30 % (bei bis zu 40 % mehr Widerstand)
Bis zu 50 % (bei bis zu 30 % mehr Widerstand)
Bis zu 40 % (bei bis zu 30 % mehr Widerstand)
fragen.erklaerung: OM-A nennt bis zu 30 % Auftriebsverlust und bis zu 40 % Widerstandszunahme, was besonders beim Takeoff kritisch ist.
fragen.zitat: will result in as much as a 30% reduction of lift (with the corresponding increase in stalling speed) and up to 40 % increase in drag
kontext:
8.2.4.1 General

Winter operations require awareness of specific situations. Snow or ice creates hazardous airport conditions and affects significantly aircraft performance.
For this reason, take-off must not be attempted unless the CMD has ensured that the: wings

tail

control surfaces

engine intakes

other critical surfaces (e.g. fuselage surface in front of engines)

of the airplane are free of ice, frost and snow (Exception see 8.2.4.2.10 - Frost).
This international ruling recognizes the hazardous effects of ice deposits on airfoils and control surfaces through changes in the aerodynamic profiles and, to a lesser degree, through the increase in weight.
Flight crews must be aware that even the slightest buildup of ice, frost or snow

will result in as much as a 30% reduction of lift (with the corresponding increase

in stalling speed) and up to 40 increase in drag.

These effects cause degradation in performance which will be critical during take-off.
Controllability is affected due to the variation in lift degradation along the wings.
Thus the roll characteristics are changed. In addition the forward movement of

the center of lift causes a rapid pitch up during rotation. This is further

aggravated by the need to select a higher than normal attitude to achieve the lift required for take-off and could ultimately result in a stall. A contaminated wing will

stall at a lesser than normal Angle of Attack (AOA), which may even not be

sufficient to activate the stall warning system.

It is, therefore, imperative that:

any deposit adhering to a parked aircraft is completely removed

if conditions exist for the formation of ice before take-off, the aircraft horizontal surfaces and controls are coated with an ice-preventing agent,

which will retain its effectiveness for the period between its application and take-off. (Holdover times)
fragen.frage_en: By how much can lift be reduced according to OM-A by even the slightest deposits of ice, frost or snow?
antworten_en: Up to 10 % (with up to 20 % more drag)
Up to 30 % (with up to 40 % more drag)
Up to 50 % (with up to 30 % more drag)
Up to 40 % (with up to 30 % more drag)
fragen.erklaerung_en: OM-A states up to 30 % loss of lift and up to 40 % increase in drag, which is particularly critical at takeoff.

fragen.frage: Welche Frostablagerung darf gemäss OM-A vor dem Take-off vernachlässigt werden?
antworten: Frost unter 3 mm Dicke auf der Flügelunterseite
Frost unter 1 mm auf der Flügeloberseite
Raureif (hoar frost) an den Vorderkanten
Frost unter 5 mm auf dem Höhenleitwerk
fragen.erklaerung: Frostschichten unter 3 mm auf der Flügelunterseite haben keinen Effekt; dünner Frost am Rumpf ist zulässig, solange Markierungen lesbar sind.
fragen.zitat: frost layers of less 3 mm thickness on the lower surface of a wing have no effect and may be discounted
kontext:
8.2.4.2.10 Frost

Frost consists of ice crystal deposits formed on cold, clear nights by sublimation on surfaces, which have a temperature lower than the surrounding air.
These deposits on leading edges and upper surfaces, even when they are very thin (hoar frost) can seriously affect an aircraft performance.
However,
frost layers of less 3 mm thickness on the lower surface of a wing have no effect and may be discounted.
Also thin frost on the fuselage is acceptable to such a degree that labels, placards and markings can still be read.
fragen.frage_en: Which frost deposit may be disregarded before takeoff according to OM-A?
antworten_en: Frost under 3 mm thickness on the underside of the wing
Frost under 1 mm on the upper surface of the wing
Hoar frost on the leading edges
Frost under 5 mm on the horizontal stabiliser
fragen.erklaerung_en: Frost layers under 3 mm on the underside of the wing have no effect; thin frost on the fuselage is permissible as long as markings remain legible.

fragen.frage: Welchen Freezing Point Buffer muss ein Type II oder Type IV Fluid gemäss LOUT-Definition mindestens aufweisen?
fragen.erklaerung: Der Buffer beträgt mindestens 10 °C für Type I und 7 °C für Type II, III oder IV Fluids.
fragen.zitat: 7°C for Type II, III or IV fluids
kontext:
8.2.4.2.14 Lowest operational use temperature (LOUT)

The lowest temperature at which a fluid has been tested and certified as acceptable in accordance with the appropriate aerodynamic acceptance test whilst still maintaining a freezing point buffer of not less than: 10°C for a Type I fluid or
7°C for Type II, III or IV fluids.
fragen.frage_en: What minimum freezing point buffer must a Type II or Type IV fluid have according to the LOUT definition?
fragen.erklaerung_en: The buffer is at least 10 °C for Type I and 7 °C for Type II, III or IV fluids.

fragen.frage: Ab wann wird die Holdover Time bei einem Two-Step-Verfahren gerechnet?
antworten: Ab Beginn des ersten Schritts (De-icing)
Ab Beginn des zweiten Schritts (Anti-icing)
Ab Ende des zweiten Schritts
Ab Erhalt des Anti-icing Codes durch die Crew
fragen.erklaerung: Die Schutzzeit wird ab Behandlungsbeginn gemessen, beim Two-Step-Verfahren ab Beginn des zweiten Schritts.
fragen.zitat: The protection period is measured from the time of treatment start (start of second step during two-step procedure).
kontext:
8.2.4.15 Information to the Commander

After de-icing the successful completion of either the visual check or the clear ice check (if required) shall be transmitted to the Commander (CMD Under normal circumstances a qualified ground handling agent is responsible for the correct and comprehensive de-icing of the aircraft and for the visual check upon completion, paying particular attention to the upper surfaces of the wings and stabilizer. The visual check may be performed by a flight crew member.
After completion of a deicing only procedure, where no anti-icing holdover time is applicable the Post Deicing Report shall be transmitted to the flight crew with following elements: fluid type statement that anti-icing holdover time do not apply date (optional) the statement “post-deicing check completed”

After completion of anti-icing procedure anti-icing code has to be transmitted by qualified staff to the flight crew to confirm satisfactory de-icing/anit-icing. The Commander (CMD will decide whether the Holdover Time (HOT) is adequate for taxiing and take-off.
The anti-icing code states the treatment (de-icing or anti-icing) applied to the aircraft.
It includes the:

fluid type and name

concentration

local time at start of anti-icing

date (optional)

statement: “post de-icing/anti-icing check completed”

The protection period is measured from the time of treatment start (start

of second step during two-step procedure).

Example 1:
Type 1, 25/75, 0630H, 01.11.01, post de-icing anti-icing check completed

Example 2:
Type 4, Killfrost ABC-S Plus,100/0, 0600H, 01.02.02, post de-icing anti-

icing check completed The mixing ratio is stated by volume with the de-icing fluid quoted first. A 25/75

mixture contains 25% de-icing fluid and 75% of water. When the mixture used

differs from those tabulated, the next lower concentration code shall be used.
fragen.frage_en: When does the holdover time start for a two-step procedure?
antworten_en: From the start of the first step (de-icing)
From the start of the second step (anti-icing)
From the end of the second step
From receipt of the anti-icing code by the crew
fragen.erklaerung_en: The protection time is measured from the start of treatment; for the two-step procedure, from the start of the second step.

8.2.4.13.3 Pre- De-/Anti-icing (“early treatment”)

Aircraft may be de-/anti-iced several hours prior to departure, when weather conditions allow for a long holdover time, usually at frost.
Pre- de-/anti-icing is allowed under following conditions: qualified person must confirm required treatment

the aircraft must be configured for de-/anti-icing fluid application

treatment for anti-icing shall be performed with undiluted (100 Type II or

IV fluid. The application of a diluted Type II or IV fluid with a mixture of 75% 25% is only allowed if all influencing factors have been considered (e.g.

wing skin temperature, high moisture content, high wind velocity)

anti-icing code shall be provided to the flight crew in written form as follows:

deliver the information to respective flight supervisor who will pass it on to the crew with first contact

or use a waterproof plastic bag attached to nose gear or adjacent to door 1L, or to the forward passenger stair

fragen.frage: Bei welcher gemeldeten Braking Action ist ein Take-off gemäss OM-A 8.2.4.23 verboten?
antworten: Poor (Bremskoeffizient 0.25 oder weniger)
Medium (Bremskoeffizient 0.35 oder weniger)
Medium to poor (Bremskoeffizient 0.30 oder weniger)
Good to medium (Bremskoeffizient 0.40 oder weniger)
fragen.erklaerung: Take-off ist unter anderem verboten, wenn die Braking Action als poor gemeldet wird (Koeffizient 0.25 oder weniger).
fragen.zitat: the runway braking action is reported as poor (braking coefficient 0.25 or less)
kontext:
8.2.4.23 Take-off in Icing Conditions

Take-off is prohibited if any of the following conditions exist: snow, ice or frost deposits are adhering to the wings, tail, control surfaces, engine intakes and other critical surfaces of the aircraft.

heavy fall of wet snow with ambient temperatures around the freezing point freezing rain or freezing drizzle (i.e. FZRA, +FZRA, FZDZ, +FZDZ)

(unless otherwise stated in the specific aircraft type OM-B)
the runway braking action is reported as poor (braking coefficient 0.25 or less)

Performance limitations for take-off must be observed. Acceleration will be adversely affected by slush or standing water on the runway, which cause

significantly greater drag.

Flight crews must be alert for conditions which could affect stopping and directional control, should it become necessary to reject the take-off.

Careful line up ensures that the nose wheel is straight, as skidding of an offset nose wheel could upset directional control.

For the take off procedure, refer to type specific OM-B 2.

Asymmetric thrust application must be avoided since it would affect directional

control.
The take-off rotation following any de-icing treatment shall be made smoothly as the full aerodynamic efficiency of the wing might not have been attained yet.
fragen.frage_en: At which reported braking action is takeoff prohibited according to OM-A 8.2.4.23?
antworten_en: Poor (braking coefficient 0.25 or less)
Medium (braking coefficient 0.35 or less)
Medium to poor (braking coefficient 0.30 or less)
Good to medium (braking coefficient 0.40 or less)
fragen.erklaerung_en: Takeoff is prohibited, among other cases, if braking action is reported as poor (coefficient 0.25 or less).

fragen.frage: Was ist bei einem Taxi-Through De-icing mit laufenden Engines zu beachten?
antworten: APU abstellen, um Fluid-Ansaugung zu verhindern
Engines auf erhöhte Leistung setzen, um Icing der Einlässe zu verhindern
Air-conditioning ausschalten, damit kein Fluid in die Kabine gelangt
Flaps vor der Einfahrt in die Anlage auf Take-off-Stellung setzen
fragen.erklaerung: Beim Taxi-Through De-icing ist die geringstmögliche Leistung zu verwenden und das Air-conditioning auszuschalten, damit kein De-icing Fluid in die Kabine gelangt.
fragen.zitat: The air-conditioning must be switched off to prevent de-icing fluid from entering the cabin.
kontext:
8.2.4.17 Taxi-through De-icing

De-icing with engines running may be performed in taxi-through facilities at particular airports. The Operations Manual OM-B prescribes procedures and checklists accordingly. Pre-briefing must be conducted between the flight crew and the ground personnel conducting the de-icing to ensure that the ground personnel is aware of any specific requirement called for by the flight crew. VHF radio or interphone contact must be maintained with the de-icing supervisor throughout the operation. The de-icing supervisor is responsible for confirming that the aircraft is completely free of ice or snow prior to its release.
The lowest possible power setting shall be used.
The air-conditioning must be switched off to prevent de-icing fluid from entering the cabin.

It is recommended to operate the windscreen wipers to prevent fluid from drying on the windscreen.
Before leaving the facility, a flight control and flaps check shall be performed while ground personnel can observe control surface movement.
As soon as the aircraft is clear of the facility, the type specific checks according to the Operations Manual OM-B must be completed. Taxi and before take-off checklists must be completed after the de-icing procedure (i.e. double-checked if previously performed).
fragen.frage_en: What must be observed during taxi-through de-icing with engines running?
antworten_en: Shut down the APU to prevent fluid ingestion
Set engines to increased power to prevent icing of the inlets
Switch off air conditioning so that no fluid enters the cabin
Set flaps to takeoff position before entering the facility
fragen.erklaerung_en: During taxi-through de-icing, use the lowest possible power and switch off air conditioning so that no de-icing fluid enters the cabin.

fragen.frage: Wann erfolgt nach OM-A die generelle Übergabe der operationellen Verantwortung nach dem De-Icing an die Flight Crew?
antworten: Sobald sich das Flugzeug mit eigener Kraft zu bewegen beginnt
Mit Erhalt des Anti-icing Codes
Beim Lösen der Parkbremse vor dem Pushback
Mit Beginn des Takeoff Rolls
fragen.erklaerung: Die Person, die das Flugzeug nach dem De-Icing freigibt, ist für die Durchführung verantwortlich; die generelle Übergabe erfolgt, wenn sich das Flugzeug mit eigener Kraft bewegt.
fragen.zitat: The general transfer of operational responsibilities takes place at the moment the aircraft starts movement under its own power.
kontext:
8.2.4.10 Responsibilities

The aircraft Commander (CMD) is responsible for effective de-icing and anti-icing in accordance with the provisions of the Operations Manual OM-B.
His request for the de-icing treatment and for the fluid mixtures used will always take precedence over locally recommended procedures.
The Commander (CMD) has the authority to obtain de/ anti-icing whenever he determines that it is necessary.
For large aircraft, the Commander (CMD) may not be able to personally check for the correct treatment. In this case, the person releasing the aircraft after the de-icing process is responsible for its performance and verification of the results.
He will communicate the ISO, AEA or SAE de-icing code to the flight crew to confirm the correct de-icing.
The general transfer of operational responsibilities takes place at the moment the aircraft starts movement under its own power.

If, at any time prior to take-off, the Commander (CMD) requires conformation of the ice free status of the aircraft, he must: carry out a visual inspection, or order a visual inspection, or return to the ramp
fragen.frage_en: When, according to OM-A, does the general handover of operational responsibility to the flight crew take place after de-icing?
antworten_en: As soon as the aircraft starts to move under its own power
On receipt of the anti-icing code
On releasing the parking brake before pushback
At the start of the takeoff roll
fragen.erklaerung_en: The person releasing the aircraft after de-icing is responsible for its execution; the general handover takes place when the aircraft moves under its own power.

fragen.frage: Wie definiert OM-A All Weather Operations (AWO) bzw. Low Visibility Operations (LVO)?
antworten: Betrieb mit RVR unter 800 m oder DH unter 200 ft
Betrieb mit RVR unter 400 m oder DH unter 100 ft
Betrieb mit RVR unter 550 m oder DH unter 200 ft
Betrieb mit RVR unter 550 m oder DH unter 250 ft
fragen.erklaerung: AWO/LVO ist der Betrieb mit einer RVR von weniger als 550 m oder einer DH von weniger als 200 ft.
fragen.zitat: the operation of an aircraft with a runway visual range less than 550 m or with a decision height less than 200 ft
kontext:
8.4.1.1 All Weather Operation

All Weather Operations (AWO), also named Low Visibility Operations (LVO), is
the operation of an aircraft with a runway visual range less than 550 m or with a decision height less than 200 ft.

The term All Weather Operations (AWO), includes:

Low Visibility Taxi (LVTAXI)

Low Visibility Take-Off (LVTO) landing Category II (Cat II)

landing Category III (Cat III)

The main objective of Low Visibility Operations (LVO) is to provide a level of safety equivalent to other operations, but in more adverse weather conditions

and lower visibility.

Weather limitations (i.e. visibility) applied to Low Visibility Operations (LVO) are called minima. For each airport procedure, approved minima are indicated in the

Operations Manual OM-C. When these published minima are higher than the minima published in the Operations Manual 8.1.3 - Methods for Determination

of Aerodrome Operating Minima, the Operations Manual OM-C minima take precedence.

The applied minima for take-off and landing must be congruent with:

the minima for which the aircraft is certified

the crew ratings the certification status of the usable runway aids.

The limitations of the aircraft are indicated in the Operations Manual OM-B and in the Aircraft Flight Manual (AFM).

OM-A 8 Operating Procedures
fragen.frage_en: How does OM-A define All Weather Operations (AWO) or Low Visibility Operations (LVO)?
antworten_en: Operations with RVR below 800 m or DH below 200 ft
Operations with RVR below 400 m or DH below 100 ft
Operations with RVR below 550 m or DH below 200 ft
Operations with RVR below 550 m or DH below 250 ft

kontext:
8.4.1.2 Low Visibility Take-Off (LVTO)

A LVTO is a take-off where the Runway Visual Range (RVR) is less than 550m.

if LVPs are required for such operations, LVPs are in effect

fragen.frage: Welche minimale RVR gilt für einen CAT III-Approach mit einer DH zwischen 50 und 99 ft?

kontext:
8.4.1.4 Category III Approaches

A category III (CAT III) approach is a precision approach with lower than CAT II minima. Where the Decision Height (DH) and Runway Visual Range (RVR) do not fall within the same category, the RVR will determine in which category the operation is to be considered.
In contrast to other operations, some category III weather minima do not provide sufficient visual references to allow a manual landing. The minima only permit the pilots to decide if the aircraft will land in the touchdown zone and to ensure safety during roll-out. Therefore an automatic landing system is mandatory to perform category III operations. Its reliability must be sufficient to control the aircraft to touchdown and if applicable during roll-out phase until reaching a safe taxi speed.
The DH shall be determined by the use of a radio altimeter and be not lower than the highest of: the minimum DH specified in the type specific AFM or the DH to which the flight crew is qualified to operate

Operations with no DH should only be conducted if: operation with no DH is specified in the type specific AFM

there is no published information indicating that the approach aid or aerodrome facilities cannot support operations with no DH

the flight crew is qualified to operate with no DH The minimum RVR is a function of the Decision Height (DH):

DH (ft) Roll-out Control Guidance System RVR (m)

50
– 99 not required 175
fail-passive 125 0 – 40 or no DH fail-operational 75
fragen.frage_en: What minimum RVR applies to a CAT III approach with a DH between 50 and 99 ft?
fragen.erklaerung_en: For DH 50-99 ft, 175 m applies; for DH 0-40 ft or no DH, 125 m (fail-passive roll-out) or 75 m (fail-operational).

fragen.frage: Welche RVR ist für die Fortsetzung eines Approaches controlling, und welche gilt, wenn diese nicht gemeldet wird?
antworten: Midpoint-RVR; falls nicht gemeldet, die Touchdown-RVR
Die tiefste der drei gemeldeten RVR
Roll-out-RVR; falls nicht gemeldet, die Midpoint-RVR
Touchdown-RVR; falls nicht gemeldet, die Midpoint-RVR
fragen.erklaerung: Die Touchdown-RVR ist controlling; fehlt sie, wird die Midpoint-RVR controlling.
fragen.zitat: The touchdown RVR shall be the controlling RVR for the purpose of continuation of an approach.
kontext:
8.4.1.9 Runway Visual Range (RVR)

The Runway Visual Range (RVR) is the range over which a pilot of an aircraft on the centerline of a runway can: see the runway surface markings

see the lights delineating the runway

identify its centerline

Category II and III operations require rapidly updated and reliable reports of the RVR that a flight crew may expect to encounter in the touchdown zone and along the runway.
The Runway Visual Range (RVR) measurements are provided by a system of calibrated transmissometers that account for the effects of ambient background light and the intensity of runway lights.
Transmissometer systems are strategically located to provide Runway Visual Range (RVR) measurements associated with three basic portions of a runway: the touchdown zone (TDZ)

the mid-runway portion (MID)

the rollout portion or stop end (RO)
The touchdown RVR shall be the controlling RVR for the purpose of continuation of an approach.
If touchdown RVR is not reported, then the midpoint RVR shall be the controlling RVR.
fragen.frage_en: Which RVR is controlling for continuing an approach, and which applies if it is not reported?
antworten_en: Midpoint RVR; if not reported, the touchdown RVR
The lowest of the three reported RVRs
Roll-out RVR; if not reported, the midpoint RVR
Touchdown RVR; if not reported, the midpoint RVR
fragen.erklaerung_en: The touchdown RVR is controlling; if it is missing, the midpoint RVR becomes controlling.

Mindestens ein Centre Line Light

Die Runway-Schwelle und die PAPI-Lichter

fragen.zitat: unless visual reference containing a segment of at least 3 consecutive lights being
kontext:
8.4.6.1.4 Visual References Category III

For category III operations conducted either with fail-passive flight control systems, or with the use of an approved HUD or an equivalent display

system the flight crew may not continue an approach below the category III decision height
unless visual reference containing a segment of at least 3 consecutive lights being:

the centerline of the approach lights

or

touchdown zone lights

or

runway centerline lights or

runway edge lights or

a combination of these

is attained and can be maintained.

For operations conducted either with fail-operational flight control systems or with a fail-operational hybrid landing system using a DH, at least one centre line light

to be attained and maintained by the flight crew.
For operations with no DH, there is no specification for visual reference with the

runway prior to touchdown.

antworten_en: A segment of at least 3 consecutive lights and a lateral element (e.g. crossbar, threshold or TDZ barrette)
At least one centre line light
A segment of at least 5 consecutive lights, without a lateral element
The runway threshold and the PAPI lights

antworten: Sofort Go-around einleiten
Kein Go-around; Roll-out mit eingeschaltetem Autopilot bis Taxi Speed fortsetzen (sofern Roll-out-Funktion vorhanden)
Autopilot trennen und mit Maximalbremsung anhalten
Reverse Thrust abbrechen und manuell auf der Runway-Mitte bleiben

kontext: 8.4.6.2.2 After Touchdown
If the visual references are lost after touchdown, a go-around shall not be attempted.
The roll-out shall be continued with the autopilot engaged until taxi speed is reached (if roll-out function technically available).
fragen.frage_en: What must be done if visual references are lost after touchdown during an LVO approach?
antworten_en: Initiate a go-around immediately
No go-around; continue the roll-out with autopilot engaged to taxi speed (if roll-out function available)
Disconnect the autopilot and stop with maximum braking
Cancel reverse thrust and stay on the runway centre manually

fragen.frage: Bei einem Rejected Takeoff mit sehr geringer Visibility passieren die ersten rot/weissen Centreline Lights unter der Flugzeugnase. Was bedeutet das?
antworten: Es verbleiben 300 m Runway; die Groundspeed sollte unter 60 kt liegen
Es verbleiben 600 m Runway; die Groundspeed sollte unter 80 kt liegen
Es verbleiben 900 m Runway; die Groundspeed sollte keinesfalls höher als 100 kt sein
Es verbleiben 1200 m Runway; die Groundspeed sollte unter 120 kt liegen
fragen.erklaerung: Rot/weisse Centreline Lights markieren die letzten 900 m; ab nur noch roten Lichtern verbleiben weniger als 300 m.
fragen.zitat: As soon as the first red / white centreline lights pass under the nose of the aircraft, there are 900 m of runway left and ground speed should in no case be higher than 100 kts.
kontext:
8.4.4 Low Visibility Take-off (LVTO)

A Low Visibility Take-off (LVTO) is a take-off with the reported Runway Visual Range (RVR) of less than 550 m.
However, if at the airport of departure no Low Visibility Procedures (LVP) are established, or if established Low Visibility Procedures are not in force, the lowest authorized RVR for take-off is 400 m. For further details refer to 8.1.3.3 - Take-off Minima.

The maximum Runway Visual Range (RVR) at take-off is rather independent of the aircraft type and aircraft equipment, with the exception of very low Runway Visual Range (RVR) values. The take-off minima are mainly determined by the airport installations (e.g. runway lighting system, RVR measurement system).

A static take-off shall be performed if the visibility RVR is at or close to the take-

off minimum.

For the static take-off procedure refer to type specific OM-B.

If it is necessary to abandon the take-off and visibility is very limited, directional

control with reference to the runway lights will become progressively more difficult as speed is reduced, especially with brake application.

As soon as the

first red white centreline lights pass under the nose of the aircraft, there are

900 m of runway left and ground speed should in no case be higher than 100 kts.

Remember that the far end of the runway may have less braking action due to

rubber deposit. If all centreline lights are red, there is less than 300 m runway available and action should be taken accordingly.

Note: The closer centreline and touchdown zone lights cannot be seen as clearly as those further away because of a relatively low light beam

angle.

OM-A 8 Operating Procedures
fragen.frage_en: During a rejected takeoff in very low visibility, the first red/white centreline lights pass under the aircraft nose. What does this mean?
antworten_en: 300 m of runway remain; groundspeed should be below 60 kt
600 m of runway remain; groundspeed should be below 80 kt
900 m of runway remain; groundspeed should on no account be higher than 100 kt
1200 m of runway remain; groundspeed should be below 120 kt
fragen.erklaerung_en: Red/white centreline lights mark the last 900 m; once only red lights remain, less than 300 m is left.

fragen.frage: Welcher vertikale Mindestabstand ist beim Überfliegen von Gewitterwolken zu den Wolkenobergrenzen einzuhalten?
fragen.erklaerung: Beim Überfliegen ist immer mindestens 5000 ft vertikaler Abstand zu den Cloud Tops einzuhalten.
fragen.zitat: vertical separation from cloud tops of at least 5 000 ft must always be maintained
kontext:
8.3.8.2 Thunderstorms

Thunderstorms are classified as:

frontal thunderstorms

air mass thunderstorms

Frontal thunderstorms may exist as:

warm front thunderstorms

cold front thunderstorms

occluded front thunderstorms

Air mass thunderstorms are divided into:

convective thunderstorms

orographic thunderstorms

Frontal thunderstorms form in squall lines and generate heavy rain and possibly hail and produce strong gusty winds and possibly tornadoes.
Large horizontal wind changes in speed and direction at different altitudes are characteristic for a frontal thunderstorm. Resulting airflows in the storm accelerate to much higher vertical speeds, which ultimately results in higher horizontal wind speeds at the surface.
Air mass thunderstorms are caused either by thermal convection or by moist air moving uphill on the windward side of a mountain.
Air mass thunderstorms appear to be randomly distributed in unstable air and develop from local heating of the earth’s surface. As the heated air rises it cools and subsequently forms cumulus clouds. As the cumulus stage continues to develop, precipitation forms in the higher portion of the cloud and falls out.
Precipitation signals the beginning of the mature stage and pressure of a downdraft.
In the later stages of development, the heated updraft creating the thunderstorm is cut off by rainfall, and the thunderstorm begins to dissipate. Many thunderstorms produce an associated cold air gust front as a result of the down flow and out rushing rain-cooled air. These gust fronts are usually very turbulent and are a serious threat during take-off and landing.
The vertical extension of thunderstorms is up to 25 000 ft during winter time and up to the troposphere during summer, the horizontal range is 10 to 20 km.
Besides the dangerous situations already mentioned, there may be additional dangers from sudden heavy precipitation with poor visibility below the clouds, possibly hail showers, heavy icing formation, and severe turbulence.

Lightning is not a direct danger for the crew and passengers of an aircraft in flight, as the electrical load will remain at the surface of the aircraft (Faraday Cage). Lightning strikes may, however, disturb or damage the navigation system.

OM-A 8 Operating Procedures

Flight Weather Radar Echo Characteristics Altitude Gradient of Rate of Shape Intensity (in 1000 ft) Intensity Change avoid by avoid by avoid by avoid by 10 NM 10 NM echoes 5 NM echoes 5 NM echoes echoes with with with showing 0 20 hooks fingers, sharp edges or strong rapid change scalloped edges strong gradients of of shape, or other intensities intensity height or protrusions intensity 20 25 avoid all echoes by 10 miles 25 30 avoid all echoes by 15 miles above 30 avoid all echoes by 20 miles

If storm clouds have to be over flown,
vertical separation from cloud tops of at least 5 000 ft must always be maintained.

It is difficult to estimate this separation, but Air Traffic Control (ATC) or meteorological charts may provide information about the altitude of the cloud.
If the aircraft is not equipped with radar or if the radar is inoperative, any cloud that appears, through visual inspection: tall,

or growing rapidly, or with an anvil top

shall be laterally avoided by at least 10 NM.

The radar equipment shall be intermittently operated on long ranges in order to

avoid the development of situations where no alternative remains but the penetration of hazardous areas.

Flying under a cumulonimbus overhang shall be avoided, too. If it is unavoidable, antenna tilt shall occasionally be selected to full up to determine, if possible, whether precipitation (which may be hail) exists in or is falling from the overhang.
Flight crews are strongly advised to continue monitoring the weather radar in order to select the safest track for penetration under all circumstances.
The local activity of thunderstorms can often be of relatively short nature, (i.e. 20 to 30 minutes). Therefore, if a take-off or landing is planned during times of thunderstorm activity, consideration of the development of the storm shall determine whether avoidance of the worst effects can be accomplished with a delay.
Rule of thumb to estimate buildup of thunderstorms (ts):
Calculate difference in temperature between FL180 (500 hPa) and FL50 (850 hPa).
If difference is: 25° or less: no ts or very unlikely

26° - 27°: ts possible

28° - 31°: ts likely

32° or more: severe ts likely
fragen.frage_en: What minimum vertical clearance above cloud tops must be maintained when overflying thunderstorm clouds?
fragen.erklaerung_en: When overflying, always maintain at least 5000 ft vertical clearance from the cloud tops.

If difference is: 25° or less: no ts or very unlikely

26° - 27°: ts possible

28° - 31°: ts likely

32° or more: severe ts likely

kontext:
8.3.8.5 Wind Shear

In order to avoid dangerous wind shear phenomena it is important to know what wind shear is and in which meteorological and geographical environment it can be expected.
The following definition seems to be the most suitable for aviation:

wind shear is any rapid change in wind direction or speed along the flight path of an aircraft

Wind shear, with or without turbulence, alters the lift force acting on an aircraft, resulting in a significant sinking or rising motion.

Therefore, wind shear may be categorized as:

increasing performance shear caused by increasing headwind or decreasing

tailwind component or vertical updrafts

decreasing performance shear caused by decreasing headwind or

increasing tailwind component or vertical downdrafts

Conditions for potentially hazardous wind shears are: convective conditions (e.g. thunderstorms, rain or snow showers)

frontal systems

jet streams

strong or gusty surface winds

other cases (temperature inversion, mountain waves, sea breeze circulations)

Wind shear events are typically one to two miles in diameter and mostly occur near the ground (typically below 500 ft AGL) during take-off and landing. Both situations would see the aircraft in a low energy condition. Therefore,
there is only limited time for wind shear recognition and counteraction, typically 5 to 15 seconds.

Several factors can impede wind shear recognition: marginal weather conditions

high crew work load conditions

illusion of normality; during the initial part of the wind shear encounter, everything may appear normal; even severe wind shear onset may not

provide dramatic early indications to the flight crew

Standard response of the flight crew should be: control of flight path through pitch attitude; resistance to a downward change

in pitch attitude as normal response to low airspeed

immediate increase of thrust, maximum thrust shall be applied

an approach shall be aborted

unusual stick forces may be required to maintain pitch attitude during

airspeed variations away from normal target airspeed

low airspeed must be accepted, flying at airspeeds below normal reference

speeds may be required in order to utilize the full performance capability of the aircraft (speed increments under expected wind shear threat are stated

in Operations Manual OM-B)

The term downburst describes a severe downward rush of air and its outburst of

damaging winds near the ground. It has been classified into macroburst and microburst. They are different in their size with radial outflow at the earth’s surface lasting from 3 to 20 minutes.

Downbursts can occur wherever convective weather conditions exist.
Approximately 5% of all thunderstorms produce microburst.
Downdrafts associated with microburst are typically only a few hundred to thousand meters across. When the downburst hits the ground, it spreads out horizontally and may form one or more horizontal vortex rings around the downdraft up to 2 000 ft AGL.
In downbursts with vortices very powerful updrafts and roll forces in conjunction with wind speed changes up to 45 knots can be expected.
The time period over which wind speeds exceed half the peak value may last from 1 to 8 minutes. Depending on the movement and the height of the base of parent cloud, microburst may occur as: stationary or moving

surface or midair

wet or dry

Microburst has occurred in relatively dry conditions of light rain or precipitation that evaporates before reaching the earth’s surface.
Frontal wind shear is present in both cold and warm fronts, but exists in a different relative location in each type of front. Because the cold front boundary slopes back behind the frontal surface, the wind shear line also slopes back. The frontal boundary of the warm front slopes upward ahead of the surface front and

so does the wind shear. Significant wind shears can be expected if there is a large difference in surface temperature 6°C) across the front and if the front is moving rapidly at more than 30 knots.
Large wind speeds changes near the ground can be found in many

meteorological situations, including the frontal conditions. Terrain irregularities or

buildings, which interrupt the wind flow, can produce significant wind shears close to the ground.

kontext:
8.3.8.8 Volcanic Ash Clouds

Flying through an ash cloud should be avoided by all means because of extreme hazard for the engines and the aircraft. Volcanic ash may extend for several hundred miles, and eruptions may send ash plumes up to 40 000 ft.
The weather radar can detect neither ash clouds nor volcanic dust.
If the aircraft enters an ash cloud the flight crew can expect: smoke, dust or acrid odors similar to electric sparks in the cockpit

at night heavy static discharges around the windshield

at night, St. Elmo fire or other static discharges accompanied by a bright orange glow in the engine inlets

engine surge or overheat

engine failure

unreliable airspeed indication

pressurization and electrical systems may be affected

When encountering ash cloud the following procedures are recommended: turn on continuous ignition

declare an emergency do not climb in order to over fly the ash cloud

reduce power to idle to provide additional engine stall margin and lower

turbine temperature

try to escape the ash cloud by descending and flying a 180° turn (if terrain clearance permits)

monitor attitude versus airspeed

keep as many engines running as possible

restart any engine, which was shut down due to EGT exceeding the limits; if an engine fails to restart repeated attempts should be made immediately to

avoid solidification of molten ash on the turbine blades,

turn on all accessory air bleeds including all air conditioning packs, nacelles,

and wing anti-ice; this will provide an additional engine stall margin by

reducing engine pressure

For additional procedures refer to the type specific OM-B.

Following an encounter with an ash cloud a landing at the next suitable airport is mandatory. If the visibility through the windshield is impaired a runway with auto land capability should be considered.
Flight crews are requested to make special air reports: when a volcanic eruption is observed, or when volcanic ash cloud is observed or encountered

Information on volcanic activities, including pre-eruption activity, volcanic eruption and volcanic ash clouds are transmitted to aircraft operating on routes that could be affected.
This information is also published by NOTAM and SIGMET up to a 12 hours validity period and, if necessary, recommendations on re-routings will be included.
fragen.frage_en: What action does OM-A recommend when entering a volcanic ash cloud?
antworten_en: Climb to overfly the ash cloud
Increase thrust to cross the cloud as quickly as possible
Reduce thrust to idle to increase stall margin and lower turbine temperature
Switch off all bleeds and packs to increase engine pressure
fragen.erklaerung_en: Recommended, among others: continuous ignition, declare an emergency, do not climb, thrust to idle, exit by descending with a 180° turn, and switch all bleeds on.

kontext:
8.3.9 Wake Turbulence

Wake turbulence is generated by air exchange due to the pressure differential between the lower and upper surface of the wing. This exchange causes counter rotating vortices trailing from the outer wing tips. The larger the aircraft the larger are the vortices. The wake of a large aircraft may require large control inputs on an aircraft flying in the area behind it. These control inputs may exceed the roll control capability of the following aircraft. The flight crew must be aware of the location of the vortex flow generated by a preceding aircraft and adjust his flight path accordingly.
Tests with large and heavy aircraft have shown that the vortex flow field – in a plane cutting through the wake at any point downstream – covers an area about twice the wing span in width and one wing span in depth. The vortices from the two tips remain spaced and will drift with the wind.
The vortices will sink with a rate of descent of 400 – 500 fpm. There is a tendency that the vortices will level off at about 800 – 1 000 ft below the flight path.

Vortex strength diminishes with time and distance behind the aircraft.
Vortex generation will begin on rotation when the nose wheel lifts off the ground and ends, when the nose wheel touches down on landing. In conditions with very weak or calm winds, the remaining vortices from a landing aircraft may persist up to 5 minutes or even longer.
All this has prompted National Aviation Authorities (NAA) and ICAO to establish minimum separation criteria.

OM-A 8 Operating Procedures

ICAO Definitions The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) classifies aircraft into wake turbulence categories based on their maximum certificated take-off mass (MTOM) and the strength of the wake vortices they generate.
Category MTOM Examples Light (L) 7.000 kg Cessna 172 Medium (M) 7.000 kg - 136.000 kg Embraer E-Jets Heavy (H) (1) 136.000 kg Boeing 747 Super (J) exceptionally strong wake turbulence Airbus A380

Note 1: Some types like the Boeing 757, despite having an MTOM below 136.000 kg, are treated as Heavy due to their strong wake turbulence.

Note: In the United Kingdom the aircraft series Boeing 707, DC-8, VC-10 and IL-62 are considered medium (M) and shall be announced as such in the initial contact with ATC. However, this regulation does not affect the composition of flight plans which shall be completed in accordance with the ICAO wake turbulence categorisation.

ICAO Wake Turbulence Separation Leading

Following Radar Non Radar Aircraft Aircraft heavy EN Separation 6 NM Separation 3 minutes super medium 7 NM 3 minutes

light 8 NM 4 minutes

Route Manual Tool – Europe Airway Manual – Air Traffic Control – Air Traffic Control Data Europe – RECAT EU Note: Embraer 190/195-E1 are classified as Lower Medium (CAT-E).
Embraer 190/195-E2 are classified as Upper Medium (CAT-D).

The same may apply for operations into parallel or near parallel runways, where in crosswind situations the danger may exist, that vortices are encountered from a preceding aircraft approaching or departing from the parallel runway.
On the other hand separation may be reduced in strong crosswind conditions when operating into or out of single runway environments.
A departing aircraft will not be permitted to commence take-off until the preceding departing aircraft has crossed the end of the runway-in-use or has started a turn or until all preceding landing aircraft are clear of the runway-in-use.
A landing aircraft will not be permitted to cross the beginning of the runway on its final approach until the preceding departing aircraft has crossed the end of the

runway-in-use, or has started a turn, or until all preceding landing aircraft are clear of the runway-in-use.
More information can be found in OM-C Chapter Rules and Regulation.

encountered despite adequate separation, the following should be remembered:

during approach and landing behind a vortex generating aircraft, landing

should be aimed at a touch down point at the runway past the touch down

point of the heavier aircraft – if runway length permits

when taking-off, the lift-off point of the preceding aircraft should be remembered; if possible arrangement shall be made for a lift-off point well

before the lift-off point of the preceding aircraft; if this cannot be done,

delaying the take-off for some seconds – depending upon the size of the preceding aircraft and wind conditions on ground may be considered

that flying above the flight path of the preceding aircraft means to avoid the vortex zones – at least until short before touch down.

kontext:
8.2.1.5 Fuelling with Passengers on Board

During normal operations it may be necessary to fuel or de-fuel an aircraft with passengers on board. Passengers may embark, disembark or remain on board during fuelling and de-fuelling operation provided that the following precautions are observed: local procedures must be verified and adhered to
a member of the flight crew must remain on the flight deck

a two way communication between the flight crew member in the cockpit and a cabin crew member in the cabin must be established

a two way communication between ground crew supervising the refuelling and the qualified personnel on board the airplane is assured (via intercommunication system, direct person-to-person contact or any other method of communication)

fuelling personnel shall be informed that passengers will be on board during fuelling and immediate communication to a flight crew member being on the flight deck shall be established either via inter-communication system or direct person-to-person contact

all cabin crew members shall be informed by the Commander (CMD).
For callouts refer to 8.3 App. 1 - Communication Wording CSPM 2 Appendix 1 Communication Wording

all cabin crew members shall be able to communicate among cabin crew members and passengers (e.g. via PA, hand signals (body language) or megaphone)

cont.

the fuelling may start only after positive confirmation of the Senior cabin crew member (SEN) towards the Commander CMD has taken place verifying that the following precautionary measures are taken (for callouts refer to 8.3 App. 1 - Communication Wording CSPM 2 Appendix 1 Communication Wording): the fasten seat belt signs must be off, the no smoking signs must be on, together with interior lighting to enable emergency exits to be identified

passengers are to be briefed not to smoke at any time on the ground and to remain seated until the fuelling has been completed, refer to OM- 0 4 CCM

in principle, for all aircraft types, at least a minimum of two passenger cabin doors shall be opened and passenger stairs jetways must be positioned at these doors

if only one passenger stair jetway is available, the requirement for the second passenger cabin door may be met by positioning a cabin crew member, who will remain at a second door throughout the refuelling process. The door should not be automatic armed, unless required in an emergency

in the cabin, a cabin crew member shall be positioned next to the boarding door and be prepared for an immediate emergency evacuation, the rest of the cabin crew members shall be positioned in the vicinity of their assigned doors/exits (refer to CSPM 5 Standard

Operation Position/Area “Fuelling with Passengers on Board”) on all exits the outside-area shall remain clear during fuelling operations

routes to the emergency exits shall be unobstructed

if the presence of fuel vapour is detected inside the aircraft, or any other

hazard arises fuelling or de-fuelling shall be stopped immediately

if deemed necessary by the crew, a de-boarding shall be performed via the stairs or an evacuation via the escape slides, if deemed necessary limited to

the non-spilled side

fuelling and de-fuelling with wide cut fuel (e.g. Jet B or equivalent) is prohibited with passengers on board

after completion of fuelling the Commander (CMD) will notify the Senior

cabin attendant (SEN) which means that normal duties may be resumed.
For callouts refer to 8.3 App. 1 - Communication Wording

CSPM 2 Appendix 1 Communication Wording

Commander (CMD) is responsible for evaluating the situation on the particular airport at the given time, and determining a person responsible for the fueling operation and communication to the flight crew during fueling with passengers on board. That can be one of the following positions: ground staff (ideally flight supervisor)

fueling personnel, should there be means of communication with the flight crew in place

one of the flight crew members

If none of the above positions can assure proper supervision, fueling with passengers on board shall not be performed.
