Fuelling with Jet A-1 with the APU running
Overwing fuelling with Jet A
Fuelling with only one door open when a cabin crew member is at the second door
fragen.erklaerung_en: Fuelling and defuelling with wide-cut fuel is prohibited with passengers on board.

fragen.frage: Was gilt bezüglich der APU während der Betankung?
antworten: Die APU muss während der Betankung abgestellt sein
APU-Start ist während der Betankung erlaubt, wenn keine Passagiere an Bord sind
Betankung mit laufender APU ist ohne Einschränkung erlaubt, ein APU-Start während der Betankung jedoch nicht
Betankung mit laufender APU ist nur mit Feuerwehr in Bereitschaft erlaubt
fragen.erklaerung: APU-Start während der Betankung ist nicht erlaubt; Betankung mit bereits laufender APU ist ohne Einschränkung erlaubt.
fragen.zitat: APU start during fuelling is not allowed fuelling with APU running is allowed without restrictions
kontext:
8.2.1.4 Safety Precautions

Weather If thunderstorms are in the vicinity, fuelling and de-fuelling operations must be suspended.
Operation of Electrical Systems During pressure refuelling, electrical and electronic systems except for weather radar and HF transmitters, may be operated to the extent required for pre-flight preparation. In the event of an emergency (e.g. APU fire, smoke of unknown origin), the operation must be stopped and an immediate disembarkation, eventually even an evacuation must be initiated.
Fuel Spillage If during refuelling a fuel spill is noticed by the crew, handling agent or fuel service provider, the following actions shall be initiated without delay.
Below listed actions shall be applied whenever fuel spill is noticed, no matter if crew or passengers are on board or not. fuelling process shall be stopped immediately

appropriate ground handling personnel shall be informed

airport fire brigade shall be alerted for immediate actions

qualified person on board shall be informed immediately

(e.g. flight crew, maintenance) Operation of Engines and APU

engine start during fuelling is not allowed

refuelling with an engine running is not allowed

APU start during fuelling is not allowed

fuelling with APU running is allowed without restrictions

Precautions for Fuelling with Wide-Cut Fuel Wide-cut fuel (designated JET B, JP-4 or AVTAG) is an aviation turbine fuel that falls between gasoline and kerosene in the distillation range and consequently, compared to kerosene (e.g. JET A, JET A1), it has the properties of higher volatility (vapour pressure), lower flash point and lower freezing point Wherever possible, the use of wide-cut fuel types should be avoided.
If a situation arises such that only wide-cut fuels are available for refuelling/defuelling, flight crews shall be aware that mixtures of wide-cut fuels and kerosene turbine fuels can result in the air/fuel mixture in the tank being in the combustible range at ambient temperatures.
The extra precautions set out below are advisable to avoid arcing in the tank due to electrostatic discharge. The risk of this type of arcing can be minimised by the use of a static dissipation additive in the fuel. When this additive is present in the proportions stated in the fuel specification, the normal fuelling precautions set out below are considered adequate.

wide-cut fuel is considered to be involved when it is being supplied or when it is already present in aircraft fuel tanks

when wide-cut fuel has been used, this shall be recorded in the technical log. The next two uplifts of fuel should be treated as though they too involved the use of wide-cut fuel

when refuelling defuelling with turbine fuels not containing a static dissipator, and where wide- cut fuels are involved, a substantial reduction on fuelling flow rate is advisable. Reduced flow rate, as recommended by fuel suppliers has the following benefits: it allows more time for any static charge build-up in the fuelling

equipment to dissipate before the fuel enters the tank

it reduces any charge which may build up due to splashing

until the fuel inlet point is immersed, it reduces misting in the tank and

consequently the extension of the flammable range of the fuel

the flow rate reduction necessary is dependent upon the fuelling equipment in use and the type of filtration employed on the airplane fuelling distribution

system. It is difficult, therefore, to quote precise flow rates. Reduction in flow

rate is advisable whether pressure fuelling or over-wing fuelling is employed

with over-wing fuelling, splashing should be avoided by making sure that the delivery nozzle extends as far as practicable into the tank. Caution should

be exercised to avoid damaging bag tanks with the nozzle
fragen.frage_en: What applies regarding the APU during refuelling?
antworten_en: The APU must be shut down during refuelling
APU start is permitted during refuelling if no passengers are on board
Refuelling with the APU running is permitted without restriction, but APU start during refuelling is not
Refuelling with the APU running is only permitted with fire service on standby
fragen.erklaerung_en: APU start during refuelling is not permitted; refuelling with the APU already running is permitted without restriction.

antworten: Betankung ist nur noch ohne Passagiere erlaubt
Betankung ist nur mit reduzierter Flussrate erlaubt
Betankung und Enttankung müssen eingestellt werden

fragen.frage: Auf wie viele Cabin Crew Members darf die Besetzung am Boden mit Passagieren an Bord bei den E-Jets reduziert werden, und bis zu welcher Passagierzahl?
antworten: Auf 1, bei maximal 50 Passagieren (ohne Infants)
Auf 2, bei maximal 120 Passagieren (ohne Infants)
Auf 3; eine Reduktion ist nicht zulässig
Auf 2, bei maximal 100 Passagieren (ohne Infants)
fragen.erklaerung: Für alle E-Jet-Varianten kann die Mindestbesatzung von 3 auf 2 Cabin Crew Members reduziert werden, sofern höchstens 100 Passagiere (ohne Infants) an Bord sind.
kontext:

Operations with Passengers

When the airplane is on the ground at a parking place, the number of cabin crew present in the passenger cabin may be reduced below the number determined in 4.1.9 - Minimum Crew Complement.
The minimum number of cabin crew required in these circumstances shall be

one per pair of floor-level emergency exits on each passenger deck, or one for

every 50, or fraction of 50, passengers present on board, whichever is greater.

During ground operations, if reducing the applicable minimum required number of cabin crew, the following conditions apply: the reduced cabin crew includes a senior cabin attendant

special standard operating procedures apply that an equivalent level of safety is achieved with the reduced number of cabin crew (refer to CSPM 5)

fragen.frage_en: To how many cabin crew members may the ground staffing with passengers on board be reduced on the E-Jets, and up to what number of passengers?
antworten_en: To 1, with a maximum of 50 passengers (excluding infants)
To 2, with a maximum of 120 passengers (excluding infants)
To 3; a reduction is not permitted

fragen.frage: Wie unterscheidet OM-A die Verantwortung für den Flugbetrieb insgesamt von jener für einen einzelnen Flug?
antworten: Gesamtverantwortung für den Flugbetrieb beim Nominated Person Flight Operations (FOP), tatsächliche Verantwortung für einen Flug beim Commander (CMD)
Gesamtverantwortung beim Accountable Manager, Verantwortung für einen Flug beim OCC
Gesamtverantwortung beim Crew Manager, Verantwortung für einen Flug beim Pilot Flying
Gesamtverantwortung beim Safety Manager, Verantwortung für einen Flug beim FOP
fragen.erklaerung: OM-A 2.4.1 nennt als Beispiel die Gesamtverantwortung für den Flugbetrieb beim FOP, die tatsächliche Verantwortung für einen Flug aber beim CMD.
fragen.zitat: overall responsibility for the flight operation by the Nominated Person Flight Operations (FOP), but actual responsibility for a flight by the Commander (CMD)
kontext:
2.4.1 Introduction

Operational control is understood as the active directing process of the helvetic operational activities by the Operations Management (OPM). Other than supervision as a more passive, overseeing part of the management, control is continuous and omnipresent. There are strategic and tactical components leading to a system of measures which form the control process. The strategic orientation processes and the tactical, day-by-day conduct of the helvetic operation must be well-balanced in dynamic and stability.
Therefore the: management structure, duties and responsibilities (OM-A 1)

management procedures (OM-A 2)

system of barriers and defences (OM-A 3)

must be clearly defined.
Responsibilities and duties are distributed widely throughout the operation and may vary according to the situation (e.g.
overall responsibility for the flight operation by the Nominated Person Flight Operations (FOP), but actual responsibility for a flight by the Commander (CMD).

Therefore, all definitions must be context-sensitive.

2.4.2 helvetic Operations Management (OPM)

The helvetic Operations Management consists of the:
Accountable Manager (ACM)

Safety Manager (SM)

Compliance Monitoring Manager (CMM)

Security Officer (SEO)

Nominated Person Flight Operations (FOP)

Nominated Person Training (TNG)

Nominated Person Ground Operations (GOP)

Nominated Person Continuing Airworthiness (PCA)

Crew Manager (CMR)

Head of Cabin Crew (HCC)

It is the leading body to initiate, negotiate and decide philosophies, policies and procedures.
fragen.frage_en: How does OM-A distinguish overall responsibility for flight operations from responsibility for an individual flight?
antworten_en: Overall responsibility for flight operations lies with the Nominated Person Flight Operations (FOP), actual responsibility for a flight with the Commander (CMD)
Overall responsibility with the Accountable Manager, responsibility for a flight with OCC
Overall responsibility with the Crew Manager, responsibility for a flight with the Pilot Flying
Overall responsibility with the Safety Manager, responsibility for a flight with the FOP
fragen.erklaerung_en: OM-A 2.4.1 gives as an example overall responsibility for flight operations with the FOP, but actual responsibility for a flight with the CMD.

fragen.frage: Welche Steig- und Sinkflugphasen gelten als kritische Flugphasen (Sterile Flight Deck)?
antworten: Unterhalb FL100, unabhängig von der Flugplatzhöhe
Unterhalb 10000 ft über Departure- bzw. Zielflugplatz, ausser Reiseflug
Unterhalb 5000 ft über Flugplatzhöhe
Unterhalb der Transition Altitude bzw. ab Transition Level
fragen.erklaerung: Kritisch sind Steig- und Sinkflug unter 10000 ft über dem Departure- bzw. Zielflugplatz (ausser Reiseflug); die Phase hängt daher von der Flugplatzhöhe ab.
fragen.zitat: climb and descent below 10.000 feet above the aerodrome of departure after take-off and the aerodrome of destination before landing, except for cruise flight
kontext:
8.3.10.1.1 Critical Phases of Flight

Critical phases of flight are: taxi phase

take-off run

take-off flight path
climb and descent below 10.000 feet above the aerodrome of departure after take-off and the aerodrome of destination before landing, except for cruise flight

final approach

landing including the landing roll

any other phases of flight at the discretion of the Commander (CMD)

Sterile Light (if available):
For use of sterile light refer to CSPM 5 or OM-B 2.
Note: Although the sterile light is normally switched off according to a FL/ALT,

the critical flight phase depends on airport elevation.
fragen.frage_en: Which climb and descent phases are considered critical phases of flight (Sterile Flight Deck)?
antworten_en: Below FL100, regardless of aerodrome elevation
Below 10000 ft above departure or destination aerodrome, except cruise
Below 5000 ft above aerodrome elevation
Below the transition altitude or from transition level
fragen.erklaerung_en: Climb and descent below 10000 ft above the departure or destination aerodrome (except cruise) are critical; the phase therefore depends on aerodrome elevation.

fragen.frage: Wie lange darf eine Controlled-Rest-Periode höchstens dauern, und welche Erholungszeit folgt?
antworten: Max. 30 Minuten, gefolgt von 15 Minuten Erholung
Max. 60 Minuten, gefolgt von 20 Minuten Erholung
Max. 40 Minuten, gefolgt von 30 Minuten Erholung
Max. 45 Minuten, gefolgt von 20 Minuten Erholung
fragen.erklaerung: Eine Ruheperiode soll nicht länger als 45 Minuten dauern, gefolgt von 20 Minuten Recovery; sie muss mindestens 30 Minuten vor TOD enden.
fragen.zitat: the rest period should not be longer than 45 minutes, followed by a recovery period of 20 minutes
kontext:
8.3.10.3 Controlled Rest - Flight Crew Members

During all phases of flight each flight crew member shall remain alert. If a lack of alertness is encountered or fatigue is experienced the controlled rest procedure can be organized by the Commander (CMD) if workload permits. Controlled rest taken in this way has always to be considered as duty time.
To cover unexpected fatigue the controlled rest procedure can be used.
Controlled rest means a period of Time «off task», which may include actual sleep. Its use may be decided by the commander as follows: controlled rest should be taken during low workload phases

only one crew member at a time shall take rest

the harness should be used and the seat positioned to minimize unintentional interference with the controls

the crew member on duty should be briefed before taking over full controls

the aircraft must be flown with both, auto throttle and autopilot fully operational

the flying crew member shall wear the headset

system intervention, which would normally require a cross check should be avoided until the resting crew member resumes his duties
the rest period should not be longer than 45 minutes, followed by a recovery period of 20 minutes

an appropriate alarm system in close contact with the cabin crew shall be

established. Procedure detailed in 8.3.10.3.1 - Controlled Rest

Alarm/Communication Procedure between Flight Crew and Cabin

Crew

controlled rest periods should terminate at least 30 minutes before top of

descent

at least a 20-minute period should be allowed between rest periods

If necessary, a flight crew member may take more than one rest period according

to the restrictions above.
Controlled rest according to the procedure above shall not be considered to be

part of a rest period for purposes of calculating flight time limitations nor used to justify any duty period.

Supernumerary flight crew members may be requested by the Commander (CMD) to occupy an assigned station on the flight deck, whenever he deems such course of action necessary in the interest of safety.

8.3.10.3.1 Controlled Rest Alarm/Communication Procedure between Flight Crew and Cabin Crew

To establish an appropriate alarm system, the following procedure shall be followed: before the start of the controlled rest period, the flight crew informs the SEN briefs the SEN on this procedure

the active flight crew member calls the SEN every 20 minutes and reports
fragen.frage_en: What is the maximum duration of a controlled rest period, and what recovery time follows?
antworten_en: Max. 30 minutes, followed by 15 minutes recovery
Max. 60 minutes, followed by 20 minutes recovery
Max. 40 minutes, followed by 30 minutes recovery
Max. 45 minutes, followed by 20 minutes recovery
fragen.erklaerung_en: A rest period should not exceed 45 minutes, followed by 20 minutes recovery; it must end at least 30 minutes before TOD.

fragen.frage: Unter welchen Bedingungen darf unter FL100 schneller als 250 KIAS geflogen werden?
antworten: Auf Anfrage der Crew, wenn ATC zustimmt
Immer über 3000 ft AGL, wenn kein Luftraum C/D vorliegt
Nur auf ATC-Anfrage und nur über 5000 ft MSL
Auf ATC-Anfrage in jeder Höhe
fragen.erklaerung: Höhere Speeds unter FL100 werden nur auf ATC-Anfrage und nur über 5000 ft MSL akzeptiert; die Crew darf nicht selbst danach fragen.
fragen.zitat: Higher speeds can be accepted on ATC request only above 5000 ft MSL
kontext:
8.3.2.20 Operation below FL100

A speed limitation of 250 KIAS must be observed below FL 100.
Higher speeds can be accepted on ATC request only above 5000 ft MSL

Flight Crews shall not ask for higher speeds below FL 100 by themselves. OM-B limitations must be observed.
If FMS programming or any other task requires "head down" for prolonged time

below FL 100 the task shall be delegated to the PM. If not possible a transfer of controls shall be considered. A state of both pilots "head down" shall be avoided.
When flying below FL 100 the PF shall closely observe aircraft inputs and be able to intervene immediately. This shall be accomplished by putting hands on

thrust levers and on or close to the control column if no other task is being

performed.

However, during takeoff, both hands shall be placed on the control column by the

PF after V1 until 400ft AAE.

During manual flight the PM shall not hinder the PF in making any inputs, but he shall be ready to take over controls at anytime (e.g. placing his hands close to

the controls).
fragen.frage_en: Under what conditions may speeds above 250 KIAS be flown below FL100?
antworten_en: On crew request, if ATC agrees
Always above 3000 ft AGL if not in Class C/D airspace
Only on ATC request and only above 5000 ft MSL
On ATC request at any altitude
fragen.erklaerung_en: Higher speeds below FL100 are accepted only on ATC request and only above 5000 ft MSL; the crew shall not ask for it themselves.

fragen.frage: Ab welcher Runway-Länge muss der LSP für das Landing Pilot Flying sein?
antworten: Bei einer LDA kürzer als 1800 m
Bei einer LDA kürzer als 2500 m
Bei einer LDA kürzer als 1500 m
Bei einer LDA kürzer als 2000 m
fragen.erklaerung: Auf Runways mit einer LDA unter 2000 m ist der LSP PF (Ausnahme: LIFUS nach Entscheid des LTC).
fragen.zitat: The LSP shall be PF for landing on runways with LDA shorter than 2000m.
kontext:
8.3.2.42 Landing

A normal landing shall be performed in such a way to ensure: crossing the threshold at 50ft (except on steep approach operation)

correct attitude

correct speed

correct configuration touch down within the touchdown zone (TDZ)
The LSP shall be PF for landing on runways with LDA shorter than 2000m.

(exemption: during LIFUS the LTC may decide to be PF as RSP.)

For landing the actual mean wind and crosswind gusts shall be within type

specific OM-B limitations. However, if not limited by the type specific OM-B, crosswind gusts shall not exceed the mean wind limit for crosswind plus 5 kts,

taking into account the runway condition.

When receiving the landing clearance, the Pilot Monitoring (PM) shall announce the applicable crosswind with its direction and any tailwind component.

Whenever requested by ATC, or if the braking action during landing roll is

different than reported by the aerodrome operator, the flight crew should provide a braking action report.

A runway braking action encountered worse than reported shall be

communicated to ATC (i.e. GOOD, MEDIUM, or POOR).
fragen.frage_en: From what runway length must the LSP be Pilot Flying for landing?
antworten_en: With an LDA shorter than 1800 m
With an LDA shorter than 2500 m
With an LDA shorter than 1500 m
With an LDA shorter than 2000 m
fragen.erklaerung_en: On runways with an LDA below 2000 m, the LSP is PF (exception: LIFUS at the LTC's discretion).

fragen.frage: Welche Passagierkategorie wird auf helvetic-Flügen grundsätzlich NICHT akzeptiert?
antworten: Personen, die an den Füssen gefesselt oder geknebelt werden müssen (z.B. Gefangene)

kontext:
8.2.0 Policy for Acceptance of Passengers Requiring Special Handling

This policy addresses the acceptance of passengers that require any sort of special handling, either by ground staff at the airport or by crew on board.
On helvetic flights following special category passenger are accepted: unaccompanied Minor (UMNR)

infants (INF)

pregnant women

passenger with Reduced Mobility (PRM)

passenger requiring medical clearance (MEDA)

deportees Unaccompanied/Accompanied (DEPU/DEPA)

inadmissible (INAD)

diplomats (DIP)

escorts and bodyguards

groups

intoxicated (refer to GOM 4.1.8 - Unruly Passengers Policy Special category passengers not accepted are as follows:
all persons who need to be foot-manacled or gagged (i.e. prisoners)

all persons who require special treatments and attentions like seating behind

curtains in specially assigned cabin areas

Use of disability aid or restraint aid (other than CARES child safety device) that requires to be secured around the back of the seat is subject to approval by

helvetic GOP and shall not be accepted if it’s installation poses any risk to the safety of the passenger seated on the seat behind.

Exceptions to the special category passengers indicated procedures and limitations may be granted on prior written approval request from the helvetic

Security Department.

However, the commander has the final authority for the refusal of accepted

fragen.frage: Welche Mindestbesetzung gilt an Bord, solange Passagiere einsteigen, an Bord sind oder aussteigen?

kontext:
8.2.2.1 Embarkation and Disembarkation

Before the embarkation of the passengers, the ground staff must brief them on all relevant safety aspects (e.g. no smoking regulations) effective during boarding the aircraft. When jet ways are in use, ground staff must be positioned at appropriate locations to provide supervision and assistance.
When passengers are required to walk on the ramp, they shall be escorted by ground staff to the aircraft or their approved transport; passenger routes shall be clear of oil, ice, snow and other hazards and shall be selected in a way that prevents from damages and accidents (e.g. no passing below wings or engines).
Whenever passengers are embarking, on board or disembarking at least one flight crew member shall be on board.

Boarding shall not commence until the Commander (CMD) or his representative (i.e. Senior Cabin Attendant – SEN) has given the clearance.
Disembarkation shall not commence until the crew has received confirmation from the ground staff that passenger steps or jet ways are safely in position and that ground equipment will not be a hazard.
For embarkation and disembarkation when fuelling is in progress, refer to 8.2.1.5 - Fuelling with Passengers on Board.
Only in exceptional cases and with the consent of the Commander (CMD), the embarkation or disembarkation of passengers is permissible with one engine of the aircraft operating.
fragen.frage_en: What minimum staffing applies on board while passengers are embarking, on board or disembarking?
antworten_en: Both pilots must be on the flight deck
The Commander must be personally on board
At least one flight crew member must be on board
The Senior Cabin Attendant at the front door is sufficient
fragen.erklaerung_en: According to OM-A 8.2.2.1, at least one flight crew member must be on board during embarkation, stay and disembarkation of passengers.

fragen.frage: Bis zu welcher Slot-Verspätung darf das Boarding durch die Crew nicht gestoppt oder verzögert werden?
antworten: 30 Minuten oder weniger
45 Minuten oder weniger
2 Stunden oder weniger
1 Stunde oder weniger

fragen.zitat: slot delay is 1 hour or less
kontext:
8.2.2.1.1 Boarding of Passengers with Slot Delay EN

To avoid further delay due to organisational issues, (e.g. lack of ground

personnel) in case of a slot delay, the passenger boarding shall not be stopped

or delayed by the crew if the following is true:
slot delay is 1 hour or less

To react on short notice improvement on slot delays, the crew shall prepare the

aircraft to be ready for departure within the original scheduled departure time.
OCC shall be contacted to coordinate and the passengers shall be informed

properly by the CMD.

Note: If the slot delay is more than one hour, the flight crew shall coordinate the further steps with OCC.

OM-A 8 Operating Procedures
fragen.frage_en: Up to what slot delay shall boarding not be stopped or delayed by the crew?
antworten_en: 30 minutes or less
45 minutes or less
2 hours or less
1 hour or less
fragen.erklaerung_en: With a slot delay of 1 hour at most, boarding is not stopped; for more than one hour, the flight crew coordinates further action with OCC.

fragen.frage: Welche Regel gilt für die Anzahl Persons with Reduced Mobility (PRM) auf einem Flug?
antworten: Pro Paar Notausgänge ist höchstens ein PRM zulässig
Höchstens 10 % der Passagiere dürfen PRM sein
Die Anzahl PRM darf die Anzahl Able Bodied Persons nicht übersteigen
Es sind maximal vier PRM pro Flug zulässig

fragen.zitat: The number of PRM`s shall not exceed the number of able bodied persons.
kontext:
8.2.2.3.2 Handling and Boarding

Before accepting sick, disabled and handicapped passengers for transportation, helvetic shall have ascertained the availability, from departure to arrival, of staff trained and qualified to meet their needs and of the appropriate medical equipment.
The number of PRM`s shall not exceed the number of able bodied persons.

They shall be briefed separately by the crew. Consider that in an emergency, the cabin crew can only assist them, once the cabin has been evacuated.
Passengers with disabilities as circumscribed under WCHR, WCHS and WCHC above, shall be allocated seat rows between passenger cabin doors and over- wing but not at the over wing exits. (for airplane specific limitations refer to CSPM 2) They shall be seated next to the window. In this way, when the aircraft is being evacuated, they can – without impeding others – be assisted to reach the end of the line forming at the emergency exits and to leave the aircraft.
Sick and disabled passengers and PRM should be boarded separately (normally prior to all other passengers) as well as disembarked separately (normally after all other passengers have left the cabin).
Note: It is the care company’s duty to escort the PRM to and from their seat (not only to and from the aircraft door) and to assist with cabin baggage storage.

The Commander (CMD) shall be notified by the Senior Cabin Attendant (SEN) if Persons with Reduced Mobility (PRM) are listed on the Passenger Information

List (PIL).
For the carriage of gas cylinders, drugs, medicines, other medical material, wet cell or lithium battery powered wheel chairs refer to the 9.4.4 - Carriage of Wheelchairs and Other Mobility Aids and 10 - Security.

No transportation, under any circumstances, shall be provided to a person who:

has a contagious or infectious disease (e.g. open tuberculosis, infectious

hepatitis; scarlet fever, diphtheria, chickenpox)

has suffered a heart attack or stroke within the last eight weeks

requires medical treatment by pneumatically or electrically operated

apparatus, which, for specific reasons, is not allowed to be operated on board (for limitations refer to the Operations Manual OM-A 10)
fragen.frage_en: What rule applies to the number of Persons with Reduced Mobility (PRM) on a flight?
antworten_en: A maximum of one PRM per pair of emergency exits is permitted
A maximum of 10 % of passengers may be PRM
The number of PRM must not exceed the number of Able Bodied Persons
A maximum of four PRM per flight is permitted
fragen.erklaerung_en: OM-A 8.2.2.3.2 limits the number of PRM to the number of available Able Bodied Persons.

fragen.frage: Welche PRM-Kategorie wird von helvetic aufgrund einer Company Restriction nicht transportiert?
antworten: WCHC
MEDA
DPNA

fragen.zitat: (company restriction: helvetic does not allow transport of STCR)
kontext:
8.2.2.3.1 Definitions

The following definitions of ECAC document 30 constitute commonly agreed indications for the degree of immobility and extent of the assistance required for the journey:
STCR – passengers who can only be transported on a stretcher; these passengers may or may not have social protection or specific insurance.
(company restriction: helvetic does not allow transport of STCR)

WCHR – passengers who can walk up and down stairs and move about in an aircraft cabin, but who require a wheelchair or other means for movements between the aircraft and the terminal, in the terminal and

between arrival and departure points on the city side of the terminal WCHS – passengers who cannot walk up or down stairs, but who can move about in an aircraft cabin and require a wheelchair to move between the

aircraft and the terminal, in the terminal and between arrival and departure

points on the city side of the terminal

WCHC – passengers who are completely immobile, who can move about only with the help of a wheelchair or any other means and who require

assistance at all times from arrival at the airport to seating in the aircraft or, if necessary, in a special seat fitted to his specific needs, the process being

inverted at arrival

BLIND – blind or visually impaired passengers

DEAF – passengers who are deaf, or who are deaf without speech

DEAF BLIND – blind and deaf passengers, who can move about only with the help of an accompanying person

DPNA – Disabled Passenger with intellectual or developmental disability Needing Assistance. This covers persons with disabilities such as learning difficulties, dementia, Alzheimer’s or Down’s syndrome who travel alone and will need ground assistance.

MEDA – passengers whose mobility is impaired, due to clinical cases with medical pathology in progress, being authorized to travel by medical authorities; these passengers usually have social coverage in relation to the illness or accident in question

MAAS (meet and assist) – all other passengers in need of special help (not available on helvetic flights)

antworten_en: WCHC
MEDA
DPNA
STCR (Stretcher)

fragen.frage: Was gilt auf einem DEPA-Flug während des Boardings der Deportees für die Flight Crew?

Der CMD begrüsst die Deportees an der vorderen Tür

kontext:
8.2.2.4.1 DEPA Flights – Special Procedures

General For DEPA charter flights the following special procedures shall be applied:

Any Flight-Phase any crew member not feeling physically and/or mentally able to conduct a DEPA flight shall contact CCO as soon as possible to arrange a replacement

the deportees may be bonded and may wear helmets

the crew is not allowed to communicate with the deportees. The communication shall be done via the police officers

deportees may act highly emotional especially during boarding, trying to prevent the transportation by all means (e.g. crying, aggressive behaviour, threatening)

additional information can be found in the special briefing. Procedures in the special briefing supersede any content of this paragraph

Pre-Flight special police briefing (CMD and SEN) will normally be organised by Fedpol

check-in time may be extended as per special briefing

Aircraft Security Search (ASS) shall be performed and completed before boarding starts
during boarding of deportees, the flight crew members shall be inside the cockpit and the cockpit door shall be closed

no crew member present in the front galley area during boarding

before commencing the flight, all passengers must be briefed about the type specific matters (i.e. location of emergency exits) and verify that there are no open questions concerning the safety procedures

conduct the safety briefing after boarding of all passengers as follows:

the cabin crew shall omit all public announcements as per CCM except for chapter 4 Safety the safety briefing shall be held as per CCM 4.3 in English language only In-Flight crew members shall not wear nametags

cabin crew members shall not wear ties or foulards to minimize the distraction of the police officers on board, no public announcements from the cockpit and in the cabin shall be done, except

in case of emergency

the responsibility for all passenger relevant issues on board (i.e.

medical, pax disturbance) lies with the responsible police officers as long as the flight safety is not directly affected

Post-Flight during de-boarding, the cockpit crew shall be inside the cockpit and the

cockpit door shall be closed

the SEN shall be present in the forward galley and both CABs shall wait

in the rear galley

Aircraft Security Search (ASS) shall be performed after de-boarding
fragen.frage_en: What applies to the flight crew during boarding of deportees on a DEPA flight?
antworten_en: They are on the flight deck with the cockpit door closed
The CMD greets the deportees at the front door
A pilot monitors boarding from the front galley
The flight crew communicates directly with the deportees to calm them
fragen.erklaerung_en: During boarding of deportees, the flight crew must be on the flight deck with the cockpit door closed; communication with deportees is only via the police.

the Commander (CMD) and handling staff shall ensure that no animal is carried in the cabin, which may impede an emergency evacuation the Commander (CMD) will brief the cabin crew about all animals carried in the cabin

fragen.frage: Wie wird die Flight Crew über lebende Tiere im Frachtraum informiert, die als Gepäck eines mitreisenden Passagiers befördert werden?
antworten: Es ist immer ein NOTOC erforderlich
Eine Information ist nicht notwendig
Nur durch einen Eintrag im Aircraft Technical Log
Eine Supplementary Info (SI) auf dem Loadsheet genügt
fragen.erklaerung: AVI als Fracht erfordert einen NOTOC; als begleitetes Gepäck genügt eine SI auf dem Loadsheet. Das Handling muss die Crew in jedem Fall informieren.
fragen.zitat: a supplementary info (SI) on the loadsheet is sufficient as information to the flight crew
kontext:
8.2.2.9.4 Live Animals in Cargo Compartments (AVI)

The carriage of live animals in cargo compartments shall take into account the specific needs of the animals. The carriage requires pressurization, ventilation, heating and lighting of the relevant compartment.
For general restrictions refer to 4.2-14 - Animal in Hold (AVIH) (AVIH).
For type specific restrictions refer to the relevant Operations Manual OM-B.
If AVI are transported as cargo, a NOTOC is required.
If AVI are transported as baggage accompanied by a passenger on the same flight,
a supplementary info (SI) on the loadsheet is sufficient as information to the flight crew.

The handling staff shall inform the flight crew before departure about all live animals, their requirements and their location in any case.
Summary of loading restrictions: stowage and loading of animals shall follow the principles outlined under 8.2.2.6 - Loading and Securing of Items in the Aircraft

containers shall be stowed in a manner that guarantees sufficient air circulation and therefore be placed as close as possible to the cargo ventilation inflow

containers shall be large enough that the animal can stand up, turn and lie down in a natural manner

containers shall be accessible, without needing to be offloaded, when care of the animals is required at transit stations

containers shall be clean, leak-, escape- and claw proof (soft sided “pet bags” are NOT suitable)

live animal shall be clean, healthy, harmless, odourless and not pregnant

a maximum of two adult animals of comparable size up to 14kg each that are used to cohabitation may be shipped in the same container

in the event of excessive delays, special care – according to shipper’s

instructions – shall be taken of the animal(s)

live animals which are natural enemies shall not be loaded in close proximity to each other

live animals shall not be loaded in close proximity to any other load, which

might have a negative effect on their well-being or health

live animals must be separated from HUM – Human remains shipments by at least 1 m.
fragen.frage_en: How is the flight crew informed about live animals in the cargo compartment carried as baggage of a travelling passenger?
antworten_en: A NOTOC is always required
No information is necessary
Only by an entry in the Aircraft Technical Log
A Supplementary Info (SI) on the loadsheet is sufficient
fragen.erklaerung_en: AVI as cargo requires a NOTOC; as accompanied baggage, an SI on the loadsheet is sufficient. Handling must inform the crew in every case.

Law requires a loop belt for Infant. Each adult travelling with an infant must use the infant belt during the phases of flight and conditions specified in 8.3.11.3 - Passengers.
The infant must not be fastened together with the adult person using the regular seat belt.
fragen.frage_en: How must an infant be secured when travelling with an adult on the same seat?
antworten_en: Together with the adult in the regular seat belt
In the adult's arms without an additional belt
With an infant loop belt; the infant must not be belted together with the adult in the regular seat belt
In a baby cradle, also during takeoff and landing
fragen.erklaerung_en: The regulation requires a loop belt for infants; the infant must not be belted in the adult's regular seat belt. Baby cradles are not permitted for takeoff and landing.

fragen.frage: Wann muss die Flight Crew im Flug das Headset tragen (ausser bei Abwesenheit eines Piloten)?
antworten: Unter Transition Altitude/Level bzw. im Steig-/Sinkflug unter 10'000 ft über dem Flugplatz, je nachdem was höher ist
Nur unter FL100
Nur während Takeoff und Landing bis 1000 ft AAL
Während des gesamten Fluges ab Engine Start
fragen.erklaerung: OM-A 8.3.10.4 verlangt das Headset unter TA/TL bzw. im Steig- und Sinkflug unter 10'000 ft über Departure-/Zielflugplatz, je nachdem was höher ist, sowie auf Anordnung des CMD.
fragen.zitat: when flying below transition altitude / level
kontext:
8.3.10.4 Use of Headset

Each flight crew member required to be on flight deck shall wear the headset and use the boom microphone as the primary device for communication.
On Ground: when receiving the ATC departure clearance via voice communication

when engines are running

Note: The reception of the departure clearance (e.g SID) is of special importance. Therefore, it has to be assured, that both flight crew members listen to the given clearance.

In Flight:
when flying below transition altitude level

or climb and descent below 10.000 feet above the aerodrome of departure after take-off and the aerodrome of destination before landing, except for cruise flight, whichever is higher

whenever deemed necessary by the Commander (CMD)

inflight according to 8.3.10.2 - Flight Crew Members Leaving their Station
fragen.frage_en: When must the flight crew wear the headset in flight (except when a pilot is absent)?
antworten_en: Below transition altitude/level or in climb/descent below 10'000 ft above the aerodrome, whichever is higher
Only below FL100
Only during takeoff and landing up to 1000 ft AAL
During the whole flight from engine start
fragen.erklaerung_en: OM-A 8.3.10.4 requires the headset below TA/TL or in climb and descent below 10'000 ft above departure/destination aerodrome, whichever is higher, and as ordered by the CMD.

fragen.frage: Wann muss jedes Flight Crew Member mit allen verfügbaren Gurten und Harnesses gesichert sein?
antworten: Nur unter 1000 ft AGL
Nur bei eingeschaltetem Fasten Seat Belt Sign
Unter der Transition Altitude bzw. dem Transition Level
Während Takeoff und Landing (d.h. unter FL100) und wann immer vom CMD angeordnet
fragen.erklaerung: Während Takeoff und Landing (unter FL100) und auf Anordnung des CMD sind alle Gurte und Harnesses zu tragen; in den übrigen Phasen genügt der Sitzgurt.
fragen.zitat: During take-off and landing (i.e. below FL 100), and whenever deemed necessary by the Commander (CMD) in the interest of safety, each flight crew member shall be properly secured
kontext: 8.3.11.1 Crew Members and Occupants at the Flight Deck
During take-off and landing (i.e. below FL 100), and whenever deemed necessary by the Commander (CMD) in the interest of safety, each flight crew member shall be properly secured

by all safety belts and harnesses provided.
During all other phases of the flight, each flight crew member on the flight deck shall keep his safety belt fastened while at his station.
These provisions also apply to any other occupant of the flight deck not being a flight crew member.
fragen.frage_en: When must each flight crew member be secured with all available belts and harnesses?
antworten_en: Only below 1000 ft AGL
Only with the Fasten Seat Belt sign on
Below the transition altitude or transition level
During takeoff and landing (i.e. below FL100) and whenever ordered by the CMD
fragen.erklaerung_en: During takeoff and landing (below FL100) and when ordered by the CMD, all belts and harnesses must be worn; in other phases the seat belt is sufficient.

kontext:
8.3.12 Admission to Flight Deck

No person, other than flight crew members assigned to a flight, shall be admitted to, or carried on, the flight deck unless the Commander (CMD) himself or his designated deputy is present on the flight deck, and unless this person: is a member of the operating crew or is an auditor listed on the flight assignment (e.g IOSA, CARA) or is a representative of the Swiss FOCA with an appropriate identification and is required for the performance of his official duties

Alternatively other persons may be accepted if the following conditions are fulfilled: admission to flight deck (Cockpit permit) is granted by the Commander (CMD)

a valid passenger or observer ticket has been issued for the flight or a series of flights for flight deck observers not employed by helvetic, the process for the issuance of tickets is described in OM-0 9

A cockpit permit may be granted provided:

the passenger is personally known to a crew member or is staff of an airline within the Lufthansa group (identification through crew member-certificate or company ID)

or

the passenger holds an airport ID from Zurich Airport (AIC) containing at

least one of the ZRH airport zones (i.e. bold capital letters), irrespective of

the colour of the airport identification cards or

the passenger has successfully completed the process described in OM-0 9 Observer Flights for non-2L Observers

Note:
Any passenger occupying the Cockpit Jump-Seat shall be at least 12 Years of age

The Commander (CMD) is responsible that a person who has been granted a permission to enter the flight deck: has received a briefing on all safety relevant aspects including the sterile flight deck policy and escape path to be used in case of emergency prior to departure and as necessary for the reminder of the flight

does not cause distraction or interference with the operation of the flight

refrains from use of any audio or video recording devices (e.g. tape recorder, cameras of any kind, mobile phone). Exceptions in written form may be granted by the Accountable Manager (ACM) or Nominated Person Flight Operations (FOP)

Note: Special regulations may apply for certain countries (e.g. UK, Israel).
Refer to OM-C Route Competence for further information.

No cockpit permit is required for: persons according to the List of helvetic Employees in the OM-0 9

In all cases, the final acceptance of the person admitted to flight deck remains with the Commander (CMD).

As stated in OCM 3.18, Operations Control (OCC) is in charge to coordinate the

exchange of information between all relevant parties.
The granted admission to the flight deck shall be noted in the Flight Briefing Documentation Tool or on the relevant flight assignment.

Refer to 8.1.13 - Flight Assignment Folder.

antworten_en: 14 years
12 years
16 years
18 years

fragen.frage: Was gilt mit Passagieren an Bord für die Flight Deck Door im Flug?
antworten: Sie darf geschlossen, aber unverriegelt sein, solange die Sterile Flight Deck Phase nicht gilt
Sie muss nur während Takeoff und Landing verriegelt sein
Sie ist geschlossen und verriegelt; geschlossen aber unverriegelt ist im Flug nicht zulässig
Sie bleibt im Reiseflug offen, solange der Vorhang geschlossen ist
fragen.erklaerung: Die Tür ist vom Schliessen der Aussentüren nach dem Boarding bis zum Öffnen für das Deboarding geschlossen und verriegelt; closed but not locked ist im Flug nicht erlaubt.
fragen.zitat: A situation in which the doors are closed but not locked during flight is not permitted.
kontext:
8.3.12.1 Closing and Locking of Flight Deck Door

Three different terms are used in connection with the flight deck door:

1. open

2. closed (but not locked)

3. locked (closed and secured with a lock)

with passengers on board the flight deck door shall be closed and locked from the time all external doors are closed following embarkation until any such door is opened for disembarkation, except when necessary to permit access and egress by authorized persons.
A situation in which the doors are closed but not locked during flight is not permitted.

for communication and identification between the flight deck and cabin the interphone shall be used

if a curtain is installed, it shall be closed before the flight deck door is opened to prevent view to the flight deck area. If no curtain is installed, a trolley shall be used to block the way to the forward galley

before opening the flight deck door check that the area behind the flight deck door, the forward entrance area, and the galley area are clear of any passengers or other unauthorised persons by using the cabin surveillance

system or alternative means Possible special requirements by foreign authorities will be communicated via

OM-C 3 Route Competence.

OM-A 8 Operating Procedures
fragen.frage_en: What applies to the flight deck door in flight with passengers on board?
antworten_en: It may be closed but unlocked as long as the Sterile Flight Deck phase does not apply
It must only be locked during takeoff and landing
It is closed and locked; closed but unlocked is not permitted in flight
It remains open in cruise as long as the curtain is closed
fragen.erklaerung_en: The door is closed and locked from closing the outer doors after boarding until opening for deboarding; closed but not locked is not permitted in flight.

fragen.frage: Was wird nach dem Passagierboarding vor dem Schliessen der Türen gemacht?
antworten: Der Ramp Agent meldet dem PM die Passagierzahl, die SEN schliesst die Türen selbständig
Die SEN meldet dem CMD den Headcount, der CMD vergleicht mit dem Loadsheet und ordnet das Schliessen der Türen an
Der CMD zählt die Passagiere selbst und schliesst die Türen
OCC übermittelt die Passagierzahl via ACARS, danach werden die Türen geschlossen
fragen.erklaerung: Die SEN meldet den Headcount an den CMD, der ihn mit dem Loadsheet verifiziert und dann das Schliessen der Türen anordnet.
fragen.zitat: He will then verify the total according to the load sheet and orders the doors to be closed.
kontext:
8.3.15.4 Prior to Taxiing

Whilst embarking of passengers the cabin crew must be present in the cabin.
The minimum crew during embarkation is defined in 8.2.2.1.2 - Minimum Number of Cabin Crew required during Ground Operations with Passengers CSPM 2.1.2.1.1 - Minimum Number of Cabin Crew required during Ground Operations with Passengers. all cabin crew members must be stationed according to the defined boarding position (refer to CSPM 5), until the boarding is completed

Cabin Attendants (CAB) must distribute the infant belts and if necessary the infant life vest and explain how to use them. Passengers must be informed to return the respective equipment to the cabin crew while leaving the aircraft.
After passenger boarding the Senior Cabin Attendant (SEN) shall report the total passenger (headcount) on board to the Commander (CMD).
He will then verify the total according to the load sheet and orders the doors to be closed.

For callouts refer to 8.3 Appendix 1, After Boarding CSPM 2 Appendix 1 Communication Wording After closing of all doors and after the appropriate announcement of the flight crew for arming the doors, each Cabin Attendant (CAB) shall ensure that each assisting means for emergency evacuation, that deploys automatically, is armed at the doors and emergency exits for which he has been designated responsible (i.e. arming lever armed).
For callouts refer to 8.3 Appendix 1, Cabin Crew Arm the Slide CSPM 2

Appendix 1 Communication Wording.
Cabin crew member must check if the seating of handicapped passengers, children, infants and persons in custody complies with the provisions of 8.2.2.2 -

Allocation of Seats. If not, they must arrange for their reseating.

The cabin crew shall ensure that: all passengers are seated

no food, beverage or tableware is located at any passenger seat

food and beverage trays (folding tables), as well as passengers backrests are in the upright position

procedures regarding 8.3.28 - Portable Electronic Devices (PED) are strictly adhered to

In addition, the cabin crew shall be ascertained that all passenger and crew baggage, catering equipment and other cabin load is properly secured and stowed where it cannot impede evacuation or cause injury by falling, or other movement. Overhead bins shall be closed.
The cabin crew must strictly enforce the no smoking instruction.
All exits and escape paths shall be unobstructed. If it is necessary to pass through a doorway or curtain to reach any required emergency exit from any passenger seat, the door or curtain shall be secured in the open position.
All relevant emergency equipment shall remain easily accessible for immediate use.
When the cabin is ready for taxi, the SEN shall report this to the flight deck only if required according to the aircraft specific procedures.

For callouts refer to 8.3 Appendix 1, Cabin Crew Arm the Slide CSPM 2 Appendix 1 Communication Wording
fragen.frage_en: What is done after passenger boarding before the doors are closed?
antworten_en: The ramp agent reports the passenger count to the PM; the SEN closes the doors independently
The SEN reports the headcount to the CMD, the CMD compares it with the loadsheet and orders the doors to be closed
The CMD counts the passengers personally and closes the doors
OCC transmits the passenger count via ACARS, then the doors are closed
fragen.erklaerung_en: The SEN reports the headcount to the CMD, who verifies it against the loadsheet and then orders the doors to be closed.

fragen.frage: Wie ist die Kabinenbeleuchtung für den Takeoff bei Nacht einzustellen?
antworten: Gedimmt, wie am Tag
Volle Helligkeit, um eine Evakuierung zu erleichtern
Nur die Notbeleuchtung eingeschaltet
Ausgeschaltet, um die Nachtsicht von Crew und Passagieren zu verbessern
fragen.erklaerung: Am Tag wird die Kabinenbeleuchtung gedimmt, in der Nacht ausgeschaltet, um die Nachtsicht zu verbessern.
fragen.zitat: during night the lights shall be switched off in order to improve the night
kontext:
8.3.15.9 Prior to Landing

Approximately 15 minutes before landing, the descent phase will be initiated by the flight crew, informing the cabin crew to conclude passenger services and to prepare the cabin for landing. Latest by then, the seat belt signs shall be switched on. Movement within the cabin and visits to the lavatories are no longer permitted (refer to OM-0 4 CCM).

For callouts refer to OM-A 8.3 App. 1.2-7 - Prior to Landing.
All Cabin Attendants (CAB) shall, in due time, occupy their designated position stations and fasten seat belts and harnesses.

The Senior Cabin Attendant (SEN), having received the appropriate cabin report from each Cabin Attendant (CAB), shall now expeditiously report to the flight crew, confirming: passengers are seated with seat belts fastened, backrests are upright and tables or trays are in the stowed position and armrests are in down position

all infants are correctly restraint

all window-shutters are open

equipment and baggage is properly secured, galleys and lavatories are checked, locked, secured, stowage spaces and bins are closed,

all exits and escape paths are unobstructed, curtains and doors are secured in the open position,

passenger briefing is completed (refer to OM-0 4 CCM)

ensure that passengers refrain from the use of Portable Electronic Devices (PED) which are not endorsed during landing refer to 8.3.28.6 - Summary CSPM 2.1.5 Portable Electronic Devices (PED)

check all electronic devices disconnected from in-seat USB power supply

cabin attendants occupy their assigned position stations and have their safety belts and, if installed, their harnesses fastened

cabin lights shall be adapted to the light conditions outside of the aircraft: during day the lights should be dimmed;

during night the lights shall

be switched off in order to improve the night

vision of cabin crew and

passengers, (refer to CSPM 5)

electronic galley equipment (oven, coffee maker) are switched off

lavatory check performed according to the lavatory check procedure (door must be locked)

The cabin secure report shall be acknowledged by the assigned flight crew member (read back).

For callouts refer to 8.3 Appendix 1, Prior to Landing CSPM 2 Appendix 1 Communication Wording
fragen.frage_en: How must the cabin lighting be set for takeoff at night?
antworten_en: Dimmed, as by day
Full brightness to facilitate an evacuation
Only emergency lighting on
Off, to improve the night vision of crew and passengers
fragen.erklaerung_en: By day, cabin lighting is dimmed; at night it is switched off to improve night vision.

fragen.frage: Ungefähr ab wann gibt die Flight Crew die Cabin Crew nach dem Takeoff normalerweise frei (wenn keine Turbulenz zu erwarten ist)?
antworten: Bei 1000 ft AAL
Beim Erreichen der Reiseflughöhe
Ungefähr bei FL100
Beim Passieren der Transition Altitude
fragen.erklaerung: Die Flight Crew gibt die Cabin Crew ungefähr bei FL100 frei, oder nach eigenem Ermessen bezüglich Turbulenz und Wetter.

kontext:
8.3.15.7 Release of Cabin Crew after Take-off

After take-off, all Cabin Attendants (CAB) shall remain seated with seat belt and harnesses fastened until the seat belt sign has been switched off

or

having been released via PA by the Pilot Monitoring (PM); if the flight crew deems it necessary to leave the seat belt sign on, but would like to release the cabin attendants

For callouts refer to 8.3 Appendix 1, After Take-off CSPM 2 Appendix 1 Communication Wording From this point the Cabin Attendants (CAB) are released for their duties.
Normal cabin to flight deck communication is permitted again. However, at commander’s discretion the sterile light, if available, may be switched on. In this case, the communication to the flight deck shall be limited to procedural calls.
For sterile light refer to OM-B 2 or CSPM 5
The flight crew releases the cabin crew at approximate FL 100
or within the discretion of the flight crew concerning suspected turbulence or weather conditions.
fragen.frage_en: Approximately when does the flight crew normally release the cabin crew after takeoff (if no turbulence is expected)?
antworten_en: At 1000 ft AAL
On reaching cruise altitude
Approximately at FL100
On passing the transition altitude
fragen.erklaerung_en: The flight crew releases the cabin crew at approximately FL100, or at their own discretion regarding turbulence and weather.

fragen.frage: In welchem Intervall sind im Flug Lavatory Checks durchzuführen?
antworten: Mindestens alle 15 Minuten
Mindestens alle 30 Minuten
Mindestens alle 60 Minuten
Nur vor Takeoff und Landing
fragen.erklaerung: Lavatory Checks gemäss Verfahren sind mindestens alle 15 Minuten durchzuführen.
fragen.zitat: Lavatory checks according to the established procedure shall be performed at least every 15 minutes.
kontext:
8.3.15.8.2 Surveillance of Cabin, Galleys, and Lavatories

Maintaining vigilance to detect any unusual situations early is crucial. Any such occurrences shall be reported to the flight crew immediately.
Both during flight and on the ground cabin crew shall be aware of: unusual passenger behavior

engine irregularities

smoke

burning smells

potential hazards from unsecured trolleys and galley equipment
Lavatory checks according to the established procedure shall be performed at least every 15 minutes.
Galleys shall be attended to at all times, except when engaged in duty-related tasks.
fragen.frage_en: At what interval must lavatory checks be performed in flight?
antworten_en: At least every 15 minutes
At least every 30 minutes
At least every 60 minutes
Only before takeoff and landing
fragen.erklaerung_en: Lavatory checks according to procedure must be performed at least every 15 minutes.

fragen.frage: Was gilt für grössere PED (Laptops, Notebooks) während Taxi, Takeoff und Landing?
antworten: Sie dürfen im Flight Mode benutzt werden
Sie dürfen in der Hand gehalten werden, wenn sie ausgeschaltet sind
Sie dürfen an den USB-Ports geladen werden
Sie müssen sicher verstaut sein
fragen.erklaerung: Grössere PED dürfen beim Boarding und im Flug im Flight Mode benutzt werden, müssen aber während Taxi, Takeoff und Landing verstaut sein.
fragen.zitat: During taxi, take-off and landing they must be stowed away safely.
kontext:
8.3.28.4 Policy for the Use of Portable Electronic Devices (PED)

Hand-held PED or T-PED may be used from gate to gate. From “doors closed” until farewell speech after landing they must be either set to “flight mode” or switched off. The devices must be safely secured in the passenger's hand or a pocket during taxi, take-off and landing. Accessories, such as headphones, must not obstruct access to the aisle.
Larger PED or T-PED (laptops, notebooks) may be used during boarding and inflight (seatbelts off to seatbelts on during take-off and landing phase) provided set to “flight mode”.
During taxi, take-off and landing they must be stowed away safely.

Any T-PED tool without “flight mode”, auto or manual deactivation function shall be switched off for the duration of the flight.
Medical equipment, (e.g. heart pacemaker, hearing aid) may be used without restrictions.
Personal headphones can be used for all phases of the flight and may be attached to the personal device or to the aircraft’s in-flight entertainment system.
The use of electronic equipment required for flight operation is allowed in “flight mode” during any phase of flight but shall considered to be switched off in case of suspected interference or misuse. Cabin crew shall inform flight crew about any irregularities and measures taken by them.
fragen.frage_en: What applies to larger PEDs (laptops, notebooks) during taxi, takeoff and landing?
antworten_en: They may be used in flight mode
They may be held in the hand if switched off
They may be charged at the USB ports
They must be securely stowed
fragen.erklaerung_en: Larger PEDs may be used in flight mode during boarding and in flight, but must be stowed during taxi, takeoff and landing.

fragen.frage: Ein Exit ist laut MEL inoperativ. Unter welcher Bedingung darf das Flugzeug betrieben werden?
antworten: Immer, sofern die MEL das Item erlaubt, ohne weitere Einschränkung
Nur wenn in der MEL die entsprechende Passagierzahl festgelegt ist und der Exit vor dem Boarding verschlossen gesichert wird
Nur auf Ferry Flights ohne Passagiere
Wenn ein Cabin Attendant während des Fluges am Exit sitzt
fragen.erklaerung: Selbst wenn die MEL es erlaubt, darf nur mit der dort festgelegten Passagierzahl operiert werden; der Exit ist vor dem Boarding verschlossen zu sichern.
fragen.zitat: An airplane shall not be operated with an inoperative exit, even if permitted by the MEL, unless the appropriate number of passenger has been specified in that document.
kontext:
8.3.27 Operation of airplanes with an Inoperative Exit

An exit is considered to be inoperative when: the exit does not function correctly, or the evacuation slide, if required, is not serviceable, or the exit sign is not serviceable, or the floor proximity exit identifier is not serviceable, or the exit interior emergency lighting is not serviceable, or the exit exterior emergency lighting is not serviceable during night-time operations
An airplane shall not be operated with an inoperative exit, even if permitted by the MEL, unless the appropriate number of passenger has been specified in that document.

The inoperative exit must be secured closed prior to passengers boarding and must not be used for any purpose whilst passengers are on board.
During the passenger briefing the current state and conditions of the airplane’s escape facilities shall be represented.
In the event of an exit that has been used for boarding becoming unserviceable,

all passengers must be fully briefed before take-off on the inoperative exit and the revised emergency procedures that are to be used.
fragen.frage_en: An exit is inoperative according to the MEL. Under what condition may the aircraft be operated?
antworten_en: Always, provided the MEL allows the item, without further restriction
Only if the MEL specifies the corresponding passenger number and the exit is secured closed before boarding
Only on ferry flights without passengers
If a cabin attendant sits at the exit during the flight
fragen.erklaerung_en: Even if the MEL permits it, operation is only allowed with the passenger number specified there; the exit must be secured closed before boarding.

fragen.frage: Auf welchen Wert ist die Cross-Track Deviation bei RNAV/RNP-Operationen im Normalfall zu begrenzen?
antworten: ±1/2 der Navigationsgenauigkeit der Route (z.B. RNP 5 = 2.5 NM)
±1 x die Navigationsgenauigkeit (z.B. RNP 5 = 5 NM)
±2 x die Navigationsgenauigkeit (z.B. RNP 5 = 10 NM)
±1/4 der Navigationsgenauigkeit (z.B. RNP 5 = 1.25 NM)
fragen.erklaerung: Im Normalbetrieb ±1/2 der Navigationsgenauigkeit; nur kurzzeitig in und nach Kurven bis 1 x die Genauigkeit.
fragen.zitat: shall be limited to ±1/2 the navigation accuracy associated with the route (i.e. for RNP 5 = 2.5 NM)
kontext:
8.3.2.8.1 Policy

Flight Crews are expected to maintain route center lines, as depicted by on- board lateral deviation indicators or flight guidance, during all RNP operations unless authorized to deviate by ATC or under emergency conditions.
For normal operations, cross-track error or deviation (the difference between the RNAV or RNP system computed path and the aircraft position relative to the path)
shall be limited to ±1/2 the navigation accuracy associated with the route (i.e. for RNP 5 2.5 NM).

Brief deviations from this standard (e.g. overshoots or undershoots) during and immediately after turns, up to a maximum of one times the navigation accuracy (i.e. for RNP 5 5 NM), are allowed.

Note: Some aircraft do not display or compute a path during turns. Pilots of these aircraft may not be able to adhere to the ±1/2 accuracy standard during route turns, but are still expected to satisfy the standard during intercepts following turns and on straight segments.

The numerical figure succeeding the term RNAV or RNP refers to the lateral navigation accuracy (Total System Error (TSE)) in NM, which has to be achieved at least 95% of the flight time (e.g. RNP 5 refers to a to required accuracy of 5NM). For RNP APCH and A-RNP, the lateral navigation accuracy depends on each segment.

8.3.2.8.1.1 RNAV vs. RNP PBN operations are predicated on defined navigation performance requirements.

Navigation specifications establish the performance criteria that the area

navigation system shall meet for operation on a specific route, procedure, or

within designated airspace. These specifications, comprising RNAV and RNP

navigation specifications, define the required levels of accuracy, integrity, continuity, availability, and functionality.

RNAV

kontext:
8.3.2.8.1 Policy

Flight Crews are expected to maintain route center lines, as depicted by on- board lateral deviation indicators or flight guidance, during all RNP operations unless authorized to deviate by ATC or under emergency conditions.
For normal operations, cross-track error or deviation (the difference between the RNAV or RNP system computed path and the aircraft position relative to the path) shall be limited to ±1/2 the navigation accuracy associated with the route (i.e. for RNP 5 2.5 NM). Brief deviations from this standard (e.g. overshoots or undershoots) during and immediately after turns, up to a maximum of one times the navigation accuracy (i.e. for RNP 5 5 NM), are allowed.

Note: Some aircraft do not display or compute a path during turns. Pilots of these aircraft may not be able to adhere to the ±1/2 accuracy standard during route turns, but are still expected to satisfy the standard during intercepts following turns and on straight segments.

The numerical figure succeeding the term RNAV or RNP refers to the lateral navigation accuracy (Total System Error (TSE)) in NM, which has to be achieved at least 95% of the flight time (e.g. RNP 5 refers to a to required accuracy of 5NM). For RNP APCH and A-RNP, the lateral navigation accuracy depends on each segment.

8.3.2.8.1.1 RNAV vs. RNP PBN operations are predicated on defined navigation performance requirements.

Navigation specifications establish the performance criteria that the area

navigation system shall meet for operation on a specific route, procedure, or

within designated airspace. These specifications, comprising RNAV and RNP

navigation specifications, define the required levels of accuracy, integrity, continuity, availability, and functionality.

RNAV

A navigation specification based on area navigation that does NOT include the

requirement for performance monitoring and alerting, designated by the prefix RNAV (e.g. RNAV 5, RNAV 1, RNAV APCH).

A navigation specification based on area navigation that includes the requirement

for performance monitoring and alerting, designated by the prefix RNP (e.g. RNP
5, RNP 1, RNP APCH).

RAIM – Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring: autonomous: without external aid or sensors

integrity: the ability of the system to provide timely warnings to users when the system should not be used for navigation

RAIM monitors and verifies integrity and geometry of satellites and notifies crews if they are not providing necessary coverage

as four satellites are required to determine position and altitude, five of them are required to compare which four are correct which is RAIM-prediction

declares itself as not available

8.3.2.8.1.4 Precision Area Navigation (PRNAV) Operation

Precision Area Navigation (PRNAV) supports the gradual decommissioning of ground-based navigation infrastructure and enables more efficient routing within terminal areas. The onboard PRNAV system must achieve an accuracy of ±1 NM for at least 95% of the flight time.
For PRNAV operation only hard coded waypoints may be used. The manual creation of new waypoints is not permitted.

Flight progress must be monitored using primary flight displays and verified through cross-checks with conventional navigation aids, supported by the MCDU.

Before reaching the Initial Approach Waypoint (IAWP), a navigation reasonableness check is required as follows:

For multi-sensor systems (i.e. GPS and IRS): the flight crew must confirm before commencing the approach that the GNSS sensor is the active source for position computation

the flight crew must verify that the displayed RNP value is suitable for the intended PBN operation

If no GPS equipment is available:

navigation must rely on conventional aids (e.g. display the bearing and range to a VOR/DME using the RNAV system and compare it with the RMI indication tuned to the same VOR/DME) The difference in bearing and range shall not be greater than 5° 1 NM.

The flight crew must be prepared to be able to revert to a conventional arrival

procedure in case of loss of PRNAV capability and inform ATC:

“UNABLE RNP 1 DUE TO (state reason)”.

kontext:
8.2.2.12.3 Door Operation in Strong Winds

For the operation of aircraft doors in strong winds (i.e. maximum permissible

wind speeds, other particulars to be observed) refer to the Operations Manual OM-B. If difficulties occur when attempting to close doors in strong winds, the

aircraft shall be moved in order to
position the doors concerned on the downwind side.

8.2.2.13 Safety on the Ramp, including Fire Prevention, Blast and Suction Areas

The following provisions concerning the safety of all aircraft, crews, passengers, staff and load on the ramp shall be observed: only authorized person shall have access to the ramp

the use of open fire is strictly prohibited

ramp surfaces shall be frequently checked to prevent accidents caused by slipping or skidding on oil, ice or snow; these checks shall, as far as possible, also serve to detect foreign objects on the ramp surfaces, which must be removed in order to prevent Foreign Object Damage (FOD) to the tires and other parts of the aircraft, and to preclude foreign object ingestion by an engine

ramp personnel shall wear ear protection permanently, crew members shall do so while on the ramp.

generally the yellow reflective vest must be worn on the tarmac except for crew boarding and deboarding.

Certain systems of the aircraft shall not be operated on the ramp (e.g., weather radar). For details refer to the Operations Manual OM-B.
No passenger shall enter the security zones. Access to checked baggage cannot

be granted and must be prevented by ground staff. This applies also to excess hand baggage loaded into cargo holds.

kontext:
8.3.2.10.4 Ground Movement

8.3.2.10.4.1 Policy

During any ground movement, the sterile flight deck policy applies. Actions which could distract pilots and requiring “head down” shall be avoided as far as possible. Passenger announcements or crew briefings should be completed before starting taxi. The cockpit to cabin communication and vice versa shall be limited to procedural calls.

8.3.2.10.4.2 Taxi

Following guidance has been established and shall be adhered to: during ground movement both pilots shall have access to an airport layout chart for reference and shall keep a constant vigilant look-out for conflicting traffic and obstructions of the taxi way

get used to airport charts and the special marked hot spots and take it into account during the departure briefing according to 8.3.2.14 - Departure Briefing

the pilot taxiing the aircraft shall announce in advance his intentions to the pilot monitoring with his own words (e.g. “straight ahead – second right”)

all taxi clearances shall be understood by each flight crew member. If one pilot is not listening to the ATC communication (e.g. due to communication

with cabin) he shall be briefed about the instructions received by the other pilot the pilot monitoring shall monitor the taxi progress and adherence to the

clearances and shall assist the pilot taxiing. Whenever possible, the taxi

clearance should be typed into the scratch pad of the FMS Control unit

all taxi clearances shall be cross-checked against the aerodrome chart and aerodrome surface markings, signs, and lights

never cross illuminated red stop bars when lining up on, or crossing a

runway unless contingency procedures are in use, communicated and confirmed by the ATC that specifically allows it to do so

if there is any doubt about the clearance or the position at an aerodrome,

stop the aircraft, contact ATC immediately and follow the associated instructions

be “head-up” for a continuous watch during aerodrome surface operations

identify issues (e.g. checklist items) that shall be re-accomplished in the event of a runway change

re-briefings should be done, when possible, with parking brake set

any action which may disturb the flight crew from taxi activity shall be avoided or done with the parking brake set (e.g. announcement by PA)

Before requesting the taxi clearance, both pilots shall verify and confirm that the ground crew has given the clear signal, indicating that all ground equipment has been removed and the airplane is safe to move.
The flight crew shall carefully evaluate the situation around the aircraft, particularly the distances to other airplane and objects, select an adequate taxi speed and handle throttles accordingly. Good taxi speeds are in the range of 15 knots but may depend on the actual traffic situation.
However, taxi speed shall not exceed 30 knots unless required by ATC (e.g. backtrack).

The flight crew must consider the runway condition and adapt the taxi speed whenever operating on contaminated surfaces.
It is good practice to minimize blast effects and noise, particularly during the start of the taxi roll after standstill. Braking shall be applied steady and smoothly and only in intervals. Do not “ride the brakes”.

8.3.2.10.4.3 Push Back and Towing Push back and towing movements require type specific certified equipment and the procedures are based on a close communication between flight and ground

crew members. Towbarless towing is allowed, provided the vehicle is designed to

prevent damage to the airplane.

The following specific wordings must be used to avoid misunderstandings:

Flight crew:

kontext:
CONFIRM BRAKES SET

8.3.2.10.4.4 Low Visibility Taxi

A high degree of awareness is required for all low visibility taxi operations.
In order to render the aircraft visible to other traffic, display of all lights is recommended unless the own vision is thereby impaired. However, care shall be taken not to blind other traffic or ground handling staff.

8.3.2.10.4.5 Runway and Taxiway Incursion

A runway incursion is defined as any occurrence at an aerodrome involving the incorrect presence of an aircraft, vehicle or person on the protected area of a surface designated for the landing and take-off of aircraft. It may lead to a serious incident or accident with significant loss of life.
Runway incursions can be divided into several recurring scenarios.
Common scenarios are: an aircraft or vehicle crossing in front of a landing aircraft

an aircraft or vehicle crossing in front of a departing aircraft

an aircraft or vehicle crossing the runway-holding position marking

an aircraft or vehicle unsure of its position and inadvertently entering an active runway

a breakdown in communications leading to failure to follow an air traffic

control instruction In addition pilot factors that may result in a runway incursion include inadvertent non-compliance with ATC clearances. Often these cases result from a break-

down in communications or a loss of situational awareness in which pilots think

that they are at one location on the aerodrome (such as a specific taxiway or

intersection) when they are actually elsewhere, or they believe that the clearance

issued was to enter the runway, when in fact it was not.

8.3.2.10.4.6 Entering or Crossing a Runway

Crossing and line-up approval must be read back to ATC completely and both pilots must report to each other the reception thereof.
Before entering any runway the respective approach area has to be checked, also any potential conflicting traffic on the runway shall be identified.
When lining up on the departure runway both pilots shall: check heading

check runway markings (i.e. centerline lights and RWY designator)

check correct line-up (on the centerline)

perform time check

For specific callouts refer to type specific OM-B.
If lined up on the runway and held more than 90 seconds beyond anticipated departure time, contact ATC

and advise that you are holding on the runway.

8.3.2.10.4.7 Taxi by Other Personnel than the Commander or the Copilot

Operator’s restriction: no other personnel than the commander or copilot shall taxi an airplane.

Following provisions would apply: if other personnel than the commander or the copilot is taxing an aeroplane it must be ensured that he has received instructions in respect of aerodrome

layout, routes, signs, markings, lights, air traffic control signals and the

operational standards of helvetic and he is competent to use radiotelephony.

fragen.erklaerung_en: If you are standing on the runway more than 90 seconds beyond the expected departure time, ATC must be contacted.

8.2.2.8 Securing of Load – Holds

The following shall systematically be tied-down or blocked: all high density packages, whatever their weight, with sharp angles liable to damage hold linings, or packages liable to slip through meshes of the separation nets or between the net and the linings, or the floor, e.g. steel extrusions, metallic trunks

incompatible cargo

heavy pieces (HEA) classified packages, whose unit weight ranges from 150 to 500 kg.

boxes carrying life animals (AVI), in order to keep sufficient free air volume around, and to avoid their tipping.

Blocking by baggage or other packages is acceptable and may be considered as equivalent to tie-down if the following conditions are met: the total load in the same section must have the same destination.

the packages must be effectively blocked by other baggage or cargo in all directions, including upward.

packages or baggage blocking heavy or dense packages with sharp angles must be capable to prevent the latter from moving without themselves being damaged.
Blocking used to ensure separation of incompatible cargo must only be used in

the horizontal direction.

Never obstruct the surfaces designed for the ventilation of the container.

fragen.zitat: The following policy shall be applied to trace tasks, balance workload and avoid Controlled Flight Into Terrain (CFIT).
kontext:
8.3.0.2 Priorities

During daily flight operations crews sometimes encounter situations where different kinds of actions should be done at almost the same time (multi-tasking).
The following policy shall be applied to trace tasks, balance workload and avoid Controlled Flight Into Terrain (CFIT).

1. Aviate

attitude (pitch, bank)

energy (angle of attack, thrust)

values (speed, altitude, heading)

2. Navigate

general terrain awareness: actual position tracking in relation to height (take-off, enroute, approach and missed approach) desired position

tools (update of FMS, NAV-settings)

3. Communicate

information update within flight crew (e.g. re-assessment, briefings)

information update to Air Traffic Control (ATC)

information update to cabin crew

information update to third parties (e.g. Operations Control (OCC), local handling agent)
fragen.frage_en: In what order are tasks to be prioritised at high workload according to OM-A policy?
antworten_en: Aviate, Communicate, Navigate
Navigate, Aviate, Communicate
Aviate, Navigate, Communicate
Communicate, Aviate, Navigate
fragen.erklaerung_en: OM-A 8.3.0.2 defines the priorities Aviate, Navigate, Communicate to distribute workload and avoid CFIT.

8.3.0.3 Cross-Checking of Critical Actions

Some actions might result in non-reversible consequences if performed either the wrong way or too quickly. Therefore, cross-checking and confirmation is required. airplane configuration changes (gear, slats/ flaps, speed brakes)

altimeter subscale settings (barometric pressure setting)

altitude (window) selections (“altitude pre-selector and alerter”)

transfer of flight controls

changes in Flight Guidance System (FD/ AP), Flight Management System (FMS) and navigation aids during departure and approach

mass and balance calculations and associated FMS entries

performance calculations or inputs into the FMS

For abnormal operations only. Confirmation according to 8.3.19.2.3 - Vital Items Closed Loop is required for: thrust levers (abnormal operations only)

fuel master or control switches (abnormal operations only)

engine fire handles or switches engine fire extinguisher discharge switches (if not automatically armed in

conjunction with associated fire handles or switches)
IDG/ CSD disconnect switch

fragen.frage: Wer entscheidet über einen Rejected Takeoff und wann ist der Befehl idealerweise zu geben?
antworten: Der Pilot Flying; spätestens bei VR
Derjenige Pilot, der den Fehler erkennt; spätestens bei V1

Immer der Commander; spätestens bei V1 + 10 kt
