fragen.zitat: The order for a take-off rejection shall be given ideally before V1-10 kts but latest before reaching V1 and shall be followed.
kontext:
8.3.2.18 Take-off Rejection

Continuous monitoring and cross-checking of the flight and engine instruments and the annunciator panel by the Pilot Monitoring (PM) during take-off and initial climb-out is of utmost importance.
The decision to abort a take-off is always by the Commander (CMD) and is initiated by calling out: “REJECT” (E-Jet)
The order for a take-off rejection shall be given ideally before V1-10 kts but latest before reaching V1 and shall be followed.

Low High Speed Reject Policy Low speed reject: speeds below a value defined in aircraft specific OM-B: rejects are usually not critical on non-restricting and dry runways.
Rejects can therefore be considered for minor items as well

High speed reject: speeds above a value defined in aircraft specific OM-B: result in rejects coming closer to V1 and should be considered only in case of major failures (e.g. engine related, fire, structural damage) or suitable conditions (e.g. non contaminated runway).

For the setting of reverse power consult the aircraft specific OM-B.
For tasks to be performed after a take-off rejection, consult the aircraft specific OM-B 3.
fragen.frage_en: Who decides on a rejected takeoff and when shall the command ideally be given?
antworten_en: The Pilot Flying; at the latest at VR
The pilot who detects the failure; at the latest at V1
Always the Commander; ideally before V1 – 10 kt, at the latest before V1
Always the Commander; at the latest at V1 + 10 kt
fragen.erklaerung_en: The decision to reject the takeoff always lies with the CMD (callout "REJECT"), ideally before V1 – 10 kt, at the latest before V1.

kontext:
8.3.2.16 Take-off Clearance

The flight crew shall verify the proper reception of the take-off clearance with a read-back including: call sign

restrictions or flight path information received with the clearance

runway

Both pilots shall report to each other the reception of the take-off clearance.
If there is an uncertainty about the clearance, verification shall be made.
A time check shall be performed or verified to determine TOGA thrust time limit (automatically performed time check by the system upon lift-off is considered acceptable).
If the take-off has been delayed by the flight crew for any reason after the reception of the take-off clearance, “ROLLING” shall be reported to ATC upon starting the take-off roll.
For take-off the actual mean wind and crosswind gusts shall be within type specific OM-B limitations. However, if not limited by the type specific OM-B,
crosswind gusts shall not exceed the mean wind limit for crosswind plus 5 kts,

considering the runway condition. Refer to Runway Condition Assessment Matrix
(RCAM).

For specific callouts refer to type specific of OM-B.

antworten_en: Mean wind limit for crosswind plus 10 kt
Mean wind limit for crosswind plus 5 kt
Mean wind limit for crosswind plus 15 kt
Equal to the mean wind limit
fragen.erklaerung_en: Without an OM-B limit, crosswind gusts must not exceed the mean wind limit for crosswind plus 5 kt (taking runway conditions into account).

kontext:
8.3.2.23 Holding Pattern, Procedure Turns

For holding procedures and procedure-turns refer to the Operations Manual OM-C.
In holding patterns and procedure turns the rate of descent shall not exceed 1500 fpm.

Great attention shall be paid to the compliance with the holding speed limitations.
For local regulations refer to the Operations Manual OM-C.
If unable to comply (i.e. when holding in a clean configuration is not possible at the assigned speeds) and if the limitations are not in force for the purpose of obstacle clearance a higher than standard holding speed may be negotiated with ATC.
For the timing of a holding pattern refer to the Operations Manual OM-C (Route Manual). When a clearance is received specifying the time of departure from the holding fix, the flight crew shall adjust the pattern within the limits of the established holding procedure in order to leave the fix as near to the time specified as practicable.
Corrections shall be made in both heading and timing to compensate for the effects of wind. A correction shall also be made if the entry speed was excessive due to an unexpected holding clearance.
Turning to the inbound leg of a holding pattern not utilizing the FMS, a 90o – 45o interception shall be flown.
Holdings and procedure turns should be flown with 25° bank.

fragen.erklaerung_en: In holdings and procedure turns, the rate of descent must not exceed 1500 fpm; flown with 25° bank.

kontext:
8.3.6.4 Reaction to TCAS TA and TCAS RA

Traffic Advisories (TA) A Traffic Advisory (TA) is intended to alert the flight crew that a Resolution Advisory (RA), requiring a change in flight path, may follow.
For detailed actions and callouts refer to type specific OM-B.

Resolution Advisories (RA) A Resolution Advisory (RA) is intended to advise pilots of the vertical manoeuvre they should carry out in order to achieve or maintain adequate separation from an established threat.
The manoeuvres shall follow the indication of the advisory and never be made in a direction opposite to that given by the system.
If an instruction to manoeuvre is received simultaneously from a Resolution Advisory (RA) and from ATC, and both instructions are in conflict, the advice given by the Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) must be followed.
Note: Visually acquired traffic may not be the same traffic causing an RA.
The visual perception of an encounter may be misleading, particularly at night.
Whenever a Resolution Advisory (RA) requires a climb while the aircraft is in landing configuration, a go-around shall be initiated.

It is emphasized that the Traffic Collision Avoidance System Mark II (TCAS II) relies upon information received from the transponders of the surrounding

aircraft. Resolution Advisories (RA) will only be generated if both the receiving

aircraft and the potential intruder are transmitting transponder signals in mode C or higher. The equipment is not capable of resolving with complete accuracy the

bearing, heading or vertical rates of intruding aircraft. Pilots should therefore not

attempt to manoeuvre on the basis of the system display.

For detailed actions and callouts refer to type specific OM-B.
fragen.frage_en: A TCAS RA requires a climb while the aircraft is in landing configuration. What must be done?
antworten_en: Ignore the RA, as TCAS should be inhibited in landing configuration
A go-around must be initiated
Only stop the descent and continue the approach
Ask ATC for confirmation before manoeuvring
fragen.erklaerung_en: If an RA in landing configuration requires a climb, a go-around must be initiated.

fragen.frage: Wer führt im PPAA-Schema die Analyse einer abnormalen Situation an?
antworten: Der Pilot Flying (PF)
Immer der Commander
Der Pilot Monitoring (PM)
Die Senior Cabin Attendant
fragen.erklaerung: Im PPAA-Schema übernimmt der PF Power und Performance, die Analyse erfolgt durch beide Piloten unter Führung des PM.
fragen.zitat: analyze lies with the Pilot Monitoring (PM)
kontext:
8.3.21.2 RAAR PPAA FORD NITS

Whenever for technical or operational reasons during a flight abnormal or emergency procedures must be applied all company policies remain intact.
Abnormal and emergency procedures consist of four major phases:
R ecognition

A nalysis

A ction

R eassessment

During the application of abnormal and emergency procedures the Crew Resource Management (CRM) becomes, compared with normal operations, an even more crucial component. Therefore, the Commander (CMD) must concentrate with the highest priority on the assessment and distribution of its human and technical resources and to constantly reevaluate and optimize his decisions. The crew must prevent itself from any form of actionist behavior and uncoordinated or unfocused dealing with the problem at hand.
Whenever confronted with an emergency or abnormal situation, the first priority lies in the proper flying and monitoring of the aircraft.
Crew duties must be distributed clearly, basically the following sequence applies:
P ower the PF takes the initiative. Check thrust and order appropriate

setting for the engine(s) operating normally P erformance check configuration and minimum maximum speed

A nalysis both pilots shall assess the situation, where the lead of the
analyze lies with the Pilot Monitoring (PM)

A ction action shall be taken according to emergency abnormal

checklist, OM-B abnormal operation, flight procedures and knowledge

Use company channels and co-operate as soon as possible with the cabin crew.
Create favorable conditions for approach and landing by e.g:

requesting ATC assistance (Priority, Emergency)

careful selection of landing airport with suitable weather conditions, approach aids, runway as applicable

For the abnormal operation helvetic uses abnormal and emergency checklists.
All checklists are named.
When the situation changes to the worse the aim for the safety of the aircraft, its passengers, crew and cargo become the only operational goal.
If this goal can no longer be achieved by the use of the helvetic Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), diversion from these published procedures will be accepted. Any diversion from published procedures for the safety of the aircraft, its passengers, crew and cargo must be exercised only after due consideration by the crew (i.e. no matter how inconvenient such a decision might be for either or both helvetic and passengers).
If the helvetic Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) seem no longer adequate to deal with the situation at hand, an emergency must be declared.
As a general guideline, a declaration of an emergency or urgency can be evaluated and communicated to ATC as follows:
EICAS WARNING land at the nearest suitable airport:
fragen.frage_en: Who leads the analysis of an abnormal situation in the PPAA scheme?
antworten_en: The Pilot Flying (PF)
Always the Commander
The Pilot Monitoring (PM)
The Senior Cabin Attendant
fragen.erklaerung_en: In the PPAA scheme, the PF takes over Power and Performance; the analysis is done by both pilots, led by the PM.

fragen.frage: Unter welchen Bedingungen darf jedes Crew Member (nicht nur der CMD) eine Notevakuierung anordnen?

Wenn der CMD auf die Frage der SEN nicht innert 10 Sekunden antwortet, auch im Flug

Flugzeug am Boden und zum Stillstand gekommen, und schwere strukturelle Schäden, explosives Feuer oder nach einem Ditching

kontext:
8.3.21.5.3 Evacuation Required

When the need for an emergency evacuation arises it must be clearly ordered and carried out expeditiously. The objective of an evacuation is to remove the passengers from the aircraft as fast as possible according to the situation.
Generally, the Commander (CMD) will initiate an evacuation.
But any crew member can order an emergency evacuation when:
the aircraft is on ground and ceased moving,

and there is severe structural damage, or there is explosive fire, or after ditching

An emergency evacuation is ordered by shouting: for callout refer to 8.3 Appendix 1, Evacuation Orders CSPM 2 Appendix 1 Communication Wording

the order must be shouted continuously and it supersedes all previously given orders. An emergency evacuation cannot be canceled – once initiated it must be carried out by all aircraft occupants.
Note: once initiated, an evacuation must not be stopped!

passengers must leave their carry-on baggage in the aircraft and should be directed to a safe distance away from the aircraft.
fragen.frage_en: Under what conditions may any crew member (not only the CMD) order an emergency evacuation?
antworten_en: For any smoke in the cabin, also during taxi
If the CMD does not answer the SEN's question within 10 seconds, also in flight
Only after a rejected takeoff with brake overheat
Aircraft on the ground and stopped, and severe structural damage, explosive fire or after a ditching
fragen.erklaerung_en: Any crew member may evacuate if the aircraft is on the ground and there is severe structural damage, explosive fire or a ditching.

fragen.frage: Welche Voraussetzungen gelten für eine Rapid Disembarkation?
antworten: Escape Slides armiert, damit sie bei Bedarf benutzt werden können
Treppen oder Jetways sind vorhanden, Engines abgestellt und Escape Slides nicht armiert
Sie darf nur nach einem Ditching angeordnet werden
Ein Engine muss für das Electrical System laufen
fragen.erklaerung: Rapid Disembarkation erfolgt nur mit Treppen/Jetways; zuvor müssen Engines abgestellt, Treppen/Jetty in Position und Slides disarmed sein.
fragen.zitat: only be applied if stairs or jet ways are available.
kontext:
8.3.21.5.2 Rapid Disembarkation

For certain reasons the Commander (CMD) may want to abandon the airplane without taking the risks of an emergency evacuation. In this case he may order a rapid disembarkation:
For callouts refer to 8.3 Appendix 1, Rapid Disembarkation Order CSPM 2 Appendix 1 Communication Wording Other, than during an emergency evacuation, the passengers and the crew

would leave the airplane expeditiously, but not in a hurry. This procedure shall
only be applied if stairs or jet ways are available.

Typical scenarios for a decision to execute a rapid disembarkation are in e.g.:

bomb threats,

or being parked next to an aircraft which is suffering from an open fire

Before initiating the procedure the flight crew has to ensure that the engines are

shut down, the jetty and or stairs are in place and the escape slides are not armed.
fragen.frage_en: What prerequisites apply to a rapid disembarkation?
antworten_en: Escape slides armed so that they can be used if needed
Stairs or jetways are available, engines shut down and escape slides not armed
It may only be ordered after a ditching
One engine must be running for electrical power
fragen.erklaerung_en: Rapid disembarkation is only carried out with stairs/jetways; beforehand, engines must be shut down, stairs/jetway in position and slides disarmed.

fragen.frage: Medical Emergency über Zentraleuropa, Fall als lebensbedrohlich eingestuft (z.B. Herzinfarkt). Was empfiehlt die Entscheidungstabelle?

Weiterflug zur Destination, Crew hält sich informiert
Weiterflug, aber Enroute Alternate prüfen

kontext:
8.3.21.8.1 Initial Decision-Making

The aim of the following tables is to help crew members taking a decision concerning the continuation or termination of a flight if a medical incidence or emergency occurs while being enroute.
Minor case Severe case Life-threatening case e.g. circulatory e.g. epilepsy, e.g. angina pectoris, failure, unconsciousness, heart attack, hyperventilation, grand mal seizure, circulatory standstill, choking, asthma, arterial bleeding, stroke, epilepsy, bleeding, shock, birth on 3. degree burns 1.&2. degree burns board.
Central Europe 1 2B 3 Eastern Europe 1 2A 3 Africa 1 2A 3 North America 1 2B 3 South America 1 2A 3

Cabin crew asks for medical trained personnel (e.g. doctor, nurse) amongst passengers. His advice should be considered and followed.

Unless medical personnel gives different advice, the following procedures should be followed: 1 continue flight to destination. Cabin crew keeps flight crew informed about wellbeing of passenger.

2A continue flight to destination, but check for enroute alternate aerodrome in case the medical emergency becomes worse. Cabin crew keeps flight

crew informed about wellbeing of passenger.

2B divert to a major enroute alternate aerodrome to grant medical

infrastructure or personnel. 3
landing at next adequate aerodrome
For follow-up items to consider, refer to next page.
fragen.frage_en: Medical emergency over central Europe, case classified as life-threatening (e.g. heart attack). What does the decision table recommend?
antworten_en: Land at the nearest adequate aerodrome
Continue to destination, crew stays informed
Continue, but check en-route alternate

kontext:
8.3.21.9 Duties of the Commander after an Abnormal or Emergency

Situation

Whenever one of the following is true: distress situation

accident

serious incident

unsolved security threat (1)

any event causing emotional stress which impairs fitness to fulfill flight duties

the Commander (CMD) shall perform the following duties as soon as practicable after the flight: inform Operations Control Center (OCC) or the Piquet Officer (PQO)
do not continue operation until released by FOP, ACM or PQO

coordinate with the PQO if a deactivation of the flight recorders is required. If necessary, the deactivation of all flight recorders shall be done in coordination with maintenance

if required, coordinate passenger care

if required, coordinate with local authorities (if support is required, contact FOP via OCC)

write an occurrence report

Note 1: This excludes straightforward situations that the crew can resolve

independently by following established procedures and verifying that the threat has been fully cleared - without requiring a

back-office risk assessment - such as: unruly passenger level 1-2 events

threat level 1-2 situations

laser beam attacks

offloading of passengers or baggage

clearing of suspicious items

fragen.frage: Wie oft darf ein ausgelöster Circuit Breaker im Flug zurückgesetzt werden?
antworten: Bis zu zwei Reset-Versuche im Abstand von mindestens 2 Minuten
Nur ein Reset-Versuch (gemäss Checkliste oder im Notfall); nach einem zweiten Auslösen kein Reset mehr

kontext:
8.3.24 Circuit Breaker Reset

Tripped circuit breakers usually indicate a system malfunction and a reset should be carefully evaluated, as the risk of an electrical fire should never be underestimated. No cabin crew member shall reset a circuit breaker without prior consultation with the Commander (CMD).
In flight, only one reset attempt shall be performed and only according to the appropriate check list

in an emergency situation, if the safety of the flight is definitely improved by doing so
No reset is allowed after a second trip of any circuit breaker.

On ground a reset shall only be performed after maintenance has ascertained the reason for the circuit breaker trip and has established that there is no airworthiness concern.
No flight shall be commenced with a tripped circuit breaker which is not secured by a safety ring. (e.g. If a system has been deactivated and deferred according to CAMP, due to a tripped circuit breaker, a circuit breaker ring shall be installed)

Note: Maintenance may pull some circuit breakers as part of there normal procedures. In case of doubt a crosscheck with maintenance shall be performed.

Refer also to:
E1: OM-B 3.1 Circuit Breaker Reset

E2: OM-B 3.1 Circuit Breaker Reset
fragen.frage_en: How often may a tripped circuit breaker be reset in flight?
antworten_en: Up to two reset attempts at least 2 minutes apart
Only one reset attempt (per checklist or in an emergency); after a second trip no further reset
As often as desired, as long as no smoke occurs
Not at all, CB resets are only permitted on the ground by Maintenance
fragen.erklaerung_en: In flight, only one reset attempt is permitted per checklist or in an emergency; after a second trip, no reset is allowed.

12.2.5 Procedures Prior to RVSM Airspace Entry EN

The following equipment shall be operating normally at entry into RVSM

airspace:

two primary altitude measurement systems

one automatic altitude-control system

one altitude-alerting device Note: the dual equipment requirements for altitude-control systems will be

established by regional agreement after an evaluation of criteria

surveillance

fragen.frage: Um wie viel darf das cleared Flight Level beim Levelwechsel im RVSM-Luftraum maximal über- oder unterschritten werden?
antworten: 100 ft

fragen.zitat: When changing levels, the aircraft shall not be allowed to overshoot or undershoot the cleared flight level by more than 45m (150 ft).
kontext:
12.2.6.1 Normal Practices and Procedures after entering RVSM Airspace

Flight crews shall comply to any aircraft operating restrictions, if required for the specific aircraft group: limits on indicated Mach number (basic flight envelope upper Mach boundary), given in the RVSM airworthiness approval Note: all helvetic aircraft with RVSM approval shall be compliant to full RVSM flight envelope

Emphasis shall be placed on promptly setting the sub-scale on all primary and standby altimeters to 1013.2 hPa when passing the transition altitude, and rechecking for proper altimeter setting when reaching the initial cleared flight level.
In level cruise it is essential that the aircraft is flown at the cleared flight level.
This requires that particular care is taken to ensure that ATC clearances are fully understood and followed. The aircraft shall not intentionally depart from a cleared flight level without a positive clearance from ATC, unless the crew is conducting contingency or emergency manoeuvres.
When changing levels, the aircraft shall not be allowed to overshoot or undershoot the cleared flight level by more than 45m (150 ft).

If installed, the level off should be accomplished using the altitude capture feature of the automatic altitude-control system.

An automatic altitude-control system shall be operative and engaged during level cruise, except when circumstances, such as the need to re-trim the aircraft or turbulence, require disengagement. In any event adherence to the assigned cruise level should be done by reference to one of the two primary altimeters.
Following loss of the automatic height keeping function, any consequential

restrictions will need to be observed.

Therefore:

ensure that the altitude-alerting system is operative

cross-check at intervals of approximately one hour the primary altimeters; a minimum of two shall agree within ±200 ft (±60 m); failure to meet this

condition will require that the altimetry system is reported as defective and

notified to ATC; the usual scan of flight deck instruments shall suffice for altimeter cross-checking on most flights

in normal operations, the altimetry system being used to control the aircraft

shall be selected for the input to the altitude reporting transponder, transmitting information to ATC

OM-A 12 Rules of the Air

If the pilot is notified by ATC of an assigned altitude deviation of 300 ft (90 m) or more then the flight crew shall take appropriate action to return to the cleared flight level as quickly as possible.
If the pilot is advised in real time that the aircraft has been identified by a height- monitoring system that the Total Vertical Error (TVE) is greater than ±300 ft (±90m) and or if an Altimetry System Error (ASE) greater than ±245 ft (±75 m) is experienced, the flight crew should follow established regional procedures to protect the safe operation of the aircraft. This assumes that the monitoring system will identify the TVE or ASE within the set limits for accuracy.
Caution should be exercised due to problems of visual perceptions of other aircraft during darkness at 1000 ft separation, and when encountering local phenomena such as northern lights. This applies to aircraft in the opposite and same flight direction, and during turns. Use of the TCAS will verify what actual separation exists from nearby aircraft.

antworten_en: 100 ft
200 ft
150 ft
300 ft
fragen.erklaerung_en: During a level change, the cleared flight level must not be overshot or undershot by more than 45 m (150 ft).

fragen.frage: Welche Phraseologie wird bei einem Ausrüstungsmangel verwendet, der die RVSM-Fähigkeit beeinträchtigt?

"Unable RVSM due Equipment"

fragen.zitat: Equipment failure - "Unable RVSM due Equipment"
kontext:
12.2.6.4 Pilot Reports

Equipment
failure - "Unable RVSM due Equipment"

where an aircraft's Mode C displayed level at the controller's traffic display differs from the cleared flight level by 300 ft or more, the controller shall inform the pilot accordingly and the pilot shall be requested to both, check the pressure setting and confirm the aircraft's level

when informed by the pilot that the aircraft's equipment has degraded to

below RVSM MASPS compliance levels while operating within the RVSM

airspace, the controller shall either provide for a minimum vertical

separation of 2 000 ft or an appropriate horizontal separation; controllers

shall normally clear the aircraft below FL 290 (or, alternatively, above FL 410 if the destination aerodrome is outside the lateral limits of the RVSM airspace) before the next transfer of control, unless otherwise coordinated

OM-A 12 Rules of the Air

Turbulence (not forecast) - "Unable RVSM due Turbulence" for the case of an individual aircraft reporting severe turbulence preventing the aircraft from maintaining its cleared flight level, the controller shall establish either an appropriate horizontal separation, or an increased minimum vertical separation; for the case of immediate requirements where a controller has received no advance warning of impending meteorological conditions that could create severe turbulence, the controller shall provide for an increased minimum vertical separation or an appropriate horizontal separation, and the following action(s), although not exhaustive, should be considered

since each real time situation will demand very specific, distinct actions, the controller should use his best judgment to ensure the safety of the aircraft under her responsibility

the controller should pass traffic information to the extent possible

the controller will coordinate with the supervisor for the purpose of determining whether RVSM operations will be suspended entirely or within a specific level band or area

if a reversion to a 2000 ft vertical separation minimum is deemed necessary, coordination with adjacent ACC shall be accomplished to ensure an orderly progression to the transfer of traffic using a 2000 ft vertical separation as the minimum

supervisors may coordinate, to the extent deemed necessary, a request for the deactivation of any airspace restrictions or reservations required to provide additional radar vectoring airspace necessary to facilitate the transition to a 2000 ft vertical separation minimum

the supervisor should coordinate with the parent Flight Management

Position (FMP) to adjust the applicable sector capacities

OM-A 12 Rules of the Air

Turbulence (forecast) - "Unable RVSM due Turbulence" for the case of meteorological conditions causing severe turbulence, predicted by meteorological services, the procedures required will be of a strategic nature; a meteorological forecast, predicting severe turbulence, received by an ACC, will demand of the ACC supervisor a decision as to whether RVSM operations are to be interrupted, for what period of time, and for what specific level(s) or area; should an increased vertical separation be necessary, the supervisor will coordinate with the adjacent ACC concerned as to the flight levels appropriate for the transfer of traffic, unless a contingency flight level allocation scheme (FLAS) has been determined in the letter of agreement. The supervisor should coordinate with the parent Flight Management Position (FMP) to establish the applicable sector capacities; the issuance of a NOTAM should be considered as circumstances require

12.2.6.3 Special Procedures for In-Flight Contingencies

The flight crew shall notify ATC of contingencies (equipment failures, weather) which affect the ability to maintain the cleared flight level, and co-ordinate an appropriate plan of action.
Examples of equipment failures which shall lead to notification to ATC: failure of all automatic altitude control systems aboard the aircraft

loss of redundancy of altimetry systems

any other equipment failure affecting the ability to maintain cleared flight level

kontext:
12.2.6.1 Normal Practices and Procedures after entering RVSM Airspace

Flight crews shall comply to any aircraft operating restrictions, if required for the specific aircraft group: limits on indicated Mach number (basic flight envelope upper Mach boundary), given in the RVSM airworthiness approval Note: all helvetic aircraft with RVSM approval shall be compliant to full RVSM flight envelope

Emphasis shall be placed on

promptly setting the sub-scale on all primary and standby altimeters to 1013.2 hPa when passing the transition altitude, and rechecking for proper altimeter setting when reaching the initial cleared flight level.

In level cruise it is essential that the aircraft is flown at the cleared flight level.
This requires that particular care is taken to ensure that ATC clearances are fully understood and followed. The aircraft shall not intentionally depart from a cleared flight level without a positive clearance from ATC, unless the crew is conducting contingency or emergency manoeuvres.
When changing levels, the aircraft shall not be allowed to overshoot or undershoot the cleared flight level by more than 45m (150 ft). If installed, the level off should be accomplished using the altitude capture feature of the automatic altitude-control system.

An automatic altitude-control system shall be operative and engaged during level cruise, except when circumstances, such as the need to re-trim the aircraft or turbulence, require disengagement. In any event adherence to the assigned cruise level should be done by reference to one of the two primary altimeters.
Following loss of the automatic height keeping function, any consequential

restrictions will need to be observed.

Therefore:

ensure that the altitude-alerting system is operative

cross-check at intervals of approximately one hour the primary altimeters; a minimum of two shall agree within ±200 ft (±60 m); failure to meet this

condition will require that the altimetry system is reported as defective and

notified to ATC; the usual scan of flight deck instruments shall suffice for altimeter cross-checking on most flights

in normal operations, the altimetry system being used to control the aircraft

shall be selected for the input to the altitude reporting transponder, transmitting information to ATC

OM-A 12 Rules of the Air

If the pilot is notified by ATC of an assigned altitude deviation of 300 ft (90 m) or more then the flight crew shall take appropriate action to return to the cleared flight level as quickly as possible.
If the pilot is advised in real time that the aircraft has been identified by a height- monitoring system that the Total Vertical Error (TVE) is greater than ±300 ft (±90m) and or if an Altimetry System Error (ASE) greater than ±245 ft (±75 m) is experienced, the flight crew should follow established regional procedures to protect the safe operation of the aircraft. This assumes that the monitoring system will identify the TVE or ASE within the set limits for accuracy.
Caution should be exercised due to problems of visual perceptions of other aircraft during darkness at 1000 ft separation, and when encountering local phenomena such as northern lights. This applies to aircraft in the opposite and same flight direction, and during turns. Use of the TCAS will verify what actual separation exists from nearby aircraft.

kontext:
8.3.3.3.2 In Cruise

During flights above the transition altitude an aircraft is flown with the altimeters set to standard reading Flight Levels (FL).
In some regions Flight Levels (FL) are metric and the complete altimeter reading is stated as meters standard (e.g. 5000 meters (16400 ft) is called FL 5000 meters standard).
The transition level is the lowest Flight Level (FL) available for use above the transition altitude and is dependent on the local QNH. By nature the transition level must be higher than the transition altitude.
The airspace between the transition altitude and the transition level is called the transition layer and its vertical dimension varies according to atmospheric conditions.
Where vertical separation is required, the vertical dimension of the transition layer will be at least 1000 feet.

as helvetic policy, the published Minimum En-route Altitude (MEA) shall be used as the minimum altitude for both flight planning and actual flight execution. However,

8.1.1.2 Minimum En-route Altitude

For the practical application of the above basic requirements the Minimum En- route Altitude (MEA) is defined as the lowest published altitude between radio fixes that meets obstacle clearance requirements between those fixes and in most areas assures acceptable navigational and radio signal coverage.
The published Minimum En-route Altitude (MEA) provides a terrain clearance of at least 1000 ft over the highest obstacle within the normal airway width (5 NM each side of the airway centerline) and

kontext:
8.3.2.23 Holding Pattern, Procedure Turns

For holding procedures and procedure-turns refer to the Operations Manual OM-C.
In holding patterns and procedure turns the rate of descent shall not exceed 1500 fpm.

Great attention shall be paid to the compliance with the holding speed limitations.
For local regulations refer to the Operations Manual OM-C.
If unable to comply (i.e. when holding in a clean configuration is not possible at the assigned speeds) and if the limitations are not in force for the purpose of obstacle clearance a higher than standard holding speed may be negotiated with ATC.
For the timing of a holding pattern refer to the Operations Manual OM-C (Route Manual). When a clearance is received specifying the time of departure from the holding fix, the flight crew shall adjust the pattern within the limits of the established holding procedure in order to leave the fix as near to the time specified as practicable.
Corrections shall be made in both heading and timing to compensate for the effects of wind. A correction shall also be made if the entry speed was excessive due to an unexpected holding clearance.
Turning to the inbound leg of a holding pattern not utilizing the FMS, a 90o – 45o interception shall be flown.
Holdings and procedure turns should be flown with 25° bank.

8.3.4.2.1 Altitude Awareness

To stay actively alert flight crews shall: crosscheck that the assigned altitude is above the minimum safe altitude confirm assigned altitudes or flight levels towards ATC and to each other

monitor the Flight Guidance System (FGS) and automatic altitude alerting

system during dynamic phases very closely (e.g. altitude capturing, change

of vertical speed) and refrain from or interrupt other duties during this period of time (e.g. briefings, recordings on OFP, other communication)

The flight crew members shall inform each other of any doubts regarding the reliability of the altitude alerting system. If there is any doubt about the cleared

altitude the Pilot Monitoring (PM) must reconfirm it with ATC.

During climb, the Altitude Pre-selector Alerter (APA) shall be set to the altitude or Flight Level (FL), to which the flight is cleared to climb.
During cruise, the Altitude Pre-selector Alerter (APA) shall be set to the assigned cruising level.
When descending, the Altitude Pre-selector Alerter (APA) shall be set to the altitude or Flight Level (FL), to which the flight is cleared to descend.
During an approach to a VFR airport without air traffic control the Altitude Pre- selector Alerter (APA) shall be set to the minimum terrain clearance altitude.

kontext:
8.3.1 VFR IFR Policy

Except for non revenue flights described in the Operations Manual 8.7 - Non- Revenue Flights, no helvetic flight shall be operated without the full use of air traffic control or advisory services.
In general, all flights shall be operated in accordance with the Instrument Flight Rules (IFR).

Exemptions from this general policy are permitted only according to 8.0.1.5 - Flight Rules.
These flights will be identified on the ATC-flight plan as follows: “Y” – when the flight is started under IFR and later changed to VFR

“Z” – when the flight is started under VFR and later changed to IFR

“V” – for pure VFR flights

Refer to 8.3.1.6 - IFR in Uncontrolled Airspace or procedure on how to obtain respective IFR-clearances.

8.3.1.1 Flights Taking-off from VFR Airports expecting an IFR Clearance for the En-route Portion of the Flight

No flight shall take-off from a VFR airport unless able to maintain full Visual Meteorological Conditions (VMC) until the IFR clearance becomes effective.

kontext:
8.3.1.6 IFR in Uncontrolled Airspace

In general, flights into uncontrolled airspace (classes F and G) shall be avoided.
However, Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) operations in uncontrolled airspace are applied in some countries.
While flying IFR in uncontrolled airspace the following procedures and restrictions shall be applied: airspace classes F and G: for air traffic advisory service and Flight Information Service (FIS) refer to OM-C 1 Route Manual, Rules, ICAO Rules of the air

usually, only one IFR traffic at the time given may fly IFR in the assigned airspace F

cruising levels: shall be selected appropriate to the magnetic track, refer to OM-C/ Rules and Regulations

communication: maintain a listening watch and establish two-way communication with Air Traffic Services (ATS). Standard position reports (e.g. blind transmissions) shall be given

take-off and departure: the IFR departure clearance must be obtained prior to departure by any means (e.g. radio communication, phone call to ATC).
Separation between IFR traffic can be granted by timed clearance expiries

approach and landing: the IFR approach clearance must be obtained prior to start the approach from the Initial Approach Fix (IAF). Thereafter, ATC will usually give instruction to monitor the local aerodrome frequency (e.g. AFIS).
Standard position reports shall be transmitted enabling as well VFR traffic to gain an overview concerning the traffic situation. In VMC conditions with

local VFR traffic special attention must be given to the behavior of such

aeroplanes (e.g. basic flying instruction, solo-flights) which might dictate a

smooth integration into the local VFR traffic patterns

special attention must be given to an active and systematic look-out when

flying in mixed IFR/VFR airspace (airspace classes E and F)

Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) shall be operative
CAT II, CAT II/III operation is not allowed

kontext:
12.3.1.3 Figures and Numbers

Figures indicating hundreds and thousands in round number, as for ceiling heights, and upper wind levels up to 9 900 shall be spoken in accordance with the following.
Example: 500 “five hundred”

4 500 “four thousand five hundred”

Numbers above 9900 shall be spoken by separating the digits preceding the word "thousand." Example: 10 000 “one zero thousand”
13 500 “one three thousand five hundred”

When a radio frequency contains a decimal point, the decimal point is spoken as "decimal".
Example: 122.1 “one two two decimal one”

OM-A 12 Rules of the Air

kontext:
12.3.1.11 Corrections and Repetitions

When an error has been made in transmission, the word “CORRECTION” shall

be spoken, the last correct group or phrase repeated, and then the correct

version transmitted.

If a correction can best be made by repeating the entire message,

the phrase

“CORRECTION, I SAY AGAIN” shall be used before the message is transmitted a second time.

If the receiving station is in doubt as to the correctness of the message received,

a repetition either in full or in part shall be requested.
If repetition of an entire message is required, the words “SAY AGAIN” shall be

spoken.

If repetition of a portion of a message is required, the phrase “SAY AGAIN ALL BEFORE… (first word satisfactorily received)” shall be used or “SAY AGAIN…

(word before missing portion) TO…(word after missing portion)” or “SAY AGAIN ALL AFTER… (last word satisfactorily received)”.

OM-A 12 Rules of the Air

12.3.2.3 Clarification and Acceptance of Clearances

Several factors such as use of non-standard wordings, high workload of ATC- controllers or flight crews, ambiguous wordings, formally correct but substantially questionable contents, non-standard routings, call sign confusion, or requests may lead to critical situations. For this reason,
at least two flight crew members must monitor and confirm clearances issued by ATC.

If any flight crew member is in doubt if a clearance has been understood correctly or if one flight crew member has missed a clearance, confirmation from ATC must be requested, by use of different simple and clear words.
High alertness of crews is required in relation to vertical navigation, especially in mountainous or hilly terrain during radar vectoring.
Example:

flight crew: ”To confirm – our position is 20 miles west of minimum radar vectoring altitude is 6000 feet, confirm descent to 4000 feet at present position

usually, ATC will realize the error and revise their instruction

However, an emergency must always be declared, if one of the following conditions exists: fire or smoke on board or

kontext:
10.13.6.3.1 Communication actual breach into Flight Deck

The cabin shall discreetly notify the flight crew in the event of suspicious activity or security breaches in the cabin by use of the aircraft interphone. An aircraft interphone handset is located at each cabin crew station.
In case of a real threat situation against the flight deck the cabin attendant shall initiate the routine access procedure and shall identify him-/herself via interphone as “cabin attendant six” instead of using his name.
In such a situations the flight deck must remain locked.
The crew shall:
set transponder to A7500

if not under radar control include phrase transponder A7500 in call sign or next ATC communication

monitor 121.500 MHz and expect to be intercepted by military aircraft

land as soon as possible at the nearest suitable aerodrome

contact and inform Operations Control Centre (OCC)

In case of an actual breach of the flight deck, the crew shall additionally: try to maintain at the controls at all times and at all costs

ask for help via PA or directly from cabin crew and/or passengers, as discreetly as deemed necessary

defend the flight deck using whatver force and resources are necessary to

eliminate the threat

after landing and when stopped, perform the emergency evacuation

procedure or parts of it, if possible, to disable the aircraft from further

movements

cooperate with local authorities and file an IT report

kontext:
12.2.3.6 Maintenance Flights

ATS providers have established policies to enable aircraft that are temporarily non-RVSM compliant to fly in RVSM airspace for the purpose of positioning the aircraft to a maintenance facility.
These policies require prior coordination with appropriate ATC centers so that 2000 feet separation can be applied between the non-compliant aircraft and other aircraft.

The Flight Operations Officer (FOO) must be informed of and comply with the policies for such operations published in NOTAMS, Aeronautical Information Publications (AIP) and other appropriate documents.

4000 ft, without prior coordination
No special separation, provided ACAS II is operative
fragen.erklaerung_en: For maintenance positioning flights of non-compliant aircraft, prior coordination with ATC is required so that 2000 ft separation can be applied.

fragen.frage: Wann darf das automatische Altitude-Control-System im Level Cruise im RVSM-Luftraum ausgeschaltet werden?

fragen.zitat: An automatic altitude-control system shall be operative and engaged during level cruise, except when circumstances, such as the need to re-trim the aircraft or turbulence, require disengagement.
kontext:
12.2.6.1 Normal Practices and Procedures after entering RVSM Airspace

Flight crews shall comply to any aircraft operating restrictions, if required for the specific aircraft group: limits on indicated Mach number (basic flight envelope upper Mach boundary), given in the RVSM airworthiness approval Note: all helvetic aircraft with RVSM approval shall be compliant to full RVSM flight envelope

Emphasis shall be placed on promptly setting the sub-scale on all primary and standby altimeters to 1013.2 hPa when passing the transition altitude, and rechecking for proper altimeter setting when reaching the initial cleared flight level.
In level cruise it is essential that the aircraft is flown at the cleared flight level.
This requires that particular care is taken to ensure that ATC clearances are fully understood and followed. The aircraft shall not intentionally depart from a cleared flight level without a positive clearance from ATC, unless the crew is conducting contingency or emergency manoeuvres.
When changing levels, the aircraft shall not be allowed to overshoot or undershoot the cleared flight level by more than 45m (150 ft). If installed, the level off should be accomplished using the altitude capture feature of the automatic altitude-control system.
An automatic altitude-control system shall be operative and engaged during level cruise, except when circumstances, such as the need to re-trim the aircraft or turbulence, require disengagement.

In any event adherence to the assigned cruise level should be done by reference to one of the two primary altimeters.
Following loss of the automatic height keeping function, any consequential

restrictions will need to be observed.

Therefore:

ensure that the altitude-alerting system is operative

cross-check at intervals of approximately one hour the primary altimeters; a minimum of two shall agree within ±200 ft (±60 m); failure to meet this

condition will require that the altimetry system is reported as defective and

notified to ATC; the usual scan of flight deck instruments shall suffice for altimeter cross-checking on most flights

in normal operations, the altimetry system being used to control the aircraft

shall be selected for the input to the altitude reporting transponder, transmitting information to ATC

OM-A 12 Rules of the Air

If the pilot is notified by ATC of an assigned altitude deviation of 300 ft (90 m) or more then the flight crew shall take appropriate action to return to the cleared flight level as quickly as possible.
If the pilot is advised in real time that the aircraft has been identified by a height- monitoring system that the Total Vertical Error (TVE) is greater than ±300 ft (±90m) and or if an Altimetry System Error (ASE) greater than ±245 ft (±75 m) is experienced, the flight crew should follow established regional procedures to protect the safe operation of the aircraft. This assumes that the monitoring system will identify the TVE or ASE within the set limits for accuracy.
Caution should be exercised due to problems of visual perceptions of other aircraft during darkness at 1000 ft separation, and when encountering local phenomena such as northern lights. This applies to aircraft in the opposite and same flight direction, and during turns. Use of the TCAS will verify what actual separation exists from nearby aircraft.
fragen.frage_en: When may the automatic altitude control system be switched off in level cruise in RVSM airspace?
antworten_en: At any time at the PF's discretion
Only above FL 370
When, for example, a re-trim of the aircraft or turbulence requires it
Only with prior ATC clearance
fragen.erklaerung_en: The system must be operative and engaged in level cruise, unless circumstances such as re-trim or turbulence require it to be switched off.

fragen.frage: Welche Situation gehört NICHT zu den im OM-A aufgeführten genehmigten RVSM-Contingency-Verfahren?

Schwere Turbulenz, nicht vorhergesagt
Ausfall des ACAS II
Schwere Turbulenz, vorhergesagt
fragen.erklaerung: Die genehmigten Contingency-Verfahren sind: Degradation der Ausrüstung, schwere Turbulenz nicht vorhergesagt und vorhergesagt. ACAS II ist für RVSM nicht vorgeschrieben.
fragen.zitat: degradation of aircraft equipment – pilot reported severe turbulence – not forecast severe turbulence – forecast
kontext:
12.2.6.2 Contingency Procedures

There are a number of approved contingency procedures:

degradation of aircraft equipment – pilot reported

severe turbulence – not forecast

severe turbulence – forecast

An in-flight contingency affecting a flight in the RVSM airspace pertains to

unforeseen circumstances that directly impact on the ability of one or more aircraft to operate in accordance with the vertical navigation performance requirements of the RVSM airspace, as specified above. Such in-flight contingencies can result from degradation of aircraft equipment associated with

height-keeping, and from turbulent atmospheric conditions.

The pilot shall inform air traffic control as soon as possible of any circumstances

where the vertical navigation performance requirements for the RVSM airspace

cannot be maintained. In such cases, the flight crew shall obtain a revised air traffic control clearance prior to initiating any deviation from the cleared route or

flight level, whenever possible. Where a revised air traffic control clearance cannot be obtained prior to a deviation, the flight crew shall obtain a revised

clearance as soon as possible thereafter.

Air traffic control shall render all possible assistance to a flight crew experiencing an in-flight contingency. Subsequent air traffic control actions will be based on

the intentions of the flight crew, the over-all air traffic situation and the real-time dynamics of the contingency.

OM-A 12 Rules of the Air
fragen.frage_en: Which situation is NOT among the approved RVSM contingency procedures listed in OM-A?
antworten_en: Degradation of aircraft equipment (reported by pilot)
Severe turbulence, not forecast
Failure of ACAS II
Severe turbulence, forecast
fragen.erklaerung_en: The approved contingency procedures are: equipment degradation, severe turbulence not forecast and forecast. ACAS II is not required for RVSM.

fragen.frage: Welcher Ausfall ist im OM-A NICHT als Beispiel für einen ATC zu meldenden Ausrüstungsausfall im RVSM-Luftraum genannt?

fragen.erklaerung: Genannt sind Ausfall aller Altitude-Control-Systeme, Verlust der Altimetry-Redundanz, Schubverlust mit nötigem Sinkflug und jeder andere Ausfall, der die Höhenhaltung beeinträchtigt.
fragen.zitat: loss of redundancy of altimetry systems loss of thrust on an engine necessitating descent
kontext:
12.2.6.3 Special Procedures for In-Flight Contingencies

The flight crew shall notify ATC of contingencies (equipment failures, weather) which affect the ability to maintain the cleared flight level, and co-ordinate an appropriate plan of action.
Examples of equipment failures which shall lead to notification to ATC: failure of all automatic altitude control systems aboard the aircraft

loss of redundancy of altimetry systems

loss of thrust on an engine necessitating descent

any other equipment failure affecting the ability to maintain cleared flight level

The flight crew shall notify ATC when encountering greater than moderate turbulence.
If unable to notify ATC and obtain an ATC clearance prior to deviating from the assigned cleared flight level, the pilot should follow the established contingency procedures and obtain ATC clearance as soon as possible.
fragen.frage_en: Which failure is NOT given in OM-A as an example of an equipment failure in RVSM airspace to be reported to ATC?
antworten_en: Failure of a pack
Failure of all automatic altitude control systems
Loss of redundancy of the altimetry systems
Loss of thrust of an engine requiring a descent
fragen.erklaerung_en: Named are failure of all altitude control systems, loss of altimetry redundancy, loss of thrust requiring descent, and any other failure affecting altitude keeping.

Turbulence (not forecast) - "Unable RVSM due Turbulence" for the case of an individual aircraft reporting severe turbulence preventing the aircraft from maintaining its cleared flight level, the controller shall establish either an appropriate horizontal separation, or an increased minimum vertical separation; for the case of immediate requirements where a controller has received no advance warning of impending meteorological conditions that could create severe turbulence, the controller shall provide for an increased minimum vertical separation or an appropriate horizontal separation, and the following action(s), although not exhaustive, should be considered

since each real time situation will demand very specific, distinct actions, the controller should use his best judgment to ensure the safety of the aircraft under her responsibility

the controller should pass traffic information to the extent possible

the controller will coordinate with the supervisor for the purpose of determining whether RVSM operations will be suspended entirely or within a specific level band or area

if a reversion to a 2000 ft vertical separation minimum is deemed necessary, coordination with adjacent ACC shall be accomplished to ensure an orderly progression to the transfer of traffic using a 2000 ft vertical separation as the minimum

supervisors may coordinate, to the extent deemed necessary, a request for the deactivation of any airspace restrictions or reservations required to provide additional radar vectoring airspace necessary to facilitate the transition to a 2000 ft vertical separation minimum

the supervisor should coordinate with the parent Flight Management

Position (FMP) to adjust the applicable sector capacities

OM-A 12 Rules of the Air

Turbulence (forecast) - "Unable RVSM due Turbulence" for the case of meteorological conditions causing severe turbulence, predicted by meteorological services, the procedures required will be of a strategic nature; a meteorological forecast, predicting severe turbulence, received by an ACC, will demand of the ACC supervisor a decision as to whether RVSM operations are to be interrupted, for what period of time, and for what specific level(s) or area; should an increased vertical separation be necessary, the supervisor will coordinate with the adjacent ACC concerned as to the flight levels appropriate for the transfer of traffic, unless a contingency flight level allocation scheme (FLAS) has been determined in the letter of agreement. The supervisor should coordinate with the parent Flight Management Position (FMP) to establish the applicable sector capacities; the issuance of a NOTAM should be considered as circumstances require

12.2.7 Post Flight

In making technical log entries against malfunctions in height keeping systems, the flight crew shall provide sufficient details to enable maintenance to effectively troubleshoot and repair the system. primary and standby altimeter readings

kontext:
12.3.1.7 Time

Aviation communication uses Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) for all operations. The word "local" or the time zone equivalent shall be used to denote local when local time is given during radio and telephone communications.
The term "Zulu" may be used to denote UTC.
Example: 0920 UTC “zero niner two zero”

Time may be stated in minutes only (two figures) in radiotelephone communications when no misunderstanding is likely to occur.
When stating an estimate generally the time at the event must be stated rather than the duration until the event.

Example:

“helvetic 121, what is your estimate over EKRIT?”

“helvetic 121, estimate EKRIT at 1915”

With the distance, e.g. "EKRIT 85 miles"
With local time without addition, e.g. "EKRIT at 2115"

kontext:
12.3.1.11 Corrections and Repetitions

When an error has been made in transmission, the word “CORRECTION” shall

be spoken, the last correct group or phrase repeated, and then the correct

version transmitted.

If a correction can best be made by repeating the entire message, the phrase

“CORRECTION, I SAY AGAIN” shall be used before the message is transmitted a second time.

If the receiving station is in doubt as to the correctness of the message received,

a repetition either in full or in part shall be requested.
If repetition of an entire message is required, the words “SAY AGAIN” shall be

spoken.

If repetition of a portion of a message is required, the phrase “SAY AGAIN ALL BEFORE… (first word satisfactorily received)” shall be used or “SAY AGAIN…

(word before missing portion) TO…(word after missing portion)” or
“SAY AGAIN ALL AFTER… (last word satisfactorily received)”.
OM-A 12 Rules of the Air

"REPEAT LAST PART"

Yes, if the flight is in uncontrolled airspace
No, the Commander remains responsible for obtaining a corresponding clearance

fragen.frage: ATC erteilt im Radar Vectoring "descend to 4000 feet", die Minimum Radar Vectoring Altitude beträgt aber 6000 ft. Die Crew ist auch nach Rückfrage im Zweifel. Wie geht sie gemäss OM-A vor?
antworten: ATC die Nichtbefolgung melden und die Absicht mitteilen, z.B. "unable to comply, we descend to 6000 feet until overhead due terrain clearance"
Auf 4000 ft sinken, da ATC für die Terrain Clearance verantwortlich ist
Ohne Meldung auf der aktuellen Höhe bleiben
Sofort Mayday erklären und auf MSA steigen
fragen.erklaerung: Ist die Crew nach der Rückfrage noch im Zweifel, informiert sie ATC über die Nichtbefolgung und ihre Absichten.
fragen.zitat: if the flight crew is still in doubt, they shall inform ATC concerning their non- compliance and advise them about their intentions:
kontext:
12.3.2.3 Clarification and Acceptance of Clearances

Several factors such as use of non-standard wordings, high workload of ATC- controllers or flight crews, ambiguous wordings, formally correct but substantially questionable contents, non-standard routings, call sign confusion, or requests may lead to critical situations. For this reason, at least two flight crew members must monitor and confirm clearances issued by ATC. If any flight crew member is in doubt if a clearance has been understood correctly or if one flight crew member has missed a clearance, confirmation from ATC must be requested, by use of different simple and clear words.
High alertness of crews is required in relation to vertical navigation, especially in mountainous or hilly terrain during radar vectoring.
Example:
ATC: “helvetic 385, descend to 4000 feet,

flight crew: ”To confirm – our position is 20 miles west of minimum radar vectoring altitude is 6000 feet, confirm descent to 4000 feet at present position

usually, ATC will realize the error and revise their instruction
if the flight crew is still in doubt, they shall inform ATC concerning their non- compliance and advise them about their intentions:
unable to comply, we descend to 6000 feet until overhead due terrain clearance, helvetic 385.”
fragen.frage_en: ATC issues "descend to 4000 feet" during radar vectoring, but the minimum radar vectoring altitude is 6000 ft. The crew is still in doubt after querying. How does it proceed according to OM-A?
antworten_en: Report non-compliance to ATC and state the intention, e.g. "unable to comply, we descend to 6000 feet until overhead due terrain clearance"
Descend to 4000 ft, as ATC is responsible for terrain clearance
Stay at the current altitude without reporting
Declare Mayday immediately and climb to MSA
fragen.erklaerung_en: If the crew is still in doubt after the query, it informs ATC of the non-compliance and its intentions.

fragen.frage: Welche Reihenfolge hat ein Request gemäss OM-A?
antworten: "request", Inhalt, Rufzeichen
Rufzeichen, "request", Inhalt, wenn möglich der Grund
Inhalt, Grund, Rufzeichen, "request"
Rufzeichen, Grund, "request", Position
fragen.erklaerung: Ein Request besteht aus Rufzeichen, der Phrase "request", dem Inhalt und wenn möglich dem Grund.
fragen.zitat: the aircraft identification (call sign) the phrase “request” the content of the request the reason for the request if feasible
kontext:
12.3.3 Request

If a flight crew wishes to alter or amend a clearance, or if a clearance limit is reached and a new clearance is required, it shall issue a request by stating:

the aircraft identification (call sign)

the phrase “request”

the content of the request

the reason for the request if feasible

(e.g. for convenience items)

Example: “helvetic 130, request flight level 330”

“helvetic 250, approaching KELIP, request further clearance”

convenience item: “helvetic 7000, to shorten taxi time request rwy 16”

OM-A 12 Rules of the Air
fragen.frage_en: What is the sequence of a request according to OM-A?
antworten_en: "request", content, call sign
Call sign, "request", content, if possible the reason
Content, reason, call sign, "request"
Call sign, reason, "request", position
fragen.erklaerung_en: A request consists of call sign, the phrase "request", the content and, if possible, the reason.

"wilco"
"monitoring"

kontext:
12.3.4 Frequency Change

ATC issues a frequency change by stating: the aircraft identification (call sign)

the phrase “contact”, “stand by”, or “monitor”

the unit name

the new frequency

Example: “helvetic 213, monitor apron 121.750”

“helvetic 301, contact Brindisi 133.345”
The frequency change is acknowledged by the flight crew by stating: the phrase “contacting”, “standing by”, or “monitoring”

the unit name

the new frequency

the aircraft identification (call sign)

Unless differently requested by ATC, a report of the cleared altitude shall be done during the first contact with a new ATC unit.

OM-A 12 Rules of the Air
fragen.frage_en: ATC says "helvetic 213, monitor apron 121.750". With which phrase does the correct acknowledgement begin?
antworten_en: "contacting"
"wilco"
"monitoring"
"roger"
fragen.erklaerung_en: Frequency changes are acknowledged with "contacting", "standing by" or "monitoring" as per the instruction, followed by unit, frequency and call sign.

Nächste Position und Zeit darüber
Darauffolgender Significant Point
Restkraftstoff (Fuel on board)
fragen.erklaerung: Ein Position Report enthält Rufzeichen, Position, Zeit, FL/Altitude, nächste Position mit Zeit und den darauffolgenden Significant Point.

kontext:
12.3.5 Position Reporting

Whenever the need for a position report arises (e.g. reaching a mandatory reporting point in a none radar environment) the report must contain: the aircraft identification (call sign)

position

time

flight level or altitude

next position and time over

ensuing significant point
Example: “helvetic 170, position GOKEL at 1012, flight level 290, MAVAR at 34, next Skopje”

antworten_en: Flight level or altitude
Next position and time over it
Following significant point
Remaining fuel (fuel on board)

fragen.frage: Wie ist eine Deviation wegen Wetter bei ATC anzufragen?
antworten: Mit der Anzahl Meilen und der Richtung der gewünschten Abweichung
Nur mit der gewünschten neuen Flughöhe
Mit dem gewünschten Heading und der Dauer in Minuten
Nur mit "request weather deviation" ohne weitere Angaben
fragen.erklaerung: Eine Deviation wird unter Angabe der Anzahl Meilen und der Richtung angefragt.
fragen.zitat: request to deviate off course by stating the number of miles and the direction of the requested deviation;
kontext:
8.3.8.1 Air Traffic Control In-flight Weather Avoidance Assistance

To the extent possible, ATC controllers will issue pertinent information on weather or chaff areas and assist flight crews in avoiding these areas when requested.
Flight crews should respond to a weather advisory by acknowledging it and, if considered necessary, requesting an alternative course of action as follows:
request to deviate off course by stating the number of miles and the direction of the requested deviation;

when the requested deviation is approved, the flight crew is expected to provide its own navigation, maintain the altitude as assigned by Air Traffic Control (ATC) and to remain within the specified range (mileage) of his original course

request a new route to avoid the affected area

request a change of altitude

request radar vectors around the affected areas.

For obvious reasons of safety, the flight crew operating under IFR with traffic separation provided by Air Traffic Control (ATC)) shall not deviate from the course or altitude respectively flight level without a proper clearance. When weather conditions encountered are so severe that an immediate deviation is necessary and time will not permit approval from Air Traffic Control (ATC) the flight crew’s emergency authority may be exercised.

When a flight crew requests clearance for a deviation or for an Air Traffic Control (ATC) radar vector, the controller shall evaluate the air traffic situation within the affected area and coordinate with other controllers before replying to the request.
Therefore, it should be remembered by flight crew members that the controller’s primary function is to provide safe separation between aircraft. Any additional

service, (e.g. weather avoidance assistance), can only be provided to the extent

that it is not detrimental to the primary function. The separation workload is

generally greater than normal when weather disrupts the usual flow of traffic.

It is very important that the request for deviation or radar vectors is forwarded to

Air Traffic Control (ATC) as far in advance as possible.

The following information should be furnished to Air Traffic Control (ATC) when requesting clearance to detour around weather activity: the flight number

a general statement about the intention

the reason for the request

proposed point where detour will commence

proposed route and extent of detour (direction and distance)

point where original route will be resumed

flight conditions (VMC or IMC)

time limitations when necessary

The assistance that might be rendered by Air Traffic Control (ATC) will depend upon the weather information available to controllers. Due to the extremely transitory nature of severe weather situations, the controller’s weather information may be of limited value if based on weather observed on radar only.
Frequent updates by pilots giving specific information can be of considerable value. Therefore, a Pilot Report (PIREP) shall be offered by flight crews who encounter severe weather conditions.
fragen.frage_en: How is a weather deviation to be requested from ATC?
antworten_en: With the number of miles and the direction of the desired deviation
Only with the desired new altitude
With the desired heading and the duration in minutes
Only with "request weather deviation" without further information
fragen.erklaerung_en: A deviation is requested by stating the number of miles and the direction.

Die Crew darf die Höhe frei wählen, solange sie im genehmigten Bereich bleibt

Always, provided the deviation is less than 10 NM
When the weather is so severe that an immediate deviation is necessary and there is no time for an ATC approval (emergency authority)

fragen.frage: Wie lange muss die Crew bei einer Interception den Signalen und Anweisungen des Interceptors folgen?
antworten: Bis sie positiv entlassen (positively released) wird
Bis der Interceptor nicht mehr sichtbar ist
Bis ATC Funkkontakt herstellt
Höchstens 10 Minuten
fragen.erklaerung: Die Crew befolgt die Signale und Anweisungen des Interceptors, bis sie positiv entlassen wird.
fragen.zitat: continue to comply with interceptor aircraft signals and instructions until positively released
kontext:
12.3.9 Interception by Military Aircraft

General rules:
If you are intercepted by a military or law enforcement aircraft: remain predictable

do not adjust your altitude, heading, or airspeed until directed to by the intercepting aircraft

adhere to instructions relayed through the use of visual devices, visual signals, and radio communications from the intercepting aircraft

attempt to establish radio communications with the intercepting aircraft or with the appropriate ATC facility by making a general call on guard (121.5 MHz), giving the identity, position, and nature of the flight

if transponder operable, squawk 7700 unless otherwise instructed by ATC
continue to comply with interceptor aircraft signals and instructions until positively released

Detailed Information:

Refer to OM-C 1 Route Manual Pubs (applicable region) General Airway

Manual Emergency Data – International Civil Aviation Authority International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)

OM-A 12 Rules of the Air
fragen.frage_en: For how long must the crew follow the signals and instructions of the interceptor during an interception?
antworten_en: Until positively released
Until the interceptor is no longer visible
Until ATC establishes radio contact
10 minutes at most
fragen.erklaerung_en: The crew follows the interceptor's signals and instructions until positively released.

fragen.frage: Was sollen Flüge, die längere Zeit über FL280 fliegen, bezüglich CPDLC tun?
antworten: Nichts, CPDLC ist bei helvetic nur auf Anfrage von ATC zu nutzen
Sich bei CPDLC einloggen, wenn die UIR CPDLC anbietet
Sich nur im Notfall einloggen
Sich nur auf Langstreckenflügen über 3 Stunden einloggen
fragen.erklaerung: Flüge über FL280 für längere Zeit sollen sich einloggen, wenn die UIR CPDLC-Kommunikation anbietet.
fragen.zitat: Flights above FL280 for a considerable time should logon to CPDLC if the UIR provides CPDLC communications.
kontext:
12.5 Operation of Controller Pilot Data Link Communications

(CPDLC)

CPDLC is an additional communication channel used for flights during the cruise phase generally above FL280. In some areas CPDLC can be available at lower levels. For detailed operation refer to OM-B E2 2.4.1.12 and OM-C 1 Route Manual.

Flights which do not reach a cruise level of above FL280 are not required to logon to CPDLC.
Flights above FL280 for a considerable time should logon to CPDLC if the UIR provides CPDLC communications.

OM-A 13 Aircraft Leasing

13 Aircraft Leasing 13.0-1
fragen.frage_en: What should flights flying above FL280 for an extended period do regarding CPDLC?
antworten_en: Nothing, CPDLC at Helvetic is only used on ATC request
Log on to CPDLC if the UIR offers CPDLC
Log on only in an emergency
Log on only on long-haul flights over 3 hours
fragen.erklaerung_en: Flights above FL280 for an extended period should log on if the UIR offers CPDLC communication.

fragen.frage: Was unterscheidet gemäss OM-A eine "prepared emergency" von einer "unprepared emergency"?
antworten: Die prepared emergency ist im OFP geplant, die unprepared nicht
Die prepared emergency tritt nur am Boden auf
Bei der prepared emergency gibt es vorgängige Hinweise, die Vorbereitung, Briefings und einen Aktionsplan ermöglichen
Die unprepared emergency betrifft nur die Kabine
fragen.erklaerung: Eine prepared emergency kündigt sich an und erlaubt spezifische Vorbereitungen und Briefings; eine unprepared emergency tritt ohne oder mit kaum Vorwarnung auf.
fragen.zitat: A prepared emergency therefore allows for specific preparations of the aircraft, inter-crew communication, advice to and from other parties and briefings of crew and passengers.
kontext:
8.3.21.1.2 Prepared Emergencies

A prepared emergency describes a situation where the crew is confronted with

an emergency receiving previous indications about the pending emergency

situation.

A prepared emergency therefore allows for specific preparations of the aircraft,

inter-crew communication, advice to and from other parties and briefings of crew and passengers.

For prepared emergencies a plan of action can be worked out by the crew according to the specific situation.

Example: Emergency evacuation, following an in-flight cabin fire.
fragen.frage_en: What distinguishes a "prepared emergency" from an "unprepared emergency" according to OM-A?
antworten_en: The prepared emergency is planned in the OFP, the unprepared is not
The prepared emergency only occurs on the ground
With the prepared emergency there are prior indications that allow preparation, briefings and an action plan
The unprepared emergency only affects the cabin
fragen.erklaerung_en: A prepared emergency announces itself and allows specific preparations and briefings; an unprepared emergency occurs with little or no warning.

fragen.frage: Welches Beispiel nennt das OM-A für eine unprepared emergency?
antworten: Evakuierung nach einem Kabinenfeuer im Flug
Engine-Ausfall im Reiseflug mit anschliessender Diversion
Fahrwerksproblem mit geplanter Notlandung
Runway Excursion nach dem Landing mit strukturellem Schaden
fragen.erklaerung: Als unprepared emergency nennt das OM-A die Runway Excursion nach dem Landing mit strukturellem Schaden; die Evakuierung nach Kabinenfeuer ist das Beispiel für eine prepared emergency.
fragen.zitat: Example: Runway excursion after aircraft landing, leading to structural damage to the aircraft.
kontext:
8.3.21.1.1 Unprepared Emergencies

An unprepared emergency describes a situation where the crew is confronted with an emergency receiving no or very little previous indications about the pending emergency situation. An unprepared emergency must be dealt with on

short notice and with virtually no possibility for particular preparations.
For unprepared emergencies general rules and guide lines and the contents of general briefings (e.g. received during crew briefing after check-in) must be applied.

Example: Runway excursion after aircraft landing, leading to structural damage

to the aircraft.
fragen.frage_en: Which example does OM-A give for an unprepared emergency?
antworten_en: Evacuation after a cabin fire in flight
Engine failure in cruise with subsequent diversion
Landing gear problem with planned emergency landing
Runway excursion after landing with structural damage
fragen.erklaerung_en: OM-A gives the runway excursion after landing with structural damage as an unprepared emergency; evacuation after a cabin fire is the example for a prepared emergency.

kontext:
8.3.21.2 RAAR PPAA FORD NITS

Whenever for technical or operational reasons during a flight abnormal or emergency procedures must be applied all company policies remain intact.
Abnormal and emergency procedures consist of four major phases:

R ecognition

A nalysis

A ction

R eassessment

During the application of abnormal and emergency procedures the Crew Resource Management (CRM) becomes, compared with normal operations, an even more crucial component. Therefore, the Commander (CMD) must concentrate with the highest priority on the assessment and distribution of its human and technical resources and to constantly reevaluate and optimize his decisions. The crew must prevent itself from any form of actionist behavior and uncoordinated or unfocused dealing with the problem at hand.
Whenever confronted with an emergency or abnormal situation, the first priority lies in the proper flying and monitoring of the aircraft.
Crew duties must be distributed clearly, basically the following sequence applies:
P ower the PF takes the initiative. Check thrust and order appropriate

setting for the engine(s) operating normally P erformance check configuration and minimum maximum speed

A nalysis both pilots shall assess the situation, where the lead of the

analyze lies with the Pilot Monitoring (PM)

A ction action shall be taken according to emergency abnormal

checklist, OM-B abnormal operation, flight procedures and knowledge

Use company channels and co-operate as soon as possible with the cabin crew.
Create favorable conditions for approach and landing by e.g:

requesting ATC assistance (Priority, Emergency)

careful selection of landing airport with suitable weather conditions, approach aids, runway as applicable

For the abnormal operation helvetic uses abnormal and emergency checklists.
All checklists are named.
When the situation changes to the worse the aim for the safety of the aircraft, its passengers, crew and cargo become the only operational goal.
If this goal can no longer be achieved by the use of the helvetic Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), diversion from these published procedures will be accepted. Any diversion from published procedures for the safety of the aircraft, its passengers, crew and cargo must be exercised only after due consideration by the crew (i.e. no matter how inconvenient such a decision might be for either or both helvetic and passengers).
If the helvetic Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) seem no longer adequate to deal with the situation at hand, an emergency must be declared.
As a general guideline, a declaration of an emergency or urgency can be evaluated and communicated to ATC as follows:
EICAS WARNING land at the nearest suitable airport:

antworten_en: Recognition, Analysis, Action, Reassessment

Recognition, Assessment, Action, Report
Review, Analysis, Assignment, Reassessment
fragen.erklaerung_en: Abnormal and emergency procedures consist of the four phases Recognition, Analysis, Action, Reassessment.

fragen.frage: Was ist die notwendige Voraussetzung, damit TCAS ein anderes Flugzeug erkennen kann?
antworten: Das andere Flugzeug muss ADS-B Out besitzen
Das andere Flugzeug muss einen korrekten Transpondercode senden (Mode C oder Mode S)
Beide Flugzeuge müssen auf derselben ATC-Frequenz sein
Das andere Flugzeug muss auf dem Wetterradar sichtbar sein
fragen.erklaerung: TCAS kann nur Flugzeuge erkennen, die einen korrekten Transpondercode senden; Voraussetzung ist der Betrieb des Transponders in Mode C oder Mode S.
fragen.zitat: The Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) can only detect aircraft which transmit a correct transponder code.
kontext:
8.3.6.1 General

The Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) is a technology which found its way into aviation during the late nineties of the past century. The motivation for its introduction has been the desire for an improvement of flight safety in an increasing traffic density, especially around major hubs. Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) addresses the problem through recognition and avoidance of potential hazard of in-flight collisions. It does neither replace traffic separation by Air Traffic Control (ATC) nor the sharp look-out of the flight crew whenever visibility permits. It does, however, support the flight crew in situations when the visual recognition of conflicting traffic is impaired (e.g. IMC conditions, night, traffic from dead-angle positions). It also assists in decision-making about the necessary correcting actions when a traffic conflict starts to develop.
Flight crews shall therefore use the Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) at all times. Nevertheless, they should bear in mind that several problems and limitations of the system have been identified during the first years of implementation. Future improvements in hardware and software are to be expected.
Necessary prerequisite to the function of any Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) equipment is the operation of the transponder in Mode C or Mode S.
In other words:
The Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) can only detect aircraft which transmit a correct transponder code.

It should be noted that Traffic Collision Avoidance System Mark II (TCAS II) is not

capable of accurately resolving the bearing and heading of conflicting traffic.
Traffic Advisory (TA) information for conflicting traffic is limited to vertical avoidance manoeuvres.
fragen.frage_en: What is the necessary prerequisite for TCAS to detect another aircraft?
antworten_en: The other aircraft must have ADS-B Out
The other aircraft must transmit a correct transponder code (Mode C or Mode S)
Both aircraft must be on the same ATC frequency
The other aircraft must be visible on the weather radar
fragen.erklaerung_en: TCAS can only detect aircraft transmitting a correct transponder code; the prerequisite is operation of the transponder in Mode C or Mode S.

antworten: Nur im kontrollierten Luftraum

Nur unterhalb FL 100
fragen.erklaerung: Flight Crews müssen TCAS zu jeder Zeit verwenden, auch wenn das System Einschränkungen hat.
