fragen.frage: Eine RA und eine gleichzeitige ATC-Anweisung widersprechen sich. Was gilt?
antworten: Der ATC-Anweisung ist zu folgen
Der Commander entscheidet nach Sichtkontakt
Die Höhe ist zu halten, bis der Konflikt geklärt ist
Der TCAS-RA ist zu folgen
fragen.erklaerung: Bei widersprüchlichen Anweisungen von RA und ATC muss die Anweisung des TCAS befolgt werden.
fragen.zitat: If an instruction to manoeuvre is received simultaneously from a Resolution Advisory (RA) and from ATC, and both instructions are in conflict, the advice given by the Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) must be followed.
kontext:
8.3.6.4 Reaction to TCAS TA and TCAS RA

Traffic Advisories (TA) A Traffic Advisory (TA) is intended to alert the flight crew that a Resolution Advisory (RA), requiring a change in flight path, may follow.
For detailed actions and callouts refer to type specific OM-B.

Resolution Advisories (RA) A Resolution Advisory (RA) is intended to advise pilots of the vertical manoeuvre they should carry out in order to achieve or maintain adequate separation from an established threat.
The manoeuvres shall follow the indication of the advisory and never be made in a direction opposite to that given by the system.

If an instruction to manoeuvre is received simultaneously from a Resolution Advisory (RA) and from ATC, and both instructions are in conflict, the advice given by the Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) must be followed.

Note: Visually acquired traffic may not be the same traffic causing an RA.
The visual perception of an encounter may be misleading, particularly at night.

Whenever a Resolution Advisory (RA) requires a climb while the aircraft is in landing configuration, a go-around shall be initiated.

It is emphasized that the Traffic Collision Avoidance System Mark II (TCAS II) relies upon information received from the transponders of the surrounding

aircraft. Resolution Advisories (RA) will only be generated if both the receiving

aircraft and the potential intruder are transmitting transponder signals in mode C or higher. The equipment is not capable of resolving with complete accuracy the

bearing, heading or vertical rates of intruding aircraft. Pilots should therefore not

attempt to manoeuvre on the basis of the system display.

For detailed actions and callouts refer to type specific OM-B.
fragen.frage_en: An RA and a simultaneous ATC instruction conflict. What applies?
antworten_en: The ATC instruction is to be followed
The Commander decides after visual contact
The altitude is to be maintained until the conflict is resolved
The TCAS RA is to be followed
fragen.erklaerung_en: In case of conflicting instructions from RA and ATC, the TCAS instruction must be followed.

Die RA als echt behandeln und sofort handeln
Den TCAS-Modus auf TA ONLY wählen

kontext:
8.3.6.5 Unwanted Warnings

Unwanted (i.e. false or nuisance) warnings may be received during normal, safe operation due to the limitations of the Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS).
Even if TCAS Traffic Advisories (TA) and TCAS Resolution Advisories (RA) are suspected to be nuisance or false advisories,
they shall be treated as genuine because it is difficult to evaluate if the traffic is of an existing danger in a short time.
Therefore, in any case immediate action is required by the flight crew.
fragen.frage_en: The crew suspects that an RA is a nuisance warning. How must it react?
antworten_en: Ignore the RA and inform ATC
First establish visual contact and only then act
Treat the RA as genuine and act immediately
Select TCAS mode TA ONLY
fragen.erklaerung_en: Even suspected nuisance or false advisories are to be treated as genuine, as the danger can hardly be assessed in the short time available.

fragen.frage: Welche maximale Vertikalgeschwindigkeit gilt innerhalb 1000 ft der Cleared Altitude, wenn potenziell konfliktierender Verkehr vorhanden ist?

1000 fpm
2000 fpm

fragen.zitat: 1000 FPM in the presence of potentially conflicting traffic when within 1000 feet of the cleared altitude
kontext:
8.3.2.21.2 TCAS

The rate of climb or descent shall be selected based on operational conditions.
Given the widespread use of collision avoidance systems (ACAS II), the rate of climb or descent must be closely monitored to ensure it does not exceed: 1500 FPM when within 2000 feet of the cleared altitude

1000 FPM in the presence of potentially conflicting traffic when within 1000

feet of the cleared altitude

When passing 2000 feet before the cleared altitude or flight level and the rate exceeds 1500 FPM:

the PM shall call out "APPROACHING ALTITUDE FLIGHT LEVEL."

the PF will then take corrective action and respond with "CHECKED."

Note: The directive to make a call at 2000 feet is based on European Airspace recommendations. These guidelines advise reducing the vertical speed

to a maximum of 1500 feet per minute (FPM) to prevent unnecessary

Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) alerts caused by high closure rates.

These rate restrictions do not apply during departure when climbing to the initial

cleared altitude or flight level, as defined in the SID or departure clearance.

antworten_en: 500 fpm
1500 fpm
1000 fpm

kontext:
8.3.6.3 Avoidance of Aircraft Collision

The see-and-avoid strategy with a careful look out is a basic element for the avoidance of collisions, regardless of advanced aircraft operations and more sophisticated ground and in-flight devices. Thus, whenever weather conditions permit, it is the duty of the flight crew to keep a sharp look out.
The flight crew shall organize the flight deck work in a way that at least one crew member may fulfill this requirement. The ACAS II (TCAS) indication must be used for assistance. It must, however, be understood that the ACAS II indication is limited to aircraft with an operating transponder. That may exclude the indication of other traffic (e.g. balloons, gliders).
Flight crew members must keep “head down work” to a minimum: in the vicinity of an aerodrome

during descent to an aerodrome

during climb out from an aerodrome

in areas where the traffic is dense

An early engagement of the autopilot is required in order to facilitate the look out.
Irrespective of the type of clearance received from ATC a look out for conflicting traffic in VMC is an absolute necessity.
Traffic information given by ATC is of great value. It must, however, always be

kept in mind that ATC information includes known traffic only and therefore may be incomplete.
In order to protect the eyes from the sun, only the use of sunglasses and sun visors is permitted.

The use of objects restricting the look out is prohibited during

flight.

kontext:
8.3.9 Wake Turbulence

Wake turbulence is generated by air exchange due to the pressure differential between the lower and upper surface of the wing. This exchange causes counter rotating vortices trailing from the outer wing tips. The larger the aircraft the larger are the vortices. The wake of a large aircraft may require large control inputs on an aircraft flying in the area behind it. These control inputs may exceed the roll control capability of the following aircraft. The flight crew must be aware of the location of the vortex flow generated by a preceding aircraft and adjust his flight path accordingly.
Tests with large and heavy aircraft have shown that the vortex flow field – in a plane cutting through the wake at any point downstream – covers an area about twice the wing span in width and one wing span in depth. The vortices from the two tips remain spaced and will drift with the wind. The vortices will sink with a rate of descent of 400 – 500 fpm. There is a tendency that the vortices will level off at about 800 – 1 000 ft below the flight path. Vortex strength diminishes with time and distance behind the aircraft.
Vortex generation will begin on rotation when the nose wheel lifts off the ground and ends, when the nose wheel touches down on landing.

In conditions with very weak or calm winds, the remaining vortices from a landing aircraft may persist up to 5 minutes or even longer.
All this has prompted National Aviation Authorities (NAA) and ICAO to establish minimum separation criteria.

OM-A 8 Operating Procedures

ICAO Definitions The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) classifies aircraft into wake turbulence categories based on their maximum certificated take-off mass (MTOM) and the strength of the wake vortices they generate.
Category MTOM Examples Light (L) 7.000 kg Cessna 172 Medium (M) 7.000 kg - 136.000 kg Embraer E-Jets Heavy (H) (1) 136.000 kg Boeing 747 Super (J) exceptionally strong wake turbulence Airbus A380

Note 1: Some types like the Boeing 757, despite having an MTOM below 136.000 kg, are treated as Heavy due to their strong wake turbulence.

Note: In the United Kingdom the aircraft series Boeing 707, DC-8, VC-10 and IL-62 are considered medium (M) and shall be announced as such in the initial contact with ATC. However, this regulation does not affect the composition of flight plans which shall be completed in accordance with the ICAO wake turbulence categorisation.

ICAO Wake Turbulence Separation Leading

light 8 NM 4 minutes

heavy 4 NM 2 minutes

light 6 NM 3 minutes

medium medium 3 NM 2 minutes light 4 NM 2 minutes

RECAT-EU Defintions For RECAT-EU definitions refer to:
Route Manual Tool – Europe Airway Manual – Air Traffic Control – Air Traffic Control Data Europe – RECAT EU Note: Embraer 190/195-E1 are classified as Lower Medium (CAT-E).
Embraer 190/195-E2 are classified as Upper Medium (CAT-D).

Additional Information Apart from the above ICAO or RECAT standards for vortex separation, the controller or the flight crew may arrange for a larger separation to compensate for calm conditions or for other terrestrial factors, which might enforce or retain the vortex energy for a longer time. The same may apply for operations into parallel or near parallel runways, where in crosswind situations the danger may exist, that vortices are encountered from a preceding aircraft approaching or departing from the parallel runway.
On the other hand separation may be reduced in strong crosswind conditions when operating into or out of single runway environments.
A departing aircraft will not be permitted to commence take-off until the preceding departing aircraft has crossed the end of the runway-in-use or has started a turn or until all preceding landing aircraft are clear of the runway-in-use.
A landing aircraft will not be permitted to cross the beginning of the runway on its final approach until the preceding departing aircraft has crossed the end of the

runway-in-use, or has started a turn, or until all preceding landing aircraft are clear of the runway-in-use.
More information can be found in OM-C Chapter Rules and Regulation.
In case adequate separation cannot be provided or when vortices are

encountered despite adequate separation, the following should be remembered:

during approach and landing behind a vortex generating aircraft, landing

should be aimed at a touch down point at the runway past the touch down

point of the heavier aircraft – if runway length permits

when taking-off, the lift-off point of the preceding aircraft should be remembered; if possible arrangement shall be made for a lift-off point well

before the lift-off point of the preceding aircraft; if this cannot be done,

delaying the take-off for some seconds – depending upon the size of the preceding aircraft and wind conditions on ground may be considered

when approaching behind a vortex generating aircraft, it should be realized,

that flying above the flight path of the preceding aircraft means to avoid the vortex zones – at least until short before touch down.

Mental preparation to abandon the approach using proper Operations Manual OM-B technique including use of maximum thrust setting is important.

8.3.9 Wake Turbulence

Wake turbulence is generated by air exchange due to the pressure differential between the lower and upper surface of the wing. This exchange causes counter rotating vortices trailing from the outer wing tips. The larger the aircraft the larger are the vortices. The wake of a large aircraft may require large control inputs on an aircraft flying in the area behind it. These control inputs may exceed the roll control capability of the following aircraft. The flight crew must be aware of the location of the vortex flow generated by a preceding aircraft and adjust his flight path accordingly.
Tests with large and heavy aircraft have shown that the vortex flow field – in a plane cutting through the wake at any point downstream – covers an area about twice the wing span in width and one wing span in depth. The vortices from the two tips remain spaced and will drift with the wind. The vortices will sink with a rate of descent of 400 – 500 fpm. There is a tendency that the vortices will level off at about 800 – 1 000 ft below the flight path. Vortex strength diminishes with time and distance behind the aircraft.
Vortex generation will begin on rotation when the nose wheel lifts off the ground and ends, when the nose wheel touches down on landing. In conditions with very weak or calm winds, the remaining vortices from a landing aircraft may persist up to 5 minutes or even longer.

kontext:
8.3.9.1 En-route Wake Turbulence

En-route, the vortices evolves in altitudes at which the rate of decay leads to a typical persistence of 2-3 minutes, with a typical sink rate of about 400ft/min.
Wakes will also be transported by wind.
Considering the high operating air speeds in cruise and the standard 1000 ft vertical separation in RVSM airspace,
wake turbulence can be encountered up to 25 nautical miles (NM) behind the generating airplane. The most significant encounters are reported within a distance of 15 NM.

However, no specific horizontal wake turbulence separation minima are detailed within PANS-ATM for en-route flight, with states utilising procedural or surveillance-based separation minima.
The encounters are mostly reported by pilots as sudden and unexpected events.
The awareness of hazardous traffic configuration and risk factors is therefore of particular importance to anticipate, avoid and manage possible wake encounters.
In the en-route phase of flight, three major factors contribute to increase the likelihood of wake turbulence: crossing traffic situation: In the case that crossing traffic is climbing or descending in proximity (either the generating or following airplane), the wake generated might cross the follower’s trajectory with minimum time for decay, so stronger wake turbulence might be encountered

thermal tropopause altitude: Wake vortex decays more slowly below the tropopause where there is therefore an increased risk of encountering

severe wake turbulence weight of the generating airplane: Heavier airplane types generate stronger wake vortices and are likely to induce more severe wake turbulence encounters, especially for smaller airplane types

The typical hazardous trajectory crossing configurations are the following. They

are shown hereafter in a vertical plane, although the respective flight path might

also be crossing on the horizontal plane. When crossing horizontally, the lower

the crossing angle the higher the wake effect. See the following examples.

kontext:
8.3.9.1.4 Precautionary Measurements and Reactions

The variability in the generator airplane rate of climb or descent makes it quite difficult to estimate exactly where the vortex is. Consequently, during the en- route phase of flight, pilots should expect possible wake encounters when other traffics in proximity appear to be on similar tracks ahead, crossing above your level, climbing or descending ahead through your flight path, while wind direction is likely to move the wake towards your trajectory.
As precautionary measures, operators and pilots should be aware that: when possible, condensation trails should be used to visualise wakes and estimate if their flight path brings them across

more attention should be given when flying below the tropopause altitude, as the likelihood of wake encounter increases. The tropopause altitude varies (between days, between locations) and can be found on meteorological charts
upwind lateral offset should be used if the risk of a wake encounter is suspected,

when allowed by airspace regulations or via specific ATC approval. Also, a change of FL to cross “HEAVY” or “SUPER” traffics from above can be used when feasible and authorised by ATC

In case of a wake encounter, pilots should: be aware that experience has demonstrated that if the pilot reacts at the first

roll motion, when in the core of the vortex, the roll motion could be potentially amplified by this initial piloting action be aware that some in-flight incidents have demonstrated that pilot inputs may exacerbate the unusual attitude condition with rapid roll control

reversals carried out in an “out of phase” manner

be aware that if the autopilot is engaged, intentional disconnection can

complicate the scenario, and the autopilot will, in most cases, facilitate the recovery

try to avoid large rudder deflections that can create important lateral

accelerations, which could then generate very large forces on the vertical

stabiliser that may exceed the structural resistance. Although some recent aircraft types are protected by fly-by-wire systems, typically, the use of the

rudder does not reduce the severity of the encounter nor does it improve the ease of recovery

make use of specific guidance in the OM-B where available

Reduce speed to turbulence penetration speed and disengage the autopilot
Descend 200 ft below the flight path of the generator
Fly an upwind lateral offset
fragen.erklaerung_en: If a wake risk is suspected, an upwind lateral offset should be flown if permitted; alternatively an FL change to cross a heavy/super from above.

Sie können grosse Querbeschleunigungen und Kräfte auf das Seitenleitwerk erzeugen, die dessen strukturelle Festigkeit überschreiten
Sie deaktivieren den Yaw Damper dauerhaft
Sie verstärken den Abwind des Wirbels auf den Höhenruderbereich
fragen.erklaerung: Grosse Seitenruderausschläge können wichtige Querbeschleunigungen und sehr grosse Kräfte auf das Seitenleitwerk erzeugen, die die strukturelle Festigkeit übersteigen können.
fragen.zitat: try to avoid large rudder deflections that can create important lateral accelerations,
kontext:
8.3.9.1.4 Precautionary Measurements and Reactions

The variability in the generator airplane rate of climb or descent makes it quite difficult to estimate exactly where the vortex is. Consequently, during the en- route phase of flight, pilots should expect possible wake encounters when other traffics in proximity appear to be on similar tracks ahead, crossing above your level, climbing or descending ahead through your flight path, while wind direction is likely to move the wake towards your trajectory.
As precautionary measures, operators and pilots should be aware that: when possible, condensation trails should be used to visualise wakes and estimate if their flight path brings them across

more attention should be given when flying below the tropopause altitude, as the likelihood of wake encounter increases. The tropopause altitude varies (between days, between locations) and can be found on meteorological charts

upwind lateral offset should be used if the risk of a wake encounter is suspected, when allowed by airspace regulations or via specific ATC approval. Also, a change of FL to cross “HEAVY” or “SUPER” traffics from above can be used when feasible and authorised by ATC

In case of a wake encounter, pilots should: be aware that experience has demonstrated that if the pilot reacts at the first

roll motion, when in the core of the vortex, the roll motion could be potentially amplified by this initial piloting action be aware that some in-flight incidents have demonstrated that pilot inputs may exacerbate the unusual attitude condition with rapid roll control

reversals carried out in an “out of phase” manner

be aware that if the autopilot is engaged, intentional disconnection can

complicate the scenario, and the autopilot will, in most cases, facilitate the recovery

try to avoid large rudder deflections that can create important lateral

accelerations,

which could then generate very large forces on the vertical

stabiliser that may exceed the structural resistance. Although some recent aircraft types are protected by fly-by-wire systems, typically, the use of the

rudder does not reduce the severity of the encounter nor does it improve the ease of recovery

make use of specific guidance in the OM-B where available
fragen.frage_en: Why should large rudder inputs be avoided during a wake vortex encounter?
antworten_en: They automatically trigger a stall warning
They can generate large lateral accelerations and loads on the vertical stabiliser that exceed its structural strength
They permanently deactivate the yaw damper
They amplify the vortex downwash on the elevator area
fragen.erklaerung_en: Large rudder inputs can generate significant lateral accelerations and very large loads on the vertical stabiliser that can exceed its structural strength.

fragen.frage: Wie ist vorzugehen, wenn unter FL 100 länger dauernde Head-down-Arbeit (z.B. FMS-Programmierung) nötig ist?
antworten: Der PF erledigt sie, während der PM die Funkfrequenz übernimmt
Beide Piloten erledigen sie gemeinsam mit eingeschaltetem Autopilot
Die Aufgabe an den PM delegieren; ist das nicht möglich, einen Transfer of Controls erwägen
Sie ist unter FL 100 grundsätzlich verboten
fragen.erklaerung: Längere Head-down-Arbeit unter FL 100 wird an den PM delegiert, sonst ist ein Transfer of Controls zu erwägen; beide Piloten head down ist zu vermeiden.
fragen.zitat: the task shall be delegated to the PM. If not possible a transfer of controls shall be considered.
kontext:
8.3.2.20 Operation below FL100

A speed limitation of 250 KIAS must be observed below FL 100. Higher speeds can be accepted on ATC request only above 5000 ft MSL Flight Crews shall not ask for higher speeds below FL 100 by themselves. OM-B limitations must be observed.
If FMS programming or any other task requires "head down" for prolonged time

below FL 100
the task shall be delegated to the PM. If not possible a transfer of controls shall be considered.

A state of both pilots "head down" shall be avoided.
When flying below FL 100 the PF shall closely observe aircraft inputs and be able to intervene immediately. This shall be accomplished by putting hands on

thrust levers and on or close to the control column if no other task is being

performed.

However, during takeoff, both hands shall be placed on the control column by the

PF after V1 until 400ft AAE.

During manual flight the PM shall not hinder the PF in making any inputs, but he shall be ready to take over controls at anytime (e.g. placing his hands close to

the controls).
fragen.frage_en: What is the procedure if prolonged head-down work (e.g. FMS programming) is required below FL 100?
antworten_en: The PF does it while the PM takes over the radio
Both pilots do it together with the autopilot engaged
Delegate the task to the PM; if that is not possible, consider a transfer of controls
It is generally prohibited below FL 100
fragen.erklaerung_en: Prolonged head-down work below FL 100 is delegated to the PM, otherwise a transfer of controls is to be considered; both pilots head down is to be avoided.

fragen.frage: Unter welcher Bedingung darf mit ATC eine höhere als die Standard-Holding-Speed verhandelt werden?
antworten: Wenn Holding in Clean Configuration bei der zugewiesenen Speed nicht möglich ist und die Limiten nicht der Hindernisfreiheit dienen
Immer, wenn dadurch Fuel gespart wird
Nur oberhalb FL 140
Nur in Notfällen nach Mayday-Erklärung
fragen.erklaerung: Ist Holding clean nicht möglich und dienen die Limiten nicht der Hindernisfreiheit, kann eine höhere Holding-Speed mit ATC verhandelt werden.
fragen.zitat: a higher than standard holding speed may be negotiated with ATC.
kontext:
8.3.2.23 Holding Pattern, Procedure Turns

For holding procedures and procedure-turns refer to the Operations Manual OM-C. In holding patterns and procedure turns the rate of descent shall not exceed 1500 fpm.
Great attention shall be paid to the compliance with the holding speed limitations.
For local regulations refer to the Operations Manual OM-C.
If unable to comply (i.e. when holding in a clean configuration is not possible at the assigned speeds) and if the limitations are not in force for the purpose of obstacle clearance
a higher than standard holding speed may be negotiated with ATC.

For the timing of a holding pattern refer to the Operations Manual OM-C (Route Manual). When a clearance is received specifying the time of departure from the holding fix, the flight crew shall adjust the pattern within the limits of the established holding procedure in order to leave the fix as near to the time specified as practicable.
Corrections shall be made in both heading and timing to compensate for the effects of wind. A correction shall also be made if the entry speed was excessive due to an unexpected holding clearance.
Turning to the inbound leg of a holding pattern not utilizing the FMS, a 90o – 45o interception shall be flown.
Holdings and procedure turns should be flown with 25° bank.
fragen.frage_en: Under what condition may a higher than standard holding speed be negotiated with ATC?
antworten_en: If holding in clean configuration at the assigned speed is not possible and the limits are not for obstacle clearance
Whenever fuel is saved as a result
Only above FL 140
Only in emergencies after a Mayday declaration
fragen.erklaerung_en: If holding clean is not possible and the limits are not for obstacle clearance, a higher holding speed may be negotiated with ATC.

Die Clearance ablehnen, da Holdings nur mit Standard-Timing geflogen werden

fragen.frage: Ab wann ist der Commander (CMD) gemäss OM-A für den Betrieb und die Sicherheit des Flugzeugs (operation and safety of the airplane) verantwortlich?
antworten: Ab dem Moment, in dem das Flugzeug erstmals zum Taxi vor dem Take-off bereit ist, bis zum endgültigen Stillstand mit abgestellten Engines
Ab dem Check-in der Crew bis zum Check-out
Ab dem Schliessen der Türen bis zum Öffnen der Türen nach dem Flug
Ab dem Betreten des Flugzeugs bis zum Verlassen des Flugzeugs
fragen.erklaerung: Für "operation and safety of the airplane" gilt der Zeitraum ab Taxi-Bereitschaft bis zum Stillstand mit abgestellten Engines. Die anderen Zeiträume betreffen Crew, Personen an Bord bzw. die Sicherheit von Crew, Passagieren und Cargo.
fragen.zitat: He is responsible, from the moment the airplane is first ready to move for the purpose of taxiing prior to take-off until the moment it finally comes to rest at the end of the flight and the engines used as primary propulsion units are shut down
kontext:
1.4.1 Authority, Duties and Responsibilities of the Commander (CMD)

The Commander (CMD) exercises the final authority over the safe operation of the helvetic aircraft he is assigned to fly.
He is responsible, as soon as he arrives on board until he leaves the airplane at the end of the flight, for: the safety of all crew members, passengers and cargo

He is responsible to adapt the operationally applicable elements of the SSCC defined in OMM 1.1 to the given situation and implement them in a mission- focussed manner.

He is responsible, from the moment the airplane is first ready to move for the purpose of taxiing prior to take-off until the moment it finally comes to rest at the end of the flight and the engines used as primary propulsion units are shut down,

for: the operation and safety of the airplane

All persons on board the aircraft shall obey all lawful directions given by the Commander (CMD). The Commander (CMD) exercises command over all crew members:

from check-in until check-out for a flight or series of flights The Commander (CMD) has the final responsibility regarding

flight initiation according to 8.1.10 - Operational Flight Plan

continuation, termination or diversion of a flight according to 8.3.2.24 -

Meteorological Information.

OM-A Responsibilities

He exercises full command over all other persons on board of a helvetic aircraft: from the time the doors are closed for the initiation of a flight until the doors are opened after the completion of a flight

While exercising his authority the Commander (CMD) has the right to: give all commands he deems necessary for the purpose of ensuring the safety of the aircraft and of persons or property carried therein

to disembark any person or any part of the cargo, which, in his opinion, may represent a potential hazard to the safety of the aircraft or its occupants

not allow a person to be carried in the aircraft who appears to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs to the extent that the safety of the aircraft or its occupants is likely to be endangered

to refuse transportation of inadmissible passengers, deportees or persons in custody, if their carriage poses any risk to the safety of the aircraft or its occupants

OM-A Responsibilities
fragen.frage_en: From when is the Commander (CMD) responsible for the operation and safety of the airplane according to OM-A?
antworten_en: From the moment the aircraft is first ready to taxi before takeoff until final stop with engines shut down
From crew check-in until check-out
From door closing until door opening after the flight
From boarding the aircraft until leaving the aircraft
fragen.erklaerung_en: For "operation and safety of the airplane", the period from readiness to taxi until stop with engines shut down applies. The other periods relate to the crew, persons on board, or the safety of crew, passengers and cargo.

fragen.frage: Während welches Zeitraums übt der Commander (CMD) Befehlsgewalt über alle Crew Members aus?
antworten: Vom Schliessen bis zum Öffnen der Türen
Von Block off bis Block on
Von Check-in bis Check-out für einen Flug oder eine Serie von Flügen
Vom Beginn des Boardings bis zum Ende des Deboardings
fragen.erklaerung: Die Befehlsgewalt über die Crew beginnt mit dem Check-in und endet mit dem Check-out des Flugs bzw. der Flugserie.

The Commander (CMD) must: ensure that all passengers are briefed on the location of emergency exits and the location and use of relevant safety and emergency equipment

ensure that all operational procedures and checklists are complied with in accordance with the provisions of this Operations Manual (OM)

From block off to block on
From check-in to check-out for a flight or series of flights
From the start of boarding to the end of deboarding

fragen.frage: Ab wann hat der Commander (CMD) volle Befehlsgewalt (full command) über alle anderen Personen an Bord?

Ab Pushback bis zum Erreichen der Parkposition
Ab dem Schliessen der Türen zur Durchführung des Flugs bis zum Öffnen der Türen nach Abschluss des Flugs

fragen.zitat: He exercises full command over all other persons on board of a helvetic aircraft: from the time the doors are closed for the initiation of a flight until the doors are opened after the completion of a flight
kontext:
1.4.1 Authority, Duties and Responsibilities of the Commander (CMD)

The Commander (CMD) exercises the final authority over the safe operation of the helvetic aircraft he is assigned to fly.
He is responsible, as soon as he arrives on board until he leaves the airplane at the end of the flight, for: the safety of all crew members, passengers and cargo

He is responsible to adapt the operationally applicable elements of the SSCC defined in OMM 1.1 to the given situation and implement them in a mission- focussed manner.
He is responsible, from the moment the airplane is first ready to move for the purpose of taxiing prior to take-off until the moment it finally comes to rest at the end of the flight and the engines used as primary propulsion units are shut down, for: the operation and safety of the airplane

All persons on board the aircraft shall obey all lawful directions given by the Commander (CMD). The Commander (CMD) exercises command over all crew members:

from check-in until check-out for a flight or series of flights The Commander (CMD) has the final responsibility regarding

flight initiation according to 8.1.10 - Operational Flight Plan

continuation, termination or diversion of a flight according to 8.3.2.24 -

Meteorological Information.

OM-A Responsibilities

He exercises full command over all other persons on board of a helvetic aircraft: from the time the doors are closed for the initiation of a flight until the doors are opened after the completion of a flight

While exercising his authority the Commander (CMD) has the right to: give all commands he deems necessary for the purpose of ensuring the safety of the aircraft and of persons or property carried therein

to disembark any person or any part of the cargo, which, in his opinion, may represent a potential hazard to the safety of the aircraft or its occupants

not allow a person to be carried in the aircraft who appears to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs to the extent that the safety of the aircraft or its occupants is likely to be endangered

to refuse transportation of inadmissible passengers, deportees or persons in custody, if their carriage poses any risk to the safety of the aircraft or its occupants

OM-A Responsibilities

The Commander (CMD) must: ensure that all passengers are briefed on the location of emergency exits and the location and use of relevant safety and emergency equipment

ensure that all operational procedures and checklists are complied with in accordance with the provisions of this Operations Manual (OM)

ensure that all crew members occupy their stations prior to take-off, final approach and landing

not permit any crew member to perform any activity during critical phases of flight except those for duties required for the safe operation of the aircraft

coordinate the work distribution within the crew to obtain a maximum of good airmanship for the conduct of the flight

ensure precise navigation and observation of minimum altitudes

comply with operating limitations and ensure the proper use and handling of the aircraft

enforce the strict use of all checklists (normal, abnormal, emergency checklists, MEL CDL refer to 8.1.11.1 - Aircraft Technical Log (ATL) - General Description

ensure that a flight is not commenced unless sufficient fuel is on board the

aircraft to complete the planned flight safely ensure that the amount of usable fuel remaining suffices to proceed to an airport where a safe landing can be made, with final reserve fuel

remaining

maintain close contact with the cabin crew in order to ensure that all requirements concerning cabin safety are being followed

ensure that the flight and technical logs are completed

ensure correctness of performance and mass balance calculations

comply with occurrence reporting policy according to 11.3 - Occurrence Reporting Policy

not permit a Flight Data Recorder (FDR) to be disabled, switched off or

erased during flight nor permit recorded data to be erased after flight in the event of an accident or incident subject to mandatory reporting

OM-A Responsibilities

not permit a Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) to be disabled or switched off during flight unless he believes that the recorded data, which otherwise would be erased automatically, should be preserved for incident or accident investigation

decide whether or not to accept an airplane with unserviceability allowed by the Minimum Equipment List (MEL) and Configuration Deviation List (CDL).
If the Commander (CMD) is dissatisfied with any aspect of the airworthiness or maintenance status of the airplane, he must reject an airplane prior to departure

ensure that the pre-flight inspection has been carried out

not operate an airplane unless he is qualified for duty in accordance with 5.2
- Flight Crew. (summary see 5.2.15 - Overview of Courses for Flight Crews)

ensure that relevant emergency equipment remains easily accessible for immediate use

immediately return his licence or certificate to the competent authority if the licence has been suspended or revoked

check the distribution tool at least once a week or before flight duty after a longer period away; read and acknowledge the relevant contents

check e-mail at least once a week and before flight or training duties, whichever results in more current information 1.4.1.1 1.4.1.1 Safety Management System (SMS)

Accountability

none

Authority

to initiate risk assessments

TEM (8.0.1.7 - Threat and Error Management (TEM))

FORD (8.0.1.6 - Decision Finding Process (FORD-Model))

Responsibility

to report according to OM-A 11

OM-A Responsibilities

Only if he believes that data otherwise automatically erased should be preserved for an incident or accident investigation
At the request of the First Officer to protect privacy
During controlled rest in cruise

fragen.frage: Der Commander wird im Flug incapacitated. Wer übernimmt das Kommando?
antworten: Immer der First Officer, unabhängig von anderen Piloten an Bord
Der dienstälteste Pilot an Bord, auch wenn er als Passagier reist
Der Senior Cabin Attendant bis zum Landing
Der First Officer, ausser es ist ein voll qualifizierter Pilot an Bord, der bei helvetic als Commander ernannt ist (z.B. LTC)
fragen.erklaerung: Grundsätzlich übernimmt der COP als Second in Command, ausser ein als CMD ernannter, voll qualifizierter Pilot wie ein LTC ist verfügbar.
fragen.zitat: the Copilot (COP – second in command) must take over command, unless there is a fully qualified and competent pilot available who has an appointment as Commander (CMD) with helvetic
kontext:
4.3.1 Flight Crew Member Incapacitation

If the Commander (CMD) of a flight becomes incapacitated in-flight the
Copilot (COP – second in command) must take over command, unless there is a fully qualified and competent pilot available who has an appointment as Commander (CMD) with helvetic
(e.g. Line Training Commander – LTC during line introduction).
fragen.frage_en: The Commander becomes incapacitated in flight. Who takes command?
antworten_en: Always the First Officer, regardless of other pilots on board
The most senior pilot on board, even if travelling as a passenger
The Senior Cabin Attendant until landing
The First Officer, unless a fully qualified pilot who is nominated as Commander at helvetic (e.g. LTC) is on board
fragen.erklaerung_en: As a rule the COP takes over as Second in Command, unless a fully qualified pilot nominated as CMD, such as an LTC, is available.

Die Position 2R
Die Position 2L
Der dienstälteste Cabin Attendant
fragen.erklaerung: Bei gleicher Qualifikation übernimmt standardmässig Position 2R; dies kann im Crew Briefing geändert werden.

antworten_en: Position 1L
Position 2R
Position 2L
The most senior Cabin Attendant

fragen.frage: Während LIFUS sitzt der LTC auf dem Jump Seat. Wer ist Commander des Flugs?
antworten: Der LTC, da er immer als Commander designiert ist
Der LTC, sofern er im Flight Assignment so eingetragen ist
Nicht der LTC, da er vom Jump Seat keinen Zugang zu den Flight Controls hat
Der Trainee, sobald er 10 Sektoren absolviert hat
fragen.erklaerung: Sitzt TRI oder LTC während LIFUS oder LOE auf dem Jump Seat, kann er mangels Zugang zu den Controls nicht CMD sein.
fragen.zitat: occupies the flight deck jump seat, he can not act as Commander (CMD) of the flight, since he has no access to the flight controls
kontext:
4.2.1 Flights with Two Pilots Qualified as Commander

If more than one flight crew member of the same crew holds the qualification for Commander (CMD) only one pilot is designated as Commander (CMD) of the flight.
The command of the flight is assigned on the flight assignment.
During any flight, other than:

training flights, or line flying under supervision, or

check flights and non-revenue flights

the CMD of the aircraft occupies the left hand seat on the flight deck.

OM-A 4 Crew Composition

This means that the CMD holding the qualification to operate in either pilot’s seat will act as Copilot (COP) on the right hand seat despite of the fact that he might be more experienced than the pilot on the left hand seat.

During: training flights

check flights

line flying under supervision

where the responsible instructor has access to the controls, the Type Rating Instructor (TRI) or the Line Training Commander (LTC) is always designated as the Commander (CMD) of the flight. He then may have to occupy the right hand seat in the flight deck.

During: line flying under supervision

Line Orientated Evaluation of Competence (LOE)

where the Type Rating Instructor (TRI) or the Line Training Commander (LTC)
occupies the flight deck jump seat, he can not act as Commander (CMD) of the flight, since he has no access to the flight controls.

When more than one flight crew member of the same crew holds the qualification for Commander (CMD) it is of the utmost importance to properly and clearly brief all other crew members about the actual chain of command. Any change in command during a flight shall be announced to all crew members in a clear

manner.

OM-A 4 Crew Composition
fragen.frage_en: During LIFUS the LTC sits on the jump seat. Who is Commander of the flight?
antworten_en: The LTC, as he is always designated as Commander
The LTC, provided he is entered as such in the Flight Assignment
Not the LTC, as he has no access to the flight controls from the jump seat
The trainee, as soon as he has completed 10 sectors
fragen.erklaerung_en: If a TRI or LTC sits on the jump seat during LIFUS or LOE, he cannot be CMD for lack of access to the controls.

antworten: Bis zum Erreichen des 65. Altersjahres
Bis zum Erreichen des 60. Altersjahres
Bis zum Erreichen des 63. Altersjahres
Bis zum Erreichen des 67. Altersjahres
fragen.erklaerung: Die Altersgrenze beträgt 65 Jahre, vorausgesetzt der Pilot fliegt in einer Multi-Pilot Crew.
fragen.zitat: may act as a pilot in commercial operations until reaching the age of 65, provided that he is:
kontext:
4.1.1.1 Licence Holders – Maximum Age

A helvetic flight crew member
may act as a pilot in commercial operations until reaching the age of 65, provided that he is:
a member of a multi-pilot crew
fragen.frage_en: Up to what age may a helvetic pilot fly in commercial operations, provided he is a member of a multi-pilot crew?
antworten_en: Until reaching the age of 65
Until reaching the age of 60
Until reaching the age of 63
Until reaching the age of 67
fragen.erklaerung_en: The age limit is 65 years, provided the pilot flies in a multi-pilot crew.

fragen.frage: Ein Pilot hat eine OML (Operational Multi-Pilot Limitation) auf seinem Medical. Welche Bedingung muss der andere Pilot unter anderem erfüllen?
antworten: Er darf keine OML haben und das 60. Altersjahr noch nicht erreicht haben
Er muss Commander mit mindestens 1000 h auf dem Typ sein
Er muss TRI oder LTC sein
Er darf das 55. Altersjahr noch nicht erreicht haben
fragen.erklaerung: Der andere Pilot muss voll qualifiziert auf dem Typ sein, keine OML haben und jünger als 60 Jahre sein.
fragen.zitat: when the other pilot is fully qualified on the relevant type of aircraft, is not subject to an OML and has not attained the age of 60 years
kontext:
4.1.1.2 Flight Crew Member other than full-time Employees

Flight crew members who are self-employed or working on a freelance or part time contract must hold the same qualifications and fulfill identical requirements

as every regularly employed flight crew member.
The total number of airplane types or variants for which a separate licence endorsement is required in commercial operations must not exceed two.

4.1.1.3 Flight Crew Member with Operational Multi-Pilot Limitation (OML)

Flight crew members with an OML on their medical certificate shall only operate a helvetic aircraft in multi-pilot operations

when the other pilot is fully qualified on

the relevant type of aircraft, is not subject to an OML and has not attained the

age of 60 years.

The flight crew member must report any non-standard restriction to the superior.

OM-A 4 Crew Composition
fragen.frage_en: A pilot has an OML (Operational Multi-Pilot Limitation) on his medical. Which condition, among others, must the other pilot meet?
antworten_en: He must have no OML and must not yet have reached the age of 60
He must be a Commander with at least 1000 h on type
He must be a TRI or LTC
He must not yet have reached the age of 55
fragen.erklaerung_en: The other pilot must be fully qualified on type, have no OML and be younger than 60 years.

fragen.frage: Ab wann darf ein unerfahrener Pilot nach Type Rating oder Command Course mit einem anderen unerfahrenen Piloten fliegen (eine der beiden Bedingungen)?
antworten: Nach 50 Flugstunden und 10 Sektoren innerhalb von 90 Tagen
Nach 100 Flugstunden und 20 Sektoren innerhalb von 60 Tagen
Nach 150 Flugstunden und 10 Sektoren innerhalb von 120 Tagen
Nach 100 Flugstunden und 10 Sektoren innerhalb einer Consolidation Period von 120 aufeinanderfolgenden Tagen
fragen.erklaerung: Alternativ gelten 150 Flugstunden und 20 Sektoren ohne Zeitlimit; gezählt wird ab dem LOE.
fragen.zitat: 100 flight hours and 10 sectors within a consolidation period of 120 consecutive days
kontext:
4.1.3.1.1 Flight Crew Members

The initial line flying shall not take place in a crew with another inexperienced pilot until he has completed:
100 flight hours and 10 sectors within a consolidation period of 120 consecutive days,

or

150 flight hours and 20 sectors (no time limit) Hours and sectors start counting after the Line Orientated Evaluation of Competence (LOE) following a type rating or command course.
fragen.frage_en: When may an inexperienced pilot after type rating or command course fly with another inexperienced pilot (one of the two conditions)?
antworten_en: After 50 flight hours and 10 sectors within 90 days
After 100 flight hours and 20 sectors within 60 days
After 150 flight hours and 10 sectors within 120 days
After 100 flight hours and 10 sectors within a consolidation period of 120 consecutive days
fragen.erklaerung_en: Alternatively, 150 flight hours and 20 sectors without time limit apply; counting starts from the LOE.

fragen.frage: Wie berechnet sich die Mindestanzahl Cabin Crew (neben dem Wert aus der Zertifizierung)?
antworten: Ein Cabin Crew Member pro 50 (oder Bruchteil von 50) installierten Passagiersitzen auf demselben Deck
Ein Cabin Crew Member pro 50 tatsächlich beförderten Passagieren
Ein Cabin Crew Member pro 40 installierten Passagiersitzen
Ein Cabin Crew Member pro Paar Notausgänge
fragen.erklaerung: Massgebend sind die installierten Sitze (1 pro 50 oder Bruchteil), bzw. der grössere Wert aus der Zertifizierung.
fragen.zitat: one cabin crew member for every 50, or fraction of 50, passenger seats installed on the same deck of the aircraft
kontext:
4.1.4 Cabin Crew Composition

The minimum number of cabin crew members is the greater of:
one cabin crew member for every 50, or fraction of 50, passenger seats installed on the same deck of the aircraft,

or number of cabin crew members established during the aircraft certification process for the aircraft cabin configuration used by helvetic

The cabin crew’s primary function is to perform duties in the interest of safety.
The minimum cabin crew complement for all flight phases on helvetic aircraft is stated in 4.1.9 - Minimum Crew Complement.
Note: This minimum cabin crew complement must be carried on all revenue flights with one or more passengers on board.

Each cabin crew member must fulfill the qualification requirements according to 5.3 - Cabin Crew No person shall accept an assignment to flight duty knowing that he is not qualified and fit for.

OM-A 4 Crew Composition
fragen.frage_en: How is the minimum number of cabin crew calculated (besides the value from certification)?
antworten_en: One cabin crew member per 50 (or fraction of 50) installed passenger seats on the same deck
One cabin crew member per 50 passengers actually carried
One cabin crew member per 40 installed passenger seats
One cabin crew member per pair of emergency exits
fragen.erklaerung_en: The installed seats are decisive (1 per 50 or fraction), or the greater value from certification.

4.1.9.1 Minimum Crew Complement – Normal Operation

For passenger carrying flights the minimum crew complement shall never be less than the values in the following table:

For all other flights not carrying passengers, the minimum crew complement shall never be less than the values in the following table:

Aircraft Minimum Flight Crew Minimum Cabin Crew E-Jet 2 0

antworten_en: 96 seats
110 seats
112 seats

fragen.frage: Wie viele Personen dürfen auf einem Non-Revenue Flight ohne Passagiere maximal zusätzlich zur Flight und Cabin Crew mitfliegen (ausserhalb von Trainingsflügen)?
antworten: Drei
Zwei
Vier
Sechs
fragen.erklaerung: Zusätzliche Personen (mit Duty Assignment und erweitertem Safety Briefing) sind auf drei begrenzt; bei Type-Rating- oder Upgrade-Training ist die Zahl der Trainees nicht begrenzt.
fragen.zitat: the number of persons in addition to the flight and cabin crew does not exceed three
kontext:
4.1.8.2 Other Crew Member during Non-Revenue Flights

For non-revenue flights not carrying passengers, other persons may be carried on board provided the person: is employed by helvetic or a subcontractor or customer (e.g. tour operator)

has a duty assignment for this flight (e.g. technician for trouble shooting, flight or service evaluation, positioning)

has received an extended safety briefing by the aircraft commander

and
the number of persons in addition to the flight and cabin crew does not exceed three.

Exception for Training Flights: during flight training for type ratings or upgradings to commander the number of trainees is not restricted

should a trainee not be employed by helvetic (e.g. third party training), he must previously demonstrate written proof concerning his adequate personal insurance

In any other case the additional person(s) must be considered as passengers.

Refer to 8.7.6 - Passengers on Non-Revenue Flights for additional

procedures.

OM-A 4 Crew Composition
fragen.frage_en: How many persons may fly in addition to the flight and cabin crew on a non-revenue flight without passengers (outside of training flights)?
antworten_en: Three
Two
Four
Six
fragen.erklaerung_en: Additional persons (with duty assignment and extended safety briefing) are limited to three; for type rating or upgrade training, the number of trainees is not limited.

fragen.frage: Welche Regel gilt gemäss OM-A für Supernumeraries?
antworten: Sie dürfen eine Required Cabin Crew Station besetzen, wenn der Jump Seat belegt ist
Sie gehören nicht zum Minimum Crew Complement und dürfen keine Uniform tragen, die sie als qualifizierte Crew Members erkennbar macht
Sie zählen zum Minimum Crew Complement, sofern sie eine Safety-Schulung haben
Sie gelten immer als Passagiere und brauchen keinen designierten Sitz
fragen.erklaerung: Supernumeraries sind nicht Teil der Minimum Crew, tragen keine Crew-Uniform und besetzen keine Required Cabin Crew Stations.
fragen.zitat: Supernumeraries are not part of the minimum crew complement as stated under 4.1.9 - Minimum Crew Complement. They shall not wear a uniform which may identify them to passengers as a qualified crew member
kontext:
4.1.11 Supernumeraries

A person in addition to the crew that is not a crew member, but is on board during commercial or non-commercial operations and is not classified as a passenger by the operator or the authority.

Such person is typically any of the following: an inspector, auditor or observer authorized by helvetic and the State to be on board the aircraft in the performance of his or her duties (e.g. CAA flight operations inspector, IOSA auditor, IOSA observer)

assigned to a passenger flight by helvetic to conduct certain customer service activities (e.g. serving beverages, conducting customer relations, selling tickets) in the cabin; not designated to perform any safety duties

any other individual that has a relationship with helvetic, is not classified as a passenger by the authority and authorised by helvetic and the State to be on board the aircraft (e.g. courier, contract coordinator, individual with operator required knowledge and abilities travelling to/from a duty assignment, company employee or dependent)

Non-operating crew members, company employees and employee dependents occupying passenger seats on passenger flights are considered as passengers.

Supernumeraries are not part of the minimum crew complement as stated under

4.1.9 - Minimum Crew Complement. They shall not wear a uniform which may identify them to passengers as a qualified crew member,

shall not occupy required cabin crew assigned stations and do not impede the cabin crew members in their duties.

A supernumerary shall be assigned a designated seat, which may be either a

jump seat or a passenger seat.

OM-A 4 Crew Composition
fragen.frage_en: Which rule applies to supernumeraries according to OM-A?
antworten_en: They may occupy a required cabin crew station if the jump seat is occupied
They are not part of the minimum crew complement and must not wear a uniform that identifies them as qualified crew members
They count toward the minimum crew complement provided they have safety training
They are always considered passengers and do not need a designated seat
fragen.erklaerung_en: Supernumeraries are not part of the minimum crew, do not wear a crew uniform and do not occupy required cabin crew stations.

fragen.frage: Welche Recent Experience muss ein Pilot für den Einsatz als Commander oder First Officer erfüllen?
antworten: Mindestens 3 Take-offs und 3 Landings als PF oder PM in den vorangehenden 60 Tagen
Mindestens 3 Take-offs und 3 Landings als PF in den vorangehenden 90 Tagen auf dem Typ (Flugzeug oder qualifizierter Simulator)
Mindestens 5 Sektoren als PF in den vorangehenden 90 Tagen
Mindestens 3 Take-offs und 3 Landings als PF in den vorangehenden 120 Tagen
fragen.erklaerung: Gefordert sind 3 Take-offs und 3 Landings als Pilot Flying innerhalb von 90 Tagen, im Flugzeug oder im Simulator Level CG, C oder D.
fragen.zitat: within the preceding 90 days, at least three take-offs and three landings as Pilot Flying (PF) in an aircraft or an approved flight simulator of the type to be used
kontext:
5.2.2 Recent Experience for Commanders

A pilot must not operate an aircraft as Commander (CMD) unless he has carried out,
within the preceding 90 days, at least three take-offs and three landings as Pilot Flying (PF) in an aircraft or an approved flight simulator of the type to be used.

The flight simulator must be acceptable to the National Aviation Authority (NAA) and qualified to level CG, C or D.
The period of 90 days may be extended up to a maximum of 120 days by line flying under the supervision of a Type Rating Instructor (TRI).
When the above-mentioned period is expired, a flight training including at least three take-offs and landings as Pilot Flying (PF) of an aircraft not carrying passengers or cargo or an equivalent simulator training must be accomplished.
The aircraft or flight simulator must be of the relevant type.
The responsibility for compliance with these requirements lies with the respective pilot. He must log the relevant data in a pilot’s logbook. For back-up, dispatch maintains an overview of each flight crew member’s recency.
In addition to the recent experience mentioned above, the following rules shall be applied:
If a Commander (CMD) is absent for more than 4 months, but still within the validity of the checks required according to OM-D 2.1.6, a Requalification Training (RQT) is required.
For the Requalification training refer to OM-D 2.1.9

kontext:
5.2.9 Low Visibility Operation (LVO)

To maintain a category II III (CAT II III) qualification pilots must have conducted a minimum of three approaches and landings using CAT II III procedures during the period between 2 EBT modules (real or simulated CAT II III approaches).
If a flight crew member is authorised to operate as pilot flying and pilot monitoring, the flight crew member shall complete the required number of approaches in each operating capacity.
If above mentioned requirements are not met a re-qualification has to be performed. For that purpose the approaches may be conducted during normal line operation as simulated CAT II III approaches.
However, recency for low visibility take-off and Cat II/III approaches is maintained by the recurrent training and checking.
If the commander was not previously qualified for Cat II III operations with an EASA operator,

the following minima apply until 100 hours or 40 route sectors (including line flying under supervision) have been achieved on type:
Cat II/III minimum RVR 100 m

Upgraders moving from the right onto the left seat (not being new on type) are not affected by this limitation. helvetic does not define a further increase of minima depending on the experience of flight crew members.

CAT II/III minimum RVR + 100 m until 100 hours or 40 sectors on type are reached
No CAT III operations during the first 6 months
fragen.erklaerung_en: For such Commanders, RVR + 100 m applies until 100 h or 40 sectors (incl. LIFUS); upgraders who are not new to the type are not affected.

kontext:
5.2.14 Flight Crew operating on more than one Type or Variant

Operation on more than one Variant

Assignments of crew members on different variants during one duty period shall be minimised as far as possible. However, a flight crew member is allowed to operate on more than one airplane variant during the same flight duty period with the following restrictions: before operating a different variant, a review of aircraft specific data (e.g. limitations, flight guidance panel layout) shall be done by the flight crew.

Note: The awareness briefing before departure is a good opportunity.

Additional limitations to operate on E2 and E1 variant:
flight crews with a flight duty workload of less than 40% shall not be planned to operate on the E2 and E1 variants concurrently

or the above limit may be superseded by special FOP approval, depending on the experience of concerned flight crew member (i.e. analysis on an individual basis required)

Note: The FOP approval is stored on “TEAM Flightops - General Personnel”.

Operation on more than one Type

Operator’s restriction: helvetic does not utilise flight crews that are concurrently qualified to operate aircraft of different types.

For different types the following provisions would apply:

A flight crew member may hold a maximum of two airplane type ratings used

under EASA Air Operations conform commercial operations.

Before the flight crew member commences conversion onto a new type he must have a minimum experience on the first type of at least:

150 block hours

3 months

one recurrent simulator training performed after the skill test

After completion of the initial Line Orientated Evaluation of Competence (LOE) on the new type, 50 hours flying or 20 sectors must be achieved solely on the

airplane of the new type.

For the operation of each type the recent experience requirements according to 5.2.2 - Recent Experience for Commanders and 5.2.4 - Copilots respectively, must be met.
There will be no flights on different types during the same calendar day.

fragen.erklaerung_en: Crews with less than 40 % flight duty workload are not deployed on E2 and E1 in parallel; FOP may approve exceptions individually.

kontext:
6.2.3 Alcohol and Intoxicating Liquids

A crew member and operations personnel other than crew members shall not:
consume alcohol less than 8 hours prior to the specified reporting time for any duty within operations

(e.g. flight duty, training or the commencement of standby duty)

commence any duty within operations (e.g. flight duty period) with a blood alcohol level in excess of (the lowest is applicable): 0.2 %o or 0,1 mg alcohol per litre respiratory air or the national statutory limits (zero alcohol)

consume alcohol during any duty within operations (e.g. flight duty, training or the commencement of standby duty)

Since the metabolism of alcohol in the blood is very slow, it is highly recommended that crew members refrain from the consumption of alcohol 16 hours before the expected commencement of flight duty, training or reserve duty (standby). As a matter of helvetic company policy, employees in uniform (e.g. crew members after termination of flight duty, deadheading crew members) shall not consume any alcoholic beverages.
The misuse of any intoxicating liquids is strictly prohibited for crew members and

operations personnel other than crew members.

fragen.zitat: Vaccination and Revaccination shall take place not less than 24 hours before commencement of flight duty, unless otherwise stated.
kontext:
6.1.2 Immunization

In accordance with the World Health Organization’s (WHO) International Health Regulations many countries prescribe vaccination of crew members and passengers against defined diseases, often specifying that such immunization is only required upon entry “after leaving or transiting infected areas”.
Each crew member scheduled for flight duty abroad must satisfy any requirement for vaccination, to have himself vaccinated in time, and to be able to produce – during his tour of duty – the appropriate WHO-approved “Certificate of Vaccination or Revaccination”.
Vaccination and Revaccination shall take place not less than 24 hours before commencement of flight duty, unless otherwise stated.

In case of strong reaction medical advice shall be obtained in view of a possible impairment of fitness for flight duty. No alcoholic beverages shall be consumed for a period of at least 24 hours after vaccination.

Vaccinations which may be obligatory and their validity:
Yellow fever (from 10 days after, for lifetime)

Vaccinations which are recommended and their validity:
Cholera (from 7 days until 6 months after vaccination)

Typhoid (from 7 days until 3 years after vaccination)

Poliomyelitis (after 3 vaccinations up to 10 years) Tetanus (after 3 vaccinations up to 10 years)

COVID-19(1) (from 1 to 2 weeks after the vaccination)

Note 1: Crew members must not be engaged in any safety relevant duty (e.g. flight duty) for a period of 48 hours after each dose of COVID-

19 vaccine. In case side effects persist for more than 48 hours following the vaccination, crew members shall consult their AME.

The waiting period shall be extended until the time when the side

effects completely disappear.

OM-A 6 Health Precautions

Malaria prophylaxis, though not immunization in the strict sense of the word, should be mentioned here; crew members scheduled for flight duty to malaria infected countries shall obtain, on the advice of their flight medical doctor, the appropriate medication and apply it as prescribed.
Note: Crew members shall be aware of the fact that there are many extremely dangerous diseases against which vaccination is not possible.

Only general rules may be given here for health-conscious behavior in foreign countries: observe strict hygiene in eating drinking (amoebic dysentery, brucellosis),

do not bathe in stagnant water (bilharziasis),

in infested (e.g., bush/jungle) areas, wear long sleeved shirts and long trousers to prevent or minimize bites by disease-carrying insects (filariasis, malaria, encephalitis, sleeping sickness) or by outright poisonous insects or animals (spiders, scorpions, snakes); use insect-repellant.

OM-A 6 Health Precautions

fragen.erklaerung_en: Vaccinations must be given at least 24 h before flight duty start; afterwards no alcohol for 24 h. For COVID-19 a 48 h ban applies.

7.1.6.1 Duty Hour Limitations

Any work, the entire duration of a flight, deadhead time (positioning), training and office duties, which a crew member performs on behalf of helvetic shall count as duty period.
Any duty by a crew member according to 7.1.14.2 - Recording of Duty, Flight Duty and Rest Periods by the Crew Member counts as duty time. helvetic shall ensure that the total duty period to which a crew member is assigned does not exceed: 190 duty hours in any 28 consecutive days, spread as evenly as practicable throughout this period

the Crew Member.

kontext:
7.1.7 Maximum Daily Flight Duty Period (FDP)

Any duty, including training and office duties, performed prior to a flight or prior to a series of flights (except standby – refer to 7.1.10 - Standby, Reserve and Duties at the Airport) shall count as Flight Duty Period (FDP). helvetic plans all crew members to report 60 minutes before scheduled time of departure of the first flight. This shall provide ample time allowing all crew members to perform safety related pre flight duties such as flight planning and preparation of the aircraft before departure (also valid for pre flight duties after a break – refer to split duty rules).
For line introduction and Line Orientated Evaluation of Competence (LOE) for flight crew and familiarization flights or line check for cabin crew, a reporting time of 75 minutes shall be planned.

Travel longer than 3 hours shall count fully as Flight Duty Period (FDP) if followed by a subsequent flight duty period.
For the maximum flight duty period for flight training refer to OM-D 3.4.8.

OM-A 7 Flight Time Limitations

kontext:
7.1.9 Split Duty

The maximum FDP specified in 7.1.7 - Maximum Daily Flight Duty Periode (FDP) may be increased due to a break on the ground by up to 50 of the break.
The conditions shall be in accordance with the following: the break on the ground shall count in full as FDP
the break on the ground within the FDP has a minimum duration of 3 consecutive hours

the break excludes the time required for post and pre-flight duties and travelling (longer than 15 minutes one way)

helvetic ensures that suitable accommodation is provided either for a break

of 6 hours or more or for a break that encroaches the window of circadian low (WOCL)

if only accommodation is provided, any time of the actual break exceeding 6

hours or any time of the break that encroaches the WOCL does not count for the extension of the FDP

if during the break of a split duty period the total travelling time in both

directions between the airport and accommodation exceeds 30 minutes, any travelling time in excess of the 30 minutes total shall be deducted from the break for the purpose of calculating the increased flight duty period

split duty shall not follow a reduced rest

At least 3 consecutive hours; increase by up to 50 % of the break
At least 4 consecutive hours; increase by up to 25 % of the break
fragen.erklaerung_en: The break counts fully as FDP, must last at least 3 h and allows an FDP increase of up to 50 % of the break.

fragen.frage: Wie lange muss die Minimum Rest Period vor einer FDP ab Home Base sein (ohne von helvetic gestellte Suitable Accommodation)?

kontext:
7.1.12.1 Minimum Rest at Home Base

The minimum rest which must be provided before undertaking a Flight Duty Period (FDP) starting at home base
shall be at least as long as the preceding duty period or 12 hours whichever is the greater.

However, if helvetic provides a suitable accommodation at home base, the minimum rest can be reduced to 10 hours duration or the preceding duty period, whichever is the greater. This applies only if the crew member does not rest at his residence, or temporary accommodation.
fragen.frage_en: How long must the minimum rest period before an FDP from home base be (without suitable accommodation provided by helvetic)?
antworten_en: At least as long as the preceding duty period or 12 hours, whichever is greater
At least as long as the preceding duty period or 10 hours, whichever is greater
Always exactly 12 hours
At least 11 hours
fragen.erklaerung_en: At home base, max(duty period, 12 h) applies; with suitable accommodation provided by helvetic it can be reduced to max(duty period, 10 h).

fragen.zitat: the opportunity of a 8 hours uninterrupted sleep possibility not affected by travel from airport to suitable accommodation

the minimum rest which must be provided before undertaking a Flight Duty Period (FDP) starting away from home base shall be at least as long as the preceding duty period or 10 hours whichever is the greater. In any case helvetic additionally has to ensure that every crew member has

and vice versa and other physiological needs (meals)

if the travelling time to the suitable accommodation is more than 30 minutes, the rest period shall be increased by twice the amount of difference of travelling time above 30 minutes

when helvetic elects to place a crew member for a long term period to a

base other than at home base (more than 30 days in a row), the same rest

time rules as for home base shall apply as described within

7.1.12.1 - Minimum Rest at Home Base

OM-A 7 Flight Time Limitations

7.1.13.1 Days Free of Duty per Month

helvetic plans all duty rosters to ensure that every crew member receives a
minimum of 7 local days free of duty within every single calendar month.

holidays, sickness, accident or military service. Days free of duty shall normally

be planned at home base.

kontext:
7.1.12.3 Increase in Minimum Rest when crossing Time Zones

kontext:
7.2.1 Modification of the Limits on Flight Duty, Duty or Rest Periods

During actual flight operation, which starts after the whole crew has reported for any duty, the Commander (CMD) shall have the possibility to modify the limits on flight duty, duty and rest periods in the event of conditions described as unforeseen circumstances.
The exercise of commander’s discretion shall be considered exceptional and shall be avoided at home base when standby or reserve crew members are available.
The conditions shall comply with the following: the maximum daily FDP which results after applying 7.1.7 - Maximum Daily Flight Duty Periode (FDP) or 7.1.9 - Split Duty may not be increased by more than 2 hours.

the maximum basic daily FDP that results after applying 7.1.7.1 - Maximum Daily FDP for Acclimatised Crew Members shall be used to calculate the limits of commander’s discretion, if commander’s discretion is applied to an FDP which has been extended under the provisions of 7.1.7.3 - Maximum Daily FDP for Acclimatised Crew Members with the Use of Extensions without In-flight Rest

if on the final sector within a FDP the allowed increase is exceeded because of unforeseen circumstances after take-off, the flight may continue to the planned destination or alternate aerodrome

the rest period following the FDP may be reduced but can never be less

than 10 hours

The commander shall consult all crew members on their alertness levels before deciding the modifications.
Additionally, he shall take due consideration of additional factors that might decrease a crew member’s alertness levels, such as:
WOCL encroachment

weather conditions

complexity of the operation and/or airport environment

airplane malfunctions or specifications

flight with training or supervisory duties

increased number of sectors

circadian disruption

individual conditions of affected crew members (time since awake, sleep- related factor, workload, etc.)

7.2.2 Duties in case of Modification of the Limits on Flight Duty, Duty or Rest Periods

helvetic will assess on a regular basis the series of pairings where commander’s

discretion has been exercised in order to be aware of possible inconsistencies in their rostering. The FRMS meeting monitors the amount of FTL modifications and other FTL exceedances via the BI tool according to 2.4.5.1.8 - FRMS Meeting.

The Commander (CMD) shall submit an IT report to helvetic flight operations

management whenever a limit on flight duty, duty or rest period has been

modified by his discretion or whenever a limitation as stated within this chapter has been violated in excess of one hour. This report shall be handled according

to OMM 7 Reporting Scheme.

Whenever the above-mentioned modification or a reported violation is beyond one hour, helvetic shall send a copy of the report to the competent authority not

later than 28 days after the event.

The RPO will monitor FTL exceedances and request reports from the commander, whenever a report is missing.

kontext:
10.0.5.2 The Tokyo Convention

The Tokyo convention of 1963 was introduced to civil aviation to ratify jurisdiction over what is often referred to as “Crime in the Air.” It assigns, by way of extended jurisdiction, the legal right of a state to apprehend, detain and punish offenders who commit crime in flight. This right should be seen in the same context as if the crime was committed in the streets of the cities in the state of registration of the aircraft.
The convention also clarifies and justifies the actions of the commander of a commercial flight to suppress the actions of passengers committing penal offences or actions that may otherwise jeopardize good order and discipline on

board.
The commander has powers of arrest and can delegate those powers to members of his crew and to passengers on the flight.

Since the Tokyo convention contains provisions with regard to the powers of the

aircraft commander and since the other two conventions are not directly related to the authority and duties of the commander, the next subjects only deal with the relevant provisions of the Tokyo convention.

fragen.erklaerung_en: The Tokyo Convention governs offences on board and gives the Commander powers of arrest, which he may delegate to crew and passengers.

fragen.frage: Ab wann gilt ein Flugzeug gemäss Montreal Convention als "in flight"?

fragen.erklaerung: "In flight" beginnt mit dem Schliessen aller Aussentüren; "in service" dagegen ab Pre-flight Preparation bis 24 h nach dem Landing.
fragen.zitat: An aircraft is considered to be “in flight” from the moment when all its external doors are closed following embarkation until the moment when such doors are opened for disembarkation.
kontext:
10.0.5.4 The Montreal Convention

The Montreal convention of 1971 was introduced to civil aviation with the intent to create uniformed legislation to suppress instances of bombing and the threatened bombing of commercial aircraft. The convention specifically deals with incidents that take place on an aircraft while “in flight” or while “in service”.
The convention defines a wide spectrum of unlawful acts against the safety of civil aviation, in particular sabotage or destruction of an aircraft in service or damaging air navigation facilities, likely to endanger the safety of an aircraft in service.
An aircraft is considered to be “in flight” from the moment when all its external doors are closed following embarkation until the moment when such doors are opened for disembarkation.

In case of a false landing (in flight diversion), the flight is deemed to continue until the competent authorities take responsibility for the aircraft and for the persons and property on board.
An aircraft is considered to be “in service” from the commencement of the pre- flight preparation by ground personnel or crew and for a period of twenty-four hours after landing. The convention covers the covert planting of an explosive device and the sabotage of an aircraft before departure and after arrival, not covered in previous conventions.
fragen.frage_en: From when is an aircraft considered "in flight" according to the Montreal Convention?
antworten_en: From closing of all external doors after boarding until opening of these doors for disembarkation
From the start of pre-flight preparation until 24 hours after landing
From takeoff until landing
From block off to block on
fragen.erklaerung_en: "In flight" begins with the closing of all external doors; "in service", on the other hand, runs from pre-flight preparation until 24 h after landing.

kontext:
10.4.6.2 Levels of Threat

Four levels of unruly passenger behaviour have been identified to give a

common reference for characterising an ongoing incident.

Level 1 – disruptive behaviour, including suspicious or verbally threatening

behaviour

Level 3 – life-threatening behaviour

Level
4 – attempted or actual breach of the flight crew compartment

kontext:
11.6 Reporting of Occurrence

Any cockpit or cabin crew member shall report to the commander any fault, failure, malfunction or defect which she/he believes may affect the airworthiness or safe operation of the aircraft, including emergency systems, and any incident that endangered or could have endangered the safety of operation. The tables in chapter 11.6.2 - Mandatory Occurrence Reporting list the expected reporter (flight crew, cabin crew, maintenance staff and ground handling) to each mandatory occurrence. However, during flight operation the crew may define one crew member who writes the report. The final responsibility lies with the CMD.
If a crew member other than the CMD writes the report, the safety management will ensure the CMD of the affected flight will be informed as well.
Any occurrences shall be reported as fast as reasonably possible, but no later than 72 hours.

Guideline for checking if operational occurrence or other legal reporting requirement is present:

1. First check with: a. 11.6.2 - Mandatory Occurrence Reporting b. 11.7 - List of Other Legal Reporting Requirements Note: Table of Contents for faster access is presented on next page.

2. Depending on the severity of the occurrence decide between: a. Accident or Serious Incident Reporting (Definition in 11.2 - Definitions)

b. Otherwise Occurence Reporting

c. Check if Occurrence requires immediate ATC Notification as specified

in 11.6.2.4 - ATC Reporting

Note: As a general rule: Whenever you are in doubt, file an “Occurence Report” via the helvetic SMS Tool.

OM-A Reporting Occurences

Table of Contents for faster Access
