fragen.zitat: Above Mach 0.5, stick shaker and Low Speed Awareness (LSA) are not available.
kontext:
SHAKER ANTICIPATED

Avoid side slipping the airplane. If speed is above Mach 0.5, limit airspeed to a minimum of 250 KIAS.
NOTE:
Above Mach 0.5, stick shaker and Low Speed Awareness (LSA) are not available.

If the FLAP (SLAT) FAIL message is displayed, accomplish the FLAP (SLAT) FAIL Procedure.
If the FLAP (SLAT) FAIL message is not displayed, on the final approach, set slat/flap full, set VREF FULL and limit bank angle to 20° maximum.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) SHAKER ANTICIPATED above Mach 0.5: What minimum speed applies and why?
antworten_en: 250 KIAS, because above Mach 0.5 stick shaker and LSA are not available
200 KIAS, because the stick shaker activates too late
Green dot + 20 kt, because the AOA limit is not available
VREF + 80 kt, because stall protection has failed
fragen.erklaerung_en: Above Mach 0.5, stick shaker and low speed awareness are not available; therefore at least 250 KIAS.

fragen.frage: (E1) RUDDER LIMITER FAIL: Welche Rudder Authority besteht im Flug und was ist zu vermeiden?
antworten: 15°; kein Einsatz des Yaw Damper
30°; keine abrupten Pedaleingaben und kein voller Ruderausschlag
30°; keine Landung mit Flaps FULL
Vollausschlag nur unter 175 KIAS zulässig
fragen.erklaerung: Der Rudder Position Limiter ist inoperativ, die Authority beträgt 30°; abrupte Pedaleingaben und voller Ausschlag sind zu vermeiden.
fragen.zitat: Rudder position limiter is inoperative and rudder authority in flight is 30°.
kontext: RUDDER LIMITER FAILURE
Rudder position limiter is inoperative and rudder authority in flight is 30°.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) RUDDER LIMITER FAIL: What rudder authority exists in flight and what must be avoided?
antworten_en: 15°; no use of the yaw damper
30°; no abrupt pedal inputs and no full rudder deflection
30°; no landing with flaps FULL
Full deflection permitted only below 175 KIAS
fragen.erklaerung_en: The rudder position limiter is inoperative, the authority is 30°; abrupt pedal inputs and full deflection are to be avoided.

fragen.frage: (E1) STABILIZER LOCK FAULT: Was gilt für den Pitch Trim?
antworten: Beide Pitch Trim Cutout Buttons sofort drücken
Pitch Trim nur über den Backup Switch
Pitch Trim nach Bedarf, aber keinen Pitch Trim System Cutout Button drücken
Autopilot einschalten, damit er den Drift kompensiert
fragen.erklaerung: Der Stabilizer kann bis 0.5°/min driften; Pitch Trim nach Bedarf verwenden, Cutout Buttons nicht drücken.
fragen.zitat: DO NOT PRESS ANY PITCH TRIM SYSTEM CUTOUT BUTTON.
kontext: CAUTION:

DO NOT PRESS ANY PITCH TRIM SYSTEM CUTOUT

BUTTON.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) STABILIZER LOCK FAULT: What applies for the pitch trim?
antworten_en: Press both pitch trim cutout buttons immediately
Pitch trim only via the backup switch
Pitch trim as required, but do not press any pitch trim system cutout button
Engage the autopilot so that it compensates the drift
fragen.erklaerung_en: The stabilizer can drift up to 0.5°/min; use pitch trim as required, do not press the cutout buttons.

fragen.frage: (E1) ELEVATOR LH (RH) FAILURE: Was gilt beim Bremsen nach dem Landing?
antworten: Sofort nach dem Aufsetzen des Main Gear voll bremsen
Nur Autobrake HI verwenden
Nur Emergency/Parking Brake verwenden
Erst bremsen, wenn das Nose Gear aufgesetzt hat
fragen.erklaerung: Laut AFM wird erst gebremst, nachdem das Nose Gear aufgesetzt hat; zudem Slat/Flap 5 und VREF FULL + 15 KIAS.
fragen.zitat: Apply brakes only after the nose landing gear touches down.
kontext:
ELEVATOR LH (RH) FAILURE

If the failure occurs above 175 KIAS, the current airspeed is the maximum speed for the remainder of the flight.
If the failure occurs below 175 KIAS, the maximum speed for the remainder of the flight is 175 KIAS.
NOTE: Expect less elevator control authority and slower response, especially during landing flare.
For landing configuration, set slat/flap to 5 and set VREF FULL 15 KIAS.
Apply brakes only after the nose landing gear touches down.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) ELEVATOR LH (RH) FAILURE: What applies for braking after landing?
antworten_en: Brake fully immediately after the main gear touches down
Use autobrake HI only
Use the emergency/parking brake only
Brake only once the nose gear has touched down
fragen.erklaerung_en: According to the AFM, braking is applied only after the nose gear has touched down; additionally slat/flap 5 and VREF FULL + 15 KIAS.

fragen.frage: (E1) SPOILER FAULT: Welche ersten Massnahmen sieht das AFM vor?
antworten: Speedbrake schliessen, Autopilot ausschalten, Spoilers Mode Button einmal resetten
Speedbrake ausfahren und Spoilers Mode Button gedrückt lassen
Ground Spoiler CB ziehen
Nur den Autopilot ausschalten
fragen.erklaerung: Bei SPOILER FAULT wird die Speedbrake geschlossen, der AP ausgeschaltet und der Spoilers Mode Button einmal (IN, dann OUT) resettet.
fragen.zitat: Close the speedbrake and disengage the autopilot.
kontext: SPOILER FAULT
Close the speedbrake and disengage the autopilot.

Reset the flight controls mode spoilers button one time.
If the SPOILER FAULT message persists:
If any spoiler panel is failed opened or if it is not possible to determine the spoiler panel position, for landing configuration set slat/flap to 5 and set VREF FULL 15 KIAS.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) SPOILER FAULT: Which initial actions does the AFM specify?
antworten_en: Close the speedbrake, disengage the autopilot, reset the spoilers mode button once
Extend the speedbrake and keep the spoilers mode button pressed
Pull the ground spoiler CB
Only disengage the autopilot
fragen.erklaerung_en: For SPOILER FAULT, the speedbrake is closed, the AP is disengaged and the spoilers mode button is reset once (IN, then OUT).

fragen.frage: (E1) Nach einem AUTOPILOT FAILURE: Wann kann der Autopilot frühestens wieder verfügbar sein?
antworten: Nach 30 Sekunden
10 Sekunden nach dem Disengagement
Erst nach einem Power-Reset am Boden
Nach 1 Minute
fragen.erklaerung: Laut Note kann der AP 10 Sekunden nach dem Disengagement wieder verfügbar sein; dasselbe gilt für den AT.
fragen.zitat: The AP may be available for re-engagement 10 seconds after disengagement.
kontext:
AUTOPILOT FAILURE

Fly the airplane manually.
NOTE:
The AP may be available for re-engagement 10 seconds after disengagement.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) After an AUTOPILOT FAILURE: what is the earliest the autopilot can be available again?
antworten_en: After 30 seconds
10 seconds after disengagement
Only after a power reset on the ground
After 1 minute
fragen.erklaerung_en: According to the note, the AP can be available again 10 seconds after disengagement; the same applies to the AT.

fragen.frage: (E1) AILERON LH (RH) FAILURE wird am Boden vor dem Takeoff angezeigt. Was gilt?
antworten: Takeoff mit Bank-Limit 25° erlaubt
Takeoff erlaubt, wenn das andere Aileron funktioniert
Nicht starten
Takeoff nur mit Flaps 4
fragen.erklaerung: Am Boden gilt: nicht starten. Im Flug sind Querneigung auf 25° und grosse Aileron-Eingaben zu vermeiden.
fragen.zitat: On ground, do not takeoff.
kontext: AILERON LH (RH) FAILURE
On ground, do not takeoff.

Inflight:
Avoid abrupt and large aileron inputs and limit bank angle to 25°.
Establish landing configuration early. For landing configuration, set slat/flap 5 and maintain VREF FULL 10 KIAS.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) AILERON LH (RH) FAILURE is displayed on the ground before takeoff. What applies?
antworten_en: Takeoff permitted with a bank limit of 25°
Takeoff permitted if the other aileron is working
Do not take off
Takeoff only with flaps 4
fragen.erklaerung_en: On the ground: do not take off. In flight, limit bank to 25° and avoid large aileron inputs.

fragen.frage: (E1) Im Approach wird eine Aileron-Schwergängigkeit festgestellt, die Rollkontrolle ist aber nicht verloren. Was empfiehlt das OM-B?
antworten: Sofort das JAMMED CONTROL WHEEL (ROLL) Procedure durchführen
Immer einen Go-around durchführen
Den Autopilot einschalten und Bank auf 15° begrenzen
Die Crew darf den Flug normal fortsetzen
fragen.erklaerung: Ist die Rollkontrolle nicht verloren, darf die Crew normal weiterfliegen; erst bei beeinträchtigter Rollfähigkeit das Jammed-Control-Wheel-Verfahren.
fragen.zitat: In case aileron stiffness is experienced but roll control is not lost,
kontext:
3.0.3 Malfunctions during Approach

Any airplane malfunction requiring crew action below 1000 ft AFE under IMC should lead to a go-around.
Malfunctions above 1000 ft AFE are to be evaluated by the crew.

It should lead to a go-around if necessary procedures cannot be completed before reaching 1000 ft.

Note: In case of any failure that affects the flight director approach mode

or the ability to continue the same approach category, the decision

to continue on a downgraded approach category must be made if approach minimums have been set at or above 500 ft AFE.

In case of a go-around, follow the normal go-around procedure. A new approach may only be performed when the appropriate action is accomplished and malfunction consequences properly evaluated.
In case aileron stiffness is experienced but roll control is not lost,

flight crew may elect to continue the flight normally. If roll capability is compromised, perform the JAMMED CONTROL WHEEL (ROLL) abnormal procedure. Although aileron stiffness is more susceptible to occur on the descent and approach phase, the preceding recommendation is valid for all phases of flight.

For Autoland, a go-around should be initiated in case flight controls malfunctions are identified on final approach above 50 ft.
Following an Autothrottle failure below 500 ft, the approach may be continued if

the airspeed is under control and stabilized.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) On approach, aileron stiffness is noticed, but roll control is not lost. What does the OM-B recommend?
antworten_en: Immediately perform the JAMMED CONTROL WHEEL (ROLL) procedure
Always perform a go-around
Engage the autopilot and limit bank to 15°
The crew may continue the flight normally
fragen.erklaerung_en: If roll control is not lost, the crew may continue normally; the jammed control wheel procedure only applies when roll capability is impaired.

fragen.frage: (E2) Wie ist die Arbeitsteilung bei der Flugvorbereitung gemäss Empfehlung im OM-B E2 vorgesehen?
antworten: PM: Flight Deck Preparation inkl. Power Up; PF: External Inspection
PF: Flight Deck Preparation inkl. Internal Safety Inspection und Power Up; PM: External Inspection
Der Commander führt Flight Deck Preparation und External Inspection selbst durch
PF: External Inspection und Loadsheet; PM: Internal Safety Inspection und Power Up
fragen.erklaerung: Das OM-B E2 empfiehlt, dass der PF das Cockpit vorbereitet (Internal Safety Inspection und Power Up), während der PM die External Inspection macht.
fragen.zitat: It is recommended that the PF performs the flight-deck preparation which includes the Internal Safety Inspection and Power-Up while the PM performs the external inspection.
kontext: 2.1.1 Flight Deck Preparation PFI
It is recommended that the PF performs the flight-deck preparation which includes the Internal Safety Inspection and Power-Up while the PM performs the external inspection.
Note: If the flight crew leaves the aircraft unattended, a power down must be accomplished.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) How is the division of work for flight preparation intended according to the recommendation in the OM-B E2?
antworten_en: PM: flight deck preparation incl. power up; PF: external inspection
PF: flight deck preparation incl. internal safety inspection and power up; PM: external inspection
The commander performs flight deck preparation and external inspection himself
PF: external inspection and loadsheet; PM: internal safety inspection and power up
fragen.erklaerung_en: The OM-B E2 recommends that the PF prepares the cockpit (internal safety inspection and power up) while the PM performs the external inspection.

fragen.frage: (E2) Power Up: Nach BATT 1 ON und BATT 2 AUTO sind mehr als die Displays 1 und 4 verfügbar. Was folgt daraus?
antworten: Das Flugzeug darf nicht dispatcht werden
Normal, solange alle Displays flag-frei sind
Display 2 und 3 manuell über den REVERSIONARY PANEL ausschalten und weiterfahren
Power Up mit BATT 2 ON wiederholen; danach ist der Dispatch erlaubt
fragen.erklaerung: Laut CAUTION im Power-Up-Verfahren dürfen nur die Displays 1 und 4 verfügbar sein. Sind es mehr, darf das Flugzeug nicht dispatcht werden.
fragen.zitat: Verify that only displays 1 and 4 are available. if more than displays 1 and 4 are available, the airplane must not be dispatched.
kontext:
2.1.3 Power Up

The POWER UP procedures and checklist must be performed every

time airplane power needs to be established.
If receiving the airplane already powered up, following items (marked with an asterisk in the checklist) must be performed:
FIRE EXTINGUISHER panel DVDR CONTROL panel Electronic CBs

Note: Ensure the airplane is not moved before the IESS is initialized.

For Power Up under Cold Soak Operation refer to 2.8.3.2.1 - Power up and 2.8.3.3.3 - Cabin Warm-up

CHALLENGE ACTION (performed by)

BATT 1 Knob ON (PF) BATT 2 Knob AUTO (PF)

CAUTION:
Verify that only displays 1 and 4 are available. if more than displays 1 and 4 are available, the airplane must not be dispatched.

Batteries Voltage CHECK (PF)
CAUTION: Each battery voltage must be at least 22 volts.

If batteries voltage is between 21 V and 22 V, recharge the

batteries prior to takeoff, through any AC source (including engines

during taxi) for:

30 minutes if batteries temperature is at or above 0°C, or

35 minutes if batteries temperature is at or above -5°c and below 0°C,

or 40 minutes if batteries temperature is at or above -10°C and

below -5°C, or

50 minutes if batteries temperature is below -10°C.

If batteries voltage is below 21 V, report to maintenance.

Note: Minimize the time the airplane is left with batteries as the only power source, to avoid discharging.

OM-B E2 2 Normal Procedures

CHALLENGE ACTION (performed by)

EICAS Messages CHECK DISPLAYED (PF)

Note: Once EICAS messages start blinking, the airplane electrical system is ready to have the AC power either through the GPU or APU.
It is not required to wait until the last EICAS message is triggered.

GPU Button (if applicable) PUSH IN (PF) Verify AVAIL light illuminated before pushing in. When GPU is not available, or is not necessary, maintain GPU Button pushed out.
The Electrical PBIT is automatically performed after the airplane is powered by any AC source and takes about 2 minutes to complete. The Electrical PBIT will be interrupted if any Hydraulic Sys ELEC PUMP is running or if AC power is interrupted while the test is running.

*FIRE EXTINGUISHER Panel CHECK (PF) Verify there are no fire protection fail messages displayed on the EICAS after Power Up.

Press and hold the Fire Extinguisher TEST button and observe the following EICAS messages, lights and warnings:
Aural warning.

FIRE EXTINGUISHER Handles illuminated.
Cargo Smoke AFT Button illuminated.
Cargo Smoke FWD Button illuminated.
Fire Extinguisher APU Button illuminated.
Upper half of the APU EMER STOP Button illuminated.

Master WARNING lights flashing.

“CRG AFT SMOKE” EICAS message.

“CRG FWD SMOKE” EICAS message.

“APU FIRE” EICAS message. “ENG 1 FIRE” EICAS message.

“ENG 2 FIRE” EICAS message. “FIRE” warning annunciation displayed inside ITT indicators.

“AFT EBAY SMOKE” EICAS message.

“CTR EBAY SMOKE” EICAS message. “FWD EBAY SMOKE” EICAS message.

CHALLENGE ACTION (performed by)

APU CONTROL Panel AS REQUIRED (PF) Verify APU EMER STOP Button is PUSHED OUT and not illuminated.

The APU FADEC is ready for use when APU rpm and EGT dashed indications are replaced by numbers.

If AC source is lost due to unintentional GPU or APU generator disconnection, power down the airplane and perform the power up procedure.
DVDR CONTROL Panel CHECK (PF) Press and hold TEST Button for three seconds and verify no fail messages displayed on EICAS.

Cockpit Lights ANNUNCIATORS TEST Button PRESS (PF) Verify all cockpit associated lights illuminated.

EMER LT Selector ON (PF) Verify the EMR LT ON and EMER LT NOT ARMED messages displayed on the EICAS.

EMER LT Selector ARMED (PF) External Lights NAV Switch

Switch off displays 2 and 3 manually via the REVERSIONARY PANEL and continue
Repeat power up with BATT 2 ON; dispatch is then permitted

kontext:
2.3.5.4.3 Climb Speed

Adjust the climb speeds using the following criteria:
Obstacle Clearance: recommended Green Dot until MSA or above;

Weather Conditions: recommended Green Dot +50 kt to clear low altitude turbulence;

kontext:
LONG RANGE CRUISE

In the Long Range Cruise schedule (LRC), the airplane is flown at a speed

corresponding to a specific range equal to 99% of maximum specific range.
Although not the most fuel efficient speed, LRC is usually adopted to save fuel

because it is considerably faster than Maximum Range Cruise and just 1% less

fuel efficient.

kontext:
TRIMMING TECHNIQUE

Yaw Trimming:
With the autopilot engaged, ensure that the fuel is properly balanced, engine thrust is symmetric, and HDG mode is selected.
Proper monitoring of the Sky Pointer, Roll Pointer and Slip/Skid Indicator is fundamental for a correct airplane trimming.
The YAW Trim Controller is actuated in the direction that corresponds to the Slip/Skid Indicator position. In most cases, only small and brief actuations are enough.
To avoid over trimming, allow approximately three to five seconds between

actuations and observe the results. As the Slip/Skid Indicator gets closer to the

center (below the Roll Pointer) only sharp, brisk actuations are required.

Roll Trimming:
Roll trimming should be performed after the airplane has been trimmed for yaw.

An exception to this rule would be a wing heavy condition in manual flight when the slip/skid indicator is centered.

In this case, actuate the ROLL Trim Switch in the same direction where the pilot

input is required, or towards the down side of the control wheel. Both parts of the ROLL Trim Switch must be pressed simultaneously and in most cases, only sharp, brisk movements are required.

fragen.erklaerung_en: To avoid over-trimming, about three to five seconds are waited between operations and the effect is observed.

kontext:
2.4.1.11 Holding

For maximum fuel economy, holding should be performed at clean configuration, gear up and minimum fuel consumption speed (Maximum Endurance speed), even if flying under turbulent conditions. The Green Dot can be used as reference, since it is approximately equal to the minimum fuel consumption speed.
The holding tables for clean configuration are provided in the OM-B 5 Flight Planning Data. They are calculated for the condition of minimum fuel

consumption or green dot, whichever is higher, with A/I OFF and A/I ON.
Considering fuel conservation, performing a holding pattern with flaps extended should be avoided, since it significantly increases fuel flow. In case the minimum Flaps Up maneuvering speed exceeds maximum holding pattern speed, pilot should obtain ATC clearance to maintain present speed or use minimum flap/slat setting to comply to speed restriction.
For flaps 1, fuel flow increases by approximately 20%.

Crew should start slowing to the appropriate holding speed, at least, 10 NM before entering the HOLD Pattern, configured with: Flaps UP and Gear UP.

For Holding in Cold Soak Operation refer to 2.8.3.3.13 - Holding

kontext:
2.4.1.11.1 FMS Holding Calculation

The default holding is a standard holding pattern at the designated holding fix with the inbound course set to the flight plan course into the holding fix.
Leg times are defaulted to 1 minute below 14000 ft and 1.5 minutes at or above 14000 ft.

However, those values can be modified by the pilot.
Inbound Course:
Inbound course, turn direction and quadrant can be modified by the pilot. Entry procedure entries are not permitted.

If a new inbound course or turn direction is entered by the pilot, a new quadrant is automatically set by the FMS.
Quadrant entries are not recommended, because when pilot entries a new quadrant, FMS sets the new inbound course to the cardinal heading associated with the entered quadrant. This procedure overwrites any other inbound course set previously.
Leg Time Distance:
Leg time or distance can also be entered by the pilot. If a leg time is entered, FMS computes the leg distance. When leg distance is entered, leg time is computed.
FMS calculations for leg time and distance use Green Dot Speed for holding patterns above or below 14000 ft.
Speed:

The FMS displays a speed for holding at 1R on the HOLDING PATTERN page.
FMS computations are based on the Performance Mode selected on PERFORMANCE INIT page:

FMS calculations for leg time and distance use the following Hold Speed

priority for holding patterns above or below 14000 ft:

Speed entered by the pilot on FMS Holding Pattern page.

Green Dot (in case Green Dot is valid and EDS Ice Status is also valid).

210 kt (in case Green Dot is invalid or EDS Ice Status is invalid).

Note: In ice conditions, maintain Maximum Endurance speed or Green Dot speed, whichever is higher.

2.4.1.11.1.1 EFC (Expect Further Clearance)

EFC time (ZULU time) can be entered pressing 4R. In this case, all time and fuel

predictions for waypoints beyond the Hold are based on remaining in the hold

until the expected clearance time has elapsed.

Note: All entries are inhibited 1 minute before entering holding.

kontext:
2.4.2.1 Descent – Expanded Procedure

For Descent in Cold Soak Operation refer to 2.8.3.3.12 - Descent

CHALLENGE ACTION (performed by)

Approach Briefing COMPLETE (PF PM) It is recommended to perform the approach briefing before starting descent.
Refer to OM-A 8.3.2.26 Approach Briefing. The approach preparation flow on the MCDU is done using LSK 6R to scroll through the pages and fill in all the necessary information.
It is recommended to verify on ACTIVE FPL PLAN page on MCDU that the descent altitude constraints are displayed as DES.
Set performance data on EFB and check the information. Assess the landing distance for current conditions and compare with the runway length available. If conditions affecting airplane performance change during the approach, reassess the evaluation. Note that the EFB must be kept secured and viewable below 10000 ft.
If the destination airport runway is reported to be slippery or contaminated, it is necessary to discuss the outcome on the landing distance during the approach briefing. The same discussion is applicable if the crew has planned to use additional speed for the approach due to wind/gust

conditions.
If any failure that affects the required landing distance occurs in the final approach, consider a missed approach in order to better evaluate the situation and an appropriate runway length. Failures that affect the landing

distance are commonly associated to brakes, ground spoilers and/or thrust

reversers.

On EFB, if applicable, prepare the approach charts. A thorough

understanding by the PF and PM of all the applicable approach charts and NOTAMS is essential, including taxi-in procedures.

Both pilots should set RA BARO minimums, pre-select radios and courses

for the approach.

If ILS is chosen on MCDU Arrival page, preview function automatically sets the ILS frequency and final approach course at 150 NM from destination

airport.
Verify GO AROUND LIMIT page settings.

With VNAV engaged the PF should select the Altitude Selector only to altitudes cleared by ATC.

For ETOPS operation the crew must perform a Fuel Crossfeed Test in the last hour of cruise phase.

CHALLENGE ACTION RESPONSE (performed by)

External Lights ON (PM) At FL100 or 10`000 ft QNH:

Turn ON the Landing LEFT, NOSE and RIGHT switches.

LFE Indication on EICAS CHECK (PM) Verify the LFE indication (EICAS) is in accordance to the destination airport elevation.

AUTOBRAKE Selector (If Applicable) SET (PF) Set the AUTOBRAKE OFF, LOW, MED or HI in accordance with the runway analysis calculations for landing.

Landing Data SET (PF) Check on the LANDING INIT page the expected landing weight. Insert all data according to the type of approach and runway conditions to set VREF, VAP, VAC and VFS.
If Landing Speeds Computation is available (TOLD), FMS automatically calculates the landing speeds VREF, VAP, VAC and VFS, displayed on page LANDING 1/1. However, compare the speeds with the calculated landing

speeds from the performance calculation software to be within 1 kts and confirm the speeds to indicate it on the the PFD.
If the difference between TOLD and the performance calculation software is bigger than 1 kts, the speeds from the performance calculation software
shall be inserted manually on the LANDING page (overwrite).

Enter the average of both calculations
Use the higher of the two VREFs and confirm the remaining TOLD speeds

kontext:
2.5.8.3 Go-Around

No approach should be initiated unless the prevailing conditions have been understood and the crew found that landing is acceptable without undue risk.
Philosophically all approaches should be treated as approaches followed by missed approaches, and landing should be treated as the alternate procedure.
This mindset depends on a good approach briefing, on the knowledge of the missed approach procedure and on proper programming of the FMS.
Enough visual cues must exist to continue the approach below DA(DH) or MDA.

If visual cues are lost due to shallow fog, snow flurries, or heavy precipitation, immediately initiate a go-around and fly the published missed approach procedure.
Although the PF is initially the responsible for the go-around callout, the PM may also make this callout. The PF immediate response to this callout by the PM is execution of a missed approach.
Go around, when properly executed, involve little loss of altitude below the altitude at which the go-around is “started”.
Conducting a missed approach when not stabilized on a final approach course should be as follows:

2.5.8.4 Discontinued Approach

During the initial phase of the approach, there may be a situation where the approach needs to be discontinued.
If the aircraft is above the missed approach altitude, a discontinued approach shall be performed.

However, if the aircraft is below the missed approach altitude, a normal go around procedure should be accomplished.
Whenever a discontinued approach is necessary, take the following actions: press ALT Button

verify or adjust ALT SEL Controller for desired altitude

select FMS if it is not the navigation source, select LNAV to follow the missed approach profile and activate the missed approach prompt on MCDU. The HDG mode may also be selected to comply with ATC instructions (1)

select the most appropriate vertical mode (VS, FPA, or FLCH)

resume proper airplane configuration (gear and flaps) and speed as desired

Approach). This prompt appears after the IAF (Initial Approach Fix) and allows missed approach lateral profile to be activated without pressing the TO/GA Button.

fragen.frage: (E2) Der Autothrottle fällt unter 500 ft im Approach aus. Was gilt?
antworten: Ein Go-Around ist zwingend

kontext:
3.0.3 Malfunctions during Approach

Any airplane malfunction requiring crew action below 1000 ft AFE under IMC should lead to a go-around.
Malfunctions above 1000 ft AFE are to be evaluated by the crew.
It should lead to a go-around if necessary procedures cannot be completed before reaching 1000 ft.

Note: In case of any failure that affects the flight director approach mode or the ability to continue the same approach category, the decision to continue on a downgraded approach category must be made if approach minimums have been set at or above 500 ft AFE.

In case of a go-around, follow the normal go-around procedure. A new approach may only be performed when the appropriate action is accomplished and malfunction consequences properly evaluated.

In case aileron stiffness is experienced but roll control is not lost, flight crew may elect to continue the flight normally. If roll capability is compromised, perform the JAMMED CONTROL WHEEL (ROLL) abnormal procedure. Although aileron stiffness is more susceptible to occur on the descent and approach phase, the preceding recommendation is valid for all phases of flight.

For Autoland, a go-around should be initiated in case flight controls

malfunctions are identified on final approach above 50 ft.
Following an Autothrottle failure below 500 ft, the approach may be continued if the airspeed is under control and stabilized.

The approach may be continued if the speed is under control and stable
The approach may only be continued with Autoland
The approach may only be continued if VAP is increased by 10 kt
fragen.erklaerung_en: According to OM-B E2 3.0.3, the approach may be continued after an autothrottle failure below 500 ft if the speed is under control and stabilized.

fragen.frage: (E2) Abnormal Conditions, ePerf nicht verfügbar: Welcher maximale VAP gilt auf einer nassen Runway (kein OEI Autoland)?

VREF NEW + 5 kt
fragen.erklaerung: Der VAP ist auf VREF NEW + 10 kt (trocken) bzw. + 20 kt (nicht trocken) begrenzt. Für OEI Autoland auf trockener oder nasser Runway gilt + 10 kt.

kontext:
3.0.4 Approach and Landing Speeds for Abnormal Conditions

For approach and landing speeds determination, ePerf shall be used as the primary calculation method.
If ePerf is unavailable the VREF, VAC and VFS speeds are presented in the QRH.
VREF Setting for Abnormal Conditions If ePerf is unavailable, a new VREF must be defined with information derived from the QRH:

VREF NEW VREF FLAPS FULL abnormal speed correction

VAP Setting for Abnormal Conditions The recommended method for approach speed calculation is to add one half of the steady headwind component plus the gust increment above the steady wind to the reference speed:

VAP VREF NEW 1/2 steady headwind component gust increment

The VAP is limited to:
Minimum: VAP VREF NEW 0 kt

Maximum:
VAP V REF NEW 10 kt on dry runways or
VAP V REF NEW 20 kt on other than dry runways

or VAP V REF NEW 10 kt OEI Autoland on dry or wet runways

VAC Setting for Abnormal Conditions

If ePerf is unavailable, for landing in abnormal conditions, VAC shall be set to the

highest of:
fragen.frage_en: (E2) Abnormal conditions, ePerf not available: what maximum VAP applies on a wet runway (no OEI Autoland)?
antworten_en: VREF NEW + 10 kt
VREF NEW + 15 kt
VREF NEW + 20 kt
VREF NEW + 5 kt
fragen.erklaerung_en: VAP is limited to VREF NEW + 10 kt (dry) or + 20 kt (not dry). For OEI Autoland on a dry or wet runway, + 10 kt applies.

fragen.frage: (E2) Im Approach tritt Aileron Stiffness auf, die Rollkontrolle ist aber nicht verloren. Was empfiehlt das OM-B E2?
antworten: Sofort JAMMED CONTROL WHEEL (ROLL) durchführen und den Aileron Disconnect Handle ziehen
Der Flug darf normal fortgesetzt werden; nur bei beeinträchtigter Rollfähigkeit JAMMED CONTROL WHEEL (ROLL) durchführen
Go-Around einleiten und das FLIGHT CONTROL NORMAL MODE FAILURE Verfahren durchführen
Autopilot trennen und LAND AT THE NEAREST SUITABLE AIRPORT
fragen.erklaerung: Bei Aileron Stiffness ohne Verlust der Rollkontrolle darf die Crew normal weiterfliegen. Erst bei beeinträchtigter Rollfähigkeit wird JAMMED CONTROL WHEEL (ROLL) durchgeführt; das gilt für alle Flugphasen.
fragen.zitat: In case aileron stiffness is experienced but roll control is not lost, flight crew may elect to continue the flight normally.
kontext:
3.0.3 Malfunctions during Approach

Any airplane malfunction requiring crew action below 1000 ft AFE under IMC should lead to a go-around.
Malfunctions above 1000 ft AFE are to be evaluated by the crew.
It should lead to a go-around if necessary procedures cannot be completed before reaching 1000 ft.

Note: In case of any failure that affects the flight director approach mode or the ability to continue the same approach category, the decision to continue on a downgraded approach category must be made if approach minimums have been set at or above 500 ft AFE.

In case of a go-around, follow the normal go-around procedure. A new approach may only be performed when the appropriate action is accomplished and malfunction consequences properly evaluated.
In case aileron stiffness is experienced but roll control is not lost, flight crew may elect to continue the flight normally.

If roll capability is compromised, perform the JAMMED CONTROL WHEEL (ROLL) abnormal procedure. Although aileron stiffness is more susceptible to occur on the descent and approach phase, the preceding recommendation is valid for all phases of flight.

For Autoland, a go-around should be initiated in case flight controls

malfunctions are identified on final approach above 50 ft.
Following an Autothrottle failure below 500 ft, the approach may be continued if the airspeed is under control and stabilized.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) Aileron stiffness occurs on approach, but roll control is not lost. What does the OM-B E2 recommend?
antworten_en: Immediately perform JAMMED CONTROL WHEEL (ROLL) and pull the aileron disconnect handle
The flight may be continued normally; perform JAMMED CONTROL WHEEL (ROLL) only if roll capability is impaired
Initiate a go-around and perform the FLIGHT CONTROL NORMAL MODE FAILURE procedure
Disconnect the autopilot and LAND AT THE NEAREST SUITABLE AIRPORT
fragen.erklaerung_en: With aileron stiffness without loss of roll control, the crew may continue normally. JAMMED CONTROL WHEEL (ROLL) is performed only if roll capability is impaired; this applies to all phases of flight.

fragen.frage: (E2) Darf ein ausgelöster Circuit Breaker im Flug zurückgesetzt werden?
antworten: Nur wenn es für die sichere Beendigung des Flugs zwingend ist oder die Checkliste es verlangt; nach erneutem Auslösen kein weiterer Versuch
Ja, einmalig bei jedem CB, sofern der Commander zustimmt

fragen.zitat: Circuit breakers must not be reset in-flight, unless it is imperative to reset the circuit breaker for the safe completion of the flight.
kontext:
3.1 Circuit Breaker Reset

A tripped circuit breaker is usually a result of an abnormality in the electrical load or in associated wiring.
Circuit breakers must not be reset in-flight, unless it is imperative to reset the circuit breaker for the safe completion of the flight.

Should the circuit breaker trip again, no further attempt should be made to reset that circuit breaker. The reset of a circuit breaker is also permitted were the checklist specifically directs to do so.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) May a tripped circuit breaker be reset in flight?
antworten_en: Only if it is essential for the safe completion of the flight or the checklist requires it; no further attempt after it trips again
Yes, once for each CB, provided the commander agrees
Yes, up to two times, with at least 2 minutes of cooling time
Never, not even if the checklist requires it
fragen.erklaerung_en: CBs are reset in flight only if it is essential for the safe completion of the flight or the checklist requires it. If the CB trips again, no further attempt is made.

kontext:
3.7.2 Abnormal Slat Flap Configuration

If flap or slat fails at a specific position, select the desired flap or slat position and use data according to QRH configuration tables. The best performance combination of Slat/Flap is the one that results in the lowest speed.
The following items are valid for all abnormal Slat/Flap configuration approaches and landings: use of autopilot is recommended

if possible reduce gross weight to lowest practicable (burn off fuel) to reduce VREF

check landing distance (select the longest runway available)

limit bank angle to 20° maximum when maneuvering for landing
establish a long final approach, at least 8 NM at recommended speed

attitude and speed are higher than normal

establish landing configuration early, flight large patterns and long final

plan touchdown at 1000 ft touchdown zone, a go-around should be made if landing occurs beyond touchdown zone

flare enough just to reduce the rate of descent, do not float and touchdown at the normal touchdown zone over threshold set thrust levers to IDLE

after touchdown, apply forward control column, reverse thrust and

brakes without delay

fragen.frage: (E2) Bis zu welcher Höhe ist ein Unpressurized Flight mit Passagieren begrenzt?
fragen.erklaerung: Mit Passagieren ist der Flug ohne Pressurization auf 10000 ft begrenzt. Ohne Passagiere ist mehr möglich, wenn die Crew Sauerstoff verwendet.
fragen.zitat: Limit flight level to 10000 ft if carrying passengers.
kontext: 2.8.1.3 Unpressurized Flight
Limit flight level to 10000 ft if carrying passengers.

For flight without passengers, flight level may be greater than 10000 ft provided crew uses oxygen (Refer to appropriate regulations).
For flights with air conditioning packs inoperative (MMEL Item 21-51-00), the following recommendations apply: prior to flight, if a Ground Air Conditioning System is available, precondition the cabin in order to avoid high peak temperatures,

consideration should be given to passenger comfort and TAT expected to be encountered in flight. When carrying passengers or TAT is hotter than 20°C, close passenger window shades and turn off unnecessary lights in order to minimize cabin heat. Operating at TAT hotter than 32°C is not recommended due to the resulting high temperatures in the cabin and cockpit,

flight crew can use Total Air Temperature to predict cabin and cockpit tem- peratures during Ram Air operation, especially at longer duration flights.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) Up to what altitude is an unpressurized flight with passengers limited?
fragen.erklaerung_en: With passengers, unpressurized flight is limited to 10000 ft. Without passengers more is possible if the crew uses oxygen.

kontext:
2.8.1.2 ECS OFF Takeoff

The Engines or the APU can supply bleed air for the air conditioning system during takeoff. To have an additional engine thrust during takeoff, the FADEC may send an ECS OFF signal to the AMS Controllers requesting that no bleed air is extracted from the engines for the air conditioning system operation. In this case, bleed air for the air conditioning system can be provided by the APU.
On the MCDU T/O DATASET MENU, the ECS ON or OFF option is displayed.
The ECS ON selection commands the engine bleed to remain on and the ECS OFF selection commands the engine bleed to OFF until the first 500 ft AGL.
It is possible to maintain the airplane pressurized during the initial 500 ft AGL if the following conditions occur:
REF ECS is selected to OFF

REF A/I is selected to OFF or ENG

APU is available and BLEED APU is PUSHED IN

By accomplishing the recommended procedure, the engine bleed valves will remain closed and the APU will supply bleed air for PACKS operation during takeoff, until 500ft AGL.
If APU bleed is unavailable the PACKS will remain OFF until 500 ft AGL.

2.8.1.2.1 ECS OFF Takeoff Procedure Note: APU will supply bleed air for PACKS operation during takeoff until 500 ft AGL.

If APU bleed is unavailable, the PACKS will remain OFF until 500 ft AGL.

The APU bleed cannot be used for the anti-ice system operation. During

takeoff, if the REF A/I is set to ENG, the engine anti-ice system will be

supplied by engines and the PACKS will be supplied by the APU. If the REF A/I is set to ALL, the engine and wing anti-ice systems will be
supplied by engines and the PACKS will switch OFF.
Before Start

fragen.erklaerung_en: With REF A/I ALL, the engines supply engine and wing anti-ice, and the PACKS switch OFF. Only with REF A/I OFF or ENG does the APU supply the PACKS.

LAND AT THE NEAREST SUITABLE AIRPORT und Alternate Gear Extension planen
fragen.erklaerung: Werden HYD 2 OVERHEAT und HYD 3 OVERHEAT zusammen angezeigt, handelt es sich laut AFM um einen Spurious-Zustand; es ist keine Aktion erforderlich.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-03-22 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM 2 OVERHEAT, S. 2
fragen.zitat: When both messages HYD 2 OVERHEAT and HYD 3 OVERHEAT are displayed on EICAS together, it indicates a spurious condition.
kontext:
REVISION 20 - ANAC APPROVED

If HYD 2 OVERHEAT message is also displayed:
NOTE:
When both messages HYD 2 OVERHEAT and HYD 3 OVERHEAT are displayed on EICAS together, it indicates a spurious condition.

No action is required.
If HYD 2 OVERHEAT message is not displayed:
Set the electric hydraulic system 3 pump A and pump B knobs to OFF.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) HYD 2 OVERHEAT and HYD 3 OVERHEAT appear simultaneously on the EICAS. What must be done?
antworten_en: Both electric hydraulic pumps 3A and 3B to OFF
Press the engine 2 pump shutoff button and shut down engine 2
No action; the combination indicates a spurious condition
LAND AT THE NEAREST SUITABLE AIRPORT and plan alternate gear extension
fragen.erklaerung_en: If HYD 2 OVERHEAT and HYD 3 OVERHEAT are displayed together, according to the AFM it is a spurious condition; no action is required.

fragen.frage: (E2) FUEL 1 (2) LOW LEVEL: Welche Fluglagen sind zu vermeiden?
antworten: Mehr als 15° Nose up, Querneigungen über 30°
Mehr als 8° Nose up oder down, unkoordinierte Manöver und negative g
Mehr als 5° Nose down sowie Speedbrake-Einsatz
Mehr als 10° Nose up oder down und Querneigungen über 25°
fragen.erklaerung: Die CAUTION bei FUEL LO LEVEL verlangt, Fluglagen über 8° Nose up oder down, unkoordinierte Manöver und negative g zu vermeiden.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-03-20 FUEL 1 (2) LOW LEVEL, S. 1
fragen.zitat: AVOID ATTITUDES IN EXCESS OF 8° NOSE UP OR DOWN, UNCOORDINATED MANEUVERS, AND NEGATIVE G'S.
kontext: CAUTION:

AVOID ATTITUDES IN EXCESS OF 8° NOSE UP OR

DOWN, UNCOORDINATED MANEUVERS, AND

NEGATIVE G'S.

If fuel leak is suspected, accomplish the FUEL LEAK Procedure.
If fuel leak is not suspected and center fuel tank is empty, operate fuel crossfeed as required.
If fuel leak is not suspected and center fuel tank is not empty, set the fuel transfer knob to ON.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) FUEL 1 (2) LOW LEVEL: Which attitudes must be avoided?
antworten_en: More than 15° nose up, bank above 30°
More than 8° nose up or down, uncoordinated maneuvers and negative g
More than 5° nose down and speedbrake use
More than 10° nose up or down and bank above 25°
fragen.erklaerung_en: The CAUTION for FUEL LO LEVEL requires avoiding attitudes above 8° nose up or down, uncoordinated maneuvers and negative g.

fragen.frage: (E2) FUEL LEAK: Das Leck befindet sich im rechten Flügeltank. Welche zusätzliche Massnahme verlangt das AFM?
antworten: Die APU abstellen und mit asymmetrischem Thrust die Flügelbalance halten
Den Fuel Transfer Knob auf AUTO stellen und die Reichweite überwachen
Den Crossfeed auf LOW 2 öffnen
Engine 2 sofort abstellen
fragen.erklaerung: Bei einem Leck im rechten Tank wird die APU abgestellt und die Balance mit asymmetrischem Thrust gehalten. Fuel Transfer auf AUTO gilt für ein Leck im Center Tank.
fragen.zitat: If fuel leak is identified on the right side tank, turn off the APU.
kontext:
LAND AT THE NEAREST SUITABLE AIRPORT.

Close the crossfeed and turn off the fuel transfer. Identify the affected fuel tank.
If fuel leak is identified on the center tank, set the fuel transfer knob to AUTO and monitor airplane fuel range.
If fuel leak is identified on the right side tank, turn off the APU.

Use asymmetric thrust to improve or maintain wing fuel balance.
If fuel leak is identified on the left side tank, use asymmetric thrust to improve or maintain wing fuel balance.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) FUEL LEAK: The leak is in the right wing tank. What additional action does the AFM require?
antworten_en: Shut down the APU and use asymmetric thrust to maintain wing balance
Set the fuel transfer knob to AUTO and monitor range
Open the crossfeed to LOW 2
Shut down engine 2 immediately
fragen.erklaerung_en: With a leak in the right tank, the APU is shut down and balance is maintained with asymmetric thrust. Fuel transfer to AUTO applies to a leak in the center tank.

fragen.frage: (E2) LOSS OF ALL FUEL QUANTITY INDICATIONS: Welche Referenz kann für die Gesamt-Fuel-Menge verwendet werden?
antworten: Die FUEL Synoptic Page des MFD
Die IESS-Anzeige
Die FMS PROGRESS Seite mit den Destination-Werten
Die FMS PERFORMANCE INIT Seite 2/3
fragen.erklaerung: Bei Verlust aller Fuel-Quantity-Anzeigen kann die FMS PERFORMANCE INIT 2/3 als Referenz dienen. Der automatische Fuel Transfer ist dann inoperativ.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-02-01 LOSS OF ALL FUEL QUANTITY INDICATIONS, S. 13
fragen.zitat: The FMS PERFORMANCE INIT 2/3 page may be used, as a reference, for the total fuel quantity indication.
kontext:
LAND AT THE NEAREST SUITABLE AIRPORT.

NOTE: – Automatic fuel transfer is inoperative.
– The fuel system EICAS messages may not be displayed, except the FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL message.
–
The FMS PERFORMANCE INIT 2/3 page may be used, as a reference, for the total fuel quantity indication.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) LOSS OF ALL FUEL QUANTITY INDICATIONS: Which reference can be used for the total fuel quantity?
antworten_en: The FUEL synoptic page on the MFD
The IESS indication
The FMS PROGRESS page with the destination values
The FMS PERFORMANCE INIT page 2/3
fragen.erklaerung_en: With loss of all fuel quantity indications, FMS PERFORMANCE INIT 2/3 can serve as a reference. Automatic fuel transfer is then inoperative.

fragen.frage: (E2) FLIGHT CONTROL NORMAL MODE FAILURE bleibt bestehen. Was gilt beim Sinkflug auf 35000 ft?
antworten: Mit Full Speedbrake rasch auf 35000 ft sinken
Auf Mach 0.70 verzögern und dann mit Speedbrake sinken
Keine Speedbrakes verwenden; aktuelle IAS halten, abrupte grosse Ausschläge vermeiden
Autopilot trennen und manuell mit maximal 1000 ft/min sinken
fragen.erklaerung: Bei weiterbestehendem Fehler wird die aktuelle IAS gehalten und die Höhe auf 35000 ft begrenzt; im Sinkflug dorthin darf der Speedbrake nicht verwendet werden.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-03-16 FLIGHT CONTROL NORMAL MODE FAILURE, S. 1
fragen.zitat: Do not use the speedbrake during descent to 35000 ft.
kontext:
5-15, "LANDING IN ABNORMAL

CONFIGURATIONS".

If a go around is required, set slat/flap to 3 and limit minimum airspeed to VREF FULL 20 KIAS.
If BATT DISCHARGING message extinguishes:
Maintain current airspeed and limit maximum altitude to 35000 ft.
NOTE:
Do not use the speedbrake during descent to 35000 ft.

Avoid abrupt and large flight controls inputs.
Exit/avoid icing conditions.
At or below 35000 ft, limit maximum airspeed to 280 KIAS/ 0.79 M.
NOTE: – Do not accomplish the FLIGHT CONTROL NORMAL
fragen.frage_en: (E2) FLIGHT CONTROL NORMAL MODE FAILURE persists. What applies when descending to 35000 ft?
antworten_en: Descend rapidly to 35000 ft with full speedbrake
Decelerate to Mach 0.70 and then descend with speedbrake
Do not use speedbrakes; maintain current IAS, avoid abrupt large inputs
Disconnect the autopilot and descend manually at a maximum of 1000 ft/min
fragen.erklaerung_en: If the fault persists, the current IAS is maintained and altitude is limited to 35000 ft; the speedbrake must not be used in the descent to that altitude.

fragen.frage: (E2) AILERON LH (RH) FAILURE: Welche Speed- und Querneigungsbegrenzung gilt?
antworten: Max. 250 KIAS, Querneigung max. 30°
Max. aktuelle Speed oder 175 KIAS (der höhere Wert), Querneigung max. 25°
Max. aktuelle Speed oder 175 KIAS (der tiefere Wert), Querneigung max. 15°
Max. 200 KIAS, Querneigung max. 20°
fragen.erklaerung: Die Speed wird auf den aktuellen Wert oder 175 KIAS begrenzt, je nachdem was höher ist, und die Querneigung auf 25°.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-03-16 AILERON LH (RH) FAILURE, S. 3
fragen.zitat: Limit maximum airspeed to the current value or 175 KIAS, whichever is higher. Avoid abrupt and large aileron inputs and limit bank angle to 25°.
kontext: REVISION 6 - ANAC APPROVED
Limit maximum airspeed to the current value or 175 KIAS, whichever is higher. Avoid abrupt and large aileron inputs and limit bank angle to 25°.
Establish landing configuration early.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) AILERON LH (RH) FAILURE: What speed and bank limitation applies?
antworten_en: Max. 250 KIAS, bank max. 30°
Max. current speed or 175 KIAS (whichever is higher), bank max. 25°
Max. current speed or 175 KIAS (whichever is lower), bank max. 15°
Max. 200 KIAS, bank max. 20°
fragen.erklaerung_en: Speed is limited to the current value or 175 KIAS, whichever is higher, and bank to 25°.

fragen.frage: (E2) ELEVATOR LH (RH) FAILURE: Wann dürfen nach dem Landing die Brakes betätigt werden?
antworten: Erst nachdem das Nose Gear aufgesetzt hat
Sofort nach dem Aufsetzen des Main Gear
Erst unter 60 KIAS
Erst nach dem Einfahren der Ground Spoiler
fragen.erklaerung: Bei Elevator Failure sind Höhenruderwirkung und Ansprechverhalten im Flare reduziert. Gebremst wird erst nach dem Aufsetzen des Nose Gear.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-03-16 ELEVATOR LH (RH) FAILURE, S. 3
fragen.zitat: Apply brakes only after nose landing gear touches down.
kontext: ABNORMAL CONFIGURATIONS".
Apply brakes only after nose landing gear touches down.
If a go around is required, set slat/flap to 4 and limit minimum airspeed to VREF FULL 15 KIAS.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) ELEVATOR LH (RH) FAILURE: When may the brakes be applied after landing?
antworten_en: Only after the nose gear has touched down
Immediately after the main gear touches down
Only below 60 KIAS
Only after the ground spoilers have retracted
fragen.erklaerung_en: With elevator failure, elevator effectiveness and response in the flare are reduced. Braking is applied only after the nose gear has touched down.

fragen.frage: (E2) FLAP (SLAT) FAIL erscheint nach dem Bewegen des Slat/Flap Levers. Was sind die ersten Massnahmen?
antworten: Höhe auf max. 15000 ft begrenzen und den Lever in der neuen Position belassen
FLAP OVRD drücken und sofort die Flaps wählen
Lever auf 0 stellen und 30 Sekunden warten
Höhe auf max. 20000 ft begrenzen, Lever in die vorherige Position zurück, nach 10 Sekunden neu wählen
fragen.erklaerung: Das AFM verlangt eine Höhenbegrenzung auf 20000 ft, das Zurückstellen des Levers und eine erneute Wahl nach 10 Sekunden.
fragen.zitat: Limit maximum altitude to 20000 ft and return the slat/flap lever to the previous position.
kontext:
ORIGINAL - ANAC APPROVED

If the FLAP (SLAT) FAIL message was displayed after its lever actuation:
Limit maximum altitude to 20000 ft and return the slat/flap lever to the previous position.

After 10 seconds, reselect the slat/flap lever to the desired position.
If the FLAP (SLAT) FAIL message persists, return the slat/flap lever to the previous position. Wait 10 seconds and reselect the slat/flap lever to the desired position.
If the FLAP (SLAT) FAIL message persists or was displayed when the lever was not being actuated:
For landing, disengage the autothrottle, limit the maximum bank angle to 20°, press the flap override button (if applicable), and select the desired slat/flap position. Use the position indicated on the EICAS as a reference to select the landing data from the applicable table.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) FLAP (SLAT) FAIL appears after moving the slat/flap lever. What are the first actions?
antworten_en: Limit altitude to max. 15000 ft and leave the lever in the new position
Press FLAP OVRD and immediately select the flaps
Set the lever to 0 and wait 30 seconds
Limit altitude to max. 20000 ft, return the lever to the previous position, reselect after 10 seconds
fragen.erklaerung_en: The AFM requires an altitude limitation to 20000 ft, returning the lever and reselecting after 10 seconds.

fragen.frage: (E2) HORIZONTAL STABILIZER LOCK FAULT: Welche WARNING enthält das Verfahren?
antworten: Den Pitch Trim nicht mehr verwenden
Beide Pitch Trim Cutout Buttons drücken und manuell fliegen
Keinen Pitch Trim System Cutout Button drücken
Den Autopiloten nicht trennen
fragen.erklaerung: Bei HORIZONTAL STABILIZER LOCK FAULT wird der Pitch Trim nach Bedarf verwendet, aber kein Pitch Trim System Cutout Button gedrückt (WARNING).
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-03-16 HORIZONTAL STABILIZER LOCK FAULT, S. 6
fragen.zitat: DO NOT PRESS ANY PITCH TRIM SYSTEM CUTOUT BUTTON.
kontext: WARNING:

DO NOT PRESS ANY PITCH TRIM SYSTEM CUTOUT

BUTTON.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) HORIZONTAL STABILIZER LOCK FAULT: Which WARNING does the procedure contain?
antworten_en: Do not use the pitch trim any more
Press both pitch trim cutout buttons and fly manually
Do not press any pitch trim system cutout button
Do not disconnect the autopilot
fragen.erklaerung_en: With HORIZONTAL STABILIZER LOCK FAULT, pitch trim is used as required, but no pitch trim system cutout button is pressed (WARNING).

fragen.frage: (E2) RUDDER FAILURE: Welche Crosswind-Situation ist beim Landing zu vermeiden?
antworten: Crosswind von der Gegenseite des Ruderausschlags über 20 kt
Crosswind von derselben Seite, auf die das Seitenruder ausgeschlagen ist (und Komponenten über 10 kt)
Jeder Crosswind über 5 kt, unabhängig von der Seite
Nur Rückenwind; Crosswind ist unkritisch
fragen.erklaerung: Bei RUDDER FAILURE soll kein Landing mit Crosswind von der Seite des Ruderausschlags und keines mit Crosswind-Komponenten über 10 kt erfolgen.
fragen.zitat: AVOID LANDING WITH CROSSWIND FROM THE SAME SIDE THE RUDDER IS DEFLECTED.
kontext: CAUTION: –

AVOID LANDING WITH CROSSWIND FROM THE

SAME SIDE THE RUDDER IS DEFLECTED.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) RUDDER FAILURE: Which crosswind situation must be avoided at landing?
antworten_en: Crosswind from the opposite side of the rudder deflection above 20 kt
Crosswind from the same side as the rudder deflection (and components above 10 kt)
Any crosswind above 5 kt, regardless of side
Only tailwind; crosswind is not critical
fragen.erklaerung_en: With RUDDER FAILURE, do not land with a crosswind from the side of the rudder deflection or with crosswind components above 10 kt.

fragen.frage: (E2) JAMMED RUDDER PEDALS: Wie lange wird der Nosewheel Steering Handle nach dem Aufsetzen des Bugrads gehalten?
antworten: Bis das Flugzeug vollständig steht
Bis unter 60 KIAS
Bis die Thrust Levers auf Idle sind
Bis zum Verlassen der Runway
fragen.erklaerung: Nach dem Aufsetzen des Bugrads wird der Steering Disengage Switch losgelassen und der Nosewheel Steering Handle gehalten. Er darf erst losgelassen werden, wenn das Flugzeug vollständig steht.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-02-01 JAMMED RUDDER PEDALS, S. 8
fragen.zitat: DO NOT RELEASE THE NOSEWHEEL STEERING HANDLE UNTIL THE AIRPLANE IS COMPLETELY STOPPED.
kontext: CAUTION:

DO NOT RELEASE THE NOSEWHEEL STEERING

HANDLE UNTIL THE AIRPLANE IS COMPLETELY

STOPPED.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) JAMMED RUDDER PEDALS: How long is the nosewheel steering handle held after nose wheel touchdown?
antworten_en: Until the aircraft has come to a complete stop
Until below 60 KIAS
Until the thrust levers are at idle
Until vacating the runway
fragen.erklaerung_en: After nose wheel touchdown, the steering disengage switch is released and the nosewheel steering handle is held. It may be released only when the aircraft has come to a complete stop.

fragen.frage: (E2) ABNORMAL LANDING GEAR EXTENSION: Was ist zu tun, wenn das Landing Gear nach dem Setzen des Levers auf DOWN nicht als ausgefahren angezeigt wird?
antworten: Den Landing Gear Lever mehrmals zyklieren
Den Downlock Release Button drücken
Sofort das PARTIAL OR GEAR UP LANDING Verfahren durchführen
Den Alternate Gear Extension Lever ziehen
fragen.erklaerung: Wird das Landing Gear nicht als unten bestätigt, wird der Alternate Gear Extension Lever gezogen. Erst wenn es dann noch nicht bestätigt ist, folgt PARTIAL OR GEAR UP LANDING.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-02-01 ABNORMAL LANDING GEAR EXTENSION, S. 9
fragen.zitat: If the landing gear indications are not confirmed down, pull the alternate gear extension lever.
kontext:
REVISION 8 - ANAC APPROVED

Move landing gear lever to down.
If the landing gear indications are not confirmed down, pull the alternate gear extension lever.
If the landing gear indications are still not confirmed down, accomplish the PARTIAL OR GEAR UP LANDING Procedure.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) ABNORMAL LANDING GEAR EXTENSION: What must be done if the landing gear is not indicated as extended after setting the lever to DOWN?
antworten_en: Cycle the landing gear lever several times
Press the downlock release button
Immediately perform the PARTIAL OR GEAR UP LANDING procedure
Pull the alternate gear extension lever
fragen.erklaerung_en: If the landing gear is not confirmed down, the alternate gear extension lever is pulled. Only if it is still not confirmed does PARTIAL OR GEAR UP LANDING follow.

fragen.frage: (E2) BRAKE OVERHEAT im Flug: Wann darf das Landing Gear wieder eingefahren werden?
antworten: Sofort nachdem BRK OVERHEAT erloschen ist
10 Minuten nach dem Ausfahren, unabhängig von der Meldung
5 Minuten nachdem BRK OVERHEAT erloschen ist
Erst nach dem Landing; es bleibt unten
fragen.erklaerung: Das Landing Gear wird ausgefahren. Nach dem Erlöschen von BRK OVERHEAT wird 5 Minuten gewartet, dann wird es wieder eingefahren.
fragen.zitat: After the BRK OVERHEAT message extinguishes, wait 5 minutes and, then, retract the landing gear.
kontext:
ORIGINAL - ANAC APPROVED

Set the landing gear lever to down.
After the BRK OVERHEAT message extinguishes, wait 5 minutes and, then, retract the landing gear.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) BRAKE OVERHEAT in flight: when may the landing gear be retracted again?
antworten_en: Immediately after BRK OVERHEAT has gone out
10 minutes after extension, regardless of the message
5 minutes after BRK OVERHEAT has gone out
Only after landing; it stays down
fragen.erklaerung_en: The landing gear is extended. After BRK OVERHEAT goes out, wait 5 minutes, then retract it again.

fragen.frage: (E2) LANDING GEAR WOW SYSTEM FAILURE: Welche Systeme sind nach dem Landing möglicherweise nicht verfügbar?
antworten: Nur die Autobrake
Thrust Reversers, Steering, Ground Spoilers, Wing Anti-Ice und Ground Idle
Normal Brakes und Antiskid
Flaps und Slats
fragen.erklaerung: Laut NOTE können bei WOW-Systemausfall Thrust Reversers, Steering, Ground Spoilers, Wing Anti-Ice und Ground Idle nicht verfügbar sein.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-03-26 LANDING GEAR WOW SYSTEM FAILURE, S. 5
fragen.zitat: Thrust Reversers, Steering, Ground Spoilers, Wing Anti-Ice and Ground Idle may not be available.
kontext:
ABNORMAL CONFIGURATIONS".

NOTE:
Thrust Reversers, Steering, Ground Spoilers, Wing Anti-Ice and Ground Idle may not be available.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) LANDING GEAR WOW SYSTEM FAILURE: Which systems may not be available after landing?
antworten_en: Only the autobrake
Thrust reversers, steering, ground spoilers, wing anti-ice and ground idle
Normal brakes and antiskid
Flaps and slats
fragen.erklaerung_en: According to the NOTE, with WOW system failure thrust reversers, steering, ground spoilers, wing anti-ice and ground idle may be unavailable.

fragen.frage: (E2) PARTIAL OR GEAR UP LANDING: Welche Vorbereitungen verlangt das AFM vor dem Approach?
antworten: APU aus, DUMP drücken, Gear Lever down, Slat/Flap FULL, Cockpit-Tür entriegeln
APU an, Landing Gear oben lassen, Slat/Flap 3, Cockpit-Tür verriegeln
APU aus, Gear Lever up, Slat/Flap 5, Batterien OFF
Packs aus, Gear Lever down, Slat/Flap 2, Cockpit-Tür verriegeln
fragen.erklaerung: Die APU wird abgestellt, DUMP gedrückt, das Landing Gear ausgefahren, Slat/Flap auf FULL gesetzt und die Cockpit-Tür entriegelt.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-02-01 PARTIAL OR GEAR UP LANDING, S. 20
fragen.zitat: Turn off the APU and press the DUMP button. Set landing gear down and slat/flap to full position. Unlock the cockpit door.
kontext:
REVISION 7 - ANAC APPROVED

Plan to land on available gear and burn off fuel to reduce touchdown speed.
Before approach, set the Aural Warning System to OFF on the MCDU, as required.
Turn off the APU and press the DUMP button. Set landing gear down and slat/flap to full position. Unlock the cockpit door.

If a go around is required, maintain landing gear down.
Just before touchdown, announce impact.
After landing, set thrust levers to idle, set the start/stop selectors to STOP, pull and rotate the fire extinguisher handles. Announce emergency evacuation and set batteries to OFF.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) PARTIAL OR GEAR UP LANDING: What preparations does the AFM require before the approach?
antworten_en: APU off, press DUMP, gear lever down, slat/flap FULL, unlock the cockpit door
APU on, leave the gear up, slat/flap 3, lock the cockpit door
APU off, gear lever up, slat/flap 5, batteries OFF
Packs off, gear lever down, slat/flap 2, lock the cockpit door
fragen.erklaerung_en: The APU is shut down, DUMP is pressed, the landing gear is extended, slat/flap is set to FULL and the cockpit door is unlocked.

fragen.frage: (E2) BLEED 1 (2) FAIL bleibt nach dem Schliessen und Wiederöffnen der Bleed bestehen. Welche Höhenbegrenzung gilt?
antworten: 10000 ft oder MEA
fragen.erklaerung: Bleibt BLEED FAIL bestehen oder kehrt zurück, wird die maximale Höhe auf 31000 ft begrenzt.
fragen.zitat: If the BLEED 1 (2) FAIL message persists or returns, limit maximum altitude to 31000 ft.
kontext:
ORIGINAL - ANAC APPROVED

Close the affected bleed and wait 1 minute.
If the BLEED 1 (2) FAIL message extinguishes, open the affected bleed.
If the BLEED 1 (2) FAIL message persists or returns, limit maximum altitude to 31000 ft.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) BLEED 1 (2) FAIL persists after closing and reopening the bleed. What altitude limitation applies?
antworten_en: 10000 ft or MEA
fragen.erklaerung_en: If BLEED FAIL persists or returns, the maximum altitude is limited to 31000 ft.

fragen.frage: (E2) PRESSURIZATION AUTO FAILURE bleibt bestehen, die Kabine wird manuell geregelt. Was ist im Approach auf 5000 ft AGL zu tun?
antworten: Den DUMP Button drücken
Den Cabin Altitude Controller 60 Sekunden auf DOWN halten
Den Cabin Altitude Controller 50 Sekunden auf UP halten
Pack 1 ausschalten
fragen.erklaerung: Bei manueller Druckregelung nach PRESN AUTO FAIL wird auf 5000 ft AGL der Cabin Altitude Controller 50 Sekunden auf UP gehalten.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-03-04 PRESSURIZATION AUTO FAILURE, S. 5
fragen.zitat: At 5000 ft AGL, hold the cabin altitude controller up for 50 seconds.
kontext:
REVISION 8 - ANAC APPROVED

Set the pressurization to MAN, then to AUTO.
If the PRESN AUTO FAIL message persists, set the pressurization to MAN and control the cabin altitude according to the pressurization conversion table, contained in LOSS OF PRESSURIZATION INDICATION Procedure.
At 5000 ft AGL, hold the cabin altitude controller up for 50 seconds.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) PRESSURIZATION AUTO FAILURE persists, the cabin is controlled manually. What must be done on approach at 5000 ft AGL?
antworten_en: Press the DUMP button
Hold the cabin altitude controller at DOWN for 60 seconds
Hold the cabin altitude controller at UP for 50 seconds
Switch off pack 1
fragen.erklaerung_en: With manual pressure control after PRESN AUTO FAIL, the cabin altitude controller is held at UP for 50 seconds at 5000 ft AGL.

fragen.frage: (E2) PRESN MAN FAIL zusammen mit PRESN AUTO FAIL: Wann wird Pack 1 ausgeschaltet?
antworten: Auf 31000 ft
Auf 25000 ft
Auf 10000 ft oder MEA
Sofort beim Erscheinen der Meldungen
fragen.erklaerung: Die Höhe wird auf 10000 ft oder MEA begrenzt. Auf 25000 ft wird Pack 1 ausgeschaltet, auf 10000 ft/MEA Pack 2 und DUMP gedrückt.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-03-04 PRESSURIZATION MANUAL FAILURE, S. 5
fragen.zitat: At 25000 ft, turn off the pack 1.
kontext:
ORIGINAL - ANAC APPROVED

If the PRESN MAN FAIL message is associated to PRESN AUTO FAIL message, limit the maximum altitude to 10000 ft or MEA, whichever is higher.
At 25000 ft, turn off the pack 1.
At 10000 ft or MEA (whichever is higher), turn off the pack 2 and press the DUMP button.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) PRESN MAN FAIL together with PRESN AUTO FAIL: when is pack 1 switched off?
antworten_en: At 31000 ft
At 25000 ft
At 10000 ft or MEA
Immediately when the messages appear
fragen.erklaerung_en: Altitude is limited to 10000 ft or MEA. At 25000 ft pack 1 is switched off, at 10000 ft/MEA pack 2 is switched off and DUMP is pressed.

fragen.frage: (E2) WINDSHIELD IMPAIRED OR CRACKED: Welche Speed- und LFE-Einstellung verlangt das AFM?
antworten: Max. 220 KIAS, LFE auf 10000 ft
Max. 250 KIAS, LFE auf 8000 ft
Max. 200 KIAS, LFE auf Destination Elevation
Max. 160 KIAS, LFE auf 14500 ft
fragen.erklaerung: Die Speed wird auf 220 KIAS begrenzt und die LFE auf 10000 ft gesetzt. Sind im Approach beide Seiten beeinträchtigt, gilt max. 160 KIAS.
fragen.quelle: AFM E2 4-02-01 WINDSHIELD IMPAIRED OR CRACKED, S. 21
fragen.zitat: Limit maximum airspeed to 220 KIAS. Set the LFE to 10000 ft.
kontext:
ORIGINAL - ANAC APPROVED

Turn off the associated windshield heating and close the cockpit door.
Limit maximum airspeed to 220 KIAS. Set the LFE to 10000 ft.

POSITIVE PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE (SAFETY

VALVE)

NORMAL OPERATION

The cross bleed is commanded open when the XBLEED Button is pushed in (AUTO) and any of the following conditions is met:
– One side provides manifold pressure and there is not a bleed air source on the opposite side,

– Engine #2 start in the air,

– Bleed leak, unless starting an engine,
– Engine FIRE EXTINGUISHER Handle pulled,

kontext:
AC ELECTRICAL POWER DESCRIPTION

AC electrical power is the main source for airplane systems and comprises:
– Two integrated drive generators (IDGs).
– An auxiliary power unit (APU) generator.
– A ram air turbine (RAT).
– A static inverter (AC/DC inverter).
Both IDGs and the APU generator are rated at 40 kVA, 115 VAC, 400 Hz, three-phase.

On ground, the APU AC generator or AC ground power unit (AC GPU) can supply power to all AC BUSES. The APU generator may also be used in flight, as a replacement to an IDG, according to the APU operational envelope. In flight, the RAT is used as an emergency generator, supplying power to the ESS BUSES when both AC BUSES 1 and 2 are not powered.

kontext:
INTEGRATED DRIVE GENERATOR (IDG)

Each engine has an IDG monitored and controlled by a dedicated generator control unit (GCU). When an engine starts, the IDG will automatically come on line, powering the respective AC BUS. The previous power source is disconnected from that AC BUS.

For automatic operation of the electrical system, the IDG selector knob must be set to the AUTO position. Moving the selector knob to OFF position, the generator line contactor opens, tripping off-line and de- exciting the selected IDG.

When the IDG oil pressure drops below 140 psi 25 psi, or the IDG oil temperature reaches 335°F 10°F (168°C 5°C), the EICAS message IDG 1 (2) OIL is displayed and an amber led illuminates near the IDG selector knob on the overhead panel. This led indicates which IDG must be disconnected and extinguishes after the IDG disconnection.
Manual IDG disconnection is achieved by selecting the respective IDG knob to the DISC position and holding for one second.

NOTE: Do not hold IDG knob to the DISC position for more than three seconds.

Automatic IDG disconnection occurs when manual disconnection is not performed, and the IDG oil temperature reaches 366°F (185.6°C).

In both cases, the disconnection is mechanical and the flight crew cannot reconnect the IDG.

fragen.erklaerung_en: Manual disconnection is done by holding in DISC for one second; the button should not be held in DISC for longer than three seconds. The disconnection is mechanical and cannot be reversed.

fragen.zitat: Whenever AC power sources are not powering AC buses, the RAT is automatically deployed, and after 8 s, supplies power to the AC ESS BUS.
kontext:
RAM AIR TURBINE (RAT)

The RAT is an AC electrical device installed in the airplane nose section, which converts the kinetic energy of airflow across the turbine into AC power. The electrical power produced is rated at 15 kVA, 115 V AC, 400 Hz, three-phase.
Whenever AC power sources are not powering AC buses, the RAT is automatically deployed, and after 8 s, supplies power to the AC ESS BUS.

Once deployed it will create a very loud noise due to the high

14-05-10

REVISION 22 AC System Page 3/6

rotation speed, and cannot be stowed back in flight, even if normal electrical power is reestablished. DC ESS BUSES are powered through the ESS TRU. To avoid total loss of power during this 8 s period, batteries are used as backup to power the DC ESS BUSES and the STANDBY AC BUS.

The RAT electrical power drives the AC Motor-driven Pump (ACMP 3A) for primary flight control tasks. These include high lift system actuation and power for essential avionics, communication and battery recharging.

In flight, there is no altitude restriction for RAT deployment.

130 kt is required to ensure the RAT continues supplying AC/DC ESS BUSES. At speeds below this, the RAT may only supply the AC ESS BUS, and the batteries will automatically provide electrical power to the DC ESS BUSES and the STANDBY AC BUS through the static inverter (AC/DC inverter). As airspeed decreases, load shedding occurs and the AC ESS BUS is no longer powered.

In case of automatic RAT deployment failure, a deployment handle is provided to manually deploy the RAT.
EM170AOM140063.DGN

fragen.frage: Wie lange versorgen die Batterien in einer ELECTRICAL EMERGENCY die Essential Loads, solange die RAT nicht voll ausgefahren ist bzw. RAT Stall Speed erreicht ist?

fragen.zitat: In an ELECTRICAL EMERGENCY, while the RAT is not fully deployed and also if RAT stall speed is reached, batteries supply essential loads for 10 min.
kontext:
TRANSFORMER RECTIFIER UNIT (TRU)

Three TRUs convert 115 VAC power into 28 VDC. Each TRU works in isolation. If one of them fails, the BUSES are automatically powered by the remaining TRUs, as long as the DC BUS TIES toggle switch is selected to AUTO.

TRU 1 provides DC power to DC BUS 1, DC ESS BUS 1, DC GND SVC BUS, HOT BATT BUS 1 and battery #1 charging.

TRU 2 provides DC power to DC BUS 2, DC ESS BUS 2, HOT BATT BUS 2 and battery #2 charging.

TRU ESS provides DC power to DC ESS BUS 3.

BATTERIES

Two NiCd 22.8 VDC, 27 A batteries power up the airplane and are also used as a backup for the DC essential electrical system.

The batteries charges constantly by any AC source through the TRUs, including the AC GPU and the RAT.
In an ELECTRICAL EMERGENCY, while the RAT is not fully deployed and also if RAT stall speed is reached, batteries supply essential loads for 10 min.

Whenever the battery temperature reaches 70°C for at least 2 s, the associated indication becomes red and the EICAS WARNING message BATT 1 (2) OVERTEMP is triggered.

On ground, if the airplane is powered only by the batteries for more than 5 min, a horn sounds to alert the ground personnel.

NOTE: The check for batteries voltage is not valid if any AC source is powering the airplane. In this case, the TRU voltage is indicated instead of the batteries voltage.

fragen.frage: Bei ungefähr welcher N2 kommandiert das FADEC nach Light-off den Starter-Cutout?

fragen.zitat: After a light off occurs, the FADEC commands the starter to cutout at approximately 50% N2
kontext:
GROUND START

190/195 models, Post-Mod ENGINE FADEC 5.61

The FADEC initiates ignition at approximately 7% N2 and the fuel flow (metering valve opens) from 20% to 25% N2, depending on the engine start altitude.

If no light off is detected within 15 s of fuel on, FADEC automatically turns off ignition and fuel, continue dry motoring for 30 s, then turn on single ignition and turn on fuel again.

After 7 s of single ignition is applied, FADEC commands dual ignition for 8 s.

If no light off is detected after 15 s of the reintroduction of fuel or after start duty limit is reached, whichever occurs first, the FADEC does not turn off fuel or ignition automatically.

In case of cold soaked engine or high altitude conditions and no light off is detected, FADEC inhibits the EICAS messages "ENG 1 (2) NO DISPATCH" during the first attempt cycle for engine start.
After a light off occurs, the FADEC commands the starter to cutout at approximately 50% N2,

and commands the FMU fuel metering valve to accelerate the engine to ground idle speed.

At high altitudes, the fuel flow schedule is also increased to provide higher torque and therefore quicker starts.

kontext:
SYSTEMS DESCRIPTION AIRPLANE

Thrust reverser deployment occurs only if the airplane is on ground.
The thrust reverser trigger can be lifted within 30 seconds after an engine inoperative condition is detected.

After this time, the thrust reverse trigger is not released, and the respective thrust lever cannot be moved to the reverse positions.

Idle reverse thrust is commanded while the thrust reverser cowls are in transit. After total deployment of the thrust reverser cowls, maximum reverse thrust is commanded if the thrust levers are held in MAX REV position.

In case one thrust reverser fails, when selecting both TLA to MAX REV position, the operative thrust reverser provides minimum reverse thrust only. Selecting only the operating thrust reverser TLA to MAX REV position enables maximum reverse thrust on this engine.

The thrust reverser is not designed to operate in flight. In case of uncommanded thrust reverser deployment, the engine thrust is limited to idle.

The Flight Control System is comprised of the primary and the secondary flight control systems and their associated system components.

The primary flight control system consists of:
– Ailerons and the multi function roll spoilers for roll axis control.
– Elevators for pitch axis control.
– Rudder for yaw axis control.
The secondary flight control system consists of:
– Horizontal stabilizer.
– Flaps and Slats.
– The multi-function spoiler (when used as speed brakes or ground spoilers).
– Dedicated ground spoilers.
Hydraulic actuators control the respective flight control surfaces. These are referred to as Power Control Units (PCUs).
The ailerons are commanded by conventional control cables that run from each control wheel back to a pair of hydro-mechanical actuators.

Elevators, rudders, roll spoilers as well as all secondary flight control systems, including the horizontal stabilizer, flaps and slats, ground spoilers and speed brakes, are controlled electronically using Fly-by- Wire (FBW) technology.

The primary flight control electronics include two complementary parts:
– The Primary Actuator Control Electronics (P-ACE).
– The Flight Control Module (FCM).
Primary Actuator Control Electronics (P-ACE) and/or Flight Control Modules (FCM) are employed to operate the respective electro- hydraulic or electro-mechanical actuators.

kontext:
MULTI-FUNCTION AND GROUND SPOILERS

DEPLOYMENT

After touchdown the FCM will command all multifunction spoiler surfaces to the 40° extended position and the ground spoiler surfaces to 60° when the following conditions are simultaneously met:
– Weight on wheels on ground.
– Wheel speed is above 45 kt or airspeed is above 60 KIAS.
– Thrust Lever Angle (TLA) below 26°.
Following rollout, the spoilers will automatically retract when wheel speed is below 45 kt for at least 5 s. If the throttles are moved beyond 35° (TLA) after landing, the spoiler panels will automatically retract.

In a bounced landing, the FCM holds the “on ground” signal for 5 s after the WOW signals indicate “in air”. However, if the pilot commands TLA greater than 35° the ground spoilers are retracted.
NOTE: In the direct mode, ground spoilers are not available.

kontext:
MANUAL TRIM

The manual trim is commanded through switches installed on the control wheels or a backup switch located on the main pedestal. The HS-ACE receives the commands from the control wheels or the

14-08-15

Page 8/10 Pitch Control REVISION 25

backup switches and then controls an electrical servo motor coupled to the HSA.

The control wheels and backup trim switches are dual split. Both halves of the switch must be pressed simultaneously to command the horizontal stabilizer surface.

There is no movement in the horizontal stabilizer surface when only one half of the switch is actuated. If half switch is kept actuated and this disagreement persists for more than 7 s, that switch is automatically deactivated and the applicable advisory PITCH TRIM SW FAIL message is displayed on EICAS. If this condition persists with only half switch pressed for more than 8 s, even though the horizontal stabilizer surface is not moving, the aural warning "TRIM" is activated as an indication of disagreement. The switch remains deactivated until next Power Up or PITCH TRIM SYS CUTOUT is actuated.

Manual commands via PITCH TRIM Switches and Pitch Trim BACKUP SW Switch are limited to 3 s. After the wheels or backup switches have both halves pressed for more than 3 s, the horizontal stabilizer control surface stops moving and if the switch remains pressed, the aural warning “TRIM” triggers. When the switch is no more pressed, the aural warning stops. In case of stick shaker activation, the HS-ACE is prevented from responding to any pitch trim up commands by a stick shaker signal from the AFCS.

Stabilizer Trim priority Logic

The HS-ACE responds to all trim commands with the following priority:
1. Backup switches.

2. LH PITCH TRIM Switch (Captain).
3. RH PITCH TRIM Switch (First Officer).
4. FCM (auto-trim) commands.

FLY-BY-WIRE (FBW) BACKUP BATTERY

In case of an extremely improbable failure that would render complete loss of normal and emergency electrical power to the FBW,
the backup power system, with no pilot intervention, keeps the appropriate number of elevator and rudder actuators operating for at least 15 min.

There is no dedicated message to indicate the failure of this system; therefore there is no flight crew action required if this happens.

This backup system is comprised by a dedicated battery, distribution bus and circuit breakers.

REVISION 22 FCS Description Page 9/10

The backup battery consists of sealed lead acid cells with built-in-test (BIT) capability and an internal heater that guarantees the minimum battery temperature.
EMBRAER 190/195 models PRE-MOD SB190-27-0047 The backup battery is charged by the DC ESS BUS 3 during normal operation.

EMBRAER 190/195 models POST-MOD. SB170-27-0047 or with an equivalent modification factory incorporated The backup battery is charged by the DC ESS BUS 1 during normal operation.

Although the battery is connected to the airplane buses, the use of an internal rectifier keeps it from powering back the buses, assuring isolation in case of failure in the main electrical power system.

The Power Up Built in Test (PBIT) reduces the flight control system exposition to latent faults, ensuring that the system components remain capable of executing their functions.

The PBIT is provided for both the Electrical and Hydraulic systems.

CAUTION message will only be displayed after landing.

Hydraulic System 2 is comprised of one reservoir, one engine-driven pump (EDP 2), one electric hydraulic pump, one accumulator and one PTU. The Hydraulic System 2 supplies the following systems:
