kontext:
ELECTRIC HYDRAULIC PUMPS

Both Electric Hydraulic Pumps are alternating current motor pumps (ACMP).
Electric Hydraulic Pump 3A (ACMP 3A) is the primary power source for Hydraulic System 3 and it is powered by the AC ESS BUS.

A two-position selector knob located on the hydraulic panel enables the flight crew to select OFF or ON positions. There is no automation associated with this pump. So in normal operation, the flight crew will turn the pump ON and OFF during engine start and shutdown, respectively.

Electric Hydraulic Pump 3B (ACMP 3B) is the backup for the Electric Hydraulic Pump 3A and it is powered by the AC BUS 2. The flight crew selects manual or automatic operation through the three-position selector knob on the hydraulic control panel. Normal operation is automatic.

In flight, with the selector knob in the AUTO position, the hydraulic system logic turns on the electric pump 3B whenever the electric pump 3A fails. When the selector knob is set to the ON position, the electric pump operates continuously overriding the system automation.

fragen.zitat: Under normal conditions, the low-level warning message activation point is set at 400 kg of fuel in the associated wing tank.
kontext:
FUEL LOW-LEVEL WARNING

Each wing tank has a dedicated Fuel Low-Level Sensor located in the collector box. The Fuel Low-Level Sensor is independent of the fuel quantity indication system. Whenever the fuel level in the collector box is below the sensor level, it sends a fuel low-level signal to the warning system, thus triggering the FUEL LO LEVEL warning EICAS message.

NOTE: FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL may appear spuriously when flying with high pitch and/or bank angles.
Under normal conditions, the low-level warning message activation point is set at 400 kg of fuel in the associated wing tank.

If any scavenge pump stops transferring fuel to the Collector Box, which might be caused by an engine failure, loss of motive flow or scavenge pumps failure/blockage, the fuel contained in the Collector Box flows out so that the fuel level inside the Collector Box and the rest of the tank reaches the same level.

Under this condition, if there is up to 2800 kg (approximately) of fuel inside that tank it is possible that the level equivalent to the low-level warning activation point will be reached as the fuel level inside the collector box decreases, then FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL warning EICAS message displays indicating that fuel level is below the Low-Level Sensor.

Therefore, in case of loss of the transfer system to the Collector Box, the EICAS WARNING message FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL may display even though fuel quantity indication on the EICAS or MFD Fuel System Synoptic Page is up to 2800 kg in that tank.

NOTE: – In case of loss of the transfer system to the Collector Box followed by the EICAS warning message, fuel quantity indication monitoring during the flight is achieved through EICAS, or MFD Fuel System synoptic page.
– Engine flameout due to fuel starvation may occur if the airplane is subjected to attitudes greater than 15° nose up or down, uncoordinated maneuvers or negative g’s.

kontext:
REF A/I MODES OF OPERATION

The REF A/I mode of operation can be selected on ground using the OAT/visible moisture table presented in ICING CONDITIONS, COLD WEATHER AND COLD SOAK OPERATIONS supplementary procedure, in block 3-75.

The MCDU setting operates the anti-ice system and inhibits the ice detectors activation logic during takeoff until 1700 ft AGL or 2 min after liftoff, whichever occur first. The settings actuate as described below:

OFF – The anti-ice valves will be inhibited closed until the end of takeoff phase, considered in the logic as 1700 ft AGL or 2 min after liftoff. After that, the engine and wing anti-ice valves will open if ice is detected.

ENG – Only the engine anti-ice valve will be kept open after engine start. The wing anti-ice valves remains inhibited closed. The EICAS status message ENG TDS REF A-I ENG will be displayed to confirm the MCDU selection.

ALL
– The engine anti-ice valves are commanded open after completion of engine start and the wing anti-ice valves are commanded open with wheel speed above 40 kt.

The EICAS status message ENG TDS REF A-I ALL will be displayed to confirm the MCDU selection.

In ENG or ALL operation modes, the anti-ice valves will rely on ice detection above 1700 ft AGL or 2 min after liftoff.

In OFF or ENG operation modes and anti-ice mode selector knob set to ON position, the caution message “ENG REF A-I DISAG” and the advisory message “A-I MODE NOT AUTO” will be displayed on the EICAS. In this case, the pilot needs to rotate the selector knob to AUTO position.

If the REF A/I is set to ENG on the MCDU and the OAT temperature entered at the Takeoff Data Setting is below 5°C, the CAS message “ENG REF A-I DISAG” will be displayed.

kontext:
EICAS MESSAGES CATEGORIZATION

There are four message priority levels:
– Warning.
– Caution.
– Advisory.

REVISION 25 Visual Warning Page 1/16

– Status.
WARNING (red): indicates an emergency or airplane system condition that requires immediate corrective or compensatory crew action.

CAUTION (amber): indicates an abnormal operational or airplane system conditions that require immediate crew awareness and should require a subsequent corrective or compensatory action.
ADVISORY (cyan): indicates operational or airplane conditions that require crew awareness.

Subsequent or future crew action may be required.

STATUS (white): indicates information/status messages. The pilot can use the system efficiently when the appropriate action is accomplished.

A fifth level is provided for maintenance and is not available during flight operation. It is accessed only on ground.

Messages with the higher priority precede other messages when shown simultaneously. The EICAS displays up to 15 messages simultaneously.

The MCDU displays some messages in the event of a failure of both MFD and the EICAS.

kontext:
DUMP MODE ACTIVATION:

The DUMP function is activated pushing in the DUMP button on the pressurization panel. The DUMP function is operational for CPCS either in Automatic or Manual Modes.

In case the DUMP is activated, the CPCS automatically:
– Sets the ECS packs and recirculation fans to OFF
– In CPCS Automatic Mode,
controls the OUTFLOW VALVE to maintain the cabin rate of climb at 2000 ft/min up to 12400 ft for normal takeoff and landing operation,

In case higher cabin rates of climb are necessary, the manual mode can be used selecting the cabin altitude to up position on the CABIN ALT rotary knob on the pressurization panel.

To improve fuel consumption, a feature in AMS software named Smart ECS controls packs flow in normal operation conditions. The SMART ECS calculates the optimum pack flow for each flight altitude based on airplane's model, passenger cabin layout (LOPA), and on number of occupants on board.

The input of occupants on board is retrieved from pilots entered data on FMS PERFORMANCE INIT PAGE 2/3.
If the pilot fills in 0 for the number of occupants (PASS 0), the SMART ECS is disabled.

If the pilot does not fill in the number of occupants (PASS the SMART ECS considers full pax, according to airplane LOPA. The number of occupants on board must consider passengers and crew.

kontext:
RAM AIR TURBINE (RAT)

The Ram Air Turbine (RAT) is an emergency AC electrical device installed in the airplane nose section.
In flight, there is no altitude restriction for the RAT deployment, and the minimum deployment speed is 150 kt.

If the minimum deployment speed is respected, whenever the AC power sources are not powering the AC buses, the RAT is automatically deployed. In about 8 s, the RAT starts supplying power to the AC ESS BUS.

The RAT also powers the DC ESS BUSES through the ESS TRU. To avoid total loss of power during the RAT deployment and speeding up period, batteries are used as backup to power the DC ESS BUSES.

14-05-10

REVISION 15 AC System Page 3/6

Even if normal electrical power is re-established, once deployed, the RAT cannot be stowed back in flight. In this case, the RAT keeps providing power to the AC ESS BUS and DC ESS BUS 3.

The RAT electrical power drives the AC Motor-driven Pump (ACMP 3A) for commands on primary flight controls, including high lift system actuation. It also provides power to the essential avionics, communication, and battery recharging.

The RAT requires a minimum of 130 kt to ensure continuous power supply to AC/DC ESS BUSES. At speeds below 130 kt, the RAT is not capable of supplying power to all essential buses, so the batteries automatically connect to the DC ESS BUSES, while the RAT keeps feeding the AC ESS BUS until a certain airspeed.

In case of failure on automatic RAT deployment, a deployment handle is available to release the RAT manually.

kontext:
INTEGRATED DRIVE GENERATOR (IDG)

Each engine has an IDG. A dedicated generator control unit (GCU) controls and monitors each IDG. As an engine spools up, the respective IDG automatically comes on line, powering the respective AC BUS. The previous power source is disconnected from that AC BUS.

Each IDG selector knob in AUTO position sets the electrical system to automatic operation.

If a selector knob is moved to the OFF position, the respective generator line contactor opens, tripping off-line and de-exciting the related IDG.

When an IDG low oil pressure or oil overtemperature condition is detected, the CAS message IDG 1 (2) OIL displays. Additionally, an amber light illuminates next to the respective IDG selector knob on the overhead panel. The amber light indicates the IDG to be disconnected and extinguishes after the IDG disconnection.

14-05-10

Page 2/6 AC System REVISION 15
Manual IDG disconnection is achieved by selecting the respective IDG knob to the DISC position and holding for one second.

Automatic IDG disconnection occurs when flight crew does not perform the manual disconnection after an abnormal detection and indication of oil low pressure or oil overtemperature.

An IDG disconnection means that the IDG is mechanically disconnected. The flight crew cannot perform a reconnection and the IDG remains disconnect until a maintenance action is performed.

fragen.erklaerung_en: The manual IDG disconnect is done by holding in DISC for 1 s; after that, reconnection is possible only by maintenance (OFF merely opens the line contactor).

fragen.frage: Bei welcher N2 schliesst der FADEC beim Start das Starter Control Valve (Starter Cutout)?

Zwischen 49 % und 55 % N2, abhängig von den Umgebungsbedingungen

fragen.zitat: The FADEC closes the SCV when the starter cutout speed is reached, which is a function of ambient conditions and varies between 49% and 55% N2.
kontext:
STARTING SYSTEM

The engine starting system consists of:
– Air Turbine Starter (ATS), and
– Starter Control Valve (SCV).
The pneumatic system provides bleed air to the ATS to rotate the rotorspeed and start the engine. The FADEC opens the SCV, providing bleed air from the APU, a ground source, or the opposite engine. The Air Turbine Starter (ATS) is a turbine that accelerates the engine to a self-sustaining rpm level.
The FADEC closes the SCV when the starter cutout speed is reached, which is a function of ambient conditions and varies between 49% and 55% N2.
fragen.frage_en: At what N2 does FADEC close the starter control valve during start (starter cutout)?
antworten_en: Fixed at 58 % N2
Between 49 % and 55 % N2, depending on ambient conditions
Fixed at 45 % N2
Between 20 % and 27 % N2
fragen.erklaerung_en: The starter cutout speed depends on ambient conditions and is between 49 % and 55 % N2; at 20–27 % N2 ignition and fuel are switched on.

fragen.frage: Wie viele Fuel-Depulse-Zyklen darf der FADEC bei einem Ground Start höchstens versuchen?
fragen.erklaerung: Am Boden sind bis zu 2 Fuel-Depulse-Zyklen möglich (Fuel 2 s aus, 12 s an), im Flug bis zu 10.
fragen.zitat: On the ground, FADEC may attempt up to 2 fuel depulse cycles.
kontext:
GROUND START

During an engine start, the FADEC automatically sequences the starting system, ignition system, and fuel flow to start the engine.

The FADEC commands open the start air valve to allow the starter to accelerate the engine, and a green AES indication is displayed on EICAS. The Motor to Start (MTS) is commanded at low N2 to clear any bow in the rotor. The ignition and fuel flow are commanded once N2 has reached enough speed (from 20% to 27% N2) to provide actuation pressure to the fuel metering valve. The SCV closes and ignition is off when the predetermined starter cutout speed is reached, and fuel flow is scheduled to bring the engine to idle.

NOTE: FADEC 9.6.6 increases the motor to start (MTS) dwell time from 30 seconds to 45 seconds during engine start. This time may be extended by the FADEC if the engine is warmer than typical.

During a ground start, protection against starting failures is provided, including:
– Hot start
– Hung start
– Failure of N1 to rotate
– Failure to light, and
– Inability to control the igniter or fuel flow.
NOTE: – When FADEC detects a surge or an impending hot start, a fuel depulse is commanded. Fuel is cycled off for 2 seconds and back on for 12 seconds.
On the ground, FADEC may attempt up to 2 fuel depulse cycles.

– When FADEC detects a fail to light or a hot or hung start, an auto-restart attempt is performed. Fuel and ignition are commanded off for at least 30 seconds. If the auto-restart attempt fails, FADEC aborts the start and commands a 30 seconds dry motoring before commanding the starter valve to close.

14-06-20

Page 2/4 Start and Ignition System REVISION 14

Keine Protection gegen Hot Start, Hung Start oder Failure to Light. Die Crew muss überwachen und manuell abbrechen
Automatischer Auto-Restart mit 30 s Dry Motoring
Nur Hot-Start-Protection mit automatischem Abbruch nach 2 Depulse-Zyklen

fragen.zitat: The FADEC has no protection for hot starts, hung starts, or failure to light off for in flight engine starts.
kontext:
INFLIGHT START

When the airplane is within the assisted start envelope (refer to ENGINE AIRSTART ENVELOPE) the FADEC commands the starter to accelerate the engine. A white AES indication is displayed when the FADEC identifies that the engine is within the assisted restart envelope. The AES indication becomes green when FADEC is commanding an assisted restart.

Outside the assisted restart envelope, the starter is not commanded, allowing the engine to windmill in the airstream to accelerate. A white WML indication is displayed when the FADEC identifies that the engine is within the windmilling restart envelope. If the N2 is lower than 8.5% within the windmilling start envelope, the FADEC commands an assisted engine start and the green AES indication is displayed. The WML indication becomes green when FADEC is commanding a windmilling start.

When the engine reaches the speed to provide actuation pressure to the fuel metering valve, the FADEC commands ignition and fuel flow.

The FADEC commands the depressurization of the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) if N2 is below 25%.
The FADEC has no protection for hot starts, hung starts, or failure to light off for in flight engine starts.

NOTE: – When FADEC detects a surge or an impending hot start, a fuel depulse is commanded. Fuel is cycled off for 2 seconds and back on for 12 seconds. In flight, FADEC may attempt up to 10 fuel depulse cycles.
– This logic does not abort the engine start automatically.
Flight crew remains responsible for monitoring engine parameters and manually abort the start.
fragen.frage_en: What start protection functions does FADEC provide during an inflight engine start?
antworten_en: Full protection including automatic start abort as on the ground
No protection against hot start, hung start or failure to light. The crew must monitor and abort manually
Automatic auto-restart with 30 s dry motoring
Only hot start protection with automatic abort after 2 depulse cycles
fragen.erklaerung_en: For inflight starts, FADEC has no protection against hot/hung start or failure to light; the crew remains responsible for monitoring and aborting.

ASSUMED TEMPERATURE REDUCED THRUST

In many situations, the airplane takes off at weights lower than the maximum permissible takeoff weight. In consequence, it is possible to continue complying with performance limitations using a decreased engine thrust adapted to the actual weight. This is called flex takeoff thrust method. This method is also known as assumed temperature reduced thrust.

kontext:
ENGINE FIRE EXTINGUISHER BOTTLE

A total of two fire extinguisher bottles named A and B are installed in the airplane to serve either or both engines.

Each fire handle is connected to both fire extinguisher bottles.

OPERATION

Pulling the FIRE HANDLE closes the fuel shutoff valve and the engine is shut down, allowing the operation of extinguisher bottles.
Rotating the FIRE HANDLE counter clockwise discharges extinguisher bottle A into the associated engine.

Rotating clockwise discharges extinguisher bottle B into the same engine.

NOTE: When an engine fire extinguisher bottle is discharged, fire handle illumination may be lost. In this case if the EICAS message is still active the fire condition persists.

fragen.frage: Bis zu welchem Querneigungswinkel halten die Control Laws im Normal Mode bei neutralem Control Wheel die Roll Rate auf null?
fragen.erklaerung: Bei neutralem Steuer wird die Roll Rate bis 33° Bank auf null gehalten; darüber führt die Bank Protection das Flugzeug auf 33° zurück.
fragen.zitat: If the control wheel is kept at neutral position, the control laws command the surfaces to maintain zero roll rate up to 33° of bank.
kontext:
NORMAL MODE ROLL CONTROL

After Power On, the flight control system starts its operation with the ground control laws. The surface deflection is essentially a direct function of the control wheel position. As the airplane gains speed, the direct relationship between inceptor and surface position remains with an active yaw damper on ground.

When the airplane is in air, a different set of functions becomes active.
The standard lateral control law in air essentially converts the wheel deflection on a roll rate demand.
If the control wheel is kept at neutral position, the control laws command the surfaces to maintain zero roll rate up to 33° of bank.

In normal mode, the lateral control laws automatically provide turn coordination. Turns are performed without the need to apply pedal, since the control law automatically deflects the control surfaces to maintain turn coordination.

Two extra protections are also available in normal mode. When a high bank angle or high-speed condition is reached, they become active.
fragen.frage_en: Up to what bank angle do the control laws in normal mode hold the roll rate at zero with a neutral control wheel?
fragen.erklaerung_en: With a neutral control wheel, roll rate is held at zero up to 33° bank; above that, bank protection returns the aircraft to 33°.

fragen.frage: Bei welchen Pitch-Winkeln greift die Pitch Attitude Protection im Normal Mode?

Unter 15° nose down oder über 25° nose up

fragen.zitat: The pitch protection engages when the pitch angle is lower than 15° pitch down or higher than 30° pitch up.
kontext:
PITCH PROTECTION

The flight control system provides the pitch attitude protection as an additional function provided to increase the effectiveness of the stall protection and high-speed protection.

The low pitch protection creates an additional positive load factor command and reduces the column pitch down authority.

The high pitch protection creates an additional negative load factor command and reduces the column pitch up authority.
The pitch protection engages when the pitch angle is lower than 15° pitch down or higher than 30° pitch up.

The pitch protection is essentially the default in air normal mode behavior with an additional command to avoid excessive pitch angles.

There are no hard limits in terms of achievable attitude angles. Even with the authority restricted in this specific situation to make harder the achievement of unusual attitudes, the pilot is left with enough authority to maneuver the airplane.

14-08-15

REVISION 12 Pitch Control Page 7/12

kontext:
DIRECT MODE PITCH CONTROL

The Direct Mode is a degraded mode of operation and has a more limited set of functions compared to the Normal Mode. There is no envelope protection when the flight control system is in direct mode.

Direct Mode is engaged automatically after loss of inertial or air data sensing, or manually by the flight crew when pressing the button in Flight Control Mode Panel.

Direct Mode requires the following minimum operational sensor configuration:
– Any two inertial sensor units.
– Any single ADSP.

When operating in direct mode, both in air and on ground, the elevator moves as a direct function of the column position. In direct mode, there is stability augmentation in pitch and yaw axes. The elevator deflection is scheduled as a function of flap position and airspeed.

In direct mode, the pitch trim switches directly command the horizontal stabilizer position. The rate of change in the horizontal stabilizer is scheduled by airspeed.

fragen.erklaerung_en: Direct mode requires at least any two inertial sensor units and any one ADSP.

kontext:
POWER UP BUILT IN TEST (PBIT)

The Power Up Built in Test (PBIT) consists of a set of automatic tests to reduce the flight control system exposition to latent faults.

The PBIT is provided for both the Electrical and Hydraulic systems.
The PBIT expires after 50 hours (elapsed time) since the last successful execution.

Once the PBIT is expired, FLT CTRL BIT EXPIRED EICAS CAUTION message is displayed. This EICAS message is provided for both Electrical PBIT and Hydraulic PBIT. The message remains displayed on EICAS until a new Electrical and Hydraulic PBIT is successfully performed.

The EICAS Message FLT CTRL BIT EXPIRED is only displayed when the airplane is on ground.

kontext:
FLY-BY-WIRE BACKUP BATTERY

The fly-by-wire backup system provides power for essential functions after complete loss of normal electrical power to the flight control system. This backup system consists of a dedicated battery, distribution bus, and circuit breakers. The backup battery is located in the forward electronic bay.
With no pilot intervention, the backup system keeps the appropriate number of electronic units operating for at least 30 min when fully charged.

There is no dedicated message to indicate the failure of this system.

OPERATING WITH RAM AIR TURBINE (RAT)

In Electrical Emergency conditions, the Ram Air Turbine (RAT) is the only source of electric power. During Electrical Emergency, the flaps and slats operate in sequential actuation and half speed. Additionally,
the flaps and slats are prevented to deploy beyond position three to assure adequate airspeed for the RAT.

fragen.frage: Was bewirkt der Pitch Trim Switch im Normal Mode in der Luft?
antworten: Er verstellt den Elevator direkt proportional zur Betätigungsdauer
Er ist in der Luft inhibitiert
Er ändert das Speed Target der Control Laws
Er bewegt den Horizontal Stabilizer direkt
fragen.erklaerung: Im Normal Mode in der Luft bewegt der Trim Switch den Stabilizer nicht direkt, sondern verändert das Speed Target; am Boden und im Direct Mode wirkt er direkt auf den Stabilizer.
fragen.zitat: Pressing the trim switch represents a change in the speed target for the control laws.
kontext:
NORMAL MODE PITCH CONTROL

After Power On, the flight control system starts its operation with the ground control laws. The elevator surface deflection is essentially a direct function of the control column position, scheduled with flap position and airspeed.

During the takeoff run, as the Thrust Levers are moved towards TO/GA, a nose-down elevator offset is automatically commanded to increase steering controllability.

During takeoff roll, a rotation function is activated to make easier the procedure of capturing a specific pitch attitude during takeoff.

Once the airplane is in air, the default control law in air becomes active.

The control column displacement is not directly related to an elevator deflection, but it is proportional to a rate of change in the flight path angle. The control laws calculate and command the amount of elevator deflection needed for the maneuver.

In normal mode, a load factor protection is always active, which varies if the flaps are deflected or not. Even if the pilot applies full control column command, the load factor commanded never exceeds the maximum load factor allowable by the control laws.

To trim the airplane in a new trim airspeed, as a conventional airplane, it is necessary to apply control columns or trim inputs. If trim inputs are not applied, the airplane gradually returns to its original trim speed after the control column is released.

If the airplane is trimmed in a determined airspeed and the elevator position is greater than a given threshold, the offload function activates. This function offloads the elevator by converting its deflection to an equivalent Horizontal stabilizer position.

In that sense, if the airplane is in air in normal mode, the trim switch does not directly move the horizontal stabilizer.
Pressing the trim switch represents a change in the speed target for the control laws.

The FCCs then command the proper amount of elevator to trim the airplane in the new airspeed and, if needed, the offload function is

14-08-15

Page 2/12 Pitch Control REVISION 12

activated. Therefore, the trim scale may not immediately reflect the trim operation as the trim switches are commanded by the pilots.

On ground, the pitch trim switches directly commands the horizontal stabilizer surface.

During turns, the Lift Compensation feature partially compensates the natural loss of lift due to the airplane roll. To maintain a level flight, only a small column compensation in pitch axes is required.

During a landing procedure, the de-rotation function becomes available on ground. It controls the airplane rotation rate during touchdown, so airplane behavior is uniform, regardless of mass and CG location.

14-08-15

REVISION 12 Pitch Control Page 3/12

fragen.erklaerung_en: In normal mode in the air, the trim switch does not move the stabilizer directly but changes the speed target; on the ground and in direct mode it acts directly on the stabilizer.

indicating a low- level condition on the respective wing tank when the fuel quantity is below 400 kg (880 lb).

kontext:
FUEL CROSSFEED

The crossfeed operation permits fuel supply to both engines from one wing tank, leveling fuel quantities in both wing tanks and avoiding a fuel imbalance condition. During single engine operation, the crossfeed is also used to supply fuel to the operative engine from both wing tanks.

Setting the crossfeed selector knob to either LOW 1 or LOW 2 position:
– opens the crossfeed valve
– activates the AC fuel pump of the opposite wing tank.
The EICAS message FUEL IMBALANCE displays when an imbalance condition between both wing tanks is equal or greater than 360 kg (800 lb).

After the imbalance is less than 45 kg (100 lb), the EICAS message FUEL EQUAL – XFEED OPEN displays, indicating a crossfeed operation with no imbalance condition.

If a crossfeed operation is commanded before the EICAS message FUEL IMBALANCE is triggered, the EICAS message FUEL EQUAL – XFEED OPEN displays.

The following table shows the position of crossfeed selector knob to correct or avoid a fuel imbalance.

REFUELING AND DEFUELING

There is a single pressurized refueling/defueling point and a refuel/ defuel control panel located under the right wing. When the access panel door is opened with the airplane energized, the following effects occur:
– Indication of door open displays on MFD status page and on EICAS through DOOR FUELING OPEN advisory message.

Pressurized refueling is performed with the airplane energized either by AC or battery power. A switch at the refueling panel enables selection of either power sources.

The refuel port on top of each wing also allows the refueling of wing fuel tanks.
Gravity refueling is not available for center tank.

The individual fuel quantity is displayed on EICAS or MFD synoptic page.

kontext:
ELECTRIC HYDRAULIC PUMPS

Both Electric Hydraulic Pumps are alternating current motor pumps (ACMP). Electric Hydraulic Pump 3A (ACMP 3A) is the primary power source for Hydraulic System 3. The AC ESS BUS powers the ACMP 3A.

A two-position selector knob on the hydraulic panel enables the flight crew to select OFF or ON positions.
There is no automation associated with this pump. So in normal operation, the flight crew turns the pump ON and OFF during engine start and shutdown, respectively.

Electric Hydraulic Pump 3B (ACMP 3B) is the backup for the Electric Hydraulic Pump 3A. The AC BUS 2 power the ACMP 3B. The flight crew selects manual or automatic operation through the three-position selector knob on the hydraulic control panel. Normal operation is automatic.

POWER TRANSFER UNIT (PTU)

The PTU consists of a hydraulic pump in Hydraulic System 2 driven by a hydraulic motor installed in Hydraulic System 1.
It is used for landing gear retraction in case of EDP 2 or engine 2 failure.

A three-position selector knob on the hydraulic panel enables the flight crew to select OFF, AUTO, or ON positions. Normal operation is automatic.

– Flaps not set to zero or landing gear not up and locked

EMERGENCY/PARKING BRAKE

The Emergency/Parking Brake is used to stop the airplane when a failure happens simultaneously on both hydraulic systems or if both brake controls fail.

The Emergency/Parking Brake is operated through a lever located in the pedestal control panel, mechanically commanded by cable, and powered by hydraulic systems 1 and 2.

The Emergency/Parking Brake system has pressure accumulators isolated from both normal hydraulic systems.
The accumulators have enough trapped pressure to provide six full-brake applications in case that both hydraulic systems fail.

ANTISKID PROTECTION

Antiskid protection prevents tire skidding and maximizes brake efficiency.

The system controls the hydraulic pressure applied to the brakes and, if necessary, reduces the wheel brake pressure to recover wheel speed and prevent tire skidding.
For wheel speeds below 10 kt, the antiskid protection is deactivated,

thus allowing the pilot to lock and pivot on a wheel for maneuvering.

Antiskid protection is not available for the Emergency/Parking Brake system.

RUDDER PEDAL STEERING MODE

The rudder pedal steering mode is designed to be used on high-speed operations on the ground or whenever a large turn angle is not required.

OPERATION

Rudder pedal steering is active on the ground at any time the EICAS message STEER OFF is not displayed and the handwheel is not pressed. kontext:
ICE PROTECTION SYSTEM

The ice protection system includes two ice detectors and ice protection for wings, engines, windshield, air data smart probes, TAT probes and water lines. The engines and wings anti-ice systems use hot bleed air from the engines as a heat source. Windshield, air data smart probes, TAT probes, and water lines use electrical power.

During normal operation, the system automatically controls the engine and the wing anti-ice valves operation.

If both ice detectors fail, manual operation of anti-ice system is possible.

The windshield heaters have two dedicated controllers for operation, one per side.

The front windshields are equipped with two independent wipers operated through dedicated wiper control knobs on the overhead panel.

kontext:
PASSENGER OXYGEN SYSTEM

Individual chemical generators supply oxygen to passengers and flight attendants during an emergency descent in the event of cabin depressurization. Gaseous oxygen supply is provided in the lavatories.

Passenger oxygen masks are located under the overhead bin above the passenger seats.

Each passenger dispensing unit contains either two or three masks.
Two oxygen masks are available in each lavatory. Two oxygen masks are available at each Flight Attendant station, as well as in each galley. 12 minutes Oxygen Generator

The chemical system supplies oxygen for approximately 12 min. The gaseous oxygen system supplies 14 min.

22 minutes Oxygen Generator

The chemical system supplies oxygen for approximately 22 min. The gaseous oxygen system supplies 22 min.

Passenger oxygen mask can be automatically or manually deployed.
The masks are automatically deployed when the cabin altitude is between 14000 ft to 14750 ft.

Manual deployment is possible from the cockpit by positioning the Passenger Oxygen selector knob to the OVRD position. A manual release tool located near each flight attendant station releases the dispensing unit door in case of a failure.

The flight crew monitors the deployment status of the passenger oxygen masks through EICAS messages and an indicator light on the overhead panel.

FULL-FACE MASK OPERATING MODES

Normal: Normal Mode provides supplemental oxygen diluted with cabin air according to the cabin pressure altitude until a preset point where the user inhales 100% oxygen. This feature is to conserve the amount of oxygen consumed from the supply source while still maintaining protective physiological levels.

100%: 100% Mode provides nondiluted oxygen to the crew regardless of cabin altitude.

Flight crew should use this setting to eliminate condensation or to purge smoke and toxic fumes that may get into the mask.

kontext:
EICAS MESSAGES PRESENTATION

The messages are grouped and presented in a chronological order accordingly to its category. The Warning category is placed at the top of the EICAS display. Below this category the system presents the Caution, Advisory, Information and Status category, in this order.

When new Warning, Caution and Advisory alert messages are displayed, they are presented flashing in inverse video for crew acknowledgment.

The warning and caution alert messages shall remain flashing in inverse video until manual crew acknowledgment via Master Warning or Caution button (respectively) is pressed.
Advisory messages automatically revert from inverse to normal video after 5 s they started to be displayed.

After the acknowledgment, the new message remains in steady normal video, at the top of its category on the EICAS display, until a new message belonging to that group appears.

The EICAS messages cannot be cancelable. They shall remain active as long as its activation condition exists.

REVISION 15 Visual Warning Page 5/16

– (W) Warning.
– (C) Caution.
– (A) Advisory.
– (S) Status.
The INHIBITION column indicates the k-codes.

One channel is active while the other works as a hot spare.

kontext:
AUTOLAND MODES

Five modes are related to Autoland:
– Align (ALIGN): engages at 150 ft and maintains the lateral guidance while the airplane aligns with the runway centerline by means of aileron and rudder control.
–
Flare (FLARE): engages at 50 ft and provides vertical guidance

for the transition from glideslope to main gear touchdown.
– Retard (RETD): if the autothrottle is engaged, retard engages at 30 ft and commands throttle to idle.
– De-rotation (D-ROT): engages at main gear touchdown and commands a nose pitch down, touching nose gear down.
– Roll out (RLOUT): engages at main gear touchdown and provides lateral guidance to maintain airplane on the runway centerline.

kontext:
RADIO ALTIMETER SYSTEM

The radio altimeter function measures the airplane height above terrain and sends this information to be displayed on the PFD and to be used by the other airplane systems.

To determine the height the radio altimeter transmits a signal to the ground and processes the time it takes to receive the signal return converting it into radio altitude.
The radio altimeter range of operation is -20 ft to 2500 ft.

When the airplane is parked at the gate or nearby, in the presence of irregular surfaces (i.e. tools, tool carts, stairs, cables, etc), the radio altimeter altitude measurements may be affected. NORMAL OPERATION

The IESS is powered as soon as the airplane battery 1 is selected to ON and airplane battery 2 is selected to AUTO. Then, the IESS starts its alignment phase.
The initial IESS alignment takes about 90 seconds to be completed

and can be identified on the screen by the “INIT 90 s” flag.

Moving the airplane during this period can cause in-flight attitude indication errors that may not be noticeable on ground.

kontext:
ELECTRONIC DISPLAY SYSTEM (EDS)

The EDS is an advanced system that displays primary flight, navigation and system information to the flight crew and consists of:
– Five Display Units (DU).
– One Guidance Panel.
– Two Cursor Control Devices (CCD).
– Two Multi-function Control Display Units (MCDU).
– One EICAS FULL panel.
– Two Reversionary Panels.
– MAU hardware.
– Control I/O modules.
– EDS application software on processor module.
Five display units (DUs) are located on the main instrument panel.
There are two Primary Flight Displays (PFD), two Multifunction Displays (MFD) and one Engine Indication and Crew Alerting System (EICAS). They are identical and interchangeable.

The guidance panel is located in the center of the glareshield above the DUs. The two CCDs, one EICAS FULL panel and the MCDUs are located on the pedestal, whereas the reversionary panels are located on the main instrument panel.

There are four different modes for the DU reversion control for each pilot: PFD, MFD, EICAS and AUTO.
Only DU 2 and DU 4 can be reverted.

DU 1 and DU 5 always operate as PFDs, and DU 3 is always an EICAS. In case of failure of one display, an automatic logic transfer will allow its information to be presented in the remaining units provided that the display selector knob is set to auto position. If the failed display is recovered, it is necessary to manually revert the affected side display selector knob to have the MFD information on associated DU (DU 2 or DU 4) and then return to the AUTO position.
Both sides need to be in AUTO position in order to restore the DU failure mode condition and normal reversion operation.

Rotating the display selector knob to a position other than AUTO forces that selection onto the MFD. When a pilot selected reversion

REVISION 27 Electronic Display System Page 1/26

kontext:
SYSTEM (EICAS) DISPLAY

The EICAS displays engine and system parameters such as flap, gear, spoilers and trim positions, total fuel quantity, APU and environmental information. The EICAS also displays crew awareness messages. For further information on engine parameters and CAS messages shown, refer to section 14-06 Engine and 14-15 Warnings respectively. In case of failure in the EICAS display, its information may be presented in the MFD by appropriately setting the reversionary panel.

An automatic mode de-clutters the EICAS after takeoff.
De-cluttering occurs 30 seconds after landing gear retraction and flap/slat retraction, if all parameters are displaying normal indications.

The following items are de-cluttered from EICAS:
– APU,
– Autobrake,
– Engine vibration,
– Flap position,
– Landing gear position,
– Oil pressure,
– Oil temperature,
– Pitch trim green band,
– Slat position, and
– Speed brake position.
The EICAS FULL pushbutton on the control pedestal inhibits the automatic de-clutter of EICAS. The EICAS is fully displayed when a cautionary condition is detected on one of de-cluttered indications.

In normal conditions, de-clutter is disabled when the landing gear is extended, flap/slat is not at 0, speed brake is deployed, APU on, and/or autobrake (when installed) is armed.

REVISION 27 Electronic Display System Page 15/26

kontext:
COMPARATORS WARNINGS

A comparison between the localizer, glide slope and radio altitude deviation indications are performed when the following conditions are met:
– On-side radio altitude valid and below 1500 ft.
– APR mode selected on Flight Guidance Panel.
– SLAT/FLAP 5.

– CAT II Decision Height setting on both Display Control Panels.
– On-side VOR/LOC active course valid.
– Cross-side data valid.
– Go-around not selected on either side.
– No back course selected.
For localizer, the following additional condition is required:
– Both LOC signals tuned and valid for at least 15 s.
If LOC indications differ by values above approximately 1/2 dot, an amber LOC annunciator will appear flashing (for 10 s).

Refer to ADI/HSI Miscompares in 14-09-05 for details.

For glide slope, the following additional condition is required:
– Both glide slope signals valid and both LOC signals tuned and valid for at least 15 s.
If GS indications differ by values above approximately 2/3 dot, an amber GS annunciator will appear flashing (for 10 s). Refer to ADI/HSI Miscompares in 14-09-05 for details.

For radio altitude, the following additional condition is required:

REVISION 27 Flight Guidance Control System Page 29/36

– Both radio altimeters signals valid and on scale.
If radio altimeters indications differ more than a set point, an amber RA annunciator will appear flashing (for 10 s). Refer to ADI/HSI Miscompares in 14-09-05 for details.

kontext:
INERTIAL REFERENCE SYSTEM (IRS)

The inertial system computes airplane position, ground speed, heading and attitude.

The main component of the IRS is the Inertial Reference Unit (IRU), which interfaces with the Modular Avionic Unit (MAU), Global Positioning System (GPS) and the Air Data Computer (ADC). The IRU provides output data to the PFD, weather radar, Multifunction Control Display Unit (MCDU), Flight Management System (FMS) and reversionary panel.

Primary source for the Captain`s PFD is the IRS 1 and for the First Officer`s PFD is IRS 2. In case of mode failure, power loss or loss of one IRU, the affected station can source select the other side station by means of the IRS reversionary panel button.

An automatic power up (on ground) and alignment is provided.
The alignment on ground (up to 17 min) must be performed with the airplane not in movement

and position manually entered primarily via MCDU or obtained automatically from the GPS. In flight alignment is also possible to recover navigation capability using data from the GPS.
The alignment time can be checked on the IRS STATUS PAGE 1/1 on the MCDU.

REVISION 22 Navigation Page 1/36

fragen.zitat: In order to compute RAIM, the GPS must have a minimum of five satellite signals.
kontext:
RECEIVER AUTONOMOUS INTEGRITY MONITOR

(RAIM)

The GPS module executes a RAIM test to insure the integrity of the data transmitted by the satellite. RAIM is a software function that supplies an alert to the cockpit when the integrity limit exceeds a flight phase dependant threshold.

The GPS has RAIM outputs for the current position and time in the form of horizontal and vertical integrity limit (HIL and VIL) at some future place and time.
In order to compute RAIM, the GPS must have a minimum of five satellite signals.

The FMS does not accept GPS data unless a valid RAIM figure is available.

The FMS produces an alert for the flight crew on the MCDU when the GPS has lost integrity: “GPS RAIM ABOVE LIMITS”. Also an alert is generated by the FMS when the integrity will exceed the limit: “RAIM WILL EXCEED LIMIT”. A third alert will be generated by the FMS when RAIM is not available: “GPS RAIM UNAVAILABLE”.

Three
Six

fragen.erklaerung_en: Four satellites suffice for position determination; at least five are needed for RAIM.

kontext:
FMS ANNUNCIATORS

Annunciators are displayed on the electronic display system (EDS).
Magenta indicates an advisory annunciator and amber indicates an alerting annunciators.
– Dead Reckoning (DR) - DR is an alerting (amber) annunciator. This annunciator is displayed or lit when operating in the DR mode. The FMS enters DR mode after loss of required navigation performance (see DGRAD) and
loss of radio updating and all other position sensors (IRS and GPS) for greater than 2 minutes.

fragen.frage: Welches ist der Default-Climb-Speed-Schedule des FMS?
fragen.erklaerung: Default Climb Schedule ist 280 kt/0.73 M (unter 10000 ft gilt das Default-Limit 250 kt); Descent Default 290 kt/0.76 M/3.0°.
fragen.zitat: The default climb schedule is 280 kt/0.73 M.
kontext:
SPEED COMMAND FLIGHT PHASES

In order to perform the speed calculations and to define the FGCS targets in automatic mode, the FMS divides the flight in flight phases as follows:

REVISION 22 Flight Management System Page 5/100

Takeoff: The FMS speed control does not provide guidance while in the Takeoff mode. However, it sends inputs to the PFD to show the V2, until V2 is reached, then it ramps to V2 10 kt until the vertical mode is changed.
Departure: Speed command is the one selected on the DEP/APP speeds page. The default departure speed is 200 kt for 4 NM below 2500 ft.
Climb: Following departure, the command is the speed restriction set on the PERF INIT page 3/3. The default limit is 250 kt below 10000 ft.
After clearing the limitation, the FMS commands the lower value between MACH or CAS set on the climb schedule.
The default climb schedule is 280 kt/0.73 M.

During step climbs the FMS commands climb speed schedule if the difference between the current and the intended level is more than 5000 ft, otherwise it remains in cruise speed schedule.
Cruise: When in VALT or ALT and the present altitude is equal to the cruise altitude selected on the PERF INIT, the speed command is the cruise schedule selected. If the airplane levels-off at an altitude lower than the Initial Cruise altitude, the speed command continues on the climb schedule.
Descent: The default descent speed schedule is 290 kt/0.76 M/3.0°.
During step descents, the descent speed schedule will be the default speed commanded by the FMS. After level off FMS commands cruise speed schedule if the aircraft is before 50 NM from the TOD or descend speed schedule if it is within this range. Approaching the set limitation in the Speed/Altitude limit of the PERF INIT page 3/3, the FMS commands a speed reduction to comply with any existing the speed constraint.
Approach: The transition to approach speeds is at 15 flight plan nautical miles from the destination or 5 NM from the first approach fix.
This selection is made on the DEP/APP speeds pages.
When the flaps are set to position 1, the FMS commands speeds for the next flap. These speeds are calculated by the FMS for the actual airplane weight.
NOTE: Waypoint speed constraints have priority over approach speeds, therefore the FMS can command speeds below the green dot or flap maneuvering speeds for speed constrained waypoints.

Page 6/100 Flight Management System REVISION 22

LOAD 25 and previous

The approach speed limit activation logic considers the distance to destination airport and altitude AGL (default values are 15.0 NM and 3000 ft AGL).

Go-around – When the flight director is set to G/A the FMS speeds schedule changes for go-around as defined in the PERF INIT.
If a new approach is set while in go-around speed schedule the FMS reverts to approach speeds.
While in go-around, if a new destination is set, the FMS transitions to climb schedule speeds.
Waypoint Speed Constraints – If a speed is set in a flight plan waypoint, the FMS guides the AFCS to comply with this speed.
During a climb, the FMS commands the speed set in the speed constraint waypoint for all previous waypoints. After passing the speed constraint waypoint, the FMS reverts to the speed schedule set in the initialization up to the TOC.
During cruise and descent, the FMS commands the AFCS to cross the waypoint at the selected speed and applies this speed for the subsequent waypoints. As the airplane approaches the waypoint, the FMS may anticipate the speed constraint so that the airplane crosses the waypoint at the speed constraint.
fragen.frage_en: What is the FMS default climb speed schedule?
fragen.erklaerung_en: The default climb schedule is 280 kt/0.73 M (below 10000 ft the default limit of 250 kt applies); descent default 290 kt/0.76 M/3.0°.

fragen.zitat: commands a 1000 FPM descent up to the point where the planned descent path or the next altitude constraint is intercepted.
kontext:
NORMAL OPERATION

Climb: VNAV performs all climb profiles contained in the VFLCH mode. If the FMS levels-off at an altitude constraint defined over a waypoint, it resumes the climb automatically upon sequencing the waypoint. If the FMS levels-off at an altitude set on the Altitude Pre Selector, after setting the Altitude Pre Selector to a higher altitude, the FLCH button must be pressed on the guidance panel in order for the VNAV to transition from VALT to VFLCH.

Cruise: The FMS will transition to cruise phase when reaching the initial cruise altitude set in the PERF INIT page. If the airplane levels at an altitude lower than the initial cruise altitude, the FMS does not transition to cruise.

If the ALT SEL is set to an altitude higher than the FMS cruise altitude, after few seconds, the cruise altitude in the PERF INIT page is reset to match with the ALT SEL selection.

NOTE: To reset the FMS cruise altitude to an altitude lower than the current FMS cruise altitude, it may be necessary to delete the current cruise altitude in the FMS CRUISE PAGE 1/1 prior to insert the new altitude.

To leave cruise level to either climb or descent, the altitude selector must be set to an altitude higher or lower than the present altitude and a vertical DIRECT-TO or VFLCH must be commanded.

REVISION 22 Flight Management System Page 3/100

When TCS is used to exit a leveled altitude, the command logic is to return to the original altitude when the change is less than 50 ft. For changes greater than 50 ft, the new achieved altitude is maintained.

TOD: The Top of Descent is calculated using the values inserted in the PERF INIT page and is displayed in the VNAV page and on the PFD/ MFD.
Post-Mod. LOAD 21.2 and Post-Mod. LOAD 27.1

The DES NOW prompt is displayed on the FMS DESCENT, FLIGHT PLAN and ROUTE pages providing an easy command to start the descent when the airplane is 50 NM or less from the calculated TOD.

When selected, the Flight Director commands the airplane to descent according to the airplane position relative to the predicted TOD.
– Early Descent: selecting the DES NOW prompt before the TOD is reached enables the Early Descent mode, where the FD
commands a 1000 FPM descent up to the point where the planned descent path or the next altitude constraint is intercepted.

– Late Descent: selecting the DES NOW prompt after the planned TOD is reached enables the Late Descent mode, where the FD commands a descent angle 1.5° steeper than the planned descent angle to intercept the planned path.
NOTE: If this descent angle is not enough to intercept the previously planned path a UNABLE PATH INTERCEPT scratchpad message is displayed.

Descent: One minute prior to the TOD, a vertical track alert is given.
When reaching the TOD, the FMS automatically starts the descent in VFLCH or VPATH if the altitude selector is set to a lower altitude.
– VFLCH Descents – The descent is in VFLCH mode if there is no altitude constraint down to 1500 ft/10 NM prior to the destination airport. VFLCH also complies with the speed/altitude limit. After an intermediate level-off at the altitude selector altitude, the next descent must be initiated selecting the altitude selector to a lower altitude and pressing FLCH on the GP.

Page 4/100 Flight Management System REVISION 22

– VPATH Descents – The descent is in VPATH anytime an altitude constraint exists in the descent path and the airplane is within the capture logic of VPATH mode. FMS must be the navigation source and LNAV must be engaged in order the VPATH to become available. When the FMS passes through the last altitude constraint waypoint, it reverts to VFLCH to complete the descent.
During VPATH descents, significant modifications of the flight plan may result the VPATH mode to drop to FPA mode.
Vertical DIRECT-TO: This operation is similar to the lateral DIRECT- TO. It is performed selecting the desired altitude from the scratch pad to the line adjacent to the desired waypoint.
Post-Mod. LOAD 21.2 and Post-Mod. LOAD 27.1

The FMS calculates the predicted altitudes at which the airplane should pass the waypoints and then applies the altitude constraints to these altitudes, if necessary.

VNAV and HOLDING PATTERNS: The following applies:
– If descending on VFLCH and a holding pattern is entered, the active mode remains VFLCH;
– If a PPOS holding is entered while in VPATH, the active mode changes to VFLCH;
– If a hold is entered while in VPATH descent, the command changes to VALT.

antworten_en: A descent on a path 1.5° steeper than planned
An idle descent in VFLCH to the altitude selector altitude
A 3° path from the present position
A descent at 1000 ft/min until the planned path or the next altitude constraint is reached
fragen.erklaerung_en: Early Descent: 1000 FPM until intercepting the path; Late Descent (after TOD): 1.5° steeper than the planned path.

kontext:
SYSTEM (RAAS)

The Runway Awareness and Advisories System (RAAS) provides short and discrete pieces of aural information designed to improve situational awareness and break the link in the sequence of events leading to runway incursions, but cannot be used to guide an airplane in or around the terminal area.

The advisory aural messages are provided to the flight crew during taxi, takeoff, approach and landing/roll-out operations. These aural messages cannot be used for navigation purposes.

The design of RAAS does not include knowledge of ATC clearance and/or flight crew intent, and therefore factors such as clearance misunderstandings; incorrect/inappropriate clearances cannot necessarily be mitigated by use of RAAS.

RAAS is not designed to enhance traffic awareness and therefore its use does not ensure protection for loss of separation with other traffic.

RAAS may become not available at any time due to loss of accuracy of GPS signals.
RAAS advisories have the lowest priority over the airplane aural warnings and tones.

RAAS advisories may be issued during ATC radio communications, flight crew/cockpit communications, or during other aural messages provided in the cockpit by other airplane systems.

RAAS advisories do not ensure that the airplane will, or can be, stopped before hold lines, the runway edges or the runway end. RAAS distance advisories do not imply that the airplane can or cannot be safely landed, stopped, or taken off from a runway.

RAAS advisories do not take into account airplanes performance factors, such as airplane weight, wind, runway condition, slope, air temperature and altitude of airport.

Not all airports/runways in the EGPWS Terrain Threat Database are RAAS enabled. RAAS advisories will not occur at an airport located in the EGPWS Terrain Threat Database unless it is RAAS enabled.

PASSENGER AND SERVICE DOORS

This airplane has one passenger door located at the left forward fuselage section and another located at the aft fuselage section.

One service door is located at the right forward fuselage section and another located at the aft fuselage section. Service doors are used for galley servicing and cabin cleaning between flights. It may also be used as an emergency exit. The operation of service and passenger doors is identical.

One external, three internal handles and one vent flap are installed in each door for opening and closing operation.
Passenger and service doors were designed to support winds up to 65 kt while the door is fully open and locked.

Therefore, doors must be closed before the wind speed achieves 65 kt.

A wind of 40 kt was considered during design for door operation (opening or closing). Therefore, if the wind is above 40 kt and door operation is needed, caution must be taken during door operation since the wind direction may affect door displacement.

kontext:
ESCAPE SLIDE

The escape slides are designed to provide passengers and crew a means to safely descend from the airplane to the ground during an emergency evacuation. In the event of emergency evacuation, the slides deploy automatically when the exit door is opened.

Upon completion of the inflation sequence, the slide is fully inflated and ready to assist passengers and crew in descending to the ground.

The emergency evacuation slides are equipped with a lighting system independent from the airplane. The unfolding process activates the lighting system illuminating the sliding surface and the area where evacuees make first contact with the ground. A battery contained within the slide provides electrical power to the lights.

The escape slides are armed by raising the slide arming lever cover located on the door and moving the slide arming lever to the “armed” position (down). The lever movement attaches the girt bar to the cabin floor brackets. The escape slide is attached to the girt bar by means of a fabric girt.
Opening the door from the outside automatically disengages the girt bar from the floor fittings, disarming the slide.

A dedicated battery powers the escape slide lights, which will be on for a minimum of 10 min even after the escape slide is disconnected.

The escape slide may be used as a flotation device after disconnection from airplane.

If the mooring line is not manually detached from the airplane in an emergency situation, the system is fail safe in that the mooring line will break free from the slide if enough load is applied.

Emergency lighting consists of internal and external lights. The internal emergency lights are powered by six dedicated Emergency Lights Power Units (ELPU) with internal batteries connected to the DC BUS

The charge of the batteries is sufficient to supply all emergency lights for approximately 10 minutes.

An EMER LT Selector located in the cockpit enables the pilots to turn ON, OFF, or ARM the emergency lights. Additional buttons on the FWD and AFT Flight Attendant Panels enable flight attendant to turn ON or OFF (ARM) the emergency lights. In ARM mode (EMER LT Selector in the cockpit), the emergency lights are activated automatically when the airplane loses its normal electrical power.

Exit markings comprises:

– Exit marker lights: Located close to the exits to provide location and identification of the emergency exits.

fragen.zitat: RED: a flashing red indicator illuminates when the flight crew makes an emergency call to the flight attendant from the cockpit.
kontext:
RAINBOW LIGHTS

The rainbow lights located on the forward and aft main ceiling panel areas provide a visual indication to attendants when there is a call from the flight crew or passengers.

The rainbow lights consist of following colored indicator lights:
– ORANGE: a steady orange light illuminates when a passenger calls from the lavatory. Flashing orange light illuminates when smoke is detected in the lavatory.
– BLUE: a steady blue light illuminates when a passenger calls from the main cabin area.
–
RED: a flashing red indicator illuminates when the flight crew makes an emergency call to the flight attendant from the cockpit.

The light stops flashing after the call is taken.
– GREEN: a flashing green indicator illuminates when the pilot calls the flight attendant from the cockpit. The light stops flashing after the call is taken.
– AMBER: a steady amber light illuminates for a sterile light call.
An audible tone is sounded by the passenger address system whenever a passenger presses any attendant call switch located in a PSU or the attendant call switch in the lavatory or flight crew call switches. There is also a blue steady light on the cabin ceiling, indicating from which cabin area the respective passenger call was made.

NOTE: There is no indication on the rainbow lights when a flight attendant calls another flight attendant station. It only flashes green on both handset cradles.

Sterile cockpit phase active
fragen.erklaerung_en: Flashing red = emergency call from the flight deck; flashing orange = lavatory smoke; blue = PSU call; amber = sterile light.

fragen.frage: Bei welcher IDG-Öltemperatur erfolgt die automatische IDG-Trennung, wenn die Crew nicht manuell trennt?
fragen.erklaerung: IDG 1 (2) OIL erscheint bei 168°C ± 5°C bzw. Öldruck < 140 psi; die automatische Trennung erfolgt bei 185.6°C.
fragen.zitat: Automatic IDG disconnection occurs when manual disconnection is not performed, and the IDG oil temperature reaches 366°F (185.6°C).
kontext:
INTEGRATED DRIVE GENERATOR (IDG)

Each engine has an IDG monitored and controlled by a dedicated generator control unit (GCU). When an engine starts, the IDG will automatically come on line, powering the respective AC BUS. The previous power source is disconnected from that AC BUS.

For automatic operation of the electrical system, the IDG selector knob must be set to the AUTO position. Moving the selector knob to OFF position, the generator line contactor opens, tripping off-line and de- exciting the selected IDG.

When the IDG oil pressure drops below 140 psi 25 psi, or the IDG oil temperature reaches 335°F 10°F (168°C 5°C), the EICAS message IDG 1 (2) OIL is displayed and an amber led illuminates near the IDG selector knob on the overhead panel. This led indicates which IDG must be disconnected and extinguishes after the IDG disconnection.

Manual IDG disconnection is achieved by selecting the respective IDG knob to the DISC position and holding for one second.

NOTE: Do not hold IDG knob to the DISC position for more than three seconds.
Automatic IDG disconnection occurs when manual disconnection is not performed, and the IDG oil temperature reaches 366°F (185.6°C).
In both cases, the disconnection is mechanical and the flight crew cannot reconnect the IDG.
fragen.frage_en: At what IDG oil temperature does automatic IDG disconnect occur if the crew does not disconnect manually?
fragen.erklaerung_en: IDG 1 (2) OIL appears at 168°C ± 5°C or oil pressure < 140 psi; automatic disconnect occurs at 185.6°C.

fragen.frage: Wann wird die WARNING BATT 1 (2) OVERTEMP ausgelöst?
antworten: Batterietemperatur 70°C während mindestens 2 s
Batterietemperatur 60°C während mindestens 5 s
Batterietemperatur 85°C sofort
Batteriespannung unter 22.8 V während 2 s
fragen.erklaerung: Ab 70°C während mindestens 2 s wird die Anzeige rot und BATT 1 (2) OVERTEMP erscheint.
fragen.zitat: Whenever the battery temperature reaches 70°C for at least 2 s, the associated indication becomes red and the EICAS WARNING message BATT 1 (2) OVERTEMP is triggered.
kontext:
TRANSFORMER RECTIFIER UNIT (TRU)

Three TRUs convert 115 VAC power into 28 VDC. Each TRU works in isolation. If one of them fails, the BUSES are automatically powered by the remaining TRUs, as long as the DC BUS TIES toggle switch is selected to AUTO.

TRU 1 provides DC power to DC BUS 1, DC ESS BUS 1, DC GND SVC BUS, HOT BATT BUS 1 and battery #1 charging.

TRU 2 provides DC power to DC BUS 2, DC ESS BUS 2, HOT BATT BUS 2 and battery #2 charging.

TRU ESS provides DC power to DC ESS BUS 3.

BATTERIES

Two NiCd 22.8 VDC, 27 A batteries power up the airplane and are also used as a backup for the DC essential electrical system.

The batteries charges constantly by any AC source through the TRUs, including the AC GPU and the RAT.

In an ELECTRICAL EMERGENCY, while the RAT is not fully deployed and also if RAT stall speed is reached, batteries supply essential loads for 10 min.
Whenever the battery temperature reaches 70°C for at least 2 s, the associated indication becomes red and the EICAS WARNING message BATT 1 (2) OVERTEMP is triggered.

On ground, if the airplane is powered only by the batteries for more than 5 min, a horn sounds to alert the ground personnel.

NOTE: The check for batteries voltage is not valid if any AC source is powering the airplane. In this case, the TRU voltage is indicated instead of the batteries voltage.

14-05-15

Page 2/4 DC System REVISION 22

antworten_en: Battery temperature 70°C for at least 2 s
Battery temperature 60°C for at least 5 s
Battery temperature 85°C immediately
Battery voltage below 22.8 V for 2 s
fragen.erklaerung_en: From 70°C for at least 2 s the indication turns red and BATT 1 (2) OVERTEMP appears.

fragen.frage: Wie viele Igniter energiert das FADEC bei einem normalen Bodenstart bzw. bei einem Start im Flug?

Immer beide Igniter

fragen.zitat: The FADEC energizes one igniter for on-ground engine starts and both igniters for in-flight engine starts.
kontext:
IGNITION SYSTEM

The ignition system provides an electrical spark for fuel combustion during ground/in-flight start attempts and for automatic re-light.
The FADEC energizes one igniter for on-ground engine starts and both igniters for in-flight engine starts.

In case of an engine airstart, engine flameout, a missed light off, cold soak condition on ground, ground start at high altitude airports, or when the ignition selector knob is placed on the OVRD position, both igniters on each engine are energized. Igniters 1B and 2B are connected to SPDA 2. In case of SPDA 2 failure, setting the selector knob to OVRD energizes at least the igniter A.

NOTE: The frequent use of ignition selector knob at the OVRD position causes the significative reduction of ignitor's lifetime.

Always only one igniter, except in OVRD
fragen.erklaerung_en: The FADEC uses one igniter on the ground and both in flight; OVRD, flameout, airstart etc. also activate both.

fragen.frage: Bodenstart: Kein Light-off innerhalb von 15 s nach Fuel On. Was macht das FADEC?
antworten: Es bricht den Start ab und zeigt ENG NO DISPATCH
Es schaltet sofort auf Dual Ignition, ohne Fuel abzustellen
Es motort 60 s trocken und erwartet einen manuellen Neustart
Es schaltet Zündung und Fuel ab, motort 30 s trocken und startet dann mit Single Ignition und Fuel neu
fragen.erklaerung: Nach 15 s ohne Light-off: Zündung und Fuel aus, 30 s Dry Motoring, dann erneut Single Ignition und Fuel (nach 7 s Dual Ignition).
fragen.zitat: If no light off is detected within 15 s of fuel on, FADEC automatically turns off ignition and fuel, continue dry motoring for 30 s, then turn on single ignition and turn on fuel again.
kontext:
GROUND START

190/195 models, Post-Mod ENGINE FADEC 5.61

The FADEC initiates ignition at approximately 7% N2 and the fuel flow (metering valve opens) from 20% to 25% N2, depending on the engine start altitude.
If no light off is detected within 15 s of fuel on, FADEC automatically turns off ignition and fuel, continue dry motoring for 30 s, then turn on single ignition and turn on fuel again.

After 7 s of single ignition is applied, FADEC commands dual ignition for 8 s.

If no light off is detected after 15 s of the reintroduction of fuel or after start duty limit is reached, whichever occurs first, the FADEC does not turn off fuel or ignition automatically.

In case of cold soaked engine or high altitude conditions and no light off is detected, FADEC inhibits the EICAS messages "ENG 1 (2) NO DISPATCH" during the first attempt cycle for engine start.

After a light off occurs, the FADEC commands the starter to cutout at approximately 50% N2, and commands the FMU fuel metering valve to accelerate the engine to ground idle speed.

At high altitudes, the fuel flow schedule is also increased to provide higher torque and therefore quicker starts.
fragen.frage_en: Ground start: No light-off within 15 s after fuel on. What does the FADEC do?
antworten_en: It aborts the start and shows ENG NO DISPATCH
It immediately switches to dual ignition without shutting off fuel
It dry motors for 60 s and expects a manual restart
It switches off ignition and fuel, dry motors for 30 s and then restarts with single ignition and fuel
fragen.erklaerung_en: After 15 s without light-off: ignition and fuel off, 30 s dry motoring, then single ignition and fuel again (dual ignition after 7 s).

fragen.zitat: The minimum flex takeoff thrust is limited to 75% maximum rated takeoff thrust or CLB-2 + 1% N1, whichever is higher.
kontext:
FLEXIBLE TAKEOFF

Flexible takeoff is a reduced takeoff thrust based on assumed temperature.

All takeoff modes are eligible for a flexible takeoff.

14-06-30

Page 4/10 Engine Control System REVISION 25

The assumed temperature must be higher than the TO TEMP and is set on the MCDU TAKEOFF DATA SET MENU page.

The indication FLEX TO-1, FLEX TO-2 or FLEX TO-3 will be displayed on the EICAS for the respective flexible takeoff thrust.
The minimum flex takeoff thrust is limited to 75% maximum rated takeoff thrust or CLB-2 1% N1, whichever is higher.

Flexible takeoff is possible with ATTCS ON or OFF. When flexible takeoff mode is used, moving the thrust levers to MAX position resets the assumed temperature and sets the maximum thrust available (refer to the Thrust Ratings Table).
fragen.frage_en: What is the minimum flex takeoff thrust limited to?
antworten_en: 75% of maximum takeoff thrust or CLB-2 + 1% N1, whichever is higher
60% of maximum takeoff thrust
CON thrust
75% of maximum takeoff thrust or CLB-1, whichever is lower
fragen.erklaerung_en: Flex thrust must not be below 75% of max takeoff thrust or CLB-2 + 1% N1 (higher value).

kontext:
AUTO RELIGHT

The FADEC monitors N2 and automatically turns on both igniters and schedules the relight fuel flow in the event of an engine flameout. In addition a WML icon is displayed next to the respective engine N2 and represents an auto relight actuation during the engine auto relight attempts.

If the engine relight does not occur within 30 s or N2 falls below 7.2%, the automatic relight can be considered unsuccessful and should be manually terminated by moving the START/STOP selector knob to the STOP position.

For in flight auto relight, the FADEC has no protection for hot starts, hung starts or failure to light off.
During ground operations, auto relight attempts are terminated and fuel is shutoff if the engine rpm falls below 52 percent N2.

14-06-20

REVISION 22 Start and Ignition System Page 3/4

14-06-20

Page 4/4 Start and Ignition System REVISION 22

fragen.zitat: The EICAS displays up to 15 messages
kontext:
EICAS MESSAGES CATEGORIZATION

There are four message priority levels:
– Warning.
– Caution.
– Advisory.

REVISION 25 Visual Warning Page 1/16

– Status.
WARNING (red): indicates an emergency or airplane system condition that requires immediate corrective or compensatory crew action.

CAUTION (amber): indicates an abnormal operational or airplane system conditions that require immediate crew awareness and should require a subsequent corrective or compensatory action.

ADVISORY (cyan): indicates operational or airplane conditions that require crew awareness. Subsequent or future crew action may be required.

STATUS (white): indicates information/status messages. The pilot can use the system efficiently when the appropriate action is accomplished.

A fifth level is provided for maintenance and is not available during flight operation. It is accessed only on ground.

Messages with the higher priority precede other messages when shown simultaneously.
The EICAS displays up to 15 messages

simultaneously.

The MCDU displays some messages in the event of a failure of both MFD and the EICAS.
fragen.frage_en: How many messages can the CAS window of the EICAS display at one time before scrolling is required?
fragen.erklaerung_en: The EICAS displays up to 15 messages; in case of overflow, scrolling is possible with the CCD (WARNINGs are never scrolled out).

fragen.frage: Wann erscheint die Anzeige "CAS MSG" auf beiden PFDs?
antworten: Wenn die CAS-Listen der beiden MWF während 20 s ununterbrochen voneinander abweichen
Wenn mehr als 15 Meldungen anstehen
Wenn eine WARNING nicht innerhalb von 20 s quittiert wurde
Wenn beide MWF ausgefallen sind
fragen.erklaerung: CAS MSG zeigt einen Miscompare der beiden Monitor-Warning-Listen an, wenn diese 20 s lang verschieden sind.
fragen.zitat: If the two CAS message lists are continuously different for 20 s, a miscompare indication is annunciated.
kontext:
CAS SOURCE SELECTION

The CAS List Message Comparison Annunciation is shown on both PFDs to indicate that the CAS lists from the two monitor warning systems do not match. The annunciation consists of the letters "CAS MSG" displayed inside a cutout box.
If the two CAS message lists are continuously different for 20 s, a miscompare indication is annunciated.

The CAS MSG source can be visualized or manually changed on the MCDU avionics SETUP page through LSK 2R from CAS 1 to CAS 2 or vice versa.

CAS SOURCE SELECTION options are only enabled on the MCDU SETUP page 1/1 when a miscompare is detected between CAS 1 and CAS 2 lists, otherwise just the label CAS SOURCE SELECTION is displayed.

SETUP 1 1
fragen.frage_en: When does the "CAS MSG" indication appear on both PFDs?
antworten_en: When the CAS lists of the two MWFs differ continuously for 20 s
When more than 15 messages are pending
When a WARNING has not been acknowledged within 20 s
When both MWFs have failed
fragen.erklaerung_en: CAS MSG indicates a miscompare of the two monitor warning lists if they differ for 20 s.

fragen.frage: Welche Bedingung hat bei den Voice Messages Vorrang vor Windshear-, EGPWS- und TCAS-Alerts?
antworten: Eine Takeoff Configuration Warning
Ein Stall-Zustand
Ein Engine Fire
Ein Autopilot Disconnect
fragen.erklaerung: Bei Windshear-, TCAS- oder EGPWS-Alerts werden andere Voice Messages unterdrückt; nur Stall hat Vorrang.
fragen.zitat: Only a stall condition takes precedence over windshear, EGPWS and TCAS alerts.
kontext:
VOICE MESSAGES

Voice messages are generated whenever a potentially dangerous condition exists, as determined by the EGPWS, TCAS, and windshear detection system.

Some voice messages may be canceled, but others are only canceled when the cause that activates them ceases. When a windshear, TCAS or EGPWS alert condition takes place, a special situation exists. In that case, no other voice messages are presented so that the flight crew can clearly hear the information messages.
Only a stall condition takes precedence over windshear, EGPWS and TCAS alerts.

REVISION 25 Aural Warning Page 3/4

Page 4/4 Aural Warning REVISION 25
fragen.frage_en: Which condition takes priority over windshear, EGPWS and TCAS alerts among the voice messages?
antworten_en: A Takeoff Configuration Warning
A stall condition
An Engine Fire
An Autopilot Disconnect
fragen.erklaerung_en: On windshear, TCAS or EGPWS alerts, other voice messages are suppressed; only stall takes priority.

fragen.frage: Wann werden die Air Data Smart Probes (ADSP) im AUTO-Modus beheizt?
antworten: Nur in der Luft
Nur bei OAT unter 10°C
Sobald ein Engine läuft oder das Flugzeug in der Luft ist
Nur wenn der Ice Detector Icing meldet
fragen.erklaerung: Die ADSPs werden automatisch beheizt, sobald ein Engine läuft oder das Flugzeug airborne ist; am Boden kann manuell übersteuert werden.
fragen.zitat: The ADSPs are heated whenever an engine is running or the airplane is airborne.
kontext: AUTO MODE
The ADSPs are heated whenever an engine is running or the airplane is airborne.

The TATs are heated when at least one of the following conditions is met:

Post-Mod. SB 190-34-0051
– The OAT is below 10°C (50°F) with an engine running,
– Airspeed is above 50 kt, or
– The airplane is airborne.
Upon landing, the TAT heating disables when airspeed is below 45 kt.
fragen.frage_en: When are the Air Data Smart Probes (ADSP) heated in AUTO mode?
antworten_en: Only in the air
Only at OAT below 10°C
As soon as an engine is running or the aircraft is airborne
Only when the Ice Detector reports icing
fragen.erklaerung_en: The ADSPs are heated automatically as soon as an engine is running or the aircraft is airborne; on the ground they can be overridden manually.

fragen.frage: Wann führt das Wing-Anti-Ice-System im Flug seinen automatischen Selbsttest (SAI IBIT) durch?
antworten: Beim Durchsteigen von 1700 ft AGL
Vor jedem Top of Descent
2 min nach dem Takeoff oder bei 5000 ft AGL, was zuerst eintritt
10 min nach dem Takeoff oder bei 10000 ft AGL, was zuerst eintritt
fragen.erklaerung: Der SAI IBIT erfolgt 10 min nach Takeoff oder bei 10000 ft AGL; dabei öffnen die Slat Anti-Ice Valves kurz.
fragen.zitat: The wing anti-ice system tests itself during flight (SAI IBIT) 10 min after takeoff or at 10000 ft AGL, whichever occurs first.
kontext:
ICE PROTECTION SYSTEM

The Ice Protection TEST Controller provides a manual test for the wing and engine anti-ice systems for maintenance use.
The wing anti-ice system tests itself during flight (SAI IBIT) 10 min after takeoff or at 10000 ft AGL, whichever occurs first.

At this time the Slat Anti-Ice Valves will be opened (EICAS messages A-I WING VLV OPEN and A-I Synoptic page will indicate that valves have opened).

If a failure occurs during IBIT, the message A-I WING FAIL will be displayed.
Post-Mod Black Label 9.0

The SAI IBIT duration is 80 s (maximum). The test can be finished earlier if all slat temperature sensors have an increase of 5.5°C (10°F).

fragen.frage_en: When does the Wing Anti-Ice system perform its automatic self-test (SAI IBIT) in flight?
antworten_en: When passing 1700 ft AGL
Before every Top of Descent
2 min after takeoff or at 5000 ft AGL, whichever occurs first
10 min after takeoff or at 10000 ft AGL, whichever occurs first
