fragen.frage: Unter welchen Bedingungen wechselt der laterale Mode beim Takeoff automatisch von ROLL auf TRACK?
antworten: IAS über 80 kt und Querneigung ≤ 5° für mehr als 5 s
Beim Passieren von 50 ft Radiohöhe
IAS über 100 kt und Querneigung ≤ 3° für mehr als 10 s
Beim Einfahren des Landing Gears
fragen.erklaerung: Die automatische Transition ROLL→TRACK beim Takeoff erfolgt bei IAS > 100 kt und Bank ≤ 3° für mehr als 10 s.
fragen.zitat: IAS is greater than 100 kt, and – Bank angle is at 3° or below for more than 10 s.
kontext:
TRACK HOLD (TRACK)

The track select mode is used to intercept and maintain an inertial derived airplane track from the IRS. This mode is used for Takeoff and Go-Around.

TAKEOFF

The automatic transition from ROLL to TRACK during takeoff occurs when:
–

IAS is greater than 100 kt, and
– Bank angle is at 3° or below for more than 10 s.
fragen.frage_en: Under which conditions does the lateral mode change automatically from ROLL to TRACK on takeoff?
antworten_en: IAS above 80 kt and bank ≤ 5° for more than 5 s
When passing 50 ft radio altitude
IAS above 100 kt and bank ≤ 3° for more than 10 s
When the landing gear is retracted
fragen.erklaerung_en: The automatic ROLL→TRACK transition on takeoff occurs at IAS > 100 kt and bank ≤ 3° for more than 10 s.

fragen.frage: TO Mode aktiv: Ein Engine fällt zwischen V2 und V2 + 10 kt aus. Welche Speed führt der Flight Director?
antworten: Die aktuelle Speed
V2
V2 + 10 kt
VFS
fragen.erklaerung: Bei Engine Failure zwischen V2 und V2 + 10 kt führt der FD die aktuelle Speed; unter V2 führt er V2, über V2 + 10 kt führt er V2 + 10 kt.
fragen.zitat: Engine failure between V2 and V2 + 10 kt: guides present speed.
kontext:
TO PITCH ANGLE LOGIC

Initially, the system guides the pitch to the calculated angle. When airborne and IAS is greater than speed target, the guidance is as follows:
– All engines operating: V2 10 kt.
– One engine inoperative:
– Engine failure below V2: guides V2
–
Engine failure between V2 and V2 10 kt: guides present speed.

– Engine failure above V2 10 kt: guides V2 10 kt.

In TO mode the pitch is limited to a minimum of 7° and a maximum of 25°. The maximum speed target is VFE - 5 kt and minimum speed target is VSHAKER 10 kt for all engines operating. For one engine inoperative the minimum speed target is VSHAKER 3 kt.

REVISION 15 Flight Guidance Control System Page 9/40

NOTE: If actual flap selection disagrees with FMS selection, the aural warning “NO TAKEOFF FLAPS” is triggered whenever the airplane is on ground and takeoff thrust is applied or Takeoff configuration button is pressed.
fragen.frage_en: TO mode active: An engine fails between V2 and V2 + 10 kt. Which speed does the Flight Director command?
antworten_en: The current speed
V2
V2 + 10 kt
VFS
fragen.erklaerung_en: On engine failure between V2 and V2 + 10 kt the FD commands the current speed; below V2 it commands V2, above V2 + 10 kt it commands V2 + 10 kt.

fragen.frage: Welche Speed führt der GA Mode mit beiden Engines, sobald die IAS über dem Speed-Target liegt?
antworten: VREF + 20 kt
VAC
VREF + 10 kt
V2 + 10 kt
fragen.erklaerung: Im GA Mode ist das Speed-Target mit allen Engines VREF + 20 kt, mit einem Engine VAC.
fragen.zitat: All engines operating: VREF + 20 kt.
kontext:
GA LOGIC:

The GA mode first guidance sets pitch at a fixed angle which depends on the flap position. After 5 s from gear up command the GA mode switches to another pitch reference also dependent on the flap

Page 12/40 Flight Guidance Control System REVISION 15

position. If the rate of descent is negative, the FD increments the airplane pitch gradually until the rate of descent is zero.

When IAS is greater than the speed target, the guidance is the speed target according to the following:
–
All engines operating: VREF 20 kt.

– One engine inoperative: VAC (approach climb).

The VREF and VAC are inserted on the MCDU LANDING page.

If speed target is not valid, the airplane guides to pitch 8°.

In GA mode, the pitch is limited to a minimum of 7° and a maximum of 18°. The maximum speed target is Vfe - 5 kt and minimum speed target is Vshaker 10 kt for all engines operating. For one engine inoperative the minimum speed target is Vshaker 3 kt.
fragen.frage_en: Which speed does the GA mode command with both engines once IAS is above the speed target?
antworten_en: VREF + 20 kt
VAC
VREF + 10 kt
V2 + 10 kt
fragen.erklaerung_en: In GA mode the speed target is VREF + 20 kt with all engines and VAC with one engine.

fragen.frage: Welches automatische Bank Limit gilt für HDG/NAV-Kurven oberhalb von 25000 ft?

15°, mit weissem Limit-Arc auf dem PFD
30°, ohne Limit-Arc
20°, mit amberfarbenem Limit-Arc

kontext:
LOW BANK LIMIT ARC

Page 2/16 Controls and Indications REVISION 15

The low bank limit arc is manually commanded to on or off, or automatically commanded by the AFCS.

The logic used by the AFCS for bank limit transition is:
–
Above 25000 ft the bank limit is 15°, and the white limit arc on the roll pointer of PFD is presented.
– Below 25000 ft the bank limit is 30°, and there is no white limit arc presented.

15°, with white limit arc on the PFD
30°, without limit arc
20°, with amber limit arc
fragen.erklaerung_en: Above 25000 ft the AFCS sets a bank limit of 15° (white arc); below that, 30° without arc applies.

fragen.frage: Der TO Mode ist aktiv, der AP ist nicht engaged. Was bewirkt das Drücken des FD-Buttons?
antworten: Der FD wird auf beiden PFDs ausgeschaltet
Nichts, die FD-Modes bleiben auf beiden PFDs unverändert
Der FD wird nur auf der gedrückten Seite ausgeschaltet
Der FD wechselt in den FPA Mode

Pressing the FD button on the display control panel removes the flight director presentation on the PFD only with AP disengaged.

NOTE:
When the TO, GA, WSHR, or dual coupled approach modes are active, pressing the FD button has no effect in both PFDs leaving the FD modes unchanged.

The FD is switched off only on the side pressed
The FD changes to FPA mode

fragen.frage: Wie ist der Autopilot der E2 aufgebaut?
antworten: Ein einzelner Autopilot mit Triple-Channel-Konfiguration
Zwei unabhängige Autopiloten (AP 1 und AP 2)
Ein Autopilot mit Dual-Channel-Konfiguration
Drei unabhängige Autopiloten, wählbar über SRC
fragen.erklaerung: Die E2 hat einen einzelnen Autopiloten mit dreikanaliger Konfiguration; ein Kanal ist aktiv, die anderen arbeiten als Slave.
fragen.zitat: The E-Jets E2 have a single autopilot with a triple channel flight control system configuration.
kontext: AUTOPILOT (AP)
The E-Jets E2 have a single autopilot with a triple channel flight control system configuration.

One channel is active while the others works in slave configuration.

In a failure of the active channel, the system alternates the channel automatically, and also after each landing.
fragen.frage_en: How is the E2 autopilot designed?
antworten_en: A single autopilot with triple-channel configuration
Two independent autopilots (AP 1 and AP 2)
A single autopilot with dual-channel configuration
Three independent autopilots, selectable via SRC
fragen.erklaerung_en: The E2 has a single autopilot with triple-channel configuration; one channel is active, the others operate as slave.

fragen.frage: Welche Aktion führt zu einer Non-normal Disengagement des Autopiloten?
antworten: Drücken und Halten des TCS-Buttons
Drücken des A/T-Buttons
Betätigen eines manuellen Pitch Trim Switch
Wechsel des FD-Source mit SRC
fragen.erklaerung: Das AP trennt u.a. bei Drücken des AP-Buttons, Betätigung eines manuellen Pitch Trim Switch, AoA Limiter oder Windshear Escape Guidance. TCS übersteuert den AP nur vorübergehend.

NON-NORMAL DISENGAGEMENT

If one of the following conditions occurs, the autopilot also disengages:
– On the guidance panel, the AP button is pressed
–
Either manual pitch trim switch is actuated

– AoA Limiter is activated, or
– Windshear escape guidance is activated.

Pressing the A/T button
Operating a manual pitch trim switch
Changing the FD source with SRC
fragen.erklaerung_en: The AP disconnects, among other things, when the AP button is pressed, a manual pitch trim switch is operated, on AoA limiter or windshear escape guidance. TCS overrides the AP only temporarily.

fragen.frage: Wann wird der VGP Mode beim Drücken von APPR armiert?
antworten: Innerhalb 30 NM Radialdistanz zum FAF und mit einem Non-Localizer-Approach mit publiziertem konstantem Gleitwinkel im FMS
Innerhalb 5 NM Radialdistanz zum FAF unabhängig vom Approach-Typ
Erst nach Überfliegen des FAF
Innerhalb 150 NM von der Destination mit aktivem PREV
fragen.erklaerung: VGP armiert bei APPR innerhalb 30 NM vom FAF und bei einem Non-Localizer-Approach mit konstantem Glide Path; engagen tut er innerhalb 5 NM entlang Track vom FAF.
fragen.zitat: pressing the APPR button on the Guidance Panel when within 30 NM radial distance from the FAF, and
kontext:
VGP ACTIVATION

The VGP mode is armed:
–
pressing the APPR button on the Guidance Panel when within 30 NM radial distance from the FAF, and

– a nonlocalizer based approach with a published constant glide path angle is selected in the FMS.
The VGP mode is engaged when:
– the airplane is within 5 NM from the FAF along track distance or at any distance within 30 NM from destination whenever using ACTIVATE VECTORS, and
– the first approach waypoint is the FAF.
– LNAV is active.
If any change in the vertical procedure profile is made, the VGP does not engage.

NOTE: – If glide path is below the current airplane position and the APPR button is pressed, the VGP engages, commanding a descent to intercept the final approach path.
– If performing HOLD PATTERN, arm the VGP only after exiting the HOLD. Otherwise the VGP may intercept the final approach descent path during the HOLD track.
fragen.frage_en: When is VGP mode armed when APPR is pressed?
antworten_en: Within 30 NM radial distance of the FAF and with a non-localizer approach with a published constant glide angle in the FMS
Within 5 NM radial distance of the FAF regardless of approach type
Only after crossing the FAF
Within 150 NM of the destination with PREV active
fragen.erklaerung_en: VGP arms with APPR within 30 NM of the FAF and for a non-localizer approach with a constant glide path; it engages within 5 NM along track from the FAF.

fragen.frage: Welche Bedingung gehört zu den Voraussetzungen für APPR 2 (CAT II)?
antworten: RA-BARO Selector auf BARO und Radiohöhe unter 1000 ft
Nur der Selector auf der Seite der FD-Source auf RA
Beide RA-BARO Selector auf RA und Radiohöhe zwischen 800 ft und 1500 ft
SLAT/FLAP FULL
fragen.erklaerung: APPR 2 verlangt u.a. beide RA-BARO auf RA, RA zwischen 800 und 1500 ft, gültige Minimums auf beiden PFD, beide NAV auf korrekter LOC-Frequenz und SLAT/FLAP 5.
fragen.zitat: Both RA-BARO selector knobs set to RA. – Radio altitude between 800 ft and 1500 ft.
kontext:
CAPABILITY REQUIREMENTS

When ILS modes are requested via the APPR button, the system arms for the highest capability available as long as all conditions are satisfied:

APPR 1

The APPR 1 is the flight director mode used for ILS CAT I approaches.

The requirements to engage APPR 1 are:
– RA-BARO selector set to BARO.
– NAV frequency set to the correct LOC frequency in the MCDU.
– NAV or PREV selected.
These selections are necessary only on the PFD where the FD source is pointing.

When APPR button is pressed, the system attempts to arm to the highest capability available, this case APPR 1.

Page 26/40 Flight Guidance Control System REVISION 15

APPR 2

The APPR 2 is the flight director mode used for ILS CAT II approaches.

The requirements to engage APPR 2 are:
–

Both RA-BARO selector knobs set to RA.
– Radio altitude between 800 ft and 1500 ft.

– Minimums displayed on both PFDs are valid.
– Both NAV frequencies set to correct LOC frequency in the MCDU.
– Both PFDs set to correct LOC inbound course (NAV or PREV).
– SLAT/FLAP 5.

These preceding selections are necessary on both PFDs.

If there is a discrepancy, the RA-BARO window on the noncoupled side flashes amber upon crossing 1500 ft when APPR mode is selected.

If the required items to engage are not met or a system failure exists, an EICAS message APPR 2 NOT AVAILABLE is presented inflight.

If the flap setting is the only remaining condition to be satisfied for CAT II, the armed status remains displayed down to 800 ft RA. This condition suggests there is still one pilot action pending.
fragen.frage_en: Which condition is among the prerequisites for APPR 2 (CAT II)?
antworten_en: RA-BARO selector on BARO and radio altitude below 1000 ft
Only the selector on the FD source side on RA
Both RA-BARO selectors on RA and radio altitude between 800 ft and 1500 ft
SLAT/FLAP FULL
fragen.erklaerung_en: APPR 2 requires, among other things, both RA-BARO on RA, RA between 800 and 1500 ft, valid minimums on both PFDs, both NAV on the correct LOC frequency and SLAT/FLAP 5.

fragen.frage: Ab welcher Abweichung wird im CAT-II-Approach (zwischen 500 ft und 80 ft RA) eine Localizer Excessive Deviation angezeigt?
antworten: Ungefähr 1/2 Dot
Ungefähr 1/3 Dot
Ungefähr 1 Dot
Ungefähr 2/3 Dot
fragen.erklaerung: Bei einer Localizer-Abweichung grösser als ca. 1/3 Dot werden Pointer und Skala amber (Skala blinkt); für den Glideslope gilt ca. 1 Dot.
fragen.zitat: If a localizer deviation greater than approximately 1/3 dot is detected:
kontext:
EXCESSIVE LOCALIZER AND GLIDE SLOPE DEVIATIONS

WARNINGS

The on-side localizer and glideslope excessive deviations are compared to the CAT II limits and displayed when the following conditions are met:
– APR mode selected on Guidance Panel.
– SLAT/FLAP 5.

– CAT II Decision Height setting on Guidance Panel.
– VOR/LOC is the active course is valid.
– On-side radio altitude between 500 ft and 80 ft.
– On-side localizer tuned and valid.
– on-side glideslope valid.
– No back course selected.
– Go-around not selected on either side.

Page 28/40 Flight Guidance Control System REVISION 15

Localizer excessive deviation:
If a localizer deviation greater than approximately 1/3 dot is detected:

– the pointer of excessive lateral deviation changes from green to amber
– the lateral deviation scale changes from white to amber, and flash.
Refer to ADI Indications in 14-09-05 for details.

NOTE: The on-side excessive deviation warning is also displayed when the cross-side system has detected an excessive deviation.

Glideslope excessive deviation:

If a glideslope deviation greater than approximately one dot is detected:
– the GS pointer changes from green to amber
– the GS scale changes from white to amber, and flash.
Refer to ADI Indications in 14-09-05 for details.

NOTE: The on-side excessive deviation warning is also displayed when the cross-side system has detected an excessive deviation.

REVISION 15 Flight Guidance Control System Page 29/40
fragen.frage_en: At what deviation is a Localizer Excessive Deviation displayed during a CAT II approach (between 500 ft and 80 ft RA)?
antworten_en: Approx. 1/2 dot
Approx. 1/3 dot
Approx. 1 dot
Approx. 2/3 dot
fragen.erklaerung_en: With a localizer deviation greater than approx. 1/3 dot, pointer and scale turn amber (scale flashes); for the glideslope approx. 1 dot applies.

fragen.frage: Wie verhält sich das Autoland-System der E2 bei einem Systemfehler?
antworten: Fail-passive: Autoland trennt ohne wesentliche Bahn- oder Lageabweichung, das automatische Landing ist aber nicht mehr möglich
Fail-operational: Das Landing wird automatisch mit dem verbleibenden Kanal fortgesetzt
Autoland geht automatisch in den GA Mode über
Das System schaltet in den Direct Mode und der AP bleibt engaged
fragen.erklaerung: Das Autoland ist fail-passive: Bei einem Fehler trennt es ohne wesentliche Abweichung, die Fähigkeit zum automatischen Landing geht verloren.
fragen.zitat: The Autoland is a fail-passive system.
kontext:
APPR II NOT AVAILABLE

AUTOLAND

The E-Jets E2 are optionally equipped with an Autoland system. The system has capability to perform CAT I, CAT II, or CAT III (Minimum DH limited to 50 ft) approaches.
The Autoland is a fail-passive system.

Therefore, in the event of a failure, the Autoland disengages with no significant deviation of flight path or attitude, but the capability to complete the landing operation automatically is lost.

AUTOLAND 1 consists of approach, touchdown, and 5 seconds of rollout. Autoland is able to be performed with or without autothrottle, with or without autobrake, and with one engine inoperative.
fragen.frage_en: How does the E2 autoland system behave on a system failure?
antworten_en: Fail-passive: autoland disconnects without significant path or attitude deviation, but automatic landing is no longer possible
Fail-operational: the landing is continued automatically with the remaining channel
Autoland automatically changes to GA mode
The system switches to Direct Mode and the AP remains engaged
fragen.erklaerung_en: Autoland is fail-passive: on a failure it disconnects without significant deviation and the capability for automatic landing is lost.

fragen.frage: AUTOLAND 1 ist armiert, aber die Flaps sind beim Durchsinken von 800 ft RA noch nicht auf 5. Was geschieht?
antworten: AUTOLAND 1 disarmiert, APPR 1 engaged und APPR 1 ONLY erscheint amber
AUTOLAND 1 bleibt armiert bis 150 ft
Der Autopilot trennt mit Aural "NO AUTOLAND"
Es wird automatisch ein Go-Around eingeleitet
fragen.erklaerung: Sinkt das Flugzeug mit armiertem (nicht engaged) Autoland unter 800 ft RA, disarmiert AUTOLAND 1, APPR 1 engaged und APPR 1 ONLY wird amber angezeigt.
fragen.zitat: If Autoland is armed and the aircraft descends below 800 ft RA the following events occur:
kontext:
CONDITIONS TO ARM/ENGAGE

The operational conditions to arm Autoland are:
– EICAS message AUTOLAND 1 NOT AVAIL not presented,
– Autoland enabled in the MCDU (AUTOLAND OFF not present),
– Autopilot engaged,
– PFD 1 and PFD 2 lateral and vertical deviations are valid and not miscompare,
– MINIMUMS Knob (OUTER) set to RA on both sides,
– Minimums selected to the same value on both PFDs and at or above 50 ft,
– Both PFDs set to the same ILS Course (NAV or Preview),
– Steep Approach not armed or engaged,

Page 34/40 Flight Guidance Control System REVISION 15

– Both NAV Radios tuned to the same ILS/LOC frequency,
– Approach modes LOC/GS armed or active,
– RADALT 1(2) CAS messages and -RA amber indication inside the radio altitude box are not displayed.
The operational conditions to engage Autoland are:
– AUTOLAND 1 armed,
– Flaps 5,
– Glideslope and Localizer being tracked, and
– Both radio altimeters indicating less than 1500 ft and more than 800 ft.
If the flap setting is the only remaining condition to be satisfied for Autoland, the armed status will remain displayed down to 800 ft RA, suggesting there is still one pilot’s action pending.
If Autoland is armed and the aircraft descends below 800 ft RA the following events occur:

– AUTOLAND 1 disarms and the annunciation is removed,
– APPR 1 engages. APPR 1 annunciation displays at the top right side of the FMA and flashes inverse video for 5 seconds,
– APPR 1 ONLY annunciation displays at the top left side of the FMA, flashes amber inverse video for 5 seconds, and then steady, and
– The Minimum digits on the PFD flash amber inverse video for 5 seconds and then steady

AUTOTHROTTLE ENGAGEMENT

The AT engages on ground when all of the following conditions occur:
– no AT active failures.
– AT button pressed on the guidance panel.
– both thrust levers above 50° TLA.
The AT engages on flight when all of the following conditions occur:
– no AT active failures.
– AT button pressed on the guidance panel.
–
airplane at or above 400 ft AGL.

fragen.zitat: In this case, turn the flight director OFF to revert the AT to SPDT.
kontext:
SPEED ON ELEVATOR MODE (SPDE)

The AT maintains a fixed thrust setting, and the flight director adjusts the pitch attitude to maintain the selected airspeed.

For small altitude changes the AT commands only the necessary thrust in order to maintain a comfortable predetermined schedule based on vertical speed.

For large altitude changes the AT commands:
– idle thrust for descent
– maximum thrust limited by the N1 target chevron.
The vertical modes related to SPDE mode are:
– flight level change (FLCH)
– overspeed (OVSP)
– VNAV flight level change (FLCH magenta).

14-03-20

Page 4/10 Thrust Management REVISION 14

NOTE: With the AT mode in SPDE and the AP disengaged, deviating from the flight director commands may lead to an undesired airspeed, as the AT keeps the engine thrust fixed and pitch attitude changes controls the airspeed.
In this case, turn the flight director OFF to revert the AT to SPDT.
This procedure is to have engine thrust controlling airspeed.

kontext:
RETARD MODE (RETD)

The Retard mode reduces the thrust levers to the idle during flare on landing. The Retard mode arms when all of the following conditions occur:
– radio altimeter with valid information,
– autothrottle engaged,
– Slat/Flap lever position at 5 or FULL and landing gear down, and
– radio altitude below 150 ft AGL.
Retard mode engages at or below 30 ft.

In a normal flare, the retard mode is scheduled to reduce thrust levers to idle so that idle thrust is achieved upon airplane touch down. In case of the Slat/Flap position is different than 5 or Full, the retard mode activates only when the airplane touches down.

ABNORMAL OPERATION LOGIC

kontext:
IESI SENSOR FAILURE

If a single sensor failure occurs, for example the static air pressure or total air pressure, the affected indication becomes lost or unreliable.

In case of unreliable information, the indicator looks normal but the information presented is incorrect when compared to the other similar indicators. To demonstrate a split between similar indicators, an yellow "ALT" or "IAS" flag is presented accordingly on the PFD.

In case of lost information a red flag is displayed over the failed indicator.

The CAS message “ADS MISCOMPARE” is associated with erroneous altitude or airspeed data provided by two or more ADSPs. The thresholds to activate the message are the same as the thresholds for the ADS miscompare flags:
200 ft for altitude and 5 kt for airspeed.

kontext:
RADIO ALTIMETER SYSTEM

The radio altimeter function measures the airplane height above terrain and sends this information to be displayed on the PFD and to be used by the other airplane systems.

To determine the height, the radio altimeter transmits a signal to the ground. The time it takes to receive the signal return is converted into radio altitude.
The radio altimeter range of operation is -20 ft to 2500 ft.

When the airplane is parked at the gate or nearby, the presence of irregular surfaces (tools, tool carts, stairs, cables) can affect the measurements of radio altimeter altitude. As a result, both PFDs may display the miscompare RAD ALT and may trigger the EICAS message APPR 2 NOT AVAIL.

kontext:
RADIO ALTIMETER TEST

The system has a self test that may be performed by the pilot on the MENU page on the MCDU performing the following steps:
– Push the LSK 1L (MISC)
– Push the LSK 4R (TEST)
– On the TEST page 2/2, push the LSK 3L (RAD ALT) and check the MCDU showing RAD ALT test ON.
The expected radio altitude indication is 50 ft ±5 ft on PFD 1 and PFD 2.

NOTE: If the indication is any other than 50 ft ±5 ft, the radio altitude indicated is not reliable.

– Push the LSK 3L (OFF) to stop the test.

fragen.zitat: The initial IESS alignment takes about 90 seconds to be completed
kontext:
NORMAL OPERATION

During normal operation, the IESS computes and displays attitude, slip-skid indication, altitude (baro corrected), airspeed, vertical speed, Mach number and IESS.

The buttons functionalities are:
– CAGE pushbutton: if depressed, the standby performs a CAGE in the internal gyros to cancel the accumulated drift.
– ILS button: if pressed, glideslope and localizer deviations is displayed.
– STD button: if pressed, STD baro is set. To adjust baro, rotate the knob.
– and buttons: controls display brightness.
– "Push FT-M" in the Guidance Panel: automatically displays altitude in meters.
– "MAIN PNL" in the Overhead Panel: controls IESI bezel illumination.
The IESS is powered as soon as the airplane battery 1 is selected to ON and airplane battery 2 is selected to AUTO. Then, the IESS starts its alignment phase.
The initial IESS alignment takes about 90 seconds to be completed

and can be identified on the screen by the "INIT 90 s" flag.

NOTE: The airplane must not be moved during the first 90 seconds after power-up, while the IESS is undergoing alignment.
Moving the airplane during this period can cause in-flight attitude indication errors that may not be noticeable on ground.

fragen.frage: In welchem Modus arbeitet das GPS, wenn weniger als vier Satelliten getrackt werden?

Differential
Failed

fragen.zitat: When fewer than four satellites are tracked, altitude aiding is the active mode
kontext:
– ALTITUDE AIDING

– FAILED

REVISION 14 Navigation Page 7/72

After power is applied, the acquisition mode is used to acquire satellites. The GPS tracks four satellites to acquire its position.
When fewer than four satellites are tracked, altitude aiding is the active mode,

otherwise choose the appropriated navigation mode. In altitude aiding mode GPS uses altitude from the digital air data computer (ADS) to help position determination.

The GPS is also capable to receive Satelite-Based Augmentation System (SBAS) to improve signals and provide a more accurate position output.
The approach with LPV minimums is selected in the FMS and inserted on the active flight plan. Once LPV mode is engaged, the autopilot also uses the GPS deviations to control the airplane.
Any faults within the GPS module is reported on the FMS MCDU and on the EICAS. The Message ("MSG") indicator on the PFD illuminates, and "GPS 1 FAIL" or "GPS 2 FAIL" advisory CAS message is displayed. The GPS STATUS SENSOR page also displays the GPS failure indication.

fragen.zitat: VDR 3 provides voice communication as well as data communications through ACARS
kontext:
RADIO COMMUNICATION VHF

The VHF digital radios (VDR) 1 and 2 are located in the Modular Radio Cabinets (MRC). VDR 1 and 2 interfaces with the audio system through the audio or microphone busses, and with the MCDU or PFD through the ASCB. VDR channels 1 and 2 are for voice communication only.

VDR 3 interfaces with audio system, MCDU and PFD indirectly via MRC 2 and directly to MAU 1 to data transmission. The VHF radio 3 is on a separated radio Mini Cabinet.
VDR 3 provides voice communication as well as data communications through ACARS

(Aircraft Communication Addressing and Reporting System) applications.

NOTE: While transmitting in one VHF channel by pressing the PTT button, the audio received on the other channels from a ground station at a distance greater than 130 NM may be degraded or muted. Once the PTT button is released, the communication is re-established without the degradation.

The VHF data radio modules provide communication in the frequency range of 118.000 MHz to 136.975 MHz with 8.33 kHz or 25 kHz. The VHF frequency is tuned and activated through the MCDU (primary controller) or CCD/PFD (secundatry controller) and adhere to the ICAO FM immunity requirement.

A tuning backup is available in MCDU 2 in case of loss of both MAUs.
In the same way, if the audio bus is lost there are audio backups.

The flight crew may tune the VHF frequency on the MCDU as follows:

VHF 1/2

TCAS WARNING INHIBITIONS

The INCREASE DESCENT command is inhibited at altitudes below 1450 ft AGL during descent, or below 1650 ft AGL during climb.

The DESCENT command is inhibited at altitudes below 1000 ft AGL during descent, or below 1200 ft AGL during climb.
The TCAS automatically reverts to TA ONLY mode and inhibits RAs for altitudes below 900 ft AGL during descent,

All TCAS aural advisories are inhibited when the present position altitude is below 400 ft AGL during descent, or 600 ft AGL during climb.

kontext:
TCAS ALTITUDE RANGE MODES

The altitude range is the region, from the present position altitude, covered by TCAS system. There are four different ways to set the TCAS altitude range:
–
NORMAL: shows targets that are within 2700 ft above or below current airplane altitude.

– ABOVE: shows targets that are within 9900 ft above and 2700 ft below current airplane altitude.
– BELOW: shows targets that are within 2700 ft above to 9900 ft below current airplane altitude.
– EXPANDED: shows targets that are within 9900 ft above or below current airplane altitude.

kontext:
GROUND PROXIMITY WARNING SYSTEM

The EGPWS calculates these seven basic functions by comparing the airplane position to an internal terrain database to output alerts and displays that show the airplane situation.

Mode 1 - Excessive descent rates with SINK RATE and PULL UP aural warnings.

NOTE: Steep Approach operation implies to the airplane a vertical speed higher than the normal. For this reason the Steep Approach mode once activated, adds fixed positive biases to both the SINK RATE curve, and the PULL UP curve permitting steeper than normal instrument approaches without unwanted alerts.

Mode 2 - Excessive terrain closure rates with TERRAIN, TERRAIN and PULL UP aural warnings.

Mode
3 - Altitude loss after takeoff with a DON'T SINK, DON'T SINK aural warnings.

Mode 4 - Unsafe terrain clearance with TOO LOW TERRAIN, TOO LOW GEAR and TOO LOW FLAPS aural warnings.

Mode 5 - Excessive deviation below glideslope with a GLIDESLOPE aural warning.

Mode 6 - Advisory callouts with BANK ANGLE, APPROACHING MINIMUMS, MINIMUMS, and selected callout altitude aural warnings.
Mode 7 - Windshear alerting as WINDSHEAR, WINDSHEAR,
WINDSHEAR.

(EGPWS)

kontext:
PASSENGER AND SERVICE DOORS

This airplane has one passenger door at the left forward section of the fuselage and another at the aft fuselage section. Passenger door operation is manual and it is identical for both passenger doors.
Passenger doors are plug type and they are of type 1 design.

One service door is at the right forward section of the fuselage and another at the aft fuselage section. Service doors are primarily used for galley servicing and cabin cleaning between flights. It also serves as an emergency exit. The operation of service and passenger doors is identical.

One external, two internal handles and one vent flap are installed in each door for opening and closing operation.
Passenger and service doors were designed to support winds up to 65 kt while the door is fully open and locked.

Therefore, doors must be closed before the wind speed achieves 65 kt.

REVISION 15 Doors Page 1/20

A wind of 40 kt was considered during design for door operation (opening or closing). Therefore, if the wind is above 40 kt and door operation is needed, caution must be taken during door operation since the wind direction may affect door displacement.

fragen.frage: Was geschieht mit der Escape Slide einer Passenger/Service Door, wenn die Tür von aussen geöffnet wird?

kontext:
ESCAPE SLIDE

The escape slides are designed to provide passengers and crew means to safely descend from the airplane to the ground during an emergency evacuation. In the event of emergency evacuation, the slides deploy automatically when the exit door is opened.

The emergency evacuation slides are equipped with a lighting system independent from the airplane. The unfolding process activates the lighting system illuminating the sliding surface and the area where crew and passengers make first contact with the ground. A battery contained within the slide provides electrical power to the lights.

A dedicated battery powers the lights for a minimum of 10 minutes even after the escape slide is disconnected.

The escape slides on the passengers and service doors are armed by opening the slide arming lever cover located on the door and moving the slide arming lever down to the armed position.
Opening the door from the outside automatically disarms the slide.

The overwing emergency exits (OWE) are also equipped with escape slides to support evacuation. The slides are installed on the wing- fuselage fairing and are always armed during operation. The status from the slide cylinder pressure is displayed on the Flight Attendant Panel. The slide inflates automatically when the door is open and it is only disarmed through maintenance procedures. The OWE escape slides are also equipped with emergency lights to illuminate the surrounding surface.

In ditching condition, the escape slides from the passenger and service doors are used as flotation devices after disconnection from the airplane. The OWE escape slides do not disconnect from the airplane, and may not deploy or be usable in this condition, due to the system is partially submerged. Therefore, the OWE escape slides are not considered as flotation devices.

If the mooring line that connects airplane and slide is not manually detached from the airplane, the line breaks free if enough load is applied.

14-01-50

REVISION 14 Escape Slide Page 1/8

kontext:

Actuating the EMERGENCY ENTRY pushbutton on the galley G1, the chime alarm sequence starts. The DING-DONG sound chime remains on for 4 s and is repeated three times at 9-second intervals during which the sound chime remains paused.

kontext:
ELECTROMECHANICAL LATCH

The electrical operation is through the cockpit control panel. The control panel in the cockpit sends an electrical pulse to the electromechanical latch, which locks the door. The door is unlocked when a new electrical pulse is sent to the electromechanical latch.

The DC ESS BUS 3 powers the electromechanical latch.
In case of electrical failure, the door latch stays in its previous setting.

Manual operation is through the manual lock/unlock knob on the electromechanical door latch. The latch locks the door when the knob is moved upwards. Once it is locked, a green indication is exposed on the latch. The latch unlocks when the manual lock/unlock knob is moved upwards again. When it is unlocked, a red indication is exposed on the latch.

The door latch indication in green and red indicates when the door is locked and open, respectively. The indication is also independently of how the electromechanical latch is operated, electrically or manually.

If the electromechanical latch is locked while the door is opened, the door does not close. It is necessary to unlock the electromechanical latch to move the door to the closed position.

kontext:
INTEGRATED DRIVE GENERATOR (IDG)

Each engine has an IDG. A dedicated generator control unit (GCU) controls and monitors each IDG. As an engine spools up, the respective IDG automatically comes on line, powering the respective AC BUS. The previous power source is disconnected from that AC BUS.

Each IDG selector knob in AUTO position sets the electrical system to automatic operation.

If a selector knob is moved to the OFF position, the respective generator line contactor opens, tripping off-line and de-exciting the related IDG.

When an IDG low oil pressure or oil overtemperature condition is detected, the CAS message IDG 1 (2) OIL displays. Additionally, an amber light illuminates next to the respective IDG selector knob on the overhead panel. The amber light indicates the IDG to be disconnected and extinguishes after the IDG disconnection.

14-05-10

Page 2/6 AC System REVISION 15

Manual IDG disconnection is achieved by selecting the respective IDG knob to the DISC position and holding for one second.
Automatic IDG disconnection occurs when flight crew does not perform the manual disconnection after an abnormal detection and indication of oil low pressure or oil overtemperature.
An IDG disconnection means that the IDG is mechanically disconnected. The flight crew cannot perform a reconnection and the IDG remains disconnect until a maintenance action is performed.

fragen.erklaerung_en: If the crew does not perform a manual disconnect after low oil pressure or oil overtemperature, an automatic IDG disconnect occurs; reconnection by the crew is not possible.

fragen.zitat: The ICCs remote thermal CBs can only be reset by maintenance personal when the airplane is on ground.
kontext:
CIRCUIT BREAKERS (CB)

Circuit Breakers are classified as either thermal or electronic CBs.

Some thermal CBs are on the cockpit sidewall panels and others are located inside the ICCs in the electronics bays.

The electronic CBs are located inside the SPDAs, in the electronics bays.

All CBs located in the electronics bays are considered remote CBs.

The flight crew can visually monitor all circuit breakers located inside the cockpit and, via MCDUs, the remote CBs in the electronics bays.
The ICCs remote thermal CBs can only be reset by maintenance personal when the airplane is on ground.

The flight crew can reset the SPDA remote electronic CBs via the
MCDU.
fragen.frage_en: Who can reset the remote Thermal Circuit Breakers in the ICCs?
antworten_en: The flight crew via the MCDU
The flight crew at the cockpit sidewall panel
The SPDA automatically after 3 s
Maintenance personnel on the ground only
fragen.erklaerung_en: The remote thermal CBs of the ICCs can be reset only by maintenance on the ground; the electronic SPDA CBs can be reset by the crew via the MCDU.

fragen.zitat: During the APU starting cycle, BATT 2 is isolated from the network.
kontext:
APU GENERATOR

The APU Generator supplies power to the AC BUSES on the ground or in-flight.

On the ground, the APU Generator can supply power to the entire airplane with no operational degradation.
During the APU starting cycle, BATT 2 is isolated from the network.

In flight, the APU Generator is limited to the availability of at least one IDG, otherwise the load shedding functionality is automatically activated.

In automatic mode, the APU Generator has priority over the AC GPU in supplying power to the airplane.
fragen.frage_en: What happens to BATT 2 during the APU start cycle?
antworten_en: BATT 2 is connected in parallel with BATT 1
BATT 2 is isolated from the network
BATT 2 supplies DC ESS BUS 3
BATT 2 is charged via TRU ESS
fragen.erklaerung_en: During the APU start cycle BATT 2 is isolated from the rest of the network (it supplies the APU START BUS).

fragen.zitat: is 10°C or below and visible moisture in any form is present
kontext:
1.4.7.1 Operation in Icing Conditions

Icing conditions may exist whenever the Outside Air Temperature (OAT) on the ground or for takeoff, or Total Air Temperature (TAT) inflight,
is 10°C or below and visible moisture in any form is present

(such as clouds, fog with visibility of one mile or less, rain, snow, sleet, and ice crystals).
Icing conditions may also exist when the OAT on the ground and for takeoff is 10°C or below when operating on ramps, taxiways, or runways where surface snow, ice, standing water, or slush may be ingested by the engines, or freeze on engines, nacelles, or engine sensor probes.

CAUTION: On ground, do not rely on visual icing evidence or ice detector actuation to turn on the anti-icing system. use the temperature and visual moisture criteria as specified above. delaying the use of the

anti- icing system until ice build-up is visible from the cockpit may result in ice ingestion and possible engine damage or flame-out.

For detailed procedure refer to 2.8.3.2 - Icing Conditions, Cold Weather and

Cold Soak Operation

kontext:
0.8 Definitions and Symbols

For the purpose of this MEL the following definitions shall apply: a. «Visual Meteorological Conditions (VMC) means the atmospheric environment is such that would allow a flight to proceed under the Visual Flight Rules applicable to the flight. This does not preclude operating under Instrument Flight Rules. b. «Day» operation is any flight conducted from the point of take-off to landing between 30 minutes before sunrise and 30 minutes after sunset. c. (dash) in columns 3 or 4 indicates a variable quantity. Additionally, a dash is used when the exact item count is not operationally significant, for example: when the component cannot be individually quantified or when the quantity is inherently large and non-limiting for dispatch a. «Icing Condition the atmospheric environment is such that ice can form on the aircraft or in the engine(s) b. «Commencement of flight the point when an aircraft begins to move under its own power for the purpose of preparing for take off. c. «Inoperative means the equipment does not accomplish its intended purpose or is not consistently functioning within its design operating limits or tolerances. d. Some systems have been designed to be fault tolerant and are monitored by digital computers which transmit fault messages to a centralised computer for the purpose of maintenance. The presence of this category of message does not mean that the system is inoperative. e. «Combustible Material» material which is capable of catching fire and burning. In particular: if a MEL item prohibits loading of combustible (or flammable or inflammable) material, no material may be loaded except the following:
1. Cargo handling equipment (unloaded, empty or with ballast);
2. Fly away kits (excluding e.g. cans of hydraulic fluid, cleaning solvents, batteries, capacitors, chemical generators, etc.); NOTE: If serviceable tyres are included, they should only be inflated to a minimum pressure that preserves their serviceability;
3. Inflight service material (return catering only closed catering trolleys/boxes, no newspapers, no alcohol or duty free goods). f. Print in different typeface (e.g. italics): items which according to MEL are subject to national regulations (e.g. «as required by EASA») text or numbers that are different from the original MMEL entry.

Normally these procedures are accomplished by maintenance personnel; any other personnel qualified and authorized to perform certain functions must be defined in the MME and MEL. Appropriate (M)-procedures are required to be published as part of the operator`s manual or MEL. k.

which must be accomplished in planning for and/or operating with the listed item inoperative. Normally these procedures are accomplished by the flight crew; any other personnel qualified and authorized to perform certain functions must be defined in the MME and in the MEL. Appropriate (O)- procedures are required to be published as part of the operator`s manual or l. «(P)» symbol requires inoperative equipment, component, system or function to be placarded in the flightdeck to inform and remind the crewmembers of the equipment condition. m. «Deleted» in the remarks column after a sequence item indicates that the item was previously listed but is now required to be operative if installed. n. «Out of sight» remark means that inoperative equipment shall be be stowed in a place which prevents it to be used or mistaken as operational equipment. o. «Extended Overwater» means operations over water at a distance away from land suitable for making an emergency landing, greater than that corresponding to 120 minutes at cruising speed or 400 NM, whichever is the lesser.

kontext:
1.4.7.1 Operation in Icing Conditions

There is no temperature limitation for anti-icing system automatic operation.

On ground:

The TO DATASET MENU on the MCDU must be set to ENG when OAT is within 5-10°C and:

if there is any possibility of encountering visible moisture up to 1700 ft AFE,

or when operating on ramps, taxiways, or runways where surface snow, ice, standing water, or slush may be ingested by the engines, or freeze on engines, nacelles, or engine sensor probes.
The TO DATASET MENU on the MCDU must be set to ALL when OAT is below 5°C:

if there is any possibility of encountering visible moisture up to 1700 ft AFE, or when operating on ramps, taxiways, or runways where surface snow, ice, standing water, or slush may be ingested by the engines, or freeze on engines, nacelles, or engine sensor probes.

OM-B E1 1 Limitations

In flight:
The engine and wing anti-ice systems operate automatically, in case of ice encounter when the Ice Protection MODE Knob is in the AUTO position.
If either one or both ice detectors are failed, the crew must set the mode selector to ON when icing conditions exist or are anticipated at or below 10°C TAT with visible moisture.

Closely monitor the TAT indication and presence of moisture.

If environmental ice conditions exist, even intermittent, check the windshield, windshield wiper (if installed), and wing surface for ice accumulation. To

visualize ice formation, if necessary, use a flashlight on the windshield and

the wing inspection light on the wing.
If any ice formation is detected or suspected, select the antiice protection system override knob to ON. When flying in detected or suspected ice conditions, use ice speeds as reference.

Note: Icing conditions may exist whenever the Outside Air Temperature (OAT) on ground or for takeoff, or Total Air Temperature (TAT) in flight, is 10°C or less and visible moisture in any form is present (such as clouds, fog with visibility of one mile or less, rain, snow, sleet, and ice crystals).

Icing conditions may also exist when the OAT on ground or for takeoff is 10°C or less when operating on ramps, taxiways, or runways where surface snow, ice, standing water, or slush may be ingested by the engines, or freeze on engines, nacelles, or engine

sensor probes.
CAUTION: On ground, do not rely on visual icing evidence or ice detector

actuation to turn on the anti-icing system. Use the temperature and

visual moisture criteria as specified above. Delaying the use of the

antiicing system until ice build-up is visible from the cockpit may result in ice ingestion and possible engine damage or flameout.

For detailed procedure refer to 2.8.3.2 - Icing Conditions, Cold Weather and

Cold Soak Operation.

fragen.frage: Wann sollen die predictive EGPWS-Funktionen manuell inhibiert werden?
antworten: Bei jedem Visual Approach
Beim Landing auf einem Flughafen, der nicht in der Airport Database ist
Bei Steep Approaches
Bei Nacht-Landings ohne ILS
fragen.erklaerung: Zur Vermeidung unerwünschter Alerts sind die predictive Funktionen bei Flughäfen ausserhalb der Datenbank (sowie bei QFE ohne GPS) zu inhibieren.
fragen.zitat: The use of predictive EGPWS functions should be manually inhibited when landing at an airport that is not in the airport database to avoid unwanted alerts.
kontext:
ORIGINAL - ANAC APPROVED

Navigation is not to be predicated on the use of the Terrain Awareness System.
The use of predictive EGPWS functions should be manually inhibited when landing at an airport that is not in the airport database to avoid unwanted alerts.

Pilots are authorized to deviate from their current Air Traffic Control (ATC) clearance to the extent necessary to comply with an EGPWS warning.
The Terrain Display is intended to be used as a situational tool only and may not provide the accuracy and/or fidelity on which to solely base terrain avoidance maneuvering.
The use of predictive EGPWS functions should be manually inhibited during QFE operations if GPS data is unavailable or inoperative.
fragen.frage_en: When should the predictive EGPWS functions be inhibited manually?
antworten_en: On every visual approach
When landing at an airport that is not in the airport database
On steep approaches
On night landings without ILS
fragen.erklaerung_en: To avoid unwanted alerts, the predictive functions are to be inhibited at airports outside the database (and at QFE without GPS).

fragen.frage: (E2) Was gilt für das Synthetic Vision System (SVS)?
antworten: Es erlaubt eine Reduktion der Minima um 50 ft
Es darf als primäre Navigationsreferenz dienen
Es darf nicht für IFR-Kredit unter den publizierten Minima verwendet werden
Es ist nur für CAT II zugelassen
fragen.erklaerung: Das SVS dient nur der Situational Awareness; Kredit für IFR-Operationen unter Minima ist verboten.
fragen.zitat: The use of the SVS to take credit for IFR operations below published minima is prohibited.
kontext:
ORIGINAL - ANAC APPROVED

The Synthetic Vision System (SVS) function is intended to be used as an aid to situational awareness only. The SVS must not be used as primary flight information for navigation purpose.
The use of the SVS to take credit for IFR operations below published minima is prohibited.

LIMITATIONS

fragen.frage: Wie definiert die MEL den Begriff 'Inoperative'?

kontext:
0.8 Definitions and Symbols

For the purpose of this MEL the following definitions shall apply: a. «Visual Meteorological Conditions (VMC) means the atmospheric environment is such that would allow a flight to proceed under the Visual Flight Rules applicable to the flight. (dash) in columns 3 or 4 indicates a variable quantity. Additionally, a dash is used when the exact item count is not operationally significant, for example: when the component cannot be individually quantified or when the quantity is inherently large and non-limiting for dispatch a. «Icing Condition the atmospheric environment is such that ice can form on the aircraft or in the engine(s) b. «Commencement of flight the point when an aircraft begins to move under its own power for the purpose of preparing for take off. c. «Inoperative
means the equipment does not accomplish its intended purpose or is not consistently functioning within its design operating limits or tolerances.

The presence of this category of message does not mean that the system is inoperative. e. «Combustible Material» material which is capable of catching fire and burning. In particular: if a MEL item prohibits loading of combustible (or flammable or inflammable) material, no material may be loaded except the following:

2. Fly away kits (excluding e.g. cans of hydraulic fluid, cleaning solvents, batteries, capacitors, chemical generators, etc.); NOTE: If serviceable tyres are included, they should only be inflated to a minimum pressure that preserves their serviceability;
3. Inflight service material (return catering only closed catering trolleys/boxes, no newspapers, no alcohol or duty free goods). f. Print in different typeface (e.g. italics): items which according to MEL are subject to national regulations (e.g. «as required by EASA») text or numbers that are different from the original MMEL entry.

Normally these procedures are accomplished by maintenance personnel; any other personnel qualified and authorized to perform certain functions must be defined in the MME and MEL. Appropriate (M)-procedures are required to be published as part of the operator`s manual or MEL. k. «(O)» symbol indicates a requirement for a specific operations procedure which must be accomplished in planning for and/or operating with the listed item inoperative. Normally these procedures are accomplished by the flight crew; any other personnel qualified and authorized to perform certain functions must be defined in the MME and in the MEL. Appropriate (O)- procedures are required to be published as part of the operator`s manual or l. «(P)» symbol requires inoperative equipment, component, system or function to be placarded in the flightdeck to inform and remind the crewmembers of the equipment condition. m. «Deleted» in the remarks column after a sequence item
indicates that the item was previously listed but is now required to be operative if installed.

n. «Out of sight» remark means that inoperative equipment shall be be stowed in a place which prevents it to be used or mistaken as operational equipment. o. «Extended Overwater» means operations over water at a distance away from land suitable for making an emergency landing, greater than that corresponding to 120 minutes at cruising speed or 400 NM, whichever is the lesser.

kontext:
0.1 Introduction

This Minimum Equipment List [MEL] is based on the Embraer170/175/190/195 series EASA Master Minimum Equipment List [MMEL] This MEL takes into consideration Helvetic Airways AG particular aircraft equipment, configuration and operational conditions, the area of operation, EUOPS requirements and FOCA requirements.
This MEL will not deviate from any applicable Airworthiness Directive or any other Requirement and will be no less restrictive than the MMEL.
The operational and maintenance procedures referenced in the MEL are based on the operational and maintenance procedures referenced in the MMEL.
Modified procedures by helvetic provide at least the same level of safety, as required by the MMEL.
Operational and maintenance notes present advisory information and are not procedures required to be followed per MEL.

The MEL is intended to permit operations with inoperative items of equipment for a specified period of time until rectification has to be accomplished.
Rectifications are to be accomplished at the earliest opportunity, but within the time-frame specified in the MEL.
MEL Conditions and Limitations do not relieve the Commander from determining that the aircraft is in a fit condition for safe operation with specified unserviceable items or systems allowed by the MEL.
The provisions of the MEL are applicable until the aircraft commences the flight, i.e. the point when an aeroplane begins to move under its own power for the purpose of preparing for take-off.
Any decision to continue a flight following a failure or unserviceability which becomes apparent after the commencement of a flight must be the subject of pilot judgement and good airmanship. If a failure or unserviceability is subject to a MEL restriction and will result in an AOG condition due to a lack of maintenance personnel or equipment at the destination, depending on the moment of occurrence, a return to point of departure shall be considered. The Commander may continue to make reference to and use of the MEL as appropriate.
By approval of the MEL the Authority permits dispatch of the aircraft for revenue, ferry or training flights with certain items or components inoperative provided an acceptable level of safety is maintained by use of appropriate operational or maintenance procedures, by transfer of the function to another operating component, or by reference to other instruments or components providing the required information.

kontext:
BEFORE START:

Affected PITCH TRIM Switch.........................ACTUATE
NOTE:

The affected PITCH TRIM Switch must be verified in both directions (UP and DOWN).
Make sure that there is no movement of the horizontal stabilizer. Use the Pitch Trim Position Indication on EICAS. If the EICAS indication is not available, use the tail cone markings.
If the horizontal stabilizer moves, or if the switch is not inactive, do as follows:
- Actuate and hold any half of the switch for 7 seconds.
NOTE:

The PITCH TRIM BKUP FAIL Advisory EICAS message may be displayed.
- Repeat the verification of the switch.
- If the procedure was not successful, perform it again with the other half of the switch.
NOTE:

The switch may become active again after:
- Cycling the Pitch Trim SYS 1 and SYS 2 CUTOUT Buttons, or
- An airplane power down and power up procedure.

fragen.frage: Bis zu welcher Wassertiefe gilt eine Runway gemäss OM-B als "wet" (und noch nicht als contaminated)?
antworten: Bis und mit 3 mm
Bis und mit 6 mm
Bis und mit 2 mm
Bis und mit 13 mm
fragen.erklaerung: Wet runway ist definiert als Oberfläche mit sichtbarer Feuchtigkeit oder Wasser bis und mit 3 mm Tiefe im benutzten Bereich.
fragen.zitat: Wet runway means a runway whose surface is covered by any visible dampness or water up to and including 3 mm deep
kontext: 4.0.1.1 Wet and Contaminated

Wet runway means a runway whose surface is covered by any visible dampness

or water up to and including 3 mm deep

within the area intended to be used.

Contaminated runway is a runway where a significant portion of its surface area (whether in isolated areas or not) within the length and width being used, is covered by standing water or slush, or that has an accumulation of snow or ice.
However, in certain other situations it may be appropriate to consider the runway contaminated. For example, if the section of the runway surface that is covered with standing water or slush is located where rotation and lift-off occurs, or during the highspeed part of the takeoff roll, the retardation effect is far more significant than if it were encountered early in the takeoff while at low speed. In this situation, the runway might better be considered 'contaminated' rather than 'wet'.

Takeoff and landing performance calculation assumes a homogeneous contaminant type and depth along the entire runway length and width. If runway conditions are reported for runway thirds, performance calculation should consider the most penalizing contaminant. However, a part of the runway may be

disregarded if the performance calculation accounts for the respective runway reduction.
fragen.frage_en: Up to what water depth is a runway considered "wet" (and not yet contaminated) according to OM-B?
antworten_en: Up to and including 3 mm
Up to and including 6 mm
Up to and including 2 mm
Up to and including 13 mm
fragen.erklaerung_en: A wet runway is defined as a surface with visible moisture or water up to and including 3 mm depth in the area in use.

antworten: Als wet, da nur ein kleiner Teil betroffen ist
Eher als contaminated statt wet, da die Verzögerungswirkung bei hoher Speed viel grösser ist
Der betroffene Abschnitt muss immer von der TORA abgezogen werden
Als dry, da der Grossteil der Runway trocken ist
fragen.erklaerung: Liegt Standing Water oder Slush im Bereich Rotation/Lift-off oder im High-Speed-Teil, ist der Bremseffekt deutlich grösser; die Runway sollte dann eher als contaminated betrachtet werden.
fragen.zitat: In this situation, the runway might better be considered 'contaminated' rather than 'wet'.

antworten_en: As wet, since only a small part is affected
Rather as contaminated than wet, since the deceleration effect at high speed is much greater
The affected section must always be deducted from the TORA

fragen.frage: Was umfasst die ASDA (Accelerate Stop Distance Available)?
antworten: Nur die befestigte Runway-Länge ohne Stopway
TORA plus Clearway
Takeoff Run plus Stopway, sofern deklariert und für das Aircraft Weight tragfähig
TODA plus Stopway
fragen.erklaerung: ASDA ist die für den Takeoff Run deklarierte Länge plus Stopway, sofern dieser deklariert und tragfähig ist. Der Clearway gehört zur TODA.
fragen.zitat: suitable for the ground run of an aircraft taking-off plus the length of stopway, if such stopway is declared available
kontext:
4.0.1.2 Declared Distances

Take Off Run Available (TORA)

The length of a runway, which is declared available by the appropriate authority

and suitable for the ground run of an aircraft taking-off.

Accelerate Stop Distance Available (ASDA)

The length of a runway, which is declared available by the appropriate authority

and
suitable for the ground run of an aircraft taking-off plus the length of stopway, if such stopway is declared available

by the appropriate authority and is capable

of bearing the mass of the aircraft under the prevailing operating conditions.

Take-Off Distance Available (TODA)

The length of a runway available, plus the length of clearway available (if provided).

Landing Distance Available (LDA) The length of a runway, which is declared available by the appropriate authority and suitable for the ground roll of an aircraft.

OM-B E1 4 Performance

Stopway An area at the end of the runway in the direction of take-off, not less wide than the runway and centred upon its existing centreline. It is able to support the aircraft during an aborted take-off, without causing structural damage to the aircraft.

Clearway

An area at the end of the runway in the direction of take-off, not less than 500ft wide, centred on the extended centreline, and under the control of the airport

authorities. It must not exceed an upslope of 1.25%, above which no object or terrain can protrude. Threshold lights may protrude but have height restrictions. A

clearway may not exceed half the runway length.
fragen.frage_en: What does the ASDA (Accelerate Stop Distance Available) comprise?
antworten_en: Only the paved runway length without stopway
TORA plus clearway
Takeoff run plus stopway, if declared and capable of bearing the aircraft weight
TODA plus stopway
fragen.erklaerung_en: ASDA is the declared takeoff run length plus stopway, provided the stopway is declared and capable of bearing the load. The clearway belongs to the TODA.

fragen.frage: Welche Aussage zum Clearway ist gemäss OM-B korrekt?
antworten: Er wird zur ASDA hinzugerechnet
Er muss mindestens so breit wie die Runway sein und das Flugzeug bei einem Rejected Takeoff tragen können
Er darf eine Steigung von maximal 2.5 % aufweisen
Er darf höchstens die halbe Runway-Länge betragen und muss mindestens 500 ft breit sein
fragen.erklaerung: Der Clearway ist mindestens 500 ft breit, hat max. 1.25 % Steigung und darf die halbe Runway-Länge nicht überschreiten. Die Tragfähigkeit beim Rejected Takeoff beschreibt den Stopway.
fragen.zitat: A clearway may not exceed half the runway length.

fragen.frage_en: Which statement about the clearway is correct according to OM-B?
antworten_en: It is added to the ASDA
It must be at least as wide as the runway and be able to bear the aircraft in a rejected takeoff

fragen.frage: Zwischen welchen Grenzen muss V1 liegen?
antworten: Nicht kleiner als 1.05 VMCA und nicht grösser als V2
Nicht kleiner als VS1G und nicht grösser als VMBE
Nicht kleiner als VMCG und nicht grösser als VMBE
Nicht kleiner als VMCA und nicht grösser als VR
fragen.erklaerung: V1 darf nicht kleiner als VMCG (Bodenkontrollierbarkeit) und nicht grösser als VMBE (Brake Energy) sein.
fragen.zitat: V1 must not be less than Vmcg and must not be greater than Vmbe.
kontext:
4.0.1.3 Speed

General The airplane is assumed to accelerate with all engines operating from a standing start point to the point where the critical engine fails (Vef). The airplane continues to accelerate, with one engine inoperative to the point where the engine failure is recognised (V1). If the take-off is continued, using only aerodynamic control and average pilot skills, the airplane accelerates with one engine inoperative, to the point at which V2 is achieved at 35ft above the end of the runway.
If take-off is to be rejected, maximum braking is applied at V1, throttles retarded,

spoilers extended. No credit is taken for the use of reverse thrust during the certification process (dry runway).
V1

At and below V1 the take-off can be rejected and the aircraft will stop within the

accelerate stop distance available. At and above V1 the take-off can be

continued in case of an engine failure.

V1 must not be less than Vmcg and must

not be greater than Vmbe.

This is the speed at which rotation to a normal take-off attitude must begin in order to reach V2 by 35ft (dry) or 15ft (wet).VR must not be less than V1 and

must be at least 1.05 times Vmca.

V2

V2, take-off safety speed, which must be reached by 35ft (dry) or (15ft wet) with

one engine inoperative. V2 must not be less than 1.1 Vmca or 1.2Vs.

OM-B E1 4 Performance

VMCG

This is the minimum control speed on the ground, from which directional control of the airplane can be maintained on the ground after an engine failure without the use of brakes or nose-wheel steering. In other words, it is the minimum speed at which the control surfaces are effective on the ground.

VMCA

VMCA is the lowest speed, at which control of the airplane can be maintained in the air after an engine failure. Banking slightly into the good engine usually

enhances engine out capability. VMCA is determined for the airplane with a

5° maximum bank angle during certification process.

VMBE

This is the maximum speed at which the brakes can absorb all the energy required to stop the airplane at a given mass. V1 must always be less than VMBE.
fragen.frage_en: Between which limits must V1 lie?
antworten_en: Not less than 1.05 VMCA and not greater than V2
Not less than VS1G and not greater than VMBE
Not less than VMCG and not greater than VMBE
Not less than VMCA and not greater than VR
fragen.erklaerung_en: V1 must not be less than VMCG (ground controllability) and not greater than VMBE (brake energy).

fragen.frage: Welche Mindestanforderung gilt gemäss OM-B für V2?
antworten: V2 ≥ 1.1 VMCA oder 1.2 VS
V2 ≥ 1.2 VMCA oder 1.3 VS
V2 ≥ VMCG oder 1.1 VS
V2 ≥ 1.05 VMCA oder 1.13 VS
fragen.erklaerung: V2 (Take-off Safety Speed) darf nicht kleiner als 1.1 VMCA bzw. 1.2 VS sein; VR muss mindestens 1.05 VMCA betragen.
fragen.zitat: V2 must not be less than 1.1 Vmca or 1.2Vs.

35 ft
50 ft

kontext:
4.0.1.4 Flight Path

Take Off Flight Path It is the path from the end of the Take Off Distance (TOD) to the point where the aircraft passes through the screen height up to 1500ft above the take-off surface to a point where the aircraft configuration turns to the en-route configuration. Two

kinds of take off flight paths have to be taken into consideration, gross and net flight path.
Gross Flight Path

Gross flight path demonstrated performance is the performance the operator can

expect to achieve, when the aircraft is flown to the manufacturers recommended

procedures.

Net Flight Path Net flight path performance represents the gross flight path performance

degraded by a legally specific amount. This is a function of the number of engines (0.8% for a twin engine aircraft). Obstacle clearance calculations are

based on the net flight path.

OM-B E1 4 Performance

Screen Height This is the reference height that will be obtained at V2. The screen height value depends on the runway condition: dry: 35 ft
wet or contaminated: 15 ft
fragen.frage_en: Which Screen Height applies for takeoff on a wet or contaminated runway?
antworten_en: 25 ft
35 ft
50 ft
15 ft
fragen.erklaerung_en: The Screen Height is 35 ft on a dry runway and 15 ft on a wet or contaminated runway.

kontext:
5-00 ANAC APPROVED

Page 2 code 02 REVISION 22 AFM-1913
INTRODUCTION

The performance information given in this Section is applicable to all EMBRAER 195 models. For performance information related to the EMBRAER 195 equipped with a specific engine model, refer to the Supplement 1 - CAFM.
The performance data are based on the following conditions:
Pertinent power less installation, air bleed, and accessory losses.
Full temperature accountability within the operational limits for which the airplane is certified.
For landing, full brake application after touchdown.
Grooved runway data does not constitute operational approval.
The airplane operator should coordinate with each Certification and Airport authority in order that appropriate standards are followed.
The performance information is not valid if:
The airplane’s gross weight exceeds the appropriate maximum allowable limits.
Any of the limitations in Section 2 is not observed.
A reading from any graph is obtained by extrapolation (i.e. using values of parameters outside the range given on the graph).
NOTE: In the case of headwind components,
the airplane may be operated in reported components greater than 30 kt, but the effect of only 30 kt may be taken.
PERFORMANCE
fragen.frage_en: How is a reported headwind of more than 30 kt taken into account in AFM performance?
antworten_en: 50 % of the reported headwind is credited
Operation is permitted, but only the effect of 30 kt may be taken into account
Operation is prohibited
The full reported headwind is credited
fragen.erklaerung_en: According to the AFM, operation is permitted with headwind components above 30 kt, but only the effect of 30 kt is credited.

fragen.frage: Welcher minimale Steiggradient ist im Second Segment (Engine Failure nach V1) für ein zweimotoriges Flugzeug gefordert?
fragen.erklaerung: Im Second Segment (Gear up bis Flaps/Slats eingefahren) beträgt der Mindestgradient für Twins 2.4 %. 1.2 % gilt für das Third Segment.
fragen.zitat: The minimum climb gradient that is required during this segment is 2.4% (in case of engine failure after V1) for a twin engine aircraft.
kontext:
4.0.1.5 Climb Segments

First Segment

Is the segment from lift-off up to the point at which the gear is fully retracted. The climb gradient is positive which allows the airplane to reach V2 (35ft for a dry or 15ft for a wet runway) not later than at the end of the take-off distance (TOD).

Second Segment Is the segment from gear retraction to the point where the flaps and slats are retracted.
The minimum climb gradient that is required during this segment is 2.4% (in case of engine failure after V1) for a twin engine aircraft.

Third Segment (Level Off Height) This is the acceleration height, which must be at least 400ft AAE (critical engine inoperative). The program uses 1500ft AAE as the minimum first level off

segment for take-off performance calculations. This segment is used for acceleration to retract the flaps and slats and to accelerate to the optimum climb speed. This segment is assumed to be in level flight, so that excessive thrust can be used for acceleration. The minimum climb gradient is 1.2% and must remain positive.

The segment ends when maximum time allowed for use of take off thrust is reached, which depends on the regulation being used.

OM-B E1 4 Performance

Final Take Off Segment Is the segment from the end of the third segment until the aircraft reaches 1500ft above the take-off surface or more if required for obstacle clearance. This segment will only exist if thrust must be reduced to MCT before the aircraft reaches 1500ft according to regulations.
fragen.frage_en: What minimum climb gradient is required in the Second Segment (engine failure after V1) for a twin-engine aircraft?
fragen.erklaerung_en: In the Second Segment (gear up to flaps/slats retracted) the minimum gradient for twins is 2.4 %. 1.2 % applies to the Third Segment.

fragen.frage: Um welchen Betrag wird die Gross Flight Path Performance für den Net Flight Path eines Twins reduziert?
fragen.erklaerung: Der Net Flight Path ist der um 0.8 % (Twin) degradierte Gross Flight Path; er ist Basis der Hindernisberechnung beim Takeoff. 1.1 % gilt für den Enroute-Driftdown.
fragen.zitat: This is a function of the number of engines (0.8% for a twin engine aircraft).
kontext:
4.0.1.4 Flight Path

Take Off Flight Path It is the path from the end of the Take Off Distance (TOD) to the point where the aircraft passes through the screen height up to 1500ft above the take-off surface to a point where the aircraft configuration turns to the en-route configuration. Two

kinds of take off flight paths have to be taken into consideration, gross and net flight path.
Gross Flight Path

Gross flight path demonstrated performance is the performance the operator can

expect to achieve, when the aircraft is flown to the manufacturers recommended

procedures.

Net Flight Path Net flight path performance represents the gross flight path performance

degraded by a legally specific amount.
This is a function of the number of engines (0.8% for a twin engine aircraft).

Obstacle clearance calculations are

based on the net flight path.

OM-B E1 4 Performance

Screen Height This is the reference height that will be obtained at V2. The screen height value depends on the runway condition: dry: 35 ft

wet or contaminated: 15 ft
fragen.frage_en: By what amount is the Gross Flight Path performance reduced to obtain the Net Flight Path of a twin?
fragen.erklaerung_en: The Net Flight Path is the Gross Flight Path degraded by 0.8 % (twin); it is the basis for obstacle calculation at takeoff. 1.1 % applies to the enroute driftdown.

fragen.frage: Welche Distanz ist für die Takeoff Field Length massgebend?
antworten: Die AEO-Distanz multipliziert mit 1.15
Immer die OEI-Distanz
Die grössere aus OEI-Distanz und 115 % der AEO-Distanz
Die grössere aus OEI-Distanz und 110 % der AEO-Distanz
fragen.erklaerung: Die Takeoff Field Length berücksichtigt die grössere der horizontalen OEI-Distanz oder 115 % der horizontalen AEO-Distanz.
fragen.zitat: The takeoff field length performance considers the greater of the horizontal distance OEI, or 115% of the horizontal distance AEO.
kontext:
NORMAL TAKEOFF TECHNIQUE

The Takeoff performance data calculated by the software when the Normal Takeoff Mode is selected is based on the following takeoff technique:
– Thrust levers set to 60% N1 with the airplane stopped and brakes applied,
– Brakes released after the N1 from both engines are stabilized and equal to 60%, set thrust levers to TO/GA position,
– Green ATTCS indication is presented on the EICAS if it is set to ON on the MCDU,

kontext:

In many situations, the airplane takes off at weights lower than the maximum permissible takeoff weight. kontext:
6.4.1.0 Effect of Center of Gravity on Performance

In terms of takeoff performance calculation, the worst Center of Gravity (CG) position must be taken into account. Therefore, the most forward certified CG position must be considered for takeoff.

The AFM certified CG envelope indicated in chapter 1.1.4 - Mass and Centre of Gravity does not contain curtailments such as seating allowance, inflight

movements and others. In order to keep the CG within the AFM envelope during daily operations, the CG must remain inside the more restrictive "curtailed envelope".

Although curtailments change the envelope limits, the AFM forward limit is always the one taken into account for take-off performance calculation (considered automatically by ePerf for the stabilizer trim setting).
To improve the take-off performance, Embraer certified a different CG envelope called alternate CG. The alternate CG position allows a more aft CG to be used for take-off calculation.
For E190-E1, there is one alternate CG forward limit used for take-off performance: alternate CG (17% MAC)

The envelope used for loadsheet purposes presents a different forward alternate CG position compared to the AFM, since there is a curtailment related to the uncertainty about pax seating (area trim is used).

For performance calculations, the software tool (ePerf) considers either the AFM envelope forward limit or the curtailed envelope forward limit of the alternate CG.
In day by day operation, the flight crew should assure the CG position is as far as possible aft.

Therefore, consider the following to improve the take-off performance:
position the CG at or aft of 21% MAC (curtailed alternate CG)

CG aft of 21% MAC will change the stabilizer trim setting for take-off, thus

reducing the drag and improving the regulated take-off mass.

Background Information:
Regardless of the actual CG, for take-off performance calculations, the worst Center of Gravity (CG) position (most forward position) must be taken into account.
To improve the take-off performance, Embraer certified different CG envelopes called alternate CG’s. The alternate CG position allows a more aft CG to be used for take-off calculation.
The AFM certified CG envelope indicated in the chapter 1.1.4, does not contain curtailments such as seating allowance, inflight movements and others.
Therefore, they can not be used in daily operations.

In order to keep the CG within the AFM envelope during daily operations, the calculated CG must remain inside a more restrictive "curtailed envelope" as per 6.7.3.2.1.5 - Index and MAC Diagram for Manual Loadsheet E190-E2

6.7.3.2.2.5 - Index and MAC Diagram for Manual Loadsheet E195-E2

or according to AHM560 for computerized DCS Loadsheets.

The envelope for manual loadsheet purposes (curtailed envelope) presents

different alternate CG 1 and 2 forward positions compared to the AFM, due to the

curtailment related to the uncertainty about pax seating (area trim is used).
The envelope used for computerized DCS loadsheet purposes presents

alternate CG 1 and 2 forward positions practically identical to the AFM, since the

seat row trim method for passenger seating is considered (more accurate). In other words, the envelope used for computerized loadsheets is bigger. This

envelope can be found in the AHM560.
For performance calculations, the software tool (ePerf) automatically

considers the curtailed envelope forward limits of alternate CG 1 (and 2), depending on CG position.

CG positions aft of alternate CG limits will, from a performance perspective,

change the stabilizer trim setting for take-off, thus reducing the drag and improving the regulated take-off mass.

kontext:
4.0.1.1 Wet and Contaminated

Wet runway means a runway whose surface is covered by any visible dampness

or water up to and including 3 mm deep within the area intended to be used.

Contaminated runway is a runway where a significant portion of its surface area (whether in isolated areas or not) within the length and width being used, is covered by standing water or slush, or that has an accumulation of snow or ice.
However, in certain other situations it may be appropriate to consider the runway contaminated. For example, if the section of the runway surface that is covered with standing water or slush is located where rotation and lift-off occurs, or during the highspeed part of the takeoff roll, the retardation effect is far more significant than if it were encountered early in the takeoff while at low speed. In this situation, the runway might better be considered 'contaminated' rather than 'wet'.

Takeoff and landing performance calculation assumes a homogeneous contaminant type and depth along the entire runway length and width.
If runway conditions are reported for runway thirds, performance calculation should consider the most penalizing contaminant.

However, a part of the runway may be

disregarded if the performance calculation accounts for the respective runway reduction.

fragen.erklaerung_en: The calculation assumes a homogeneous surface condition; for reports per third, the most penalizing condition is to be used.

kontext:
OPERATIONAL LANDING DISTANCE

EMBRAER 195 MODELS Operational Landing Braking Action

NOTE: The operational landing tables
are provided as advisory information and are intended for in-flight assessment, not for dispatch.

The operational landing distance tables contained herein are based on FAA AC 25.32. The data do not include any multiplication factor or additional safety margin.

The distances are obtained from 50 ft above threshold until full airplane stop and consider credit for all thrust reversers.

NOTE: Local operational regulations may require an additional factor to these distances.

In order to make the in-flight assessment if the runway condition is reported, the Runway Condition Assessment Matrix (RCAM) is used. It offers a correlation between runway condition, the pilot report (PIREP) and Runway Condition Code (RWYCC). The maximum recommended crosswinds are also presented in relation to each RWYCC. Gust effects are not included and do not affect the recommended crosswind values. AOM-1502-123

fragen.frage: (E1) Die Brake Temperature Indication ist gemäss MMEL inoperativ und das Landing Weight übersteigt das Quick Turn Around Weight. Wann darf frühestens wieder ein Takeoff erfolgen?

kontext:
QUICK TURN AROUND WEIGHT

For normal operation, the brake temperature can be monitored through the brake temperature indication in the MFD.

The Quick Turn Around Weight Table must be used only when the brake temperature indication is not working properly (according to the MMEL). In this case, if the landing weight exceeds the Quick Turn Around Weight,
a subsequent takeoff must not be performed before 22 minutes after chocks on.

At the end of this time interval, check that the wheel thermal plugs have not melted.

NOTE: If the tires are not flat after 22 minutes, this is a positive indication that the wheel thermal plugs have not melted.
