kontext:
QUICK TURN AROUND WEIGHT

For normal operation, the temperature of the brakes can be monitored through the brake temperature indication in the MFD.

In accordance with the MMEL, the airplane may be dispatched when the brake temperature indication is not working properly. In this situation, if a quick subsequent takeoff is planned after landing, the Quick Turn Around Weight Tables must be used.

According to the tables, if the actual landing weight is equal to or lesser than the quick turn around weight, a subsequent takeoff can be safely performed. Otherwise,
a cooling down period of 32 minutes is required after chocks on.

Additionally, check that the wheel thermal plugs have not melted prior to the subsequent takeoff.

NOTE: If the tires are not flat after 32 minutes, the wheel thermal plugs integrity is preserved.

The tables in the following pages are provided for maximum manual braking and no runway slope.

LANDING TECHNIQUE

The Landing performance data presented by the manuals or calculated by the software are based on the following technique:

– Thrust levers are set to idle before touchdown, and
– Full manual brakes application immediately after main landing gear touchdown(2).

(2) If the use of the thrust reversers was considered in the landing performance calculation, after main landing gear touchdown the thrust levers are set to MAX REV.
At 60 KIAS, the thrust levers are set to idle.

fragen.frage: Wie wird beim Driftdown eines Twins der Net Gradient aus dem Gross Gradient bestimmt?
antworten: Gross Gradient × 0.9
Gross Gradient minus 0.8 %
Gross Gradient minus 1.1 %
Gross Gradient minus 1.6 %
fragen.erklaerung: Für zweimotorige Flugzeuge wird der Gross Gradient um 1.1 % reduziert, um den Net Gradient (Enroute Net Flight Path) zu erhalten.
fragen.zitat: gradient) decreased by 1.1% climb gradient to obtain the net gradient.
kontext:
ENGINE FAILURE

For most normal cruise weights and altitudes, the airplane is not able to maintain its cruise altitude following an engine failure. It begins to descend (drift down) and the pilot sets thrust at the remaining engine to maximum continuous. In order to remain as high as possible, the pilot may follow the optimum driftdown profile, which is based on the optimum driftdown speed. This speed reduces the absolute descent gradient, allowing the airplane to level-off at a higher altitude.

For two-engine airplanes, regulations establish that the driftdown calculations should consider the actual airplane gradient (gross
gradient) decreased by 1.1% climb gradient to obtain the net gradient.

The airplane calculated path following the net gradient is called the enroute net flight path and is used to ensure enroute obstacle clearance (FAR 25.123 CS 25.123).

During a driftdown, the available thrust increases as the airplane descends. Eventually, at a certain altitude, the available thrust becomes equal to the airplane drag, where the airplane can fly at a constant altitude. This altitude is called the gross level off altitude.
When drawing the net path, the altitude where the net gradient is equal to zero is the net level-off. Both the gross and the net level-offs depend on the airplane configuration, actual weight, and atmospheric conditions.

As the net gradient at the net level-off is zero, the actual climb gradient (gross gradient) is 1.1%.

Regulations (FAR 121.191 AIR OPS CAT.POL.A.215) require that the airplane be able to clear all terrain by a given margin when an engine fails. Two means of compliance for enroute obstacle clearance are allowed:
– The net level-off altitude must clear all enroute obstacles by at least 1000 ft; or
– The net flight path must clear all enroute obstacles between the point where the engine is assumed to fail and an airport where a landing can be made by at least 2000 ft.

REVISION 27 Emergency/Abnormal Operation Page 35/86

Gross Gradient minus 1.6 %
fragen.erklaerung_en: For twin-engine aircraft, the Gross Gradient is reduced by 1.1 % to obtain the Net Gradient (Enroute Net Flight Path).

fragen.frage: Wie wird der Point of No Return (PNR) für eine Driftdown-Strecke bestimmt, und was gilt bei einem Engine Failure vor dem PNR?
antworten: PNR = Punkt der höchsten MORA; vor PNR Emergency Descent
Schnittpunkt von Driftdown und Fuel-Kurve; vor PNR immer weiterfliegen
PNR = halbe Strecke; vor PNR weiterfliegen
Schnittpunkt zweier Driftdown-Pfade (weiter zum nächsten ERA bzw. zurück zum vorherigen); vor PNR umkehren
fragen.erklaerung: Minimum Cruise Altitude und PNR ergeben sich aus dem Schnittpunkt der Driftdown-Pfade vorwärts und zurück; bei Ausfall vor dem PNR muss umgekehrt werden.
fragen.zitat: If an engine failure occurs after the PNR, the airplane drifts down on course. If the failure occurs before PNR, the airplane has to turn back.
kontext:
OBSTACLE OBSTACLE

Prior to departure, execute a detailed route analysis using terrain data inside the obstacle accountability area, which is a corridor along the route. Alternatively, use Minimum Enroute Altitude, (MEA), or Minimum Off Route Altitude (MORA). Determine if the net level-off is, at least, 1000 ft above the highest obstacle. If not, or if the associated weight penalties are unacceptable, work on a detailed driftdown procedure, based on an engine failure at the most critical point. The airplane must clear all obstacles during the descent net path by at least 2000 ft.
Determine the minimum cruise altitude and the Point of No Return (PNR) by the intersection of two driftdown paths. The first path is to continue to the next enroute alternate airport (ERA), and the second path is to return to the previous one.
If an engine failure occurs after the PNR, the airplane drifts down on course. If the failure occurs before PNR, the airplane has to turn back.
fragen.frage_en: How is the Point of No Return (PNR) determined for a driftdown route, and what applies in case of engine failure before the PNR?

Intersection of driftdown and fuel curve; before PNR always continue
PNR = halfway point; before PNR continue
Intersection of two driftdown paths (continue to the next ERA or return to the previous one); before PNR turn back
fragen.erklaerung_en: Minimum Cruise Altitude and PNR result from the intersection of the forward and backward driftdown paths; in case of failure before the PNR, the aircraft must turn back.

fragen.frage: Wie wird bei Fuel Tankering der Break-even Fuel Price bestimmt?

fragen.zitat: The break-even fuel price is the price at departure multiplied by the fuel surplus ratio.
kontext:
FLIGHT PLANNING - FUEL TANKERING

Fuel price variations at different airports may require carrying more fuel than the minimum required on a flight leg. The procedure of loading this extra amount of fuel (or surplus fuel) in order to minimize fuel costs is known as Fuel Tankering.

Since the surplus fuel tankered results in additional fuel burnoff (due to the weight increase) it is important to analyze the costs of the extra fuel transportation operation.

The following tables are designed to determine the break-even fuel price on departure airport and it may be used whenever there is difference on fuel price comparing to destination. Tables are provided for LRC and M 0.78 cruise schedule.

Enter the trip distance on the table and read the fuel surplus ratio according to cruise altitude.
The break-even fuel price is the price at departure multiplied by the fuel surplus ratio.

If break-even fuel price is lower than destination price, it is economically feasible to execute fuel tankering.

The additional maintenance costs involved with increased weight operations (additional brakes and tires wearing) are not considered. It is important to remind that whenever fuel tankering is considered, the estimated landing weight at destination should be lower than the Maximum Landing Weight.

Example Analyze the possibility to proceed with fuel tankering between two airports distant 600 NM from each other, using LRC speed schedule cruising on FL350. Consider the following fuel prices:

Departure Airport: 1.80 US$/Gal.

Destination Airport: 2.00 US$/Gal.
– Enter the LONG RANGE CRUISE table for 600 NM trip distance and FL350, the FUEL SURPLUS RATIO is 1.05.

Page 32/34 Simplified Flight Planning REVISION 23

– The BREAK-EVEN PRICE is 1.80 (price at departure) multiplied by 1.05 1.89 US$/Gal.
Since fuel price on destination airport (2.00 US$/Gal) is greater than break-even fuel price (1.89 US$/Gal), it is economically feasible the fuel tankering operation between these two airports.

fragen.erklaerung_en: The break-even price is the departure price multiplied by the Fuel Surplus Ratio; if it is below the destination price, tankering is economical. The landing weight must remain below MLW.

kontext:
6.1.15 Different Loadsheet Envelopes

AFM Envelope This is the center of gravity envelope designed by the aircraft manufacturer during flight testing. The margins are close to the physical/aerodynamical limits

of the aircraft and therefore not usable during daily flight operations. This envelope can be found in the AFM.

DCS Loadsheet Envelope The envelope for DCS loadsheets is tailored to daily operations. Uncertainties of

actual vs. calculated mass and balance values in daily operations require more

restrictive envelope limits (e.g. use of standard passenger masses, inflight movement of passengers, seat row trim). This envelope can be found in the Aircraft Handling Manual (AHM) and is forwarded to contracted handling agencies and is usually not visible to the flight crews.
Manual Loadsheet Envelope
The envelope for a manual (IFS or paper) loadsheets is even more restrictive.

Using section trim (e.g. section A, B, C) leads to more uncertainties within the calculation process and requires a more restrictive envelope.
This envelope includes a designated section reserved for ferry flights. The ferry flight section is applicable if calculating a manual loadsheet for flights with no passengers on board.
Note: Any pantry code acc. to OM-0 9 Pantry Codes may be used for

calculating ferry flight loadsheets.

OM-B E1 6 Mass and Balance

kontext:
6.2.4.0 Procedure:

1. create a manual (paper) loadsheet and complete it until the ZFM/LIZFM section, using the original ZFM. The ZFM/LIZFM may turn out to be outside the envelope limits. (refer to APM 4 forms\Ground Operations\Manual Loadsheet E-Jet)

2. on the CG-envelope, check how much fuel is required to shift the ZFM-CG in the envelope limits, then fill out the Fuel as Ballast section on the manual loadsheet form accordingly. (refer to example on the next page)

3. confirm that the calculated AZFM and ALIZFM are now within the limits of the respective envelope. Thereafter, AZFM and ALIZFM are not needed for any further loadsheet calculations.

4. continue completing the loadsheet with the original values for ZFM and LIZFW and the total fuel (including ballast fuel). (this way prevents errors during the fuel index calculation)

5. confirm that the derived TOM/LITOM are within the envelope limits.

6. contact OCC for a recalculation of the OFP including actual fuel values

1. continue using the (un-corrected) original ZFM on the OFP
2. ballast fuel should be inserted as additional fuel on the OFP

3. if inserted as additional fuel, for enroute OFP fuel checks the ballast fuel will be included as part of the minimum required fuel
Note: Initial ZFM (without ballast fuel) shall be entered in the MCDU, since the total fuel on board is already considered by the system.

fragen.frage: (E1) Im Flug mit Dry Ice fällt ein Bleed bzw. ein Pack aus. Ist deswegen eine Diversion nötig?

kontext:
LOADING AIRPLANE

Avoid storing dry ice on airplanes for extended periods of time. Dry ice should be the last cargo to be loaded and first cargo to be unloaded.

Notify the flight crew whenever the amount of dry ice stowed in the cargo compartment exceeds 440 lb (200 kg), as recommended by the IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations. Flight crew should be aware of the effects of high concentrations of CO2. FAA AC 91-76 may be used as a reference.

In case the flight crew suspects a high concentration of CO2 in the cockpit or cabin, it is recommended to use emergency oxygen supply and land at the nearest suitable airport.

In case of an event of depressurization, flight crew must follow the appropriate QRH procedure. At FL100, the emergency ram air provides sufficient airflow to dilute CO2 concentration.

In case of failure of one bleed or one pack, the QRH procedure remains unchanged. The maximum dry ice loading considers airflow provided by one engine bleed and one air conditioning pack.

The maximum recommended load of dry ice considers that only one bleed and one pack are operative.
Therefore, flight diversion is not necessary solely due to an eventual failure of one bleed or one pack.

fragen.erklaerung_en: The recommended maximum Dry Ice load assumes that only one Bleed and one Pack are operating; such a failure alone does not require a diversion.

kontext:
4.0.1.5 Climb Segments

First Segment

Is the segment from lift-off up to the point at which the gear is fully retracted. The climb gradient is positive which allows the airplane to reach V2 (35ft for a dry or 15ft for a wet runway) not later than at the end of the take-off distance (TOD).

Second Segment Is the segment from gear retraction to the point where the flaps and slats are retracted. The minimum climb gradient that is required during this segment is 2.4% (in case of engine failure after V1) for a twin engine aircraft.

Third Segment (Level Off Height) This is the acceleration height, which must be at least 400ft AAE (critical engine inoperative). The program uses 1500ft AAE as the minimum first level off

segment for take-off performance calculations. This segment is used for acceleration to retract the flaps and slats and to accelerate to the optimum climb speed. This segment is assumed to be in level flight, so that excessive thrust can be used for acceleration.
The minimum climb gradient is 1.2% and must remain

positive.

The segment ends when maximum time allowed for use of take off thrust is reached, which depends on the regulation being used.

OM-B E1 4 Performance

Final Take Off Segment Is the segment from the end of the third segment until the aircraft reaches 1500ft above the take-off surface or more if required for obstacle clearance. This segment will only exist if thrust must be reduced to MCT before the aircraft reaches 1500ft according to regulations.

fragen.erklaerung_en: The Third Segment is assumed to be level flight for acceleration; the minimum gradient is 1.2 % and must remain positive.

The Normal Takeoff Technique is generally used when wind conditions restrict the engines thrust application with ground speed below 20 kt.

The performance data applicable to the Normal Takeoff Technique presented herein is: the Takeoff performance data calculated by the CAFM when the Static Takeoff mode is selected plus the following corrections in the takeoff distance required:

Slope -2% 0% 2% Takeoff Distance 100 m 115 m 150 m Correction[1] (328 ft) (377 ft) (492 ft)

Slope -2% 0% 2% Takeoff Distance 105 m 125 m 170 m Correction[1] (344 ft) (410 ft) (558 ft)

– Thrust levers set to 60% N1 with the airplane stopped and brakes applied,

– At 20 kt of ground speed thrust levers are set to TO/GA position,
– Green ATTCS indication is presented on the EICAS if it is set to ON on the MCDU,
– When VR is attained the airplane is rotated to the flight director pitch angle until 35 ft or until reaching either V2 for OEI or V2 10 KIAS for AEO. If the flight director is inoperative, the airplane is rotated according to the takeoff pitch angle displayed on the TAKEOFF page from the MCDU,

kontext:
QUICK TURN AROUND WEIGHT

For normal operation, the brake temperature can be monitored through the brake temperature indication in the MFD.

The Quick Turn Around Weight Table must be used only when the brake temperature indication is not working properly (according to the MMEL). In this case, if the landing weight exceeds the Quick Turn Around Weight, a subsequent takeoff must not be performed before 22 minutes after chocks on. At the end of this time interval, check that the wheel thermal plugs have not melted.

NOTE:
If the tires are not flat after 22 minutes, this is a positive indication that the wheel thermal plugs have not melted.

fragen.erklaerung_en: If the tires are not flat after 22 minutes, this is a positive sign that the Thermal Plugs have not melted.

OPERATIONAL LANDING DISTANCE

E190-E2, Operational Landing Braking Action

NOTE: The operational landing tables are intended for in-flight assessment only, not for dispatch.

The operational landing distance tables contained herein are based on FAA AC 25.32. The data do not include any multiplication factor or additional safety margin.

The distances are obtained from 50 ft above the threshold until full airplane stop, considering the credit of use of all thrust reversers.

NOTE: Local operational regulations may require the use of additional multiplication factors in these distances. Emergency or
abnormal multiplication factors were not analyzed for contaminated runways.

For Emergency or Abnormal Operations, refer to the Unfactored Landing Distance chapter.

In order to make the in-flight assessment if the runway condition is reported, the Runway Condition Assessment Matrix (RCAM) is used. It offers a correlation between runway condition, the pilot report (PIREP) and Runway Condition Code (RWYCC). The maximum recommended crosswinds are also presented in relation to each RWYCC. kontext:
SIMPLIFIED FLIGHT PLANNING

Simplified flight planning charts allow quick determination of estimated trip fuel and time from brake release to landing. The following phases are included: takeoff, climb, cruise, descent, approach and landing.

REVISION 23 Simplified Flight Planning Page 5/34

Charts are provided for Long Range Cruise (LRC) and Mach 0.78.

Alternate fuel, holding, reserve fuel and other allowances (APU usage and taxi) should be added to the trip fuel in order to obtain the total fuel required.

To determine trip fuel enter trip ground distance, correct for wind condition and estimated landing weight, move as far as the line indicating cruise pressure altitude, and read the trip fuel.

To determine trip time, enter trip ground distance, correct for wind condition, move as far as the referring cruise pressure altitude, and read the trip time.

For winds greater than those shown, enter in the chart, directly, corrected ground distance, ignore wind correction reference line, to obtain the corrected ground distance, apply the following equation.
TAS CGD GD x TAS WIND

Where:
CGD: Corrected ground distance; GD: Ground distance;
Head wind is negative; Tail wind is positive.

The alternate fuel is determined by entering the LRC Simplified Flight Planning chart with the alternate distance and wind.

The holding fuel is determined from the holding table in this section.
Depending upon national regulations, the holding fuel is normally calculated so that the aircraft can hold for 30 min, at 1500 ft above the alternate airport.

fragen.frage: Warum kann bei einem Idle Descent mit konstantem Flight Path Angle (VPATH) nach AOM-Tabellen die amber LIM-Anzeige im FMA erscheinen?
antworten: Weil die in den Tabellen publizierten Speeds nur Referenzwerte zur Sicherstellung von Idle Thrust sind und nicht tatsächlich geflogen werden
Weil VMO/MMO während des Sinkflugs überschritten wird
Weil das FMS die Constraints ignoriert
Weil die Speed Brakes ausgefahren werden müssen
fragen.erklaerung: Die publizierten Speeds werden ins FMS eingegeben, um Idle Descent zu garantieren; sie werden nicht tatsächlich geflogen, daher kann bei engagiertem Autothrottle amber LIM erscheinen.
fragen.quelle: AOM E1 6-20 Idle Descent - Constant Flight Path Angle, Page 11/18
fragen.zitat: Due this fact, the amber LIM on the FMA may be presented during the descent procedure when the autothrottle is engaged.
kontext:
SPEED EXPLANATIONS

The speeds published in the table are the speeds that must be inserted in the FMS in order to guarantee idle descent. They are not the speeds that the airplane will actually fly or reach. They are just a reference to guarantee idle thrust.
Due this fact, the amber LIM on the FMA may be presented during the descent procedure when the autothrottle is engaged.

The actual airplane speed will change according to the altitude. It will vary from the cruise speed to a range from 250 KIAS to 260 KIAS at 12000 ft, never exceeding VMO MMO.

The FMS VPATH mode prioritizes angle over speed, but if there is any waypoint with an altitude or speed constraint, the FMS will ignore the angle and respect this constraint.

antworten_en: Because the speeds published in the tables are only reference values to ensure Idle Thrust and are not actually flown
Because VMO/MMO is exceeded during the descent
Because the FMS ignores the constraints
Because the Speed Brakes must be extended
fragen.erklaerung_en: The published speeds are entered into the FMS to guarantee Idle Descent; they are not actually flown, so amber LIM can appear with the autothrottle engaged.

fragen.frage: Was bewirkt das Fliegen der Optimum Driftdown Speed nach einem Engine Failure?
antworten: Sie maximiert die Sinkrate, um schneller in dichtere Luft zu kommen
Sie minimiert den Fuel Flow
Sie entspricht der Long Range Cruise Speed
Sie reduziert den absoluten Sinkgradienten, sodass das Flugzeug auf einer höheren Altitude abfängt
fragen.erklaerung: Die Optimum Driftdown Speed reduziert den absoluten Sinkgradienten und erlaubt das Level-off auf einer höheren Altitude.
fragen.quelle: AOM E1 6-30 One Engine Inoperative - Driftdown, Page 30/86
fragen.zitat: This speed reduces the absolute descent gradient, allowing the airplane to level-off at a higher altitude.
kontext:
ENGINE FAILURE

For most normal cruise weights and altitudes, the airplane is not able to maintain its cruise altitude following an engine failure. It begins to descend (drift down) and the pilot sets thrust at the remaining engine to maximum continuous. In order to remain as high as possible, the pilot may follow the optimum driftdown profile, which is based on the optimum driftdown speed.
This speed reduces the absolute descent gradient, allowing the airplane to level-off at a higher altitude.

For two-engine airplanes, regulations establish that the driftdown calculations should consider the actual airplane gradient (gross gradient) decreased by 1.1% climb gradient to obtain the net gradient.
The airplane calculated path following the net gradient is called the enroute net flight path and is used to ensure enroute obstacle clearance (FAR 25.123 CS 25.123).

During a driftdown, the available thrust increases as the airplane descends. Eventually, at a certain altitude, the available thrust becomes equal to the airplane drag, where the airplane can fly at a constant altitude. This altitude is called the gross level off altitude.
When drawing the net path, the altitude where the net gradient is equal to zero is the net level-off. Both the gross and the net level-offs depend on the airplane configuration, actual weight, and atmospheric conditions.

As the net gradient at the net level-off is zero, the actual climb gradient (gross gradient) is 1.1%.

Regulations (FAR 121.191 AIR OPS CAT.POL.A.215) require that the airplane be able to clear all terrain by a given margin when an engine fails. Two means of compliance for enroute obstacle clearance are allowed:
– The net level-off altitude must clear all enroute obstacles by at least 1000 ft; or
– The net flight path must clear all enroute obstacles between the point where the engine is assumed to fail and an airport where a landing can be made by at least 2000 ft.

REVISION 27 Emergency/Abnormal Operation Page 35/86
fragen.frage_en: What does flying the Optimum Driftdown Speed after an engine failure achieve?
antworten_en: It maximizes the rate of descent to reach denser air sooner
It minimizes the Fuel Flow
It corresponds to the Long Range Cruise Speed
It reduces the absolute descent gradient so that the aircraft levels off at a higher altitude
fragen.erklaerung_en: The Optimum Driftdown Speed reduces the absolute descent gradient and allows level-off at a higher altitude.

fragen.erklaerung: Beim Net Level-off ist der Net Gradient null; da Net = Gross − 1.1 %, beträgt der Gross Gradient dort 1.1 %.
fragen.quelle: AOM E1 6-30 One Engine Inoperative - Driftdown, Page 30/86

Depending on the local regulations, in the event of depressurization during cruise, the flight plan calculations should consider an additional fuel in case the fuel onboard is not enough to reach an Enroute Alternate (ERA) aerodrome. Emergency Descent from cruise flight level to 10000 ft;

– Descent at the standard AOM descent speed schedule to 1500 ft AGL;

– Approach and landing.
The total time in the Fuel and Time table shows the time in minutes to fly the given air distance at the selected cruise altitude. It considers the emergency descent maneuver, the cruise, the descent, and the approach and landing. The total time does not include the 15-minute holding, which is provided separately and is intended for reference purposes only. The total fuel, however, does include the 15-minute holding fuel.

Evaluation Method: 1 - Enter the ground distance to the Enroute Alternate (ERA) aerodrome and wind in the Air Distance table to obtain the air distance. 2 - In the Fuel and Time table, enter the air distance and cruise pressure altitude to obtain the reference fuel and time at the reference weight. 3 - Then, enter the reference fuel and initial cruise weight at the Fuel Correction table to obtain the critical fuel at ISA conditions. 4 - At last, apply the footer corrections for other ISA deviations.

fragen.frage: (E1) Welche CG-Vorderkante wird für die Takeoff-Performance-Berechnung grundsätzlich herangezogen, obwohl das Loadsheet mit dem curtailed Envelope arbeitet?

fragen.zitat: the AFM forward limit is always the one taken into account for take-off performance calculation
kontext:
6.4.1.0 Effect of Center of Gravity on Performance

In terms of takeoff performance calculation, the worst Center of Gravity (CG) position must be taken into account. Therefore, the most forward certified CG position must be considered for takeoff.

The AFM certified CG envelope indicated in chapter 1.1.4 - Mass and Centre of Gravity does not contain curtailments such as seating allowance, inflight

movements and others. In order to keep the CG within the AFM envelope during daily operations, the CG must remain inside the more restrictive "curtailed envelope".

Although curtailments change the envelope limits,
the AFM forward limit is always the one taken into account for take-off performance calculation

(considered automatically by ePerf for the stabilizer trim setting).
To improve the take-off performance, Embraer certified a different CG envelope called alternate CG. The alternate CG position allows a more aft CG to be used for take-off calculation.
For E190-E1, there is one alternate CG forward limit used for take-off performance: alternate CG (17% MAC)

The envelope used for loadsheet purposes presents a different forward alternate CG position compared to the AFM, since there is a curtailment related to the uncertainty about pax seating (area trim is used).

For performance calculations, the software tool (ePerf) considers either the AFM envelope forward limit or the curtailed envelope forward limit of the alternate CG.
In day by day operation, the flight crew should assure the CG position is as far as possible aft.

Therefore, consider the following to improve the take-off performance:

position the CG at or aft of 21% MAC (curtailed alternate CG)

CG aft of 21% MAC will change the stabilizer trim setting for take-off, thus

reducing the drag and improving the regulated take-off mass.

Always the AFM Forward Limit (automatically considered by ePerf for the Stab Trim)
fragen.erklaerung_en: Even though curtailments change the limits, the AFM Forward Limit is always used for takeoff performance (ePerf accounts for this automatically).

Background Information:
Regardless of the actual CG, for take-off performance calculations, the worst Center of Gravity (CG) position (most forward position) must be taken into account.
To improve the take-off performance, Embraer certified different CG envelopes called alternate CG’s. The alternate CG position allows a more aft CG to be used for take-off calculation.
The AFM certified CG envelope indicated in the chapter 1.1.4, does not contain curtailments such as seating allowance, inflight movements and others.
Therefore, they can not be used in daily operations.

In order to keep the CG within the AFM envelope during daily operations, the calculated CG must remain inside a more restrictive "curtailed envelope" as per 6.7.3.2.1.5 - Index and MAC Diagram for Manual Loadsheet E190-E2

6.7.3.2.2.5 - Index and MAC Diagram for Manual Loadsheet E195-E2

or according to AHM560 for computerized DCS Loadsheets.

The envelope for manual loadsheet purposes (curtailed envelope) presents

different alternate CG 1 and 2 forward positions compared to the AFM, due to the

curtailment related to the uncertainty about pax seating (area trim is used).
The envelope used for computerized DCS loadsheet purposes presents

alternate CG 1 and 2 forward positions practically identical to the AFM, since the

seat row trim method for passenger seating is considered (more accurate). In other words, the envelope used for computerized loadsheets is bigger. This

envelope can be found in the AHM560.
For performance calculations, the software tool (ePerf) automatically

considers the curtailed envelope forward limits of alternate CG 1 (and 2), depending on CG position.

CG positions aft of alternate CG limits will, from a performance perspective,

change the stabilizer trim setting for take-off, thus reducing the drag and improving the regulated take-off mass.

fragen.frage: Wie ist Ballast-Fuel gemäss OM-B-Verfahren auf dem OFP zu berücksichtigen?

Als Contingency Fuel

Als Additional Fuel, mit unveränderter ursprünglicher ZFW auf dem OFP

fragen.zitat: ballast fuel should be inserted as additional fuel on the OFP
kontext:
6.2.4.0 Procedure:

1. create a manual (paper) loadsheet and complete it until the ZFM/LIZFM section, using the original ZFM. The ZFM/LIZFM may turn out to be outside the envelope limits. (refer to APM 4 forms\Ground Operations\Manual Loadsheet E-Jet)

2. on the CG-envelope, check how much fuel is required to shift the ZFM-CG in the envelope limits, then fill out the Fuel as Ballast section on the manual loadsheet form accordingly. (refer to example on the next page)

3. confirm that the calculated AZFM and ALIZFM are now within the limits of the respective envelope. Thereafter, AZFM and ALIZFM are not needed for any further loadsheet calculations.

4. continue completing the loadsheet with the original values for ZFM and LIZFW and the total fuel (including ballast fuel). (this way prevents errors during the fuel index calculation)

5. confirm that the derived TOM/LITOM are within the envelope limits.

6. contact OCC for a recalculation of the OFP including actual fuel values

1. continue using the (un-corrected) original ZFM on the OFP
2.
ballast fuel should be inserted as additional fuel on the OFP

3. if inserted as additional fuel, for enroute OFP fuel checks the ballast fuel will be included as part of the minimum required fuel

Note: Initial ZFM (without ballast fuel) shall be entered in the MCDU, since the total fuel on board is already considered by the system.

Example of procedure:

OM-B E1 6 Mass and Balance
fragen.frage_en: How is ballast fuel to be accounted for on the OFP according to the OM-B procedure?
antworten_en: As part of the ZFW
As Contingency Fuel
Not at all, only on the loadsheet
As Additional Fuel, with the original ZFW unchanged on the OFP
fragen.erklaerung_en: OCC recalculates the OFP: the original ZFW remains, ballast fuel is inserted as Additional Fuel and then counts toward the Minimum Required Fuel in enroute checks.

kontext:
LOADING AIRPLANE

Baggage/Cargo must not become a hazard to the airplane structure or systems as a result of shifting under operational loads. Therefore, sharp edge volumes (like wooden or metal containers) and/or dense cargo (objects significantly more dense than typical passenger baggage) must be arranged with adjacent soft volumes or protections thus preventing airplane damage in case of baggage/cargo shifting due to operational loads.

To ensure proper operation of the smoke detection and fire suppression systems under all operating conditions, a placard, located on the inside sidewall panel of the cargo compartment, clearly visible when the cargo door is opened, is installed in the compartment to restrict cargo from being loaded to within 2.0 in (51 mm) of the cargo compartment ceiling.
Cargo loaded up to the ceiling may cause a baffle effect and prevent dispersion of smoke in the compartment, resulting in delays in detection time.

The proper dispersion of fire suppression agent in the compartment may also be affected if the cargo is installed in such a manner that it blocks the area surrounding the protection cage of the suppression nozzle.

Airplanes equipped with Vertical Cargo Net

Baggage and cargo should be evenly distributed over the cargo compartment to avoid load concentration.

–
Vertical cargo net located at that position must be removed;

kontext:
7.12 Cargo Nets

Cargo door nets prevent cargo doors from being damaged or jammed. They also protect the ground staff from objects falling out of the hold.

Attachments in the forward and aft cargo compartments allow the installation of optional vertical and horizontal cargo nets. The vertical cargo nets prevent the objects shifting and optimizes the loading.
One optional cargo crew-luggage net is installed in the forward cargo compartment to isolate an area for crewmembers luggage.
The forward and aft cargo door nets are standard, except forward door net for live animal transport, which is optional.
The use of cargo door nets is mandatory.

The use of vertical and horizontal cargo nets is not required. If total or partial use of vertical and horizontal nets in the forward or aft cargo compartments, maximum cargo compartment section weights must be observed.
When segregated cargo nets are not used the maximum total cargo compartment weight limit must be observed.
There are placards installed in front of forward and aft cargo door indicating the maximum weight in each cargo compartment section.
Also, each net has a placard informing where it can be installed.

fragen.frage: Was gilt bezüglich Air Conditioning, solange sich Personen an Bord eines Flugzeugs mit Dry Ice befinden?

fragen.zitat: At least one air conditioning pack (or equivalent ground cart ventilation) shall be operating while persons are on board of an airplane transporting dry ice.
kontext:
GENERAL RECOMMENDATIONS

It is not recommended to transport dry ice in the cabin and in the galleys. If small quantities are present in the galley, it is required to compute this dry ice mass in the calculation of the total dry ice.
Airplanes equipped with FWD cargo compartment ventilation system

Prior to enter into the forward cargo compartment, in which a large amount of dry ice has been loaded, ensure that adequate ventilation is provided checking that the cargo ventilation system is running properly.

Live animals must not be transported on a forward cargo compartment loaded with dry ice.

In case of failure of the cargo ventilation system during flight, the CO2 sublimated in the cargo compartment is trapped. The airplane can continue the flight normally, but after landing it is required to ventilate the compartment in which CO2 buildup is suspected.

NOTE: If the cargo compartment used for dry ice transportation is not equipped with a ventilation system, make sure CO2 levels are within acceptable limits before entering the cargo compartment. When cargo door is opened, the area immediately outside the door may also experience a high CO2 concentration. It is recommended to wear oxygen mask and portable oxygen cylinder inside these areas if adequate ventilation is not provided.
At least one air conditioning pack (or equivalent ground cart ventilation) shall be operating while persons are on board of an airplane transporting dry ice.

fragen.frage: Was empfiehlt das Handbuch, wenn die Flight Crew eine hohe CO2-Konzentration im Cockpit oder in der Kabine vermutet?
antworten: Packs auf HIGH und Flug normal fortsetzen
Emergency Oxygen verwenden und am nächsten geeigneten Flugplatz landen
Auf FL100 sinken und weiterfliegen
Cargo Ventilation ausschalten
fragen.erklaerung: Bei Verdacht auf hohe CO2-Konzentration: Emergency Oxygen Supply verwenden und am nächsten geeigneten Flugplatz landen.
fragen.zitat: it is recommended to use emergency oxygen supply and land at the nearest suitable airport.
kontext:
LOADING AIRPLANE

Avoid storing dry ice on airplanes for extended periods of time. Dry ice should be the last cargo to be loaded and first cargo to be unloaded.

Notify the flight crew whenever the amount of dry ice stowed in the cargo compartment exceeds 440 lb (200 kg), as recommended by the IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations. Flight crew should be aware of the effects of high concentrations of CO2. FAA AC 91-76 may be used as a reference.

In case the flight crew suspects a high concentration of CO2 in the cockpit or cabin,
it is recommended to use emergency oxygen supply and land at the nearest suitable airport.

In case of an event of depressurization, flight crew must follow the appropriate QRH procedure. At FL100, the emergency ram air provides sufficient airflow to dilute CO2 concentration.

In case of failure of one bleed or one pack, the QRH procedure remains unchanged. The maximum dry ice loading considers airflow provided by one engine bleed and one air conditioning pack.

The maximum recommended load of dry ice considers that only one bleed and one pack are operative. Therefore, flight diversion is not necessary solely due to an eventual failure of one bleed or one pack.
fragen.frage_en: What does the manual recommend if the Flight Crew suspects a high CO2 concentration in the Cockpit or cabin?
antworten_en: Packs to HIGH and continue the flight normally
Use Emergency Oxygen and land at the nearest suitable aerodrome
Descend to FL100 and continue
Switch off Cargo Ventilation
fragen.erklaerung_en: If a high CO2 concentration is suspected: use Emergency Oxygen Supply and land at the nearest suitable aerodrome.

kontext:
7.13.2.3 Cargo Temperature Estimation

As an alternative to the simplified method of Table 2, the following tables may be used to verify if the planned flight is suitable for live animals transportation.
During flight, the temperature inside the cargo compartment varies with external conditions, such as SAT, cruise altitude, and Mach. The OAT has a significant influence due to the time the cargo door remains open during the turnaround.
Once the door is closed, the cargo ventilation system starts to warm or cool the cargo compartment.
The following tables may be used to estimate the effective temperature sensed by the animals at the end of the cruise, when the temperature tends to be the lowest. The data provided in the tables consider that the temperature sensed by the animals is increased due to the containers that are used in the transportation.
Therefore, the temperature stated in the tables already have an increment of 4°C considering an IATA standard container. The estimations consider a constant SAT during cruise.
To estimate the effective temperature for parameters in between the ones presented in the tables, use linear interpolation.
The temperature experienced by the animals during cruise should be within an acceptable range.
For cats and dogs, for example, according to SAE AIR1600, the acceptable temperature ranges from 10°C to 27°C.

For example, the transportation of a short hair dog in a flight with the following parameters:

– OAT on the ground is 0°C,
– Cruise time is 3 h,
– Mach 0.6, and
– Cruise FL is 410.

Then the effective temperature sensed by the animal at the end of the cruise is

7°C. This effective temperature is not sufficient since the minimum acceptable

temperature for short hair dogs is 10°C, so cruise Mach should be increased or cruise FL should be reduced.

OM-B E2 7 Loading

OM-B E2 7 Loading

Freigabe des Flugzeugs nach Wartungsarbeiten (Certificate of Release)
Flight Initiation sowie Continuation, Termination oder Diversion eines Flugs
Erstellung von Loadsheet und NOTOC durch den Handling Agent

fragen.zitat: The Commander (CMD) has the final responsibility regarding flight initiation according to 8.1.10 - Operational Flight Plan continuation, termination or diversion of a flight
kontext:
1.4.1 Authority, Duties and Responsibilities of the Commander (CMD)

The Commander (CMD) exercises the final authority over the safe operation of the helvetic aircraft he is assigned to fly.
He is responsible, as soon as he arrives on board until he leaves the airplane at the end of the flight, for: the safety of all crew members, passengers and cargo

He is responsible to adapt the operationally applicable elements of the SSCC defined in OMM 1.1 to the given situation and implement them in a mission- focussed manner.
He is responsible, from the moment the airplane is first ready to move for the purpose of taxiing prior to take-off until the moment it finally comes to rest at the end of the flight and the engines used as primary propulsion units are shut down, for: the operation and safety of the airplane

All persons on board the aircraft shall obey all lawful directions given by the Commander (CMD). The Commander (CMD) exercises command over all crew members:

from check-in until check-out for a flight or series of flights

The Commander (CMD) has the final responsibility regarding

flight initiation according to 8.1.10 - Operational Flight Plan

continuation, termination or diversion of a flight

according to 8.3.2.24 -

Meteorological Information.

OM-A Responsibilities

He exercises full command over all other persons on board of a helvetic aircraft: from the time the doors are closed for the initiation of a flight until the doors are opened after the completion of a flight

While exercising his authority the Commander (CMD) has the right to: give all commands he deems necessary for the purpose of ensuring the safety of the aircraft and of persons or property carried therein

to disembark any person or any part of the cargo, which, in his opinion, may represent a potential hazard to the safety of the aircraft or its occupants

not allow a person to be carried in the aircraft who appears to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs to the extent that the safety of the aircraft or its occupants is likely to be endangered

to refuse transportation of inadmissible passengers, deportees or persons in custody, if their carriage poses any risk to the safety of the aircraft or its occupants

OM-A Responsibilities

The Commander (CMD) must: ensure that all passengers are briefed on the location of emergency exits and the location and use of relevant safety and emergency equipment

ensure that all operational procedures and checklists are complied with in accordance with the provisions of this Operations Manual (OM)

ensure that all crew members occupy their stations prior to take-off, final approach and landing
fragen.frage_en: What does the Commander (CMD) bear final responsibility for according to OM-A 1.4.1?
antworten_en: Preparing the Operational Flight Plan and canceling the ATC flight plan
Releasing the aircraft after maintenance (Certificate of Release)
Flight Initiation as well as Continuation, Termination or Diversion of a flight
Preparing the Loadsheet and NOTOC by the Handling Agent
fragen.erklaerung_en: According to OM-A 1.4.1, the CMD has final responsibility for Flight Initiation (8.1.10) as well as for Continuation, Termination or Diversion of a flight.

kontext:
4.2 Designation of the Commander

For each flight helvetic designates one pilot to act as the Commander (CMD).
The designation is marked in the flight assignment.
The Commander (CMD) must occupy a seat in the flight deck with unrestricted access to the controls throughout the entire flight.

The actual handling of the aircraft and conduct of the flight may be delegated by the Commander (CMD) to any other suitably qualified flight crew member while the Commander (CMD) holds the overall responsibility for the safety of the aircraft, its crew, passengers and cargo. helvetic nominates a flight crew member as Commander (CMD) if he meets all relevant requirements of 5 - Qualification Requirements.
The position of a Commander (CMD) may be held by a pilot irrespective of the pilot’s seat he occupies at the flight deck (e.g. Line Training Commander – LTC at the right hand seat during line introduction).
fragen.frage_en: What requirement regarding his seat must the designated Commander (CMD) fulfil throughout the flight according to OM-A 4.2?
antworten_en: He must occupy the left pilot seat throughout the flight
As LTC he may also exercise command from the Jump Seat
He must act as Pilot Flying (PF) throughout the flight
He must occupy a seat in the Flight Deck with unrestricted access to the Controls
fragen.erklaerung_en: The CMD must occupy a seat in the Flight Deck with unrestricted access to the Controls throughout the flight; he may delegate the flying itself, and the seat (left/right) is not prescribed.

4.1.7 Augmented Crew Composition

An augmented flight crew consists of at least: two Commanders (CMD)

one Copilot (COP), or a third Commander (CMD)

all of whom must be qualified on the type and variant to be flown.
At least one pilot must be qualified to operate in either pilot’s seat.
One commander is assigned by helvetic Flightops department and stated on the flight assignment as commander.
The assigned commander will: act acc. to 1.4.1 - Authority, Duties and Responsibilities of the Commander (CMD) during the whole flight or series of flights

distribute the workload and organise time periods “off tasks” between the flight crew members

Augmented crew compositions do not affect maximum FDP limitations as stated in 7.1.7.4 - Maximum Daily FDP with the use of Extensions due to In-flight Rest.

An augmented cabin crew consists of at least:

the minimum cabin crew complement

an additional Cabin Attendant (CAB)

all of whom must be qualified on the type and variant.

The workload shall be distributed as evenly as possible between the cabin crew

members. The workload distribution is organised by the assigned Senior Cabin Attendant.

kontext:
5.2.9 Low Visibility Operation (LVO)

To maintain a category II III (CAT II III) qualification pilots must have conducted a minimum of three approaches and landings using CAT II III procedures during the period between 2 EBT modules (real or simulated CAT II III approaches).
If a flight crew member is authorised to operate as pilot flying and pilot monitoring, the flight crew member shall complete the required number of approaches in each operating capacity.
If above mentioned requirements are not met a re-qualification has to be performed. For that purpose the approaches may be conducted during normal line operation as simulated CAT II III approaches.
However, recency for low visibility take-off and Cat II/III approaches is maintained by the recurrent training and checking.
If the commander was not previously qualified for Cat II III operations with an EASA operator,

the following minima apply until 100 hours or 40 route sectors (including line flying under supervision) have been achieved on type:
Cat II/III minimum RVR 100 m

Upgraders moving from the right onto the left seat (not being new on type) are not affected by this limitation. helvetic does not define a further increase of minima depending on the experience of flight crew members.

kontext:
5.2.16 Zero Flight Time Training (ZFTT)

The flight training necessary after a type rating training can be substituted by a Zero Flight Time Training (ZFTT). The Zero Flight Time Training is a part of a type rating course. It replaces the mandatory flight training on an aeroplane with an additional training in a Full Flight Simulator (FFS) for pilots fulfilling the requirements specified in OM-D 2.1.11.19. The specific ZFTT session is described in the type rating syllabus and contains take-off and landing training under various conditions.
Line flying as ZFTT shall start latest 21 days after successful completion of the skill test.

kontext:
6.1.2 Immunization

In accordance with the World Health Organization’s (WHO) International Health Regulations many countries prescribe vaccination of crew members and passengers against defined diseases, often specifying that such immunization is only required upon entry “after leaving or transiting infected areas”.
Each crew member scheduled for flight duty abroad must satisfy any requirement for vaccination, to have himself vaccinated in time, and to be able to produce – during his tour of duty – the appropriate WHO-approved “Certificate of Vaccination or Revaccination”.
Vaccination and Revaccination shall take place not less than 24 hours before commencement of flight duty, unless otherwise stated. In case of strong reaction medical advice shall be obtained in view of a possible impairment of fitness for flight duty. No alcoholic beverages shall be consumed for a period of at least 24 hours after vaccination.

Vaccinations which may be obligatory and their validity:
Yellow fever (from 10 days after, for lifetime)

Vaccinations which are recommended and their validity:
Cholera (from 7 days until 6 months after vaccination)

Typhoid (from 7 days until 3 years after vaccination)

Poliomyelitis (after 3 vaccinations up to 10 years) Tetanus (after 3 vaccinations up to 10 years)

COVID-19(1) (from 1 to 2 weeks after the vaccination)

Note 1:
Crew members must not be engaged in any safety relevant duty (e.g. flight duty) for a period of 48 hours after each dose of

COVID-

19 vaccine. In case side effects persist for more than 48 hours following the vaccination, crew members shall consult their AME.

The waiting period shall be extended until the time when the side

effects completely disappear.

OM-A 6 Health Precautions

Malaria prophylaxis, though not immunization in the strict sense of the word, should be mentioned here; crew members scheduled for flight duty to malaria infected countries shall obtain, on the advice of their flight medical doctor, the appropriate medication and apply it as prescribed.
Note: Crew members shall be aware of the fact that there are many extremely dangerous diseases against which vaccination is not possible.

Only general rules may be given here for health-conscious behavior in foreign countries: observe strict hygiene in eating drinking (amoebic dysentery, brucellosis),

do not bathe in stagnant water (bilharziasis),

in infested (e.g., bush/jungle) areas, wear long sleeved shirts and long trousers to prevent or minimize bites by disease-carrying insects (filariasis, malaria, encephalitis, sleeping sickness) or by outright poisonous insects or animals (spiders, scorpions, snakes); use insect-repellant.

OM-A 6 Health Precautions

fragen.frage: Ab wann und wie lange ist die Gelbfieberimpfung (Yellow fever) gemäss OM-A 6.1.2 gültig?

Sofort nach der Impfung, für 3 Jahre

fragen.zitat: Vaccinations which may be obligatory and their validity: Yellow fever (from 10 days after, for lifetime)
kontext:
6.1.2 Immunization

In accordance with the World Health Organization’s (WHO) International Health Regulations many countries prescribe vaccination of crew members and passengers against defined diseases, often specifying that such immunization is only required upon entry “after leaving or transiting infected areas”.
Each crew member scheduled for flight duty abroad must satisfy any requirement for vaccination, to have himself vaccinated in time, and to be able to produce – during his tour of duty – the appropriate WHO-approved “Certificate of Vaccination or Revaccination”.
Vaccination and Revaccination shall take place not less than 24 hours before commencement of flight duty, unless otherwise stated. In case of strong reaction medical advice shall be obtained in view of a possible impairment of fitness for flight duty. No alcoholic beverages shall be consumed for a period of at least 24 hours after vaccination.

Vaccinations which may be obligatory and their validity:
Yellow fever (from 10 days after, for lifetime)

Vaccinations which are recommended and their validity:
Cholera (from 7 days until 6 months after vaccination)

Typhoid (from 7 days until 3 years after vaccination)

Poliomyelitis (after 3 vaccinations up to 10 years) Tetanus (after 3 vaccinations up to 10 years)

COVID-19(1) (from 1 to 2 weeks after the vaccination)

Note 1: Crew members must not be engaged in any safety relevant duty (e.g. flight duty) for a period of 48 hours after each dose of COVID-

19 vaccine. In case side effects persist for more than 48 hours following the vaccination, crew members shall consult their AME.

The waiting period shall be extended until the time when the side

effects completely disappear.

OM-A 6 Health Precautions

Malaria prophylaxis, though not immunization in the strict sense of the word, should be mentioned here; crew members scheduled for flight duty to malaria infected countries shall obtain, on the advice of their flight medical doctor, the appropriate medication and apply it as prescribed.
Note: Crew members shall be aware of the fact that there are many extremely dangerous diseases against which vaccination is not possible.

Only general rules may be given here for health-conscious behavior in foreign countries: observe strict hygiene in eating drinking (amoebic dysentery, brucellosis),

do not bathe in stagnant water (bilharziasis),

in infested (e.g., bush/jungle) areas, wear long sleeved shirts and long trousers to prevent or minimize bites by disease-carrying insects (filariasis, malaria, encephalitis, sleeping sickness) or by outright poisonous insects or animals (spiders, scorpions, snakes); use insect-repellant.

OM-A 6 Health Precautions
fragen.frage_en: From when and for how long is the yellow fever vaccination valid according to OM-A 6.1.2?
antworten_en: From 7 days after vaccination, for 10 years
From 7 days after vaccination, for 6 months
From 10 days after vaccination, lifelong
Immediately after vaccination, for 3 years
fragen.erklaerung_en: The (possibly mandatory) yellow fever vaccination is valid lifelong from 10 days after vaccination.

fragen.frage: Wen muss ein Flight oder Cabin Crew Member gemäss OM-A über eine Schwangerschaft zum frühestmöglichen Zeitpunkt informieren?
antworten: Nur den Crew Manager (CMR) und das HR
Den FOP und den Aero-Medical Doctor
Den Piquet Officer (PQO) und die Crew Control
Nur den Commander des nächsten Flugs
fragen.erklaerung: Die Schwangerschaft ist zum frühestmöglichen Zeitpunkt dem Nominated Person Flight Operations (FOP) und dem Aero-Medical Doctor zu melden.
fragen.zitat: Every flight or cabin crew member shall inform the Nominated Person Flight Operations (FOP) and the aero-medical doctor about her pregnancy at the earliest practicable time.
kontext: 6.1.10 Pregnancy
Every flight or cabin crew member shall inform the Nominated Person Flight Operations (FOP) and the aero-medical doctor about her pregnancy at the earliest practicable time.
Flight duty may be sustained after the recognition of the pregnancy based on the regulations of the Swiss Radiation Protection Act (Strahlenschutzverordnung)

The FOP and the Aero-Medical Doctor
The Piquet Officer (PQO) and Crew Control
Only the Commander of the next flight

fragen.frage: Was gilt gemäss OM-A 6.1.6 (Meal Precautions) für die Mahlzeiten der beiden Piloten?

Verschiedene Mahlzeiten nur im Flug, im Hotel ist es frei

Gleiche Mahlzeit erlaubt, wenn sie vom Caterer versiegelt ist

fragen.zitat: As a precaution against operational consequences of food poisoning, pilots shall have different meals not only in flight but also at hotels before reporting for duty.
kontext:
6.1.6 Meal Precautions

In the interest of safety flight crew members shall not eat exactly the same. (e.g. both flight crew members enjoy the same ham-sandwich).
As a precaution against operational consequences of food poisoning, pilots shall have different meals not only in flight but also at hotels before reporting for duty.

Different meals in flight only, in the hotel it is free
Same meal permitted if eaten at different times
Same meal permitted if sealed by the caterer
fragen.erklaerung_en: As a precaution against food poisoning, pilots shall eat different meals not only in flight but also in the hotel before reporting.

fragen.frage: Ein Arzt erachtet bei einem Mitarbeitenden die Einnahme eines Narcotics/Drugs als absolut notwendig. Wer muss gemäss OM-A vor weiteren Operations Duties über diesen Status informiert werden?
antworten: Der Nominated Person Training (TNG)
Der Safety Manager (SM)
Der Piquet Officer (PQO)
Der Accountable Manager (ACM)

fragen.zitat: The Accountable Manager (ACM) must be informed by the employee about this special status before further commencing any operations duty.
kontext:
6.2.4 Narcotics, Pharmaceutical Drugs

For crew members and operations personnel other than crew members, the

consumption of narcotics and drugs (except alcohol, tobacco and caffeine) is

strictly prohibited unless a medical doctor has determined, that such

consumption or use is absolutely necessary in the interest of his patient’s health.
However, in such extremely rare cases, the helvetic employee concerned shall

commence operations duty only if the appointed helvetic flight-medical doctor has certified that the physical and mental fitness for such duty is not being

impaired.

The Accountable Manager (ACM) must be informed by the employee

about this special status before further commencing any operations duty.
fragen.frage_en: A physician considers the intake of a narcotic/drug absolutely necessary for an employee. Who must be informed of this status before further Operations Duties according to OM-A?
antworten_en: The Nominated Person Training (TNG)
The Safety Manager (SM)
The Piquet Officer (PQO)
The Accountable Manager (ACM)
fragen.erklaerung_en: In addition to the certificate of the helvetic Flight-Medical Doctor, the employee must inform the Accountable Manager (ACM) before further Operations Duties.

fragen.frage: Was muss ein Crew Member nach einem chirurgischen Eingriff vor der Rückkehr in den Flugdienst vorlegen?

Ein neues Medical Class 1 nach vollständiger Erstuntersuchung
Ein von einem Aero-Medical Doctor unterschriebenes Fitness Certificate
Eine Selbstdeklaration im SMS Tool (Unfit to fly beendet)
fragen.erklaerung: Nach jedem chirurgischen Eingriff ist vor der Rückkehr in den Flugdienst ein von einem Aero-Medical Doctor unterschriebenes Fitness Certificate vorzulegen.
fragen.zitat: A fitness certificate signed by an aero-medical doctor shall be produced prior to returning to flying duties after any surgical procedure.
kontext:
6.1.9 Surgical Operation

In case of a surgical operation, the crew member needs to inform his superior directly and shall be removed from flight duty after the operation.
A fitness certificate signed by an aero-medical doctor shall be produced prior to returning to flying duties after any surgical procedure.
fragen.frage_en: What must a Crew Member present after a surgical procedure before returning to flight duty?
antworten_en: A confirmation of fitness for work from the treating general practitioner
A new Medical Class 1 after a complete initial examination
A Fitness Certificate signed by an Aero-Medical Doctor
A self-declaration in the SMS Tool (Unfit to fly ended)
fragen.erklaerung_en: After any surgical procedure, a Fitness Certificate signed by an Aero-Medical Doctor must be presented before returning to flight duty.

fragen.frage: Wie viele Duty Hours darf ein Crew Member gemäss OM-A in 14 aufeinanderfolgenden Tagen maximal leisten?
fragen.erklaerung: Die Duty-Hour-Limiten betragen 190 h in 28, 110 h in 14 und 60 h in 7 aufeinanderfolgenden Tagen.
fragen.zitat: 190 duty hours in any 28 consecutive days, spread as evenly as practicable throughout this period 110 duty hours in any 14 consecutive days
kontext:
7.1.6.1 Duty Hour Limitations

Any work, the entire duration of a flight, deadhead time (positioning), training and office duties, which a crew member performs on behalf of helvetic shall count as duty period.
Any duty by a crew member according to 7.1.14.2 - Recording of Duty, Flight Duty and Rest Periods by the Crew Member counts as duty time. helvetic shall ensure that the total duty period to which a crew member is assigned does not exceed:

190 duty hours in any 28 consecutive days, spread as evenly as practicable throughout this period

110 duty hours in any 14 consecutive days

60 duty hours in any 7 consecutive days

After the last flight during a Flight Duty Period (FDP), helvetic plans all crew members 30 minutes for post flight work counting as duty time only (post flight work before a break counts as Flight Duty Period (FDP) – refer to split duty rules).
Private duty shall count towards duty time limitations and must be reported according to 7.1.14.2 - Recording of Duty, Flight Duty and Rest Periods by

the Crew Member.
fragen.frage_en: How many Duty Hours may a Crew Member perform at most in 14 consecutive days according to OM-A?
fragen.erklaerung_en: The Duty Hour limits are 190 h in 28, 110 h in 14 and 60 h in 7 consecutive days.

fragen.frage: Die Cabin Crew benötigt mehr Zeit für das Pre-flight Briefing und meldet sich früher als die Flight Crew (staggered reporting time). Was gilt?
antworten: FDP-Verlängerung um die Differenz, max. 2 Stunden; max. FDP ab Reporting der Cabin Crew
Keine Verlängerung; die FDP der Cabin Crew beginnt erst mit Reporting der Flight Crew
FDP-Verlängerung um die Differenz, max. 1 Stunde; max. FDP ab Reporting der Flight Crew
FDP-Verlängerung um die Differenz, max. 30 Minuten; max. FDP ab Reporting der Cabin Crew
fragen.erklaerung: Die FDP der Cabin Crew darf um die Reporting-Differenz (max. 1 Stunde) verlängert werden; die max. FDP richtet sich nach dem Reporting der Flight Crew, die FDP beginnt aber beim Reporting der Cabin Crew.
fragen.zitat: The difference shall not exceed 1 hour. The maximum daily FDP for cabin crew shall be based on the time at which the flight crew report for their FDP, but the FDP shall start at the reporting time of the cabin crew.
kontext:
7.1.8 Extension of Flight Duty Period for Cabin Crew

(staggered reporting time)

Whenever cabin crew requires more time than the flight crew for their pre-flight briefing for the same sector or series of sectors, the FDP of the cabin crew may

be extended by the difference in reporting time between the cabin crew and the

flight crew.

The difference shall not exceed 1 hour. The maximum daily FDP for cabin crew shall be based on the time at which the flight crew report for their

FDP, but the FDP shall start at the reporting time of the cabin crew.
fragen.frage_en: The Cabin Crew needs more time for the Pre-flight Briefing and reports earlier than the Flight Crew (staggered reporting time). What applies?
antworten_en: FDP extension by the difference, max. 2 hours; max. FDP from Cabin Crew reporting
No extension; the Cabin Crew FDP begins only with Flight Crew reporting
FDP extension by the difference, max. 1 hour; max. FDP from Flight Crew reporting
FDP extension by the difference, max. 30 minutes; max. FDP from Cabin Crew reporting
fragen.erklaerung_en: The Cabin Crew FDP may be extended by the reporting difference (max. 1 hour); the max. FDP is based on Flight Crew reporting, but the FDP begins at Cabin Crew reporting.

fragen.zitat: If a flight crew member is called for duty out of a standby, he shall be ready for flight duty at the check-in location within certain minutes after termination of the call. all types of standby: 75 minutes
kontext:
7.1.10.4 Explanation of the used Abbreviations on the Crew Schedule

helvetic defines 4 different types of standby:
S5 05:00 - 14:00 local time

S10 10:00 - 19:00 local time

S15 15:00 - 24:00 local time

variable (maximum duration 16 hours)

All these standby can be planned irrespective of the previous duty. However, the minimum rest time has to be observed. That means that standby duty starts at the end of the minimum rest time. helvetic may extend the respective standbys by up to 4 hours (maximum duration of 16 hours) if needed. Such re-plannings should be applied in extra ordinary situations only as they might result in changes of the subsequent duties and impair the social live of employees.
Crew members shall be reachable during the whole standby period.

If a flight crew member is called for duty out of a standby, he shall be ready for flight duty at the check-in location within certain minutes after termination of the call. all types of standby: 75 minutes

If a crew member needs to be available for a short term assignment of additional flights after a rotation which allows doing so (e.g. two leg morning rotation), the following duty will be used in the crew schedule:
Available for Continuation

Crew member shall be available for a continuation within the maximum FDP

(additional flight duty) until 30 minutes after block on of the last flight.

During extraordinary and limited time periods where the economical situation

does not allow a full degree of employment, helvetic can assign the following status to a crewmember:

Kurzarbeit

With “Kurzarbeit” indicated in the duty roster, the crewmember must be

reachable during regular office hours (i.e. 0800LT until 1700LT). Reachability in this context means checking and if required confirming any change in the Winops. Duty assignments will be indicated by a message from OCC. The

crewmember is not expected to be reachable by phone. However, he must confirm assignments until 1700LT the day of issuing a duty change. The

crewmember must be ready to commence duty 24 hours after assignment.

For all other abbreviations refer to OCM Chapter 10 Crew Control

OM-A 7 Flight Time Limitations

Als FDP und als Sektor, wie ein operierender Flug

kontext:
7.1.11 Positioning

positioning is planned and listed in the crew plan of the crew member concerned

the crew member shall individually position without calling Crew Control Department (CCO)

a positioning sector immediately following an operating sector will be taken into account for the calculation of the minimum subsequent rest time

If a private positioning is planned, CCO shall be informed in advance.
When positioning by train, Winops shows a positioning schedule with a defined time period. By taking the first train within the beginning of this time period an on- time check-in at airport is assured.
When positioning by plane, the duty starts 30 minutes before scheduled Time of Departure (STD). The crew member shall report for duty at the time given in Winops, which is the time the positioning starts.
Nevertheless, it is the crew member’s responsibility to verify the correctness of

the times by checking the STD of the flight planned for the positioning.
The STD can be found in the flight overview in Winops.
The positioning ends with the arrival of the aircraft at the stand.

Type of Positioning Reporting Time Meeting Point

kontext: 7.1.12.6 Minimum Rest Period after Military Service
After military service of at least 5 days, a crew member shall be given at least 18 hours of rest period starting at 24:00 local time on the day of demobilization.

7.1.12.7 Extended Minimum Rest in the Case of a Change of the Home Base

In the case of a change of home base, the first recurrent extended recovery rest

period prior to starting duty at the new home base is increased to 72 hours, including 3 local nights. Travelling time between the former home base and the new home base is positioning.

7.1.12.6 Minimum Rest Period after Military Service

In the case of a change of home base,

fragen.frage: In welcher Situation muss Commander's Discretion gemäss OM-A 7.2.1 vermieden werden?
antworten: Auf dem letzten Sektor einer FDP nach dem Take-off

kontext:
7.2.1 Modification of the Limits on Flight Duty, Duty or Rest Periods

During actual flight operation, which starts after the whole crew has reported for any duty, the Commander (CMD) shall have the possibility to modify the limits on flight duty, duty and rest periods in the event of conditions described as unforeseen circumstances.
The exercise of commander’s discretion shall be considered exceptional and shall be avoided at home base when standby or reserve crew members are available.

The conditions shall comply with the following: the maximum daily FDP which results after applying 7.1.7 - Maximum Daily Flight Duty Periode (FDP) or 7.1.9 - Split Duty may not be increased by more than 2 hours.

the maximum basic daily FDP that results after applying 7.1.7.1 - Maximum Daily FDP for Acclimatised Crew Members shall be used to calculate the limits of commander’s discretion, if commander’s discretion is applied to an FDP which has been extended under the provisions of 7.1.7.3 - Maximum Daily FDP for Acclimatised Crew Members with the Use of Extensions without In-flight Rest

if on the final sector within a FDP the allowed increase is exceeded because of unforeseen circumstances after take-off, the flight may continue to the planned destination or alternate aerodrome the rest period following the FDP may be reduced but can never be less

than 10 hours

The commander shall consult all crew members on their alertness levels before deciding the modifications.
Additionally, he shall take due consideration of additional factors that might decrease a crew member’s alertness levels, such as:
WOCL encroachment

weather conditions

complexity of the operation and/or airport environment

airplane malfunctions or specifications

flight with training or supervisory duties

increased number of sectors

circadian disruption

individual conditions of affected crew members (time since awake, sleep- related factor, workload, etc.)

7.2.2 Duties in case of Modification of the Limits on Flight Duty, Duty or Rest Periods

helvetic will assess on a regular basis the series of pairings where commander’s

discretion has been exercised in order to be aware of possible inconsistencies in their rostering. The FRMS meeting monitors the amount of FTL modifications and other FTL exceedances via the BI tool according to 2.4.5.1.8 - FRMS Meeting.

The Commander (CMD) shall submit an IT report to helvetic flight operations

management whenever a limit on flight duty, duty or rest period has been

modified by his discretion or whenever a limitation as stated within this chapter has been violated in excess of one hour. This report shall be handled according

to OMM 7 Reporting Scheme.

Whenever the above-mentioned modification or a reported violation is beyond one hour, helvetic shall send a copy of the report to the competent authority not

later than 28 days after the event.

The RPO will monitor FTL exceedances and request reports from the commander, whenever a report is missing.
fragen.frage_en: In which situation shall Commander's Discretion be avoided according to OM-A 7.2.1?
antworten_en: On the last sector of an FDP after takeoff
Away from Home Base if a hotel is available
At Home Base if Standby or Reserve Crew Members are available
On any FDP already planned using Extension
fragen.erklaerung_en: Commander's Discretion is an exception and shall be avoided at Home Base if Standby or Reserve Crew Members are available.

kontext:
9.4.6.1 Portable Electronic Devices (PED) Containing Batteries

These Portable Electronic Devices (PED), which may include medical devices such as Portable Oxygen Concentrators (POC) and consumer electronics such as cameras, mobile phones, laptops and tablets containing batteries when carried by passengers or crew for personal use, should be carried in carry-on baggage.
These provisions apply to dry batteries, nickel-metal hydride batteries, lithium batteries and wet non-spillable batteries.
If devices are carried in checked baggage passenger must pack it so to protect the device from damage and to prevent unintentional activation, and device must be fully switched off (not in sleep or hibernation mode).
Spare batteries must be individually protected to prevent short circuits by placement in the original retails packaging or by otherwise insulating terminals, e.g. by taping over exposed terminals or placing each battery in a separate plastic bag or protective pouch and carried in carry-on baggage only.
Each person is limited to a maximum of 20 spare batteries, unless helvetic GOP would approve individual requests for carriage of more spare batteries.
Lithium batteries are subject to following conditions: each installed or spare battery must not exceed: for lithium metal or lithium alloy batteries, a lithium content of not more than 2 g or for lithium ion batteries, a watt-hour rating of not more that 100 Wh

batteries must be of type that meets the requirements of the UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, subsection 38.3

each person is limited to a maximum of 15 PED, unless helvetic GOP would

approve individual requests for carriage of more than 15 PED

articles containing lithium metal or lithium ion cells or batteries, the primary

purpose of which is to provide power to another device, e.g. power banks,

are permitted in carry-on baggage only, and must be individually protected to prevent short circuits by placement in the original retails packaging or by

otherwise insulating terminals, e.g. by taping over exposed terminals or placing each battery in a separate plastic bag or protective pouch

electronic cigarettes, e-cigars and other personal vaporizers containing

kontext:
11.9.4.1 Flight and Cockpit Voice Recorder Systems

Flight recorders on the helvetic Embraer fleet are digital recording units (DVDR) combining three different functionalities. Recording of: audio information from cockpit area microphones and primary crew microphones [cockpit voice recorder (CVR)]. datalink messages [data link recorder (DLR)] all available flight data [flight data recorder (FDR)]
CVRs have at least 2 hours of voice recording capacity and must only be

de- activated to protect records in due time.
FDRs have a flight time recording capacity which allows read out or de-activation in due time after an occurrence. De-activation during flight or on ground by the flight crew is not allowed.
Note: If a flight is conducted with a deactivated CVR check with MCC for MEL Regulation(s).

The DVDR automatically starts recording audio information as soon as the

aircraft is powered up. Flight data recording begins when the first engine is started. After power down the DVDRcontinue recording audio information for 10 minutes.
In the event the airplane becomes involved in an accident or serious incident, the

Commander must ensure the protection of all related flight records, and if

necessary, the associated DVDR to the extent possible. This can include the

retention of the DVDR in safe custody until its disposition.

The removal of the flight recorder systems from the aircraft will be determined by

the investigating authority in the state conducting the investigation with due regard to the seriousness of the occurrence.

fragen.frage: Wann gilt eine Verletzung gemäss den Definitionen in OM-A 11.2 als fatal?
