fragen.frage: Unter welchen Bedingungen kann die Wake-Turbulence-Staffelung gemäss OM-A reduziert werden?
antworten: Bei Windstille auf parallelen Runways
Bei Nacht und guter Sicht
Bei starkem Seitenwind auf einer Single Runway
Bei schwachem Rückenwind auf einer Single Runway
fragen.erklaerung: Die Staffelung kann bei starkem Seitenwind in einer Single-Runway-Umgebung reduziert werden.
fragen.zitat: On the other hand separation may be reduced in strong crosswind conditions when operating into or out of single runway environments.
kontext:
8.3.9 Wake Turbulence

Wake turbulence is generated by air exchange due to the pressure differential between the lower and upper surface of the wing. This exchange causes counter rotating vortices trailing from the outer wing tips. The larger the aircraft the larger are the vortices. The wake of a large aircraft may require large control inputs on an aircraft flying in the area behind it. These control inputs may exceed the roll control capability of the following aircraft. The flight crew must be aware of the location of the vortex flow generated by a preceding aircraft and adjust his flight path accordingly.
Tests with large and heavy aircraft have shown that the vortex flow field – in a plane cutting through the wake at any point downstream – covers an area about twice the wing span in width and one wing span in depth. The vortices from the two tips remain spaced and will drift with the wind. The vortices will sink with a rate of descent of 400 – 500 fpm. There is a tendency that the vortices will level off at about 800 – 1 000 ft below the flight path. Vortex strength diminishes with time and distance behind the aircraft.
Vortex generation will begin on rotation when the nose wheel lifts off the ground and ends, when the nose wheel touches down on landing. In conditions with very weak or calm winds, the remaining vortices from a landing aircraft may persist up to 5 minutes or even longer.
All this has prompted National Aviation Authorities (NAA) and ICAO to establish minimum separation criteria.

OM-A 8 Operating Procedures

ICAO Definitions The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) classifies aircraft into wake turbulence categories based on their maximum certificated take-off mass (MTOM) and the strength of the wake vortices they generate.
Category MTOM Examples Light (L) 7.000 kg Cessna 172 Medium (M) 7.000 kg - 136.000 kg Embraer E-Jets Heavy (H) (1) 136.000 kg Boeing 747 Super (J) exceptionally strong wake turbulence Airbus A380

Note 1: Some types like the Boeing 757, despite having an MTOM below 136.000 kg, are treated as Heavy due to their strong wake turbulence.

Note: In the United Kingdom the aircraft series Boeing 707, DC-8, VC-10 and IL-62 are considered medium (M) and shall be announced as such in the initial contact with ATC. However, this regulation does not affect the composition of flight plans which shall be completed in accordance with the ICAO wake turbulence categorisation.

ICAO Wake Turbulence Separation Leading

heavy medium 5 NM 2 minutes

medium medium 3 NM 2 minutes light 4 NM 2 minutes

heavy 3 NM 2 minutes

RECAT-EU Defintions For RECAT-EU definitions refer to:
Route Manual Tool – Europe Airway Manual – Air Traffic Control – Air Traffic Control Data Europe – RECAT EU Note: Embraer 190/195-E1 are classified as Lower Medium (CAT-E).
Embraer 190/195-E2 are classified as Upper Medium (CAT-D).

Additional Information Apart from the above ICAO or RECAT standards for vortex separation, the controller or the flight crew may arrange for a larger separation to compensate for calm conditions or for other terrestrial factors, which might enforce or retain the vortex energy for a longer time. The same may apply for operations into parallel or near parallel runways, where in crosswind situations the danger may exist, that vortices are encountered from a preceding aircraft approaching or departing from the parallel runway.
On the other hand separation may be reduced in strong crosswind conditions when operating into or out of single runway environments.

A departing aircraft will not be permitted to commence take-off until the preceding departing aircraft has crossed the end of the runway-in-use or has started a turn or until all preceding landing aircraft are clear of the runway-in-use.
A landing aircraft will not be permitted to cross the beginning of the runway on its final approach until the preceding departing aircraft has crossed the end of the

runway-in-use, or has started a turn, or until all preceding landing aircraft are clear of the runway-in-use.
More information can be found in OM-C Chapter Rules and Regulation.
In case adequate separation cannot be provided or when vortices are

encountered despite adequate separation, the following should be remembered:

during approach and landing behind a vortex generating aircraft, landing

should be aimed at a touch down point at the runway past the touch down

point of the heavier aircraft – if runway length permits

when taking-off, the lift-off point of the preceding aircraft should be remembered; if possible arrangement shall be made for a lift-off point well

before the lift-off point of the preceding aircraft; if this cannot be done,

delaying the take-off for some seconds – depending upon the size of the preceding aircraft and wind conditions on ground may be considered

when approaching behind a vortex generating aircraft, it should be realized,

that flying above the flight path of the preceding aircraft means to avoid the vortex zones – at least until short before touch down.

Mental preparation to abandon the approach using proper Operations Manual OM-B technique including use of maximum thrust setting is important.

fragen.frage: Wie stellt der PF unter FL 100 sicher, dass er sofort eingreifen kann, wenn er keine andere Aufgabe hat?

Hände an den Thrust Levers und an oder nahe der Control Column

kontext:
8.3.2.20 Operation below FL100

A speed limitation of 250 KIAS must be observed below FL 100. Higher speeds can be accepted on ATC request only above 5000 ft MSL Flight Crews shall not ask for higher speeds below FL 100 by themselves. OM-B limitations must be observed.
If FMS programming or any other task requires "head down" for prolonged time

below FL 100 the task shall be delegated to the PM. If not possible a transfer of controls shall be considered. A state of both pilots "head down" shall be avoided.
When flying below FL 100 the PF shall closely observe aircraft inputs and be able to intervene immediately.

This shall be accomplished by putting hands on

thrust levers and on or close to the control column if no other task is being

performed.

However, during takeoff, both hands shall be placed on the control column by the

PF after V1 until 400ft AAE.

During manual flight the PM shall not hinder the PF in making any inputs, but he shall be ready to take over controls at anytime (e.g. placing his hands close to

the controls).

One hand on the autopilot disconnect, the other on the MCDU
Both hands on the control column until landing
Hands on the thrust levers and on or near the control column
fragen.erklaerung_en: Below FL 100, the PF keeps his hands on the thrust levers and on or near the control column when no other task is pending.

fragen.frage: Unter welcher Voraussetzung darf die Crew eine ATC-Clearance zur Abweichung von einer publizierten Departure Route annehmen?

fragen.zitat: A flight crew may accept an ATC clearance to deviate from a published departure route, provided obstacle clearance criteria are observed and full account is taken of the operating conditions.
kontext:
8.3.2.19 Climb

The instrument departure procedures are published in the Operations Manual OM-C and must be strictly adhered to.
A flight crew may accept an ATC clearance to deviate from a published departure route, provided obstacle clearance criteria are observed and full account is taken of the operating conditions.

For speed limitations up to the minimum safe altitude after departure refer to the Operations Manual OM-C. The applications of these data must be done considering the aircraft category and the airport limitations (aircraft categories listed for the respective airport).
In case of engine failure, the engine-out climb-out procedure must be followed.
The after take-off or climb check shall be initiated according to OM-B, but earliest when traffic situation, ATC communication and navigation (i.e. FMS programming) allow to divert the attention of both flight crew members to this task.

Only in an emergency

fragen.erklaerung_en: A deviation may be accepted if obstacle clearance criteria are met and operating conditions are fully taken into account.

fragen.frage: Auf welchen Flügen dürfen abnormale Situationen oder IMC mit künstlichen Mitteln simuliert werden?

Nur auf technischen Check- oder Trainingsflügen (Level-B Non-Revenue Flights)
Auf jedem Flug mit Zustimmung des Commanders
Auf Linienflügen oberhalb FL 100 bei VMC
fragen.erklaerung: Simulationen sind auf allen helvetic-Flügen verboten, auch auf Ferry- und Positioning-Flügen; Ausnahmen sind nur technische Check- und Trainingsflüge (Level-B).
fragen.zitat: This applies also to ferry and positioning flights according to 8.7.1.1 - Level-A Non-Revenue Flights. The only exceptions are technical check flights or training flights as defined in 8.7.1.2 - Level-B Non-Revenue Flights.
kontext:
8.3.0.6 Simulation of Emergencies and Abnormalities

Any simulation of abnormal or emergency situations or flights in IMC by artificial means are strictly prohibited on all helvetic flights.

This applies also to ferry and positioning flights according to 8.7.1.1 - Level-A Non-Revenue Flights.

The only exceptions are technical check flights or training flights as defined in 8.7.1.2 - Level-B Non-Revenue Flights.
fragen.frage_en: On which flights may abnormal situations or IMC be simulated by artificial means?
antworten_en: On ferry and positioning flights without passengers
Only on technical check or training flights (Level-B non-revenue flights)
On any flight with the commander's approval
On scheduled flights above FL 100 in VMC
fragen.erklaerung_en: Simulations are prohibited on all helvetic flights, including ferry and positioning flights; exceptions are only technical check and training flights (Level-B).

Die ähnlichste OM-B-Prozedur unverändert anwenden

kontext:
8.3.0.4 Missing Procedures

Rules, instructions and procedures define the limits. Line operations shall be

performed within this framework.

However, all situations and scenarios which could occur in real life cannot be described or defined in Operations Manuals.

Should such a situation of missing definitions be encountered, crews shall carefully analyse the situation and proceed according to the defined operating

philosophy in 8.0 - Philosophy and 2.0 - Philosophy.
fragen.frage_en: How shall the crew proceed if no procedure is defined for a situation?

Delegate the decision to OCC and wait
Analyze the situation carefully and proceed according to the philosophy in OM-A 8.0 and 2.0
Apply the most similar OM-B procedure unchanged
fragen.erklaerung_en: If definitions are missing, the situation must be analyzed carefully and handled according to the operating philosophy in 8.0 and 2.0.

fragen.frage: Was ist zu tun, wenn das Flugzeug auf Eingaben ins Autoflight System nicht angemessen reagiert?

Das Autoflight System per Circuit Breaker neu starten

fragen.zitat: If the airplanes response is not appropriate or adequate, the autoflight system shall be switched off and the flight continued manually.
kontext:
8.3.0.5 Best Use of Equipment

helvetic follows the policy best use of equipment, which means that any equipment which helps to fulfill a task and therefore reduces workload shall be used if technically available.
The autoflight system is an effective tool to increase capacity of flight crews for other tasks if it is used at a level of automation appropriate for the task and monitored systematically. Such monitoring shall ensure appropriate airplane response to pilot inputs: cross-checking of mode control panels/ flight mode annunciator

observing the results of any mode changes

supervising the resulting guidance and airplane response
If the airplanes response is not appropriate or adequate, the autoflight system shall be switched off and the flight continued manually.
fragen.frage_en: What must be done if the aircraft does not respond appropriately to inputs into the autoflight system?
antworten_en: Select a different autopilot mode and wait
Restart the autoflight system by circuit breaker
Continue flying with the autopilot and inform OCC
Switch off the autoflight system and continue flying manually
fragen.erklaerung_en: If the aircraft does not respond appropriately, the autoflight system must be switched off and the flight continued manually.

fragen.frage: Welche Massnahmen sind zur Reduktion einer Ankunftsverspätung im Flug anzuwenden, sofern machbar?

kontext:
8.3.0.10.1 Management of In-Flight Delays

In order to protect subsequent operations which could be affected by delays in

day by day operation, the operating philosophy of “reliability and punctuality” may

become the higher goal. The commander shall take appropriate measures to

minimise delays which could affect subsequent flights. In doing so, the following

policy applies:

The arrival delay (arrival at the gate/parking) shall be reduced in flight. The aim must be on-time operation.

To reduce the effect on the operation due to delays, the following measures shall be applied if feasible:

high speed

optimum flight level in terms of flight time

shortcuts

If no subsequent flights are planned for the crew or aircraft, it is up to the

commander to apply appropriate measures.
fragen.frage_en: Which measures are to be applied in flight to reduce an arrival delay, if feasible?
antworten_en: High speed, optimum altitude with respect to flight time, and shortcuts
Long range cruise, lower altitude and avoiding holdings
Reducing taxi fuel and dispensing with extra fuel
Higher speed than 250 KIAS below FL 100 on own request
fragen.erklaerung_en: To reduce delays, if feasible, apply high speed, optimum flight level with respect to flight time, and shortcuts.

kontext:
8.3.0.8 Fleet Configuration

Modern airplanes used in airline operations usually carry standardised equipment and vary amongst each other only rarely within the same fleet.
Should a specific airplane within the fleet carry different equipment which could result in operational issues,
training according to OM-D 2.1.2 Differences and Familiarisation Training shall be performed by each crew member before operating this specific tail number.

8.3.0.9 8.3.0.9 MCC Principles

This chapter intends to create a mental link between higher level policies and lower level SOPs, aiming to distinguish between CRM- and MCC-principles. „Playground“ we are aware that Knowledge, Skills and Attitudes (KSA) are to be seen as fundamentals

helvetic management creates a working environment enabling flight crews intrinsically motivating themselves

we are willing to accept that striving for self-discipline and a high level of performance is fundamental

we accept that safety is paramount and not negotiable, remaining aware at the same time that safety must be embedded in a commercially effective and efficient environment

we are willing to accept that operational daily life often offers „grey zones“ requiring all parties involved to apply a holistic problem-solving process potentially leading to various suitable solutions

we take full responsibility for decisions taken when faced with situations where no procedures or guidance exists

we do not “hide” behind regulations or superiors

„Operational conclusions“ we are aware that defined requirements and SOPs shall contribute to

reduce tiring discussions about minor, non-safety relevant items

we are aware of a general increase in complexity and counteract associated

risks by remaining vigilant about the „big picture“ while reducing workload and distraction by refraining from non safety-relevant micro-management

we refrain from exaggerated individual interpretations and implementation at

purely theoretical levels without enhancing safety at a practical level

when rating risks we aim to base our judgement at a realistic level based on

the current environment meaning that we refrain from drawing conclusions based on exaggerated assumptions

we are aware of the difference between „experience” and „expertise“, remaining mentally open for technological and procedural developments

based on „what“ rather than „who“ is right

we refrain from inventing or applying derived SOPs based on oral transmission by whoever, we challenge peers distributing rumours to apply SOPs as published while aiming to capture the “spirit behind”

„Operational behaviour“ we respect the roles and associated duties as PF and PM

we actively adhere to our own and accept the peer’s role as PF and PM

we are aware that the PF‘s workload is normally higher than the PM‘s purely based on his role, meaning the PM should refrain from inputs a split second before the PF is expected to act

to minimise misunderstandings, both PF and PM refrain from performing duties of the other role unless asked to do so by their peer

the PM accepts decisions and proceedings taken by the PF as long as he remains within the defined framework

both flight crew members shall refrain from forcing peers to adjust non safety-relevant minor items to their individual preferences going beyond SOPs

we welcome sharing of experience by contributing individual thoughts as long as they are clearly declared as such and not communicated as „best industry practice“ in any form of operational recommendations or orders

we communicate in a positive-minded, straightforward and direct manner by using clear and unhidden statements, irrespective of each role or function

fragen.frage: (E1) RTO unterhalb 60 KIAS (vor dem HOLD-Callout), der AT wurde nicht getrennt und beide Thrust Levers stehen noch über 40° TLA. Was macht der Autothrottle?
antworten: Er bewegt die Thrust Levers zurück in die TO/GA-Raste.
Er trennt sich automatisch und lässt die Thrust Levers stehen.
Er geht in HOLD und reagiert nicht mehr auf die Thrust Levers.
Er reduziert die Thrust Levers automatisch auf IDLE.
fragen.erklaerung: Wird ein RTO unter 60 KIAS ohne AT-Trennung durchgeführt und bleiben die Thrust Levers nicht unter 40° TLA, fährt der AT sie zurück in die TO/GA-Raste. Erst unter 40° TLA oder mit Reverse Thrust trennt sich der AT.
fragen.zitat: if an RTO is performed below 60 KIAS (before HOLD is announced) and AT is not disconnected, Autothrottle moves the thrust levers back to TO/GA detent if both throttles are reduced to a position not below 40 degrees TLA.
kontext:
3.3.1 Rejected Takeoff - RTO

During the takeoff phase, an RTO procedure is initiated before V1 if any adverse

or abnormal event occurs that could affect the safety of flight. Many faults can cause a decision to reject, like engine fire, engine failure and some other system

faults or events. If an adequate decision to reject is taken, do not delay the RTO.
Delaying the decision increases the risk of a runway overrun, because it takes a

few seconds for the engines to spool down to idle thrust.

A successful RTO depends on:
Accurate alert and monitoring during all takeoff phase,

Captains timely decision,

All callouts made on a loud, clear, and precise communication way,

Adequate briefing, procedures, and coordination.

Responsibility Whoever first identifies the undesirable event or malfunction must announce it, but the decision and responsibility to perform an RTO remain to the captain.
Once the decision is made, initiate the RTO immediately.

Actions Actions are taken considering that, during all takeoff procedures, the LSP keeps his hand on the thrust levers until V1 is reached,

Once the RTO decision has been made, the following actions are: set thrust

levers to idle, disconnect the autothrottle, verify autobrake actuation or

manually apply maximum brakes, and apply reverse thrust as required,

The autobrake RTO mode provides the maximum deceleration rate, which is

equivalent to the maximum manual braking. To decrease workload in this scenario it is recommended to use autobrake in RTO mode, although the

pilot can manually override the autobrake as required.

Note:

if an RTO is performed below 60 KIAS (before HOLD is announced) and AT is not disconnected, Autothrottle moves the thrust levers back to TO/GA detent if both throttles are reduced to a position not below 40 degrees TLA.

If throttles are moved below 40 degrees TLA or reverse thrust is applied during an RTO, the AT disconnects,

directional control is kept by applying rudder pedal steering,

monitor airplane deceleration, cancel any aural warnings upon malfunction identification, verify reverse thrust status, and advise

ATC,

the engine should be commanded from MAX REV to MIN REV at or above 60 KIAS, and it is recommended to close the thrust reversers at 30 KIAS

if necessary, thrust reverse can be used until airplane comes to a complete stop, considering airplane speed, runway length available, slippery surfaces with ice, snow and so forth,

the airplane should remain on the runway until it is clear that an emergency evacuation is not necessary and the whole scenario is analyzed. If necessary, request external aids to vacate the runway to a safe position according to ATC instructions,

if RTO decision was taken due to fire, consider positioning the airplane so that fire is on the downwind of fuselage, if an RTO is performed, the FMS takeoff and landing data may

reset after two minutes. If a new takeoff is intended, the FMS takeoff and landing data must be re-entered and confirmed before

the takeoff.

Low and High Energy Speeds The sooner an RTO decision is taken, the greater is the chance to safely stop within runway limits. RTO above V1 may lead to a runway overrun and is the main cause of overrun accidents,

Low energy speed is considered up to, approximately, 80 KIAS,

During takeoff, the 80 KIAS callout has three main proposes: pilot

incapacitation check, airspeed crosscheck and the transition from Low to High Energy speed,

For High energy speeds only reject the takeoff if there is a malfunction that severely affects the flight safety, such as but not limited to:

Engine failures resulting in loss of thrust, Fire or fire warning, Severe damages.

For High energy speeds, it is recommended to continue the takeoff if a tire burst occurs,

Upon reaching V1, if no decision has been taken, continue the takeoff.
After V1, there is no assurance that the airplane is capable to stop within the remaining runway length.

OM-B E1 Procedures

REJECTED TAKEOFF - ACTIONS and CALLOUTS
fragen.frage_en: (E1) RTO below 60 KIAS (before the HOLD callout), the AT was not disconnected and both thrust levers are still above 40° TLA. What does the autothrottle do?
antworten_en: It moves the thrust levers back to the TO/GA detent.
It disconnects automatically and leaves the thrust levers where they are.
It goes to HOLD and no longer responds to the thrust levers.
It automatically reduces the thrust levers to IDLE.
fragen.erklaerung_en: If an RTO is performed below 60 KIAS without AT disconnection and the thrust levers do not stay below 40° TLA, the AT moves them back to the TO/GA detent. Only below 40° TLA or with reverse thrust does the AT disconnect.

fragen.frage: (E1) Nach einem RTO ist ein erneuter Takeoff geplant. Was gilt für die FMS Takeoff- und Landing-Daten?
antworten: Sie bleiben gespeichert; nur V1 muss neu bestätigt werden.
Sie können nach zwei Minuten zurückgesetzt werden und müssen vor dem Takeoff neu eingegeben und bestätigt werden.
Sie werden sofort gelöscht, sobald die Thrust Levers auf IDLE stehen.
Sie bleiben 10 Minuten gültig und müssen nur bei einem Runway-Wechsel neu eingegeben werden.
fragen.erklaerung: Nach einem RTO können die FMS Takeoff- und Landing-Daten nach zwei Minuten zurückgesetzt werden. Für einen neuen Takeoff müssen sie neu eingegeben und bestätigt werden.
fragen.zitat: if an RTO is performed, the FMS takeoff and landing data may reset after two minutes. If a new takeoff is intended, the FMS takeoff and landing data must be re-entered and confirmed before the takeoff.

fragen.frage_en: (E1) A new takeoff is planned after an RTO. What applies to the FMS takeoff and landing data?
antworten_en: They remain stored; only V1 must be reconfirmed.
They may be reset after two minutes and must be re-entered and confirmed before takeoff.

fragen.frage: (E1) Engine Failure nach V1: Innerhalb welcher Pitch-Grenzen liegt die erste Guidance des TO Mode?
antworten: Minimum 5°, Maximum 15°
Minimum 10°, Maximum 20°
Minimum 7°, Maximum 18°
Minimum 8°, Maximum 25°
fragen.erklaerung: Die erste Guidance des TO Mode basiert auf Takeoff Weight und Flap Setting und ist auf minimal 7° und maximal 18° Pitch begrenzt.
fragen.zitat: The TO mode first guidance is based on takeoff weight and flap setting, limited to a minimum pitch of 7° and maximum of 18°.
kontext:
3.6.3 Engine Failure above V1

If an engine failure occurs above V1, control airplane direction, aiming to keep airplane on runway centerline by smoothly applying rudder.
As soon as an Engine Failure or FIRE is recognized (not always followed by loss of thrust) and affected engine identified, check maximum thrust on EICAS.

After rotation, set aileron in neutral and use rudder and yaw trim to keep wings level. High aileron input raises the spoilers and increases drag.

As reference, the slip/skid indicator is approximately to off center and

between 0° to 5° of bank after engine failure. It depends on speed, gross weight,

and altitude. Generally the control wheel in the neutral position is a good indication of the lowest drag for single engine.
Crew must keep close attention at first positive rate of climb to retract landing gear, monitoring airplane profile.
The TO mode first guidance is based on takeoff weight and flap setting, limited to a minimum pitch of 7° and maximum of 18°.

Crew must follow the flight director guidance to maintain V2 to V2 10 KIAS up to acceleration altitude, according to the following three different conditions: engine failure below V2: pitch for V2

engine failure between V2 and V2 10 KIAS: pitch for the present speed

engine failure above V2 10 KIAS: pitch for V2 10 KIAS Takeoff thrust is limited to 5 (optionally 10) minutes after takeoff. It is recommended that emergency procedures to be accomplished as soon as safe

altitude has been reached (at least 400 ft AGL or according to local minimums).

When engine failure occurs after takeoff, noise abatement procedures no longer apply.

Following an Engine Failure, ATTCS adjusts operating engine thrust to its

respective RSV mode. If the maximum thrust is not reached for any reason, advance the thrust levers to maximum thrust.

On departure procedures with acceleration altitudes above 1000 ft, emphasize

during takeoff briefing that, in the event of an Engine Failure, Engine Fire (with loss of thrust), or any other malfunction requiring a memory item, actions can be

commanded at an altitude lower than the acceleration altitude, but not lower than 400 ft. Airplane must be stabilized and on the profile.

For One Engine Inoperative, limit the bank angle to:

15° at V2

20° at V2 5 KIAS

25° at V2 10 KIAS

OM-B E1 Procedures

antworten_en: Minimum 5°, maximum 15°
Minimum 10°, maximum 20°
Minimum 7°, maximum 18°
Minimum 8°, maximum 25°
fragen.erklaerung_en: The initial TO mode guidance is based on takeoff weight and flap setting and is limited to a minimum of 7° and a maximum of 18° pitch.

Spätestens bei 1000 ft AFE, unabhängig von der Distanz
Auf dem Final bei etwa 12 NM
Auf dem Final bei etwa 8 NM

kontext:
3.6.9 One Engine Inoperative 3D-Approach

The same procedure as described in chapter 3D-Approaches should be used, with the following amendments: use Slat/Flap 5 for landing

during approach, when stabilised on final:

set the rudder trim to neutral set fuel crossfeed to OFF (if applicable)

Approach Preparation

plan to be stabilised on final in landing configuration at about 8 NM

pilot should maintain the directional control using the rudder pedals

Go Around During the approach, if an engine failure occurs prior to engage the AUTOLAND mode, the approach can be performed with the AUTOLAND engaged.
If an engine failure occurs after the AUTOLAND engagement, a go-around must be performed.
During a go-around, be prepared to overcome the directional control.
The parallel rudder disengages when the Flight Director GO-AROUND mode is

changed to any other vertical mode.

refer to 2.5.3 - 3D IFR Approach
fragen.frage_en: (E1) One engine inoperative 3D approach: where should the aircraft be stabilized in landing configuration according to approach preparation?
antworten_en: On final at about 4 NM
At 1000 ft AFE at the latest, regardless of distance
On final at about 12 NM
On final at about 8 NM
fragen.erklaerung_en: For the OEI 3D approach, planning should be to be stabilized in landing configuration on final at about 8 NM.

fragen.frage: (E1) Engine Failure im Final Approach, geplant war ein Landing mit Flaps 5. Welche Referenz-Speed ist nun zu berücksichtigen?
antworten: VREF FULL + 20 kt
VREF FULL + 10 kt
VREF FULL + 15 kt
VREF FULL + 5 kt
fragen.erklaerung: Bei einem Flaps-5-Landing ist die Konfiguration bereits OEI-tauglich; zu berücksichtigen sind die neue Referenz-Speed VREF FULL + 20 kt und dass nur ein Thrust Reverser verfügbar ist.
fragen.zitat: Crew must be sure that runway distance is enough to complete landing safely. Take into account the new reference speed (VREF FULL + 20 kt) and the fact that only one thrust reverser is available.
kontext:
3.6.11 One Engine Inoperative Circling Approach

In a circling approach with one engine inoperative, the same procedure for circling approach with all engines operating is to be used. The exception is some peculiarities due to the loss of one engine.

The downwind leg should be flown with landing gear up, Slat/Flap 2 and Slat/Flap 2 maneuvering speed from the final approach fix until base leg.

Turning base leg, approximately 20 seconds (depending on altitude above the aerodrome) after passing abeam of the threshold, extend landing gear, select

Slat/Flap 3, reducing to Slat/Flap 3 maneuvering speed.

Before intercepting the final approach profile, select Slat/Flap 5, reduce to VAP and perform the Before Landing Checklist.
When stabilized and on short final, set the rudder trim to neutral. If the airplane cannot meet the stabilized approach criteria, execute a missed approach.

3.6.12 3.6.12 Engine Failure during Steep Approach

An engine failure above DA (MDA) should lead to a go-around. Below DA (MDA) the approach may be continued maintaining the current airplane configuration.

3.6.13 3.6.13 Engine Failure during Final Approach

If an engine failure occurs during final approach, it is the captain’s responsibility to decide to continue the approach or initiate a go-around. In case of any doubt that the landing can be conducted safely, accomplish a go-around.

FLAPS 5 Landing:
When landing with flaps 5 the airplane is already in the required configuration for an OEI landing. Only a speed adjustment is necessary to continue the approach.

Crew must be sure that runway distance is enough to complete landing safely.
Take into account the new reference speed (VREF FULL 20 kt) and the fact that only one thrust reverser is available.

FLAPS FULL Landing:
Considering a landing with flaps FULL, a reasonable increase in workload occurs. Few examples are MCDU setting (heads down), flaps retraction, and thrust increments to reach the target speed.
It is recommended to go-around, unless there is plenty of time to reconfigure the airplane, or if the crew judges that the safest course of action is to continue the

approach in the same configuration.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Engine failure on final approach, a landing with flaps 5 had been planned. Which reference speed must now be considered?
antworten_en: VREF FULL + 20 kt
VREF FULL + 10 kt
VREF FULL + 15 kt
VREF FULL + 5 kt
fragen.erklaerung_en: For a flaps 5 landing, the configuration is already OEI-capable; the new reference speed VREF FULL + 20 kt must be considered, and only one thrust reverser is available.

fragen.frage: (E1) Driftdown: Welche Hindernisfreiheit verlangen die Vorschriften gemäss OM-B nach einem Engine Failure auf der Strecke?
antworten: Gross Level-off Altitude mindestens 1000 ft oder Net Flight Path mindestens 1500 ft über allen Hindernissen
Net Level-off Altitude mindestens 1000 ft über allen Hindernissen oder Net Flight Path mindestens 2000 ft darüber bis zu einem Landeplatz
Net Level-off Altitude mindestens 2000 ft oder Net Flight Path mindestens 1000 ft über allen Hindernissen
Net Level-off Altitude mindestens 500 ft oder Gross Flight Path mindestens 2000 ft über allen Hindernissen
fragen.erklaerung: Zwei Nachweise sind zulässig: Die Net Level-off Altitude muss alle Hindernisse um mindestens 1000 ft überragen, oder der Net Flight Path muss sie bis zu einem Landeplatz um mindestens 2000 ft überragen.
fragen.zitat: the net level-off altitude must clear all enroute obstacles by at least 1000ft or the net flight path must clear all enroute obstacles between the point where the engine is assumed to fail and an airport where a landing can be made by at least 2000ft
kontext:
3.6.7 Engine Failure In Flight Driftdown

Following an engine failure or inflight engine shutdown, an airplane may not be able to maintain its cruise altitude. The driftdown profile assures the airplane altitude is kept as high as possible throughout the descent. The driftdown speed is represented by the Green Dot and provides the lower descent gradient.

During a driftdown, the available thrust increases as the airplane descends.

Eventually, at a certain altitude the available thrust becomes equal to the airplane drag, and the airplane levels off. This altitude is called the gross level off altitude.

The gross level off altitude, when corrected for gradient margins by 1.1% (2 engines), 1.4% (3 engines), or 1.6% (4 engines), is called the net level

off altitude. It depends on the atmospheric temperature and the airplane weight.
Regulations (FAR 121.191/CAT.POL.A.215/CAR 705.58) require that the airplane clears all terrain by a given margin when an engine fails.
Two means of compliance for enroute obstacle clearance are allowed:

the net level-off altitude must clear all enroute obstacles by at least 1000ft or the net flight path must clear all enroute obstacles between the point where the engine is assumed to fail and an airport where a landing can be made by at least 2000ft
(Drift Down Profile)
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Driftdown: which obstacle clearance do the regulations require according to OM-B after an engine failure en route?
antworten_en: Gross level-off altitude at least 1000 ft or net flight path at least 1500 ft above all obstacles
Net level-off altitude at least 1000 ft above all obstacles or net flight path at least 2000 ft above them up to an aerodrome
Net level-off altitude at least 2000 ft or net flight path at least 1000 ft above all obstacles
Net level-off altitude at least 500 ft or gross flight path at least 2000 ft above all obstacles
fragen.erklaerung_en: Two demonstrations are permitted: the net level-off altitude must clear all obstacles by at least 1000 ft, or the net flight path must clear them by at least 2000 ft up to an aerodrome.

fragen.zitat: annunciated as WSHR in green in the vertical flight mode annunciator field when active. ROLL becomes the active lateral mode and the autopilot disconnects when windshear escape guidance is activated.
kontext:
3.10.1 Windshear Policy

The most important policy is to avoid a windshear. Although windshear detection and annunciation system is installed, pilots may not perceive that an area of a potential windshear could be encountered ahead. Therefore some aids must be used by flight crews to develop an awareness of windshear causes and perceive danger signals to successfully avoid it. The following information can be used:

Presence of thunderstorms, microburst, convective clouds, squall line

Visual observation of strong winds near the ground Onboard weather radar

Pilots or Air Traffic Services reports

Windshear escape guidance is provided by the FGCS Flight Director function, and is
annunciated as WSHR in green in the vertical flight mode annunciator field when active. ROLL becomes the active lateral mode and the autopilot disconnects when windshear escape guidance is activated.

Windshear detection is enabled between 10 ft and 1500 ft AGL, and escape guidance may be initiated when the following conditions are met:
Manually when a windshear Caution or Warning is detected and the pilot presses the TO/GA Button When a windshear Warning is detected and Thrust Levers are set to TO/GA position or beyond Automatically when the AFCS flight director mode is in Takeoff or Go- Around mode and a windshear Warning is detected

The windshear escape guidance mode does not automatically revert to any other flight guidance mode. The pilot must manually select another mode in order to exit windshear escape guidance, and the ability to successfully transition to another vertical guidance mode requires that the activation criteria described

above be false.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) What happens to lateral mode and autopilot when the windshear escape guidance is activated?
antworten_en: ROLL becomes the active lateral mode and the autopilot disconnects.
HDG HOLD becomes active and the autopilot remains engaged.
LNAV remains active and the autopilot flies the escape maneuver.
TRACK becomes active and the autopilot goes to pitch hold.
fragen.erklaerung_en: With windshear escape guidance activated (WSHR green on the FMA), ROLL becomes the active lateral mode and the autopilot disconnects.

fragen.frage: (E1) Windshear Escape Maneuver aufgrund einer EGPWS-Ansage: Wann darf die Konfiguration (Gear/Flaps) geändert werden?
antworten: Sobald eine positive Steigrate bestätigt ist
Wenn Terrain Clearance gesichert ist und oberhalb 1500 ft AGL oder nachdem das WSHEAR-Label vom PFD verschwunden ist
Ab 1000 ft AGL, unabhängig von der WSHEAR-Anzeige
Erst nach Erreichen der Missed Approach Altitude
fragen.erklaerung: Gear und Flaps bleiben unverändert, bis Terrain Clearance gesichert ist und das Flugzeug über 1500 ft AGL ist oder das WSHEAR-Label vom PFD entfernt wurde.
fragen.zitat: Maintain airplane configuration. Do not change gear and flap position until terrain clearance is assured and above 1500 ft AGL or after WSHEAR label is removed from PFD.
kontext:
3.10.2 Windshear Prevention Recovery

Windshear escape maneuver due to EGPWS announcement:
Thrust Levers MAX When moving the thrust levers press TO/GA Button.

Flight Director Escape Guidance Cue FOLLOW

Maintain airplane configuration. Do not change gear and flap position until terrain clearance is assured and above 1500 ft AGL or after WSHEAR label

is removed from PFD.

The windshear escape guidance mode does not automatically revert to any other flight guidance mode. The pilot must manually select another mode or press TO/GA Button in order to exit windshear escape guidance.
Windshear escape maneuver Without EGPWS announcement or with Loss of FD indication:
Autopilot DISENGAGE Thrust Levers MAX When moving the thrust levers press TO/GA Button.

Pitch 20°, LIMITED TO PLI,
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Windshear escape maneuver due to an EGPWS callout: when may the configuration (gear/flaps) be changed?
antworten_en: As soon as a positive rate of climb is confirmed
When terrain clearance is assured and above 1500 ft AGL or after the WSHEAR label has disappeared from the PFD
From 1000 ft AGL, regardless of the WSHEAR indication
Only after reaching the missed approach altitude
fragen.erklaerung_en: Gear and flaps remain unchanged until terrain clearance is assured and the aircraft is above 1500 ft AGL or the WSHEAR label has been removed from the PFD.

kontext:
3.9.1 Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)

The pilot must not initiate evasive manoeuvres using Traffic Advisory information (TA) only, without visually sighting conflicting traffic.

The traffic display and advisories are intended for assistance to visually locate

the indicated conflicting traffic.

Manoeuvres that are in the opposite direction of the Resolution Advisory (RA) are extremely hazardous, especially RAs involving altitude crossing, and thus

are prohibited unless it is visually determined to be the only means to assure

safe separation.
WARNING: It is possible in some cases to have insufficient airplane performance to follow the TCAS command without flying into stall warning or buffet.
Conditions where this may occur include:
Bank angle in excess of 15 degrees.

Operations at airports above 5300ft MSL or temperatures greater than ISA 28°C (50°F).

Engine inoperative.

Failure to configure the airplane to go around, following a climb

RA in landing configuration.
Failure to advance thrust to max continuous thrust, following a climb RA at reduced thrust.

Speeds less than normal operating speed.

Abnormal configurations which reduce performance

(e.g. gear down).

TCAS command reversal to a "CLIMB-CLIMB NOW".

Buffet margin less than 0.3 G.

If stall warning occurs during an RA manoeuvre, immediately

abandon the RA and execute stall recovery procedures. TCAS II continues to provide RA`s during stall warning and recovery

procedure. If high speed buffet is encountered when initially responding to an RA, relax pitch force as necessary to reduce

buffet, but still continue to manoeuvre.

Note: The consequences of not following an RA may result in additional RAs in which aural alert and visual annunciations may not agree with each other. A non-compliance by one airplane can result in reduced vertical separation with the need to achieve safe horizontal separation by visual means.

Using every available means, clear the airspace into which you are

going to manoeuvre. If needed, promptly and smoothly adjust the airplane’s pitch to fly into the green rectangle (if displayed), and

fly

out of the red trapezoidal shaped avoidance zone(s). This should require no more than 0.75 g to 1.25 g manoeuvre 0.25 g).

Exaggerated responses to TCAS RAs are not desirable or appropriate, because of the other potential traffic conflicts and ATC consequences. From level flight, proper response to a TCAS RA typically results in an overall altitude deviation of 300 to 500 ft to resolve a traffic conflict.

If a CLIMB RA is issued with the airplane in the landing configuration, a normal go-around should be initiated including the appropriate thrust increase and configurationchange.

Compliance with TCAS RA is required, unless the pilotconsiders unsafe to do so.

The pilot should promptly return to the previous ATCclearance after

the TCAS voice message "Clear of Conflict" is announced.
An immediate smooth response to an RA is required to obtain maximum separations. TCAS II algorithms arebased on the pilot

starting the initial manoeuvre within 5 seconds of the RA and within 2 1/2 seconds for additionalcorrective RAs (increases or reversals).

Any delay in responding to RAs will reduce the separations provided.

TCAS II may lose the track or altitude information about the threat

airplane during an RA. If so, the RA will terminatewithout a “Clear of Conflict” annunciation.

OM-B E1 Procedures

“TRAFFIC ALTERT, Turns all external followed by a rough lights ON. description of the position of the traffic Communicates

Upon receiving (e.g. TWO with ATC.

fragen.frage: (E1) Nose Low Upset Recovery: Warum soll beim Rollen in die Horizontallage der Load Factor reduziert werden?
antworten: Es verhindert ein Überschreiten von VMO/MMO.
Es reduziert den Höhenverlust während der Recovery.
Es erhöht die Rollwirksamkeit und verringert asymmetrische Lasten am Flugzeug.
Es aktiviert die AOA-Limiting-Funktion des Fly-by-Wire.
fragen.erklaerung: Den Load Factor beim Rollen in die Horizontale zu reduzieren erhöht die Rollwirksamkeit und verringert die asymmetrischen Lasten.
fragen.zitat: It is important to reduce load factor while attempting to roll to wings level because it increases the roll effectiveness while decreasing the asymmetric loads on the airplane.
kontext:
3.11.5 Nose Low Recovery Maneuver

A large out-of-trim condition could be encountered if the autopilot is disengaged.
If the autopilot and autothrottle are responding correctly to stop the divergence, keep them engaged.

If required, the PF should disengage the autopilot and autothrottle and the PM should confirm that they are disengaged. The PM should monitor attitude and

speed of the airplane throughout the recovery and announce any continued divergence.

Even in a nose low situation, the airplane may be stalled. If necessary, the PF must recover from the stall first, applying nose down inputs, which may not be intuitive.
It is important to reduce load factor while attempting to roll to wings level because it increases the roll effectiveness while decreasing the asymmetric loads on the airplane.

The PF should use Thrust or Speed brakes to control the airspeed.
If airspeed is low, apply thrust; if airspeed is high, reduce thrust, and if necessary, extend speed brakes.

Recover to level flight may require use of pitch trim to manage control forces during large airspeed changes. Pilots should monitor pitch command to avoid

entering a stall due to premature recovery at low speed or excessive load factor at high speed.
WARNING: Excessive use of pitch trim or rudder may increase the upset divergence or may result in high structural loads.

(if required). disengaged.

fragen.frage_en: (E1) Nose low upset recovery: why should the load factor be reduced when rolling to wings level?
antworten_en: It prevents exceeding VMO/MMO.
It reduces altitude loss during the recovery.
It increases roll effectiveness and reduces asymmetric loads on the aircraft.
It activates the AOA limiting function of the fly-by-wire.
fragen.erklaerung_en: Reducing the load factor when rolling to wings level increases roll effectiveness and reduces asymmetric loads.

Nur beim Nose High Upset mit mehr als 45° Querneigung
Nur vorsichtig und nur, wenn die Rollkontrolle unwirksam ist
fragen.erklaerung: Gemäss OM-B soll Rudder nur vorsichtig und nur dann zur Rollkontrolle eingesetzt werden, wenn die Rollkontrolle unwirksam ist; auch Pitch Trim sparsam verwenden.
fragen.zitat: If needed, use pitch trim sparingly. Careful use of rudder to aid roll control should be considered only if roll control is ineffective.
kontext:
3.11.3 Upset Recovery

The pilot response to an upset must be appropriate to stop the divergence and to recover the airplane’s state. Up to full-scale control deflections may be necessary. However, initiating recovery with arbitrary full-scale control deflections could actually increase the divergence. An excessive or inappropriate control

input that overshoots the desired response can startle the pilot and cause one upset to lead to another.

Communication between crew members assists in the recovery actions.

At the first indication of a flight path divergence, both pilots should announce

what is being observed. It is necessary to use the primary flight instruments when analyzing the upset situation. Visual meteorological conditions may allow the use of references outside the airplane; however, it can be difficult to see the horizon during both high and low pitch attitudes. Pilots must be prepared to analyze the situation during darkness and when instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) exists.

The PFD is a primary reference for recovery.
For Nose High Upset Recovery, the airspeed is normally decreasing, altitude is increasing and the VSI indicates a climb.

For Nose Low Upset Recovery, the airspeed is normally increasing, altitude is decreasing and the vertical speed indicator (VSI) indicates a

descent.
The actions listed below must be part of every recovery from an upset:
Become aware about the airplane's energy state

Stop the flight path divergence;

and Recover to a stabilized flight path.

The PM has an important role in the recovery maneuver.
The PM should monitor airspeed and attitude throughout the recovery and

announce any continued divergence.

The following techniques represent a logical progression for recovering the airplane. While not strictly procedural, the templates represent a consensus view

of actions for recovery.
If needed, use pitch trim sparingly. Careful use of rudder to aid roll control should be considered only if roll control is ineffective.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Upset recovery: when should rudder be used to assist roll control?
antworten_en: Always coordinated together with the aileron
Never; rudder is prohibited in upsets
Only in a nose high upset with more than 45° bank
Only with caution and only if roll control is ineffective
fragen.erklaerung_en: According to OM-B, rudder should be used cautiously and only if roll control is ineffective; also use pitch trim sparingly.

fragen.frage: (E1) Wodurch ist der Stall im Normal Mode der Flight Controls definiert?
antworten: Durch die Control Column am hinteren Anschlag, da das AOA Limiting den kritischen AOA nicht erreichen lässt
Durch Wing Drop mit leichtem bis mittlerem Buffeting
Durch das Auslösen des Stick Shakers
Durch das Erreichen der grünen PLI-Marke auf dem PFD
fragen.erklaerung: Im Normal Mode verhindert die AOA-Limiting-Funktion das Erreichen des kritischen AOA; daher definiert die Control Column am hinteren Anschlag den Stall.
fragen.zitat: In Normal Mode, during a speed reduction, the AOA Limiting function of the Stall Protection System will not allow the airplane to reach the critical AOA. Therefore, in Normal Mode the longitudinal control column at the aft stop defines the stall.
kontext:
3.12.1 Approach to Stall

In low speed situations, with Flight Control System in Normal or Direct Mode, an artificial stall warning is provided in advance to the aerodynamic stall in the form of stick shaker (artificial stall warning).

After the stick shaker, a light buffeting (natural stall warning) indicates the proximity of the aerodynamic stall for most of the E-Jets flap/gear configurations.

In Normal Mode, during a speed reduction, the AOA Limiting function of the Stall

Protection System will not allow the airplane to reach the critical AOA. Therefore,

in Normal Mode the longitudinal control column at the aft stop defines the stall.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) How is the stall defined in normal mode of the flight controls?
antworten_en: By the control column at the aft stop, as AOA limiting does not allow the critical AOA to be reached
By wing drop with light to moderate buffeting
By activation of the stick shaker
By reaching the green PLI mark on the PFD
fragen.erklaerung_en: In normal mode, the AOA limiting function prevents reaching the critical AOA; therefore the control column at the aft stop defines the stall.

fragen.frage: (E1) Wodurch ist der aerodynamische Stall der E-Jets im Direct Mode (AOA Limiting inaktiv) vorwiegend definiert?
antworten: Durch starkes Buffeting ohne Rollbewegung
Durch Wing Drop (unkommandiertes Rollen) und/oder Control Column am hinteren Anschlag, mit leichtem bis mittlerem Buffeting
Durch einen automatischen Nose-down-Befehl des Fly-by-Wire
Durch einen Stick Pusher beim kritischen AOA
fragen.erklaerung: Im Direct Mode ist der aerodynamische Stall vorwiegend durch Wing Drop und/oder die Control Column am hinteren Anschlag mit leichtem bis mittlerem Buffeting gekennzeichnet.
fragen.zitat: stall is defined predominantly by wing drop (uncommanded roll), and/or the control column at the aft stop, with light to moderate buffeting.
kontext:
3.12.2 Full Stall

In Direct Mode, with the AOA Limiting function disabled, the airplane will be able to reduce airspeed down to the critical AOA and the aerodynamic stall. The E- Jets aerodynamic
stall is defined predominantly by wing drop (uncommanded roll), and/or the control column at the aft stop, with light to moderate buffeting.

Those characteristics are dependent on the CG position and the speed bleed rate used during the approach to stall.

Elevator, ailerons and rudder controls remain effective in the same sense of application up to the aerodynamic stall.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) How is the aerodynamic stall of the E-Jets in direct mode (AOA limiting inactive) predominantly defined?
antworten_en: By heavy buffeting without roll movement
By wing drop (uncommanded roll) and/or control column at the aft stop, with light to moderate buffeting
By an automatic nose-down command of the fly-by-wire
By a stick pusher at the critical AOA
fragen.erklaerung_en: In direct mode, the aerodynamic stall is predominantly characterized by wing drop and/or the control column at the aft stop with light to moderate buffeting.

kontext:
3.13 Overspeed Prevention/Recovery

To prevent overspeed, continuously monitor thrust, airspeed and use speedbrake as required.
If reaching overspeed conditions, select MAN SPEEDS and set a lower target

speed. Select the appropriate vertical mode, reduce thrust levers and use speedbrake as required.

If the autopilot does not appropriately reduce the

airspeed, the pilot may momentarily override the autopilot using the TCS Button to manually fly the airplane out of the overspeed.

Select slat/flap 1 to reduce speed

Select VNAV so that the FMS corrects the speed
fragen.erklaerung_en: If the autopilot does not reduce speed adequately, the pilot may briefly override it with the TCS button and manually fly out of the overspeed.

3.13.1.1 Crew Procedure

To evaluate the conditions, MCC must be contacted and the following information

presented:

maximum KIAS

slat/flap lever position during the event (e.g. 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, FULL)

duration of the single event in seconds

2. on the control pedestal, set the flap/slat lever to (0) position and wait until

the flaps/slats move to position (0)
3. make sure that none of the two messages below are indicated on the

fragen.frage: (E1) Unreliable Airspeed: Welche Anzeigen können als Referenz dienen, wenn die PFD-Anzeigen unzuverlässig sind?
antworten: Flight Path Angle und Flight Path Vector
Vertical Speed und Flight Director
Ground Speed auf dem PFD und GPS Altitude
FMS Speed Target und Autothrottle-Anzeige
fragen.erklaerung: Bei unzuverlässigen PFD-Anzeigen können die Ground Speed auf dem PFD und die GPS Altitude als Referenz verwendet werden; FPA, FPV, Altitude und VS können ebenfalls unzuverlässig sein.
fragen.zitat: Ground Speed indication available on PFD and GPS altitude may also be used as reference if PFD indication is unreliable.
kontext:
3.7.4 Unreliable airspeed

Unreliable airspeed indications are usually associated with partial loss of the pitot static system. It may happen when there is blocking, damage, or freeze as well as deterioration of system parts.
The flight crew can recognize an unusual indication by monitoring airspeed indications and crosschecking PFD 1, 2 and IESS. IAS and ALT miscompare monitor annunciations can also be used to aid pilots to identify this condition.

When this scenario occurs the Autothrottle and Autopilot must be disengaged, since these systems use the airspeed indications to adjust their gains. The Flight Director may be also unreliable and should not be followed.
With the Autothrottle and Autopilot disengaged, the crew must maintain proper

control of the airplane using pitch attitude and power settings.

QRH - Emergency and Abnormal Procedures sections present Unreliable Airspeed tables to be used on each flight phase.

The use of Speedbrake should be avoided since the capacity of the flight crew to

monitor the speed change might be compromised.

Under an Unreliable Airspeed scenario, the Flight Path Angle (FPA) on PFD, Flight Path Vector (FPV) on HGS, Altitude, and Vertical Speed indications may

also be unreliable.

Ground Speed indication available on PFD and GPS altitude may also be used

as reference if PFD indication is unreliable.

At pilot’s discretion, when the airplane is stabilized under correct pitch attitude and power setting, instruments should be crosschecked to help identify any

possible reliable instrument. In case a reliable source is identified, ADS reversion

may be attempted.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Unreliable airspeed: which indications can serve as a reference if the PFD indications are unreliable?
antworten_en: Flight path angle and flight path vector
Vertical speed and flight director
Ground speed on the PFD and GPS altitude
FMS speed target and autothrottle indication
fragen.erklaerung_en: If PFD indications are unreliable, ground speed on the PFD and GPS altitude can be used as a reference; FPA, FPV, altitude and VS may also be unreliable.

fragen.frage: (E1) Autoland: Oberhalb welcher Höhe soll bei einer im Final Approach erkannten Flight-Controls-Störung ein Go-around eingeleitet werden?

kontext:
3.0.3 Malfunctions during Approach

Any airplane malfunction requiring crew action below 1000 ft AFE under IMC should lead to a go-around.
Malfunctions above 1000 ft AFE are to be evaluated by the crew.

It should lead to a go-around if necessary procedures cannot be completed before reaching 1000 ft.

Note: In case of any failure that affects the flight director approach mode

or the ability to continue the same approach category, the decision

to continue on a downgraded approach category must be made if approach minimums have been set at or above 500 ft AFE.

In case of a go-around, follow the normal go-around procedure. A new approach may only be performed when the appropriate action is accomplished and malfunction consequences properly evaluated.

In case aileron stiffness is experienced but roll control is not lost, flight crew may elect to continue the flight normally. If roll capability is compromised, perform the JAMMED CONTROL WHEEL (ROLL) abnormal procedure. Although aileron stiffness is more susceptible to occur on the descent and approach phase, the preceding recommendation is valid for all phases of flight.
For Autoland, a go-around should be initiated in case flight controls malfunctions are identified on final approach above 50 ft.

Following an Autothrottle failure below 500 ft, the approach may be continued if

the airspeed is under control and stabilized.

fragen.frage: (E1) Abnormal Slat/Flap Configuration: Wie lang soll der Final Approach mindestens sein?

kontext:
3.7.2 Abnormal Slat Flap Configuration

If flap or slat fails at a specific position, select the desired flap or slat position and use data according to QRH configuration tables. The best performance combination of Slat/Flap is the one that results in the lowest speed.

The following items are valid for all abnormal Slat/Flap configuration approaches and landings:

use of autopilot is recommended

if possible reduce gross weight to lowest practicable (burn off fuel) to

reduce VREF

check landing distance (select the longest runway available)

limit bank angle to 20° maximum when maneuvering for landing

establish a long final approach, at least 8 NM at recommended speed

attitude and speed are higher than normal

establish landing configuration early, flight large patterns and long final

plan touchdown at 1000 ft touchdown zone, a go-around should be

made if landing occurs beyond touchdown zone flare enough just to reduce the rate of descent, do not float and touchdown at the normal touchdown zone

over threshold set thrust levers to IDLE

after touchdown, apply forward control column, reverse thrust and

brakes without delay
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Abnormal Slat/Flap Configuration: What is the minimum length of the final approach?

At least 8 NM at the recommended speed
fragen.erklaerung_en: For approaches with an abnormal slat/flap configuration, a long final approach of at least 8 NM at the recommended speed must be established.

If flap or slat fails at a specific position, select the desired flap or slat position and use data according to QRH configuration tables. The best performance combination of Slat/Flap is the one that results in the lowest speed.

The following items are valid for all abnormal Slat/Flap configuration approaches and landings:

use of autopilot is recommended

if possible reduce gross weight to lowest practicable (burn off fuel) to

reduce VREF

check landing distance (select the longest runway available)

limit bank angle to 20° maximum when maneuvering for landing

establish a long final approach, at least 8 NM at recommended speed

attitude and speed are higher than normal

establish landing configuration early, flight large patterns and long final

plan touchdown at 1000 ft touchdown zone, a go-around should be

made if landing occurs beyond touchdown zone flare enough just to reduce the rate of descent, do not float and touchdown at the normal touchdown zone

over threshold set thrust levers to IDLE

after touchdown, apply forward control column, reverse thrust and

brakes without delay

The one with the largest flap setting
The one with the least drag
The one that corresponds to the go-around configuration

fragen.frage: (E1) Overweight Landing: Welche maximale Sinkrate gilt beim Aufsetzen?
antworten: 200 ft/min
300 ft/min
500 ft/min
600 ft/min
fragen.erklaerung: Bei einer Overweight Landing beträgt die maximale Sinkrate beim Aufsetzen 300 ft/min.
fragen.zitat: The maximum rate of descend is 300 ft/min at touchdown. Use maximum reverse thrust down to 60 kt.
kontext:
3.15.1 Overweight Landing

Overweight landing may safely be accomplished by using normal landing procedures and techniques. There are no adverse handling characteristics

associated with heavier than normal landing weights.

Select the longest available runway, when feasible. Also consider the effects of runway slope and wind effect.

Where possible avoid landing in tailwinds, on runways with negative slope or

runways with less than normal braking conditions.
Reduce the landing weight as much as possible. To save time and at pilot's discretion, it can be done using high drag configuration (landing gear and/or speed brake) and flying at a lower altitude (respect MORA and MSA).
Wind additives may be impacted by flap placard speeds.
At weights above the maximum landing weight, the maximum wind correction in the final approach may be limited by the flap maneuvering speed.
Configure the airplane earlier so there is more time to get used to the higher approach speeds. Do not carry the excess of airspeed on final.
It is recommended to land under VMC. There is more time to focus on the handling of the airplane rather than on the instruments panel.

Brake energy is not exceeded for flaps 5 or FULL landing at all gross weights.
Although, give special attention to wet or slippery runways. The brake energy limits may be exceeded when landing at high gross weights at speeds associated with nonnormal procedures requiring flaps set at 5 or less.

Try a smooth landing. In the other hand, do not allow the airplane to float above the runway. If a long landing is likely to occur, consider a go-around.

The maximum rate of descend is 300 ft/min at touchdown.

Use maximum reverse thrust down to 60 kt.

If stop capability is in doubt use it until certain that the airplane stops within

limitations. Use brakes consistent with runway length. Autobrakes may be used.
Maintenance inspection is required after landing

(report AGW and rate of descent on the TLB).

Note: Alert ground crew if brake temperature is too high.

antworten_en: 200 ft/min
300 ft/min
500 ft/min
600 ft/min
fragen.erklaerung_en: For an Overweight Landing, the maximum rate of descent at touchdown is 300 ft/min.

kontext:
3.0.1 Technical Malfunction Handling Flow Chart

The QRG provides general guidance for managing technical malfunctions during daily operations. The flowchart supports a systematic approach to malfunction handling by ensuring effective use of all available resources.

When time permits, the flow shall be applied after completion of the applicable QRH procedures.

Note:
Whenever the MEL EICAS list is used during the procedure, the dispatch condition must be verified with MCC before actual dispatch.

Alternatively, dispatch is granted without further troubleshooting for

messages highlighted in gray on the list, but the related MEL item may still require maintenance or flight crew action. Further information can be found in the respective MEL.

fragen.frage: (E1) Emergency Descent: Mit welcher maximalen Querneigung darf eine Kurve eingeleitet werden?
fragen.erklaerung: Beim Emergency Descent wird geradeaus gesunken oder eine Kurve mit maximal 30° Querneigung eingeleitet.
fragen.zitat: Crew must descend straight ahead or initiate turn with maximum 30° bank. HDG mode can be used to turn the airplane off the airway, it is recommended to start a turn before commencing the Emergency Descent.
kontext:
DESCENDING WITH AUTOPILOT ENGAGED

Use of automated resources is recommended.
FLCH mode is recommended vertical mode due to airspeed and altitude protection, as well as low crew workload.
If crew performs an emergency descent, alert the maneuver via PA. Select

10000 ft ASL or MEA, whichever is higher, and select FLCH. If VNAV is engaged, press VNAV button on the guidance panel, and then press FLCH.

Set or verify thrust levers IDLE and extend speedbrake. Select SPEED Knob to MANUAL and target speed to maximum appropriate. If structural integrity is in

doubt, especially after an explosive depressurization, use flight controls with

care, and maintain current speed.

Crew must descend straight ahead or initiate turn with maximum 30° bank. HDG mode can be used to turn the airplane off the airway, it is recommended to start a turn before commencing the Emergency Descent.

Set FSTN BELTS switch and External Light LANDING switches to ON.
Advise ATC (EMERGENCY DESCENT), monitor cabin altitude, squawk 7700 on transponder and check all instrument and engines parameters.
If flying in RVSM airspace, notify ATC and follow the appropriate RVSM contingency procedure. Use TCAS as a reference in this situation.
If cabin reaches 14500 ft or above, set immediately MASKS DEPLOY selector to
OVRD.

During descent, crew must perform the EMERGENCY CHECKLIST. The flight

profile must be monitored, and TERRAIN set on MFD. At 2000 ft above the level off altitude, crew must reduce speed to 250 kt or appropriate speed. At 1000 ft above the level off altitude crew must close the speedbrake.
Altitude callouts are performed every 10000 ft (30000 ft 20000 ft 10000 ft) by

the PM to check crew awareness.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Emergency Descent: What maximum bank angle may be used when initiating a turn?
fragen.erklaerung_en: During an Emergency Descent, the descent is flown straight ahead or a turn with a maximum of 30° bank is initiated.

fragen.frage: (E1) Manueller Emergency Descent: Auf welche initiale Sinkflug-Fluglage wird die Nase abgesenkt?

Ca. 15° nose down
Ca. 10° nose down

fragen.zitat: To start descending, smoothly lower the nose to initial descent attitude (approximately 10 degrees nose down).
kontext:
MANUAL DESCENT

Exceptionally, an emergency descent can be performed manually, but additional recommendations must be considered due to an expected high crew workload.
After selecting 10000 ft ASL or MEA, whichever is higher, crew must disconnect the autothrottle and set thrust settings to idle. Then, smoothly open speedbrake and turn FD OFF.

If flying in RVSM airspace, pilot shall notify ATC and follow the appropriate

RVSM contingency procedure. Use TCAS as a reference in this situation.

To start descending, smoothly lower the nose to initial descent attitude

(approximately 10 degrees nose down).

Approximately 10 kt before achieving

target speed (VMO/MMO), slowly adjust pitch attitude to maintain this speed. If structural integrity is in doubt, especially after an explosive depressurization, use flight controls with care, and maintain current speed.
For better airplane speed and thrust control, it is recommended to use FLIGHT PATH VECTOR SPEED ERROR TAPE and FPA ACCELERATION POINTER chevron.
If cabin reaches 14500 ft, set immediately MASKS DEPLOY selector to OVRD.
Altitude callouts are performed by crew member every 10000 ft during descent to check crew situational awareness. At 2000 ft above the level off altitude, crew must reduce speed to 250 kt or appropriate speed. At 1000 ft above the level off altitude crew must close the speed brake.

fragen.frage: (E1) Innerhalb welcher Zeit soll die Crew-Sauerstoffmaske gemäss Konstruktion angelegt werden können?
antworten: 3 Sekunden
10 Sekunden
15 Sekunden
5 Sekunden
fragen.erklaerung: Die Maske ist so konstruiert, dass sie innerhalb von 5 Sekunden angelegt werden kann.
fragen.zitat: Releasing the button deflates the harness firmly fitting it to the head. The mask is designed to be donned within 5 seconds.
kontext:
LOSS OF ALTITUDE

If descending due to cabin depressurization, the crew members should don masks and establish communication immediately.
Opening the mask stowage box automatically initiates the oxygen flow. Pressing the harness inflation control valve inflates the harness, enabling its quick donning.

Releasing the button deflates the harness firmly fitting it to the head.
The mask is designed to be donned within 5 seconds.

When the oxygen mask stowage box is opened the mask microphone is

automatically activated and the headset boom microphone is deactivated.
The speakers are also automatically activated and the communication reception is possible through the speakers or the headsets.

Oxygen masks are operated at three selectable modes: The NORMAL provides supplemental oxygen, diluted with cabin air. It is capable to maintain a safe

physiologic level until a preset altitude, where the user inhales 100% oxygen.

The 100% mode is mandatory during an emergency descent, as it is not diluted

with cabin air, regardless cabin altitude. The EMER mode is useful to remove

smoke and fumes, as it is no diluted oxygen regardless of cabin altitude with a slightly positive pressure. When the mask is on emergency mode, the air pressure and flow make communication more difficult. To avoid communication

disruption, it is recommended not to use the EMER setting continuously. Select

the mode back to 100% or Normal after the mask is clear of smoke, fumes, or condensation.

Once mask usage is not necessary, pilots must close the oxygen mask stowage box and press reset button, enabling hand/headset microphone booms.

antworten_en: 3 seconds
10 seconds
15 seconds
5 seconds
fragen.erklaerung_en: The mask is designed so that it can be donned within 5 seconds.

kontext: “BRACE, BRACE”.
Plan to land with maximum flap available and burn off fuel to a minimum onboard to increase buoyancy. Leave the gear UP.

Consider landing parallel to waves taking in account wind direction and sea

condition. If at all possible, land parallel to the swell, not across it.
The best location is along the crest of the swell which minimizes the chance of a

wingtip digging into the water. Second best is in the trough or bottom of the swell.

Maintain airspeed at VREF and 200 - 300 ft/min rate of descent or as low as possible. Rotate smoothly the attitude (approx 10° to 12° nose up) during flare and keep flying the airplane at all times until touchdown. After touchdown, reduce thrust to idle. If engine is not running, maintain minimum speed of 130 KIAS.
After the airplane has come to rest, proceed to assigned ditching stations and evacuate as soon as possible, assuring that all passengers are out of the

airplane. Note that entry into water is always considered "catastrophic" and the cabin crew can initiate evacuation without further instructions from the flight

deck.

fragen.erklaerung: Flex wird annulliert und ATTCS kommandiert RSV, u. a. wenn die N1-Differenz zwischen beiden Engines grösser als 15% ist (ausserdem bei OEI, Thrust Levers in MAX oder Windshear).
fragen.zitat: Difference between both engine N1 values is greater than 15% OEI (One Engine Inoperative) Thrust levers are moved to MAX detent Windshear is detected
kontext:
2.3.3.3.7 Flex Takeoff

This method is also known as assumed temperature takeoff thrust.
A Takeoff with less thrust than the maximum takeoff thrust is used.
When operating with flex takeoff thrust, thrust setting parameters used to establish thrust for takeoff are not considered as operating limits.

If REF ATTCS (on takeoff data setting) is set to ON and one of the following events occurs, flex takeoff is canceled and ATTCS automatically commands RSV

thrust:

Difference between both engine N1 values is greater than 15%

OEI (One Engine Inoperative)

Thrust levers are moved to MAX detent

Windshear is detected

When used with derated takeoff thrust, this method provides larger thrust reductions and may increase engine life. Less severe operation means lower:
Fuel flow degradation rate, reducing fuel burn over the on-wing life of engine

Inter Turbine Temperature (ITT) degradation rate (Increases time-on-wing)

Maintenance costs, reducing shop visit rate and cost per shop visit Note: The use of this method is prohibited on contaminated runways.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Flex Takeoff with REF ATTCS ON: At what N1 difference between the engines is Flex cancelled and RSV thrust commanded?
antworten_en: More than 5%
More than 15%
More than 10%
More than 20%
fragen.erklaerung_en: Flex is cancelled and ATTCS commands RSV, among other cases, when the N1 difference between the two engines is greater than 15% (also with OEI, thrust levers at MAX or windshear).

fragen.frage: (E1) Takeoff mit LNAV, VNAV und FMS Speeds: In welcher Höhe engagiert LNAV nach dem Takeoff?
antworten: 50 ft AGL
400 ft AGL
200 ft AGL
1000 ft AGL
fragen.erklaerung: Nach dem Takeoff engagiert LNAV bei 200 ft AGL; VNAV engagiert in der im MCDU gesetzten Höhe.
fragen.zitat: After takeoff, LNAV engages at 200 ft AGL and VNAV engages at the height set on MCDU.
kontext: 2.3.3.3.5 Takeoff with LNAV, VNAV and FMS Speeds
After takeoff, LNAV engages at 200 ft AGL and VNAV engages at the height set on MCDU.

Autopilot can be engaged at the minimum engagement height even if the first vertical mode (VFLCH on this case) is not active.

In case of engine failure or fire on takeoff, the FMS automatically detects the failure and the logic associated with EO AUTO starts. The logic includes EO

VNAV capture height, FLCH, LNAV engaged with Bank Angle limitation and appropriate FMS target speeds. If an Engine Out SID exists, a modified flight

plan is created pending for activation.

Note: When using VNAV, if any altitude constraint is presented on the MCDU and ATC clears to climb with no restrictions, use CLB DIR prompt to avoid an unintended level off.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Takeoff with LNAV, VNAV and FMS speeds: At what height does LNAV engage after takeoff?
antworten_en: 50 ft AGL
400 ft AGL
200 ft AGL
1000 ft AGL
fragen.erklaerung_en: After takeoff, LNAV engages at 200 ft AGL; VNAV engages at the altitude set in the MCDU.

fragen.frage: (E1) Der F-BUG verschwindet, bevor die Slat/Flap Retraction abgeschlossen ist. Nach welcher Speed werden die Flaps weiter eingefahren?
antworten: V2 + 10 kt
Green Dot
Green Dot + 30 kt
Green Dot + 10 kt
