fragen.zitat: In case of “F-BUG” disappears before total accomplishment of Slat/Flap retraction, retract Slat/Flap following Green Dot +10 kt.
kontext:
2.3.3.3.6 Slat Flap Retraction

Flap retraction is accomplished after the specified acceleration altitude is reached. The minimum acceleration altitude for Slat/Flap retraction is 1000 ft.
The flaps should be retracted using the flap retraction speed “F-BUG” and pitch angle adjusted to maintain a slight rate of climb. After Slat/Flap retraction is complete, accelerate to enroute climb speed.
In case of “F-BUG” disappears before total accomplishment of Slat/Flap retraction, retract Slat/Flap following Green Dot +10 kt.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) The F-BUG disappears before slat/flap retraction is complete. After which speed are the flaps retracted further?
antworten_en: V2 + 10 kt
Green Dot
Green Dot + 30 kt
Green Dot + 10 kt
fragen.erklaerung_en: If the F-BUG disappears before retraction is complete, slats/flaps are retracted after Green Dot + 10 kt.

fragen.frage: (E1) Warum wird die Nose Wheel Steering während des Takeoff Roll nicht empfohlen?
antworten: Wegen ihrer hohen Wirksamkeit, die zu einer Überreaktion des Flugzeugs führen kann
Weil sie oberhalb 20 kt automatisch abgeschaltet wird
Weil sie den Autothrottle stört
Weil sie den Reifenverschleiss stark erhöht
fragen.erklaerung: Die Nose Wheel Steering ist während des Takeoff Roll wegen ihrer hohen Wirksamkeit nicht empfohlen, da sie zu Überreaktionen führen kann; gesteuert wird mit den Pedalen.
fragen.zitat: The use of nose wheel steering is not recommended during takeoff run because of its high efficiency, which might lead to airplane overreaction.
kontext:
2.3.3.3.8 Takeoff Run and Thrust Settings

Align the airplane using as reference the runway centerline. During takeoff run, pedals are used to steer the airplane.
The use of nose wheel steering is not recommended during takeoff run because of its high efficiency, which might lead to airplane overreaction.

As the groundspeed increases, the authority of nose wheel steering reduces and the rudder becomes more effective.

The takeoff (TO) mode is an FD only mode and is represented by crossbars on

the PFD. The TO mode commands the airplane to maintain a pitch attitude reference.

When the airplane lines up and is ready for takeoff, arm the AT.

Advance the thrust levers to 40% N1.
The engines should stabilize momentarily and power settings verified before both throttles are advanced beyond 50° TLA.
Advance thrust levers to TO/GA detent and verify that N1 reaches takeoff thrust (N1 target), engine parameters are normal and ATTCS set as required.
If ATTCS is ON, with thrust levers to TO/GA, ATTCS indication on EICAS changes from white to green (armed). If ATTCS indication remains white on EICAS, confirm thrust levers are set to TO/GA position.
The AT takes over above 50° TLA when advancing the thrust levers to the TO/GA detent. If any AT malfunction occurs, disconnect the AT and set the desired thrust manually. If thrust is set manually, advance thrust levers to TO/GA detent. ROLL indication changes to TRACK when the airplane is above 100 kt during takeoff

run.
The ENG TLA NOT TOGA EICAS message is displayed during the takeoff if the thrust levers are out of the TO/GA position. It happens even if the N1 has already reached the takeoff thrust (N1 target).

Make sure that the thrust levers are set to TO/GA position before 60 kt, when AT

HOLD mode is activated, to prevent this message from occurring.

If ENG TLA NOT TOGA EICAS message appears during takeoff run, PF should

advance thrust levers to TO/GA position and continue the takeoff.

After takeoff thrust is set, LSP takes control over the thrust levers until V1 is announced. The LSP is always responsible for aborting the takeoff. All

abnormalities during the takeoff run are called out in a loud and clear voice.

Note: FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL message may appear spuriously (EICAS quantity indication green) when flying with high pitch or bank angles. It happens

especially during takeoff and climb out with fuel quantity just above the expected to trigger FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL EICAS message.

OM-B E1 2 Normal Procedures
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Why is Nose Wheel Steering not recommended during the takeoff roll?
antworten_en: Because of its high effectiveness, which can lead to an overreaction of the aircraft
Because it is automatically disengaged above 20 kt
Because it interferes with the autothrottle
Because it greatly increases tire wear
fragen.erklaerung_en: Nose Wheel Steering is not recommended during the takeoff roll because of its high effectiveness, as it can lead to overreactions; steering is done with the pedals.

fragen.frage: (E1) Auf welchen Wert soll der Thrust beim Taxi möglichst begrenzt werden?
fragen.erklaerung: Aus wirtschaftlichen und Umweltgründen sowie zur FOD-Vermeidung soll der Taxi Thrust möglichst auf 40% N1 begrenzt werden; normal genügen etwa 30% N1.
fragen.zitat: it is desirable to limit the thrust to 40% N1 as much as possible. Avoid rapid accelerations and decelerations.
kontext:
2.3.1.5 Thrust Used during Taxi

Taxi is normally initiated without increasing thrust at lighter weights. Increase the thrust smoothly until the airplane starts moving to avoid setting a higher thrust than needed.

For economic and environmental reasons, FOD prevention, damage to other airplane and equipment close to the airplane,

it is desirable to limit the thrust to

40% N1 as much as possible. Avoid rapid accelerations and decelerations.

For normal operations, a setting around 30% N1 is enough for ground maneuvering.

The use of reverse thrust is not recommended during taxi.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) To what value should thrust be limited during taxi, if possible?
fragen.erklaerung_en: For economic and environmental reasons and to avoid FOD, taxi thrust should be limited to 40% N1 if possible; approx. 30% N1 is normally sufficient.

fragen.frage: (E1) Welcher maximale Steuerwinkel steht über die Rudder Pedal Steering zur Verfügung?
fragen.erklaerung: Die Rudder Pedal Steering erlaubt maximal +/- 7°; für grössere Kurven wird die Handwheel Steering verwendet.
fragen.zitat: For straight ahead taxiing or for small changes of direction, the use of rudder pedal steering mode may be used. The maximum steering angle of rudder pedal is +/- 7°.
kontext: 2.3.1.6 Rudder Steering use and Turning Radius
For straight ahead taxiing or for small changes of direction, the use of rudder pedal steering mode may be used. The maximum steering angle of rudder pedal is 7°.

At speeds between 20 kt and 40 kt use the steering handle only if necessary and exercise care as at these speeds the steering handle is very responsive.
Handwheel steering mode should be used for wider turn angles. To operate in this mode the handle must be kept pressed otherwise the system reverts to rudder pedals. Whenever the handle is pressed, the system reverts back to the handwheel steering. The wheel deflection as function of handle deflection is not linear. For detailed information refer to AOM section 14-13.

Let the airplane move a little forward before starting a turn and avoid stopping the airplane in a turn as excessive thrust is required to start taxiing again. After completing a turn and before stopping, center the nosewheel and allow the airplane to roll straight ahead for a short distance.

Nosewheel skidding may occur with:

excessive steering angle

high taxi speed during turns

on wet surfaces during turn

When taxiing, make turns with the largest feasible turn radius possible. The

minimum turn radius should still allow the tire closer to the center of the turn to continue rolling. When making a tight turn, the tires are subject to high lateral

loads and can experience damage. Asymmetric thrust may be used in tight turns to minimize side loads on gear and tires.

Minimize using thrust from outboard engine in 180° turn, particularly if outboard engine overhangs dusty areas next to the taxiway.

Depending on each airplane model, the tail tip or the wingtip have the largest arc

while turning and determines the minimum obstruction clearance path.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) What maximum steering angle is available via Rudder Pedal Steering?
fragen.erklaerung_en: Rudder Pedal Steering allows a maximum of +/- 7°; for larger turns, Handwheel Steering is used.

fragen.frage: (E1) Mit welcher Rotationsrate wird bei VR rotiert, um einen Tail Strike zu vermeiden?
antworten: Ca. 1°/sec
Ca. 5°/sec
Ca. 6°/sec
Ca. 3°/sec
fragen.erklaerung: Die Rotation wird bei VR mit etwa 3°/sec sanft in Richtung des Flight-Director-Winkels eingeleitet.
fragen.zitat: Initiate rotation at VR at approximately 3°/sec, smoothly, towards the flight director angle.
kontext:
2.3.3.3.12 Tail Strike Considerations

Although tail strikes are more common during landing phase of flight, it may also occur during takeoff and may cause extensive structural damage. The major causes identified of a tail strike during takeoffs are:
Improper Stabilizer Trim

A mistrimmed stabilizer may be a result of an erroneous input data, like loading weights for load sheet calculation, or even an incorrect stab trim

setting. In any case, the stabilizer could be wrongly set to nose up which may induce the airplane attempting to fly before V1.

Improper Rotation Speed

Wrong speed computations or early rotation could result in nose up without wing lift enough to fly exposing the airplane to a tail strike.
Excessive Rotation Rate
Initiate rotation at VR at approximately 3°/sec, smoothly, towards the flight director angle.
Rotation at a pitch higher than normal and inappropriate flight director use during rotation increase the risk of tail strike.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) At what rotation rate is the aircraft rotated at VR to avoid a tail strike?
antworten_en: Approx. 1°/sec
Approx. 5°/sec
Approx. 6°/sec
Approx. 3°/sec
fragen.erklaerung_en: Rotation is initiated smoothly at VR at approx. 3°/sec toward the flight director angle.

fragen.frage: (E1) Bis zu welcher Höhe ist die Tail Strike Avoidance (TSA) Funktion beim Takeoff aktiv?
antworten: 20 ft
10 ft
35 ft
50 ft
fragen.erklaerung: Die TSA-Funktion ist beim Takeoff bis 20 ft aktiv; sie schützt jedoch nicht vor einer stark übertriebenen Rotation.
fragen.zitat: TSA function is not capable to protect the airplane from tail strikes in over abused rotation. TSA function is enabled up to 20 ft during takeoff operation.
kontext:
TAIL STRIKE AVOIDANCE (TSA)

Tail Strike Avoidance (TSA) function is a fly-by-wire feature to avoid tail strikes.
During Takeoff TSA function controls airplane pitch angle by reducing control column authority in the nose up direction.

TSA function is not capable to protect the airplane from tail strikes in over

abused rotation.
TSA function is enabled up to 20 ft during takeoff operation.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Up to what height is the Tail Strike Avoidance (TSA) function active during takeoff?
antworten_en: 20 ft
10 ft
35 ft
50 ft
fragen.erklaerung_en: The TSA function is active during takeoff up to 20 ft; however, it does not protect against a grossly exaggerated rotation.

fragen.frage: (E1) Unterhalb welcher Speed steht beim Taxi kein Antiskid-Schutz zur Verfügung?
antworten: 5 kt
10 kt
20 kt
30 kt
fragen.erklaerung: Unterhalb 10 kt besteht kein Antiskid-Schutz; die Brakes sind entsprechend zu betätigen.
fragen.zitat: Antiskid protection is not provided below 10 kt, so apply brakes accordingly.
kontext:
2.3.1.8 Taxi Under Adverse Weather

Taxi on a wet or contaminated surface requires lower speeds.
Use the nose wheel steering with caution to avoid skidding during turns.

During cold weather, use minimum thrust for breakaway and taxiing, to avoid blowing snow or slush on personnel or airplanes nearby.

Use firm brake pressure on taxi stops whenever pavement conditions permit in order to warm up the brakes and dry moisture buildup within the disk stack.
Antiskid protection is not provided below 10 kt, so apply brakes accordingly.

During taxi, “cold set” (the condition where the tire retains the flat shape it had while parked) may induce vibration in the airplane. Vibration should disappear as the tires recover their elasticity during taxi. Turns should be performed at the largest turning radius, preferably at a speed which does not require braking during the turn. Maintain a greater than normal distance behind other airplanes while taxiing in snow or slush-covered runways, to avoid contamination by snow blown by jet blasts.
During low visibility or unfamiliar airport operation observe the ground markings and consider requesting a FOLLOW ME vehicle to proceed taxiing safely.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Below what speed is no antiskid protection available during taxi?
antworten_en: 5 kt
10 kt
20 kt
30 kt
fragen.erklaerung_en: Below 10 kt there is no antiskid protection; the brakes must be applied accordingly.

fragen.frage: (E1) Bis zu welcher Speed ist die Rudder Control beim Ausrollen ungefähr wirksam?
antworten: Ca. 30 kt
Ca. 80 kt
Ca. 60 kt
Ca. 100 kt
fragen.erklaerung: Die Rudder Control ist bis etwa 60 kt wirksam; die Rudder Pedal Steering genügt für die Richtungskontrolle beim Ausrollen.
fragen.zitat: Rudder control is effective to approximately 60 kt. Rudder pedal steering is enough for maintaining directional control during the rollout.
kontext:
2.6.1.2 Landing Procedure

For a normal landing procedure, establish the landing configuration, gear down and flaps, early on the final approach or at the outer marker on an ILS or FAF on a 2D-Approach. Airspeed, power and descent rate also should be stabilized early. Changes in airspeed require changes in thrust and attitude. If the airspeed is 10 kt above target approach speed, an airspeed deviation is considered

significant. Indicated airspeed may not be less than the VREF or VAP.
A significant deviation occurs in the vertical speed when it is greater than 1000 ft/min (precision approaches) or 1500 ft/min (non-precision approaches) when below 1000 ft AGL. If the stabilized approach parameters are not met before

reaching the stabilized approach height, initiate a go-around.

Make sure that the airplane is properly trimmed during the approach.
It maximizes elevator authority for the flare or in the event of a missed approach.
Target approach speed is VAP, which is VREF plus wind correction.
As the airplane approaches the touch down point, initiate the flare approximately at 20 ft to 10 ft. Reduce the rate of descent and slowly reduce thrust levers to idle. Plan the flare so that thrust levers are at idle when the airplane touches

down. Normally a 2° to 3° pitch change is enough for the flare.
Plan to touchdown at the runway touchdown zone, which is typically located

1000 ft ahead from the runway threshold. Monitor the final approach path using

all reference available. Do not allow the airplane to float in ground effect, which

unnecessarily increases the landing distance and risk of a tail strike.

After main wheel touches down, use autobrake or apply manual braking as required for the runway condition and length available while easing the nosewheel onto the runway. Pull the thrust reverser triggers and take the thrust levers to reverse.
Note: Pulling the thrust reverser triggers before airplane touchdown may jam the triggers and lock the mechanism. As a consequence, after touchdown the TLAs are not released to be moved below idle to deploy thrust reversers, causing ENG 1(2) REV TLA FAIL EICAS message.

Verify spoilers actuation. The autobrake disarms by gradually pressing brake pedals.
Use reverse thrust consistent with runway conditions and modulate as required.

Apply thrust reversers cautiously and observe how the airplane responds before full reverse is used.
When using MAX REV thrust, maintain MAX REV until the airspeed is approximately 80 KIAS. Smoothly reduce thrust reverse from MAX REV to MIN

REV at or above 60 KIAS, and it is recommended to close them when reaching

30 KIAS. Thrust reverser is more effective at high speeds. The use of reverse

below 60 KIAS increases the chances of foreign object ingestion by the engine. If

necessary, use the thrust reversers until the airplane comes to a complete stop.
Rudder control is effective to approximately 60 kt. Rudder pedal steering is enough for maintaining directional control during the rollout.

Do not use the nosewheel steering tiller until reaching taxi speed.

As soon as the airplane leaves the runway, turns off the strobe lights.

However, LDG LIGHTS are switched off, the nose taxi light must remain on throughout the taxi regardless of the time of the day.

Note: Performance values calculated by the performance tool (ePerf)

considers the threshold is crossed at the screen height and at VREF or according to the inputted reference speed

fragen.frage: (E1) Autobrake: Die Bremswirkung ist gut und die Autobrake-Verzögerung wird erreicht. Was gilt für die Thrust Reverser?
antworten: Sie verkürzen die Landing Distance dennoch deutlich und sind immer auf MAX REV zu setzen.
Ihre Verwendung ist dann nicht wirksam, da das Autobrake auf eine konstante Verzögerung regelt.
Sie müssen verwendet werden, da das Autobrake sonst disengaged.
Sie dürfen erst unter 60 KIAS verwendet werden.
fragen.erklaerung: Das Autobrake regelt auf eine konstante Verzögerung; bei guter Bremswirkung und erreichtem Verzögerungsziel ist der Einsatz der Thrust Reverser nicht wirksam.
fragen.zitat: The autobrake works aiming a constant deceleration rate. When the braking capability is good and the autobrake deceleration target is reached, the use of thrust reversers is not effective.
kontext:
2.6.1.4.1 Autobrake

With autobrake set to LO, MED or HI verify after touchdown the normal operation of the braking system and proper deceleration of the airplane.
At 80 kt, press the brakes pedal to disengage the autobrake and use the necessary braking force to reach a safe taxi speed.

Note: At pilot’s discretion, disengage the autobrake after touchdown at any speed by pressing the brakes pedals.
During the landing roll, if autobrake deceleration is not suitable for the stopping

distance, use manual braking as required. Apply continuous increasing pressure

to the brake pedals. Use manual braking as soon as possible to achieve maximum deceleration. Pilot must be alert for autobrake disengagement

indications during the landing roll. At pilot’s discretion, use reverse thrust with

manual braking or autobrake during landing roll until a safe speed is reached.

The autobrake works aiming a constant deceleration rate. When the braking capability is good and the autobrake deceleration target is reached, the use of

thrust reversers is not effective.

They must be used, otherwise the autobrake disengages.
They may be used only below 60 KIAS.
fragen.erklaerung_en: The autobrake regulates to a constant deceleration; with good braking action and the deceleration target achieved, the use of thrust reversers is not effective.

kontext:
2.6.1.4.2 Emergency Parking Brake

Some Emergency and Abnormal procedures require the pilot to use the Emergency Parking Brake to stop the airplane during landing.
When this event happens, the following protections are not available:
Locked Wheel Protection,

Antiskid Protection, and

Touchdown Protection.

At high speeds, apply the Emergency Parking Brake handle to stop the airplane monitoring the Emergency Parking Brake light and maintain steady pressure.
The brake system provides enough pressure to start braking.
As speed decreases the required handle deflection increases to maintain continuous braking.
If a tire burst occurs applying the Emergency Parking Brake, do not release the Emergency Parking Brake handle until the airplane stops.

CAUTION: Avoid landing on runways with RWYCC 4 through 1.

For Emergency and Abnormal procedures that require the use of the Emergency/Parking Brake to stop the airplane, landing on contaminated runways (RWYCC 4 through 1) should be avoided, as the airplane may skid during landing roll. Such procedures only present landing performance data for RWYCC

6 (DRY) and 5 (GOOD).

fragen.zitat: If the airspeed is 10 kt above target approach speed, an airspeed deviation is considered significant. Indicated airspeed may not be less than the VREF or VAP.
kontext:
2.6.1.2 Landing Procedure

For a normal landing procedure, establish the landing configuration, gear down and flaps, early on the final approach or at the outer marker on an ILS or FAF on a 2D-Approach. Airspeed, power and descent rate also should be stabilized early. Changes in airspeed require changes in thrust and attitude.

If the airspeed is 10 kt above target approach speed, an airspeed deviation is considered

significant. Indicated airspeed may not be less than the VREF or VAP.

A significant deviation occurs in the vertical speed when it is greater than 1000 ft/min (precision approaches) or 1500 ft/min (non-precision approaches) when below 1000 ft AGL. If the stabilized approach parameters are not met before

reaching the stabilized approach height, initiate a go-around.

Make sure that the airplane is properly trimmed during the approach.
It maximizes elevator authority for the flare or in the event of a missed approach.
Target approach speed is VAP, which is VREF plus wind correction.
As the airplane approaches the touch down point, initiate the flare approximately at 20 ft to 10 ft. Reduce the rate of descent and slowly reduce thrust levers to idle. Plan the flare so that thrust levers are at idle when the airplane touches

down. Normally a 2° to 3° pitch change is enough for the flare.
Plan to touchdown at the runway touchdown zone, which is typically located

1000 ft ahead from the runway threshold. Monitor the final approach path using

all reference available. Do not allow the airplane to float in ground effect, which

unnecessarily increases the landing distance and risk of a tail strike.

After main wheel touches down, use autobrake or apply manual braking as required for the runway condition and length available while easing the nosewheel onto the runway. Pull the thrust reverser triggers and take the thrust levers to reverse.
Note: Pulling the thrust reverser triggers before airplane touchdown may jam the triggers and lock the mechanism. As a consequence, after touchdown the TLAs are not released to be moved below idle to deploy thrust reversers, causing ENG 1(2) REV TLA FAIL EICAS message.

Verify spoilers actuation. The autobrake disarms by gradually pressing brake pedals.
Use reverse thrust consistent with runway conditions and modulate as required.

Apply thrust reversers cautiously and observe how the airplane responds before full reverse is used.
When using MAX REV thrust, maintain MAX REV until the airspeed is approximately 80 KIAS. Smoothly reduce thrust reverse from MAX REV to MIN

REV at or above 60 KIAS, and it is recommended to close them when reaching

30 KIAS. Thrust reverser is more effective at high speeds. The use of reverse

below 60 KIAS increases the chances of foreign object ingestion by the engine. If

necessary, use the thrust reversers until the airplane comes to a complete stop.

Rudder control is effective to approximately 60 kt. Rudder pedal steering is enough for maintaining directional control during the rollout. Do not use the nosewheel steering tiller until reaching taxi speed.

As soon as the airplane leaves the runway, turns off the strobe lights.

However, LDG LIGHTS are switched off, the nose taxi light must remain on throughout the taxi regardless of the time of the day.

Note: Performance values calculated by the performance tool (ePerf)

considers the threshold is crossed at the screen height and at VREF or according to the inputted reference speed

OM-B E1 2 Normal Procedures

2.2.3.2.4 Abnormal Engine Start Indications

Although FADEC provides automatic over-temperature protection and will automatically abort the start in the event of a hot start, hot restart or hung start, the engine start must be manually aborted when:

no positive oil pressure indication within 10 seconds after N2 speed starts to increase

during engine start with tailwind, if a positive increase of N1 is not indicated

before starter cutout (50% N2). In this case the airplaneshould be

repositioned prior to engine start to minimize tailwindeffects
if ITT does not rise within 1 minute after the fuel is applied (15 s after fuel is reapplied)

ITT exceeds start limit (hot start) if oil pressure stabilizes below the engine limits N1 and/or N2 failing to accelerate to stable idle speed (hung start). an intermittent electrical pneumatic or starter malfunction occurs before the starter disengagement

Note: In case an automatic abort occurs or engine start is manually aborted due to abnormal engine indications, its cause must be investigated and corrected before further attempts to start the engines.

The FADEC commands an automatic abort when ITT is 10°C lower than the

engine hot start limit. This will prevent ENG EXCEEDANCE EICAS message to be displayed. In this case, two additional engine starts are allowed without any cause investigation.
One additional engine start is allowed when engine start is manually aborted

due to no ITT rising 15 seconds after fuel is reapplied, and "ENG 1(2) NO

DISPATCH" or "ENG 1(2) SHORT DISPATCH" EICAS messages are not

displayed.

An engine dry motoring is recommended to purge any residual fuel or to reduce engine temperature.

engine start is manually aborted after fuel flow application and it is

a tailpipe fire is observed

fragen.frage: (E1) Welche Climb Speed wird empfohlen, um tiefliegende Turbulenz zu durchsteigen?
antworten: Green Dot + 50 kt
Green Dot
Green Dot + 10 kt
250 kt
fragen.erklaerung: Für Wetterbedingungen wird Green Dot + 50 kt empfohlen, um Turbulenz in tiefen Höhen zu durchsteigen; für Hindernisfreiheit gilt Green Dot bis MSA.
fragen.zitat: Weather Conditions: recommended Green Dot +50 kt to clear low altitude turbulence;
kontext:
Weather Conditions: recommended Green Dot +50 kt to clear low

altitude turbulence;

Specific Regulations: use the local limitation;

If the takeoff heading offset from the route track over 120°, it is recommended to use Green Dot until reaching a heading within 30° from the desired track

If none of the preceding considerations are applicable or have been cleared, accelerate to the altitude limited airspeed (usually 250 kt below 10000 ft) or climb speed.

If FMS speeds are in accordance with the desired speeds, select the SPEED Knob to FMS on the Guidance Panel if it was not previously selected.
The FMS speeds are default to the guidance mentioned below. If a different speed is required, the change is made on the PERF CLIMB page or on the PERFORMANCE INIT page.

Up to 10000 ft: 250 kt.
Above 10000 ft: 290 kt up to the IAS/MACH transition then Mach 0.75.

High-speed climbs can significantly increase fuel burn, as the flight time in a high thrust, higher drag condition is prolonged.

To avoid TCAS Resolution Advisories during level offs, monitor the rate of climb

when traffic exists in close vicinity of the adjacent flight level. Reduce the vertical

speed to 1500 ft/min or less at least 1000 ft before reaching the cleared flight

level.
Speed for Maximum Climb Angle

With flaps retracted, the recommended best Angle of Climb Speed for all

operational gross weights and takeoff altitudes is the Green Dot.
It provides for a maximum altitude gain at a minimum ground distance.

Speed for Maximum Rate of Climb

Maximum rate of climb (MROC) speed provides a maximum altitude gain in a minimum flight time, with flaps retracted and all operational gross weights.

Green Dot added by 50 KIAS is approximately the maximum rate of climb speed.
It is a function of gross weight and altitude. For accurate speeds and Mach

number, refer to AOM.

Green Dot
Green Dot + 10 kt
250 kt

Um 29000 ft
Um 31000 ft

kontext:
2.3.5.5 Enroute Climb

In general, the enroute climb speeds are attained as soon as practical to improve the flight efficiency, even at altitudes below 10000 ft where the local rules allow.
Usually a constant IAS is selected as enroute climb speed. This IAS is maintained until a certain altitude where the IAS intercepts a selected Mach

number. The Mach number is maintained until cruise altitude.

The altitude where the speed reference changes from IAS to Mach number is

called “crossover altitude” and is around 29000 ft.

fragen.frage: (E1) Yaw Trimming mit Autopilot: Wie viel Zeit soll zwischen den Betätigungen des YAW Trim Controllers gelassen werden?
antworten: Ca. eine Sekunde
Ca. zehn Sekunden
Ca. drei bis fünf Sekunden
Ca. dreissig Sekunden
fragen.erklaerung: Um Übertrimmen zu vermeiden, sollen zwischen den Betätigungen etwa drei bis fünf Sekunden liegen und die Wirkung beobachtet werden.
fragen.zitat: To avoid over trimming, allow approximately three to five seconds between actuations and observe the results.
kontext:
TRIMMING TECHNIQUE

Yaw Trimming:
With the autopilot engaged, ensure that the fuel is properly balanced, engine thrust is symmetric, and HDG mode is selected.
Proper monitoring of the Sky Pointer, Roll Pointer and Slip/Skid Indicator is fundamental for a correct airplane trimming.
The YAW Trim Controller is actuated in the direction that corresponds to the Slip/Skid Indicator position. In most cases, only small and brief actuations are enough.
To avoid over trimming, allow approximately three to five seconds between actuations and observe the results.

As the Slip/Skid Indicator gets closer to the

center (below the Roll Pointer) only sharp, brisk actuations are required.

Roll Trimming:
Roll trimming should be performed after the airplane has been trimmed for yaw.

An exception to this rule would be a wing heavy condition in manual flight when the slip/skid indicator is centered.

In this case, actuate the ROLL Trim Switch in the same direction where the pilot

input is required, or towards the down side of the control wheel. Both parts of the ROLL Trim Switch must be pressed simultaneously and in most cases, only sharp, brisk movements are required.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Yaw trimming with autopilot: How much time should be allowed between inputs of the YAW Trim Controller?
antworten_en: Approx. one second
Approx. ten seconds
Approx. three to five seconds
Approx. thirty seconds
fragen.erklaerung_en: To avoid over-trimming, approx. three to five seconds should be allowed between inputs and the effect observed.

fragen.frage: (E1) In schwerer Turbulenz wird der Autopilot getrennt. Was hat beim manuellen Fliegen Priorität?
antworten: Zuerst die Höhe exakt halten, dann die Fluglage
Zuerst die Speed exakt halten, auch mit grossen Pitch-Änderungen
Zuerst den Kurs halten, dann die Fluglage
Zuerst die Fluglage kontrollieren, dann Speed, Höhe und Kurs korrigieren
fragen.erklaerung: Wird manuell geflogen, wird zuerst die Fluglage kontrolliert und erst danach werden Speed, Höhe und Kurs korrigiert.
fragen.zitat: In this case, control the airplane attitude first, then make corrections for airspeed, altitude, and heading.
kontext:
2.4.1.9 Turbulent Air Penetration

Flight through severe turbulence must be avoided. If not possible, reduce altitude to increase buffet margin and accomplish the recommended procedure for turbulent air penetration as described in 2.8.3.3 - Turbulent Air Penetration.
The following recommendations also apply when flying through severe

turbulence:

the use of Autopilot is recommended when flying in severe turbulence. At

pilot’s discretion, the autopilot may be disengaged, reverting to manual flight.

In this case, control the airplane attitude first, then make corrections for

airspeed, altitude, and heading.

Corrective actions to regain the desired attitude should be smooth.

during climb or descent with variations in indicated airspeed, the use of FLCH mode may result in airplane pitch changes. The use of FPA mode is recommended to maintain airplane attitude.

OM-B E1 2 Normal Procedures
fragen.frage_en: (E1) The autopilot disconnects in severe turbulence. What has priority when flying manually?
antworten_en: First maintain altitude exactly, then attitude
First maintain speed exactly, even with large pitch changes
First maintain heading, then attitude
First control attitude, then correct speed, altitude and heading
fragen.erklaerung_en: When flying manually, attitude is controlled first and only then are speed, altitude and heading corrected.

kontext:
2.4.1.10 RVSM

Before entering RVSM airspace, the flight crew should review the status of the required equipment.
If any required equipment fails before entering RVSM airspace, a new ATC clearance should be obtained.

While flying in RVSM airspace:

crew should increase the vigilance to prevent deviations from the assigned flight level

when changing flight levels, the airplane should not overshoot or

undershoot FL by more than 45 m (150 ft)

the autopilot should be operative and engaged during level cruise, except for circumstances such as the need to re-trim the airplane or when it must be disengaged due to turbulence

crew should notify ATC of contingencies (equipment failures, weather conditions) which affect the ability to maintain the current flight level

if unable to notify ATC and to obtain clearance before deviating from the cleared flight level, follow established contingency procedures.
Obtain ATC clearance as soon as possible
fragen.frage_en: (E1) Before entering RVSM airspace, required equipment fails. What must be done?

Continue the flight normally and inform ATC only in case of altitude deviations

Reset the equipment after entry

fragen.frage: (E1) Um wie viel ist der Fuel Flow im Steigflug gemäss OM-B grösser als im Reiseflug?
fragen.erklaerung: Der Fuel Flow im Steigflug ist 40% grösser als im Reiseflug; der Steigflug macht bei Kurz- und Mittelstrecken 20% bis 40% der Flugzeit aus.
fragen.zitat: For short and medium range flights, the climb represents from 20% to 40% of the trip time. The fuel flow is 40% greater than on cruise phase.
kontext:
2.3.5.4.1 General

The climb phase has a significant impact on fuel consumption.

For short and medium range flights, the climb represents from 20% to 40% of the trip time.

The fuel flow is 40% greater than on cruise phase.

When considering trip fuel, do not analyze the climb phase separately.

The impact over the total trip fuel is the best way to check a climb schedule.

For Maximum Climb Angle, Maximum Rate of Climb and Standard Speed

Schedule refer to AOM.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) By how much is the fuel flow in the climb greater than in cruise according to OM-B?
fragen.erklaerung_en: The fuel flow in the climb is 40% greater than in cruise; the climb accounts for 20% to 40% of the flight time on short- and medium-haul flights.

APU Bleed ausschalten und 3 Minuten warten
Auf 10000 ft oder MEA sinken
fragen.erklaerung: Bei BLEED APU LEAKAGE wird zuerst die APU Bleed ausgeschaltet und 3 Minuten gewartet; bleibt die Meldung, wird die APU mit dem Emergency Stop Button abgestellt.
fragen.quelle: AFM E1 4-03-02, BLEED APU LEAKAGE, Page 4
fragen.zitat: Turn the APU bleed off and wait 3 minutes. If the BLEED APU LEAK message persists, press the APU emergency stop button to turn the APU OFF.
kontext: BLEED APU LEAKAGE

Turn the APU bleed off and wait 3 minutes.
If the BLEED APU LEAK message persists, press the APU emergency stop button to turn the APU OFF.

If the BLEED APU LEAK message still persists, turn the bleed 1 and the crossbleed off and verify the BLEED 1 OFF and the XBLEED SW OFF messages displayed on
EICAS.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) BLEED APU LEAKAGE: What is the first step?
antworten_en: Press the APU Emergency Stop Button immediately
Switch off Bleed 1 and Crossbleed immediately
Switch off APU Bleed and wait 3 minutes
Descend to 10000 ft or MEA
fragen.erklaerung_en: With BLEED APU LEAKAGE, APU Bleed is switched off first and 3 minutes are allowed to elapse; if the message persists, the APU is shut down with the Emergency Stop Button.

fragen.frage: (E1) AMS CONTROLLER FAILURE: Welche Höhenbegrenzung gilt?
antworten: Maximal 31000 ft
Maximal 25000 ft; ein Pack ausschalten
Maximal 15000 ft; APU Bleed einschalten
Maximal 10000 ft oder MEA (whichever is higher); bei 10000 ft Pressurization Dump Button IN
fragen.erklaerung: Bei AMS CONTROLLER FAILURE werden Icing Conditions verlassen, die Höhe auf maximal 10000 ft oder MEA begrenzt und bei 10000 ft der Dump Button gedrückt.
fragen.quelle: AFM E1 4-03-02, AMS CONTROLLER FAILURE, Page 4
fragen.zitat: AMS CONTROLLER FAILURE Exit and avoid icing conditions and limit the altitude to 10000 ft or MEA (whichever is higher) maximum. At 10000 ft, push the pressurization dump button IN.
kontext:
AMS CONTROLLER FAILURE

Exit and avoid icing conditions and limit the altitude to 10000 ft or MEA (whichever is higher) maximum. At 10000 ft, push the pressurization dump button IN.

NOTE: - Assisted crossbleed start is not available.
- Pneumatic assisted engine start is not available.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) AMS CONTROLLER FAILURE: What altitude limitation applies?
antworten_en: Maximum 31000 ft
Maximum 25000 ft; switch off one pack
Maximum 15000 ft; APU Bleed ON
Maximum 10000 ft or MEA (whichever is higher); at 10000 ft Pressurization Dump Button IN
fragen.erklaerung_en: With AMS CONTROLLER FAILURE, icing conditions are exited, the altitude is limited to a maximum of 10000 ft or MEA, and the Dump Button is pressed at 10000 ft.

fragen.frage: (E1) FUEL IMBALANCE ohne Leckverdacht: Die FMS-Fuel-Remaining-Menge ist tiefer als die EICAS-Total-Fuel-Anzeige. Was gilt?
antworten: Die FMS-Fuel-Remaining-Information wird ignoriert; die Flügeltanks werden mit den EICAS-Anzeigen überwacht
Die EICAS-Anzeige wird ignoriert und nach FMS-Werten balanciert
Der Crossfeed wird auf OFF gestellt und asymmetrischer Thrust verwendet
Die Fuel Pumps beider Seiten werden ausgeschaltet
fragen.erklaerung: Ist die FMS-Fuel-Remaining-Menge tiefer als die EICAS-Total-Fuel-Anzeige, wird die FMS-Information ignoriert und die Menge jedes Flügeltanks mit EICAS überwacht.
fragen.zitat: If FMS fuel remaining quantity is lower than EICAS total fuel indication, disregard FMS fuel remaining information. Monitor fuel quantities of each WING tank using the EICAS indications.
kontext:
FUEL IMBALANCE

CONDITION: Imbalance between wing tanks greater than 360 kg (800 lb).
If fuel leak is suspected, accomplish the FUEL LEAK Procedure.
If fuel leak is not suspected, set the airplane attitude to wings level and compare total fuel quantity indication on EICAS with fuel remaining information indicated on FMS Fuel Management page.
If FMS fuel remaining quantity is lower than EICAS total fuel indication, disregard FMS fuel remaining information. Monitor fuel quantities of each WING tank using the EICAS indications.

If left wing presents lower level, set the crossfeed selector to LOW 1.
If right wing presents lower level, set the crossfeed selector to LOW 2.
Monitor fuel imbalance and, when the desired balance is achieved, set the crossfeed selector to OFF. Monitor total fuel indication in EICAS with FMS fuel remaining information.
NOTE: The guidance to compare the total fuel quantity indication on EICAS with fuel remaining information indicated on FMS Fuel Management page is not valid when flying with one engine inoperative. In this case only the fuel indications presented on EICAS must be used.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) FUEL IMBALANCE without suspected leak: The FMS fuel remaining quantity is lower than the EICAS total fuel indication. What applies?
antworten_en: The FMS fuel remaining information is ignored; the wing tanks are monitored using the EICAS indications
The EICAS indication is ignored and balancing is done using FMS values
The crossfeed is set to OFF and asymmetric thrust is used
The fuel pumps on both sides are switched off
fragen.erklaerung_en: If the FMS fuel remaining quantity is lower than the EICAS total fuel indication, the FMS information is ignored and the quantity of each wing tank is monitored using EICAS.

fragen.frage: (E1) CABIN DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE FAILURE: Die Druckdifferenz hat das rote Limit erreicht, die Anzeige ist negativ. Was ist zu tun?
antworten: Beide Packs ausschalten und auf 10000 ft oder MEA begrenzen
Die Sinkrate des Flugzeugs reduzieren
Den Pressurization Dump Button drücken
Auf manuelle Pressurization wechseln und die Kabine steigen lassen
fragen.erklaerung: Bei negativer Anzeige ist die Sinkrate zu reduzieren; nur bei positiver Anzeige werden beide Packs ausgeschaltet und die Höhe auf 10000 ft oder MEA begrenzt.
fragen.quelle: AFM E1 4-03-02, CABIN DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE FAILURE, Page 5
fragen.zitat: If the indication is positive, turn off both packs and limit the altitude to 10000 ft or MEA (whichever is higher) maximum. If the indication is negative, reduce the airplane descent rate.
kontext:
CABIN DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE FAILURE

If the cabin differential pressure reached the red limit, check its indication.
If the indication is positive, turn off both packs and limit the altitude to 10000 ft or MEA (whichever is higher) maximum. If the indication is negative, reduce the airplane descent rate.

ABNORMAL

PROCEDURES
fragen.frage_en: (E1) CABIN DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE FAILURE: The differential pressure has reached the red limit, the indication is negative. What must be done?
antworten_en: Switch off both packs and limit to 10000 ft or MEA
Reduce the aircraft's rate of descent
Press the Pressurization Dump Button
Switch to manual pressurization and let the cabin climb
fragen.erklaerung_en: With a negative indication, the rate of descent must be reduced; only with a positive indication are both packs switched off and the altitude limited to 10000 ft or MEA.

fragen.frage: (E1) RUDDER FAILURE: Welche Landing-Konfiguration und welche Crosswind-Einschränkung gelten?
antworten: Slat/Flap 5 und VREF FULL + 15 KIAS; Crosswind über 15 kt vermeiden
Slat/Flap FULL und VREF FULL + 10 KIAS; keine Crosswind-Einschränkung
Slat/Flap FULL und VREF FULL; Crosswind über 10 kt vermeiden
Slat/Flap 3 und VREF FULL + 20 KIAS; Crosswind über 20 kt vermeiden
fragen.erklaerung: Bei RUDDER FAILURE wird mit Slat/Flap FULL und VREF FULL gelandet; Crosswind-Komponenten über 10 kt sind zu vermeiden.
fragen.zitat: For landing configuration, set slat/flap to FULL and set VREF FULL. CAUTION: AVOID LANDING WITH CROSSWIND COMPONENTS ABOVE 10 KT. If a go around is required, proceed as a normal go around limiting the airspeed to 175 KIAS.
kontext:
LAND AT THE NEAREST SUITABLE AIRPORT.

If the failure occurs above 175 KIAS, the current airspeed is the maximum speed for the remainder of the flight.
If the failure occurs below 175 KIAS, the maximum speed for the remainder of the flight is 175 KIAS.

For landing configuration, set slat/flap to FULL and set VREF FULL.
CAUTION: AVOID LANDING WITH CROSSWIND COMPONENTS

ABOVE 10 KT.

If a go around is required, proceed as a normal go around limiting the airspeed to 175 KIAS.
NOTE: As asymmetric thrust may be required to help controlling the airplane, maximum thrust on both engines may not be possible.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) RUDDER FAILURE: What landing configuration and crosswind limitation apply?
antworten_en: Slat/Flap 5 and VREF FULL + 15 KIAS; avoid crosswind above 15 kt
Slat/Flap FULL and VREF FULL + 10 KIAS; no crosswind limitation
Slat/Flap FULL and VREF FULL; avoid crosswind above 10 kt
Slat/Flap 3 and VREF FULL + 20 KIAS; avoid crosswind above 20 kt
fragen.erklaerung_en: With RUDDER FAILURE, land with Slat/Flap FULL and VREF FULL; crosswind components above 10 kt must be avoided.

fragen.frage: (E1) ELEVATOR NORMAL MODE FAILURE: Was ist zu tun?
antworten: Elevators Button einmal resetten (IN, dann OUT) und die ELEVATOR FAULT Procedure durchführen
Den Elevator Disconnection Handle ziehen
Die Pitch Trim Cutout Buttons drücken und mit Slat/Flap 5 landen
Flight Controls Mode Elevators Button IN drücken und die ANGLE OF ATTACK LIMIT FAILURE Procedure durchführen
fragen.erklaerung: Bei ELEVATOR NORMAL MODE FAILURE wird der Elevators Mode Button IN gedrückt, die ELEVATOR FAULT Procedure nicht durchgeführt und die AOA LIMIT FAILURE Procedure ausgeführt.
fragen.quelle: AFM E1 4-03-08, ELEVATOR NORMAL MODE FAILURE, Page 3
fragen.zitat: ELEVATOR NORMAL MODE FAILURE Push the flight controls mode elevators button IN. Do not accomplish the ELEVATOR FAULT Procedure. Accomplish the ANGLE OF ATTACK LIMIT FAILURE procedure.
kontext:
ELEVATOR NORMAL MODE FAILURE

Push the flight controls mode elevators button IN. Do not accomplish the ELEVATOR FAULT Procedure.
Accomplish the ANGLE OF ATTACK LIMIT FAILURE procedure.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) ELEVATOR NORMAL MODE FAILURE: What must be done?
antworten_en: Reset the Elevators Button once (IN, then OUT) and perform the ELEVATOR FAULT procedure
Pull the Elevator Disconnection Handle
Press the Pitch Trim Cutout Buttons and land with Slat/Flap 5
Press Flight Controls Mode Elevators Button IN and perform the ANGLE OF ATTACK LIMIT FAILURE procedure
fragen.erklaerung_en: With ELEVATOR NORMAL MODE FAILURE, the Elevators Mode Button is pressed IN, the ELEVATOR FAULT procedure is not performed, and the AOA LIMIT FAILURE procedure is carried out.

fragen.frage: (E1) PITCH TRIM FAILURE: Der Pitch Trim bewegt sich auch nach dem Reset nicht. Was gilt für Cutout Buttons und Landing-Konfiguration?
antworten: Pitch Trim System 1 und 2 Cutout Buttons IN; Landing mit Slat/Flap 5 und VREF FULL + 15 KIAS
Cutout Buttons OUT lassen; Landing mit Slat/Flap FULL und VREF FULL
Nur Cutout Button 1 IN; Landing mit Slat/Flap 3 und VREF FULL + 20 KIAS
Cutout Buttons IN; Landing mit Slat/Flap FULL und VREF FULL + 10 KIAS
fragen.erklaerung: Bewegt sich der Pitch Trim nicht, werden beide Cutout Buttons hineingedrückt (kein Pitch Trim mehr); gelandet wird mit Slat/Flap 5 und VREF FULL + 15 KIAS.
fragen.quelle: AFM E1 4-03-08, PITCH TRIM FAILURE, Page 8
fragen.zitat: If pitch trim is not moving upon command, push in the pitch trim system 1 and 2 cutout buttons. No more pitch trim is available. For landing configuration, set slat/flap to 5 and set VREF FULL + 15 KIAS.
kontext:
PITCH TRIM FAILURE

If the failure occurs above 175 KIAS, the current airspeed is the maximum speed for the remainder of the flight.
If the failure occurs below 175 KIAS, the maximum speed for the remainder of the flight is 175 KIAS.
Reset (push IN, then OUT) the pitch trim system 1 and 2 cutout buttons.
Actuate pitch trim switches.

If pitch trim is not moving upon command, push in the pitch trim system 1 and 2 cutout buttons. No more pitch trim is available.
For landing configuration, set slat/flap to 5 and set
VREF FULL 15 KIAS.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) PITCH TRIM FAILURE: The pitch trim does not move even after the reset. What applies to the cutout buttons and landing configuration?
antworten_en: Pitch Trim System 1 and 2 Cutout Buttons IN; landing with Slat/Flap 5 and VREF FULL + 15 KIAS
Leave Cutout Buttons OUT; landing with Slat/Flap FULL and VREF FULL
Only Cutout Button 1 IN; landing with Slat/Flap 3 and VREF FULL + 20 KIAS
Cutout Buttons IN; landing with Slat/Flap FULL and VREF FULL + 10 KIAS
fragen.erklaerung_en: If the pitch trim does not move, both cutout buttons are pressed in (no pitch trim any more); land with Slat/Flap 5 and VREF FULL + 15 KIAS.

fragen.frage: (E1) SLAT-FLAP LEVER DISAGREE: Was ist zu tun?
antworten: Den Slat/Flap Lever bis zu dreimal zyklisch betätigen
Den Slat/Flap Lever in die vorherige Position zurückstellen und dann wie erforderlich verwenden
Die FLAP FAIL Procedure durchführen und mit Slat/Flap 5 landen
Den Slat/Flap Lever nicht mehr bewegen und mit Slat/Flap 0 landen
fragen.erklaerung: Bei SLAT-FLAP LEVER DISAGREE wird der Lever in die vorherige Position zurückgestellt und danach wie erforderlich verwendet.
fragen.quelle: AFM E1 4-03-08, SLAT-FLAP LEVER DISAGREE, Page 10
fragen.zitat: SLAT-FLAP LEVER DISAGREE Return the slat/flap lever to previous position and then use it as required.
kontext:
SLAT-FLAP LEVER DISAGREE

Return the slat/flap lever to previous position and then use it as required.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) SLAT-FLAP LEVER DISAGREE: What must be done?
antworten_en: Cycle the Slat/Flap Lever up to three times
Return the Slat/Flap Lever to the previous position and then use it as required
Perform the FLAP FAIL procedure and land with Slat/Flap 5
Do not move the Slat/Flap Lever any more and land with Slat/Flap 0
fragen.erklaerung_en: With SLAT-FLAP LEVER DISAGREE, the lever is returned to the previous position and then used as required.

fragen.frage: (E1) ELEVATOR FAULT und SPOILER FAULT werden gleichzeitig angezeigt. Wie wird vorgegangen?
antworten: Zuerst ELEVATOR FAULT, danach SPOILER FAULT
Nur ELEVATOR FAULT durchführen; SPOILER FAULT entfällt
Zuerst die SPOILER FAULT Procedure, danach ELEVATOR FAULT (Elevators Button einmal resetten)
Keine der beiden Procedures; nur die AOA LIMIT FAILURE Procedure
fragen.erklaerung: Wird zusätzlich SPOILER FAULT angezeigt, ist die SPOILER FAULT Procedure vor der ELEVATOR FAULT Procedure durchzuführen; danach wird der Elevators Mode Button einmal resettet.
fragen.zitat: ELEVATOR FAULT NOTE: If the SPOILER FAULT message is also displayed, accomplish the SPOILER FAULT procedure prior to this procedure. Reset (push IN, then OUT) the flight controls mode elevators button one time.
kontext:
ELEVATOR FAULT

NOTE: If the SPOILER FAULT message is also displayed, accomplish the SPOILER FAULT procedure prior to this procedure.
Reset (push IN, then OUT) the flight controls mode elevators button one time.
If the ELEVATOR FAULT message persists, accomplish the ANGLE OF ATTACK LIMIT FAILURE Procedure.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) ELEVATOR FAULT and SPOILER FAULT are displayed at the same time. How is this handled?
antworten_en: First ELEVATOR FAULT, then SPOILER FAULT
Perform only ELEVATOR FAULT; SPOILER FAULT is omitted
First the SPOILER FAULT procedure, then ELEVATOR FAULT (reset the Elevators Button once)
Neither procedure; only the AOA LIMIT FAILURE procedure
fragen.erklaerung_en: If SPOILER FAULT is also displayed, the SPOILER FAULT procedure must be performed before the ELEVATOR FAULT procedure; the Elevators Mode Button is then reset once.

fragen.frage: (E1) ANGLE OF ATTACK LIMIT FAILURE: Welche Aussage ist gemäss AFM korrekt?
antworten: Der Stick Shaker ist ausgefallen; die Speed ist auf mindestens 250 KIAS zu begrenzen.
Der Elevator Disconnection Handle ist zu ziehen.
Der Autopilot darf nicht mehr verwendet werden.
Side Slipping vermeiden; der Stick Shaker bleibt verfügbar.
fragen.erklaerung: Bei ANGLE OF ATTACK LIMIT FAILURE ist Side Slipping zu vermeiden; der Stick Shaker bleibt gemäss Note in Betrieb.
fragen.quelle: AFM E1 4-03-08, ANGLE OF ATTACK LIMIT FAILURE, Page 5
fragen.zitat: ANGLE OF ATTACK LIMIT FAILURE Avoid sideslipping the airplane. NOTE: The stick shaker remains operative.
kontext:
ANGLE OF ATTACK LIMIT FAILURE

Avoid sideslipping the airplane.
NOTE: The stick shaker remains operative.
fragen.frage_en: (E1) ANGLE OF ATTACK LIMIT FAILURE: Which statement is correct according to the AFM?
antworten_en: The Stick Shaker has failed; speed must be limited to at least 250 KIAS.
The Elevator Disconnection Handle must be pulled.
The autopilot must no longer be used.
Avoid side slipping; the Stick Shaker remains available.
fragen.erklaerung_en: With ANGLE OF ATTACK LIMIT FAILURE, side slipping must be avoided; according to the note, the Stick Shaker remains operative.

fragen.frage: (E2) Welches Engine wird gemäss OM-B E2 normalerweise zuerst gestartet?
antworten: Engine 2, sofern ein Verfahren keine andere Reihenfolge verlangt
Das Engine auf der dem Ground Crew abgewandten Seite
Beide Engines werden gleichzeitig gestartet
Engine 1, sofern ein Verfahren keine andere Reihenfolge verlangt
fragen.erklaerung: Gemäss OM-B E2 wird Engine 1 vor Engine 2 gestartet, ausser ein Verfahren verlangt eine andere Reihenfolge.
fragen.zitat: Engine 1 should be started before engine 2 unless procedures require a different sequence.
kontext: 2.2.3 Engine Start
Engine 1 should be started before engine 2 unless procedures require a different sequence.

For Engine Start under Cold Soak Operation refer to 2.8.3.2.5 - Engine Start

For Engine Crossbleed Start refer to 2.8.2.1 - Engine Crossbleed Start For Engine Start with ASU refer to 2.8.2.2 - Engine Ground Pneumatic Start For Engine Battery Start refer to 2.8.2.3 - Engine Battery Start For Manual Starter Valve Ops refer to 2.8.2.4 - Manual Starter Valve Operation
fragen.frage_en: (E2) Which engine is normally started first according to OM-B E2?
antworten_en: Engine 2, unless a procedure requires a different sequence
The engine on the side away from the ground crew
Both engines are started simultaneously
Engine 1, unless a procedure requires a different sequence
fragen.erklaerung_en: According to OM-B E2, Engine 1 is started before Engine 2, unless a procedure requires a different sequence.

fragen.frage: (E2) Engine Start bei Kälte: Auf welchen Wert wird das maximale Öldrucklimit erhöht, wenn die Öltemperatur unter 49 °C liegt?
antworten: 200 psig
250 psig
235 psig
285 psig
fragen.erklaerung: Bei einer Öltemperatur unter 49 °C wird das maximale Öldrucklimit auf 235 psig erhöht.
fragen.zitat: The time to accelerate to idle may be longer. When oil temperature is less than 49°C, the maximum oil pressure limit is increased to 235 psig.
kontext:
2.2.3.2.3 Icing, Cold Weather and Cold Soak Conditions

Do not start the engine until all ice deposits have been removed from air inlet.
Perform normal engine start. If the engine does not start, maintenance

procedures may be required. Ground heating may be necessary to warm the

nacelle, Air Turbine Starter (ATS) and Starting Control Valve (SCV).

During start in cold temperatures engine start characteristics may change.

However, all existing limits and restrictions apply.

The time to accelerate to idle may be longer. When oil temperature is less than 49°C, the maximum oil

pressure limit is increased to 235 psig.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) Engine start in cold conditions: To what value is the maximum oil pressure limit raised if the oil temperature is below 49 °C?
antworten_en: 200 psig
250 psig
235 psig
285 psig
fragen.erklaerung_en: With an oil temperature below 49 °C, the maximum oil pressure limit is raised to 235 psig.

fragen.frage: (E2) Cold Soak: Welche Temperatur dürfen Engine-Teile und Cowl-Oberflächen beim Aufheizen (Ground Heating) nicht überschreiten?
fragen.erklaerung: Die CAUTION im OM-B E2 begrenzt die Temperatur von Engine-Teilen und Cowl-Oberflächen auf 81 °C (179 °F).
fragen.zitat: CAUTION: DO NOT ALLOW THE TEMPERATURE OF THE ENGINE PARTS AND COWL SURFACES TO EXCEED 81 °C (179 °F).
kontext:
CAUTION: DO NOT ALLOW THE TEMPERATURE OF THE ENGINE

PARTS AND COWL SURFACES TO EXCEED 81 °C (179 °F).
fragen.frage_en: (E2) Cold Soak: What temperature must engine parts and cowl surfaces not exceed during ground heating?
fragen.erklaerung_en: The CAUTION in OM-B E2 limits the temperature of engine parts and cowl surfaces to 81 °C (179 °F).

fragen.frage: (E2) Ein Engine Start wurde wegen eines Hot Start manuell abgebrochen. Was wird empfohlen?
antworten: Sofort einen zweiten Startversuch durchführen
Den Start als Crossbleed Start wiederholen
Die APU abstellen und den Start mit GPU wiederholen
Ein Engine Dry Motoring durchführen
fragen.erklaerung: Nach einem manuellen Startabbruch wegen Hot Start wird ein Engine Dry Motoring empfohlen.
fragen.zitat: in case the engine start is manually aborted due to a hot start, an engine dry motoring is recommended.
kontext:
2.2.3.2.5 Abnormal Engine Start Indications

On ground, the FADEC provides automatic protection against starting failures and will automatically command an auto-restart in the event of an impending hot start, hung start or a failure to light. If the auto-restart attempt fails, the engine start will be automatically aborted by the FADEC.
Even with the protections provided by the FADEC, the engine start must be manually aborted when an Abnormal Engine Start indication is observed.

The Abnormal Engine Start indications are:

no positive oil pressure indication within 10 seconds after N2 speed starts to increase

there is no positive N1 speed indication after N2 reaches 45%

ITT exceeds start limit (Hot Start)

oil pressure stabilizes below the engine limits

an intermittent electrical, pneumatic, or starter malfunction occurs before the starter disengagement

Note: in case an automatic abort occurs or engine start is manually aborted due to abnormal engine indications, its cause must be investigated and corrected before further attempts to start the engines.
in case the engine start is manually aborted due to a hot start, an engine dry motoring is recommended.

one additional engine start is allowed if the FADEC commands an

automatic abort in case the N2 speed does not increase after the

START/STOP Selector is placed to the run position or the N2

speed begins to decrease before commanded fuel flow, provided “ENG 1(2) NO DISPATCH” or “ENG 1(2) SHORT DISPATCH”

EICAS messages are not displayed, nor are other abnormal parameters observed.

OM-B E2 2 Normal Procedures
fragen.frage_en: (E2) An engine start was aborted manually because of a Hot Start. What is recommended?
antworten_en: Immediately make a second start attempt
Repeat the start as a crossbleed start
Shut down the APU and repeat the start with GPU
Perform an Engine Dry Motoring
fragen.erklaerung_en: After a manual start abort due to a Hot Start, an Engine Dry Motoring is recommended.

fragen.frage: (E2) Welche Taxi Speed wird für Taxi geradeaus auf trockener Oberfläche empfohlen?
antworten: 20 kt
25 kt
30 kt
40 kt
fragen.erklaerung: Die empfohlene Taxi Speed für Straight / DRY beträgt 30 kt.
fragen.zitat: Recommended taxi speed: Straight / DRY: 30 kt Straight / WET or CONTAMINATED: 10 kt

Recommended taxi speed:
Straight DRY: 30 kt

Straight WET or CONTAMINATED: 10 kt

Turns DRY: 10 kt

Turns WET or CONTAMINATED: 5 kt
fragen.frage_en: (E2) What taxi speed is recommended for straight taxiing on a dry surface?
antworten_en: 20 kt
25 kt
30 kt
40 kt
fragen.erklaerung_en: The recommended taxi speed for Straight / DRY is 30 kt.

fragen.frage: (E2) Unterhalb welcher Speed steht beim Taxi kein Antiskid-Schutz zur Verfügung?
antworten: 5 kt
10 kt
20 kt
30 kt
fragen.erklaerung: Antiskid Protection ist unter 10 kt nicht verfügbar; die Brakes sind entsprechend zu dosieren.
fragen.zitat: Antiskid protection is not provided below 10 kt, so apply brakes accordingly.
kontext:
2.3.1.8 Taxi Under Adverse Weather

Taxi on a wet or contaminated surface requires lower speeds.
Use the nose wheel steering with caution to avoid skidding during turns.
During cold weather, use minimum thrust for breakaway and taxiing, to avoid blowing snow or slush on personnel or airplanes nearby.
Use firm brake pressure on taxi stops whenever pavement conditions permit in order to warm up the brakes and dry moisture buildup within the disk stack.
Antiskid protection is not provided below 10 kt, so apply brakes accordingly.

During taxi, “cold set” (the condition where the tire retains the flat shape it had while parked) may induce vibration in the airplane. Vibration should disappear as the tires recover their elasticity during taxi. Turns should be performed at the largest turning radius, preferably at a speed which does not require braking during the turn. Maintain a greater than normal distance behind other airplanes while taxiing in snow or slush-covered runways, to avoid contamination by snow blown by jet blasts.
During low visibility or unfamiliar airport operation observe the ground markings and consider requesting a FOLLOW ME vehicle to proceed taxiing safely.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) Below what speed is no antiskid protection available during taxi?
antworten_en: 5 kt
10 kt
20 kt
30 kt
fragen.erklaerung_en: Antiskid protection is not available below 10 kt; the brakes must be modulated accordingly.

fragen.frage: (E2) Mit welcher Ground Speed wird ein 180-Degree Turn auf der Runway geflogen?
antworten: Rund 5 kt
Rund 10 kt
Rund 3 kt
Rund 15 kt
fragen.erklaerung: Während des 180-Grad-Manövers wird eine Ground Speed von rund 5 kt gehalten.
fragen.zitat: During the maneuver, maintain a ground speed around 5 kt. Exercise additional care on wet or contaminated runways, as tires may skid.
kontext:
2.3.1.6 Rudder Steering use and Turning Radius

For straight ahead taxiing or for small changes of direction, the use of rudder pedal steering mode may be used. The maximum steering angle of rudder pedal is 7°.
Exercise care on the operation of the steering handle at speeds above 10 kt, as it’s very responsive.
Handwheel steering mode should be used for wider turn angles. To operate in this mode the handle must be kept pressed otherwise the system reverts to rudder pedals. Whenever the handle is pressed, the system reverts back to the handwheel steering.

The wheel deflection as function of handle deflection is not linear. For detailed information refer to AOM section 14-13.
Let the airplane move a little forward before starting a turn and avoid stopping the airplane in a turn as excessive thrust is required to start taxiing again. After

completing a turn and before stopping, center the nosewheel and allow the

airplane to roll straight ahead for a short distance.

Nosewheel skidding may occur with:

Excessive steering angle;

High taxi speed during turns;

On wet surfaces during turn.

When taxiing, make turns with the largest feasible turn radius possible. The minimum turn radius should still allow the tire closer to the center of the turn to continue rolling. When making a tight turn, the tires are subject to high lateral

loads and can experience damage. Asymmetric thrust may be used in tight turns to minimize side loads on gear and tires.

Minimize using thrust from outboard engine in 180° turn, particularly if outboard engine overhangs dusty areas next to the taxiway.
The tail tip or the wingtip, depending on each airplane model, have the largest arc while turning and determines the minimum obstruction clearance path.

2.3.1.7 180-Degree Turn
During the maneuver, maintain a ground speed around 5 kt. Exercise additional care on wet or contaminated runways, as tires may skid.

Start aligned over the centerline and use the handwheel steering to turn the airplane left 30° in the direction of the runway edge. When LSP is over the runway edge apply progressively full right steering command. If necessary, use asymmetric thrust and/or differential braking. Once completed 180-degree turn, return the handwheel steering to the neutral position re-aligning the airplane with the centerline.

kontext:
2.3.3.3.12 Tail Strike Considerations

Although tail strikes are more common during landing phase of flight, it may also occur during takeoff and may cause extensive structural damage. The major causes identified of a tail strike during takeoffs are:
Improper Stabilizer Trim A mistrimmed stabilizer may be a result of an erroneous input data, like loading weights for load sheet calculation, or even an incorrect stab trim setting. In any case, the stabilizer could be wrongly set to nose up which may induce the airplane attempting to fly before V1.
Improper Rotation Speed Wrong speed computations or early rotation could result in nose up without wing lift enough to fly exposing the airplane to a tail strike.
Excessive Rotation Rate
Initiate rotation at VR at approximately 3°/sec, smoothly, towards the flight director angle.
Rotation at a pitch higher than normal and inappropriate flight director use during rotation increase the risk of tail strike.

fragen.zitat: difference between both engine N1 values is greater than 15%, OEI (One Engine Inoperative), thrust levers are moved to MAX detent, windshear is detected.
kontext:
2.3.3.3.7 Flex Takeoff

This method is also known as assumed temperature takeoff thrust.
A Takeoff with less thrust than the maximum takeoff thrust is used.
When operating with flex takeoff thrust, thrust setting parameters used to establish thrust for takeoff are not considered as operating limits.
If REF ATTCS (on takeoff data setting) is set to ON and one of the following events occurs, flex takeoff is canceled and ATTCS automatically commands RSV thrust:

difference between both engine N1 values is greater than 15%,

OEI (One Engine Inoperative),

thrust levers are moved to MAX detent,

windshear is detected.

When used with derated takeoff thrust, this method provides larger thrust reductions and may increase engine life. Less severe operation means lower: fuel flow degradation rate, reducing fuel burn over the on-wing life of engine,

Inter Turbine Temperature (ITT) degradation rate (Increases time-on-wing),

maintenance costs, reducing shop visit rate and cost per shop visit.
Note: The use of this method is prohibited on contaminated runways.

kontext:
2.3.3.3.14 Noise Abatement Procedures

Noise abatement procedures minimize the overall exposure to noise on the ground and at the same time maintain the required levels of flight safety. There are several methods, including preferential runways and routes, as well as noise abatement procedures for takeoff and approach. The appropriateness of any of the procedures depends on the physical layout of the airport and its surroundings. In all cases give priority to safety considerations.
Pilots are required to adhere to the noise abatement procedures published specifically for each airport. There are different procedures for noise abatement, and the items listed here are just a guide to help pilots to perform a takeoff with noise reduction:
Set speed required for the procedure on SPEED Knob or on FMS DEPARTURE page. If using FMS SPEED, set 3000 ft as the vertical limit.
Use MCDU DEPARTURE LIMIT page to set the speed limit and VNAV engagement height. The DEPARTURE LIMIT page has the following fields:
Speed Limit: The crew should adjust this value to speed limit of the applicable noise abatement procedure,

AFE Limit: This field is used to enter the vertical limit of the departure area,

VNAV CAP AFE: This field is used to set the VNAV capture height.

Note: The FMS departure speed limit functionality commands the speed restriction during takeoff only when the airplane is flying below the vertical limit.

If an engine failure occurs, terminate the noise abatement procedure.

In this case, an engine failure procedure and profile should be performed.

Note: Some charts make reference to ICAO A or ICAO B procedures which are

similar to NADP 1 and NADP 2 respectively.

The characteristic difference between ICAO A and ICAO B, resides on the

location of the noise relief area. The difference is maintained for NADP 1 and NADP 2. ICAO A and NADP 1 are procedures to protect areas located close to

the airport. ICAO B and NADP 2 are procedures to protect areas located distant from the airport.

For take-off, noise abatement profile NADP 2 should be used unless a different

profile is published. Information regarding noise abatement profiles can be found

in the Jeppesen route manual. The acceleration altitude shall be minimum 1000 ft AFE. The altitude and speed constraints on the departure route must be respected.
Refer to OM-A 8.3.2.17 - Flight Profiles Take-off

2.3.3.3.14.1 NADP 1 ICAO A Procedure
Climb at V2 +10 KIAS until 800 ft (NADP 1) or 1500 ft (ICAO A) AFE.

Verify VNAV engagement at the height set on MCDU: at or above 800 ft (NADP 1) or 1500 ft (ICAO A) AFE. Verify that climb thrust is set and continue climbing at V2 10 to 20 KIAS.

At 3000 ft AFE, the airplane is released from the speed limit. Accelerate and retract SLAT/FLAP on schedule or following the F-BUG.

2.3.3.3.14.2 NADP 2 ICAO B Procedure

Climb at V2 +10 KIAS until 800 ft (NADP 2) or 1000 ft (ICAO B) AFE.

Verify VNAV engagement at the height set on MCDU: at or above 800 ft (NADP 2) or 1000 ft (ICAO B) AFE.
Verify that climb thrust is set and maintain VFS 10 KIAS until 3000 ft

At 3000 ft AFE, accelerate to the enroute climb speed.

fragen.erklaerung_en: In the NADP 1 / ICAO A procedure, the climb is flown at V2 +10 KIAS up to 800 ft (NADP 1) or 1500 ft AFE (ICAO A).

kontext:
2.3.3.3.8 Takeoff Run and Thrust Settings

Align the airplane using as reference the runway centerline. During takeoff run, pedals are used to steer the airplane. The use of nose wheel steering is not recommended during takeoff run because of its high efficiency, which might lead to airplane overreaction. As the groundspeed increases, the authority of nose wheel steering reduces and the rudder becomes more effective.
The takeoff (TO) mode is represented by crossbars on the PFD and commands the airplane to maintain a pitch attitude reference.

When the airplane lines up and is ready for takeoff, arm the AT.
Advance the thrust levers to 40% N1.
The engines should stabilize momentarily and power settings verified before both throttles are advanced beyond 50° TLA.
Advance thrust levers to TO/GA detent and verify that N1 reaches takeoff thrust (N1 target), engine parameters are normal and ATTCS set as required.
If ATTCS is ON, with thrust levers to TO/GA, ATTCS indication on EICAS changes from white to green (armed). If ATTCS indication remains white on EICAS, confirm thrust levers are set to TO/GA position.
The AT takes over above 50° TLA when advancing the thrust levers to the TO/GA detent. If any AT malfunction occurs, disconnect the AT and set the desired thrust manually. If thrust is set manually, advance thrust levers to TO/GA detent.

ROLL indication changes to TRACK when the airplane is above 100 KIAS during

takeoff run.

The ENG TLA NOT TOGA EICAS message is displayed during the takeoff if the thrust levers are out of the TO/GA position. It happens even if the N1 has already reached the takeoff thrust (N1 target).

Make sure that the thrust levers are set to TO/GA position before 60 kt, when AT HOLD mode is activated, to prevent this message from occurring.
If ENG TLA NOT TOGA EICAS message appears during takeoff run, PF should advance thrust levers to TO/GA position and continue the takeoff.

Note: After takeoff thrust is set, LSP takes control over the thrust levers until V1 is announced. The LSP is always responsible for aborting the takeoff. All abnormalities during the takeoff run are called out in a loud and clear voice.

FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL message may appear spuriously (EICAS quantity indication green) when flying with high pitch or bank angles.
It happens especially during takeoff and climb out with fuel quantity just above the expected to trigger FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL EICAS message.

fragen.frage: (E2) Welches ist die minimale Acceleration Altitude für das Einfahren von Slat/Flap?

kontext: 2.3.3.3.6 Slat Flap Retraction
Flap retraction is accomplished after the specified acceleration altitude is reached. The minimum acceleration altitude for Slat/Flap retraction is 1000 ft.

The flaps should be retracted using the flap retraction speed “F-BUG” and pitch

angle adjusted to maintain a slight rate of climb. After Slat/Flap retraction is complete, accelerate to enroute climb speed.

During flap retraction, the next flap setting should be selected when the F-Bug is

reached.

The F-Bug calculation algorithm is designed so as to meet minimum safe margins to VFE and Shaker speed. A minimum margin of 20% above the stall

speed is set for the next flap.
In case of “F-BUG” disappears before total accomplishment of Slat/Flap

retraction, retract Slat/Flap following Green Dot +10 kt.

kontext:
2.6.1.4.1 Autobrake

With autobrake set to LO, MED or HI verify after touchdown the normal operation of the braking system and proper deceleration of the airplane.
At 80 kt, press the brakes pedal to disengage the autobrake and use the necessary braking force to reach a safe taxi speed.

Note: At pilot’s discretion, disengage the autobrake after touchdown at any speed by pressing the brakes pedals.

During the landing roll, if autobrake deceleration is not suitable for the stopping

distance, use manual braking as required. Apply continuous increasing pressure to the brake pedals. Use manual braking as soon as possible to achieve

maximum deceleration. Pilot must be alert for autobrake disengagement

indications during the landing roll. At pilot’s discretion, use reverse thrust with

manual braking or autobrake during landing roll until a safe speed is reached.
The autobrake works aiming a constant deceleration rate. When the braking

capability is good and the autobrake deceleration target is reached, the use of

thrust reversers is not effective.

fragen.frage: (E2) Um wie viel nimmt die Landing Distance ungefähr zu, wenn der Flare um 3 Sekunden verlängert wird?
antworten: Etwa 10%
Etwa 35%
Etwa 25%
Etwa 80%
fragen.erklaerung: Ein um 3 Sekunden verlängerter Flare erhöht die Landing Distance um etwa 25%.
fragen.zitat: Extending the flare by 3 seconds increases the landing distance by approximately 25%.
kontext:
2.6.1.9 Operational Factors Affecting Landing Distance

The required landing distance for dispatch is calculated considering that the landing is performed with:
Airplane crossing the runway threshold at the screen height of 50 ft;

Airplane crossing the runway threshold at VREF;

Use of maximum manual braking.

In order to stay within the operational margins of the required landing distance, conduct a stabilized approach and landing using the correct landing techniques.
Several environment factors, such as airport elevation, runway slope, runway conditions, and winds may affect the landing distance. However, aside those factors, if the approach and landing are performed with deviations from the standard procedures, the operational margin available reduces or may even be exceeded.
The following operational factors, among others, affect the airplane landing distance:
Unstabilized approach;

Crossing runway threshold with airspeed above VREF;

Crossing runway threshold above the screen height; Extended flare, touching down the runway beyond the touchdown zone; No proper application of the available deceleration devices (brakes, spoilers,

and thrust reverse);

Deceleration devices not applied until a safe taxi speed is achieved.

If the airplane crosses the threshold with 10 kt above the VREF, the landing

distance increases by approximately 20%. Crossing the threshold at 100 ft instead of the normal screen height increases the landing distance by

approximately 35%.

Extending the flare during landing increases the landing distance. The airplane touches down the runway at a point ahead of the runway touchdown zone, which is located at 1000 ft from the runway threshold.
Extending the flare by 3 seconds increases the landing distance by approximately 25%.

Considering an unstabilized approach, with the airplane crossing the threshold at 100 ft, above VREF and with 3 seconds of extended flare, the landing distance increases by approximately 80%. In this situation, the distance necessary to stop the airplane exceeds the operational margins provided by the dispatch required landing distance.

The preceding information, and the graphic that follows, assumes an airplane landing at maximum landing weight, on dry runway.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) By approximately how much does the landing distance increase if the flare is extended by 3 seconds?
antworten_en: About 10%
About 35%
About 25%
About 80%
fragen.erklaerung_en: A flare extended by 3 seconds increases the landing distance by about 25%.

fragen.frage: (E2) Unter welchem Pitch-Winkel soll die Fluglage bei der Landing gehalten werden, um die Heckfreiheit sicherzustellen?
antworten: Unter 8°
Unter 10°
Unter 12°
Unter 15°
fragen.erklaerung: TSA bietet keinen vollständigen Schutz; bei der Landing ist der Pitch unter 10° zu halten, um die Tail Clearance sicherzustellen.
fragen.zitat: TSA function does not provide full protection against tail strikes. During landing, the pitch angle should be maintained below 10° to ensure tail clearance.
kontext:
2.6.1.13 Tail Strike During Landing

Tail strikes are more frequent during landings than takeoffs.
Based on information gathered from tail strike occurrences, deviation from the normal landing maneuver, in the following paragraphs, is the main cause of tail strikes.

The mistakes most commonly made are:
Approach at improper pitch, speed, thrust, and glide path;

Prolonged flare, hold-off for a smooth touchdown;

Starting to flare the airplane too high above the runway;

Improper crosswind correction during flare;

Over rotation during a touch and go.

Of these commonly made mistakes, flaring the airplane too high above the runway has the greatest potential for a tail strike and resulting damage.
When the flare is started too high above the runway, airspeed decreases below VAPP causing the pilot to compensate. When placed in this situation, the tendency is to continue to increase pitch to stop the excessive sink rate. The correct action to take is to immediately lower the pitch attitude and fly the airplane to the

runway before the airspeed dissipates any further. This corrective action prevents a tail strike.
Lack or poor handling could lead to a destabilized approach thus increasing the tail strike exposure.

Tail Strike Avoidance (TSA)

TSA function controls airplane pitch angle as it reduces control column authority in the nose up direction. The crew may override the TSA actuation by applying

large pitch up column inputs.

TSA function does not provide full protection against tail strikes. During landing,

the pitch angle should be maintained below 10° to ensure tail clearance.
For TSA range of operation, refer to AOM Vol. 2 - TAIL STRIKE AVOIDANCE (TSA) system description.
fragen.frage_en: (E2) Below what pitch angle should the attitude be kept during landing to ensure tail clearance?
antworten_en: Below 8°
Below 10°
Below 12°
Below 15°
fragen.erklaerung_en: TSA does not provide complete protection; during landing, pitch must be kept below 10° to ensure tail clearance.

fragen.frage: (E2) Was ist nach einem schweren Bounce beim Landing zu tun?
antworten: Go-Around einleiten und die Flare-Attitude halten, bis die Engines hochgelaufen sind
Normale Landelage wiederherstellen und das zweite Aufsetzen mit Thrust abfedern
Den Pitch erhöhen, um ein zweites hartes Aufsetzen zu vermeiden
Thrust Levers auf IDLE und mit MAX REV und Maximalbremsung stoppen
fragen.erklaerung: Bei einem schweren Bounce wird nicht gelandet: TO/GA drücken, Thrust auf TO/GA, Flare-Attitude bis zum Hochlaufen der Engines halten und Stabilizer Trim zurücksetzen.

When a more severe bounce occurs, initiate a go-around and do not attempt to

land. Press the TO/GA button and advance thrust levers to TO/GA.
Hold the flare attitude until the engines spool up and reset stabilizer trim,

then

follow normal go-around procedures.

fragen.frage_en: (E2) What must be done after a heavy bounce on landing?

antworten: 5 kt
15 kt

10 kt
