kontext:
NORMAL OPERATION

Climb: VNAV performs all climb profiles contained in the VFLCH mode. If the FMS levels-off at an altitude constraint defined over a waypoint, it resumes the climb automatically upon sequencing the waypoint. If the FMS levels-off at an altitude set on the Altitude Pre Selector, after setting the Altitude Pre Selector to a higher altitude, the FLCH button must be pressed on the guidance panel in order for the VNAV to transition from VALT to VFLCH.

Cruise: The FMS will transition to cruise phase when reaching the initial cruise altitude set in the PERF INIT page. If the airplane levels at an altitude lower than the initial cruise altitude, the FMS does not transition to cruise.

If the ALT SEL is set to an altitude higher than the FMS cruise altitude, after few seconds, the cruise altitude in the PERF INIT page is reset to match with the ALT SEL selection.

NOTE: To reset the FMS cruise altitude to an altitude lower than the current FMS cruise altitude, it may be necessary to delete the current cruise altitude in the FMS CRUISE PAGE 1/1 prior to insert the new altitude.

To leave cruise level to either climb or descent, the altitude selector must be set to an altitude higher or lower than the present altitude and a vertical DIRECT-TO or VFLCH must be commanded.

REVISION 22 Flight Management System Page 3/100

When TCS is used to exit a leveled altitude, the command logic is to return to the original altitude when the change is less than 50 ft. For changes greater than 50 ft, the new achieved altitude is maintained.

TOD: The Top of Descent is calculated using the values inserted in the PERF INIT page and is displayed in the VNAV page and on the PFD/ MFD.
Post-Mod. LOAD 21.2 and Post-Mod. LOAD 27.1

The DES NOW prompt is displayed on the FMS DESCENT, FLIGHT PLAN and ROUTE pages providing an easy command to start the descent when the airplane is 50 NM or less from the calculated TOD.

When selected, the Flight Director commands the airplane to descent according to the airplane position relative to the predicted TOD.
– Early Descent: selecting the DES NOW prompt before the TOD is reached enables the Early Descent mode, where the FD commands a 1000 FPM descent up to the point where the planned descent path or the next altitude constraint is intercepted.
–

Late Descent: selecting the DES NOW prompt after the planned TOD is reached enables the Late Descent mode, where the FD commands a descent angle 1.5° steeper than the planned descent angle to intercept the planned path.

NOTE: If this descent angle is not enough to intercept the previously planned path a UNABLE PATH INTERCEPT scratchpad message is displayed.

Descent: One minute prior to the TOD, a vertical track alert is given.
When reaching the TOD, the FMS automatically starts the descent in VFLCH or VPATH if the altitude selector is set to a lower altitude.
– VFLCH Descents – The descent is in VFLCH mode if there is no altitude constraint down to 1500 ft/10 NM prior to the destination airport. VFLCH also complies with the speed/altitude limit. After an intermediate level-off at the altitude selector altitude, the next descent must be initiated selecting the altitude selector to a lower altitude and pressing FLCH on the GP.

Page 4/100 Flight Management System REVISION 22

– VPATH Descents – The descent is in VPATH anytime an altitude constraint exists in the descent path and the airplane is within the capture logic of VPATH mode. FMS must be the navigation source and LNAV must be engaged in order the VPATH to become available. When the FMS passes through the last altitude constraint waypoint, it reverts to VFLCH to complete the descent.
During VPATH descents, significant modifications of the flight plan may result the VPATH mode to drop to FPA mode.
Vertical DIRECT-TO: This operation is similar to the lateral DIRECT- TO. It is performed selecting the desired altitude from the scratch pad to the line adjacent to the desired waypoint.
Post-Mod. LOAD 21.2 and Post-Mod. LOAD 27.1

The FMS calculates the predicted altitudes at which the airplane should pass the waypoints and then applies the altitude constraints to these altitudes, if necessary.

VNAV and HOLDING PATTERNS: The following applies:
– If descending on VFLCH and a holding pattern is entered, the active mode remains VFLCH;
– If a PPOS holding is entered while in VPATH, the active mode changes to VFLCH;
– If a hold is entered while in VPATH descent, the command changes to VALT.

kontext:
REFUELING AND DEFUELING

There is a single pressurized refueling point and a refuel/defuel control panel located under the right wing. When the access panel door is opened, an overhead panel lamp comes on for night or low light operations.

Pressurized refueling is performed with the airplane energized either by AC or battery power. A switch located on the refueling panel enables selection of either power sources.

Refueling operation modes can be either AUTO or MANUAL. When the refueling switch is in the OPEN position, the refuel control valves open enabling fuel flow. Refueling in AUTO mode the FCU (Fuel Conditioning Unit) controls the refuel shutoff valves, automatically halting refueling when the preselected value is reached. In MANUAL mode, the FCU is bypassed. Setting of the CLOSED position in the refueling control switch halts refueling.

In automatic mode, the desired wing tank fuel quantity may be selected on the fuel quantity remaining display via the INCR/DECRT switch.

In the pressurized refueling, the system will automatically close the shutoff to prevent overfilling whenever the fuel rises up to a certain level. Moreover, the STOP L/R OVR message(s) will appear on the Refueling/Defueling control panel display when the quantity in the right, left or both wing tanks, respectively, is above its capacity.

The wing fuel tanks may be partially or completely refueled using the gravity refuel port located on top of each wing. The individual fuel quantity can be determined using the EICAS or the magnetic level indicators.

NOTE:

The maximum fuel quantities indicated on the AFM are not achieved through pressurized refueling only. To achieve the maximum tank capacities, gravity refueling must be used to fill the remainder of the tank.

The airplane can be defueled by suction and/or pressure. The defuel shutoff valve is controlled by the DEFUEL switch located on the refuel/ defuel control panel.

kontext:
FUEL LOW-LEVEL WARNING

Each wing tank has a dedicated Fuel Low-Level Sensor located in the collector box. The Fuel Low-Level Sensor is independent of the fuel quantity indication system. Whenever the fuel level in the collector box is below the sensor level, it sends a fuel low-level signal to the warning system, thus triggering the FUEL LO LEVEL warning EICAS message.

NOTE: FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL may appear spuriously when flying with high pitch and/or bank angles.

Under normal conditions, the low-level warning message activation point is set at 400 kg of fuel in the associated wing tank.

If any scavenge pump stops transferring fuel to the Collector Box, which might be caused by an engine failure, loss of motive flow or scavenge pumps failure/blockage, the fuel contained in the Collector Box flows out so that the fuel level inside the Collector Box and the rest of the tank reaches the same level.

Under this condition, if there is up to 2800 kg (approximately) of fuel inside that tank it is possible that the level equivalent to the low-level warning activation point will be reached as the fuel level inside the collector box decreases, then FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL warning EICAS message displays indicating that fuel level is below the Low-Level Sensor.

Therefore, in case of loss of the transfer system to the Collector Box, the EICAS WARNING message FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL may display even though fuel quantity indication on the EICAS or MFD Fuel System Synoptic Page is up to 2800 kg in that tank.

NOTE: – In case of loss of the transfer system to the Collector Box followed by the EICAS warning message, fuel quantity indication monitoring during the flight is achieved through EICAS, or MFD Fuel System synoptic page.

The Electric Hydraulic Pump 1 (ACMP 1B) is an alternating current motor pump. It serves as a backup for the EDP 1 and it is powered by the AC BUS 2.

In flight, with the selector knob set to AUTO position, the Hydraulic System logic activates the electric pump in case of:
– EDP or engine fail, or
– Flaps selected to any position greater than 0°.
During landing operations, the Electric Hydraulic Pumps remain activated for 60 seconds to avoid abrupt hydraulic pressure variations in an event of engine failure.

– Flaps selected to any position greater than 0° and:
– Thrust levers set to takeoff thrust, or
– Airspeed greater than 50 kt.

If the fluid temperature reaches 125°C, the shutoff valve (SOV) automatically actuates, thus isolating the EDP 1 from the respective hydraulic flow line.

During specific conditions, the wing anti ice system will be activated, regardless of the airplane being in icing conditions. In this case the system will be activated but the message ICE CONDITION will not be displayed.

Altitude below 22000 ft.

kontext: AIR GROUND POSITIONING SYSTEM

Two proximity sensor electronic modules (PSEM) process signals from the six weight-on-wheels (WOW) proximity sensors to determine if the airplane is on ground or in flight. Two WOW sensors are installed on each landing gear.

Each PSEM monitors the six WOW proximity sensors. The inputs are logically combined by the PSEMs, and other airplane systems, to provide the overall airplane air/ground (WOW) indication to those systems.

If two WOW sensors on the same landing gear leg fail, the PSEMs will activate a logic that prevents the landing gear lever from moving up.

In this case, with the airplane on ground, the LG NO DISPATCH caution message is displayed on the EICAS. In-flight the failure is recognized through the landing gear lever stuck in the DOWN position and the EICAS message LG WOW SYS FAIL may be presented.

BRAKES

The brake system employs brake-by-wire rudder pedals located at both pilot stations. Hydraulic system 1 provides pressure to the outboard brakes and hydraulic system 2 provides pressure to the inboard brakes.

The Emergency/Parking brake has the ability to stop the airplane if a failure happens simultaneously on both hydraulic systems or if both brake control modules fail.

The brake wear can be monitored through the brake wear pins located on each main wheel.

kontext:
MAIN LANDING GEAR DOORS

Each main landing gear (MLG) has three doors: lower, middle, and upper door.

The upper door is hinged to a rib of the MLG bay in the wing. Rods attach the upper door to the MLG main fitting.

The middle door is not hinged. It is attached by bolts directly to the MLG main fitting.

The lower door is hinged to the middle door. When the MLG extends, the lower door opens and provides clearance for the full stroke of the MLG shock absorber.
The MLG doors do not cover the wheel and tire assemblies when the MLG is fully retracted.

LANDING GEAR RETRACTION

Positioning the landing gear lever to the UP position releases hydraulic pressure for the nose and main landing gear locks, and pressurizes the respective actuators to retract the landing gear. When retraction is completed, the landing gear is held in place by uplocks.

When the weight on wheels signal is no longer valid (airplane in-flight status) the mechanical lock is released allowing the landing gear lever to move to the UP position.

kontext:
NOSE WHEEL STEERING SYSTEM

The airplane nose landing gear has steer-by-wire control powered by hydraulic system 2 and electronically controlled by the Nose Wheel Steering Control Module.

OPERATION

To engage the nose wheel steering system:
–

The hydraulic system 2 needs to be pressurized.
– The external steering disengage switch must be in the engaged position.

– The handwheel steering must be pressed and released for rudder pedal steering or kept pressed for handwheel steering.
NOTE: After a power up, the first steering engagement must be performed with the airplane stopped. If this condition is not met, the hardover test might not be successfully accomplished by the system and STEER FAIL message may be displayed.

The nose wheel steering has three modes of operation: the handwheel steering mode, the rudder pedal steering mode and the free wheel steering mode.

kontext:
2.3.1.6 Rudder Steering use and Turning Radius

For straight ahead taxiing or for small changes of direction, the use of rudder pedal steering mode may be used. The maximum steering angle of rudder pedal is 7°.
At speeds between 20 kt and 40 kt use the steering handle only if necessary and exercise care as at these speeds the steering handle is very responsive.

Handwheel steering mode should be used for wider turn angles. To operate in this mode the handle must be kept pressed otherwise the system reverts to rudder pedals. Whenever the handle is pressed, the system reverts back to the handwheel steering. The wheel deflection as function of handle deflection is not linear. For detailed information refer to AOM section 14-13.

Let the airplane move a little forward before starting a turn and avoid stopping the airplane in a turn as excessive thrust is required to start taxiing again. After completing a turn and before stopping, center the nosewheel and allow the airplane to roll straight ahead for a short distance.

Nosewheel skidding may occur with:

excessive steering angle

high taxi speed during turns

on wet surfaces during turn

When taxiing, make turns with the largest feasible turn radius possible. The

minimum turn radius should still allow the tire closer to the center of the turn to continue rolling. When making a tight turn, the tires are subject to high lateral

loads and can experience damage. Asymmetric thrust may be used in tight turns to minimize side loads on gear and tires.

Minimize using thrust from outboard engine in 180° turn, particularly if outboard engine overhangs dusty areas next to the taxiway.

Depending on each airplane model, the tail tip or the wingtip have the largest arc

while turning and determines the minimum obstruction clearance path.

fragen.frage: Warum wird gemäss OM-B die Nose Wheel Steering während des Takeoff Run nicht empfohlen?

kontext:
2.3.3.3.8 Takeoff Run and Thrust Settings

Align the airplane using as reference the runway centerline. During takeoff run, pedals are used to steer the airplane.
The use of nose wheel steering is not recommended during takeoff run because of its high efficiency, which might lead to airplane overreaction.

As the groundspeed increases, the authority of nose wheel steering reduces and the rudder becomes more effective.

The takeoff (TO) mode is an FD only mode and is represented by crossbars on

the PFD. The TO mode commands the airplane to maintain a pitch attitude reference.

When the airplane lines up and is ready for takeoff, arm the AT.

Advance the thrust levers to 40% N1.
The engines should stabilize momentarily and power settings verified before both throttles are advanced beyond 50° TLA.
Advance thrust levers to TO/GA detent and verify that N1 reaches takeoff thrust (N1 target), engine parameters are normal and ATTCS set as required.
If ATTCS is ON, with thrust levers to TO/GA, ATTCS indication on EICAS changes from white to green (armed). If ATTCS indication remains white on EICAS, confirm thrust levers are set to TO/GA position.
The AT takes over above 50° TLA when advancing the thrust levers to the TO/GA detent. If any AT malfunction occurs, disconnect the AT and set the desired thrust manually. If thrust is set manually, advance thrust levers to TO/GA detent. ROLL indication changes to TRACK when the airplane is above 100 kt during takeoff

run.
The ENG TLA NOT TOGA EICAS message is displayed during the takeoff if the thrust levers are out of the TO/GA position. It happens even if the N1 has already reached the takeoff thrust (N1 target).

Make sure that the thrust levers are set to TO/GA position before 60 kt, when AT

HOLD mode is activated, to prevent this message from occurring.

If ENG TLA NOT TOGA EICAS message appears during takeoff run, PF should

advance thrust levers to TO/GA position and continue the takeoff.

After takeoff thrust is set, LSP takes control over the thrust levers until V1 is announced. The LSP is always responsible for aborting the takeoff. All

abnormalities during the takeoff run are called out in a loud and clear voice.

Note: FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL message may appear spuriously (EICAS quantity indication green) when flying with high pitch or bank angles. It happens

especially during takeoff and climb out with fuel quantity just above the expected to trigger FUEL 1 (2) LO LEVEL EICAS message.

OM-B E1 2 Normal Procedures

kontext:
AURAL WARNING PRIORITY LEVELS

There are four aural warning priority levels, from the highest to the lowest:
– Emergency (level 3).
– Abnormal (level 2).
– Advisory (level 1).
– Information (level 0).
Emergency: corresponds to a situation that requires the pilot’s immediate action. The master warning annunciator is repeated with three-second intervals between alerts until the master warning reset switch is pressed.

Abnormal: corresponds to an abnormal situation such as system malfunction or failures that have no immediate impact on safety.
Whenever an abnormal fault occurs, a master caution tone is presented every five seconds until the master caution reset switch is

pressed.

Advisory: corresponds to the recognition of a situation such as system malfunction or failures leading to loss of redundancy or degradation of a system.

Information: corresponds to a condition or status for flight crew information.

EICAS MESSAGES PRESENTATION

The messages are grouped and presented in a chronological order accordingly to its category. The Warning category is placed at the top of the EICAS display. Below this category the system presents the Caution, Advisory and Information/Status category, in this order.

Advisory messages will automatically revert from inverse to normal video after 5 seconds

they started to be displayed.

After the acknowledgment, the new message shall remain in steady normal video, at the top of its category on the EICAS display, until a new message belonging to that group appears.

The EICAS messages cannot be cancelable. They shall remain active as long as its activation condition exists.

kontext:
MONITOR WARNING FUNCTION (MWF)

Two monitor warning function computers in separate modular avionics units (MAUs) continually monitor the status of various airplane and avionics systems.
One MWF has priority and alerts the flight crew by generating alert messages in the CAS display window. Some warnings also have sounds (voice and/or tone). The other MWF is a backup.

If the priority MWF fails, the display computer automatically selects and uses the data from the backup MWF.

Alert messages are prioritized and color-coded for display. The MWF also controls message timing, flight crew acknowledgement, and the scrolling of the CAS messages in the CAS display window.

More than one warning may be generated if more than one condition is met.

A test button is provided to allow checking the takeoff configuration by simulating power levers in the advanced position.
If the airplane is in takeoff configuration, the voice message “TAKEOFF OK” is generated.

kontext:
ROOT EICAS MESSAGES

Some single failures may trigger more than one EICAS message at a time. In the event of multiple EICAS messages, identifying the true nature of the failure and taking the appropriate corrective action is an important role.
EICAS messages which may generate more messages with them are called Root EICAS messages and they are highlighted by a preceding chevron

In most cases the corrective action will be to perform only the procedure associated with the ROOT EICAS message, but some situations may require additional actions. The pilot must always review all messages displayed on the EICAS and check if they are associated to the root EICAS message and take additional actions if required.

ROOT EICAS message procedures do not necessarily have to be performed first.

If more than one root message is displayed at the same time or displayed together with a WARNING message, the priority order to be evaluated is:

kontext:
DISTANCE REMAINING - REJECTED TAKEOFF

Distance Remaining - Rejected Takeoff advisory provides the flight crew with position awareness during a rejected takeoff.
These advisories are generated at multiples of 300 m intervals, except that the last possible advisory occurs at 100 m.

For example, a RAAS equipped airplane performing a RTO on a 3000 m runway would

14-15-37

REVISION 22 Runway Awareness and Advisory System Page 9/10

generate the following advisories: “One-Thousand-Two- Hundred Remaining”, “Nine-Hundred Remaining”, “Six-Hundred Remaining”, “Three-Hundred Remaining”, and “One-Hundred Remaining”.
Airplanes equipped with Runway Awareness and Advisory System (RAAS), Post-Mod. LOAD 27.1

The distance unit is generated after the distance value of the first distance remaining callout. For example, “One-Thousand-Two- Hundred meters Remaining”, “Nine-Hundred Remaining”, “Six- Hundred Remaining”, “Three-Hundred Remaining”, and “One-Hundred Remaining”.

The Distance Remaining -Rejected Takeoff advisory shall be enabled when all the following conditions are met:
– airplane is on the last half of the runway or on a specified distance from runway end;
– radio altitude is less than or equal to 100 ft;
– ground speed of the airplane is greater than or equal to 40 kt;
– airplane ground speed during the takeoff roll decreases by 7 kt from its maximum.

kontext:
TCAS STATUS ANNUNCIATIONS

The TCAS information is displayed on the MFD and PFD. There are six types of TCAS mode annunciations:
– TCAS
FAIL – This annunciation is displayed when a TCAS failure is indicated by TCAS data, when TCAS data is invalid or when TCAS data was not correctly received for 10 s.

– TCAS TEST – This annunciation is displayed when the TCAS computer indicates functional test is active.
– TCAS OFF – This annunciation is displayed when TCAS provides a valid indication that the computer is in stand by mode.
– TA ONLY – This annunciation indicates that the TCAS is not selected to provide resolution advisories or is inhibited. The TA mode provides only surveillance of the surrounding airspace. In this mode, TCAS tracks proximate airplane and generates traffic advisories; no resolution advisories are issued in this mode.

14-15-40

REVISION 22 Traffic Collision Avoidance System Page 3/8

– TA/RA – This annunciation is displayed when TCAS provides a valid indication that the computer is in TA/RA mode. This annunciation is only displayed on both TCAS MFD displays. TA/RA mode is the normal operation mode providing full TCAS coverage.
In this mode, TCAS tracks airplane in the surrounding airspace and generates traffic advisories or resolution advisories, as the situation requires.
– TCAS RA FAIL – This annunciation indicates that TCAS is not able to provide resolution advisories. The annunciation is displayed if the resolution advisory data is invalid or not received for 5 s or if information required to display the TCAS RA data on the PFD is missing or failed (e.g., if attitude, or groundspeed is failed or missing). This annunciation is only displayed on the PFD.

kontext:
SYSTEM (TCAS)

The TCAS detects the nearby airplanes and display symbols to represent them. The relative or absolute altitude and the vertical motion of the other airplanes are information displayed with each symbol.

The TCAS monitors a potential collision hazard and alerts the flight crew. It interrogates the mode A, mode C and mode S operating transponders in other airplanes and calculates the flight path of the possible intruder airplane.

If the intruder airplane is also equipped with operating TCAS, the systems will communicate with each other to coordinate and generate guidance for the optimal avoidance maneuver.
NOTE: Intruder airplanes that do not have operating transponders are invisible to the TCAS.

Airplanes equipped with TCAS II Change 7.1

The installed TCAS system is fully compliant with the requirements of EU 1332/2011.

kontext:
TCAS PRESENTATION ON MFD

The TCAS system can be controlled through the MCDU and on the MFD by the CCD.

The TCAS map overlay and TCAS zoom format are available on the MFD. The map overlay format displays the TCAS information on the navigation MAP mode, on MFD.

To show TCAS on the Map Overlay is necessary to open the MAP menu on the MFD and then select TCAS.

The zoom format is displayed in the lower portion of MFD and has a range control. Only one format can be displayed at a time.

The range is selected using the CCD knob. The ranges selectable are 6, 12, 20, 40, 80 and 120 NM.

Zoom display shows up when the Map Overlay format is deselected.

Captain and First Officer’s TCAS controls on the MFD’s are totally independent from each other.
NOTE: If neither map overlay nor zoom format is displayed and the range is lower than 50 NM and a TA or RA condition is encountered, the zoom format is automatically displayed.

kontext:
RADAR WEATHER DETECTION MODE (WX)

The WX mode is used to detect areas of severe weather. This will allow the pilots to avoid areas of dangerous weather conditions and possible turbulence.
If WX is selected before the initial RTA warm-up period is over (approximately 90s), WAIT is displayed in the mode field. In the wait mode, the transmitter and antenna scan are inhibited.

kontext: SECTOR SCAN (SECT) FUNCTION

The normal radar sweep is 60 degrees from the airplane nose, at a rate of 12 sweeps per minute. Selecting the SECT pushbutton reduces the angle of sweep to 30 degrees and increases the sweep rate to 24 sweeps per minute.

kontext:
TURBULENCE DETECTION (TURB) FUNCTION

The radar processes return signals in order to determine if a turbulence signature is present.
Areas of moderate, severe, or extreme turbulence are displayed in soft white. TURB may only be engaged in the WX mode and at selected ranges of 50 NM or less.

NOTE: – It may occur that the Turbulence function annunciation in MFD and PFD to remain displayed for ranges above 50 NM even though the function is deactivated.

kontext:
TILT FUNCTION

The inner knob on the CCD provides tilt control giving the pilot manual control of the antenna tilt angle. The CCD inner knob is a dedicated tilt knob if VAR Gain is not active.
Tilt can be varied between 15 degrees up (clockwise rotation) and 15 degrees down (counterclockwise rotation).

Adjusts on tilt minimizes ground clutter when viewing weather targets.
To find the ideal tilt angle after the airplane is airborne, adjust the TILT control so that ground clutter does not interfere with viewing of weather targets. Usually, this can be done by tilting the antenna downward in 1° increments until ground targets begin to appear at the display periphery. When ground targets are displayed, move the tilt angle upward in 1° increments until the ground targets begin to disappear.

Ground returns can be distinguished from strong storm cells by watching for closer ground targets with each small downward increment of tilt. The more the downward tilt, the closer the ground targets that are displayed.

Proper tilt adjustment is a pilot judgment, but typically the best tilt angle lies where ground targets are barely visible or just off the radar image.

The following table gives the approximate tilt settings for different altitudes and ranges.

fragen.frage: Welchen Bereich überwacht die Target Alert Funktion (TGT) des Wetterradars?

fragen.zitat: If such weather is detected within the monitored heading, outside the selected range until a range of 200 NM , the TGT annunciation changes from a green-armed condition to an amber alert condition on the MFD.
kontext:
TARGET ALERT (TGT) FUNCTION

The TGT function monitors for weather beyond the selected range and 7.5° on each side of the airplane heading.

If such weather is detected within the monitored heading, outside the selected range until a range of 200 NM the TGT annunciation changes from a green-armed condition to an amber alert condition on the MFD.

This annunciation advises the flight crew that potentially hazardous weather lies directly in front and outside of the selected range. When this warning is received, the flight crew should select longer ranges to view the questionable target. Note that TGT is inactive when hazards are within the selected range.

Selecting the TGT function forces the system to preset gain and turns off variable gain mode. Selections of ranges of 200 NM or greater automatically turns off TGT function and allows variable gain mode. It can only be selected in the WX mode.

Page 32/36 Navigation REVISION 22

NOTE: – The TGT annunciation on MFD may occur when the range is increased to 200 NM or greater, even though the function is deactivated.
– In such cases, system logic follows the TGT function annunciation, and gain is automatically preset.
– Selection of 1000 NM range always clears TGT annunciation.

kontext:
TECHNIQUE (REACT) FUNCTION

Used in WX mode to compensate for attenuation of the radar signal as it passes through a storm. It does this by increasing the gain of the receiver as weather is detected.
The cyan field indicates areas where further compensation is not possible. This is a warning indicating that attenuation is hiding possible severe weather and should be considered dangerous.

The REACT compensation is active in all modes except GMAP mode.

The REACT compensation can be active in all modes except GMAP mode.

Areas where no further compensation is possible: attenuation may hide severe weather
Areas outside radar range
fragen.erklaerung_en: The cyan field shows areas where no further compensation is possible; attenuation may hide hazardous weather and must be considered hazardous.

kontext:
CABIN MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (CMS)

The CMS (Cabin Management System) controls the main functions of passenger cabin and is controlled through a digital touch screen interface, used as flight attendant panel (FAP).

The CMS functions are:
– Moving map and connecting flight information
– Pre-recorded audio briefings
– Boarding music, and
– Cabin crew ground communication (ACARS – Airplane Communication Addressing and Reporting System), short messages.
Other system functions, controlled by the CMS functions are:
– Cabin Lighting control, including mood lighting
– Water and waste system monitoring
– Passenger attendant call monitoring
– Galley power control (ON/OFF)
– Cabin temperature setting
– IFE (In-Flight Entertainment) and connectivity control panel
– Smoke detector maintenance initiation test
– Interior system maintenance messages
– In-seat power ON/OFF control.
NOTE: The CMS equipment is powered by the DC GND SERVICE bus that is a non-essential bus and is shed during emergency conditions.

kontext:
COCKPIT PHILOSOPHY

The airplane flight deck is designed to:
– Provide the necessary means to accomplish the required tasks.
– Provide acceptable and reasonable workloads.
– Minimize pilot errors and its consequences.
– Facilitate training with the commonality among the E-Jets Family.
– Provide optimized ergonomics aimed at safety, ease of operation, control, and comfort requirements.
Both pilots can access all essential information and necessary controls for airplane operation.

Some knobs on the overhead panel have detent protection and must be pulled out to allow knob rotation. This protection prevents inadvertent knob rotation and is indicated with a detent mark between knob positions.

Knob stationary positions are marked with a white rectangle, and knob momentary positions are marked with a white triangle.
To assure proper signal transmission when using the selector knobs that have momentary positions, hold the knob for at least two seconds at the positions before releasing it.

System failures are primarily monitored via EICAS messages. The synoptics are included as an aid to pilot monitoring.

Critical systems give total authority to the pilot by employing intuitive procedures for maximum airplane performance with minimum workload. Cockpit design facilitates simple tasks as much as possible, thus leading to increased control of situation and systems. Automation is used only to improve the task accomplishment, complementing but not substituting for the crew.

kontext:
CARGO DOORS

The cargo doors located aft and forward of the wing on the right side of the fuselage are manually operated from the outside. They have a locking mechanism controlled by an external handle, stowed in the lower half of the door. The vent flap prevents pressurization of the airplane when the door is not fully closed, latched, and locked. The

Page 14/20 Doors REVISION 15

cargo doors open outward, are hinged along the upper edge, and are latched at the lower edge with four hooks.
The cargo doors were designed to support winds up to 60 kt while the door is fully open and locked.

Therefore, doors must be closed before the wind speed achieves 60 kt.

A wind of 40 kt was considered during design for door operation (opening or closing). Therefore, if the wind is above 40 kt and door operation is needed, caution must be taken during door operation since the wind direction may affect door displacement.

DOOR INTERNAL HANDLES

The main handle actuates mechanically the latch of the door.

The vent flap and the lock mechanism of the door are linked. The airplane pressurization loads the vent flap against the door structure.
The effort required to unlock the door (lift the vent flap lever) increases with the airplane pressurization level.

The arming lever arms and disarms the emergency system composed of the escape slide and door’s emergency opening mechanism by engaging or disengaging the girt bar.

During normal operations, when opening the passenger and service doors, the main handle must be moved upward only if the arming lever is in the disarmed position.

If the main handle is inadvertently moved upward while the arming lever is in the armed position, the girt bar is affected and the door operation is compromised.

In this case, return the door to the closed position, maintain the main handle at the downward position, move the arming lever to the disarmed position, and contact maintenance personnel before attempting to open the door again.

fragen.frage: Wie lange versorgt die eigene Batterie die Beleuchtung einer Escape Slide mindestens?
antworten: Mindestens 5 Minuten, nur solange die Slide angeschlossen ist
Mindestens 30 Minuten über das Emergency Lighting des Flugzeugs
Mindestens 10 Minuten, auch nachdem die Slide abgetrennt wurde
Mindestens 90 Minuten über BATT 1
fragen.erklaerung: Eine dedizierte Batterie versorgt die Slide-Beleuchtung mindestens 10 Minuten, auch nach dem Abtrennen der Slide vom Flugzeug.
fragen.zitat: A dedicated battery powers the lights for a minimum of 10 minutes even after the escape slide is disconnected.
kontext:
ESCAPE SLIDE

The escape slides are designed to provide passengers and crew means to safely descend from the airplane to the ground during an emergency evacuation. In the event of emergency evacuation, the slides deploy automatically when the exit door is opened.

The emergency evacuation slides are equipped with a lighting system independent from the airplane. The unfolding process activates the lighting system illuminating the sliding surface and the area where crew and passengers make first contact with the ground. A battery contained within the slide provides electrical power to the lights.
A dedicated battery powers the lights for a minimum of 10 minutes even after the escape slide is disconnected.

The escape slides on the passengers and service doors are armed by opening the slide arming lever cover located on the door and moving the slide arming lever down to the armed position. Opening the door from the outside automatically disarms the slide.

The overwing emergency exits (OWE) are also equipped with escape slides to support evacuation. The slides are installed on the wing- fuselage fairing and are always armed during operation. The status from the slide cylinder pressure is displayed on the Flight Attendant Panel. The slide inflates automatically when the door is open and it is only disarmed through maintenance procedures. The OWE escape slides are also equipped with emergency lights to illuminate the surrounding surface.

In ditching condition, the escape slides from the passenger and service doors are used as flotation devices after disconnection from the airplane. The OWE escape slides do not disconnect from the airplane, and may not deploy or be usable in this condition, due to the system is partially submerged. Therefore, the OWE escape slides are not considered as flotation devices.

If the mooring line that connects airplane and slide is not manually detached from the airplane, the line breaks free if enough load is applied.

14-01-50

REVISION 14 Escape Slide Page 1/8

fragen.frage: Der elektromechanische Cockpit Door Latch ist ausgefallen und verriegelt, die Tür steht offen. Wie kann die Tür geschlossen und verriegelt werden?

Mit dem Maintenance Lock auf der Kabinenseite

kontext:
ALTERNATE LOCK/INHIBIT KNOB

If the system is properly working, the alternate lock/inhibit knob must remain in the unlock position.

In case of electromechanical latch is inoperative and unlocked, the alternate lock/inhibit knob is used to lock the door by placing the knob on AL1 position. In case of electrical inhibit system is failed, the knob is used as an inhibition backup by placing the knob on the AL1 position.

If the electromechanical door latch is inoperative and locked with the door open, it is not possible to close the door entirely. In this case, alternate lock/inhibit knob is used to lock the door by placing the knob on AL2 position.

The only way to close and lock the cockpit door if the electromechanical latch is failed locked is through the alternate lock/ inhibit knob. This avoids the occurrence of the door locked with no one in the cockpit.

14-01-60

REVISION 14 Cockpit Door Page 5/12

Set the Alternate Lock/Inhibit Knob to AL2
With the Maintenance Lock on the cabin side

fragen.zitat: The door is unlocked when a new electrical pulse is sent to the electromechanical latch. The DC ESS BUS 3 powers the electromechanical latch.
kontext:
ELECTROMECHANICAL LATCH

The electrical operation is through the cockpit control panel. The control panel in the cockpit sends an electrical pulse to the electromechanical latch, which locks the door.

The door is unlocked when a new electrical pulse is sent to the electromechanical latch.

The DC ESS BUS 3 powers the electromechanical latch.

In case of electrical failure, the door latch stays in its previous setting.

Manual operation is through the manual lock/unlock knob on the electromechanical door latch. The latch locks the door when the knob is moved upwards. Once it is locked, a green indication is exposed on the latch. The latch unlocks when the manual lock/unlock knob is moved upwards again. When it is unlocked, a red indication is exposed on the latch.

The door latch indication in green and red indicates when the door is locked and open, respectively. The indication is also independently of how the electromechanical latch is operated, electrically or manually.

If the electromechanical latch is locked while the door is opened, the door does not close. It is necessary to unlock the electromechanical latch to move the door to the closed position.

kontext: BLOWOUT PANELS
The reinforced cockpit door assembly has two blowout devices to equalize sudden decompression: a decompression panel and a vent grill.

When a sudden decompression occurs, the decompression panel deploys automatically in the forward direction, providing pressure equalization. It deploys with the observer seat in use and without any type of interference or hazard to the observer.

The open vent grill allows ventilation air between cabins and in the event of decompression provides pressure equalization.

kontext:
RAINBOW LIGHTS

Rainbow lights at the forward and aft main ceiling panel provide a visual indication to attendants when there is a call from the flight crew or passengers.

The rainbow lights consist of following colored indicator lights:
– ORANGE:
a steady orange light illuminates when a passenger calls from the lavatory. Flashing orange light illuminates when smoke is detected in the lavatory.

– BLUE: a steady blue light illuminates when a passenger calls from the main cabin area.
– RED: a flashing red indicator illuminates when the flight crew makes an emergency call to the flight attendant from the cockpit.
The light stops flashing after the call is taken.
– GREEN: a flashing green indicator illuminates when the pilot calls the flight attendant from the cockpit. The light stops flashing after the call is taken.
– AMBER: a steady amber light illuminates for a sterile light call.
An audible tone sounds by the passenger address system whenever a passenger presses any attendant call switch in a PSU or in the lavatory. The tone also sounds when the flight crew presses the attendant call switch. There is also a blue steady light on the cabin

REVISION 14 Lighting Page 7/24

ceiling, indicating from which cabin area the respective passenger call was made.

NOTE: – There is no indication on the rainbow lights when a flight attendant calls another flight attendant station. It only flashes green on both handset cradles.

The external emergency lighting consists of External Overwing Emergency Lights and the External Exit Door Emergency Lights.

EMERGENCY RAM AIR VENTILATION

Emergency ram air ventilation is provided in case of pack shutdown or for smoke removal.

The flight deck pack emergency ram air ventilation valve is automatically commanded to OPEN only if both ECS cooling packs are commanded OFF or failed OFF or Dump push button on the pressurization Control Panel is pressed.

An emergency ram air ventilation check valve is provided and does not require electronic control. The emergency ram air check valve is open whenever the pressure in the ram air circuit is greater than cabin pressure.

During smoke removal, both ECS cooling packs are commanded OFF and therefore, the flight deck emergency ram air ventilation valve is commanded OPEN.

The FADEC may send an ECS OFF signal to the AMS controller, requesting that no bleed is extracted from the engine for the air conditioning system. The FADEC sets this signal depending on the T/O DATASET input (REF ECS OFF), pressure altitude, flight phase,

kontext:
SMART ECS FUNCTION

To improve fuel consumption, a feature in AMS software named Smart ECS controls packs flow in normal operation conditions. The SMART ECS calculates the optimum pack flow for each flight altitude based on airplane's model, passenger cabin layout (LOPA), and on number of occupants on board.

The input of occupants on board is retrieved from pilots entered data on FMS PERFORMANCE INIT PAGE 2/3. If the pilot fills in 0 for the number of occupants (PASS 0), the SMART ECS is disabled.
If the pilot does not fill in the number of occupants (PASS the SMART ECS considers full pax, according to airplane LOPA.

The number of occupants on board must consider passengers and crew.

14-02-15

Air Conditioning System REVISION 6 Page 1/6

APU BLEED

The APU supplies bleed air on the ground or inflight. However, it is used primarily as a ground pneumatic source for the air conditioning packs (ECS) and engine starting.
The APU Bleed Check Valve prevents reverse flow to APU when operating on engine bleed.

The APU Bleed Valve (ABV) controls the APU bleed airflow to the pneumatic system.

The APU Bleed Valve may be commanded to open when the following conditions occur simultaneously:
– APU switch is set to AUTO,
– APU Bleed is available,
– no APU and left bleed duct leak, and
– anti-ice system not requested (or anti-ice system requested ON and anti-ice system is failed).

Page 2/6 Bleed Air System REVISION 15

kontext:
OVERHEAT DETECTION SYSTEM

The Overheat Detection System (ODS) consists of overheat sensors and electronic control. They provide rapid and reliable overheat, and leak detection for the engine bleed, APU bleed air distribution, and anti-ice supply ducting.

14-02-10

REVISION 15 Bleed Air System Page 3/6
Normally the overheat sensors use dual loop sensing. In this configuration, an overheat is indicated only when both loops detect an overheat condition.
If a single loop fails, the remaining monitors for an overheat condition (single loop operation).

fragen.frage: Können APU und Engines gleichzeitig als Bleed-Quellen verwendet werden?

kontext:
BLEED SOURCE PRIORITIZATION

The AMS controller automatically selects the bleed source on ground and during flight between the engines, the APU, and the external connections.

The AMS controller chooses one bleed source between the APU bleed and the engine bleeds when both are available.
It is not possible to have both the APU and the engines as bleed sources simultaneously.

Yes, the APU supplies Pack 1 and Engine 2 supplies Pack 2
Yes, but only on the ground
Yes, in flight below 15000 ft
fragen.erklaerung_en: The AMS Controller selects between APU and Engine Bleed; both at the same time as the source is not possible.

fragen.frage: Bei welchem In-Flight-Engine-Start öffnet die Crossbleed (XBLEED auf AUTO) ohne weitere Bedingung?
antworten: Beim Start von Engine #1 mit APU Bleed ON
Bei jedem Start mit Windmilling
Bei keinem Start im Flug
Beim Start von Engine #2 im Flug
fragen.erklaerung: Die Crossbleed kann bei Engine-#2-Start im Flug öffnen; für Engine #1 im Flug nur bei APU Bleed OFF.
fragen.zitat: BLEED APU Button pushed out for main engine start, – Engine #2 start in the air, – APU bleed OFF and engine #1 start in the air.
kontext:
NORMAL OPERATION

The crossbleed may be commanded to open when the XBLEED Button is pushed in (AUTO) and any of the following conditions is met:
– One side provides manifold pressure and there is not a bleed air source on the opposite side,
–

BLEED APU Button pushed out for main engine start,
– Engine #2 start in the air,
– APU bleed OFF and engine #1 start in the air.

The crossbleed is commanded closed when any of the following conditions is met:
– Bleed leak, unless starting an engine,
– Engine fire extinguisher handle pulled,
– Manifold side with pressure above 90 psi.
fragen.frage_en: On which in-flight engine start does the crossbleed open (XBLEED on AUTO) without any further condition?
antworten_en: On Engine #1 start with APU Bleed ON
On any windmilling start
On no start in flight
On Engine #2 start in flight
fragen.erklaerung_en: The crossbleed can open on Engine #2 start in flight; for Engine #1 in flight only with APU Bleed OFF.

fragen.frage: Was macht die Altitude Limitation Protection der CPCS und welcher Kanal führt sie aus?
antworten: Sie öffnet das Safety Valve über 10000 ft; ausgeführt durch Channel A
Sie löst DUMP über 12400 ft aus; ausgeführt durch Channel B
Sie schliesst das OFV über 14500 ft Kabinenhöhe; ausgeführt durch den Safety Channel
Sie schliesst das NPRV über 14500 ft; ausgeführt durch Channel A
fragen.erklaerung: Die Altitude Limitation Protection fährt das OFV zu, wenn die Kabinenhöhe 14500 ft übersteigt; dies übernimmt der Safety Channel.
fragen.zitat: The altitude limitation protection function controls the outflow valve (OFV) to a closed position if the cabin altitude exceeeds 14500 ft. The function is performed by the Safety channel.
kontext:
AMS CONTROLLER (AMSC)

AMS controllers 1 and 2 controls cabin pressure by commanding the outflow valve to modulate airflow through the valve from the pressurized airplane volume to the surrounding environment. AMSC 1 and 2 control both automatic and manual modes functionalities.

Each AMSC has three channels:
– Channel A performs automatic control
– Channel B performs manual control (together with the Safety Channel) and an automatic backup mode while in electrical emergency or both Channel A are failed, and
– Safety Channel is responsible for the following safety functions: cabin positive overpressure relief, cabin altitude limitation protection and cabin rate of change limitation.
The channels B and Safety provide a manual function as backup, enabling the crew to control cabin pressure by directly actuating the outflow valve (OFV) position.

14-02-20

Pressurization System REVISION 1 Page 1/10

The system protects the cabin against excessive positive pressure by an electronic and pneumatic protection.
The altitude limitation protection function controls the outflow valve (OFV) to a closed position if the cabin altitude exceeeds 14500 ft. The function is performed by the Safety channel.
fragen.frage_en: What does the CPCS Altitude Limitation Protection do and which channel executes it?
antworten_en: It opens the Safety Valve above 10000 ft; executed by Channel A
It triggers DUMP above 12400 ft; executed by Channel B
It closes the OFV above 14500 ft cabin altitude; executed by the Safety Channel
It closes the NPRV above 14500 ft; executed by Channel A
fragen.erklaerung_en: The Altitude Limitation Protection closes the OFV when cabin altitude exceeds 14500 ft; this is performed by the Safety Channel.

Elektrisch gesteuert durch AMSC 1

Pneumatisch über den Static Pressure Port gesteuert

fragen.zitat: The negative pressure relief valve is a spring loaded check valve that works without any electrical power, and is independent of the CPCS.
kontext: NEGATIVE PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE (NPRV)
The negative pressure relief valve is a spring loaded check valve that works without any electrical power, and is independent of the CPCS.
Its function is to protect the airplane structure against damages due to a negative differential pressure.
fragen.frage_en: How does the Negative Pressure Relief Valve (NPRV) work?
antworten_en: As a spring-loaded check valve without electrical power, independent of the CPCS
Electrically controlled by AMSC 1
Via the CPCS Safety Channel
Pneumatically controlled via the static pressure port
fragen.erklaerung_en: The NPRV is a spring-loaded check valve that operates without electrical power and is independent of the CPCS.

fragen.frage: Für welchen Flugplatzhöhenbereich ist die CPCS für Takeoffs und Landings ausgelegt?

-1000 ft bis 10000 ft

kontext:
AUTOMATIC MODE

The CPCS automatic operation uses different information inputs from the airplane to control the cabin altitude, the differential pressure, and the cabin altitude rate of change. The main inputs are:
– Airplane altitude
– Airplane rate of change
– Calibrated airspeed
– Weight-on-wheels position
– Doors position
– Landing field elevation
– Cruise altitude
– Baro correction
– Air conditioning status
– Engine status, and
– Engines thrust lever angle.
The CPCS internal logic is divided in flight modes to better control the cabin altitude change rate in accordance with the flight phase.
The CPCS is designed to operate for takeoffs and landings from -2000 ft to 14000 ft.
fragen.frage_en: For which airport elevation range is the CPCS designed for takeoffs and landings?
antworten_en: 0 ft to 8000 ft
-2000 ft to 9200 ft
fragen.erklaerung_en: The CPCS is designed for takeoffs and landings from -2000 ft to 14000 ft.

fragen.frage: DUMP wird bei CPCS im Manual Mode gedrückt. Welche Kabinensteigrate wird bis zu welcher Höhe geregelt?

fragen.zitat: In CPCS Manual Mode, controls the OUTFLOW VALVE to maintain the cabin rate of climb at 3000 ft/min up to 14500 ft
kontext:
DUMP MODE ACTIVATION:

The DUMP function is activated pushing in the DUMP button on the pressurization panel. The DUMP function is operational for CPCS either in Automatic or Manual Modes.

In case the DUMP is activated, the CPCS automatically:
– Sets the ECS packs and recirculation fans to OFF
– In CPCS Automatic Mode, controls the OUTFLOW VALVE to maintain the cabin rate of climb at 2000 ft/min up to 12400 ft for normal takeoff and landing operation, or 14500 ft in HALTO
–
In CPCS Manual Mode, controls the OUTFLOW VALVE to maintain the cabin rate of climb at 3000 ft/min up to 14500 ft

– When the cabin altitude reaches the above set points, it commands the OUTFLOW VALVE to full closed. From this point the cabin altitude rises due to the fuselage natural leakages.
In case higher cabin rates of climb are necessary, the manual mode can be used selecting the cabin altitude to up position on the CABIN ALT rotary knob on the pressurization panel.

fragen.erklaerung_en: In Manual Mode, with DUMP the CPCS maintains a cabin rate of climb of 3000 ft/min up to 14500 ft.

kontext:
– CRUISE FLIGHT LEVEL DATA AVAILABLE IN THE FMS:

14-02-20

Pressurization System Page 8/10 REVISION 1

– CABIN ALTITUDE CHANGE RATE - The CPCS calculates the most comfortable rate of climb according to the cruise altitude set in the FMS. The rate of climb is calculated depending on the ambient pressure at the takeoff field. The system internal range is limited to +500 ft/min for increasing cabin altitude and constant at -300 ft/min for decreasing cabin altitude.
– If the FMS cruise altitude is set at or below FL370, the cabin altitude target is set proportional to the set cruise altitude, according to the cabin pressure schedule.
At 37000 ft, the cabin altitude target is set to the maximum of 7900 ft, to a maximum cabin differential pressure of 7.8 psid.

– If either the FMS cruise altitude is set higher than FL370, the cabin altitude target is set to the maximum of 7900 ft, and the maximum nominal differential pressure is 8.4 psid at 41000 ft.
– In case a step climb is performed, the cabin altitude continuously increases even at the level off altitude until the airplane reaches the target cruise altitude set in the FMS.
– In case the airplane experiences higher altitudes than the selected on the FMS, the cabin altitude target is according to the cabin pressure schedule, proportional to the airplane altitude.

fragen.erklaerung_en: At 37000 ft the Cabin Altitude Target is set to a maximum of 7900 ft, at a maximum of 7.8 psid.

kontext:
ROLL HOLD (ROLL)

The Roll Hold is the basic lateral mode and does not provide any airplane guidance.

Depending on the airplane bank angle at the moment of ROLL activation, the autopilot maintains the following bank angles until another lateral mode is selected:
– Bank angle at 6° or below: AP levels the wings.
–

Bank angle above 6° and below 30°: AP holds present bank angle.
– Bank angle at 30° or above: AP maintains bank angle at 30°.

fragen.frage: Was ist nach dem Drücken des AP-Buttons nötig, damit Autopilot und BOID sicher engagen?

Die Thrust Levers müssen in TO/GA stehen

fragen.zitat: After pushing the AP button on the guidance panel, the control column must be in neutral position within 2 s to guarantee the engagement of autopilot and Breakout Increase Device (BOID).
kontext:
AP ENGAGEMENT AND DISENGAGEMENT

ENGAGEMENT

Autopilot engagement is inhibited on the ground.

In flight, the autopilot is engaged pushing the AP button on the guidance panel. The AP engagement is verified on the FMA on both PFDs.

With the confirmation of the AP label on the FMA the autopilot is controlling the airplane pitch, roll and yaw according to the flight director selections.
After pushing the AP button on the guidance panel, the control column must be in neutral position within 2 s to guarantee the engagement of autopilot and Breakout Increase Device (BOID).

With the autopilot engaged, the BOID actuates and provides extra resistance on the control yoke. The BOID actuates to avoid inadvertent disengagement of the autopilot by the flight crew.

Page 2/40 Flight Guidance Control System REVISION 15

DISENGAGEMENT

The Thrust Levers must be in TO/GA
The FD bars must be centered
The Control Column must be neutral within 2 s
fragen.erklaerung_en: After pressing the AP button, the Control Column must be neutral within 2 s to ensure AP and BOID engagement.

kontext:
OVERSPEED PROTECTION (OVSP)

The AFCS provides overspeed detection and protection to maintain the speed below Vmo/Mmo limits.

When the autopilot and/or the autothrottle are engaged, pitch and/or thrust are adjusted to prevent overspeed.
When the FGCS is disengaged, only aural warning “HIGHSPEED” is triggered requiring pilot input to avoid overspeeds.

When the OVSP protection activates, an amber OVSP indication displays on the FMA. The previous active mode is displayed as armed (white) and becomes active again when OVSP protection is no longer active.

The Autothrottle automatically reduces thrust
Pitch is increased automatically
There is no warning at all
fragen.erklaerung_en: If the FGCS is disengaged, only the HIGHSPEED aural warning is triggered; pilot input is required.

In case of the Slat/Flap position is different than 5 or Full, the retard mode activates only when the airplane touches down.

kontext:
CLIMB THRUST RATING (CLB)

The Pratt Whitney PW1900G engines have two modes of climb thrust:
Climb 1 (CLB-1) and Climb 2 (CLB-2).

CLB-1 is the default mode after airplane power-up. The selection of CLB-1 or CLB-2 is possible on the THRUST RATING SELECT page.

14-03-20

Page 8/10 Thrust Management REVISION 14

CLB-1 and CLB-2 thrust ratings change with altitude.
After takeoff, CLB-1 provides higher climb thrust than CLB-2. At high altitudes, CLB-2 provides higher climb thrust than CLB-1.

NOTE: At high altitudes, it is not recommended to change from CLB-1 to CLB-2 with the intention of increasing thrust.

– CLB-1: Maximum climb rate;
– CLB-2: Climb thrust derated from CLB-1.

If takeoff thrust rating is lower than the climb rating, the initial climb N1 target is modified to the takeoff thrust decreased by 1%. This logic prevents the system from increasing thrust during transition from takeoff mode to climb mode. During this transition, with AT engaged, the thrust levers move from TO/GA to corresponding initial climb position. This lever movement may cause a significant rearward movement but it represents a small N1 change. After the transition, the system resumes operational logic, changing N1 target according with altitude.
N1 target

Fuel for normal start and operation of APU is supplied by the right wing tank. If only DC power is available on ground, the DC fuel pump provides fuel to start the APU.

kontext:
RAM AIR TURBINE (RAT)

The Ram Air Turbine (RAT) is an emergency AC electrical device installed in the airplane nose section. In flight, there is no altitude restriction for the RAT deployment, and the minimum deployment speed is 150 kt.
If the minimum deployment speed is respected, whenever the AC power sources are not powering the AC buses, the RAT is automatically deployed. In about 8 s, the RAT starts supplying power

to the AC ESS BUS.

The RAT also powers the DC ESS BUSES through the ESS TRU. To avoid total loss of power during the RAT deployment and speeding up period, batteries are used as backup to power the DC ESS BUSES.

14-05-10

REVISION 15 AC System Page 3/6

Even if normal electrical power is re-established, once deployed, the RAT cannot be stowed back in flight. In this case, the RAT keeps providing power to the AC ESS BUS and DC ESS BUS 3.

The RAT electrical power drives the AC Motor-driven Pump (ACMP 3A) for commands on primary flight controls, including high lift system actuation. It also provides power to the essential avionics, communication, and battery recharging.

The RAT requires a minimum of 130 kt to ensure continuous power supply to AC/DC ESS BUSES. At speeds below 130 kt, the RAT is not capable of supplying power to all essential buses, so the batteries automatically connect to the DC ESS BUSES, while the RAT keeps feeding the AC ESS BUS until a certain airspeed.

In case of failure on automatic RAT deployment, a deployment handle is available to release the RAT manually.

Whenever an electrical power transfer is needed between the AC power sources, the electrical system performs a No-Break Power Transfer (NBPT) on ground or a Break Power Transfer (BPT) in flight.

CONTROL (FADEC)

The FADEC is the main component of the engine control system.

– Engine protection
– Control of the requested and maximum N1, and
– Control of the ATTCS.

The FADEC in-control channel is switched at every engine shutdown.

The ignition system provides an electrical spark to ignite the fuel-air mixture in the combustion chamber, during ground, inflight start attempts and for automatic relight.

kontext:
STABILIZER TRIM

The manual trim is commanded through switches installed on the control columns or a backup switch on the main pedestal.

The backup trim switch and the control wheel trim switches are dual split switches. The aural warning “TRIM” triggers for 6 s when the control wheel trim or backup trim switches have failed or when only half of switch is pressed. If only one half of the switch is actuated or the failure persists for more than 6 s, that switch is automatically deactivated. In this case, the aural warning is deactivated and the applicable advisory pitch trim switch fail message is displayed on
EICAS.
In order to avoid a possible pitch trim runaway condition, manual pilot trim commands are limited to 3 s

After the control wheel trim or backup trim switches have both halves pressed for more than 3 s, the timer stops the horizontal stabilizer control surface movement. If the trim switch remains pressed, the aural warning “TRIM” triggers. When the trim switch is no more pressed, the aural warning stops.

When flying in normal mode, the FCCs inhibit commands to the horizontal stabilizer via elevator offload function according to the following:
– Pitch up direction, in case of stall protection engagement.
– Pitch down direction, in case of high-speed protection engagement.
Stabilizer Trim Priority Logic

The FCCs and HSCU process the trim inputs with the following priority:
1. Backup switches.
2. Left seat switches.
3. Right seat switches.

fragen.zitat: If the airplane exceeds the maximum angle of attack for the Normal flight envelope, the stall protection engages. The angle of attack equivalent for engagement is near to 1.08Vsr.
kontext:
STALL PROTECTION

The stall protection activates to prevent stall either during maneuvers or gusty scenarios.
If the airplane exceeds the maximum angle of attack for the Normal flight envelope, the stall protection engages. The angle of attack equivalent for engagement is near to 1.08Vsr.

If the airplane exceeds the maximum angle of attack at the Normal Flight Envelope boundary, the stall protection engages and reduces the control column nose up authority. Further pitch up commands eventually lead to stick shaker activation.

Unusual and aggressive maneuvers, such high deceleration or high pitch rates, may anticipate the limits for stall protection engagement.
To provide suitable anticipation commands, stall protection also takes into account several effects due to Mach number, roll rate, ice conditions and anti-ice system failures.

When the protection is active the column position defines a reference angle of attack, instead of a load factor command. Full aft column deflection commands the maximum allowable safe angle of attack below stall. If the column is kept at a neutral position, the airplane gradually converges to the normal flight envelope.

kontext:
NORMAL OPERATION

During normal operation, the IESS computes and displays attitude, slip-skid indication, altitude (baro corrected), airspeed, vertical speed, Mach number and IESS.

The buttons functionalities are:
– CAGE pushbutton: if depressed, the standby performs a CAGE in the internal gyros to cancel the accumulated drift.
– ILS button: if pressed, glideslope and localizer deviations is displayed.
– STD button: if pressed, STD baro is set. To adjust baro, rotate the knob.
– and buttons: controls display brightness.
– "Push FT-M" in the Guidance Panel: automatically displays altitude in meters.
– "MAIN PNL" in the Overhead Panel: controls IESI bezel illumination.
The IESS is powered as soon as the airplane battery 1 is selected to ON and airplane battery 2 is selected to AUTO.

Then, the IESS starts its alignment phase. The initial IESS alignment takes about 90 seconds to be completed and can be identified on the screen by the "INIT 90 s" flag.

NOTE: The airplane must not be moved during the first 90 seconds after power-up, while the IESS is undergoing alignment.
Moving the airplane during this period can cause in-flight attitude indication errors that may not be noticeable on ground.

INERTIAL REFERENCE SYSTEM (IRS)

The inertial system computes airplane position, ground speed, heading and attitude.

The main component of the IRS is the Inertial Reference Unit (IRU).
The IRU interfaces with the Modular Avionic Unit (MAU), Global Positioning System (GPS) and the Air Data Computer (ADC). The IRU provides output data to the PFD, weather radar, Multifunction Control Display Unit (MCDU), Flight Management System (FMS) and reversionary panel.
Primary source for the left seat pilot PFD is the IRS 1 and for the right seat pilot PFD is IRS 2.

kontext:
– ALTITUDE AIDING

– FAILED

REVISION 14 Navigation Page 7/72

After power is applied, the acquisition mode is used to acquire satellites. The GPS tracks four satellites to acquire its position.
When fewer than four satellites are tracked, altitude aiding is the active mode, otherwise choose the appropriated navigation mode.

In altitude aiding mode GPS uses altitude from the digital air data computer (ADS) to help position determination.

The GPS is also capable to receive Satelite-Based Augmentation System (SBAS) to improve signals and provide a more accurate position output.
The approach with LPV minimums is selected in the FMS and inserted on the active flight plan. Once LPV mode is engaged, the autopilot also uses the GPS deviations to control the airplane.
Any faults within the GPS module is reported on the FMS MCDU and on the EICAS. The Message ("MSG") indicator on the PFD illuminates, and "GPS 1 FAIL" or "GPS 2 FAIL" advisory CAS message is displayed. The GPS STATUS SENSOR page also displays the GPS failure indication.

Position is taken exclusively from IRS data

kontext:
PREDICTIVE RAIM (PRAIM)

The GPS predictive RAIM function is used to predict Destination and Alternate waypoint. Predictive RAIM uses an almanac function that is updated whenever the GPS is tracking satellites. Pilot can manually deselect or enable the Satellites for destination and alternate waypoint prediction.

Page 8/72 Navigation REVISION 14

When the FMS makes the automatic RAIM prediction, if RAIM will be exceeded, the RAIM WILL EXCEED LIMIT message is displayed in the MCDU scratchpad, and the MSG annunciator is displayed on the PFD.

This function calculates whether the satellite geometry is acceptable for approach at the expected destination at the estimated time of arrival (ETA).
On ground, to compute an ETA, the pilot must enter an ETD (ORIGIN/ETD) on the initial FLT PLAN page.

The predictive RAIM page is accessed by selecting the PRED RAIM prompt from any GPS STATUS page. On PREDICTIVE RAIM page YES indicates that RAIM is predicted to be within approach criteria, and NO indicates that RAIM is predicted to be unacceptable or unavailable.

If GPS fails or the interface between the FMS and GPS not work properly, the FMS displays the message PREDICTIVE RAIM UNAVAILABLE on the PREDICTIVE RAIM page.

The selection of DEST prompt from the PREDICTIVE RAIM page displays DESTINATION RAIM page.

On this page, the pilot can exclude any GPS satellite scheduled to be out of service according to published GPS NOTAMs, from the DESTINATION RAIM predictions.

– Manually

ABNORMAL OPERATION

In case of mode failure, power loss, or loss of one IRU, the reversion of the IRS source is performed automatically.
A generic failure which affects both IRS sensors can lead the loss of the attitude information on both PFD, as well as a Direct Mode reversion.

kontext:
DIGITAL VOICE DATA RECORDER (DVDR)

SYSTEM

The digital voice data recorder system (DVDR) includes the functionalities flight data recorder (FDR), cockpit voice recorder (CVR), and Datalink Recorder (DLR) in a single unit. Two DVDR units are installed. DVDR 1 is installed in the forward electronic bay, and the DVDR 2 in the aft electronic bay. Each unit receives, records and preserves all required data parameters and voice recordings from the cockpit crew and area microphones. Additionally, the DVDR 1 is equipped with an internal RIPS (Recorder Independent Power Supply) which supplies power to the CVR whenever there is an airplane power loss.
Airplanes equipped with CVR 120 min

The DVDR unit is capable of recording the last 120 min of audio information from cockpit area microphone and primary crew microphones, 120 min of datalink messages and at least 25 h of flight data.

Airplanes equipped with CVR 25 h

The DVDR unit is capable of recording the last 25 h of audio information from cockpit area microphone and primary crew microphones, 25 h of datalink messages and at least 25 h of flight data.

Page 14/52 Communication REVISION 15

The DVDR automatically starts recording audio information as soon as power up is performed.
Flight data recording begins when the first engine is started. After power down, the DVDR continues recording audio information for 10 min.

If the DVDR power system fails, an EICAS message is generated to indicate the failure. All DVDR EICAS messages are advisory and some of them are inhibited in critical phases of flight, such as takeoff.

kontext:

kontext:
FUEL CROSSFEED

The crossfeed operation permits fuel supply to both engines from one wing tank, leveling fuel quantities in both wing tanks and avoiding a fuel imbalance condition. During single engine operation, the crossfeed is also used to supply fuel to the operative engine from both wing tanks.

Setting the crossfeed selector knob to either LOW 1 or LOW 2 position:
– opens the crossfeed valve
– activates the AC fuel pump of the opposite wing tank.
The EICAS message FUEL IMBALANCE displays when an imbalance condition between both wing tanks is equal or greater than 360 kg (800 lb).
After the imbalance is less than 45 kg (100 lb), the EICAS message FUEL EQUAL – XFEED OPEN displays, indicating a crossfeed operation with no imbalance condition.

If a crossfeed operation is commanded before the EICAS message FUEL IMBALANCE is triggered, the EICAS message FUEL EQUAL – XFEED OPEN displays.

The following table shows the position of crossfeed selector knob to correct or avoid a fuel imbalance.
fragen.frage_en: At what imbalance does the message FUEL EQUAL – XFEED OPEN appear during crossfeed?

When the imbalance has dropped below 100 kg (220 lb)
When the imbalance has reached zero
When the imbalance has dropped below 45 kg (100 lb)
fragen.erklaerung_en: When the imbalance drops below 45 kg (100 lb), FUEL EQUAL – XFEED OPEN appears as an indication of an open crossfeed without imbalance.

kontext:
HYDRAULIC PUMP 2

The Electric Hydraulic Pump 1 (ACMP 1B) and the Electric Hydraulic Pump 2 (ACMP 2B) are an alternating current motor pumps.
They serve as a backup for the EDP 1 and 2. The AC BUS 2 powers the ACMP 1. The AC BUS 1 powers the ACMP 2.

A three-position selector knob on the hydraulic panel enables the flight crew to select OFF, AUTO (normal operation), or ON positions.

In flight, the Electric Hydraulic Pump is activated in case of EDP or engine failure.

On ground, the Electric Hydraulic Pump is automatically activated in any of the following conditions:
– During the PBIT of the respective ACMP, or
– Opposite engine is running (N2 higher than 54%) and Emergency/ Parking Brake is released.

14-11-10

Page 2/6 Hydraulic System Description REVISION 15

NOTE: – If Emergency/Parking Brake is applied during engine start before N2 reaches 54%, the Electric Hydraulic Pump will not be activated until Emergency/Parking Brake is released.
– The Electric Hydraulic Pump automatically turns off after 6 min have elapsed from Emergency/Parking Brake application.

3 - SYS 1 ELEC PUMP AND SYS 2 ELEC PUMP KNOBS

OFF: turns the associated electrical pump off.
AUTO: allows the associated electrical pump to operate automatically. In flight, it activates the electric pump in case of EDP or engine fail.

kontext:
HYDRAULIC PUMP 2

The Electric Hydraulic Pump 1 (ACMP 1B) and the Electric Hydraulic Pump 2 (ACMP 2B) are an alternating current motor pumps. They serve as a backup for the EDP 1 and 2. The AC BUS 2 powers the ACMP 1. The AC BUS 1 powers the ACMP 2.

A three-position selector knob on the hydraulic panel enables the flight crew to select OFF, AUTO (normal operation), or ON positions.

In flight, the Electric Hydraulic Pump is activated in case of EDP or engine failure.

On ground, the Electric Hydraulic Pump is automatically activated in any of the following conditions:
– During the PBIT of the respective ACMP, or
– Opposite engine is running (N2 higher than 54%) and Emergency/ Parking Brake is released.

14-11-10

Page 2/6 Hydraulic System Description REVISION 15

NOTE: – If Emergency/Parking Brake is applied during engine start before N2 reaches 54%, the Electric Hydraulic Pump will not be activated until Emergency/Parking Brake is released.
–
The Electric Hydraulic Pump automatically turns off after 6 min have elapsed from Emergency/Parking Brake application.

After 2 min

antworten: EDP 1 ausgefallen

fragen.zitat: The PTU is automatically started when all of the following conditions are met: – Flaps not set to zero or landing gear not up and locked – EDP 1 not failed – Hydraulic reservoir 2 quantity above 15%.
kontext:
POWER TRANSFER UNIT (PTU)

The PTU consists of a hydraulic pump in Hydraulic System 2 driven by a hydraulic motor installed in Hydraulic System 1. It is used for landing gear retraction in case of EDP 2 or engine 2 failure.

A three-position selector knob on the hydraulic panel enables the flight crew to select OFF, AUTO, or ON positions. Normal operation is automatic.

14-11-10

REVISION 15 Hydraulic System Description Page 3/6

The PTU is automatically started when all of the following conditions are met:
– Flaps not set to zero or landing gear not up and locked
– EDP 1 not failed
– Hydraulic reservoir 2 quantity above 15%.

If any malfunction is detected in the PTU, the HYD PTU FAIL EICAS caution message is displayed. In this case, the crew may set the PTU selector knob to ON or OFF position, overriding the system logic, according to the applicable abnormal procedure.

fragen.erklaerung_en: The PTU starts automatically when Flaps are not at 0 or Landing Gear is not up and locked, EDP 1 has not failed and Reservoir 2 is above 15%.

kontext:
HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS 1 AND 2

Each hydraulic system consists of one reservoir, one Engine-Driven Pump (EDP 1 and EDP 2), one electric hydraulic pump (ACMP 1 and ACMP 2), and one accumulator. The Hydraulic system 2 has one PTU.

Hydraulic System 1 supplies the following systems:
– Elevator (LH outboard actuator)
– Rudder (upper actuator)
– Engine 1 Thrust Reverser

– Multifunction spoilers (left and right panels 4 and 5)
– Ground spoilers (left and right panel 2)
– Outboard brake, and
– Emergency/Parking Brake.
The Hydraulic System 2 supplies the following systems:
– Elevator (LH and RH inboard actuators)
– Ailerons (LH and RH inboard actuators)
– Engine 2 Thrust Reverser
– Multifunction Spoilers (LH and RH panels 3 and 6)
– Ground spoilers (LH and RH panel 1)
– Inboard brake
– Nose wheel steering
– Main landing gear (MLG) doors
– Landing gear (retraction and extension), and
– Emergency/Parking Brake.

fragen.erklaerung_en: Hydraulic System 1 supplies, among others, the LH Outboard Elevator Actuator, the Upper Rudder Actuator and the Engine 1 Thrust Reverser.

fragen.frage: Was gilt während einer Electrical Emergency für den Overheat-Schutz des Hydraulic System 3?
antworten: Er ist inhibitiert, damit die Electric Pumps nicht automatisch abgeschaltet werden
Er schaltet die ACMP 3A bereits bei HYD 3 HI TEMP ab
Er ist aktiv und schaltet automatisch auf ACMP 3B um
Er wird durch die PTU ersetzt
fragen.erklaerung: In einer Electrical Emergency ist der Overheat-Schutz von System 3 inhibitiert, damit die einzige verfügbare Hydraulikquelle nicht abgeschaltet wird; HYD 3 HI TEMP und OVERHEAT sind ebenfalls inhibitiert.
fragen.zitat: During an Electrical Emergency condition, the Hydraulic System 3 overheating protection system is inhibited, therefore preventing the Electric Hydraulic Pumps from being turned off automatically.
kontext:
ABNORMAL OPERATION

The Hydraulic System 3 is also equipped with an overheat protection system. Normal temperature display is green, high temperature is amber reverse video, and overheat is red reverse video. High and overheat temperatures generate a CAS message. In the event of hydraulic system overheating, the HYD 3 OVERHEAT EICAS warning message is displayed. In this case, the flight crew can manually switch OFF pumps 3A and 3B on the hydraulic system control panel.

NOTE:
During an Electrical Emergency condition, the Hydraulic System 3 overheating protection system is inhibited, therefore preventing the Electric Hydraulic Pumps from being turned off automatically.

In this condition, the associated EICAS messages HYD 3 HI TEMP and HYD 3 OVERHEAT are also inhibited. This inhibition prevents the flight crew from switching off the only source of hydraulic power available.

14-11-10

Page 4/6 Hydraulic System Description REVISION 15
fragen.frage_en: What applies to the overheat protection of Hydraulic System 3 during an Electrical Emergency?
antworten_en: It is inhibited so that the Electric Pumps are not shut off automatically
It shuts off ACMP 3A already at HYD 3 HI TEMP
It is active and switches automatically to ACMP 3B
It is replaced by the PTU
fragen.erklaerung_en: In an Electrical Emergency, the overheat protection of System 3 is inhibited so that the only available hydraulic source is not shut off; HYD 3 HI TEMP and OVERHEAT are also inhibited.

fragen.frage: Welche Aufgabe hat der Accumulator des Hydraulic System 3 in einer Electrical Emergency?

Er versorgt die zugehörigen Flight Controls vom RAT Deployment bis zum Neustart der ACMP 3A
Er hält den Druck für das Ausfahren des Landing Gear aufrecht
Er treibt die PTU an, bis die RAT ausgefahren ist
