abschnitte.text: **Merke:** APU Bleed nie für Anti-Ice und nie gleichzeitig mit Engine Bleed. Die CPCS braucht ein korrektes FMS Cruise Level und die richtige Destination (LFE). Fehlt die LFE, rechnet das System mit 8000 ft. Und im Manual Mode muss die Crew selbst vor der Landung depressurisieren (max. 0.2 psi bei Takeoff und Landing).
abschnitte.text_en: **Remember:** APU bleed never for anti-ice and never simultaneously with engine bleed. The CPCS needs a correct FMS cruise level and the correct destination (LFE). Without LFE the system uses 8000 ft. And in manual mode the crew must depressurize before landing (max 0.2 psi at takeoff and landing).

quellen.zitat: The Cabin Pressure Control System (CPCS) is part of the AMS, but it has a separate controller.
During the AMS operation, if the active channel fails, the control of the system will be automatically transferred to the other channel, with no interruption of AMS system functions.

Bleed air is provided to the Air Management System by the engines, or the APU. The bleed air is used for: – Environmental Control System (ECS); – Engine start; – Engine anti-ice and wing anti-ice; – Water pressurization.
The engine bleed system alternately selects between low pressure and high pressure engine bleed sources in order to maintain adequate and safe bleed supply pressure at any engine-operating condition.
– Respective bleed switch is set to AUTO. – Respective engine bleed is available. – No fire is detected in the respective engine. – No bleed duct leak is detected.
The system will automatically shut down the affected bleed system by closing the engine bleed valves when a leak, overpressure or fail condition is identified.
The APU supplies bleed air on the ground or inflight. However, it is used primarily as a ground pneumatic source for the air conditioning packs (ECS) and engine starting.
– APU switch is set to AUTO. – APU Bleed is available. – No APU and left bleed duct leak. – Left engine bleed is unavailable.

– Bleed leak, unless starting an engine, – Engine FIRE EXTINGUISHER Handle pulled, – Manifold side with pressure above 90 psi.
A dedicated high pressure Engine Start Ground Connection is available for engine starting and a low pressure Air Conditioned Ground Connection is available for air conditioning.
It is not possible to have both the APU and the engines as bleed sources simultaneously.
– Ground speed is below 50 kt and 30 s have passed after touchdown. – Either REF ECS is OFF and REF A/I is not ALL on the MCDU T/O DATA SET MENU page or the airplane is single engine taxiing.
If the ground speed exceeds 50 kt when taxiing only with the engine 2, the APU and engine 2 will supply bleed for packs 1 and 2 respectively.
The APU bleed cannot be used for the anti-ice system operation.

Each engine normally supplies bleed air to the respective pack. A single pack is capable of keeping adequate cabin/cargo hold pressurization and temperature. Single engine bleed can supply both ECS packs using the cross bleed.
During normal operation, pack 1 adjusts the airflow and flight deck temperature according to the CKPT temperature selector knob position.
The total flow entering the cockpit and the passenger cabin is made up of approximately 52% of fresh air and 48% of recirculation air.
– Both packs are commanded OFF; – During on ground, cabin warm-up mode with the APU as bleed source according to a function of ambient temperature and altitude; – The cargo bay fire signal activates;

It automatically opens whenever the gasper air supply exceeds 35°C (95°F).
In order to improve cabin temperature control, keep the operative temperature selector knob at 12 o‘clock position when on ground.

The ECS OFF signal CLOSES the packs during takeoff if any of the following conditions occur: – One engine inoperative and APU bleed is not available; – Thrust levers set to MAX position and APU bleed is not available;
– T/O DATASET REF ECS set to OFF on the MCDU and APU bleed is not available; – T/O DATASET REF ECS set to OFF and T/O DATASET REF A/I set to ALL on the MCDU.

– The airplane is above 9700 ft, for takeoff fields at 8000 ft or below and one engine inoperative; – The airplane is above 15000 ft, for takeoff fields above 8000 ft and one engine inoperative;
The AMS controller disregards the ECS OFF signal when the airplane is above 15000 ft.

artikel.kurz: Ice Detection, Engine- und Wing Anti-Ice-Logik (TO DATASET REF A/I, AUTO/ON), Windshield Heating, Probe Heating, Wiper, Ice Speeds und die wichtigsten Abnormals der E190/E195.
artikel.kurz_en: Ice detection, engine and wing anti-ice logic (TO DATASET REF A/I, AUTO/ON), windshield heating, probe heating, wipers, ice speeds and the key abnormals of the E190/E195.

abschnitte.text:
Das Ice Protection System der E1 besteht aus **Engine Anti-Ice**, **Wing Anti-Ice**, den **Windshield Heaters** und zwei **Ice Detectors**. Engine und Wing Anti-Ice arbeiten mit **Bleed Air der Triebwerke** als Wärmequelle; die Windshields werden elektrisch beheizt.

Die Engine Cowls werden mit Luft aus der **Low Stage Bleed** des jeweiligen Triebwerks beheizt, jedes Engine Anti-Ice ist unabhängig. Das Engine Anti-Ice Valve ist **fail safe open**: fehlt das elektrische oder das pneumatische Signal, geht es auf. Beim Wing Anti-Ice werden die **drei äusseren Slats** (outboard leading edges) jeder Seite beheizt, jede Engine versorgt ihre eigene Flügelseite.

Wichtig für die Praxis: Die **APU kann keine Bleed Air für Anti-Ice** liefern. Fällt eine Bleed aus, öffnet das System automatisch die **Crossbleed** und versorgt beide Flügel mit der Gegenseite. Um asymmetrisches Anti-Ice zu verhindern, wird bei einem Ausfall einer Seite auch die andere Seite inoperativ, ebenso, wenn die Crossbleed bei Single Bleed Betrieb geschlossen bleibt.

Im Normalbetrieb steuert das System die Ventile automatisch (Mode Knob **AUTO**). Eine spezielle Logik konfiguriert Anti-Ice und FADEC für den Takeoff in Icing Conditions. Gesetzt wird sie über die **T/O DATASET MENU** Seite im MCDU (REF A/I).
abschnitte.text_en:
The E1 ice protection system consists of **engine anti-ice**, **wing anti-ice**, the **windshield heaters** and two **ice detectors**. Engine and wing anti-ice use **engine bleed air** as the heat source; the windshields are heated electrically.

The engine cowls are heated with air from the **low stage bleed** of the respective engine; each engine anti-ice system is independent. The engine anti-ice valve is **fail safe open**: if either the electrical or the pressure signal is missing, it opens. Wing anti-ice heats the **three outboard slats** (outboard leading edges) on each side; each engine supplies its own wing.

Important in practice: the **APU cannot supply bleed air for anti-ice**. If one bleed fails, the system automatically opens the **crossbleed** and supplies both wings from the opposite side. To prevent asymmetric anti-ice, a failure on one side also makes the other side inoperative, likewise if the crossbleed remains closed during single bleed operation.

In normal operation the system controls the valves automatically (mode knob **AUTO**). A special logic configures anti-ice and FADEC for takeoff in icing conditions. It is set on the **T/O DATASET MENU** page in the MCDU (REF A/I).

abschnitte.text:
**Icing Conditions (OM-B 2.8.3.3 / 1.4.7.1):** OAT (am Boden) bzw. TAT (im Flug) **10°C oder weniger** und sichtbare Feuchtigkeit (Wolken, Nebel mit Sicht 1 Meile oder weniger, Regen, Schnee, Schneeregen, Eiskristalle) **oder** Eis, Schnee, Slush oder stehendes Wasser auf Ramp, Taxiway oder Runway. Ist sichtbare Feuchtigkeit nicht sicher feststellbar, ist sie anzunehmen.

**Am Boden nicht** auf sichtbaren Eisansatz oder die Ice Detectors verlassen, Temperatur- und Feuchtigkeitskriterien anwenden. Zu spätes Einschalten kann zu Ice Ingestion bis hin zu Engine Damage oder Flameout führen. Für die Anti-Ice-Automatik gibt es keine Temperaturlimite. **Takeoff in FZRA, +FZRA, FZDZ, +FZDZ ist verboten.**
abschnitte.text_en:
**Icing conditions (OM-B 2.8.3.3 / 1.4.7.1):** OAT (on ground) or TAT (in flight) **10°C or less** with visible moisture (clouds, fog with visibility of one mile or less, rain, snow, sleet, ice crystals) **or** ice, snow, slush or standing water on ramps, taxiways or runways. If visible moisture is not ascertained, assume it is present.

**On ground, do not** rely on visual icing evidence or the ice detectors. Apply the temperature and moisture criteria. Delayed activation may result in ice ingestion and possible engine damage or flameout. There is no temperature limitation for automatic anti-ice operation. **Takeoff in FZRA, +FZRA, FZDZ, +FZDZ is prohibited.**

abschnitte.titel: Ice Detectors, AUTO und ON im Flug
abschnitte.titel_en: Ice detectors, AUTO and ON in flight
abschnitte.text:
Zwei **Ice Detectors** links und rechts an der Rumpfnase. Detektieren sie im Flug Eis, öffnen sie Wing und Engine Anti-Ice Valves; diese bleiben **5 Minuten** nach Ende der detektierten Icing Condition aktiv (AOM-Konfiguration „Anti-ice with 5 minutes configuration OR PRE-MOD SB 190-24-0021“). Auf der Anti-Ice Synoptic erscheint dabei **ICE CONDITION**.

Fällt **ein Detector** aus, geht nur die Redundanz verloren. Der verbleibende aktiviert das System weiterhin. Bei **Ausfall eines oder beider Detectors** muss die Crew den Mode Selector auf **ON** stellen, wenn Icing Conditions bei **10°C TAT oder weniger** mit sichtbarer Feuchtigkeit bestehen oder erwartet werden (AFM-Procedure ICE DETECTOR FAIL: im Icing ON, **2 Minuten** nach Verlassen wieder AUTO). **ON** übersteuert die Logik im Flug und aktiviert Anti-Ice unabhängig von der Icing Condition; am Boden folgt es der Systemlogik.

Unabhängig davon bleibt die Crew verantwortlich, Icing Conditions zu überwachen und das System manuell einzuschalten, wenn die Detection es nicht tut. Wird Eis an Windshield, Wiper oder Flügel festgestellt oder vermutet: Mode Knob ON und **Ice Speeds** fliegen.

**Undetected Envelope Logic:** Unter bestimmten Bedingungen wird das **Wing** Anti-Ice auch ohne detektiertes Eis aktiviert (ohne ICE CONDITION-Anzeige): im Flug, unter **22000 ft**, passende Kombination aus Temperatur, Höhe und Speed, **150–320 KIAS** und Vertical Speed zwischen **–200 und +200 ft/min**. Sind alle Bedingungen **2 min** erfüllt, schaltet das System ein und bleibt bis **2 min** nach Wegfall einer Bedingung aktiv.

**SAI IBIT:** Das Wing Anti-Ice testet sich im Flug selbst, **10 min nach Takeoff oder bei 10000 ft AGL** (was zuerst eintritt). Dabei öffnen die Slat Anti-Ice Valves (Status A-I WING VLV OPEN). Der Test dauert maximal **80 s** und endet früher, wenn alle Slat-Sensoren um 5.5°C (10°F) gestiegen sind. Ein Fehler zeigt A-I WING FAIL.
abschnitte.text_en:
Two **ice detectors** are installed on the left and right of the nose section. If they detect ice in flight they open the wing and engine anti-ice valves, which remain active for **5 minutes** after the icing condition is no longer detected (AOM configuration “Anti-ice with 5 minutes configuration OR PRE-MOD SB 190-24-0021”). **ICE CONDITION** is shown on the anti-ice synoptic.

If **one detector** fails, only redundancy is lost. The remaining one still activates the system. With **one or both detectors failed**, the crew must set the mode selector to **ON** when icing conditions exist or are anticipated at **10°C TAT or below** with visible moisture (AFM procedure ICE DETECTOR FAIL: ON in icing, back to AUTO **2 minutes** after exiting). **ON** overrides the logic in flight and activates anti-ice regardless of icing condition; on ground it follows the system logic.

Regardless, the crew remains responsible for monitoring icing conditions and switching the system on manually if detection does not. If ice is detected or suspected on windshield, wiper or wing: mode knob ON and fly **ice speeds**.

**Undetected envelope logic:** under specific conditions the **wing** anti-ice is activated even without detected ice (no ICE CONDITION display): in flight, below **22000 ft**, a combination of temperature, altitude and speed, **150–320 KIAS** and vertical speed between **–200 and +200 ft/min**. If all conditions are true for **2 min** the system activates and stays on until **2 min** after one condition becomes false.

**SAI IBIT:** the wing anti-ice tests itself in flight **10 min after takeoff or at 10000 ft AGL** (whichever first). The slat anti-ice valves open (status A-I WING VLV OPEN). The test lasts at most **80 s** and ends earlier when all slat sensors have increased by 5.5°C (10°F). A failure shows A-I WING FAIL.

abschnitte.text:
**Windshield Heating:** Die Windshields werden elektrisch gegen Eis und Beschlag geheizt. Die Buttons bleiben gedrückt (IN), der Controller hält die Temperatur automatisch im Sollbereich. Das System arbeitet nur mit **mindestens zwei AC-Quellen**. Mit nur einer AC-Quelle am Boden (z. B. ein IDG) heizt jeder Controller im Power-up BIT für **120 Sekunden**. Mit einer einzigen AC-Quelle **im Flug** wird nur das **linke** Windshield geheizt; fällt dieses aus, wird das rechte verfügbar.

**ADSP/TAT Heating:** Vier Air Data Smart Probes und zwei TAT Probes an der Rumpfnase, jede mit eigenem Heater, im Normalfall vollautomatisch. ADSPs werden geheizt, sobald eine Engine läuft oder das Flugzeug in der Luft ist. TATs werden geheizt bei OAT unter 10°C mit laufender Engine, über 50 kt oder airborne (Post-Mod SB 190-34-0051); nach der Landung schaltet das TAT Heating unter 45 kt ab. Der **ADS PROBES HEATER** Button übersteuert die Logik am Boden, z. B. wenn Probes mit Eis oder Schnee kontaminiert sind (Before Start). Nur mit Batterien wird nur **ADSP 3** geheizt. Mit laufenden Engines Button OUT.

**Wiper:** Zwei unabhängige Wiper mit eigenen Knobs: TIMER (8 s intermittierend), OFF (in Parkstellung), LOW, HIGH. **Maximum Airspeed für Wiper-Betrieb: 253 KIAS.**
abschnitte.text_en:
**Windshield heating:** the windshields are electrically heated for anti-icing and anti-fogging. The buttons stay pushed in, and the controller automatically keeps the temperature in range. The system only operates with **at least two AC sources**. With a single AC source on ground (e.g. one IDG) each controller performs its power-up BIT, heating for **120 seconds**. With a single AC source **in flight** only the **left** windshield is heated; if it fails, the right one becomes available.

**ADSP/TAT heating:** four air data smart probes and two TAT probes on the nose, each with its own heater, normally fully automatic. ADSPs are heated whenever an engine is running or the airplane is airborne. TATs are heated with OAT below 10°C and an engine running, above 50 kt, or airborne (post-mod SB 190-34-0051); after landing TAT heating disables below 45 kt. The **ADS PROBES HEATER** button overrides the logic on ground, e.g. when probes are contaminated with ice or snow (before start). On batteries only, only **ADSP 3** is heated. Push the button out with engines running.

**Wipers:** two independent wipers with their own knobs: TIMER (8 s intermittent), OFF (stowed), LOW, HIGH. **Maximum airspeed for wiper operation: 253 KIAS.**

quellen.zitat: The ice protection system includes the engine anti-ice, wing anti-ice, windshield heaters and the ice detectors. The engines and wings anti- ice use bleed air from the engines as a heat source.
The engines cowls are heated with air from the low stage bleed, extracted from the respective engine. Each engine anti-ice system is independent.
The engine anti-ice valve is fail safe open if either the electrical or pressure signal are not present.
All three outboard leading edges are heated by bleed air extracted from the engines. Each engine provides bleed air for the respective wing anti-ice.
The APU is not capable of supplying bleed air for the anti-ice operation.
If one bleed air fails, the anti-ice system automatically opens the cross bleed valve and uses the opposite bleed for both wings anti-ice.
To prevent asymmetric ice operation, if the wing anti-ice system on one side fails, the system on the opposite side is inoperative.

If an icing condition is detected during flight, the ice detectors command the wing and engine anti-ice valves to open and remain activated for 5 minutes after the icing condition is no longer detected.
In case of a dual ice detector failure, the anti-ice operation is only possible in the manual mode.
During ground operation, at low speeds and visible moisture, ice could accumulate at the engine cowls without being detected by the ice detectors.
The MCDU setting operates the anti-ice system and inhibits the ice detectors activation logic during takeoff until 1700 ft AGL or 2 min after liftoff, whichever occur first.
ENG – Only the engine anti-ice valve will be kept open after engine start. The wing anti-ice valves remains inhibited closed.
ALL – The engine anti-ice valves are commanded open after completion of engine start and the wing anti-ice valves are commanded open with wheel speed above 40 kt.
In OFF or ENG operation modes and anti-ice mode selector knob set to ON position, the caution message “ENG REF A-I DISAG” and the advisory message “A-I MODE NOT AUTO” will be displayed on the EICAS.
If the REF A/I is set to ENG on the MCDU and the OAT temperature entered at the Takeoff Data Setting is below 5°C, the CAS message “ENG REF A-I DISAG” will be displayed.

After takeoff, the settings in the MCDU will be ignored by the airplane and the engine and wing anti-ice valves will open anytime an icing condition is detected, or the Ice Protection Panel Mode Switch is set to ON position.

The system only operates if there are at least two AC electrical sources.

When the batteries are the only electrical source to the airplane, only the ADSP 3 will be heated.
– The OAT is below 10°C (50°F) with an engine running, – Airspeed is above 50 kt, or – The airplane is airborne. Upon landing, the TAT heating disables when airspeed is below 45 kt.

The TO DATASET MENU on the MCDU must be set to ALL when OAT is below 5°C: if there is any possibility of encountering visible moisture up to 1700 ft AFE,

Take-off is prohibited in freezing rain or freezing drizzle conditions (i.e. FZRA, +FZRA, FZDZ, +FZDZ).

If SAT is lower than 5°C or there is ice accretion, plan a flap 5 landing and maintain VREF FLAP 5 ICE. CAUTION: MULTIPLY THE FULL FLAPS UNFACTORED LANDING DISTANCE BY 1.25.

artikel.titel: E1 Landing Gear, Brakes und Steering
artikel.titel_en: E1 Landing Gear, Brakes and Steering
artikel.kurz: Wie das Gear der E190/E195 aus- und einfährt, welche Backups es gibt, wie Brakes, Antiskid und Autobrake zusammenspielen und welche Steering-Winkel gelten.
artikel.kurz_en: How the E190/E195 gear extends and retracts, which backups exist, how brakes, antiskid and autobrake interact and which steering angles apply.

abschnitte.titel: Überblick: Landing Gear, Brakes und Steering
abschnitte.titel_en: Overview: landing gear, brakes and steering
abschnitte.text:
Das Landing Gear der E190/E195 (E1) ist hydraulisch betätigt und besteht aus einem Nose Gear und zwei Main Gears mit je zwei Rädern. Das Nose Gear hat ein **Steer-by-Wire**-System, die Brakes arbeiten **Brake-by-Wire** über die Rudder Pedals. Alle Parameter siehst du auf den MFD-Synoptic-Pages, Meldungen auf dem EICAS.

Zentral für fast alle Logiken ist die **Air/Ground-Erkennung**: Zwei Proximity Sensor Electronic Modules (**PSEM**) werten sechs Weight-on-Wheels-Sensoren (WOW) aus, zwei pro Bein. Fallen beide WOW-Sensoren eines Beins aus, verhindert die PSEM-Logik, dass sich der Landing Gear Lever nach UP bewegen lässt. Am Boden erscheint dann **LG NO DISPATCH**, in der Luft merkst du es am klemmenden Lever (DOWN) und an der Meldung **LG WOW SYS FAIL**.

Warum das wichtig ist: Ohne korrektes WOW-Signal funktionieren Gear-Lever-Lock, Autobrake, Ground Spoilers und Steering-Logik nicht wie erwartet. Bleibt ein Shock Absorber nach dem Takeoff eingefedert, rechnet das PSEM weiter mit "am Boden" und der Lever bleibt verriegelt.
abschnitte.text_en:
The E190/E195 (E1) landing gear is hydraulically operated and consists of a nose gear and two main gears, each a conventional dual-wheel unit. The nose gear has a **steer-by-wire** system and the brakes are **brake-by-wire** via the rudder pedals. Parameters are shown on the MFD synoptic pages, messages on the EICAS.

Almost every logic depends on **air/ground sensing**: two proximity sensor electronic modules (**PSEM**) process six weight-on-wheels (WOW) sensors, two per leg. If both WOW sensors on the same leg fail, the PSEM logic prevents the landing gear lever from moving up. On the ground **LG NO DISPATCH** is displayed; in flight the failure shows as a lever stuck in DOWN and the message **LG WOW SYS FAIL**.

Why it matters: without a correct WOW signal the gear lever lock, autobrake, ground spoilers and steering logic do not behave as expected. If a shock absorber stays compressed after takeoff, the PSEM keeps computing "on ground" and the lever stays locked.

abschnitte.text:
Die Brakes sind Brake-by-Wire. **Hydraulic System 1** versorgt die **Outboard Brakes**, **Hydraulic System 2** die **Inboard Brakes**. Gesteuert wird über zwei Brake Control Modules: **BCM 1** (DC ESS BUS 1) für outboard und **BCM 2** (DC ESS BUS 2) für inboard. Das Autobrake Module (**ABM**) hängt am DC BUS 2.

Fallen beide Hydraulic Systems oder beide BCM aus, bleibt die **Emergency/Parking Brake**. Sie hat eigene Accumulators, die von den normalen Hydraulic Systems getrennt sind und Druck für **sechs Vollbremsungen** liefern. Der Brake-Verschleiss wird über die Brake Wear Pins an jedem Hauptrad kontrolliert: sind sie bündig, müssen die Brakes ersetzt werden.
abschnitte.text_en:
The brakes are brake-by-wire. **Hydraulic system 1** supplies the **outboard brakes**, **hydraulic system 2** the **inboard brakes**. Control is via two brake control modules: **BCM 1** (DC ESS BUS 1) for the outboard and **BCM 2** (DC ESS BUS 2) for the inboard brakes. The autobrake module (**ABM**) is powered by DC BUS 2.

If both hydraulic systems or both BCMs fail, the **emergency/parking brake** remains. Its accumulators are isolated from the normal hydraulic systems and hold enough pressure for **six full-brake applications**. Brake wear is checked with the brake wear pins on each main wheel: when they are flush, the brakes need replacement.

abschnitte.fussnote: Autobrake lässt sich nur armen, wenn das normale Brake System funktioniert. Antiskid, Touchdown und Locked Wheel Protection bleiben aktiv. Wird Autobrake durch einen ABM- oder BCM-Fehler disarmed, ertönt "AUTOBRAKE".
abschnitte.fussnote_en: Autobrake can only be armed if the normal brake system is operational. Antiskid, touchdown and locked wheel protections remain active. If autobrake is disarmed by an ABM or BCM failure, the aural "AUTOBRAKE" sounds.

abschnitte.text:
Autobrake regelt auf eine **konstante Verzögerung** je nach gewählter Stufe. Mit Reverse Thrust nimmt das System entsprechend Bremsdruck weg, deshalb bringen die Reversers bei guter Bremswirkung und erreichtem Deceleration Target wenig zusätzlich. **RTO** liefert die maximale Verzögerung, gleichwertig mit maximaler manueller Bremsung; laut OM-B wird RTO empfohlen, um im Rejected Takeoff die Workload zu reduzieren.

Nach der Landing mit LO, MED oder HI: Normale Funktion und Verzögerung prüfen, bei **80 kt** die Brake Pedals drücken, um Autobrake zu deaktivieren, und auf sichere Taxi Speed abbremsen. Reicht die Autobrake-Verzögerung nicht für die verfügbare Distanz, sofort manuell bremsen.
abschnitte.text_en:
Autobrake modulates to a **constant deceleration** for the selected level. With reverse thrust the system reduces brake pressure accordingly, so with good braking and the deceleration target reached, the reversers add little. **RTO** gives the maximum deceleration, equivalent to maximum manual braking; the OM-B recommends RTO to decrease workload in a rejected takeoff.

After landing with LO, MED or HI: verify normal braking and deceleration, at **80 kt** press the brake pedals to disengage the autobrake and brake to a safe taxi speed. If the autobrake deceleration is not suitable for the stopping distance, use manual braking immediately.

– Radio altitude below 700 ft AGL, and – Either thrust lever is set below 45° for two operative engines, or – Thrust lever is set below 60° for a one-engine inoperative condition.
To prevent structural damage to the airplane the landing gear must be retracted only in case of an emergency that requires climb performance improvement.
Hydraulic system 1 provides pressure to the outboard brakes and hydraulic system 2 provides pressure to the inboard brakes.
– BCM 1 is connected to DC ESS BUS 1 and controls the outboard brakes. – BCM 2 is connected to DC ESS BUS 2 and controls the inboard brakes. – ABM is connected to DC BUS 2.
Locked wheel protection is active anytime on ground and at wheel speeds above 30 kt.
For wheel speeds below 10 kt, the antiskid protection is deactivated, thus allowing the pilot to lock and pivot on a wheel for maneuvering.
The accumulators have sufficient pressure to provide six full-brake applications.
In this case it has to be pulled carefully and slowly as there is no antiskid protection while braking with the Emergency/Parking brake.
For landing mode, the main landing gear WOW must indicate the airplane is on ground for more than 2 seconds to allow autobrake application.
RTO is the selected takeoff mode with the maximum deceleration rate. This deceleration is equivalent to the maximum manual braking.
The autobrake system can only be armed if the normal brake system is operational. Antiskid, touchdown and locked wheel protections are provided during autobrake operation.
– Pedal braking is applied (while wheel speed is above 60 kt if RTO is selected). – Brake control system failure is detected (while wheel speed is below 60 kt if RTO is selected).
To decrease workload in this scenario it is recommended to use autobrake in RTO mode, although the pilot can manually override the autobrake as required.
At 80 kt, press the brakes pedal to disengage the autobrake and use the necessary braking force to reach a safe taxi speed.

The steering handwheel command is limited to a maximum steering angle of ± 76° allowed up to 10 kt. Over around 26 kt the maximum steering deflection is 20°. Over 100 kt the maximum deflection is ± 7°.
The maximum steering angle of the rudder pedal is ±7°. FREE WHEEL STEERING MODE The free wheel steering mode is mostly used for towing or when the normal steering system fails.
The airplane nose landing gear has steer-by-wire control powered by hydraulic system 2 and electronically controlled by the Nose Wheel Steering Control Module.
– Failure of the Air/Ground signal occurs. – Nose wheel angle is greater than 76°. – Nose wheel steering system failure is detected.

abschnitte.text:
Das Automatic Flight Control System (AFCS) der E1 umfasst **Flight Director (FD)**, **Autopilot (AP)** mit gekoppeltem Go-Around und **Yaw Damper (YD)**. Es liefert Daten an das Flight Guidance Control System (**FGCS**, Lateral- und Vertical-Modes) und das Thrust Management System (**TMS**, Autothrottle und Thrust Ratings). Bedient wird alles über das Guidance Panel (GP) mit zwei unabhängigen Kanälen A und B.

Die E-Jets haben **einen Autopilot mit zwei Kanälen**: Ein Kanal ist aktiv, der andere läuft als Hot Spare. Bei einem Fehler wechselt das System automatisch, ausserdem nach jeder Landing. Da die AP-Servos an den Controls hängen, siehst du jeden AP-Input an Control Column, Control Wheel und Rudder.

Mit dem **SRC Button** wählst du, ob die linke oder rechte FMA-Seite die Quelle für den AP ist (grüner Pfeil auf der FMA). Der FD lässt sich auf der gekoppelten Seite nicht ausschalten, solange der AP engaged ist.
abschnitte.text_en:
The E1 Automatic Flight Control System (AFCS) includes the **flight director (FD)**, the **autopilot (AP)** with coupled go-around and the **yaw damper (YD)**. It supplies data to the Flight Guidance Control System (**FGCS**, lateral and vertical modes) and the Thrust Management System (**TMS**, autothrottle and thrust ratings). Everything is operated through the guidance panel (GP), which has two independent channels A and B.

The E-Jets have **a single autopilot with a dual-channel configuration**: one channel is active, the other works as a hot spare. The system switches automatically after a failure and also after each landing. Because the AP servos are connected to the controls, every AP input is visible on the control column, control wheel and rudder.

The **SRC button** selects the left or right FMA as source for the AP (green arrow on the FMA). On the coupled side the FD cannot be removed while the AP is engaged.

abschnitte.titel: Autothrottle: Engage, Disengage und Low Speed Protection
abschnitte.titel_en: Autothrottle: engage, disengage and low speed protection
punkte: Engagement am Boden: keine AT Failures, AT Button gedrückt, beide Thrust Levers über 50° TLA. In flight: zusätzlich mindestens 400 ft AGL.

Normal Disengagement: AT Disconnect Button auf den Thrust Levers oder AT Button am GP; automatisch nach Touchdown, bei Thrust Levers über TO/GA oder bei Reverse im RTO. Aural "THROTTLE", AT blinkt 5 s grün.
Non-Normal Disengagement: TLA-Differenz grösser als 8° oder AT Failure. AT blinkt rot, EICAS AT FAIL.
Low Speed Protection mit Flaps 1 bis Full: 1.2 Vs. Mit Flaps 0: unter 20000 ft 1.2 Vs, über 30000 ft 2 % über dem amber Low Speed Awareness Tape, dazwischen linear interpoliert.
SPDE mit AP OFF: Wenn du vom FD abweichst, bleibt Thrust auf Idle oder Maximum und die Speed läuft weg. Lösung laut AOM: FD ausschalten, damit AT auf SPDT zurückfällt.
punkte_en: Engagement on ground: no AT failures, AT button pressed, both thrust levers above 50° TLA. In flight: additionally at or above 400 ft AGL.

Normal disengagement: AT disconnect button on the thrust levers or AT button on the GP; automatic after touchdown, with thrust levers beyond TO/GA or with reverse during RTO. Aural "THROTTLE", AT flashes green for 5 s.
Non-normal disengagement: TLA difference greater than 8° or AT failure. AT flashes red, EICAS AT FAIL.
Low speed protection with flaps 1 to full: 1.2 Vs. With flaps 0: below 20000 ft 1.2 Vs, above 30000 ft 2 % over the amber low speed awareness tape, linear interpolation in between.
SPDE with AP OFF: if you deviate from the FD, thrust stays at idle or maximum and the speed runs away. AOM remedy: turn the FD off so the AT reverts to SPDT.

quellen.zitat: The E-JETS have a single autopilot with a dual channel configuration. One channel is active while the other works as a hot spare.
– Magenta: FMS commanded active/engaged mode. – Green: Non-FMS commanded active/engaged mode. – White: Armed mode. – Amber: Alert condition. – Red: Abnormal condition.
– Bank angle at 6° or below: AP levels the wings. – Bank angle above 6° and below 35°: AP holds present bank angle. – Bank angle at 35° or above: AP maintains bank angle at 35°.
LNAV mode is armed, LNAV will automatically engage when passing through 200 ft during a climb.
The automatic transition from ROLL to TRACK during takeoff occurs when: – IAS is greater than 100 kt and; – Bank angle is at 3° or below for more than 10 s.
The vertical speed command range goes from -8000 ft/min to +6000 ft/ min.
The GA mode first guidance sets pitch at 8°. When IAS is greater than the speed target, the guidance will be the speed target according to the following: – All engines operating: VREF + 20 kt.
The system will guide the Pitch initially to the calculated angle. When airborne and IAS is greater than speed target, the guidance will be as follows: – All engines operating: V2 + 10 kt.

The VGP mode can be armed by pressing the APP button on the Guidance Panel when within 30 NM radial distance from the destination, and a non-localizer based approach with a published constant glide path angle is selected in the FMS.
By default the FMS path angle is 3°. When required it can be manually varied from 1 to 6 degrees.
Changing the baro setting with ALT mode active may cause the airplane to inadvertently change the flight altitude, which may lead to high vertical speeds.

The autopilot also disengages if one of the following conditions occurs: – AP button is pressed on the guidance panel; – Either manual pitch trim switch is actuated; – Either stick shaker is activated.
The AT engages on ground when all of the following conditions occur: – no AT active failures. – AT button pressed on the guidance panel. – both thrust levers above 50° TLA.
HOLD mode is engaged at or above 60 KIAS during the takeoff roll. The AT servos are de-energized and thrust lever movements are not commanded up to 400 ft AGL.
The AT disengages when any of the following conditions occurs: – difference in TLA greater than 8° – autothrottle failure.
In this case, turn the flight director OFF to revert the AT to SPDT. This procedure is to have engine thrust controlling airspeed.
– Both RA/BARO selector knobs set to RA. – Radio altitude between 800 ft and 1500 ft. – Minimums displayed on both PFDs are valid.
AUTOLAND 1 consists of approach, touchdown and 5 seconds of roll out and can be accomplished on CAT I, II or IIIa approaches.
– Retard (RETD): if the autothrottle is engaged, retard engages at 30 ft and commands throttle to idle.
A pre-trim up is commanded at 800 ft radio altitude in order to prevent a nose down transient in an event of an autopilot disconnection.
CAT II – RA/BARO selector set to RA and RA minimums set to 80 ft or above.

artikel.kurz: CF34-10E5A1 mit FADEC: Limits, Starter Duty Cycle, Start-Logik, Thrust Ratings, ATTCS und Idle Modes, dazu die APS 2300 APU mit allen Altitude- und Temperatur-Limits.
artikel.kurz_en: CF34-10E5A1 with FADEC: limits, starter duty cycle, start logic, thrust ratings, ATTCS and idle modes, plus the APS 2300 APU with all altitude and temperature limits.

abschnitte.text:
Die E190-E1 und E195-E1 von Helvetic fliegen mit zwei **General Electric CF34-10E5A1**. Das CF34-10E ist ein High-Bypass Two-Spool Turbofan (N1 und N2 mechanisch unabhängig) mit integrierter Nacelle und Thrust Reverser.

Gesteuert wird jede Engine von einem **Dual-Channel FADEC**: Ein Kanal ist in Control, der zweite rechnet als Standby alle Daten mit und übernimmt bei einem Fehler. Der Control-Kanal wechselt bei jedem Engine Start. Über ca. 50 % N2 versorgt sich der FADEC selbst über den Permanent Magnet Alternator (PMA), darunter oder bei PMA-Ausfall liefert das Electrical System des Flugzeugs Backup Power.

Der FADEC übernimmt Engine Protection, die Regelung von Requested und Maximum N1 sowie die **ATTCS**-Logik. Für dich heisst das: Thrust Lever in die richtige Detent setzen, Parameter überwachen, Limits kennen. Die Zahlen unten sind die, die du im Ernstfall ohne Nachschlagen wissen solltest.
abschnitte.text_en:
Helvetic's E190-E1 and E195-E1 are powered by two **General Electric CF34-10E5A1** engines. The CF34-10E is a high-bypass dual-rotor turbofan (N1 and N2 mechanically independent) with an integrated nacelle and thrust reverser.

Each engine is controlled by a **dual-channel FADEC**: one channel is in control, the other runs as standby, processing all data, and takes over after a failure. The in-control channel alternates at every engine start. Above approximately 50 % N2 the FADEC is powered by its permanent magnet alternator (PMA); below that, or if the PMA fails, the airplane electrical system provides backup power.

The FADEC handles engine protection, control of requested and maximum N1 and the **ATTCS** logic. For you this means: set the thrust lever in the right detent, monitor the parameters, know the limits. The numbers below are the ones you should know without looking them up.

zellen: FADEC schaltet die Engine bei 102 % N2 ab
zellen_en: FADEC shuts the engine down at 102 % N2

zellen: FADEC gibt keinen Fuel frei, solange ITT über 120 °C
zellen_en: FADEC does not allow fuel flow while ITT is above 120 °C

zellen: Nach Start mit Oil Temp unter -20 °C: 5 psi bei Idle für max. 2 min
zellen_en: After start with oil temperature below -20 °C: 5 psi at idle for max. 2 min

abschnitte.fussnote_en: Source: OM-B E1 1.4.4.2. Short ITT transients above the takeoff limit are allowed: 5.5 °C for 2 s, 4.4 °C for 5 s, 3.6 °C for 15 s, 2.4 °C for 30 s.

zellen: 90 s am Boden / 120 s in flight
zellen_en: 90 s on ground / 120 s in flight

zellen: 90 s am Boden / 120 s in flight
zellen_en: 90 s on ground / 120 s in flight

abschnitte.fussnote: Die maximale kumulierte Starter-Laufzeit pro Start Attempt (Motoring plus Start) beträgt 90 s am Boden und 120 s in flight.
abschnitte.fussnote_en: The maximum cumulative starter run time per start attempt (motoring plus start) is 90 s on ground and 120 s in flight.

abschnitte.titel: Ground Start: was der FADEC macht (FADEC 5.61)
abschnitte.titel_en: Ground start: what the FADEC does (FADEC 5.61)

zellen: Start Control Valve öffnet, Fuel aber erst, wenn ITT unter 120 °C
zellen_en: Start control valve opens, but fuel only when ITT drops below 120 °C

zellen: FADEC aktiviert die Ignition (am Boden ein Igniter)
zellen_en: FADEC initiates ignition (one igniter on ground)

zellen: Metering Valve öffnet, abhängig von der Start-Altitude
zellen_en: Metering valve opens, depending on start altitude

zellen: Ignition und Fuel aus, 30 s Dry Motoring, dann Single Ignition und Fuel; nach 7 s Dual Ignition für 8 s
zellen_en: Ignition and fuel off, 30 s dry motoring, then single ignition and fuel; after 7 s dual ignition for 8 s

zellen: SCV schliesst, FADEC beschleunigt auf Ground Idle
zellen_en: SCV closes, FADEC accelerates to ground idle

zellen: FADEC unterbricht den Fuel; SCV schliesst nicht automatisch, START/STOP auf STOP
zellen_en: FADEC shuts off fuel; SCV is not closed automatically, select START/STOP to STOP

abschnitte.fussnote: Am Boden schützt der FADEC vor Hung Start, Hot Start und No Light-off. In flight gibt es diesen Schutz nicht.
abschnitte.fussnote_en: On ground the FADEC protects against hung start, hot start and no light-off. In flight this protection is not available.

punkte: Quellen für einen Airstart: Cross-Bleed, APU Bleed oder Windmilling. In flight aktiviert der FADEC beide Igniters.
Cross-Bleed Start: wie am Boden, aber Fuel wird automatisch freigegeben, wenn N2 nach 15 s noch nicht 15 % erreicht hat.
Windmill Start: Ignition bei 7 % N2, Fuel bei mindestens 7.2 % N2 oder nach 15 s, je nachdem was zuerst eintritt.
Keine FADEC-Protection gegen Hot Start, Hung Start oder fehlendes Light-off in flight. Kein Light-off innert 30 s nach Fuel Flow: Start manuell abbrechen.
FADEC 5.61: Bei ITT-Überschreitung im Airstart wird der Fuel für 4 s unterbrochen und der Start fortgesetzt, maximal 8 Mal. Der Start wird nicht automatisch abgebrochen.
Auto Relight: Bei Flameout schaltet der FADEC beide Igniters ein, WML-Icon neben N2. Kein Relight innert 30 s oder N2 unter 7.2 %: mit START/STOP auf STOP beenden.
punkte_en: Air start sources: cross-bleed, APU bleed or windmilling. In flight the FADEC energizes both igniters.
Cross-bleed start: identical to a ground start, but fuel is introduced automatically if N2 has not reached 15 % after 15 s.
Windmill start: ignition at 7 % N2, fuel at a minimum of 7.2 % N2 or after 15 s, whichever occurs first.
No FADEC protection against hot start, hung start or failure to light off in flight. No light-off within 30 s after fuel flow: abort the start manually.
FADEC 5.61: if the ITT limit is exceeded during an air start, fuel is interrupted for 4 s and the start resumes, up to 8 times. The start is not aborted automatically.
Auto relight: after a flameout the FADEC turns on both igniters, WML icon next to N2. No relight within 30 s or N2 below 7.2 %: terminate with START/STOP to STOP.

abschnitte.fussnote: Werte aus der AOM-Tabelle (Spalte CF34-10E5A1), flat rated bis ISA+15 °C. Die OEI-Spalte mit ATTCS ON zeigt den Reserve Thrust (RSV). Auf der MCDU-Seite T/O DATASET erscheinen für die CF34-10E5A1 die Kennungen 18K5 / 17K1 / 15K5.
abschnitte.fussnote_en: Values from the AOM table (column CF34-10E5A1), flat rated up to ISA+15 °C. The OEI column with ATTCS ON shows the reserve thrust (RSV). On the MCDU T/O DATASET page the CF34-10E5A1 is identified as 18K5 / 17K1 / 15K5.

abschnitte.text:
Das **ATTCS** (Automatic Takeoff Thrust Control System) ist für Takeoff und Go-Around verfügbar und standardmässig ON (MCDU TAKEOFF DATA SET MENU). Auf dem EICAS bedeutet **ATTCS weiss = enabled**, **ATTCS grün = armed**; armed wird es erst, wenn die Thrust Levers in TO/GA stehen.

Engaged und mit Thrust Levers in TO/GA kommandiert das ATTCS automatisch **RSV**, wenn: der N1-Unterschied grösser als 15 % ist, eine Engine im Takeoff oder Go-Around ausfällt oder Windshear erkannt wird. Manuell erreichst du RSV mit Thrust Levers auf **MAX**. Danach verschwindet das grüne ATTCS und der Thrust Mode erhält den Zusatz "RSV".

**Flex Takeoff** reduziert den Thrust über eine Assumed Temperature, die höher als TO TEMP sein muss. Minimum ist 75 % des maximalen Takeoff Thrust oder CLB-2 + 1 % N1, je nachdem was höher ist. Laut OM-B ist die Thrust-Reduktion auf 25 % begrenzt, Assumed Temperature ist auf Runways mit Standing Water, Slush, Snow oder Ice nicht erlaubt, und mit **MAX** lässt sich die Assumed Temperature jederzeit canceln.
abschnitte.text_en:
The **ATTCS** (automatic takeoff thrust control system) is available for takeoff and go-around and is ON by default (MCDU TAKEOFF DATA SET MENU). On the EICAS **ATTCS white = enabled**, **ATTCS green = armed**; it arms only when the thrust levers reach TO/GA.

When engaged and with thrust levers at TO/GA the ATTCS automatically commands **RSV** if: the N1 difference is greater than 15 %, an engine fails during takeoff or go-around, or windshear is detected. RSV is set manually by moving the thrust levers to **MAX**. The green ATTCS then disappears and the thrust mode shows an additional "RSV".

**Flex takeoff** reduces thrust using an assumed temperature that must be higher than TO TEMP. The minimum is 75 % of maximum rated takeoff thrust or CLB-2 + 1 % N1, whichever is higher. Per OM-B the total thrust reduction is limited to 25 %, assumed temperature is not allowed on runways contaminated with standing water, slush, snow or ice, and **MAX** cancels the assumed temperature at any time.

abschnitte.text:
Die APU sitzt im Tailcone und liefert **Bleed Air** (Engine Start und Packs) sowie **115 V AC, 40 kVA** über einen eigenen Generator. Ein eigener FADEC steuert Start, Shutdown, Fault Detection und Status.

**Start**: APU MASTER auf ON versorgt den FADEC und öffnet das Fuel Shutoff Valve, auf dem EICAS erscheinen RPM und EGT. Das AOM empfiehlt, nach dem Einschalten des EICAS **30 s** zu warten, bevor du START wählst. **3 s nach 95 %** APU Speed stehen elektrische und pneumatische Last zur Verfügung.

**Normal Shutdown** (MASTER OFF): Bleed wird sofort weggenommen, der Generator erst nach **1 min Cooldown**; danach Spooldown, bis APU SHUTTING DOWN verschwindet. Zurück auf ON bricht den Shutdown ab. Der **EMER STOP** Button schliesst das Fuel SOV und stellt die APU ohne Cooldown ab.

**Fuel**: Mit nur DC-Strom liefert die DC Fuel Pump (rechter Tank), mit AC und stehender Engine die AC Pump, bei laufender Engine die Ejector Pump. Über das Crossfeed geht auch Fuel aus dem linken Tank.
abschnitte.text_en:
The APU is in the tailcone and supplies **bleed air** (engine start and packs) and **115 V AC, 40 kVA** from its own generator. A dedicated FADEC controls start, shutdown, fault detection and status.

**Start**: APU MASTER to ON powers the FADEC and opens the fuel shutoff valve; RPM and EGT appear on the EICAS. The AOM recommends waiting **30 s** after the EICAS is energized before selecting START. **Three seconds after 95 %** APU speed, electrical and pneumatic loads are available.

**Normal shutdown** (MASTER OFF): bleed is removed immediately, electrical power only after a **1 minute cooldown**; then spooldown until APU SHUTTING DOWN disappears. Selecting ON again cancels the shutdown. The **EMER STOP** button closes the fuel SOV and shuts the APU down without cooldown.

**Fuel**: with only DC power the DC fuel pump (right tank) supplies the APU, with AC power and engine not running the AC pump, with the engine running the ejector pump. Fuel from the left tank is possible via the crossfeed.

artikel.kurz: Engines, APU, Cargo und Lavatories im Vergleich: Detection Loops, Bottles, Discharge-Logik, Fire Test und alle Fire-EICAS-Messages der E190/E195.
artikel.kurz_en: Engines, APU, cargo and lavatories compared: detection loops, bottles, discharge logic, fire test and all fire EICAS messages of the E190/E195.

abschnitte.text:
Die Fire Protection der E190/E195 (E1) deckt vier Bereiche ab: **Engines**, **APU**, **Cargo Compartments** und **Lavatories**. Dazu kommen Portable Fire Extinguishers im Cockpit und in der Kabine. Detection und Extinguishing sind pro Bereich unterschiedlich aufgebaut, und genau diese Unterschiede werden gerne gefragt: wie viele Loops, wie viele Bottles, was passiert automatisch und was musst du selbst auslösen.

Alle Komponenten ausser der Button-Beleuchtung werden laufend überwacht (Continuous Built-In Test). Ein interner Fehler erzeugt eine CAS-Meldung, z. B. ENG 1 FIRE DET FAIL. Deshalb gilt beim Power Up: keine Fire-Protection-Fail-Messages auf dem EICAS, dann den Fire Test durchführen.
abschnitte.text_en:
The E190/E195 (E1) fire protection covers four areas: **engines**, **APU**, **cargo compartments** and **lavatories**, plus portable fire extinguishers in the cockpit and cabin. Detection and extinguishing differ per area, and exactly these differences are commonly asked: how many loops, how many bottles, what happens automatically and what you have to trigger yourself.

All components except the button illumination are continuously monitored (continuous built-in test). An internal failure generates a CAS message, e.g. ENG 1 FIRE DET FAIL. Hence at power up: verify no fire protection fail messages on the EICAS, then perform the fire test.

abschnitte.titel: Engine Fire: Handle ziehen, dann drehen
abschnitte.text:
Ein Engine Fire meldet sich mit Aural Warning, Master WARNING, beleuchtetem Fire Handle, rotem **FIRE** im ITT-Instrument und der Warning **ENG 1 (2) FIRE**.

**Ziehen** des Fire Handle schliesst bei der betroffenen Engine das Fuel Shutoff Valve, die Hydraulic Shutoff Valves, das Bleed Shutoff Valve und das Crossbleed Valve. Erst danach lassen sich die Bottles auslösen: **Drehen gegen den Uhrzeigersinn = Bottle A**, **im Uhrzeigersinn = Bottle B**. Weil beide Bottles beide Engines bedienen, hast du für eine brennende Engine maximal zwei Schüsse; nach einem Schuss auf Engine 1 steht für Engine 2 nur noch die andere Bottle zur Verfügung.

Nach dem Entladen kann die Beleuchtung des Fire Handle erlöschen. Massgebend ist die CAS-Meldung: Ist ENG FIRE noch aktiv, brennt es weiter.
abschnitte.text_en:
An engine fire is indicated by the aural warning, master WARNING, illuminated fire handle, red **FIRE** in the ITT indicator and the warning **ENG 1 (2) FIRE**.

**Pulling** the fire handle closes the affected engine fuel shutoff valve, hydraulic shutoff valves, bleed shutoff valve and the crossbleed valve. Only then can the bottles be fired: **rotate counter clockwise = bottle A**, **clockwise = bottle B**. Because both bottles serve both engines, you have at most two shots for one engine; after a shot into engine 1 only the other bottle remains for engine 2.

After discharge the fire handle illumination may be lost. The CAS message is what counts: if ENG FIRE is still displayed, the fire persists.

abschnitte.text:
Bei einem APU Fire leuchtet der **rote Balken im APU EMER STOP Button**, Master WARNING und die Warning **APU FIRE** erscheinen. Drückst du **EMER STOP**, wird der rote durch einen weissen Balken ersetzt (APU abgestellt) und der **APU FIRE EXTINGUISHER Button** leuchtet ganz rot. Ein Druck darauf entlädt die Bottle. Der Button erlischt, sobald die Detectors kein Feuer mehr melden.

Wird EMER STOP nicht gedrückt, leuchtet der Extinguisher Button nach **1 min** trotzdem auf; Drücken entlädt dann die Bottle, stellt die APU ab und löscht den roten Balken. **Am Boden** schaltet sich die APU **10 s** nach Erkennung eines Feuers automatisch ab. Nach dem Entladen erscheint die Advisory APU FIREX BTL DISCH.
abschnitte.text_en:
In an APU fire the **red striped bar in the APU EMER STOP button** illuminates, together with master WARNING and the warning **APU FIRE**. Pressing **EMER STOP** replaces the red bar by a white bar (APU shut down) and the **APU FIRE EXTINGUISHER button** illuminates entirely red. Pressing it discharges the bottle. The button extinguishes when the detectors no longer sense a fire.

If EMER STOP is not pressed, the extinguisher button still illuminates after **1 min**; pressing it then discharges the bottle, shuts down the APU and turns off the red bar. **On ground** the APU shuts down automatically **10 s** after the fire condition is present. After discharge the advisory APU FIREX BTL DISCH is displayed.

abschnitte.fussnote: Drückst du den Button vor Ablauf der Minute nochmals, entlädt die Low-Rate Bottle sofort. Ohne Message armt der erste Druck die High-Rate Bottle (Button rot, EICAS FIREX HI ARM); ohne zweiten Druck innert 2 min wird das System zurückgesetzt.
abschnitte.fussnote_en: Pressing the button again before the minute has elapsed discharges the low-rate bottle immediately. Without a message, the first press arms the high-rate bottle (button red, EICAS FIREX HI ARM); without a second press within 2 min the system resets.

quellen.zitat: The fire protection system provides fire detection and extinguishing capabilities for: – Engines – APU – Cargo Compartments – Lavatories
The Engine Fire Detection System is monitored by two detector loops. When a fire condition is detected the signal goes to the MAU which generates the associated EICAS messages and alarms.
– Engine fire extinguisher: HOT BATT BUS 1 and HOT BATT BUS 2.
– the engine fuel shutoff valve – the engine hydraulic shutoff valves – the engine bleed air shutoff valve – the cross bleed shutoff valve.
A total of two fire extinguisher bottles named A and B are installed in the airplane to serve either or both engines.
Rotating the FIRE HANDLE counter clockwise discharges extinguisher bottle A into the associated engine. Rotating clockwise discharges extinguisher bottle B into the same engine.
When an engine fire extinguisher bottle is discharged, fire handle illumination may be lost. In this case if the CAS message is still active the fire condition persists.
In case of fire and 1 min has passed without APU EMER STOP pushbutton has been pressed, the APU fire extinguisher pushbutton illuminates.
On ground, the APU will automatically shut down 10 seconds after the fire condition is present.
The forward cargo compartment has four smoke detectors. The aft cargo compartment has three smoke detectors.

One minute later, the second fire extinguisher bottle discharges automatically at a reduced flow rate and the agent remains in the selected cargo compartment for 75 minutes for airplanes with 60- minute diversion time allowed.
If the button is pushed again within the next two minutes, the high-rate bottle is discharged. At this time the low-rate bottle is armed.

In case of fire on ground, the low-rate fire extinguisher bottle is not automatically discharged. The flight crew must push the cargo fire extinguisher pushbutton once again to discharge the low-rate bottle.
When the temperature inside the waste container exceeds a certain limit, the system automatically discharges the extinguisher agent.
CAUTION: IF THE FIRE DETECTION TEST BUTTON IS PRESSED FOR 10 SECONDS, THE APU WILL SHUTDOWN.
Verify there are no fire protection fail messages displayed on the EICAS after Power Up.

abschnitte.titel_en: Overview: how the E1 alerts the crew
abschnitte.text:
Die E190/E195 (E1) warnt über drei Kanäle: **Lichter** (Master WARNING/CAUTION), **EICAS-Meldungen** und **Aurals**. Das EICAS bietet ein Alerting mit **vier Stufen**; eine fünfte Stufe ist nur für Maintenance am Boden. Dazu kommen spezialisierte Systeme: Stall Protection (Stick Shaker), **EGPWS**, **TCAS** und Windshear Detection mit Escape Guidance.

Erzeugt werden die Meldungen von zwei **Monitor Warning Functions (MWF)** in verschiedenen MAUs. Eine hat Priorität, die andere ist Backup; fällt die erste aus, schaltet das Display automatisch um. Sind die beiden CAS-Listen 20 s lang verschieden, erscheint auf beiden PFDs **CAS MSG**; die Quelle lässt sich dann auf der MCDU-Setup-Seite wählen.
abschnitte.text_en:
The E190/E195 (E1) alerts the crew through three channels: **lights** (master WARNING/CAUTION), **EICAS messages** and **aurals**. The EICAS provides a **four-level** alerting system; a fifth level is for maintenance on the ground only. Specialised systems add to this: stall protection (stick shaker), **EGPWS**, **TCAS** and windshear detection with escape guidance.

The messages are generated by two **monitor warning functions (MWF)** in different MAUs. One has priority, the other is a backup; if the priority MWF fails, the display automatically uses the backup. If the two CAS lists differ continuously for 20 s, **CAS MSG** is shown on both PFDs; the source can then be selected on the MCDU setup page.

abschnitte.text: Root Messages sind mit ">" markiert: Eine Ursache kann viele Folgemeldungen erzeugen. Meist genügt das Procedure der Root Message, trotzdem alle Meldungen prüfen. Bei mehreren Root Messages ist die Reihenfolge: WARNING-Messages, dann ELECTRICAL BUSES, dann MAU.
abschnitte.text_en: Root messages are marked with ">": one cause can trigger many further messages. In most cases the root message procedure is enough, but always review all messages. With several root messages the order of evaluation is: WARNING messages, then ELECTRICAL BUSES, then MAU.

abschnitte.titel: TCAS RA: Regeln aus dem OM-B
abschnitte.titel_en: TCAS RA: rules from the OM-B
punkte: Kein Ausweichmanöver nur aufgrund eines TA ohne Sichtkontakt zum Traffic.
Manöver entgegen dem RA sind gefährlich und verboten, ausser visuell ist klar, dass nur so die Separation gesichert ist.
Die TCAS-II-Algorithmen erwarten den Beginn des Manövers innert 5 s nach dem RA und innert 2.5 s bei zusätzlichen korrigierenden RAs (Increase oder Reversal).
Ruhig in den grünen Bereich fliegen und aus der roten Zone heraus; das sollte nicht mehr als 0.75 g bis 1.25 g brauchen. Typische Höhenabweichung aus dem Level Flight: 300 bis 500 ft.
CLIMB RA in Landing Configuration: normalen Go-Around inklusive Thrust und Configuration Change einleiten.
Nach "CLEAR OF CONFLICT" sofort zur letzten ATC Clearance zurückkehren. Bei Stall Warning während eines RA: RA abbrechen und Stall Recovery fliegen.
punkte_en: Do not initiate evasive manoeuvres using TA information only without visually sighting the traffic.
Manoeuvres opposite to the RA are extremely hazardous and prohibited unless visually determined to be the only means to assure safe separation.
TCAS II algorithms assume the pilot starts the initial manoeuvre within 5 s of the RA and within 2.5 s for additional corrective RAs (increases or reversals).
Smoothly fly into the green area and out of the red zone; this should require no more than 0.75 g to 1.25 g. Typical altitude deviation from level flight: 300 to 500 ft.
CLIMB RA in landing configuration: initiate a normal go-around including thrust increase and configuration change.
After "CLEAR OF CONFLICT" promptly return to the previous ATC clearance. If stall warning occurs during an RA: abandon the RA and perform stall recovery.

quellen.zitat: An Engine Indication and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) provides the flight crew with a four- level alert messaging system. A fifth level is provided for maintenance purposes only.
If the two CAS message lists are continuously different for 20 s, a miscompare indication is annunciated.
WARNING (red): indicates an emergency or airplane system condition that requires immediate corrective or compensatory crew action.
ADVISORY (cyan): indicates operational or airplane conditions that require crew awareness. Subsequent or future crew action may be required.
Messages with the higher priority precede other messages when shown simultaneously. The EICAS displays up to 15 messages simultaneously.
Advisory messages will automatically revert from inverse to normal video after 5 seconds they started to be displayed.
If more than one root message is displayed at the same time or displayed together with a WARNING message, the priority order to be evaluated is: – WARNING messages; – ELECTRICAL BUSES and; – MAU.
The master warning annunciator is repeated with three-second intervals between alerts until the master warning reset switch is pressed.
Only a stall condition takes precedence over windshear, EGPWS and TCAS alerts.
Some EICAS messages are inhibited on takeoff or approach and landing to prevent it from being a nuisance.
K5 200 ft (landing) 30 seconds after Landing touchdown and wheelspeed below 30 kt.
– Parking brakes are applied (“NO TAKEOFF BRAKES”). – Pitch trim is out of green range (“NO TAKEOFF TRIM”). – Any spoiler panel is deployed (“NO TAKEOFF SPOILER”).

Mode 5 - Excessive deviation below glideslope with a GLIDESLOPE aural warning. Mode 6 - Advisory callouts with BANK ANGLE, MINIMUMS and selected altitudes aural warnings.
Illuminates when pressed any time below 2000 ft nominal radar altitude and will be automatically reset (light off) by climbing above 2000 ft nominal or descending below 30 ft.
The EGPWS database consists of all hard surfaces runways greater than 1067 m (3500 ft) in length.

– Is annunciated when other airplane is approximately 20 s to 30 s from the TCAS collision area.
– Cyan solid diamond: the other traffic is within 6.5 NM and 1200 ft above or below the airplane.
The TCAS automatically reverts to TA ONLY mode and inhibits RAs for altitudes below 900 ft AGL during descent, or below 1100 ft during climb.
All TCAS aural advisories are inhibited when the present position altitude is below 400 ft AGL during descent, or 600 ft AGL during climb.
TCAS II algorithms are based on the pilot starting the initial manoeuvre within 5 seconds of the RA and within 2 1/2 seconds for additional corrective RAs (increases or reversals).
The pilot must not initiate evasive manoeuvres using Traffic Advisory information (TA) only, without visually sighting conflicting traffic.
